items.statement: Stable cement demand supported by infrastructure, housing and construction; near-term influenced by monsoon and input cost volatility
items.quote: The quarter was characterized by stable cement demand, supported by infrastructure, housing and construction activity, while profitability across the industry remained under pressure from the higher imported fuel prices, elevated freight costs and geopolitical developments in West Asia.

items.statement: Good demand momentum in North, West, Central, East; South requires channel investment
items.quote: So for me, the key market remains, Manish, North, West, Central and East. All of them, for example, we are seeing a good traction. And that's how with confidence I mentioned to Navin also in terms of our estimates of guidance on the volume growth.

items.statement: Ambuja Cement (operating company) has zero debt; ICDs from ACC/Orient to parent within approved limits at 8% coupon
items.quote: So the operating company, Ambuja has no debt. And so far as the if you are alluding to the parent company debt, I would not be the right person to answer on that. Coming to the Ambuja level, as I mentioned, 0 debt, and I think we are managing our cash flows from the operating cash flows, and we have a good plan to sustain on that.

items.statement: No plans for brand merger of ACC/Ambuja into Adani Cement; company merger announced earlier
items.quote: So Rajesh, no such plans for the brand merger. Whatever the plan is for the company merger, which we have announced.

items.statement: RMC EBITDA at ~INR 33 crores in Q1 FY27 (margin ~7% vs 14-15% previous quarters)
items.quote: So okay, in terms of the RMC EBITDA for the quarter, we are at about INR33-odd crores...

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia could cause ~INR 100 PMT cost increase; mitigated by inventory and structural savings
items.quote: we are expecting, if at all, this kind of geopolitical situation continues, ballpark about say, INR100, for example, potential rise in the cost.

items.statement: Cost per ton guidance for FY27 is INR 4,250; target to reduce cost by INR 250 in FY28 to reach INR 4,000 or below per ton
items.quote: And with a high element of confidence, we are giving a guidance for INR4 to INR5 a ton for the FY27, number one. And the way we have worked upon is the next year also, we want to bring another INR250 reduction in the cost so that by end of FY28, we reach up to INR4,000 or below in terms of cost per metric ton.

items.statement: Cement volume growth target of 8-10% annually driven by capacity additions, with focus on trade segment (75%+ mix)
items.quote: When I'm adding 10% almost 10 million capacity, say, every year. So from a capacity addition perspective, we are growing almost say, 8% to 10%. And that is what, for example, we would be targeting to grow in terms of our growth plan on the trade side, especially.

items.statement: Annual capex run rate of INR 6,000-7,000 crores expected for FY28
items.quote: Yes. Yes. On a run rate, yes.

items.statement: Targeting 70-75% value-focused capacity utilization on expanded base of 119 million tons
items.quote: I think our targeted utilization now that our focus on value and all in that background, I'm saying around 70% to 75%. And this is like all value-focused capacity utilization, point number one.

items.statement: Maratha 4 million ton clinker line commissioning in Q1 FY28; Jodhpur 3 million ton clinker trials started, stabilizing in Q2 FY27; Mundra clinker project in 18-24 months (FY29)
items.quote: Maratha, we are expecting to commission next year. And that is what, for example, we have planned. So far as Jodhpur is concerned, we already have seen trials started. And in Q2, which is in this current quarter, it will start stabilizing and supplying to my grinding units.

items.statement: WHRS capacity to increase from 228 MW to 376 MW by FY28 (148 MW addition) across existing and new kiln lines including acquired assets
items.quote: So it's a combination of both the existing kiln lines and the new kiln lines basically. So in terms of the clinker new capacities coming up, say, Assam, we have announced and then Mundra, for example, then Maratha is expanding and so is the Penna, Jodhpur, which has come up now.

items.statement: Cost reduced QoQ by INR 206/ton to INR 4,241/ton in Q1 FY27 (includes RE power and fly ash sales netting); FY27 guidance INR 4,250/ton
items.quote: And every, for example, passing quarter, I will keep improving and there is going to be still a scope of improvement. So I think that's a learning curve and opportunity for us in my business.

items.statement: Green power sold at INR 3.3/unit vs grid cost INR 7-8/unit; 50% of Q1 RE power sales (45 cr units) to be consumed captively in Q2, rising to 90-95% in-house consumption within 3 quarters
items.quote: See, my blend of power, if I look at the overall, say, grid power, that comes almost at, say, INR7 to INR8 a unit. And that is the first opportunity for us to basically replace with this green power.

items.statement: Fly ash sales revenue ~INR 15 crores in Q1 FY27 vs ~INR 50 crores in Q4 FY26; long-term agreement in place, 30% consumed internally, surplus sold profitably
items.quote: So the first quarter sales is about INR25 crores to INR30 crores. Let me just confirm , can you just give me a minute I have the details with me, so Rahul, it is ~INR15 crores for the first quarter, and you are right, around INR50 crores for the last quarter.

items.statement: Curtailed ~1 million tons of low/negative EBITDA volumes in South (largely acquired assets); strategy to improve cost to make them viable and shift to trade segment
items.quote: So we actually curtailed the low and negative EBITDA volumes, and this is almost like closer to 1 million, for example, which was which we actually reduced.

items.statement: Maintenance cost accounting treatment under auditor review; currently expensed as incurred (INR 50/ton higher in Q1) vs planned quarterly amortization
items.quote: No, good point, Kamlesh. I think we are still engaging with our auditors on this point because from the accounting standard perspective, they are deliberating on this point that how we basically equalize over the four quarters.

items.statement: ISTS grid connectivity for cement plants to consume Khavda (700 MW) and Rajasthan (300 MW) RE power under execution; expected completion in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: In about say about two to three quarters in a phase-wise manner progressively. So, yes.

items.statement: Building young, energetic team with substantial L&D programs; group has methodical talent development structure
items.quote: We are building up a young team, a very enthusiastic and energetic team who are roaring to and willing to take up the larger responsibilities who have been groomed with substantial L&D programs and group has a very methodical structure on this basically.

items.statement: Acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi, Orient) are value-accretive; Orient delivers decent margins on consolidated basis including MSA benefits
items.quote: Bharat bhai, thank you for this alerting question, but we have actually got assets only, and these assets will actually start giving the results. So yes. So I think rest be assured, these are assets.

items.statement: Logistics cost elevated due to diesel shortages (West) and disruptions (East); tech platform being developed to optimize
items.quote: So, Kunal bhai, basically, there was this disruption of the diesel shortages and more so like in some of the plants in Western side and all, basically, which hampered the distribution and therefore, escalated the escalation of the costs.

items.statement: NSP aberration in Q1 due to channel investment accounting and market disruption; management expects normalization with trade share growth
items.quote: I think I mentioned to this, Rajesh, that we have seen a disruption in the June quarter coming from multiple factors which are beyond control. Therefore, for example, this was one quarter which has seen this aberration.

items.statement: Depreciation run rate to stabilize at Q1 level after Q4 merger true-up entries (Sanghi, Penna)
items.quote: the depreciation run rate would stay at the similar level in the last quarter due to the true-up entries which were taken on account of the merger of Sanghi and Penna, the depreciation was higher Q -on-Q. Otherwise, it's going to be at the similar level at this touch point.

items.statement: VRS scheme of INR 24 crores in South plant for efficiency; no impairment expected
items.quote: No, this is not to do with impairment. This is like a normal VRS scheme, which has been implemented in one of our plants in South India. And this is more about bringing more efficiency in the operations. Nothing to do with the impairment.

items.statement: RE power sales: INR 140 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR 70 crores in Q4 FY26 (24 cr units vs 45 cr units); priority shifting to captive consumption
items.quote: in terms of the overall sales, this was around 24 crores of units for the fourth quarter. Rahul Gupta: Versus 45 crores in this quarter

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected around depreciation level of INR 1,200 crores, not to exceed it
items.quote: Our annualized capex will be around the depreciation number. We will try not to exceed it, in fact be below that.

items.statement: Salt plant 82.5 KTPA in India operational by year-end, supplying by Q1 FY28; 210 KTPA South India salt plant and 50 KTPA silica plant operational during 2028
items.quote: The salt plant in India 82.5 KTPA, that should get operational by this year-end. So, you should start it supplying to market by first quarter of next financial year. The 210 KTPA Salt plant in South India, has a 24-month execution time. Similar is the execution timeline for 50 KTPA silica plant. So, they will become operational sometime during 2028.

items.statement: Input cost pressures: US logistics/transportation; UK gas prices (hedged); Kenya HFO prices up due to oil (hedged to October); India coal freight from Indonesia, limestone imports from Middle East if war continues beyond October
items.quote: Clearly watch out for Kenya HFO, India limestone beyond October, and energy cost increases in India mainly driven by logistics cost and the cost increase in US driven by again logistics cost.

items.statement: Exports to Argentina and Chile increased 53% and 32% respectively supported by lithium carbonate production; Southeast Asian demand declined marginally with maximum pricing pressure from Chinese exports
items.quote: Exports to Argentina and Chile have increased by 53% and 32% respectively, and Southeast Asian market mainly demand declined marginally; however, this is also a place where there is a maximum pricing pressure coming out of Chinese exports.

items.statement: Customers in food, pharma, industrial present across geographies want single point of accountability; New segment structure aligns with global customer view rather than geography view
items.quote: Many of our customers are present in multiple geographies. If you take customers in the food area, customers in the pharma area, customers also in industrial area, they are present in multi-geography. So, they also want a single point of accountability, which is the way we have been structured.

items.statement: Chinese soda ash inventories at all-time high 1.73 million mt; Chinese producers operating at high utilization; No significant supply curtailments announced; Market rebalancing dependent on supply rationalization
items.quote: Chinese inventories reached an all-time high of 1.73 million mt, and Chinese producers continue to operate at high utilization rate. The export volumes from China remain elevated and with no significant supply curtailments which are announced, the market rebalancing will be mainly driven off supply rationalization.

items.statement: Key risks: China oversupply keeping soda ash pricing subdued; Middle East conflict driving freight/raw material costs; Kenya HFO exposure beyond October; India limestone imports if war continues beyond October; US logistics cost pass-throug
items.quote: The operating environment remains dynamic with ongoing uncertainties and disruptions. There is a price challenge as well as the cost challenge in one of our biggest businesses, almost 50% of the revenue in soda ash.

items.statement: Sodium-ion battery pilot testing underway for stationary storage (renewable, data centers); First battery pack produced with BMS; Piloting to finish in 6-9 months; Full-scale plant 2 years after pilot; LFP battery recycling unit being set u
items.quote: we have certainly made the first battery pack and it's undergoing testing, and at the same time we are reviewing the entire business strategy for the sodium -ion battery, especially for the storage application. It will not be approp riate solution for mobility. It will remain as energy storage mainly for renewable power as well as data centers

items.statement: IMACID (JV) did not produce in Q1 due to high sulfur prices; Operations restarted in Q2; Expected to be profitable for full year
items.quote: IMACID did not produce during the quarter because of high sulfur prices. They have just begun operations during this quarter. So, we'll see how it progresses, but certainly that part of the business is under pressure in terms of margin, but they'll be profitable for the year.

items.statement: Employee cost included INR 43 crores one-off reversal (variable pay payout in Q1); Normal run rate ~INR 43 crores higher
items.quote: Employee cost you're right about 43 crore s. I think it's the normal run rate should be 43 more than that. That's a one-off during the quarter

items.statement: Will work with regulatory authorities in India to protect domestic industry from Chinese dumping threat across all markets
items.quote: we will work actively with especially since there is manufacturing facilities in India, we will work with regulatory author ities in making sure that domestic industry is kept healthy as far as we are concerned

items.statement: US exports to Southeast Asia at breakeven/unremunerative; Vacated most of SE Asia market to Chinese; Higher exports to LATAM and Northeast Asia; UK lost GBP 2.4M on EU ETS sale (may recover by October)
items.quote: In terms of US, one of the key approaches we have is that the biggest impact in the shift which has happened in terms of margin is on the export front, especially the export volumes which we were sending to Southeast Asia. They are just at breakeven level or unremunerative.

items.statement: UK business had two one-offs totaling GBP 2.4M (EU ETS sale loss and prior period adjustments); Expected EBITDA positive and PBT breakeven from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: UK had fundamentally two big events which were one-offs of adding up to about GBP 2.4 million. One was on the loss on sale of EU ETS. This is likely to come back by October quarter because we go through a cycle. And second, there has also been one-off issue related to some of the prior period adjustments.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 volume growth guided at 8-10% band
items.quote: At the current stage, we are looking at the band of 8-10% for the full FY27.

items.statement: PBDIT margin guidance maintained at 18-20% band
items.quote: We are still garnering around the guidance of 18-20% of our PBDIT margins holds.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth 9% with rural outperforming urban
items.quote: Overall, we are at about a strong 9% volume growth. The growth has been across the months in this entire quarter.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 45.6% in Q1 FY27, down sequentially but up YoY
items.quote: If you look at it from a standalone perspective, the overall gross margin trend has also been fairly strong. There was some pressure on gross margin; we were at about 45.6% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated PBDIT margin 20.6%, up 240 bps YoY
items.quote: PBDIT margins stand at about 20.6%, almost 240 bps higher YoY.

items.statement: Weighted average price increase ~7% in Q1; material inflation ~25%
items.quote: While we took price increases in April, May and June, the overall weighted average price increase was around 7%. The material inflation was still very high to the extent of about 25%.

items.statement: Price increases deferred in industrial segment due to B2B contract cycles
items.quote: If you look at the industrial segment, the price increase actions are a little more deferred and therefore the entire pricing action will not reflect here because, with some of the B2B customers and key accounts, the whole process of price increase takes a bit of time.

items.statement: Premiumization drive contributed ~3% positive mix impact in Q1
items.quote: There is almost about 3% impact, which is coming higher because of the better mix of what we have been able to sell.

items.statement: New products (3-year window) contribute 17% of revenue
items.quote: New products within the portfolio contribute 17% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: White cement plant in Fujairah fully operational at good capacities
items.quote: We have already completed our white cement plant, which is now fully operational and running at very good capacities in Fujairah, UAE.

items.statement: B2B business strong across segments; 100+ key accounts under AP Juggernaut
items.quote: Today, we have more than 100 key accounts that form part of this Juggernaut initiative, where a customer can access the entire portfolio of Asian Paints products and services under one umbrella.

items.statement: Industrial business: Auto OE top-line +13%, PBT +5%, margin 15.7% (-119 bps); General Industrial +21%, PBT margin 6.9%
items.quote: The top line has been about 13% growth of what we have achieved. We have got a strong PBT growth of about 5%. The PBT margins have been a little bit stressed here, about 15.7%, lower by 119 bps.

items.statement: Decor business: 74 Beautiful Home Stores; Kitchen & Weatherseal double-digit growth; White Teak & Bath lower
items.quote: If you look at it, we have about 74 Beautiful Home Stores, which are under one roof, you can get all the decor items, lots of collaborations here. Overall, yes, we face a lot of competition from the unorganized sector.

items.statement: Raw material volatility persists; TiO2 prices rising, monomers declining
items.quote: We have seen that the TiO2 prices were fairly stable, but it has started going up. Okay, and that trend we saw it at the end of June, when it started to happen. Some of the prices of Monomers have started to come down from where they were at earlier levels.

items.statement: Inventory days improved; raw material inventory at higher cost, low-cost finished goods benefit largely absorbed in Q1
items.quote: If you look at from an inventory point of view, in fact, we have done better from an overall number of days of inventory of what we are holding. It's just that raw material inventory, which has come 21 | in, it has come in at possibly a higher cost, which is where you are seeing a blip in the overall inventory

items.statement: Competitive intensity at all-time high across economy, premium, luxury segments
items.quote: The competitive intensity seems to be at an all-time high. I don't think there is any leeway there.

items.statement: Renewed conflict and crude volatility remain top worry for supply chain and input costs
items.quote: I think our top worry is the renewed conflict. The volatility in raw material prices continues, and it puts pressure on supply chain logistics, both from freight availability and price fluctuations across key inputs, given the fact that the paint industry is largely dependent on crude and crude derivatives.

items.statement: Services expansion: Beautiful Homes Painting Service, Total Assure, Smart Assure, MetaCare scaling nationally
items.quote: We have the world's largest home painting service, which we call the 'Beautiful Homes Painting Service'. With on-time completion, colour guidance, supervision, and the mechanization that we bring in, we are delivering a very high level of customer delight, which is measured through an NPS exercise.

items.statement: Regionalization strategy: culture-specific packaging in Rajasthan, Andhra/Telangana; Chittoor wood-finish craft on packs
items.quote: For example, in Rajasthan, we celebrate the core elements of Rajasthani culture, which adorn the packs. Customers can use the QR code to get more information about it and enjoy the area they live in. Similarly, we've done something in Andhra and Telangana this year.

items.statement: Management expects cotton prices to remain firm or increase due to global supply-demand gap of 3-4% over next 1-2 years
items.quote: So these are -- based upon this, it's our view that the cotton prices may not come down in a big way, rather may increase only as the consumption across the world are increasing.

items.statement: Spinning margins expected to moderate from current levels but remain above 9-10% lows, targeting USD0.85-0.90/kg conversion
items.quote: I think going by if the demand continues to be the Chinese demand or the overall demand supply continues to be better, it can be in the range of about USD0.85, USD0.90.

items.statement: Fabric business utilization expected to improve significantly in next 2-3 months as US orders return
items.quote: But we are now -- last 1 month or so, things have started improving, and we are expecting far better business in the next 2, 3 months from the U.S. customers as well.

items.statement: Synthetic fabric capacity utilization target of 70-80% within 6 months from current 15-20%
items.quote: And I'm hoping that our idea is within the next 6 months, we want to reach at 70%, 80% ca pacity utilization, which is 20% as of now

items.statement: INR3,600 crore capex mostly online; INR800-900 crore to spill into FY28; power projects complete in 3 months
items.quote: So most of this capex, I think only about INR800 crores, INR900 crores will go to the next year, remaining will be completed -- it's already completed or will get completed within this year.

items.statement: Open-end spinning project of 55-60 tons/day started construction, completion in ~10 months
items.quote: And we have also started working on the open-end project with a capacity of about 55, 60 tons per day. So the construction just started last week, and I'm hoping, maybe next 10 months' time or so, this capacity will also be available.

items.statement: Biomass boilers at Baddi (started last week) and Madhya Pradesh (starting in ~1 month) to reduce energy costs
items.quote: So we have started our boiler -- biomass boiler in Baddi last week only. And the another one in Madhya Pradesh is expected to start maybe in a month or so.

items.statement: Solar and wind power investments partially operational; full benefits over next 6 months
items.quote: We have also invested heavily into the solar power and the wind power. Those advantages also will -- I mean partially started coming in. I think month after month in next 6 months, more and more advantages would start coming in.

items.statement: Export order book at 90-95 days, domestic at 45-50 days; consistent with 5-year average
items.quote: Normally, in the export market, we are always sold for about 3 months. Domestic by design, I mean, domestic will never be more than 45 days. So if I look at las t 5 years history, this would be the average 90, 95 days in exports, 45 to 50 days in dom estic, and we have sold for those many number of days even today

I think rather than looking at a basic yarn because they are very strong on the garmenting, they are very strong on the fabric finishing. So it could be a possibility as a part of their strategy that rather tha n looking at

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread at USD0.90/kg in Q1; historical range USD0.85-1.00 except last 2-3 years at USD0.60-0.70
items.quote: So cotton yarn spread in this period, I'm not saying for me, normally, it is always calculated on the market prices of cotton and the market prices of yarn. In this pe riod, it was ranging about USD0.90 per kg of yarn

items.statement: 60-70% of yarn price increases passed to fabric customers; 20-30% pending but expected to close with volume growth
items.quote: today, even today, we feel almost whatever price increases happened on the yarn side, about 60%, 70% could be passed on to the consumers. Still 20%, 30% could not be passed on. But with the volume increase, hopefully, those numbers would also be better where the cost will keep coming down and p robably the margins could be restored

items.statement: Global cotton outlook: India sowing -1-2%, Brazil -5%, Australia 3.5M bales (down from last year), US West Texas drought, China reducing acreage
items.quote: Brazil, there has be en a reduction in area by about 5%. So to that extent, there could be a reduction in the crop there. Australia, there has been a major drop in the crop size. The last year figures were much higher. This year, we are expecting to be about 3.5 million bales. And going by the situation of water, maybe the next year could be even much lesser, maybe about 2.5 million bales or so. T

items.quote: Our expectation on the various fronts in terms of raw materials, yarn prices, our view is one, raw material is stabilized in international market in the range of about USD0.78 t o USD0.81 per pound, most of the time, let's say, the average USD0.80 or so

items.statement: Chinese reserve cotton selling at USD1.15-1.16/lb (post-VAT >$1), supporting yarn import demand
items.quote: And the average price of that cotton, which is sold in China as o f now is close to about USD1.15, USD1.16. items.statement: Evaluating duty-free cotton imports for next 2-3 months; Indian cotton unlikely below INR65-66K/candy next season due to 6-7% MSP hike
items.quote: The government has already announced 6%, 7% increase in the MSP. So in case one can get an opportunity to buy imported cotto n within this cost today when the duty is free, we're definitely looking at it and wherever there's a possibility, w

items.quote: If you look at China, there's some spin ning is being added in Xinjiang area, but more than that, they are stopping elsewhere. So the net-net, there's hardly any increase in China. So from a peak of about 116 million, 117 million spenders, they are down to about 84 million, 85 million as of now. If you look at Indonesia, they have reduced, they are not adding. Look at Vietnam, almost saturation is

items.statement: Customer ordering cycles shortening: yarn delivery expected in 20 days, fabric 44-45 days, garment 60-70 days; increasing pressure annually
items.quote: So any customer who is dealing with you wants a delivery of yarn, let's say, in 20 days, delivery of fabrics in about 44 to 45 days, delivery of garment in 60 days, 70 days kind of a situation. So that cycle will continue to screw and whoever is in a position to deliver will be a winner.

items.statement: Brands demand ESG compliance, green power, recycled content, and single-vendor solutions; favors organized large players
items.quote: Now look at a situation where customer wants all these in addition -- and they will not be in a position to have, let's say, 10, 20, 30 vendors. So they want everything to be done by the vendor. So any vendor who has a capacity, who has the muscles to follow the peak of the customers and in a position to deliver all these things. That advantage surely I'm finding and that's the reason the org aniz

items.statement: Synthetic fabric line (1.5M mtr/month) in early stage; two major brand approvals received; targeting basic then value-added/technical textiles
items.quote: The project started somewhere in February, March. And as of now, we have a capacity of 15 lakh meters per month. So our utilization is about 15%, 20% only as of now. But I'm happy to share last 1 month, we got two big approvals from the two big brands and where the production is starting this month itself, within August itself.

items.statement: Recycled cotton yarn feasible up to 30-40% blend on ring frame, higher on open-end; mechanical recycling mature, chemical in experimentation
items.quote: And today, up to 30%, 40% recycled fiber with the virgin fibers on the ring also is possible. We are doing it very regularly. In any case, through the open end, it is possible to do even more than that also.

items.statement: India yarn exports up from ~95-97M to ~110M kg/month (+15M kg), driven primarily by China demand
items.quote: The total export of yarn from India, it used to be about 95 million, 97 million kg or less than 100 million kg, which has increased to about 110 million kg as of now. So an increase -- net-net increase of about 15 million kg, which has primarily come from China only.

items.statement: Indian spinning capacity down 12-13M spindles permanently closed in last 3 years; only 0.5M added last year, 0.7-0.8M this year
items.quote: And the industry estimate was almost 12 million to 13 million spind les got closed permanently, and we still feel that figure is same. There's hardly anything which h as been revived in this period. Going by the overall situation, not many projects have been ann ounced even now on the spinning side. So last year, I think the additional capacity or the new capa city had come only about 0.5 million

items.statement: Fabric margins 3-4% below Q4 FY26 but comparable to Q1 FY26; expected to improve with US order recovery and cost pass-through
items.quote: in terms of absolute numbers on the fabric side, we have -- we are almost comparable to what we did last year in the first quarter, a little lower than the fourth quarter this yea r, but we are hoping that this will start

items.statement: Long-term spinning margin target 13-14% ROCE (USD0.80-0.90/kg conversion) vs 10-11% lows; structural improvement if cotton prices aligned globally
items.quote: My view is, as I mentioned earlier also, we came down to 10%, 11%, which was really a kind of a desperate situation. But my belief 13%, 14% could be the right way of looking at it, which could be -- if we convert it into the margins available per kg of yarn will give us a conversion of about $0.80, $0.85, $0.90.

items.quote: As of now, the cotton growing -- sowing is almost comparable to the previous period with a gap of only 1% or 2% in our estimate, but we are yet to understand and look at what kind of growth or what kind of crop quality would be there as there has been v ery, very different scenarios of rain in the different areas. Generally, whenever we see these kind of variations, there is -- generally, there ar

items.quote: this has been a period where lots of uncertainty because of th e U.S. Iran war happened and the crude prices, we saw the crude prices touching $100, of course, c ome down to about $87, $88 as of now. items.statement: Guided mid-teens rental income growth for FY27 and FY28

items.statement: July consumption trending at over 20% year-on-year growth
items.quote: July, we are already seeing that July will see healthy growth over 20%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 60% for Q1 FY27

items.statement: Strategic alliances preferred over joint ventures; two strategic alliances underway
items.quote: We will have strategic alliances, but not joint ventures. We will have strategic alliances, we have two underway, but joint ventures become very, very tight ropes to walk on because, you know, one customer feels you are favoring the other.

items.statement: Revenue growth 19.22% YoY in Q1 FY27 to Rs 666 crore; total income Rs 681.42 crore (+20.01% YoY)
items.quote: During the quarter, company reported revenue of Rs. 666 crore, which is reflecting growth of 19.22% year-on-year, supported by healthy demand across both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 18.73% YoY to Rs 167.47 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The EBITDA achieved during the same period was Rs. 167.47 crores, registering a growth of 18.73% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: PAT grew to Rs 83.2 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 61.46 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Profit after tax for the quarter was around Rs. 83.2 crores as against Rs. 61.46 crores achieved in Q1 FY26

items.statement: ROE 21.7% and ROCE 22.72% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our ROE and ROCE achieved during the quarter was 21.7% and 22.72% respectively.

items.statement: Healthy demand across fragrance and flavor value chain; structural trends of premiumization and innovation support specialty aroma ingredients
items.quote: Despite adverse global headwinds, demand across the fragrance and flavor value chain remained healthy during the quarter. Global customers continue to focus on supply chain diversification and dependable sourcing, while premiumization and innovation across end-to-end use category continue to support demand for specialty aroma ingredients.

items.statement: Red Sea shipping disruption ongoing but no material impact on freight costs or margins
items.quote: See, Red Sea impact now has been for quite a number of years. And we have been sailing through that impact now. I can only say that. So, with regard to freight expenses on account of the Hormuz Strait, we have not been too much impacted on that. But Red Sea continues to be as it is.

items.statement: Order book rose to INR 1,244 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from INR 1,044 crore on 31 March 2026, with 88% from products.
items.quote: The order book position as on 30th June 2026, is INR 1,244 crore out of which 88% that is INR 1,096 crore is from products. On 31 st March, 2026, the order book position was INR 1,044 crore, out of which 86%, that is INR 899 crore is from products.

items.statement: EBITDA margin fell to 3.6% in Q1 FY27 from 15.4% QoQ and 15.5% YoY due to higher delivery, marketing and admin costs.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is at INR 7.6 crore as against INR 34.6 crore QoQ and INR 33.7 crore YoY. Margins during the quarter is 3.6% as compared to 15.4% QoQ and 15.5% YoY.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 6.4% QoQ and 3.4% YoY to INR 210.4 crore; product revenue was INR 176.6 crore at 83.9% of total.
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue for the quarter is at INR 210.4 crore, a growth of 6.4% QoQ and 3.4% YoY. Product revenue during the quarter is INR 176.6 crore at 83.9% as against 84.1% during previous quarter.

items.statement: Top five clients contributed 28.1% of revenue, down from 29.3% previous quarter; three new logos added in the quarter.
items.quote: Revenue from top five clients contributed 28.1% of revenue in the quarter, as against 29.3% during previous quarter.

items.statement: Some logos left in India but three new logos were added; India revenue dip attributed to a one-time event with a large customer.
items.quote: Some of the logos have left, and in fact, we have added three new logos.

items.statement: Headcount increased to 2,059 from 2,028; attrition rose to 3% from 2% previous quarter.
items.quote: Total headcount as on 30 th June 2026 is 2,059, as compared to 2,028 as on 31 st March, 2026. Attrition during the quarter is 3% as compared to 2% during previous quarter.

items.statement: Gratuity liability reduced by INR 6.99 crore and compensated absence liability by INR 2.83 crore due to remuneration revision; RSUs granted under new scheme.
items.quote: During the quarter, pursuant to a revision in the remuneration structure, the company recognized a reduction in its gratuity liability of INR 6.99 crore and compensated absence liability of INR 2.83 crore.

items.statement: Marketing and sales expenses rose to 10% of revenue from 7.1% QoQ; G&A expenses rose to 10.1% from 7.5% QoQ, driven by salary revisions, RSUs, global marketing spend and higher diesel/power costs.
items.quote: Marketing and Sales expenses for the quarter is 10% of revenue against 7.1% QoQ and 6% YoY. General and administrative expenses for the quarter is 10.1% of revenue against 7.5% QoQ and 8.3% YoY.

items.statement: Cost of delivery increased to 76.2% of revenue from 70% QoQ and 70.1% YoY.
items.quote: Cost of delivery including cost of product development for the quarter is INR 160.4 crore, an increase of 1.9% QoQ and 5.1% YoY. It constitutes 76.2% of revenue against 70% QoQ and 70.1% YoY.

items.statement: Added almost 10 new logos in last 15 months; order book growth driven by new logo wins and AMC renewals at better prices.
items.quote: So, if we talk about in last 15 months, we have added almost 10 new logos.

items.statement: Company does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance; forward-looking statements must be reviewed with risks.
items.quote: As you all are aware, Nucleus Software does not provide any specific revenue earnings guidance. Anything which is said during this call, which may reflect company's outlook for the future, or which may be considered as forward -looking statement, must be re viewed in the conjunction with the risk that the company faces.

items.statement: Company positions as premium player; pricing pressure from competition limits ability to raise prices but maintains price segment.
items.quote: So, yes, pricing always remains a challenge in the wake of competition, but we have chosen to retain and be a premium player, because the kind of product we offer in the market is extremely, I would say, strong and solid product.

items.statement: Implementation cycles vary by customer and can extend up to 5 years; order book includes long-term AMC contracts.
items.quote: Our order book is a composition of certain contracts, which are a little long range, maybe extending up to 5 years also. There are certain orders which get 55 with a shorter period of time also.

items.statement: Client concentration risk highlighted after a top NBFC client moved to a competitor; management views it as a one-off case.
items.quote: Theoretically speaking, it's a risk, but how many clients would want to do that is the question. So theoretically, yes, that that has happened once. Practicality of it is, because the company would also want to do business with any other customers.

items.statement: AI foundation in place; organization-wide upskilling underway; AI productivity benefits not yet measurable but expected in future.
items.quote: Our enterprise AI foundation is now in place. Alongside this, we are also undertaking an organization-wide learning and upscaling initiative to equip our associates with the capabilities that are required in adopting this AI framework.

items.statement: Released FinnAxia 9.0 with embedded AI capabilities across lending lifecycle.
items.quote: Recently, we launched our similar new GA, the full-blown release 9.0, which among other things also brings embedded AI capabilities across the lending life cycle.

items.statement: Bhavit Godiwala joined as Chief Customer Success Officer with nearly three decades of banking technology experience.
items.quote: I wish to welcome Mr. Bhavit Godiwala as Chief Customer Success Officer. He brings nearly three decades of experience across banking technology and digital transformation, core banking, transaction banking domains, and he will be looking after leading the initiative of customer success organization.

items.statement: India revenue share 56%, Middle East 12%, South Asia 11%, Europe 5%; forex loss of INR 1.1 crore in quarter.
items.quote: India region constitutes 56% of revenue, followed by 12% from Middle East, 11% from South Asia, 5% from Europe and rest others.

items.statement: Management targeting high-margin deals and margin control initiatives; expects employee cost percentage to decline as revenue grows.
items.quote: So, yes, we are working on that. I feel you will see the effect of those efforts in subsequent quarters, while we can't quantify it. But yes, on ground, we are looking at this. In fact, we are focusing on high margin deals as well, as we chart our course of growth in other geographies than India.

items.statement: Middle East and Southeast Asia identified as big bets; US market footing established with auto finance segment.
items.quote: I feel Middle East and Southeast Asia are our big bet. Definitely, we have got our footing in U.S. markets also, and we see growing in these markets little differentially than other markets.

items.statement: Marketing and G&A spend calibrated to strategic priorities; no large one-off costs in the quarter; spend expected to continue.
items.quote: we will keep looking for investing in those events or in those markets, which are strategic priorities to us, and which can yield results in the coming future. That calibration will go up.

items.statement: US opportunity exists with GM Financial's North America division; one US auto finance order won last year to build upon.
items.quote: In two parts. One is, that is the way the customer business is structured. They have a North America division, and they have rest of the world. Our contract has been with outside North America. And yes, future, there is a possibility. I can't rule that out.

items.statement: High double-digit volume growth targeted for FY27 and coming years
items.quote: we are confident of high double-digit volume growth for next coming years, including FY27

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 7-8% for next 12-15 months
items.quote: we believe that 7% to 8% EBITDA margin for the next 12 to 15-months is what we are going to achieve

items.statement: Long-term target of four large plants each generating Rs.800-1,000 crore revenue with 10%+ EBITDA by FY31
items.quote: our long-term target by FY31 is to have four large plants across India, each plant contributing Rs.800 crores to Rs.1,000 crore of revenue with 10% plus EBITDA margin

items.statement: New products portfolio targeting Rs.1,000 crore revenue in next four years
items.quote: this portfolio put together and maybe some new additions going forward, that portfolio in the next four years should be generating Rs.1,000 crores revenue

items.statement: FY27 and FY28 capex of ~Rs.100 crore each year funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: in both the years, the total CAPEX will be near about Rs.200 crores divided by like Rs.100 crores in each year. This will be funded from operating cash flow

items.statement: Next leg of capex requires Rs.600-700 crore over five years, 70-80% from internal cash flows
items.quote: the next leg of CAPEX requires Rs.600-700 crores put together in five years, right? So, I think 70%-80% will be met from our internal cash flows

items.statement: South India plant land acquisition targeted in FY27, construction from Q2 FY28
items.quote: probably in FY27, this financial year, we will finish the land acquisition, and then from next year, second quarter onwards, we will start putting up the plant

items.statement: Window profiles expected to contribute 7-8% of revenue in FY27, scaling to 10% at full capacity
items.quote: For Window profile, we expect that business to contribute 7% to 8% to our revenue, okay, in FY27 and gradually, it will keep on improving and maybe it will settle at around 10%

items.statement: Q1 FY27 normalized consolidated EBITDA margin 7% (Apollo standalone 8%, Kisan standalone 6%)
items.quote: the normalized business margins at EBITDA level were like 7% for the consolidated business, out of which 8% was for Apollo standalone and 6% was for Kisan standalone

items.statement: New business costs (Varanasi + Window profiles) impacted Apollo standalone margin by ~0.5% in Q1
items.quote: At Apollo standalone level, because of Varanasi and Window profile, 0.5% will be the additional cost, right, due to the new businesses

items.statement: Majority of Q1 EBITDA impact from inventory write-downs due to PVC price crash
items.quote: When I say our business EBITDA margin was 7% in consol levels, EBITDA which came, majority was inventory losses

items.statement: Q1 volume flat YoY; April worst due to 30% PVC price drop, recovery from May; Q2 YoY double-digit growth expected
items.quote: It will be double-digit growth on YoY basis in Q2

items.statement: Construction demand (60% of sales) driving recovery; agri slow due to monsoon; July decent, restocking expected if price stability sustains 10-15 days
items.quote: if this stability sustains for say the next 10-15 days, then definitely there will be restocking, which would start and this will give boost to the overall industry sales for the second quarter

items.statement: Inventory at 80 days, debtor days stable at 30, targeting net working capital days of 30 (from 45) by FY28
items.quote: we will have a net working capital day target of 30, which right now is 45, but we are confident that there is scope of release of working capital by 10-to-15 days eventually, if not this year, but definitely by next year

items.quote: idea is to bring debtor days to maybe 25-days, maybe by FY27-end or maybe in first half of FY28, but there is a clear visibility

items.statement: Company nearly net cash; past Rs.500-600 crore capex funded from internal cash flows and promoter/foreign fund raise
items.quote: Right now, the company is almost net cash. Okay? I mean, all this CAPEX of Rs.500-600 crores in the last two-three years was done from internal cash flow and fundraise from the promoters and a foreign fund

items.statement: Kisan merger scheme filed; ~1% cost synergies expected at company level post-merger
items.quote: once everything becomes one, so there could be like a 1% cost synergies, which could come at the overall company level

items.statement: CPVC growing YoY in Q1 despite flat consolidated volumes; Lubrizol co-branding showing results
items.quote: CPVC has grown in Quarter 1 on a YoY basis despite the flattish growth for the company at a consolidated level. So, that tie-up is showing results already

items.statement: Water tanks growing double-digit; fittings single-digit growth; government infra (O-PVC/HDPE) near zero drag
items.quote: Water tank is growing in double-digit. Government infrastructure business, whether it is O-PVC or HDPE, that is like almost zero, that is one of the major drags for the overall volume to remain flat

items.statement: Targeting 25% ROC on Rs.5,000 crore revenue with Rs.1,500 crore gross block and 25-30 days working capital by FY31
items.quote: on Rs.5,000 crores revenue, even if we make 10% to 12% EBITDA margin, which is like Rs.500 crores to Rs.600 crores broad range, so that gives like 25% ROC

items.quote: if we see the global scenario, the availability is not a problem. In 10-days plus/minus there, you get the material as per the schedule. That is only the reason. And because of the extensive rain in India, that disruption is there

items.statement: Volatility causing disruption for smaller players; Apollo maintained flat volumes suggesting market share gains

items.quote: Too early for them to start stocking up, to be fair on their side, because the PVC prices have been so volatile that any call taken by them has not worked, right? So, they are being very, very cautious

items.quote: We would like to keep the guidance for financial year 2026-27 unchanged for now and we will reassess the same only after the quarter 2 results. Credit growth, 12% deposit growth, 10%, CASA 45% NIM around 3.5%, ROA maintaining around 2026 levels, ROE around 16%, GNPA below 2.25%.

items.statement: Expects actual credit growth 18-20% in FY27, with J&K at 12-13% and Rest of India at ~25%
items.quote: For this financial year, overall credit growth, I expect, although the guidance given is around 12%, but the actual credit growth will not be less than, say, 18% to 20%, I expect. With the growth coming from J&K will be somewhere around 12% to 13% and the growth coming from rest of India will be somewhere around 25%.

items.quote: In fact, I expect almost 55% to 60% growth of advances coming this year from retail itself. items.quote: It is diversified. It is diversified. It is totally diversified.

items.quote: We now have a totally a GM -headed vertical exclusively looking for improvement in CASA ratio. items.quote: See, Jammu and Kashmir, we tend to increase around 15 to 20 branches every year. But we intend to increase 50 to 70 branches in rest of India in the next 2 years.

items.quote: And I'm talking about the retail growth in Jammu and Kashmir only at the moment. With increased focus and more staff put into the Rest of India branches, we have posted 100 -odd people, and we are recruiting around 300 people in rest of India to augment our Rest of India business.

items.quote: Despite an operating environment marked by heightened macroeconomic uncertainty, our gross slippages were below 0.5% for the quarter and SMA numbers continue to moderate, which reflects the resilience of our portfolio, the quality of lending as well as the disciplined underwriting standards. items.quote: There were floods and flash floods keep on happening in this -- I mean, in any hilly terrain, but the impact has not been that much. items.statement: No stress seen in housing loan portfolio; low exposure to IT sector employees
items.quote: So we have -- see, our housing loan segment is also well diversified with the contribution from rest of India as well as Jammu and Kashmir. items.statement: INR1,250 crore capital raise approved; considering revising quantum upwards; government may dilute stake
items.quote: Capital raise, INR1,250 crores is already done that is approved and that is going to come, but we are thinking in terms of revising the quantum. I'm not in a position to divulge more because we are still waiting for the approvals

items.statement: Capital Adequacy Ratio 16.67%, CET1 13.91% as of 30 Jun 2026
items.quote: The Bank continues to build upon its capital buffers, recording a Capital Adequacy Ratio of 16.67% as on 30th June 2026, with CET1 at 13.91%.

items.quote: Risk-wise, shock-wise, I'm not witnessing anything adverse in the bank at the moment. items.quote: Given the investments we have made across markets, partnerships and portfolio expansion over the last few years, we continue to expect the Ex -US business to grow faster than the compan y average over the foreseeable future

items.statement: Expect US growth trajectory to improve over the year with H2 stronger supported by new approvals and launches
items.quote: As we indicated during the Q4 call, we believe the growth trajectory in the US should improve over the course of the year, with H2 expected to be stronger, supported by new approvals, launches and portfolio optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Underlying demand environment across key Ex-US markets remains healthy

items.quote: Ex-US revenue grew 17% year-on-year to ₹5,875 million, with growth recorded across multiple geographies.

items.quote: So as far as we are concerned, from now until 31st of March, we should be able to do about 10 launches. That's what we are working on.

items.quote: The survival of that and the operations of that comes under huge question next year, when interest then becomes another important factor for them to consider as far as their operations are concerned.

items.statement: Supreme Court stayed alteration to ethanol allocation framework, status quo ordered

items.statement: Government continues restriction on sugar exports to maintain domestic availability
