items.quote: On the screen network front, our advertising footprint now stands at 3,891 screens, comprising 2,565 multiplex screens and 1,326 single screens.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 was ₹1,118 million vs ₹1,090 million in Q1 FY26 and ₹1,342 million in Q4 FY26; EBITDA was ₹189 million vs ₹193 million in Q1 FY26 and ₹182 million in Q4 FY26; PAT was ₹56 million vs ₹65 million in Q1 FY26 an
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 stood at ₹1,118 million, against ₹1,090 million in Q1 FY26 and ₹1,342 million in Q4 FY26. EBITDA for the quarter was ₹189 million, as against ₹193 million in Q1 FY26 and ₹ 182 million in Q4 FY26. PAT stood at ₹56 million, compared with ₹65 million in Q1 FY26 and ₹45 million in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Receivables are well within historical trends in terms of debtor ageing; anything over one year old is fully provided for.
items.quote: Even as we speak, despite a much stronger performance in the advertisement business, we remain well within historical trends in terms of debtor ageing.

items.statement: Advertisement revenues grew 33% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 driven by blockbuster performance of Dhurandhar: The Revenge and select Hindi/regional titles improving advertiser participation.
items.quote: The continuing blockbuster performance of “Dhurandhar: The Revenge” along with performance of select Hindi and regional titles supported improved advertiser participation, contributing to a 33% year -on-year growth in our advertisement revenues.

items.statement: Advertising revenue mix historically 30-40% from annual advertisers and balance from tactical spending around major film releases; Dhurandhar was an outlier with unprecedented tactical spending.
items.quote: Over the years, we have seen that around 30 –40% of our advertising revenue comes from annual deals or annual advertisers, while the balance is contributed by tactical advertisers or short -term, seasonal spending around specific films or seasons.

items.statement: Sale of products declined year-on-year predominantly due to lower international product sales (down ~₹7 crores) due to war situation delaying imports into Dubai; Indian product sales increased marginally.
items.quote: The decline that you see in the current quarter is predominantly on account of lower international product sales. In India, product sales have actually increased marginally. However, internationally, there has been a significant decline of around Rs 7 crores.

items.statement: Pending international product orders remain in hand and are awaiting execution; expected to be executed in Q2 or at latest by Q3.
items.quote: The comforting factor is that these sales have not been lost. The orders continue to remain in hand and are only awaiting execution. We expect these pending orders to be executed in Q2, or at the latest by Q3.

items.statement: Consolidated cash at end of Q1 FY27 was ₹1,462 million and net cash was ₹624 million after considering outstanding debt.
items.quote: The consolidated cash at the end of the quarter was ₹ 1,462 million, and the net cash was ₹ 624 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: Off-screen advertising (lobby digital billboards) is a potential opportunity but requires new arrangements with theatres and infrastructure investment; currently focused on maximizing on-screen advertising inventory.
items.quote: Currently, however, that is an opportunity we are yet to explore because our arrangements with theatres are largely focused on on-screen advertising. The relationship would need to be expanded to include the rights to advertise in the lobby areas.

items.statement: International product sales impacted by war situation in region causing import delays into Dubai; sales not lost but deferred to Q2/Q3.
items.quote: This reduction is entirely attributable to the war situation in the region, because of which imports into Dubai could not be completed on time. As a result, the corresponding sales could not be recognized.

items.statement: Management maintains Rs 1,000 crore revenue target for FY28 despite current gap
items.quote: we would not like to revise the guidance as of right now. we'd like to because if we lower it we are not even then striving for it. So, we would still like to strive for it and hoping that we are still able to make it happen through some measures.

items.statement: Management targets 10-12% top-line growth for FY27 and Rs 600 crore revenue
items.quote: we are hopeful that we will be able to still go there. Yes, we everyday keep our fingers crossed that at least domestic and India numbers we are much more confident and the export numbers, yes, depends on our situation, but we are hoping for the best. But still, we will maintain that kind of top line guidance.

items.statement: Sanand plant yearly revenue target Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1
items.quote: So, for the Sanand unit, we have the yearly target of Rs. 40 CRs, which is the minimum we want to do. And looking at the performance which we could achieve in the 1st Quarter, I think we are on track. So, that is possible.

items.statement: Sanand plant expanded from two to three operating lines; helmet, foam cap, nasal cap production underway
items.quote: And now with two lines, we have made it into three lines which are operating already. And our helmet production and foam cap production and nasal cap production is already underway. And we are looking to further increase capacity there.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.51%, up 317 bps QoQ; PAT margin 6.03%, up 174 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 12.51%, representing an expansion of 317 basis points quarter-on-quarter. This improvement was primarily driven by better price realization, lower raw material cost and improved operational risk efficiency.

items.statement: Raw material costs remain elevated vs pre-war levels; some respite recently but volatile; gradual cost pass-through with lag due to long-term contracts
items.quote: But then there are other factors into play because we have seen all over transport costs have increased, energy costs have increased. So, overall, there has been an increment in raw material costs. Obviously, with crude prices correcting a little bit, there's been some respite. But, yes, overall, when we started the calendar year, as compared to that, it's definitely on a higher level.

items.statement: No under-recovery on raw material cost in Q1; cost pass-through exercise started at quarter beginning; no forex gain as exposures are hedged
items.quote: So, whatever cost increase was there, we have been able to pass on this to the customer, and we took this exercise at the beginning of the quarter itself. Right? So, there is no under recovery there.

items.statement: Domestic revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ, highest ever Q1 domestic revenue; international revenue Rs 46 crore
items.quote: Further, during the quarter, domestic revenue stood at Rs. 64 crores, registering a growth of 10% quarter-on-quarter and achieving the highest ever 1st Quarter domestic revenue for the company.

items.statement: Export demand weak in West due to economic situation and logistics; Europe recovering, more inquiries flowing; targeting double-digit growth missed in Q1
items.quote: Both, I would say. There has been a bleak demand also from the West because of their own crisis and their own economic situation. It's not a good situation. And other than that, because of logistics also we have lost because there's some port congestion and we are unable to ship out goods even when they are ready and sitting in our warehouse for a long time.

items.statement: Value-added products now 60-70% of sales; focus on product development, market research, supply chain for value-added, launching new products yearly
items.quote: So, at this point, I think almost 60% or 70% of what we would be selling is more value added products than the regular products, and the idea is to get into more product development, do more market research, learn from the developed countries, and quickly adapt it, have the supply chain set for more value added products, and keep on launching newer products every year.

items.statement: Launched EN812 Certified Bump Caps and European/American certified Flame Retardant workwear at Sanand plant
items.quote: we expanded our safety solution portfolio with the launch of a new mold for EN812 Certified Bump Caps and commenced its manufacturing at our Sanand plant, further strengthening our manufacturing capabilities. We also introduced European and American certified Flame Retardant workwear, enhancing our product offering and expanding opportunities in developed international markets.

items.statement: SMILE Reseller program expanded distribution to over 1,000 resellers across India
items.quote: Another key highlight during the quarter was the overwhelming response to our “SMILE” Reseller program, which has helped expand our distribution network to over 1,000 resellers across India, significantly improving our market reach and customer accessibility.

items.statement: Export sales roughly 60-70% planned/contract, 30% spot; commoditized items face L1 pricing each order
items.quote: Roughly, I would say 60% or 70% is something which are planned and the rest is something that are based on spot sales. But in each spot sales, also, it's not like for each product we have to always negotiate on the price and the best L1 wins. Some of them are planned and the prices don't change. It's just that their buying cycle is such. In some commoditized items, definitely L1 prices are conside

items.statement: Won new customers in UK, South Europe (Portugal, Spain, Turkey, Italy), Germany, Russia; targeting France, Benelux, Nordics, East Europe
items.quote: So, yes, definitely in UK, existing customers have increased their purchasing from us. They are adding new product categories. We have been able to win one new customer in UK as well. In South of Europe, Portugal, Spain, even Turkey, Italy, we have been able to get some new customers. Germany has been responding well to us. Now, target is to focus more on France, Benelux markets, and even the Nord

items.statement: No acquisition plans in Europe due to cannibalization risk; inorganic growth focus on developing markets
items.quote: Not as of right now, because it's traditionally been a market where our customers are present, and we run the risk of cannibalizing our market if we go and acquire some company and start our own distribution there. So, we have been a little skeptical of this idea, and plus our thinking is that the developing markets for our product categories. So, I think if we have to do some of the inorganic gro

items.statement: India-Europe FTA and India-UK FTA driving increased inquiries and interest from global buyers diversifying beyond China
items.quote: Yes, definitely, there is movement and especially with the news of India-Europe Free Trade Agreement and with also India-UK Free Trade now effective, there is definitely more interest and inquiries floating through us, maybe from China or any other countries. Yes, that is something which is happening continuously.

items.statement: Europe market improving, more orders and inquiries; FTA effectiveness expected next year; targeting recovery to beat last year's Rs 170 crore
items.quote: I think it's getting better. It was in a pretty bad shape earlier. I think that part is probably gone and we are getting better. There are more orders which are flowing and there's more positivity around the India-EU trade deal. So, and a lot of inquiries flowing. But the effectiveness of the trade deal only, I think, comes next year. So, we are definitely hopeful that as compared to last year, we

items.statement: US market uncertain due to changing tariff news; marketing efforts ongoing but importers skeptical; targeting to beat last year's number
items.quote: With the U.S. market, again, very volatile. Things keep changing. the different news which keeps coming. We are a little uncertain. Still don't know how to look into that market. But, yes, we are keeping our marketing efforts on and we are trying to get new customers or even the existing customers increase our market share. So, hoping that we can beat the last year's number from the North American

items.statement: Middle East supply resumed this month after container delays; Latin America customers holding stock but order flow present
items.quote: We are supplying. We are supplying. In the Middle East, we couldn't supply anything. There were containers at the sea which were not getting delivered. But now, again, this month or so, we have supplied some.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing to remain at same level due to ongoing machinery capex; term loans taken and refinanced for Sanand capex and incentives
items.quote: So, in case of working capital, it should be same, because we are still continuing to do some investment, not now in building or land, but into increasing our capacity, so in machinery. So, that CAPEX plan is already there. So, working capital borrowing should be at the same level. But in case of, during the year, we have borrowed some term loans, and again refinance against our CAPEX in Sanand, a

items.statement: Headgear production started at Sanand plant; exporting regularly to Europe; contributing to revenue
items.quote: We have already started doing it in our Sanand plant and we have already started seeing increased revenue from it whereas exporting it now regularly to the European market as well. And it's definitely helping us have a good presence in a new product category and helping us with the revenue as well.

items.statement: Port congestion caused raw material procurement and customer delivery delays; teams minimized disruption
items.quote: Congestions at major seaports resulted in delays in the procurement of certain critical raw materials as well as the customer deliveries, impacting operational timelines. Nevertheless, our teams responded effectively to minimize disruption and ensure continuity of operations.

items.statement: Domestic market evolving with labor law tailwinds, manufacturing growth, safety awareness, compliance costs; brand recall improving entry speed
items.quote: Yes, I think the Indian market overall is evolving year on year. Labor law definitely is one of the tailwinds. But in general, the more manufacturing is coming into the country, the more export-oriented the country is becoming. And even foreign companies are setting up shops here. And just the awareness about safety is increasing. The cost of life is increasing. And just the fact that non-complian

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Full-year FY27 double-digit revenue growth and improved margins expected
items.quote: Notwithstanding these quarterly variations, the current business momentum keeps us on track to deliver double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for the full year.

items.statement: Fundamental demand drivers for fragrance and taste remain intact and growing
items.quote: At this time, the fundamental demand drivers of our industry in the consumers' preferences of fragrance and taste across personal care, home care and food categories have remained intact and continued to grow.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 13.4% in Q1 FY27 from 12.6% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA rose 21% to Rs. 89 crore with EBITDA margin improving to 13.4% from 12.6% in the corresponding quarter last year, aided by operating leverage on the higher revenue base.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected around Q1 levels with potential 1% variation
items.quote: If that double-digit growth is sustained and remains there, we should be in similar margin EBITDA level at least in terms of absolute numbers. Probably percentages can vary 1% here and there based on the pricing and the sales momentum.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex of Rs. 25 crore in Europe completed; Rs. 25 crore planned for Vanvate in Q2; remaining Rs. 50 crore for India plants may be spent in Q4 or deferred to Q1 FY28
items.quote: About Rs. 25 crore was done in Europe in the quarter 1. European capex is now completed. The plant is operational since May. Our quarter 2 capex will continue on the Vanvate and Vashivali India Fragrance projects. We expect bulk of this investment capex to happen in basically before end of quarter 2 and the Vanvate factory to be operational in quarter 3. And then we have an opportunity based on ho

items.statement: Vanvate factory commissioning targeted for Q3 FY27
items.quote: When we talk about the factory, we are looking at commissioning Vanvate in the third quarter.

items.statement: Flavours revenue of Rs. 112 crore in Q1 includes ~Rs. 15 crore preponement; normalized run-rate ~Rs. 95-96 crore per quarter
items.quote: We did Rs. 112 crore revenue for Flavours this quarter and ballpark Rs. 95 crore would be on a normal basis. We expect that 1-odd month or 2 or 3 weeks of preponement of orders by clients given that the lead times and shipping times were not normal.

items.statement: ~95% of clients accepted price corrections to pass through raw material cost inflation
items.quote: We have corrected the pricing to our customers based on the cost inflation that we have ourselves received as a result of the geopolitical effect. We have passed it on. I think almost 95% plus of the clients, we were able to get reasonable price corrections.

items.statement: Strategic inventory buildup provides 6 months visibility on raw material costs; prices fixed via stock or contracts
items.quote: So, we have prepared in a manner that we have 6 months visibility on the inventory and our contracts or pricing to the client. So, we have increased the inventory to ensure that for the next 4 to 5 months, I mean, 6 months from July, effectively, we do not have any additional cost pressure on the raw material.

items.statement: Revenue mix skewed toward Flavours (above budget) and away from Ingredients (below budget) in Q1
items.quote: While the overall revenue of the quarter is in line with the budget, the internal dynamics of the product mix is skewed more towards flavours being higher than the budget and the ingredient business being lower than the budget.

items.statement: Exited low-margin domestic fragrance business in Q4 FY26; rationalized sales to improve pricing discipline
items.quote: We have taken conscious decision, as we pointed out in quarter 4 to exit from some low-margin businesses, and we have kind of held back on our sales to clients and only given what they actually regularly consume and not taken any additional advanced orders as the pricing movement has been happening in the quarter.

items.statement: FX contributed ~5% to revenue growth in Q1; like-for-like growth was 9%
items.quote: I think 9% is the like-for-like growth and net-net 5% is our additional FX sales due to exchange rate.

items.statement: Net debt increased Rs. 65 crore to Rs. 852 crore due to strategic inventory buildup and capex
items.quote: On the balance sheet, net debt increased by Rs. 65 crore during the quarter to Rs. 852 crore as of June 2026. This reflects 2 conscious decisions: strategic inventory buildup to ensure supply security for our customers in uncertain geopolitical environment and continued capital deployment towards capacity expansion and growth initiatives.

items.statement: Debt expected to remain at June level in Q2, then reduce ~Rs. 25 crore per quarter from Q3 onward
items.quote: As Jagdish mentioned, the debt level will remain high for the next quarter at the similar levels as we continue our capex this quarter and next quarter, I think from the third quarter, it will start to reduce. And our expectation is that every quarter, we will continue to reduce by approximately Rs. 25 crore quarter-on-quarter thereafter.

items.statement: Insurance claim of ~Rs. 30 crore recognized in Q1; remaining Rs. 50-60 crore expected to be settled in FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we recognized exceptional income of approximately Rs. 30 crore towards the insurance claim relating to the fire incident. The claim process is progressing well, and we expect full settlement within the current financial year.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~31.5-32% in Q1; target to bring below 30% for full year
items.quote: So even today, when we look at June quarter, we are around 31.5% to 32% kind of Q1FY2027EarningsConferenceCall ETR. Our target is that should be less than 30%. That is what we are working on that

items.statement: Depreciation run-rate expected to rise to Rs. 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate capitalization
items.quote: Right now, we are at around Rs. 35 crore per quarter. And once we do Vanvate capitalizations we will move into that, we are expecting somewhere Rs. 38 crore, Rs. 39 crore per quarter kind of a run rate.

items.statement: Target ROCE >15% in medium term, 20% long term; Europe ROCE target 17-18%
items.quote: So, I think we should have excess of 15% ROCE as our target. Our long-term target is 20%. But at the moment, we will see 3 to 5 years of slow traction towards the 15%. And then as the sales ramp up in the new initiative areas post breakeven and EBITDA plus and then we will reach that 20% ROCE level.

items.statement: Key constraint to doubling earnings in 5 years is major global macro disruptions affecting product launch pipeline
items.quote: I think main sort of concern for us is major disruptions on the global macro. Our business and nature of business is quite annual, repeat annuity basis. So, once we have a business, it grows, it sustains. The moment we have a macro like we had the pandemic or something like this, then it is affecting not only the year in which the pandemic happens, but also the pipeline for product launches in the

items.statement: Germany, USA, UK development centers expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in years 3, 4, 5 respectively
items.quote: So, Germany, which has come first, we should look at somewhere between this year and next year to have a breakeven position that we have generated enough business that covers the cost, a year later for U.S.A. and a year later for UK.

items.statement: Europe and US fragrance markets represent $10B opportunity (4-5x India market); targeting $100M addressable in near term
items.quote: So, if we look at the fragrance business market size in, let us say, just U.K. and U.S.A., which are our latest new initiatives, this market is roughly 20% to 21% of the global demand vis-a-vis India, which is 5%. So, we are talking about a market size, which is 4 to 5x bigger than the India fragrance market. It is a different magnitude of size and scale of business. So, we are putting our first,

items.statement: Backward integration and China supply chain exit completed for Global Ingredients business
items.quote: We have taken steps, as we mentioned a few years ago on backward integration and complete away from China supply chain. So those are in place.

items.statement: No impact on manufacturing or supply chain from Gujarat floods
items.quote: So far, we had no impact.

items.statement: Specialized staffing EBITDA margin target 8-9% stable state in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: Directionally, we think about 8% to 9% is the stable EBITDA margin in our specialized staffing business, which would take us another maybe 4 to 5 quarters to get there.

items.statement: EdTech EBITDA margin potential 8-10% for full year FY27
items.quote: EdTech business can go to a steady EBITDA margin of anywhere between 8% to 10%. So that's the potential.

items.statement: RegTech EBITDA margin expected ~8% for full year FY27
items.quote: RegTech also in the similar range, about 8% of EBITDA margin is what we are expecting on a full year basis.

items.statement: General staffing demand harder to forecast; clients giving only quarterly visibility due to macro variability
items.quote: it's become harder to forecast, but that's more of a demand side situation because like I had called out, there was a point in time where you could get guidance from clients with respect to the demand at their end for a few quarters at a time. But now it's maybe just a quarter at a time because that's the degree of variability that we are dealing with

items.statement: GCCs account for 45% of specialized staffing associate base and 67% of net revenue; no slowdown seen
items.quote: GCCs account for 45% of our associate base while contributing 67% of our net revenue. During quarter 1, we've hired over 700 associates for GCC customers.

items.statement: IT services hiring concentrated on AI/ML, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity, SAP; conventional tech hiring lower
items.quote: Demand was led by AI/ML, cloud and DevOps, cybersecurity and SAP requirements, while core technology skills such as application development and QA remained stable.

items.statement: Business EBITDA (ex-corporate) grew 18% YoY led by specialized staffing and HR services
items.quote: The key fallout is that the business EBITDA without corporate or unallocated costs grew 18% year-on-year, mainly led by specialized staffing and HR services.

items.statement: General staffing PAPM INR680 for Q1 FY27
items.quote: For the quarter it's INR680 in general staffing.

items.statement: General staffing open positions 17,500 with healthy pipeline
items.quote: we have 17,500 open positions and a healthy pipeline

items.statement: Specialized staffing net addition 130 associates (13% YoY growth) to 7,630 total
items.quote: We closed the quarter with 7,630 associates a net addition of 130 over the previous quarter, including 30 from our global operations, representing 13% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Degree Apprenticeship net addition ~2,100 apprentices (excl. planned exit of 5,500) and 18 new logos
items.quote: excluding the planned exit of 5,500 headcount, which we called out in Q4 commentary, we had a net addition of approximately 2,100 apprentices and added 18 new client logos in DA

items.statement: Investing in sales, hiring engines, data lake, and tech-enabled hiring in Q1-Q2 FY27 for future growth
items.quote: our priority this year is that between Q1 and Q2, we make some investments, which will help us to accelerate our growth rates as well as make our entry into some of these adjacencies productization of high-margin verticals

items.statement: General staffing at ~2.91 lakh associates, sequential net addition of 4,000
items.quote: our general staffing business closed the quarter at approximately 2.91 lakh associates, which is a sequential net addition of 4,000 associates

items.statement: Over 65% of new general staffing logos under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing
items.quote: over 65% of the new logos this quarter came in under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing

items.statement: Labor code wage redefinition raises statutory costs but passed through; clients absorbing cost to preserve associate take-home
items.quote: The wage redefinition raises statutory employer costs, which our contracts pass through, and we do not expect a P&L impact on the associate book.

items.statement: Labor codes structurally favor large organized players over unorganized contractors
items.quote: a single central license, uniform wage definitions, mandatory formal employment letter, all of these raise the compliance bar in a way that will structurally favor large organized players like us over

items.statement: DSO held at 6 days, funding exposure at 16%, both flat sequentially; TDS receivable ~INR145 cr
items.quote: DSO and staffing is held at 6 days and funding exposure at 16%. Both are flat sequentially. TDS receivable outstanding is approximately INR145 crores

items.statement: Completed INR238 cr buyback (8.8% of pre-buyback paid-up capital) funded from internal accruals
items.quote: we have completed the whole buyback process. The Board approved it in May 2026, aggregating INR238 crores, representing 8.8% of pre-buyback paid up capital

items.statement: Net free cash ~INR350 cr after buyback, aided by INR38 cr tax refund; OCF/EBITDA conversion 100%
items.quote: we funded the buyback entirely from internal accruals and still closed the quarter with about net free cash of INR350 crores, which is also aided by a tax refund of INR38 crores during the quarter. Operating cash flow in terms of OCF to EBITDA conversion was 100% for the quarter

items.statement: Exercising put option to divest 30% stake in Crystal HR with full recovery of original investment
items.quote: The Board has directed us to exercise our put option in Crystal HR. Accordingly, we are divesting our 30% stake in Crystal HR with a full recovery of our original investment cost.

items.statement: Retail inflation at 4.38%, weak monsoon, trade term uncertainty create near-term headwinds
items.quote: retail inflation has risen to 4.38%. The monsoon has been among the weakest in a decade so far and uncertainty in trade terms persist

items.statement: New leadership in technology team and Managing Director increased unallocated corporate costs
items.quote: the unallocated is mainly the increase in leadership cost at corporate level. So one is we got the new leadership in our technology team as well as the new Managing Director

items.statement: Management expects patented portfolio to be 60-70% of branded sales for the current year and future years.
items.quote: So, we believe in current year or in future, it should be anywhere higher of 60%. Now, depending upon the season, the crop, it could vary. So, we believe it would be anywhere between 60 to 70% where our patent portfolio should remain out of our total branded sales.

items.statement: Management targets 10-15% annual revenue CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
items.quote: So, we have mostly bottomed last year in March '26 and from here on, we should be in the sense, the plan is to easily be achieve a growth of 10%-15% each year.

items.statement: Management considers 13-14% EBITDA margin sustainable under normal circumstances.
items.quote: So, what you mentioned is right, EBITDA levels of, we have achieved earlier as well at much higher of 15% as well. So, 13%-14% is a pretty reasonable ask to achieve for us under normal circumstances.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 37% in Q1 FY27 from 29% in Q1 FY26 driven by product mix and price increases.
items.quote: Gross profit increased by 32% year-on-year to Rs.146 crores compared with Rs.111 crores in the corresponding quarter last year. Consequently, gross margins improved to 37% from 29%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 20% in Q1 FY27 from 12% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved significantly to 20% compared with 12% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Patented products carry gross margins of 40%+ while generics range 15-30%.
items.quote: So, broad range is for most of the patented products, we are like +40% margin. And for generics, it's in the range of say, gross margins in the range of 15% to 25%-30%.

items.statement: Patented portfolio contribution to branded sales rose to 65% in Q1 FY27 from 45% a year ago.
items.quote: During the quarter, we reduced the number of generic products, increasing the contribution of our patented portfolio to 65% from 45%.

items.statement: Three new patented products launched, taking total patented products to 12.
items.quote: And secondly, we also launched a new patent portfolio of three products. So, in addition to our previous nine products, we launched further three new products. So, as of today, we have around 12 patent products.

items.statement: Delayed monsoon subdued Q1 demand for seed treatment, herbicides and insecticides in key crops.
items.quote: Overall, the impact has been on seed treatment. Primarily, the demand has remained subdued due to the delayed planting, while lower crop establishment reduced the requirement for the first round of herbicide and insecticide applications primarily in soybeans, cotton, vegetables, chilies and groundnuts.

items.statement: Management expects demand for herbicides, insecticides, fungicides and PGRs to improve in following quarters as monsoon picks up.
items.quote: Monsoon activity has improved across most agricultural regions. As crops move into vegetative and reproductive cycles, we expect demand for herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and PGRs. to improve during the following quarters.

items.statement: Selective price increases implemented in April and May; able to pass on significant portion of raw material cost inflation.
items.quote: In first week of April, even before the season started, we had increased our prices. And then for further few of the products, we did a second round of increase in first week of May. So, for most of the price increase, we have been able to pass on.

items.statement: Inventory reduced 6% year-on-year to Rs 764 crore as of June 30; sales return provision of Rs 60 crore (20% of sales) created in Q1.
items.quote: Inventories stood at Rs.764 crores as of 30th June compared to Rs.812 crores a year ago, representing a reduction of around 6%.

items.statement: Sales return provision of Rs 60 crore created at higher gross margin to buffer Q3-Q4 volatility.
items.quote: So, we have provided a good amount of sales return. So, we have taken a number of say 20% as expected sales return and we have done a provision of around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Capex plans on hold to focus on strengthening existing business; earlier capex would have supported 20% growth.
items.quote: CAPEX plans are on hold. But with respect to the QIP, which we have done, obviously, the last date was around June '26, which ended.

items.statement: Previous QIP closed in June 2026 with investors not paying balance 75%; new QIP under discussion.
items.quote: Now, we are in discussion with the investors to say, okay, what could be our next? Obviously, we don't want investors to lose their money. So, once that discussion is still on, then possibly could be that, okay, we might come with another QIP.

items.statement: Branded sales volumes grew 13% year-on-year; patented portfolio volumes grew 37%.
items.quote: Our brand business continued to demonstrate healthy momentum during the quarter, with volumes of branded sales to dealers increasing by 13% year-on-year. Within this growth, our patented portfolio delivered an impressive 37% increase in volumes.

items.statement: Raw material costs rose due to US-Iran conflict; managed via low-cost inventory, high-cost purchases during shortage, and later stabilization.
items.quote: Despite higher raw material costs arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, we were able to successfully pass on a significant portion of the cost inflation across our product portfolio.

items.statement: Technical manufacturing unit provides supply chain resilience for key molecules in patented products.
items.quote: One of the key advantages that we have been trying to have is that we have the technical manufacturing unit, which is sort of a feeder to the critical and important molecules, which go into the patented products.

items.statement: Product registrations secured in Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Mexico; fast-track approval in Sri Lanka.
items.quote: We continue to progress in the international market with successful product registrations happening in Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, and Mexico. Our regulatory approval for patented products has also been approved for being fast-tracked in Sri Lanka.

items.statement: El Nino impact on monsoon and rabi season remains a key monitorable; sales return volatility in Q3-Q4 depends on rainfall.
items.quote: A lot of discussion is on the El Niño and the impact on that. The first half of the year, the El Niño's impact has been there, but relatively less. We will continue to monitor the situation and we will plan to be able to change our placement strategies and our sales strategies based on how the Rabi season progresses.

items.statement: Farmer engagement through field demos, village campaigns, Mandi activations and digital outreach driving repeat purchases.
items.quote: Across the country, we continue to invest in farmer engagement through field demonstrations, seed limiting, village campaigns, farmer interactions, Mandi activations, and putting a lot of focus on our digital awareness program.

items.statement: Pest resistance driving shift from generics to specialized newer molecules with different modes of action.
items.quote: There are two ways of solving this challenge. A is increasing a little bit more usage of the generics, which is not a really great idea. Other option is to go for very specialized and newer molecules, which have a lower toxicity, higher efficiency, and also are working on different modes of action.

items.statement: Management learning curve in B2C segment over last 3-4 years; now more experienced in handling inventory and seasonal challenges.
items.quote: So, yes, these few factors resulted, but now after three, four years, we are more experienced, you can say, with respect to the kind of issues we face. So, we are able to tackle it much better.

items.statement: Creditor payment delays resolved; all payments now on time; advanced collections improved.
items.quote: Till some time back, there were some delays in payment to creditors also. Those have also been all closed now. So, presently, we are at a level wherein almost all the payments and everything are paid on time.

items.statement: Patented product registrations fast-tracked in Sri Lanka; international registrations progressing in multiple countries.
items.quote: Our regulatory approval for patented products has also been approved for being fast-tracked in Sri Lanka.

items.statement: Revenue grew 4% year-on-year to Rs 396 crore; PAT more than doubled to Rs 41 crore.
items.quote: Revenue from operations increased 4% year-on-year to Rs. 396 crores. More importantly, our profitability improved significantly, with EBITDA growing 70% year-on-year and PAT doubling to a little bit or a little bit more than doubling to Rs. 41 crores.

items.statement: India volume growth expected at 20%+ post-June, minimum
items.quote: Even post-June, we are looking at a 20% plus growth at least minimum.

items.statement: India volume grew 14.4% in Q2, healthy 20%+ growth from March except flat April due to El Nino
items.quote: In India, we saw healthy volume growth in twenties since the onset of the season, i.e. from March onwards except for the month of April, which was about flat, resulting in overall volume growth for the quarter of 14.4%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 27.7%, down 76 bps YoY due to Twizza consolidation; India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 23,430.4 million, registering growth of 17.2% year-on-year with the EBITDA margin at 27.7% in Q2 of 2026. EBITDA margin declined by 76 basis points year-on-year primarily due to consolidation of Twizza business which currently operates at lower margins.

items.statement: Acquired Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) Limited for ready GTM in Kenya for CSD and energy drinks expansion
items.quote: We also entered into an agreement to acquire the business of Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) Limited , which will provide us with the ready GTM in Kenya for expansion into carbonated soft drinks and energy drinks.

items.statement: H1 2026 net capitalized capex ~Rs. 9,500 million including Rs. 2,000 million brownfield expansion in India, Rs. 1,000 million snack plant in Zimbabwe, Rs. 4,000 million market infrastructure
items.quote: During H1 2026, net capitalized capex amounted to ~Rs. 9,500 million. This included ~Rs. 2,000 million towards brownfield expansion in India including value-added dairy beverages line at Supa, ~Rs. 1,000 million towards snack manufacturing plant in Zimbabwe, and ~Rs. 4,000 million towards market infrastructure including visi -coolers, glass bottles, pallets, and vehicles, etcetera.

items.statement: Capital work-in-progress ~Rs. 4,900 million primarily for South Africa expansion and CSD line in Kenya; inorganic capex Rs. 11,314 million for Twizza acquisition
items.quote: As on 30th June 2026, capital work -in-progress stood at the level of ~Rs. 4,900 million, primarily relating to expansion in South Africa and a CSD line in Kenya. In addition, inorganic capex of Rs. 11,314 million was incurred towards the acquisition of Twizza Limited in South Africa.

items.statement: Raw material costs averaged out; sufficient inventory for Q3 at average price lower than current price; pricing to remain same
items.quote: We have now made sure that we have enough material for Q3, but obviously there is a n impact of cost and which has got mixed in as we average our cost price and we have taken part of it in the Q2. And the balance would come in the Q3. Our pricing would remain same and overall effect would not be large because we have averaged out the pricing.

items.statement: Low-sugar, no-sugar products contributed ~73% of consolidated volume in H1 2026; VAD growing >40%, Nimbooz >30%
items.quote: Low-sugar, no -sugar products contributed approximately 73% of the consolidated volume during the period.

items.statement: Extended exclusive bottling and trademark license agreement with PepsiCo India until April 2049, removed SPV restrictions
items.quote: We also extended our exclusive bottling and trademark license agreement with PepsiCo in India until April 2049 and removed the earlier restrictions requiring VBL to operate solely as the S PV for PepsiCo business, strengthening our long -term partnership and creating greater operational flexibility to pursue opportunities that can deliver scale and synergies.

items.statement: Industry growing ~20% in H1; VBL, Campa, Coke all growing; B-brands being cannibalized
items.quote: Well, we cannot give you the exact, but if we are growing at 15% in the first half, and as you said Campa is growing at 50% or doubling, and we are sure Coke is also growing. That means the industry has to be growing ~20% or so.

items.statement: FSSAI directive to remove 'energy' word from labels within 90 days; temporary dip in STING volumes in June-July, now recovering
items.quote: They have come out with a clear guideline that we should have the word energy removed within next 90 days.

items.statement: International volumes grew 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza South Africa; all African countries firing except Zambia
items.quote: International markets also delivered a healthy growth with volumes increasing by 38.4% including the contribution of 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa.

items.statement: India net debt-free with surplus cash ~Rs. 14,941 million; consolidated net debt ~Rs. 3,730 million due to Twizza acquisition; CRISIL AAA stable reaffirmed
items.quote: VBL India remains net debt -free with surplus cash of ~Rs. 14,941 million. At the consolidated level, net debt stood at ~Rs. 3,730 million as of 30th June 2026. This was primarily on account of acquisition of Twizza in South Africa. Company's long -term rating for its bank loan facilities has been reaffirmed by CRISIL at AAA stable.

items.statement: Interim dividend 25% of face value, Rs. 0.50 per share, total cash outflow ~Rs. 1,691 million
items.quote: In accordance with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in total cash outflow of ~Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: Net realization per case improved 1.2% YoY; gross margin improved 44 bps to 55%
items.quote: Net realization per case for beverages at the consolidated level improved by 1.2% supported by better realizations in international territories . Gross margin improved by 44 basis points year -on-year to 55% supported by a higher mix of international business.

items.statement: El Nino impact on seasonality: April flat, May affected; weather impact holding back growth in affected months
items.quote: Now each month when the weather impact is not there, the kind of growth we are seeing is fabulous, high double-digit growth is what we are seeing. Essentially, it is the weather impact, which is holding it back.

items.statement: Strategic alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce CALPIS brand in India, entry into fermented dairy beverage category
items.quote: We also entered a strategic alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce the iconic CALPIS brand in India, marking our entry into the value-added fermented dairy beverage category.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target is 12.5-13% blended margin
items.quote: Our ideal margin level for normal operations should be as I have always maintained between 12.5-13% which is the steady state margin so that we are not losing business, maintaining our share of business because if we endeavor to increase our margins beyond that, then competition will undercut us.

items.statement: DICVS revenue target Rs 8000 crore by FY31 (Calendar Year 30) via organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: We have also in the past given a revenue guidance for our DICVS business and we have said we hope to achieve Rs. 8000 crores by a combination of primarily organic and some amount of inorganic growth for Calendar Year '30 or FY31 of Rs. 8000 crores and I continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Polymer revenue target 2.5x FY25 base; capacity on track for FY28
items.quote: The plastics business, I said we will, when we acquired the business, whatever numbers we had in FY25, which we just had one and a half months of operation, we said we will not just double, we will do two and a half times will be our endeavor to achieve.

items.statement: DICVS to grow 5% above market; ACFMS to grow 10% above market
items.quote: In terms of the DICVS business, we will continue to maintain a delta over the market growth rate of at least about 5% with the new business that we have acquired. In the ACFMS business, we do not want to settle for just a 5% growth rate over the market. We are aiming for a 10% growth rate over the market to ensure that that division grows aggressively as we have introduced new verticals like switc

items.quote: Our EBITDA, on a quarter-on-quarter comparison between the same quarter for FY26 has grown by only 21.42%. items.statement: Polymer division Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 249 crore, EBITDA margin 7.8%
items.quote: For Q1, the Polymer division has recorded a revenue of 249 crores with EBITDA of 7.8%.

items.statement: Minimum wage increase impact ~Rs 21 crore per annum; negotiating customer absorption
items.quote: It will help, but the minimum wage cost increase of about approximately 21 crores per annum because of the government regulation, we are still navigating with the customers to see how much we can absorb and how much they are going to absorb. That is a work in progress.

items.statement: Total Rs 700 crore capex over 18-24 months: Rs 400 crore Polymer, Rs 150-180 crore DICVS, Rs 120 crore ACFMS
items.quote: We have embarked on a 700-crore overall CAPEX cycle across all divisions of the company, not just in the next 12 months, but over the next 18 to 24 months. items.quote: With the capacity that we are creating, we should comfortably go to about Rs. 2000 crores of turnover from our current Rs. 1000 crores of turnover that we are capable of producing.

items.quote: The growth of both DICVS and ACFMS has been around 25%. Both of them have equally grown because we supply to the same set of customers both these vertical of products. items.quote: Has Pricol developed an e-cockpit and proved it to the customer? The answer is yes. The absorption of e-cockpit in the Indian overall automotive industry space is going to be very less. But I must admit that some of our multinational competitors will have an edge

items.statement: Honda relationship robust; won significant plastics business; capacity constraints led to phased acceptance; Honda identified as high-value, high-growth customer for next 3 years
items.quote: Our business with Honda at the moment is quite robust. We recently won a good share of business from them for our plastics division as well, totaling to a very handsome sum. items.statement: Polymer peers post-capex: Varroc, National Plastics, Premier Polyplast
items.quote: It would perhaps be Varroc, it would be National Plastics, and it would be Premier Polyplast.

items.statement: ABS/CBS norm relaxation by MoRTH has no material impact for next 2 years as ABS not in current focus
items.quote: As I mentioned in earlier calls, ABS is not something that we are focusing on at this point in time. It is something that is in the future roadmap of the company. So, that will not have any material impact for the next two years on our company.

items.statement: M&A paused for ~1 year due to demerger, capex, new programs; will only pursue high-quality assets at right value
items.quote: We have put a pause on mergers and acquisitions, though I mentioned that we were evaluating certain acquisitions earlier. When we went through the due diligence, we were not very happy with the quality of the assets. As I have maintained, we are only looking at buying quality assets and not distressed assets or assets with fundamental issues in either technology or quality of management. So, for t

items.statement: Rupee could touch three digits vs USD; if so, further margin pressure despite indexation
items.quote: definitely we can see improved margins happening in Q2 and Q3 provided the rupee does not further weaken because there are some indications being given when we talk to the market that the rupee could touch three digits against the dollar. And prices could further increase and crude oil prices also could go back to the 90s. So, it is anyone's guess.

items.statement: DICVS market share: 2W 30-35%, CV ~66%, Off-road strong, PV 8-9% (8 of 10 Tata cars)
items.quote: what is our market share in DIS its segment wise its is different in two wheeler DIS business we have largest in India with 30-35% volume share in CVs we have almost two third market share to CVs off road vehicles In passenger vehicles, we just have about 8-9% market share because at this point in time, we are only dependent on Tata Motors, where 8 out of 10 Tata cars are coming out with a PRICOL

items.statement: Polymer ROCE to dip during heavy capex cycle, then steady state 16-18%
items.quote: The ROCE for that business will remain muted because we are going through a very heavy investment cycle for the centre of excellence. We have a state of the art plant coming up in

items.quote: It is a million-dollar question. Sorry, because it is dependent on so many governmental agencies and multiple steps. But we have been told it will take at the very minimum 4 quarters or could be longer. But we hope that we don't have any roadblocks and it goes smoothly because we are not a multinational operating in multiple countries. It is a fairly simple operation. We have been told by our inve
