items.quote: As I mentioned, disc brakes, the real revenues will only kick in from FY28. We are still in early stages. I have maintained this in an earlier call and I will continue to maintain the same because we are just starting to ramp up and starting to supply. Disc brake will be a product. Disc brake and switches will start to take relevance only from FY28 and this is what the standard I have maintained i

items.statement: BMS business discontinued; no further investment; OEMs decided to control in-house
items.quote: Mr. Vyas, I have mentioned in multiple earlier calls, BMS is something that vehicle makers and OEMs have decided to control, and we are not putting any further money into BMS. This is something that I have been maintaining for three quarters. We are not looking at investing any further money or growing that business and that will not form part of our portfolio.

items.statement: Internal benchmark to open around 15% of store base annually; actual may vary a few percentage points higher or lower due to real estate realities
items.quote: internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually

items.statement: Building management bandwidth and capabilities across all levels; upgrading key technology and data systems for tighter operations
items.quote: we will be investing heavily in building management bandwidth and capabilities across all levels of the organization. Another big priority for me will be modernizing our technology and data stack

items.statement: Pipeline to build stores is strong and confident in maintaining 15% annual store growth over coming years
items.quote: our pipeline to build so many stores is strong, and we are confident in maintaining this over the coming years

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 16 bps to 14-15% range; EBITDA margin flat at 7.85%; net margin target around 5%
items.quote: our healthy gross margin is in the range of 14% to 15%, which keeps us very, very competitive, and that's the moat that we look at

items.statement: Staff cost increased significantly due to capability building ahead of volume growth; permanent headcount up ~4,000, contractual up only 2,200 despite 85 new stores
items.quote: we have driven productivity initiatives for the manpower in the stores as well as the warehouses. So those counts are inclusive of that

items.statement: Metro stores seeing slowdown due to saturation, high throughput, capacity constraints and competition; Tier 1/2 stores performing better than metros
items.quote: we are seeing, especially in metros like Mumbai, Bangalore, et cetera, where we have stores which are, one, very old and also very dense, with very high throughputs. And so therefore, to some extent these stores are reaching a saturation point

items.statement: Category contributions steady; slight dip in non-food, marginal increase in food; garments/apparel stable at 22-23% range; no intent to push to historical levels
items.quote: we expect this particular part of the business to be somewhere in that 22% to 23% kind of a range. And it is, as I said earlier also, it is doing quite well compared to our total business

items.statement: Quick commerce competition impacting metro same-store growth; impact expected to persist for next few years; not changing store expansion strategy based on QC presence
items.quote: I'm suspecting that that's not going to change over the next few years. And so therefore, that impact would remain while we of course continue to keep driving our own assortment

items.statement: DMart Ready focusing on 11 key cities to prove sustainable profitable model; improving assortment, 6-hour delivery, user experience; no plan to integrate with physical stores
items.quote: We made a conscious choice to double down on DMart Ready in 11 key cities where the vast majority of our online business comes from. We want our team to be laser-focused on proving that we can run a truly sustainable, profitable e-commerce model here

items.statement: 68 stores on long-term leases (15 of 85 new stores last year); open to leasing where land acquisition difficult; lease costs under AS 116 hit below EBITDA
items.quote: last year, for example, we now have about 68 stores -- 65 stores which are on long leases. And so therefore, it's not a very small number, it's a reasonable number in the overall store count of 500 plus

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for older stores likely to hover at current 7-8% range; not expecting considerable improvement; new stores in Tier 1/2 performing better
items.quote: same-store growth would possibly be hovering more in the range that we are seeing today, and we are not likely to see that go up considerably, all things being constant

items.statement: Internal store expansion target is 15% CAGR, could be a couple of percentage points higher or lower depending on real estate execution
items.quote: the internal number or internal ambition that we will look at will be that 15% number. And again, depending on how the situation turns out on the real estate development, the permissions, etcetera, it could be a couple of percentage points higher or lower.

items.statement: Same store sales growth expected to be around last financial year's level for the coming financial year
items.quote: I think we've said that it will be around the current trend, what we have been seeing over the last few years.

items.statement: Capex was upwards of INR 4,000 crores last year; NCD approval of INR 1,000 crores to manage capex and reduce borrowing cost
items.quote: If you see last year, capex was upwards of INR4,000 crores, and with the increasing store count that we want to pursue, we will need some capex - that is the plan.

items.statement: NCD approval of INR 1,000 crores may take total borrowing to INR 2,000 crores by year-end; existing stores expected to fund expansion in 2-3 years
items.quote: So we might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year, but that is all going towards managing capex.

items.statement: Gross margin target range 14-15%; any sourcing or productivity benefits within this range passed to customers
items.quote: wherever we will be getting, any benefit which might be on account of sourcing, productivity, etcetera, and if it is in that ballpark 14% to 15% type of a range, we will pass that on to customers.

items.statement: Monthly shopping in metros remains stable and strong despite quick commerce; Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities show good traction
items.quote: We are actually seeing that to be, quite stable and strong. And we're continuing to see, good traction in all our Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.

items.statement: Quick commerce impact seen mainly in dense metros with infrastructure challenges; minimal impact in other cities
items.quote: this seems to be more of an impact in, let's say densely populated metros with some of the infrastructure challenges and so therefore, I think that is where we see a little bit more. And wh atever impact, if at all, would be quite minimal in other places

items.statement: Piloting fresh fruits in some Mumbai stores with strong results; no plan for full-fledged fresh portfolio currently
items.quote: There are some pilots that we are doing in some of our stores with some fresh fruits, for example, in Mumbai, which is giving some strong results. But, is there a plan to have a full -fledged fresh portfolio in DMart stores at this point of time? No.

items.statement: DMart Ready consolidated to 11 cities from 18; 165 pickup points currently; efficiency gains expected FY27 onwards
items.quote: We currently have 165 pickup points.

items.statement: Of 85 stores opened in FY26, 15 were leased; lease model challenges remain around finding right property
items.quote: Of the 85 stores that we opened last fiscal, 15 were leased.

items.statement: Employee cost up 33% in standalone financials due to wage code implementation from December 2025 and March quarter
items.quote: On the absolute number of employee cost per se, there has been a slight impact also of the wage code that we implemented from December 2025 and the March quarter. So that also has contributed to the 33% hike in employee cost in the standalone financials.

items.statement: Organized trade including quick commerce and e-commerce still in early teens; huge runway for all formats
items.quote: total organized trade including quick commerce and e -commerce still is roughly in the early teens. Yes, and this includes the brick-and-mortar as well.

items.statement: Not tracking customer shopping behavior shifts to quick commerce; no consumer insight studies conducted
items.quote: No, we haven't done that, and I think possibly you are aware as well that we do not really track customer data, especially in our brick-and-mortar stores.

items.statement: Land acquisition pipeline of 2-3 years; conversion timeline 2-3 years depending on store complexity
items.quote: we are sitting on a project execution pipeline of next two to three years of stores that we will open and i t takes as Anshul mentioned earlier, it takes varying amount of time based on complexity and the local micro-market dynamics.

items.statement: Property conversion rate steady over years; manpower increased to support store openings
items.quote: the conversion has m ore or less remained steady. So, we shortlist a lot of properties, we do diligence, some properties fall off because the documentation is not clear and some landlords also are hesitant to sell every thing and all that.

items.statement: Offline customer data not collected to keep checkout simple and fast; DMart Ready has customer data
items.quote: Offline, we do not, collect the data because I think, one of the values that this organization is built around is simplicity. We want to make sure that the experience is simple enough.

items.statement: H2 FY27 will be better than H1; return to growth by Q4 FY27
items.quote: During the outlook, we have just mentioned that H2 will be better than H1, and we will return to growth in H2 by Q4, driven by the Q4 performance and our profitability will return largely when the revenues come.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle segment expected to grow next quarter (Q2 FY27)
items.quote: On the commercial vehicle, we will be on for growth next quarter.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 22-24% by FY29 maintained
items.quote: the medium term, we do believe that we will be in a position to get where we have mentioned

items.statement: Automotive industry facing challenges from Chinese competition, tariffs, war-driven input costs; European OEMs most impacted
items.quote: Automotive industry has been for some time facing some challenges globally, especially on account of extreme competition from China. It was accentuated by certain geopolitical situations, whether it is tariff or other s in different parts of the world.

items.statement: USD 257 million deal wins in Q1 FY27 driven by connected cars, aftersales transformation, autonomous
items.quote: On the back of that, what was still good was KPIT could do USD 257 million worth wins during the quarter, which was across the world, but mainly driven through connected cars , then after sales transformation and autonomous

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA 17.2%, EBIT 12.3%, PAT INR 1.17 billion; margins to improve incrementally until revenue growth returns
items.quote: In terms of profits, the EBITDA was at 17.2%, EBIT at 12.3% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion .

items.statement: Qorix share of loss to continue for next 1-2 quarters; margin recovery tied to revenue growth
items.quote: The second is the Qorix loss, which we said, I think it will continue for at least next quarter or two that we believe that s how it will be. So mainly the driver will be the revenue coming back.

items.statement: Product and solution revenue growing (N-Dream, i-Dart, Technica, Cymotive, Beacon platform); margin accretive over time
items.quote: This is one area where product and solution is really helping us to grow, and this will be also margin accretive over the period.

items.statement: Engaging new passenger car OEMs in Japan, Korea, Europe; expanding wallet share in existing OEMs via cost reduction programs (Caresoft) and aftersales transformation
items.quote: There are some car OEMs, which are very stable and I would say, successful OEMs in Japan, Korea and also in Europe, which we have not been working with enough. Now these are some of the OEMs we have been engaging for the last few years.

items.statement: Off-highway and trucks: new logos across US, Europe, Asia; software-defined machines (SDM) tailwind; 7 new off-highway OEMs, 4 truck/bus OEMs added
items.quote: We have opened seven different OEMs in off-highway segment. And we have started working with four different OEMs in trucks and bus business.

items.statement: China: engaged with 2 Chinese OEMs, one nearing meaningful engagement; product/solution traction; leveraging global OEM partnerships in China
items.quote: We have engaged with two Chinese OEMs. And at least one of that we are about to get to a meaningful engagement in that case. The third is that we do believe that we have found a reasonable traction for our products and solutions in China.

items.statement: European OEMs discussing 30-40% product cost reduction and production cost reduction with KPIT; conversations initiated but will take time to convert to revenue
items.quote: The conversation has shifted towards how does KPIT help these OEMs reduce the cost of their product by at least 30% to 40%. And secondly, how do we help them reduce the cost of their production.

items.statement: Investing in R&D for products/solutions (N-Dream, i-Dart, Technica, Cymotive, Beacon, World Foundation Model); Microsoft partnership for global go-to-market
items.quote: We have made multiple investments in research and development. – One of the a few latest ones is N-Dream. The second I talked about is Aftersales Transformation which we brand as -Dart, Technica products, and then Cymotive, the cybersecurity company.

items.statement: Fixed-price contracting increasing 600-700 bps; combining with AI (Beacon), solutions, products to protect margins; premium pricing maintained
items.quote: Over the past two to three quarters, becoming more and more visible that your fixed price contracting is increasing 600 to 700 basis points versus where we might have been last year.

items.statement: Wage hikes delayed; will be given in stages starting with junior grades; senior grades over period
items.quote: This is the first time we have delayed. But we will do it in stages. And we will give it to the some of the younger grades soon. The senior people will get over the period.

items.statement: Other expenses up due to forex impact on consolidated accounts, acquisition provisions, European subcontracting costs
items.quote: In terms of other expenses, there has been a certain impact because of the foreign exchange rate. As you know, these are consolidated accounts. So, secondly, there have been some provision because of the acquisitions that we did and some subcontracting cost in European region that incurred for our clients.

items.statement: Constant Currency revenue growth 0.1% YoY, USD revenue decline 0.6% YoY, CC revenue decline 3.6% QoQ
items.quote: For this quarter, year -on-year revenue we had C onstant Currency revenue growth of 0.1%, year-on-year USD revenue decline of 0.6% and quarter-on-quarter Constant Currency revenue decline of 3.6%.

items.statement: Europe revenue impact ~4% in Q1; impact to continue in Q2 at geography level but offset by US and SIMA growth
items.quote: We saw a reasonable impact in Europe, which was about 4% for the quarter, about 4% or so. But we also see, as you would look at this impact for the next quarter will not be at a company level. I'm telling you at a geography level. This will be made up by growth in U.S. as well as in SIMA.

items.statement: US geography growth well balanced across commercial vehicles and passenger cars; good visibility for upcoming quarters
items.quote: The growth in the geography is fairly well balanced across the entire portfolio. We have seen good growth on the commercial vehicle side and some of our long established relationships on the passenger car side as well. I think we have a fairly good visibility for the upcoming quarters to have it continue in the same line.

items.statement: Japan SDV program cancelled last minute; European SDV program ending as planned (start of production); both impacts in base now
items.quote: One program from Europe is almost getting over now. We'll go to start of production, but that's been planned. The one in Japan that was actually cancelled at the last minute. So both these programs are coming to a natural kind of an end.

items.statement: Uncertainty on timing of European OEM deal conversion and cost reduction initiative revenue; European cost structure optimization takes longer
items.quote: What we are not sure in the case of the current part is when these deals will realize. We are not at all worried in the sense , whether we would get our share of the business. It is about the timing.

items.statement: Deep tech (hydrogen, sodium-ion) meaningful revenues years away; battery tech needs 2-3 years for pilot plant, $100M+ investment
items.quote: I think it takes about more than $100 million of investment and it takes significant time. So after that it actually gets into production. And after getting into production, there are certain milestone after which we may get entitled to royalty.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation at OEMs; KPIT winning share but believes engagement model will shift to best solutions/products/AI to compete with Chinese OEMs
items.quote: So, absolutely, yes. The answer is absolutely yes. And we are doing pretty well there. But our belief is the client engagement model will change. Even though right now, people may look at the vendor consolidation in the traditional way people are talking about. We believe that over the period, the OEMs will go to the best of the solutions where they can compete with their competition.

items.statement: Broad-based growth strategy across 4 geographies (Europe, Americas, SIMA, JKC) and practices; transformation to build resilient company
items.quote: The effort over the last six quarters has been to have a broader-based growth. That means how do we have balanced growth across Europe, Americas, SIMA, which we call Southeast Asia, India, Middle East and Africa. This is a new sort of region for us and JKC.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Guided 25% AUM growth for FY27 while maintaining profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.

items.statement: Long-term spread guidance maintained at 5% to 5.25% on blended basis
items.quote: We are committed to maintaining that 5% to 5.25% basis points spread.

items.statement: Full year Opex to Assets guidance at 2.6% to 2.7% with expected 5-10 bps year-on-year reduction
items.quote: I think full year guidance would be in the region of 2.6% to 2.7%.

items.statement: BT out rate expected to be controlled in 5% to 6% range after exceptionally low 4.5% in Q1
items.quote: But yes, we should be able to control it in that 5% to 6% kind of a range.

items.statement: Demand across markets is healthy with disciplined underwriting supporting growth
items.quote: The affordable housing opportunity remains compelling. Demand across our markets is healthy, and our growth is supported by disciplined underwriting, a granular portfolio, stable asset quality and scalable operating platform.

items.statement: NIM improved to 6.0% from 5.9% QoQ; spread ex co-lending at 5.3%; cost of borrowing down 10 bps to 7.8%
items.quote: Net interest margin was 6.0%, up from 5.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost at 7.6% with no NHB drawdown in Q1; NHB drawdown planned for Q2
items.quote: When you look at the marginal cost of borrowing at 7.6%, it is not a one-off because we have not taken any NHB drawdown.

items.statement: AUM at INR16,938 crore, up 25.7% YoY and 6.7% QoQ; disbursements at INR1,628 crore, up 31% YoY and 3.6% QoQ
items.quote: AUM stood at INR16,938 crore as of Jun'26, growing 25.7% year-on-year and 6.7% sequentially. Disbursement at INR1,628 crore is up 31.0% year-on-year and 3.6% sequentially.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements INR46 crore; co-lending book at INR617 crore (3.6% of AUM); direct assignment of INR285 crore executed
items.quote: Co-lending disbursements were INR46 crore, taking co-lending book to INR617 crore, 3.6% of the AUM.

items.statement: Added 4 branches (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh) taking network to 175 branches and 373 touch points; net addition of 133 employees to 1,988 total
items.quote: During the quarter, we added four branches, one each in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh, taking our network to 175 branches and 373 touch points. We made a net addition of 133 employees, largely in customer-facing roles, taking the total headcount to 1,988.

items.statement: Individual housing loans 83% of portfolio; home loan disbursements growing faster than LAP; ticket sizes up marginally on housing side
items.quote: Individual housing loans continued to account for 83% of the portfolio, underscoring the granular secured nature of our core franchise.

items.statement: Disbursement growth split 50-50 between volume (units) and value (ticket size) increase
items.quote: I would put it at around 50-50. There is 50% of the growth is coming from increase in units and 50% is coming from ticket size.

items.statement: Asset quality stable: 1+ DPD flat at 4.7%, 30+ DPD flat at 3.2%, Gross Stage 3 flat at 1.8%; credit cost 40 bps; total provision coverage 45.3% including overlays
items.quote: Our 1+ DPD remained flat at 4.7%, 30+ DPD remained flat at 3.2% and Gross Stage 3 remained flat at 1.8%.

items.statement: BT out rate at 4.5% in Q1, lowest in many quarters; internal processes controlling BT outs showing traction
items.quote: BT out, as we have been talking about it for the last few quarters, we have actually put in place a set of internal processes to control the BT out.

items.statement: Fully floating rate book; will pass on borrowing cost changes to customers to maintain 5-5.25% spread; PLR cut unlikely due to West Asia uncertainty
items.quote: We are in a fully floating rate book. If there is any increase in cost of borrowing, we will increase the pricing accordingly. We are committed to maintaining that 5% to 5.25% basis points spread.

items.statement: Repayment rate assumed at 16-17% for calculations; Q1 at 14.3% due to exceptionally low BT out; no behavioural change in prepayments
items.quote: Broadly, we take a 16% to 17% repayment rate. If we have an exceptionally good quarter in terms of BT out, then the numbers will come down as we have seen in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Funding diversified: 57% banks, 14% NHB, 21% assignment/co-lending, balance NCDs/ECB/NBFC; capital adequacy 42.6% (Tier 1 42.2%); net worth INR4,483 crore
items.quote: As of Jun'26, our capital adequacy ratio was 42.6% with Tier 1 at 42.2%.

items.statement: CFO Nutan Patwari stepping down effective August 31, 2026; Board evaluating candidates for replacement
items.quote: As disclosed to the stock exchanges, Nutan will step down from her executive responsibilities effective from August 31, 2026.

items.statement: ROA improved 10 bps QoQ to 4.2%; ROE improved 50 bps to 14.5%; PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore
items.quote: Return on Assets improved by 10 basis points sequentially to 4.2%, while Return on Equity improved by 50 basis points to 14.5%.

items.statement: Cost to income at 32.7% (up 70 bps QoQ); operating cost to assets at 2.8%; pre-provision operating profit up 32.9% YoY to INR224 crore
items.quote: Cost to income was at 32.7%, an increase of 70 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Tariff-related stress in pockets like Tirupur addressed; no war impact on collections; Tamil Nadu team challenges resolved
items.quote: Some of the stress buildup was because of the tariffs, which has actually now been addressed. Post the start of the war, we have not really seen any stress buildup.

items.statement: Higher LTV (80%+) portfolio increasing due to apartment segment traction in Mumbai, Pune, Gujarat, Maharashtra
items.quote: This 80% plus portfolio is generally the portfolio originated in the apartment segment. We are getting more traction in places like Bombay, Pune and larger cities across Gujarat and Maharashtra, where this portfolio is increasing slightly.

items.statement: Credit bureau scores improving (738 to 750 over 3 years); new-to-credit customers declining to 12% from 26%; 88% now have credit history
items.quote: On the bureau scores, new to credit customers, the numbers are diminishing every quarter. And that is more of a market phenomenon because more customers are getting access to credit.

items.statement: Competitive intensity on BT outs remains same; internal processes driving retention improvement, not market changes
items.quote: Competitive intensity remains the same in terms of BT out, the interest in taking BT outs etc.

items.statement: NHB drawdown of INR354 crore outstanding unchanged; planned drawdown in Q2; no regulatory changes mentioned
items.quote: If you see our NHB outstanding was INR354 crore at the end of March. It is INR354 crore at the end of June also. We actually plan to take that drawdown in Q2.

items.statement: AI strategy operationalized: 'Cue' omnichannel platform, bureau analyzer, bank statement analysis model in production; pilots in lead qualification, legal/technical valuation, income analysis
items.quote: We have operationalized 'Cue', our in-house AI-orchestrated omnichannel customer communications platform. We have also deployed in production, a bureau analyzer and a contextual bank statement analysis model.

items.statement: Green Homes initiative: 100 homes certified in quarter, cumulative 550 certified homes as of June 2026
items.quote: Under our Green Homes initiative, we have certified a further 100 homes during the quarter, taking the cumulative number of certified homes to 550 as of June 2026.

items.statement: NPS at 79 for quarter; disbursal per branch/employee and AUM per employee cited as tech-differentiation metrics
items.quote: NPS is one of the more quantifiable metric. But then in terms of overall customer experience it's something that you can probably find out through branch visits or customer visits also.

items.statement: Targets USD 100 million revenue from Kothavadi stationary engine project by FY29, on track and may exceed with new inquiries
items.quote: I'll reiterate that we have targeted USD 100 million sort of revenue in FY '29. We are on track for that.

items.statement: Expects Sunbeam EBITDA margin to reach mid-teens by Q4 FY27 after restructuring completion
items.quote: I'm very confident about Q4 mid-teens sort of an EBITDA margin for Sunbeam.

items.statement: Approved capex plan of INR 430 crores for DR Axion for current year, may spill to next year
items.quote: The approved plan is around INR 430 crores capex for DR.

items.statement: Standalone capex averaging over INR 1,000 crores annually, to continue based on growth traction
items.quote: Standalone, we have been averaging more than INR 1,000 crores, I think, capex, and that will continue.

items.statement: Hosur Unit 3 being built in phases for high-pressure die casting, not alloy wheels, to address capacity constraints
items.quote: It will be spilling out to 2 years, maybe 4, 5, 6 quarters, depending on the need.

items.statement: Aluminium segment has new orders in development for production in FY28-29, mostly FY29
items.quote: Some are a little drawn. These orders are in the development stage, which will come into production in FY 28 and FY 29. Most of the production is coming in FY 29.

items.statement: Heavy horsepower engine project has 5 of 6 customer orders received, targeting USD 100M revenue by FY30
items.quote: With the first 4 customers itself, we have filled in the first USD 100 million sort of revenue target, which we had set up for FY '29-'30.

items.statement: Powertrain margins may be depressed initially on new stationary engine capacity until utilization improves, but return ratios expected similar to current business within couple of years
items.quote: But our confidence is that the return ratios will be among similar lines on the current powertrain within a couple of years.

items.statement: Industrial segment margins improving due to operating leverage from demand upswing in material handling and storage
items.quote: The operating leverage is helping us to increase the margins. The capex cycle started in India, and we are seeing a lot of traction.

items.statement: Material cost pass-through varies by customer; confident all will align to compensate for alloy prices
items.quote: we are confident all customers will need to align to the new reality that this sort of a situation, suppliers have to be fairly compensated for the al loy prices, which should be a pass -through

items.statement: Aluminium segment on strong growth path driven by massive recent investments and maturing capacities
items.quote: Aluminium, we are on a growth path, and this growth journey will continue.

items.statement: Industrial segment seeing demand upswing in material handling and storage with orders increasing quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our orders are increasing quarter-on-quarter, I would say. So, this will keep the margins intact going forward.

items.statement: Aluminium revenue balanced between 4-wheeler (heavy) and 2-wheeler, both growing with new order wins
items.quote: We are quite balanced. We are 4-wheeler heavy, if you look at the revenue portion of it. Yes, closely followed by 2-wheeler.

items.statement: Heavy engine project has 6 large customers, 5 orders received, 1 imminent; new inquiries accelerating with faster approval cycles
items.quote: We have 6 customers. 4 customers, the orders have been received. 5 customers order has been received. 1 customer we are receiving the order shortly.

items.statement: Sunbeam exiting legacy negative-margin businesses (10-20% revenue reduction) but replacing with higher value-addition work
items.quote: Revenue, there may be a 10%, 20% sort of reduction in the top line, but there will be an increase in the gross margin or value addition.

items.statement: Capex funding from internal accruals; no need for public markets; targeting good net debt to EBITDA
items.quote: So, year after, it will be only internal accruals. Of course, the cash mismatch will be there. See, as I mentioned, there's no ever need to come to the public markets per se.

items.statement: Alloy wheel production targeting 4 million wheels in FY27 against 5.8 million installed capacity across Bhiwadi and Shoolagiri
items.quote: And this year, hopefully we'll be touching or crossing 4 million wheels on the current year, that is at the combined plant of Bhiwadi as well as Shoolagiri.

items.statement: Global uncertainties (Iran crisis mentioned) creating wait-and-watch approach on capex acceleration
items.quote: We thought because of the Iran crisis, everything will slow down and stop that was when the capex plans were made.

items.statement: Land monetization deal close to signing
items.quote: Yes, it is gaining traction. I think something is happening. I think we are close to signing a deal, I would say.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods expected to complete by end of FY27
items.quote: As Mr. Jaipuria mentioned, our proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track, and we continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: KFC SSSG target of 5% to 6% for coming periods
items.quote: Percy, as I said, we are looking at a SSSG of about 5% to 6% for KFC.

items.statement: Plan to open new stores in line with earlier guidance
items.quote: Our plan for opening new units remains in line with the guidance given earlier.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 9.6% in Q1 FY27, highest ever Operating EBITDA at INR 151 crore
items.quote: Our consolidated Operating EBITDA grew nearly 38% year-on-year and represents an EBITDA margin of 9.6%.

items.statement: KFC Brand Contribution margin expanded 1.4% YoY to deliver INR 115 crore
items.quote: The Brand Contribution margin expanded by 1.4% and delivered Brand Contribution of INR 115 crore, nearly 22% higher year-on-year.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Brand Contribution loss of INR 4 crore due to higher costs and operating deleverage
items.quote: Accordingly, Pizza Hut posted a Brand Contribution loss of INR 4 crore.

items.statement: International business Brand Contribution margin improved 1.5% YoY to 18.2%
items.quote: Effective cost management and operating leverage helped improve the Brand Contribution margin by 1.5% compared to last year and posted Brand Contribution of 18.2% for the quarter.

items.statement: Stable demand trends observed with positive July trends despite Shravan drag
items.quote: But otherwise, broadly, in terms of trends, we have seen a positive trend in the month of July, and we are on track.

items.statement: KFC offline saliency improved to 57%, up 3 percentage points YoY
items.quote: came in at positive 3.3% , with offline saliency improving to 57%, more than 3 percentage points higher than the corresponding quarter last year

items.statement: Slight price increases taken in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate LPG and wage cost inflation
items.quote: We have taken slight price increases in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate the cost impact, and we are monitoring the raw ma terial and packaging prices as we go

items.statement: LPG prices significantly increased, availability issues managed by teams
items.quote: LPG prices have significantly gone up in the last few months. Our teams have effectively managed the availability of LPG during this period.

items.statement: KFC marketing rebalanced towards dine-in visits rather than deep online discounting
items.quote: Importantly, our marketing spends at KFC have been deliberately rebalanced towards driving dine-in visits rather than deep online discounting.

items.statement: Pizza Hut focusing on back-to-basics reset with improved product quality and everyday value
items.quote: The focus this quarter was on communicating improved product quality and everyday value, building the foundation for a stronger brand.

items.statement: Opened 11 net new KFC stores and 3 net new Biryani By Kilo stores in India in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We opened 11 net new KFC stores in India and added 3 net new Biryani By Kilo stores in India.

items.statement: Total store count at 1,855 in India and 2,255 globally as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: We ended the period with 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 stores globally , as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Dine-in shift will not change capex intensity; current store formats to continue
items.quote: Absolutely. Not much change in capex, so whatever format we are opening currently, that is what is going to be happening for future also.

items.statement: KFC ADS target of 105,000-110,000 to achieve 20% Brand Contribution margin
items.quote: once we cross a threshold of 105,000 ADS to 110,000 ADS, we will be able to cross 20% Brand Contribution margins in KFC as we have demonstrated that in the past.

items.statement: KFC dine-in saliency target of 59%-60% in near future
items.quote: our target remains to get to a number of 59%-60%.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods on track with NSE and BSE approvals received in June
items.quote: We received approvals from both the NSE and the BSE in June, bringing us closer to the next phase of regulatory filings.

items.statement: New leadership team fully in place including COO, CTO, CMO; CTO from QSR background with overseas experience
items.quote: We have hired a new COO, we have hired a new CTO, the new Chief Marketing Officer and so on and so forth. The entire leadership team is in place now.

items.statement: Technology buildout using core in-house team with Cognizant Technologies for faster rollout before merger
items.quote: rather than building our full-fledged new in-house tech team, we have decided to build a core team in-house and then outsource the buildout to Cognizant Technologies.

items.statement: Biryani By Kilo target to become INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years
items.quote: Our objective is to make sure that this brand gets to INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.

items.statement: Pizza Hut remains number 2 pizza brand nationally; focus on innovation and price laddering to improve ADS
items.quote: Pizza Hut has continued to remain the number 2 pizza brand in the country on a national basis, right. Domino's is number 1 and Pizza Hut is number 2.

items.statement: Macro volatility from rupee pressure, oil prices, LPG costs, and below-normal monsoon/El Niño risk
items.quote: The external environment became more challenging, the conflict in the Middle East pushed crude oil to elevated levels through April and May, feeding into LPG and fuel costs, while the rupee remained under pressure.

items.statement: International business delivered 20%+ YoY growth with INR 523 crore quarterly revenues
items.quote: Our international business maintains its impressive run of delivering strong and consistent growth, by posting another quarter of 20% plus year-on-year and delivered INR 523 crore in quarterly revenues.

items.statement: KFC global initiatives (Kwench beverages, sauces, boneless) to be rolled out in India; Kwench test launch planned
items.quote: So all of that will happen in India as well, Devanshu. So broadly, they have taken 3 initiatives globally. One is on the beverages, there is a sub-brand called Kwench, and we are already discussing in India to experiment with Kwench.

items.statement: Softer demand across key export and domestic markets; customers cautious due to macroeconomic uncertainties
items.quote: During the quarter, we operated in a challenging business environment where we saw softer demand across key export markets and domestic market as well.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA grew 16% YoY to INR94 crores; consolidated EBITDA grew 46% YoY to INR97.9 crores with margin at 18% vs 10.9%
items.quote: EBITDA margin on consolidated basis stood at 18% as compared to 10.9% in the corresponding quarter previous year.

items.statement: Nano fertilizer segment expects couple of INR100 crores revenue over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So from the future perspective, we have a very, very optimistic plan for this segment, nano fertilizer. So there will be couple of INR100 crores revenue coming from this segment over a period of next two to three year's time.

items.statement: No heavy capex planned for next 1-2 years; focus on debt repayment
items.quote: At the same time, there will be continuous repayment because we are not going to do heavy capex for next one or two year's time.

items.statement: Sulfur/sulfuric acid prices up 8-10x from INR4-5 to INR35-40 range due to Middle East war impact
items.quote: Let's say the sulfur, which is the basic raw material which is getting converted into sulfuric acid, which is the key raw material for titanium dioxide, the normal price for this product used to be for this raw material used to be in the range of INR4 to INR5. It has gone to nearly in the range of INR35 to INR40.

items.statement: Added three new nano fertilizers: Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc; expanding registrations globally
items.quote: We have further strengthened our product offering with the newly introduced nano fertilizer products like Nano DAP, Nano NPK, and Nano Zinc. These products complement our existing product portfolio and position us well to participate in the growing adoption of next-generation crop nutrition solutions.

items.statement: Titanium dioxide plant suspended due to withdrawal of anti-dumping duty and high raw material costs; pursuing government for duty reinstatement
items.quote: In titanium dioxide, as communicated earlier, operation remained suspended due to commercial unviability arising from the elevated raw material cost and the weaker price realization following the withdrawal of anti-dumping duty.

items.statement: Low inventory at customer/distributor level across Crop Protection and Pigment; buying on spot basis
items.quote: So the good thing, be it crop protection division or be it pigment division, the good thing is there is not much inventory at the customer level or at the distributor level. So they have been buying the material on the spot basis based on their requirement.

items.statement: Amalgamation of two wholly-owned subsidiaries filed in April; second motion application filed after creditor approval; awaiting NCLT hearing
items.quote: So as per the scheme, so we have filed scheme in April, and then we had now second motion application filed after getting approval from the secured and unsecured creditors. So now we are waiting for the next date of hearing.

items.statement: Crop Protection volume declined ~17% YoY; revenue down 12% YoY
items.quote: So, as far as the volume de-growth is concerned, there has been reduction by nearly 17% volume reduction.

items.statement: Pigment EBITDA margin expansion: ~5-6% from better realization, balance from operational efficiencies
items.quote: So yes, definitely about 5% to 6% is because of the better realization, and the balance is because of the better efficiency.

items.statement: Annual debt repayment ~INR130 crores; average debt cost ~7%; finance cost savings expected
items.quote: So on yearly repayment, we have around INR130 crores this year, and our average debt cost is around 7%. So to that extent, it is going to be a saving in the finance cost.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 12-13% for FY27 (Crop Protection 15-17%, Pigment ~10%, other segments drag)
items.quote: Overall, we believe we will be in the range of about 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Crop Protection peak revenue potential INR2,500-3,000 crores at 85-90% utilization; Pigment at 40-50% utilization for INR500-600 crores
items.quote: on the better utilization, which is nearly 85% to 90% utilization for the Crop Protection segment, we can do the revenue in the range of INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores. Harshit Singhania: Okay. And for the Pigments? Ankit Patel: For the Pigment, as I mentioned, we are running in the range of nearly 40% to 50% range, where we'll be generating the revenue close to INR500 crores to INR600 crores

items.statement: Pigment pricing volatile; difficult to predict Q2/H2 FY27 due to macroeconomic factors; taking calls regularly based on market conditions
items.quote: It is very difficult to predict in current scenario where, you know, every day we have been getting different news from the macroeconomic factor point of view. If it would have been the stable scenario, then we can predict it. But in current situation, it would be very difficult to predict.

items.statement: No significant inventory buildup at distributors; healthy underlying demand but macro volatility persists
items.quote: And we have been seeing healthy demand in both the segments. The only factor is the macroeconomic factor, which is keeping everything volatile. Otherwise, from the demand point of view, there is a reasonably healthy demand.

items.statement: Food & FMCG revenue growth guided at 18-20% for FY27; EBITDA margin to average last 4-5 quarters (3-4% range)
items.quote: Revenue guidance would be in and around, I think between 18%- 20% is something we should continue to deliver.

items.statement: Edible Oil volume growth guided at 5-6% for rest of FY27; EBITDA per ton expected at INR 4,000-4,500
items.quote: I think rest of the nine months, I think we should grow in a moderate single digit, which can be anywhere between 5%-6% kind of number on volume.

items.statement: Industry Essentials volume growth guided at 8-9%; EBITDA per ton at INR 3,000-3,500
items.quote: For Industry Essential s, we continue to expect volume growth of around 8%-9% while sustaining EBITDA in the range of INR 3,000-INR 3,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Overall portfolio volume CAGR guided at 8-9% over next decade
items.quote: I think 8% -9% is something which we are saying, and this is the AVVL Agri business guidance also we are giving it for quite some time

items.statement: Steady-state annual capex assumed at INR 700 crore; Edible Oil refining at 60-61% utilisation, Food 50% tolling to convert
items.quote: A steady state for a modeling purpose, if you really want, I think you can continue to assume a CAPEX of anywhere between INR 700 crore kind of number for every year.

items.statement: Edible Oil refining capacity at 60-61% utilisation; will need capex in couple of years; Food 50% tolling to convert to own ops
items.quote: Today, our Edible Oil refining capacities are running at close to 60% -61%. In the next couple of years, it will get exhausted, and we may have to put up CAPEX.

items.statement: Madhur brand sells ~15,000 tons/month; target 20,000 tons/month by year-end; full-year revenue INR 700-800 crore
items.quote: Madhur today sells close to 15,000 tons a month. Of course, our target is to scale it up further and make it close to 20,000 tons a month, by end of the year.

items.statement: Food & FMCG EBITDA margin 6% in Q1; management says track 4-quarter average (3-4% range) as business in investment phase
items.quote: Segment EBITDA came in at INR 104 crore with margin at 6%. We see this as the right trade-off.

items.statement: Edible Oil EBITDA per ton up 33% YoY; Industry Essentials EBITDA up 47% YoY
items.quote: Edible Oil delivered resilient performance in a volatile commodity environment with revenue up 15% and EBITDA per metric ton up 33% year-on-year.

items.statement: Food & FMCG grew 22% YoY (Rice >40%, Tops 23%); Edible Oil volume +2% YoY (de-stocking); Industry Essentials volume +13%
items.quote: Food and FMCG segment grew by 22% year -on-year during the quarter with revenue of INR 1,726 crore.

items.statement: Food portfolio 80% B2C, 15-20% B2B; Madhur added to sugar portfolio; Tops sauces 23% growth
items.quote: I think for the Food , 80% is actually B2C. In fact, more than 80% is B2C, hardly 15% is B2B.

items.statement: Direct reach ~970,000 outlets; total Nielsen reach 2.6 million outlets; focus shifting to throughput over outlet addition
items.quote: Our direct reach now is close to 970,000 outlets this quarter, while our total reach as per Nielsen remains at 2.6 million outlets.

items.statement: Alternate channels (MT, e-com, quick commerce) grew 27% YoY; quick commerce +56% YoY; HoReCa and branded exports strong

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue growth expected to remain above 20%

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to return to 24%-25% range on pre-Ind AS basis by end of FY27

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex spend of approximately INR 56 crores

items.statement: Operational bed capacity increased 22% to 1,862 beds; total bed capacity grew 26% to 2,435 beds
items.quote: Over the past year, our total bed capacity has grown by 26% to 2,435 beds, while our operational bed capacity has increased by 22% to 1,862 beds.

items.statement: Indore hospital to commence in Q3 FY27; Coimbatore and Gurgaon Sector 56 in Q3 FY28; Gurgaon Sector 44 in Q1 FY29; Pune and Bangalore Seegehalli in FY29
items.quote: Our regional hub hospitals in Coimbatore and a spoke hospital in Gurgaon Sector 56 are expected to commence operations in Q3 FY28 , followed by our hub hospital in Gurgaon in Sector 44 in Q1 FY29. • Development is in progress with our Pune hospital of 150 beds and Spoke hospital in Bangalore, Seegehalli both are expected to commence operations in FY29

items.statement: Visibility of 1,200 beds under various stages of development

items.quote: In markets where we have excess capacity or available beds, we may consider allocating a portion of that capacity to government -funded healthcare schemes. However, the decision will depend on the reimbursement rates and overall economics.

items.quote: This provides us the strong financial stability and the flexibility to fund our ongoing capital expenditure program, support our expansion pipelines and pursue strategic inorganic opportunities while continuing to execute all planned investments through internal accruals.

items.quote: Our preferred approach has always been to have core doctors on a full-time employment model wherever possible. That said, there may be some degree of flexibility for certain specialty doctors, where a hybrid engagement model could be appropriate.

items.quote: Seasonality will always remain a factor in children's hospitals because disease patterns naturally fluctuate. items.quote: we are very confident that going forward, this sector , defense portfolio, would continue to give 30%, 35%, growth rate.

items.statement: Demand robust across verticals; no demand-side constraint foreseen; medical and defense scaling up

items.quote: we see going forward with high-teen to double-digit growth in second quarter onwards. High single-digit to double-digit in second quarter onwards.

items.quote: However, the next quarter or so, we may see a compression in the gross margins level because the prices of the commodities and the dollar, et cetera, has increased.

items.quote: In Quarter 1 Financial Year 2027, revenue from our domestic business increased by 10.5% year-on-year to INR3,426 crores. This growth was driven by a 15.8% increase in our chronic portfolio, growth recovery in the acute portfolio, and strong double-digit growth in BSV.

items.statement: Secondary sales per IQVIA grew 12.7% in Q1 FY27 with 4.7% volume growth (up 220 bps YoY)

items.statement: Chronic share (ex-BSV) increased 80 bps YoY to 40% in Q1 FY27; medium-term target 50%
items.quote: focused initiatives across key chronic therapies have translated into increase of 80 bps year-on-year in our chronic share, excluding BSV, to 40%, primarily driven by strong growth of 19.4% in cardiac, 12.7% in anti-diabetic. items.statement: Acute portfolio recovered to 10.9% YoY growth in Q1 FY27 from 6.1% in Q1 FY26, now broadly in line with IPM
items.quote: Our Acute portfolio has steadily recovered and is now broadly in line with IPM growth, improving from 6.1% in quarter 1 Financial Year 2026 to 10.9% in quarter 1 Financial Year 2027.

items.statement: International revenue grew 29% YoY to INR605 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Moving to our international business, revenue for the quarter grew 29% year-on-year to INR605 crores.

items.statement: BSV domestic grew ~17% YoY and international ~25% YoY in Q1 FY27; overall BSV growth ~21%
items.quote: BSV domestic is around 17%, and international is around 25%.

items.quote: To further strengthen our presence in multi-specialty business, we have launched a new division, Vistar, which would help scale some of the lesser focused brands in existing divisions.

items.statement: Modern trade and e-commerce share in Consumer Healthcare increased to 15% from 11% a year ago, supported by 38% channel growth
items.quote: our modern trade and e-commerce share increased to 15% from 11% a year ago, supported by 38% growth in that channel.

items.statement: Prescription leadership maintained at #1 with 15.2% prescription share in Q1 FY27

items.quote: The net operating working capital days for the quarter on trailing 12-month basis has increased to 52 days as compared to 48 days in the corresponding period last year, which is mainly due to increased inventory levels.

items.statement: Cash flow to EBITDA ratio declined to 77% in Q1 FY27 from 99% YoY due to higher tax rate, working capital, and base effect
items.quote: In quarter 1 FY27, our cash flow to EBITDA ratio has decreased to 77% as compared to 99% in quarter 1 FY26. This drop of 22% in cash flow to EBITDA ratio is a combination of higher effective tax rate, working capital, and base effect in quarter 1 FY26.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR3,377 crore as of June 30, 2026; net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 0.9x in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In line with our prudent financial strategy, we reduced our net debt to INR3,377 crores as of 30th June 2026, resulting in the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 0.9x in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex increased to INR198 crore from INR127 crore YoY; at 4.9% of revenue
items.quote: Our capex spend during the quarter has increased to INR198 crores in quarter 1 FY27 as compared to INR127 crores in quarter 1 FY26. The capex as a percentage of revenue is 4.9% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Sales price increases taken contributed to gross margin improvement in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Firstly, the impact of sales price increase that we have taken.

items.statement: Commodity prices and dollar increase may compress gross margins in coming quarters
items.quote: the prices of the commodities and the dollar, et cetera, has increased.

items.statement: Attrition and vacancies now back to normal levels after significant reduction over last 1.5 years
items.quote: attrition and vacancies are now in control. It has dropped significantly. It ha s come back to the normal level

items.statement: New product introduction (NI) contribution at 2.8% of sales in Q1 FY27 vs IPM at 4.1% (including GLP-1)
items.quote: If you look at Q1, the new introduction, NI contribution is 2.8% as compared to IPM 4.1%.

items.statement: West Asia crisis cited as sole reason for conservative gross margin guidance despite favorable mix
items.quote: So that's the only caveat we are putting because of the West Asia crisis. So we are taking a conservative approach.

items.quote: So Rivotril, if you see the IQVIA numbers, it is in the region of INR20 crores to INR30 crores. And we expect that it will give lot of entry to a lot of specialists because it's a textbook brand in terms of the molecule.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for full year FY27
items.quote: As we move ahead, we are firm and stick with our medium-term guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, 17% to 18% disbursement growth for the full year.

items.statement: Next three quarters targeted disbursement growth upward of 20%

items.statement: AUM at INR31,364 crores as of June 30 2026, up 18% YoY
items.quote: Our AUM as of 30th June 2026, stood at INR31,364 crores, a growth of 18% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Exit spread held at 5.8% as of June 2026 despite 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026
items.quote: Even after a 15 bps reduction in our RPLR effective February 2026, our spreads have held at 5.8% as on June 26.

items.statement: Spread guidance maintained at 5.5% upward over medium term
items.quote: We have always guided the market that at any given point in time, we will be a company which will be as a company with a spread of 5.5% upward.

items.statement: Stage 3 provision coverage ratio 34% as of June 30 2026
items.quote: As at 30th June '26, our Stage 3 provision coverage ratio stands at 34%.

items.statement: Balance transfer out rate 5%, improved 20 bps YoY
items.quote: Balance transfer out during the quarter in question stood at 5%, which is one of the lowest BT out rates in the last 8 to 10 quarters and improved by 20 bps as compared to Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for full year FY27 after seasonal Q1 elevation
items.quote: I think we are quite confident of holding the 1.1% level as we end the year. And I think that would be in the credit cost will be again settle down anywhere between 23 bps to 25 bps.

items.statement: Branch network at 628 branches across 22 states, 550+ districts; new branches reach productivity in 9-15 months

items.statement: Branch opening guidance of 45-50 branches for FY27 maintained; only 2 opened in Q1 due to timing, catch-up expected in Q2-Q3
items.quote: We stand by our numbers of 45 to 50 branches.
