items.quote: The planned turnover there would be an asset turn of 1x for SAF.

items.statement: SAF expected sales price INR180-190 per litre with 24-25% margin
items.quote: For SAF sir, our expectation is that we get a sales price of about INR180 to INR190 a litre. That's the off-take price. And with that our margin profile that we expect should be at around 24% to 25%.

items.statement: CBG capex of INR700-760 crores for 132 TPD across two JVs
items.quote: In the CBG space, we've undergone a capex of about INR700 crores under two JV companies. That is with Sumitomo to do four CBG plants of 20 TPD at a cost of INR330 crores and with GAIL to do six CBG plants of 10 TPDs each at a cost of INR425 crores.

items.statement: SAF capex of INR2,000 crores planned, construction to start in 2-3 months
items.quote: That is for the aviation fuel. There is another capex of about INR2,000 crores planned and it's already we've declared that also. But the capex will begin as early as let's say in the next two or three months.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity utilization at 60%, target 80-85%
items.quote: With the current capacity, we were able to only operate at about 60% of capacity utilization. It is fairly better than the last 2 years, but we still have a lot more of opportunity to increase the capacity utilization by another 20% to 25% at least.

items.statement: Three CBG plants near commissioning by Q3 FY27, revenue from Q4 FY27
items.quote: Happy to report that three out of the four plants are near commissioning and would be put to use hopefully by the quarter 3 of this financial year. And quarter 4, we should start seeing some revenues from these three out of the four plants.

items.statement: Six GAIL JV CBG plants land procurement from August, revenue from Q1 FY28
items.quote: We are in advanced action to procure the land and to begin construction hopefully in the month of August onwards. That should give us another six plants giving us a total of about 72 tons per day of additional capacity from hopefully Q4 of this year and revenues to be seen from quarter one of the next financial year onwards.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 ethanol EBITDA margin 23.5%, PAT margin 9.5%
items.quote: On basis of a margin analysis, the EBITDA margin stood at 23.5%, the PBT margin stood at 12.5%, the PAT margin was at 9.5%.

items.statement: CBG sustainable EBITDA >60%, PAT 40-50%
items.quote: So CBG what we have we've been seeing so far is a EBITDA of greater than 60% and a PAT margin of close to 40% to 50%. If you ask me, it seems to be the long-term case.

items.statement: Maize price INR25.50/kg currently, margin INR6-7/litre; booked at INR18-22/kg for INR15-16/litre margin
items.quote: And as on date it is at around INR25.50. So, at INR25.50, the margins come down drastically. It comes down to almost INR6 to INR7 a litre. That's the margin contribution we get. But since we have -- we are holding ample stock since the early days, that is giving us the driver for or rather the margin growth that we're seeing.

items.statement: 15 crore litres court case spillover not included in 44 crore order book
items.quote: So, the INR44 crores doesn't include the INR15 crores spillover, sir. And this INR15 crores we've been fighting tooth and nail to the -- with the OMCs and we're hopeful that it should come through anytime now.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 ethanol mix 50:50 grain:sugar; next quarter more grain
items.quote: Sanjay ji, this quarter also was almost a 50:50 blend with grain and with sugar. Going forward in the next quarter, we hope that it will be more of grains.

items.statement: CBG revenue split 58-60% gas, 40% FOM/LFOM
items.quote: In the CBG business, if I were to give a revenue split up, we achieve about 58% to 60% of revenue from gas sales and about 40% of revenue coming from FOM and LFOM put together.

items.statement: GAIL ensures 80-90% daily CBG offtake for JV plants
items.quote: And luckily for us, what gives us the moat that we carry is the tie-up with the partners where they're ensuring more than 80% to 90% of sales on a daily basis.

items.statement: Received INR150 crores viability gap funding under PM JI-VAN Yojana for SAF
items.quote: Also, we are very happy to report that we could successfully achieve about INR150 crores worth of viability gap funding from the Government of India under the PM JI-VAN Yojana.

items.statement: Active export discussions with Japan under JCM mechanism
items.quote: These are discussions that are actively happening. Especially the discussion I know is Japan and India have a mechanism to reduce their carbon footprint. It's called JCM, Joint Credit Mechanism, where countries like Japan, countries like Singapore, most of them are having targets to use ethanol with their petrol blend.

items.statement: Holding ample grain inventory procured at INR18,000-21,000/ton vs current INR25,000/ton
items.quote: Since we are still sitting on a lot of volumes, if you have seen our inventory levels in our balance sheet in March as well as currently, we're holding a lot of volumes of grains which were procured at a range of INR18,000 to INR21,000 a ton.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used to enhance working capital limits for raw material procurement
items.quote: With the gain in the working capital limits thanks to the IPO that we did and the working capital limits that we could secure from the proceeds of the IPO, company is fairly in a good position to have or build up enough raw material at a decent price.

items.statement: Fuel retail expansion of 76 outlets paused due to Middle East crisis and crude price volatility
items.quote: because of the Middle Eastern crisis and the variance in the crude prices, we still see a lot of dynamics in the fuel prices. The delta is very high. Though we have identified about 76 additional locations, we have not begun construction or we have not begun the franchise works in the additional 75 fuel retail outlets owing to the Middle Eastern

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 45-50% with operational EBITDA doubling vs FY26
items.quote: At a consolidated level, we continue to expect approximately 45% to 50% top -line revenue growth for the full year with the doubling of our operational EBITDA, a target that is weighted to the second half as consumer utilization builds through the year.

items.statement: Aerospace FY27 revenue growth 25-30% with segment EBITDA margin above 20%
items.quote: First, grow aerospace revenue profitably 25% to 30% with a segment EBITDA margins above 20%.

items.statement: Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Third, move our consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27, which will be a major inflection point in our consolidated profitability.

items.statement: Consumer utilization expected to reach 40-50% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: At this point of time, we are fairly confident to get to 40% to 50% of capacity utilization.

items.statement: Aerospace order book crossed USD1 billion, up 13% sequentially from USD889 million
items.quote: The defining achievement of the quarter was our aerospace order book crossing the USD1 billion mark, following a 13% sequential increase from USD889 million.

items.statement: New long-term agreements with two Tier-1 aerostructure customers and first contract for fully integrated Airbus A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems signed at Farnborough
items.quote: We signed long -term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers, expanding our global base. And we signed our first contract for fully integrated Airbus A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems.

items.statement: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin 23% in Q1 FY27 on 40% YoY revenue growth
items.quote: Q1 delivered 40% growth at a 23% segment margin.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA improved 3.5x sequentially from INR42 million to INR148 million, margin from 1% to 4%
items.quote: Excluding other income, ope rational EBITDA increased from INR 42 million in Q4 FY '26 to INR148 million in Q1 FY'27, an improvement of approximately 3.5x with the margin increasing from 1% to 4%.

items.statement: Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million sequentially (24% improvement) to INR361 million loss
items.quote: Sequentially, the consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR 112 million or approximately 24%, supported by increasing production volumes and improving operating performance.

items.statement: FY27 total capex guided at INR660 crores (INR500 crores consumer, INR160 crores aerospace), with potential aerospace acceleration
items.quote: So INR660 crores, I mean originally, we had given a split of about INR500 crores for consumer and INR160 crore s for aerospace. We may see some acceleration in aerospace capex and that may be compensated by some reduction or saving & optimization in consumer

items.statement: 5-year capex plan FY27-31 of USD350-400 million; Hosur investment INR1,900 crores over 10 years including JVs
items.quote: We have laid down a plan from this year to FY31 for the next five years investing about USD350 Million to USD400 Million of overall capex.

items.statement: Hosur facility first phase to commence H2 FY27-FY28 (September-March), revenue kick-off from FY29; full vertical integration by 2030
items.quote: The first facility will commence in the second half between September to March timeframe of next year of FY27 to FY28 and that's why Rajeev was reflecting that FY29 when we'll start seeing some revenue coming out of that facility.

items.statement: Aerospace utilization at ~70%, can comfortably reach 75%; adding machines weekly to support order book growth
items.quote: Order book growth means it only comes because we can get up to 75% comfortably, you know, and as we are also increasing the order book, we'll have to put a capex in there to support it.

items.statement: Consumer demand structural, not inventory restocking; "whatever we are producing, we are shipping"
items.quote: This all driven by the customer demand basically. Whatever we are producing, we are shipping. There is no issue of the demand.

items.statement: Consumer electronics customer is one of largest global brands (confidential); cookware customer Tramontina; toys customer Mattel
items.quote: consumer electronics is one of the largest, you know, manufacturer consumer electronics brand. We cannot share the name. Rushikesh: Okay. Aravind Melligeri: Because of confidentiality. And Tramontina is on our consumer durable side and Mattel is our consumer toys

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 127 to 125 days; target ~125 days for business
items.quote: We saw an improvement in the working capital efficiency with net working capital days reducing from 127 days at the end of FY'26 to 125 days in Q1 FY'27

items.statement: Debt reduced in Q4 FY26: loan repayments ~INR2,527 million, net reduction in short-term/working capital borrowings INR789 million; finance cost fell from INR358 million to INR189 million
items.quote: Finance cost reduced from INR 358 million in Q4 FY '26 to INR 189 million in Q1 FY '27, following debt reduction undertaken during the previous quarter, including lo an repayments of approximately INR 2,527 million and a net reduction of INR 789 million in a short -term and working capital borrowings.

items.statement: Likely USD150 million raise needed over plan period, not planned for FY27 unless accelerated capex or inorganic opportunity
items.quote: We did communicate that most probably about USD150 million kind of a raise we'll have to do. We are not planning to do anything this year unless there is advanced pull-in of capex or inorganic piece, you know.

items.statement: CFO transition: Dinesh Iyer stepped down end of June; search for full-time CFO progressing; Harish Bang leading finance interim
items.quote: On the CFO transition, as communicated in May, Dinesh Iyer has stepped down at the end of June and our search for a full-time CFO is progressing well. In the interim, Ha rish Bang is leading our finance function

items.statement: Raw material sourcing 99% imported; limited qualified domestic sources for aerospace alloys; customer-supported sourcing for superalloys/titanium
items.quote: I think our raw material is like 99% is imported. So , I don't think there is any possibility of changing that anytime soon , because we don't have any qualified sources in India for that to change.

items.statement: No specific impact from tariff/trade policy changes; customer supply chain strategies stable
items.quote: Look, our I mean we are not seeing any specific changes due to these tariffs. Our customers have taken strategic view of where they want to be as a global supply chain and based on that they are committing the supplier allocations and we are working with them on those activities.

items.statement: Consumer revenue growth 16% QoQ at similar utilization, driven by enhanced throughput, better product mix, improved execution
items.quote: This reflects enhanced throughput, better product mix and improved execution, enabling the business to drive higher revenue from the existing manufacturing footprint.

items.statement: Aerospace parts portfolio expanded to 5,740 parts with 86 new parts added in Q1
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 86 new parts, further expanding one of India's most extensive aerospace manufacturing portfolio to 5,740 parts.

items.statement: Consumer capex commitment conditional on utilization ramp-up; "if utilization is not going to happen then some portion of the capex will not happen"
items.quote: If the utilization is not going to happen then some portion of the capex will not happen.

items.statement: Other income dropped from INR279 million (Q4 FY26) to INR67 million (Q1 FY27), mainly due to lower foreign exchange gains; interest income to remain at Q1 levels
items.quote: On the other income, just to clarify, there are no revaluation reserve s as such. So, it's typically driven by two things. One is the interest income and second is foreign exchange fluctuation. So typically, foreign exchange fluctuation is what we don't project for future period. Our interest income will remain in the similar line as what it was in Q1.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expected 25-27% and PAT margin 22-23% after 2-3% dent from marketing spend
items.quote: So, EBITDA margins, so the current EBITDA margins that we are talking about is 29% and the PAT margins are around 23%. Like I said, 2% to 3% dent here, so anything between 25% to 27% on yearly basis and something between 22% to 23% on PAT basis is what we are expecting.

items.statement: No upward revision to guidance despite strong Q1; management prefers to under-promise and over-perform
items.quote: So we -- honestly I think Modak sir would have been a better person to answer that. As he always said that we want to under-promise and over-perform. So this is what I think that -- there is no different guidance that I have received from him.

items.statement: Plan to open 9 COCO stores in Year 1 and 7 in Year 2 post-IPO; 2 already operational
items.quote: As outlined in prospectus, we plan to open nine stores during first year of following IPO with remaining stores to be opened in second year. As on date, we remain on track to execute the expansion plan as communicated and expect to complete the rollout within the stated timeline.

items.statement: Total store network at 37 stores: 3 COCO and 34 shop-in-shop with PNGS
items.quote: We continue expanding our retail footprint with a launch of new COCO store at Amanora Mall, Pune on 7th of July, taking our total network to 37 stores comprising three COCO stores and 34 shop-in-shop stores with PNGS.

items.statement: Healthy consumer demand across all 21 cities; same-store sales growth ~50% in SIS format
items.quote: If you see the increase in turnover, it has happened on vanilla basis in almost every city that we are in. Almost we are present in 21 cities and almost in every city we are seeing that there is a really good demand and whatever the SSSG that has happened, it is across.

items.statement: Volume growth >50% on diamond caratage basis in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The volume growth that we see in diamond caratage is more than 50% is what we have seen.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 35.46%, EBITDA margin 28.76%, PAT margin 23.06%
items.quote: The gross profit for the quarter stood at INR41.83 crores, reflecting the growth of 147.25% Y-o-Y with gross margins of 35.46%. The EBITDA stood at INR33.92 crores, recording a growth of 192.88% Y-o-Y, while EBITDA margins stood at 28.76%. The PAT stood at INR27.21 crores, growing it by 265% Y-o-Y with PAT margins at 23.06%.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by economies of scale and better price realization on diamond caratage
items.quote: First of all, like you have mentioned that the economies of scale obviously played a great part. If you see there is an increasing turnover by almost it got doubled, so of course the economies of scale had played a part. And the better price realization for diamond on caratage base was also a contributor there.

items.statement: Marketing spend to ramp up in Q2-Q4 causing 200-300 bps PAT margin dent for full year
items.quote: But like I explained in my pre-note is that once we start doing marketing effort in Q2, Q3 and Q4, obviously there will be around dent of 1% or 2% on PAT basis and other than that I don't see anything fluctuating.

items.statement: 97% of business in star-melee/minus-two diamonds where lab-grown price differential is only 10-15%
items.quote: So, the competition from lab-grown is not that significant because predominantly we are dealing in star-melee and minus-two kind of diamond. So, in that particular category, the price differential between the lab-grown and natural diamond is not more than 10% to 15% on a product basis.

items.statement: Average order value ~INR1 lakh in Q1 FY27; seasonally lower than Q3 peak
items.quote: Further, addition to that our average order value also remains around INR1 lakh for the quarter Q1 of '27.

items.statement: Inventory turns 1.29x in Q1 FY27, within industry range 0.75-1.5x
items.quote: Our inventory turns stood at 1.29x during the quarter one of FY27, which is in line with the industry's accepted range for diamond which is between 0.75x to 1.5x.

items.statement: Trade payables fell from INR32 cr to INR20 cr; no material change in payment terms
items.quote: So, I think it will it is so it is not directly related to how the quantities are coming in and out. So generally, maybe towards fag end of last year it would have been, you know, raised and the credit period is still due, so that is why the payments were not made or something like that.

items.statement: Short-term debt (WCDL) reduced from INR166 cr to ~INR120 cr; quarterly interest cost to decline sequentially
items.quote: So, it was WCDL taken at the start of I think a year for the procurement of for the BTA settlement and that is been now I think repaid. 120 is part of it is repaid and currently it is around INR120 or something.

items.statement: Finance cost INR27 million: INR26.53 million pure interest, INR0.95 million lease liability interest
items.quote: So out of total INR27 million, almost INR26.53 million is the pure finance cost and about INR0.95 million is the interest on lease liability.

items.statement: No MCX hedging; natural hedge via periodic gold buy/sell; gold loan facility available but not yet used
items.quote: So, I think so basically we do have a gold loan facility available as a limit from the bank, but currently we are not using that because the gold portion is limited. So if you see the total inventory valuation, the gold portion is very short and we are not doing any hedging on MCX.

items.statement: Akshaya Tritiya revenue INR12.7 cr vs INR3.5 cr YoY (268% growth)
items.quote: During Akshaya Tritiya alone, we recorded revenue of INR12.7 crores compared to INR3.5 crores in corresponding period last year, reflecting a robust 268% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: EBO break-even: 1 year in Maharashtra, 15-18 months outside Maharashtra; inventory turn 0.75x break-even, 1.25-1.5x super-normal profits
items.quote: So, for EBO within Maharashtra, it will be one year and the we have opened three EBOs out of which one EBO is more than six months and what we are looking at that we are fairly in line with what the expectation are. So that is point number one. Outside Maharashtra, the soon I think in two or three months the EBOs will start coming up and what we are anticipating is that the BEP period would be bet

items.statement: SIS same-store sales growth ~50% YoY across all shops; COCO stores too new for SSSG
items.quote: So all the SSSG that has happened is in SIS only because all the COCO models are not even one year old since the opening. So, there is no SSSG as such right now. But in terms of SIS growth that we have seen is almost 50% SSSG is what we have seen across the shop.

items.statement: PM's appeal to reduce gold buying impacted plain gold jewellery but not diamond jewellery due to utility-based purchase nature
items.quote: But about diamond jewellery, I think the customer preference and the way customers are looking at this particular diamond jewellery is completely different from gold jewellery. It is more utility-based. So, there is no investment buying as which happens in our case.

items.statement: IPO proceeds funding 15 COCO stores; future expansion post-15 stores primarily from internal accruals
items.quote: So primarily it will be through internal accruals. Eventually if the good opportunity comes, obviously the phase-wise decision would be taken. But I think for the next couple of years we are almost sorted.

items.statement: Brand ambassador search underway; negotiations ongoing but nothing formalized yet
items.quote: So of course we are in hunt. There are certain negotiations going on, but it is very difficult to, you know, promise you right now unless it is formalized.

items.statement: Gold price correction expected to support jewellery purchases ahead of wedding/festive season
items.quote: The recent correction in gold prices is expected to support jewellery purchases ahead of upcoming wedding season and festive season, while the continued shift towards organized and branded jewellery continues to provide strong structural tailwind for the industry.

items.statement: E-commerce website on track to launch by end of August 2026
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the company's e-commerce website is also on track to launch by the end of August 2026, making an important milestone in strengthening our digital presence and expanding our direct-to-customer reach.

items.statement: Other income INR5.6 cr from interest on parked IPO proceeds
items.quote: So all the IPO proceeds which are parked in our bank is yielding of interest and that is getting accounted for.

items.statement: Revenue INR118 cr, up 119.5% YoY driven by higher diamond caratage volumes
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from operations stood at INR118 crores registering robust 119.5% year-on-year growth, driven largely by higher volumes in terms of diamond caratage and highlighting the strength of our core diamond jewellery business.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of upwards of 40% for next 12 months; confident of over-delivering
items.quote: last quarter we had said our overall growth for the next 12 months will be upwards of 40%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 15% reduction for FY27; tracking well
items.quote: We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost , and we are tracking well on that.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing to drop by minimum 100 bps in H2 FY27 as old debt runs off
items.quote: our guidance for FY, particularly H2 of FY27, that you will see the cost of borrowing dropping by 100 basis points and it will only increase as we, as the old debt basically runs off the book

items.statement: ROE target of 20%+ and ROA target of 5%+ to be delivered consistently
items.quote: we will continue to do it in a way that we are able to absorb the burn and still deliver profitability which is a 5% ROA and a 20% ROE consistently quarter on quarter

items.statement: AUM at INR 8,001 crores, up 61% YoY and 13% QoQ
items.quote: AUM stood at INR 8,001 crores, up 61% year-on-year and 13% quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Disbursements at INR 3,812 crores, up 37% YoY
items.quote: Disbursement for the quarter were INR 3,812 crore s, up 37% year -on-year.

items.statement: Off-book AUM share increased from 49.7% to 53.6%
items.quote: a rising share of off -book lending, which has gone up from 49.7% to 53.6%

items.statement: LAP AUM at INR 617 crores across 101 branches in 8 states, 7.7% of total AUM
items.quote: LAP business which we started two years back, the AUM stands at INR 617 crores across 101 branches in eight states, about 7.7% of the total AUM.

items.statement: Total income yield fell 249 bps QoQ due to deliberate shift to higher-quality, lower-risk customers and higher off-book share
items.quote: As a share of average AUM, total income fell 249 basis points over the quarter. This drop is very deliberate and is part of a conscious and concerted strategy from our part.

items.statement: Credit cost 6.80% of avg AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Recent vintages (since Dec 2025) performing materially better than a year ago on bounce, collection, early delinquency indicators
items.quote: all the new sourcing that we have done, particularly after December of last year, which is almost 7 -8 months, we are seeing a very much improv ed bounce rate and also the eventual loss expectation that we have.

items.statement: Registered users 74.6M (+33% YoY); served customers 12.25M (+26% YoY)
items.quote: The registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million. We have now served 12.25 million customers, an increase of 26% year-on-year.

items.statement: Capital adequacy in NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% post-IPO; net worth INR 2,245 crores (~4x Mar 2023)
items.quote: Capital adequacy in our NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter. Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crore s, nearly four times its level in March 2023

items.statement: On-book AUM INR 3,716 crores, off-book INR 4,284 crores (46:54 split); 45+ lending partners
items.quote: On-book AUM of INR 3,716 crores and off-book AUM of INR 4,284 crores, a 46 :54 split, supported by more than 45 lending partners.

items.statement: Underwriting model AUC 74% (up from 66% in 2023), separates good/bad customers 2.5x better than bureau score alone
items.quote: Now at an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 74%, up from 66% in 2023, and separating good customers from bad customers about 2.5 times better than a bureau score alone.

items.statement: AI voice agents in early bucket tele-collection recover at >80% of human efficiency (up from 70%)
items.quote: In early bucket tele -collection, our voice agents now recover at more than 80% of human efficiency, up from the 70% we reported earlier.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at INR 1,500-2,000 crores additional spend after INR 1,000 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: Around additional about between INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Total capex plan INR 6,800 crores with INR 3,800 crores spent and INR 3,000 crores balance
items.quote: capex is INR6,800 crores. Out of that, we have spent roughly INR3,800 crores, INR3,000 crores is balance.

items.statement: Carbon Black Phase II commissioned, total capacity now 360,000 MTPA at INR 800 crores outlay
items.quote: we commissioned our Phase II of Carbon Black plant, taking the total capacity to 360,000 -MTPA.

items.statement: Captive power plant increased to 64 megawatts at Bhuj at INR 125 crores outlay
items.quote: we have al so increased our captive power plant to 64 megawatts.

items.statement: OHT segment delivered highest ever quarterly sales volume with 16% YoY growth
items.quote: We delivered 16% sales volume growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: India OHT performed exceptionally well despite high base, gaining market share aided by infra capex
items.quote: India performed exceptionally well in Q1 despite of a high base from last year. Our marketing efforts along with superior product range is helping us gain market share.

items.statement: Americas showing better performance with tariffs settling at 10%, expect growth momentum to sustain
items.quote: In the Americas, with the tariff rate settling at 10% levels, we have seen a better performance led by the U.S.A. With a sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets, we expect growth momentum to sustain.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 20.61% impacted by raw material prices, partially offset by price hikes
items.quote: The stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR703 crores with a margin of 20.61%. The margin was particularly impacted on account of raw material prices due to geopolitical situation globally and its impact on supply chain.

items.statement: Price hike of ~5% taken scattered across Q1, full pass-through expected in Q2
items.quote: So we have taken on a price hike of about 5% scattered across the various parts of the quarter, you will see the full pass-through coming in this quarter.

items.statement: Raw material cost increased ~5%, impacting sales price ~3%, may impact margins ~2% in coming quarter
items.quote: The raw material price has increased by 5% on the cost basis of the raw material. The impact on the sales price is approximately 3%. Out of that, we are expecting it may impact 2% of our margins in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical challenges expected to impact Carbon Black pricing and supply due to increased crude prices
items.quote: Going forward, we expect geopolitical challenges to impact the pricing and supply of Carbon Black on the back of increased crude prices.

items.statement: India volume contribution increased to 40% of overall volumes, marginally impacting margins
items.quote: Further, India's contribution has increased to overall 40% of the volumes, which has impacted the margin slightly.

items.statement: India market share ~18-19%, US ~3-4%, Europe ~7-8%, end-user inventory levels normal
items.quote: So India, market share is around close to 18%, 19%. U.S. is about 3% to 4%. And we are working to improve this. The end user levels of inventories are normal, there is no buildup or there is no shortage at the moment.

items.statement: US revenue share expected to return to historical 15-16% levels from current 11-12%
items.quote: in the U.S.A., we expect the markets to go back to, as you rightly said, 15%, 16%.

items.statement: No pre-buying observed in Europe despite price increases, inventory levels normal
items.quote: No, we don't see any prebuying in the sense the level that -- as I mentioned earlier, the levels are normal. So we don't see that.

items.statement: Applied for US tariff refunds, too early to comment on timing of returns
items.quote: Yes. As all companies have, we have, but it's too early to make comments on when the returns and all are going to come.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 4,690 crores, cash INR 2,965 crores, net debt INR 1,725 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: As on June 30, '26, gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR4,690 crores and INR2,965 crores, respectively. Accord ingly, we have a net debt of approximately INR1,725 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended first interim dividend of INR 4 per equity share
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a first interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: Appointed Ashish Kumar Datta as Carbon Black Business Head effective July 3, 2026 with 36 years experience
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have appointed Mr. Ashish Kumar Datta as Business Head for Carbon Black effective July 3, 2026. Ashish brings al ong with him 36 years of cross-functional leadership experience across the chemicals, coatingsand polymer industry

items.statement: Employee cost increased 18% YoY to INR 153 crores due to Gujarat wage hike, staff increments, and new business hiring
items.quote: I think -it is a permutation combination of 2, 3 things. One is, as you rightly said, the increase in wages in Gujarat -. And apart from this, we have given the increment also to our staff, and we had increased the staff -to support the new business also.

items.statement: OHT segment volume 93,770 metric tons, 16% YoY growth
items.quote: For the quarter, our OHT segment volume stood at 93,770 metric tons, a growth of 16% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone revenue INR 3,409 crores, 24% YoY growth including INR 36 crores realized forex loss
items.quote: Our stand-alone revenue for the quarter stood at INR3,409 crores, registering a growth of 24% year-on-year. This includes realized loss of foreign exchange pertaining to the sales of INR36 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions, vessel/container availability, freight costs, weather challenges in Europe, sketchy monsoon in India are key near-term variables
items.quote: For upcoming quarters, we would like to highlight geopolitical uncertainty with supply chain impacts on both availability of mate rials as well as the costs, availability of vessels, containers and freight costs as well. These, along with weather challenges in Europe and the sketchy monsoon expected in India, are key variables towards near-term performance -.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance ~12% with EBITDA margin ~14% including ~150 bps drag from retail
items.quote: We have given a guidance earlier in the last quarter of about approximately 12% revenue growth with a 14% kind of EBITDA margin with a drop of 150-odd basis points of the retail business.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR100 cr, of which INR40-50 cr for retail expansion
items.value: INR100 cr total, INR40-50 cr retail
items.quote: The capital expenditure that we had envisaged for this year, as indicated earlier, was close to about INR100 crores with about INR40 crores to INR50 crores going into the retail project.

items.statement: Added 3 ZECODE and 2 DEVO stores in Q1 FY27; target ~70 total stores across both brands in FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 3 ZECODE stores and 2 DEVO stores, taking the total store count to 30 and 19, respectively. We pla n to reach approximately total 70 stores across both brands in FY27

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA INR40 cr, margin 8.6%; PAT INR11 cr, margin 2.4%
items.quote: We are pleased to report an EBITDA of INR40 crores for the quarter compared to INR33 crores in the corresponding period of last year, registering year -on-year growth of 22.3%. EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 8.6%.

items.statement: Demand stable in Q1; wedding/occasion consumption moderated due to Maas period; consumers value-conscious
items.quote: Coming to the overall industry, the demand environment remained stable during the quarter, although wedding and occasion-led consumption witnessed some moderation due to the Maas period, which traditionally leads to the postponement of discretionary purchases.

items.statement: Input cost inflation persists; some price pass-through done in Q1, more may follow if raw materials stay high
items.quote: Some pass on was done in the first quarter. If raw materials remain high and margins start getting shrunk, then some might continue to be passed on, which is the general standard that we follow.

items.statement: Retail revenue Q1 FY27 ~INR30 cr; full-year retail revenue target ~INR160 cr (vs ~INR80 cr last year)
items.quote: From the retail business, in this quarter, we've generated about close to INR30 crores of revenue. As indicated earlier as well, the full year expectation is about INR160 crores.

items.statement: Inventory built for festive/wedding season; March-to-March working capital days similar to last year; retail adds incremental inventory
items.quote: If you look at the March number, then in the number of days, similar to that as per last year. Of course, because of the increase of retail business, there is an additional inventory that we have to put out that adds on to the balance sheet.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.24 as of 30 June 2026; positive free cash flow expected in FY27
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity as on 30th June '26 stood at 0.24.

items.statement: NCLT approved bonus issue of cumulative non-convertible redeemable preference shares; effective 30 July 2026; record date 22 Aug 2026
items.quote: As a significant corporate development during the quarter, the scheme for issuing cumulative nonconvertible redeemable preference shares by way of bonus to the equity shareholders of the company has been approved by the NCLT, Mumbai vide its order 21st July 2026.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 total income INR466 cr (+16.4% YoY); revenue mix: Fabrics 71%, Garments 19%, Yarn & Others 10%
items.quote: Our total income for Q1 FY27 stood at INR466 crores as compared to INR400 crores in the Q1 FY26, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 16.4%.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA drag budgeted at ~150 bps annually; confident to stay within that range
items.quote: We have already given an indication of an annual drop in EBITDA by about 150 basis points. We hope to be well within that budget.

items.statement: Land development charges INR24.6 cr moved from inventory to P&L per accounting standards; net effect nil; no revenue booked yet on residential project
items.quote: This is the land development charges, which as per the standard, we'll have to route it through the profit and loss account. So it is included in the other income and the same manner, it was included in the inventory also. The net effect is nil.

items.statement: Real estate project construction to start in Q2 FY27; expected completion in 24 months
items.quote: In this quarter, we expect to start construction, and we expect 24 months for this project to be completed.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance for carbon black maintained at INR16,500-17,000, implying 14-15% improvement over FY26 average
items.quote: On a full year basis, if you refer to our last quarter's investor call, we had given a guidance of 14% to 15% improvement over our FY26 average EBITDA. With which will be somewhere around, say, INR16,500, INR17,000 per ton. So we stick to that.

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY27 around INR300 crores plus/minus INR50 crores, mostly maintenance and productivity enhancement
items.quote: Capex outlook this year, we are largely through with our ground field expansion. Small capex here and there, which is more like maintenance capex plus some new developments for productivity enhancement, yield improvement, etc.. My sense is that it should be somewhere around INR300 crores, maybe plus-minus INR50-odd crores.

items.statement: Cost optimization program targeting INR200-250 crores savings over next 4-6 quarters still on track
items.quote: And we believe that the target we had identified earlier of INR200 crores to INR250 crores of savings over the next 4 to 6 quarters still holds, and we look forward to starting to deliver that in our results.

items.statement: Domestic carbon black volumes grew 15% YoY to 102,985 tons in Q1 FY27, supported by steady demand and some customer inventory building
items.quote: Domestic sales were a bright spot this quarter with steady demand across key segments driving strong growth. Domestic volumes were also supported by an element of inventory building by our customers in the last quarter.

items.statement: Indian tire industry estimated to grow high single-digit over FY27-29, supported by aging fleet, premiumization and EV penetration
items.quote: Closer home, Indian tire sector is on a healthy growth path after a solid 7% to 8% this fiscal, industry estimates for growth is in a similar high single-digit range over FY '27 to '29, supported by a growing aging vehicle fleet, premiumization and rising EV penetration.

items.statement: Aquapharm home care and water solutions volumes decreased marginally YoY, application-specific solutions grew 10% YoY, oil and gas down 35% YoY but up 50% sequentially
items.quote: During this quarter, home care and water solutions sales volume decreased marginally on a year-over-year basis, whereas application-specific solutions posted a double-digit growth of 10%. Oil and gas segment, while saw 35% year-over-year decrease, sequentially, the segment reported a strong growth of 50%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA grew 23% YoY to INR400 crores; carbon black EBITDA per ton at INR22,900 including inventory gains
items.quote: For the quarter, we did about INR22,900 a ton.

items.statement: Low-cost inventory benefit of ~INR70 crores in Q1, estimated INR40-50 crores reversal in Q2
items.quote: My estimation is about INR40 crores to INR50 crores, we might have to give away because of the change in the inventory position.

items.statement: Power business EBIT jumped due to realization increase from INR3.66 to INR5.39 per unit (~50% jump)
items.quote: Last quarter our realization was INR3.66, which has jumped to INR5.39. It's almost 50% jump in power realization and consequent the increase in the EBIT.

items.statement: Green chelates order booking running ahead of current capacity; new facility under discussion; qualified with P&G, Reckitt, Henkel
items.quote: On green chelates, order booking is running ahead of our current capacity, and we are now getting qualified with key accounts like P&G, Reckitt and Henkel. To build further on this shift towards green chelates, we are in discussion around a new facility.

items.statement: New annual contracts for carbon black exports being negotiated; expect significant growth in U.S. followed by EU volumes
items.quote: Going forward, we expect a significant growth as new annual contracts are getting deliberated and negotiated as we move forward. We are in a very good position to compete against the other countries in U.S., so we should see a significant growth in U.S. followed by EU as well.

items.statement: 20,000 MTPA specialty black line at Mundra commissioned in Q1 FY27; total installed carbon black capacity now 900,000 MTPA
items.quote: The 20,000 MTPA specialty black line in Mundra was commissioned in Q1 FY27. With this, our total installed carbon black capacity now stands at 900,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Nanovace pilot plant at Palej received consent to operate; individual machine trials started; customer sampling to begin in August
items.quote: Our Nanovace pilot plant in Palej is in progress, and we have received the consent to operate for R&D and customer sampling. At the individual machine level, we have already started trials, and we are in readiness to start sampling in the coming weeks of August.

items.statement: 1,000 MTPA super-conductive specialty black facility at Palej commissioned; market development started for battery, conductive polymers, electronics
items.quote: To address growing demand from battery semiconductors and advanced polymer applications, we have set up a 1,000 metric ton per annum super-conductive specialty black facility in Palej and have commenced market development activities across battery, conductive polymers and electronic applications.

items.statement: Coal tar distillation project business plan being finalized; OEM talks ongoing; capex approval expected this quarter
items.quote: We are progressing very well on the definition of the project for the coal tar distillation. The business plan is being checked, and we are also in talks with the OEM suppliers of equipment, etc.. By this quarter, we should be looking at getting an approval -- on all the capexes that are required as we refine the business model.

items.statement: Andhra greenfield capex spend mainly in FY28; FY27 strategic capex ~INR100 crores, rest maintenance/efficiency
items.quote: So greenfield expense this year will be limited because the Andhra facility, while we are getting the licenses, etc, in place, it will be -- the expense will actually happen more in the next year rather than this year. Most of the capex spend this year will be mostly efficiency capex. As I mentioned earlier, we are looking at cost efficiency program, and to ensure that those get through, we are sp

items.statement: Brent crude averaged USD 97/barrel in Q1 FY27 vs USD 78 in Q4 FY26; CBFS costs moved with crude; higher inward freight raised raw material bill
items.quote: Brent crude averaged USD 97 per barrel during the quarter compared to USD 78 per barrel in Q4 FY26, largely on account of the escalation of the West Asia conflict. CBFS costs moved in line with crude and together with higher inward freight, this raised our raw material bill during the quarter.

items.statement: CBO-CBFS price difference remains ~USD 150/ton with CBO higher; both moved up during quarter
items.quote: The difference continues to be close to USD 150-odd, CBO being higher. So that equation is still holding good.

items.statement: Logistics costs remain elevated and erratic due to Middle East crisis; surcharges recovered from most customers but not 100%
items.quote: It continues to be erratic. It's a reflection of how the Middle East crisis keeps ebbing and flowing. And -- so we are quite agile in looking for capacities as well as prices. So we'll just need to be agile and nimble on this one. We are still seeing high prices both for inbound as well as outbound logistics for this quarter.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black volumes grew 23% YoY to 19,748 tons in Q1 FY27; rich product mix and increasing customer acceptance
items.quote: Specialty sales grew a strong 23% year-on-year to 19,748 tons.

items.statement: Aquapharm launching new commercial phosphonate products qualified for sale in next 3 quarters; green chelates capacity oversubscribed
items.quote: On the phosphonates portfolio, we are actively launching commercial products right now. They have been qualified, and we are looking towards selling them in next 3 quarters. That will bring growth -- revenue growth and margin growth both on the phosphonates side.

items.statement: ~70% of specialty carbon black volumes exported to strategic customers; ensured no supply disruption during logistics crisis
items.quote: On specialty, around 70% of our volumes are sold in international market. Most of our customers are strategic customers, and like Nilesh mentioned in his speech, we ensured that none of our strategic customers suffered because of supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: Aquapharm expanding U.S. oil & gas footprint with New Mexico approval; rebuilding in Venezuela and Mexico; Europe expansion in pipeline
items.quote: We have attained approvals to operate in New Mexico or sell in New Mexico. So that is progressing in expanding geographies in U.S. In Latin America, we are putting a lot of effort in countries like Venezuela, where there is a lot of rebuild happening, and trying to reestablish ourselves in Mexico.

items.statement: India's trade deals (US, EU, UK, EFTA, Oman, NZ) create preferential access; U.S. tariffs on Indian carbon black materially lower than China/Russia; Russian supply contracting due to refinery strikes
items.quote: India's trade architecture has strengthened remarkably over the past several quarters. The India-U.S. trade deal discussion in February this year has brought tariffs on Indian exports down sharply from the peak levels seen last year. And subsequent negotiations have secured for India one of the most favorable tariff years among major exporting nations.

items.statement: India-EU FTA concluded Jan 2026 progressing through ratification; expected to eliminate 4.5% EU import duty on Indian tires
items.quote: The India-EU FTA concluded in January 2026 is progressing through ratification and opens up duty-free access to European markets. It's also expected to eliminate 4.5% EU import duty on Indian tires, enhancing the competitiveness of the Indian tire manufacturers in an important export market and in turn supporting domestic carbon black demand.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 export volumes: Europe ~16,000 tons, USA ~4,800 tons; deliberate reallocation to domestic spot market for better margins
items.quote: In Europe, we did around 16,000 tons of volume, and U.S.A. we did about close to 4,800 tons.

items.statement: Tariff refund application filed for INR40-45 crores (PCBL + Aquapharm); expected receipt in 2-4 weeks
items.quote: Between Aquapharm and PCBL, the amount would be somewhere between INR40 crores to INR45-odd crores. We have already made application, and we are tracking it very closely. My own sense is maybe in next 2 to 4 weeks' time, we should be receiving that refund.

items.statement: Rohit Narang appointed CEO of Aquapharm; 25+ years global leadership experience including Eastman Chemicals P&L and M&A
items.quote: I'd like to take this moment to introduce Mr. Rohit Narang as the new CEO of Aquapharm Chemicals, something I mentioned in the last call. Rohit brings over 25 years of global leadership experience across general management, strategy and M&A. His last stint was with Eastman Chemicals, where he led global P&Ls across large-scale specialty portfolios and spearheaded multi-billion dollar M&A transacti

items.statement: Near-term volumes may be temporarily affected in Q2 due to cautious customer procurement; viewed as timing not demand effect
items.quote: In the very near-term, the operating environment remains dynamic and some customers have adopted a more cautious procurement approach than we could have temporarily -- that will probably have a temporary effect on volumes in Q2. We see this as a timing effect, not a demand effect and therefore, remain constructive on the second half of FY27.

items.statement: Targeting 20% consolidated EBITDA margin long-term; no quarterly or FY27 guidance given
items.quote: We are not giving any guidance for the second quarter or the year as a whole. Of course, on a targeted level, we are looking at 20% EBITDA margin. That's our sta ted target for a very long term, right

items.statement: Barium segment EBITDA margin target 25% sustained; one-time INR8 crore retrospective baryte price adjustment in prior quarter
items.quote: We believe the EBITDA margins will continue to remain at 25% moving forward.

items.statement: Strontium business EBITDA positive but not at target; expect to reach target EBITDA levels by end of FY27
items.quote: Strontium, again, currently, we have achieved the volumes, but not the targeted EBITDA. So we remain EBITDA positive at the mom ent. Let me put it that way. So we need to ramp up volume, improve the yields and so on. I mean we remain positive in strontium probably by end of this year, we'll be at those EBITDA levels, given the traction from the customers

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin currently 44-45%; targeting 50% by end of FY27 with chrome ore integration and product mix improvement
items.quote: Currently, our gross margins, we are at 44%, 45%. Ideally, we will be getting to 50% -- towards the end of this year. That will definitely get us to what we are targeting of 20% EBITDA, let me put it that way.

items.statement: Chromium higher value-added derivatives (Chromic Acid, Chrome Oxide Green) now ~50% of sales vs 40% in FY26
items.quote: the higher value -added derivatives contributed to nearly 50% of our sales in the quarter gone by as comp ared to, say, 40% in FY26 as a

items.statement: Strategic shift in chromium mix toward higher value-added derivatives; reducing Basic Chrome Sulphate volumes sequentially
items.quote: And our focus will remain to be on Chrome Oxide mainly going into chrome metal, refractory segments as well a s Chromic Acid going into functional plating. And once we move in the direction which we are, there will be a lot more -- there will be improvement in the gross margin

items.statement: Long-term supply agreement for Chrome Oxide Green with European client; binding take-or-pay with formula-driven pricing for 10 years
items.quote: We are looking at a certain fixed volumes for the over next 10 years, specifically for our Chrome Oxide Green product. And this supply will be a binding supply agreement linked to an exchange plus the incidentals like the logistics cost and movement -- whereas in the current environment, the products, what we do is more on a quarterly like on a spot basis, what our peers are doing, whereas this on

items.statement: Solar capacity expansion from 5 MW to 20 MW; capex INR5-6 crores, rest under SPV model with fixed long-term pricing
items.quote: The total capex outlay for solar will be close to about INR5 crores to INR6 crores, and the rest will be under the SPV model, wherein we will be able to buy the solar at a fixed price on the longer term.

items.statement: Strontium capacity ~10,000 tonnes; currently 50% utilization, targeting 65-75% by end of FY27
items.quote: We have a capacity of close to about 10,000 tonnes in strontium business. We are currently operating at 50% utilization over there. And we would like to end the year at close to about 65% to 75% capacity utilization.

items.statement: South Africa operations restart progressing; production expected to start end of current month, volumes from H2 FY27
items.quote: We are expecting the production to start anytime towards end of this month. With that being said, volumes will start coming from the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Barium demand robust; expect 15-20% growth in barium division this year
items.quote: Things we remain positive, and we expect it to grow 15%, 20% this year in the barium division as well.

items.statement: Logistics cost 9-10% of revenue in Q1 FY27; could rise to 20%+ in Q2 FY27 due to Red Sea crisis; partially passable to customers
items.quote: For the quarter gone by, it's abou t 9% to 10% is the logistics cost, but it is going to change quite a bit for this quarter. It could be upwards of 20%, depending on

items.statement: EU anti-dumping duty on Chinese barium carbonate adding 4-5% margin benefit; benefit already captured in numbers
items.quote: The benefit already captured in the numbers, let me put it that way. So we have -- I mean it has added 4%, 5% margin on top of the regular pricing what we see in other markets. And that we believe will continue.

items.statement: Sulphur byproduct value up 300-400% in recent months, improving barium blended realizations
items.quote: One of the byproducts, which is coming sulphur, even the product value has gone up over 300%, 400% in the last few months. So the blended realizations have improved and will continue to improve.

items.statement: Total debt INR527 crores as of March 31, 2025 (debt-to-equity 0.49); quarterly debt figures not disclosed
items.quote: As per the balance sheet that we have reported ending 31st March, the total debt in our books is about INR527 crores. That includes our long-term borrowings and short-term borrowings, which is at a debt-to-equity level, so 0.49.

items.statement: Effective tax rate 28.05% in Q1 FY27; FY26 average 27.17%, in line with tax regime
items.quote: The tax rate in this quarter was 28%, precisely about 28.05%. So on an average throughout the year last year, FY27, the tax rate was 27.17%, which is in line with our tax regime that we follow.

items.statement: Transfer pricing regulations govern South Africa-India chrome ore transfers; margins split between entities per arm's length pricing
items.quote: we have to follow the transfer pricing mechanism, which is already in place. And we have to look at that aspect before deciding on the price at which the transfer will happen because we cannot hav e too much of margin sitting in either of these countries

items.statement: DMSO commercial production expected next financial year; capex INR200+ crores, first organic product venture
items.quote: We do. I think it's as per the plan. I mean, the construction as well as implementation of the equipment is progressing. So we remain positive that we'll be able to start commercia l production by next financial year

items.statement: Chrome metal project decision imminent; linked to strategic long-term supply partnership; announcement expected soon
items.quote: Chrome metal, very soon we'll be -- I think we've been going back and forth with this for quite some time, but we decided to take a call now. I think you'll receive an announcement very soon, which will be a little strategic in nature, which is linked to a long-term supply and a strategic business partnership moving forward.

items.statement: Expect ECU prices to remain in current range or higher; chlorine price currently minus INR 7,000 to minus INR 8,000
items.quote: we do expect the prices; current ECU is in the range of just below INR30,000. So, we expect it to be in this range or higher. As for the chlorine price, currently it is in the minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000 range.

items.statement: Effective cash tax outgo expected at 19% for at least next five years due to MAT credit utilization
items.quote: effectively for, you know, let's say anywhere between 5 to 10 years, at least 5 I can see in the foreseeable future, my effective tax rate will be 19% or tax outgo will be 19%.

items.statement: Net debt expected to remain at similar levels by end of FY27 with potential reduction of around INR 200 crore
items.quote: It should be around the similar levels, not a significant reduction because we do have capex of around INR1,000 crore this year. And yes, there will be some reduction by about INR200-odd crore probably

items.statement: Debt to EBITDA will not breach 1.5x as a financial discipline guardrail
items.quote: what we ensure, Subhankar, is that our debt to EBITDA does not breach 1.5. So we are more governed by that so that the financials remain healthy

items.statement: Capex of around INR 1,000 crore planned for FY27
items.quote: It should be around the similar levels, not a significant reduction because we do have capex of around INR1,000 crore this year.

items.statement: Two acquisitions completed in FY26 adding up to close to INR 450 crore
items.quote: over this period, we have done two acquisitions adding up to close to about INR450 crore.

items.statement: Aluminum chloride and calcium chloride projects at Bharuch in final pre-commissioning; commercial production expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our projects in aluminum chloride and calcium chloride at Bharuch are in the final stages of pre-commissioning, and commercial production is expected to commence during Q2

items.statement: 68 MW peak hybrid renewable power project at Kota under commissioning with average 25 MW injection in July
items.quote: The 68-megawatt peak hybrid renewable power project at Kota is currently under commissioning with average power injection of 25 megawatts for the month of July.

items.statement: Peak renewable energy capacity across Bharuch and Kota expected to reach around 176 MW upon commissioning of Serentica agreement
items.quote: Upon commissioning, our peak renewable energy capacity across Bharuch and Kota is expected to increase to around 176 megawatts

items.statement: Chemicals capacity utilization at 82% in Q1 FY27; will improve as downstream projects commission
items.quote: Capacity utilization during the quarter stood at 82%. This will improve further as our downstream projects get commissioned.

items.statement: Hydrogen peroxide plant operating at around 85% capacity utilization
items.quote: The plant has delivered a healthy operating performance with capacity utilization at around 85%.

items.statement: Epichlorohydrin and epoxy plants operating at around 70% capacity utilization each
items.quote: Our epichlorohydrin and epoxy plants are currently operating at around 70% capacity utilization each

items.statement: Vinyl capacity utilization at 100% in Q1 FY27 versus 98% last year
items.quote: Capacity utilization stood at 100% for Q1 FY27 versus 98% last year.

items.statement: Grain-based ethanol capacity defined at up to 260 KLD; will optimize based on margins
items.quote: we have a defined capacity for grain, right, where we can go up to 260 KLD for grain. So we will optimize wherever we get better margins

items.statement: Chemicals PBDIT rose 24% to INR 274 crore aided by higher volumes and better realizations in advanced materials, partially offset by elevated input costs
items.quote: On profitability, PBDIT rose by 24% to INR274 crore, aided by higher volumes and better realizations in the advanced materials, though partially offset by elevated input costs.

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT improved 88% to INR 43 crore driven by higher realizations, partially offset by elevated input costs
items.quote: PBDIT improved 88% to INR43 crore, driven by higher realizations, partially offset by elevated input costs.

items.statement: Sugar and Ethanol PBDIT at INR 22 crore vs negative INR 7 crore last year, largely due to one-time provision for retrospective ethanol duty of ~INR 36 crore last year
items.quote: PBDIT came in at INR22 crore against negative INR7 crore last year, largely due to a one-time provision for retrospective ethanol duty of approximately INR36 crore last year.

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT grew 13% to INR 40 crore; higher volumes partially offset by product mix change and higher fixed expenses for new platforms and marketing
items.quote: On profitability, PBDIT for the quarter grew 13% year-on-year to INR40 crore. The contribution from higher volumes was partially offset by a change in product mix along with higher fixed expenses towards setting up new revenue platforms and elevated marketing expense.

items.statement: Shriram Farm Solutions PBDIT higher by 22% at INR 30 crore led by improved margins across verticals
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was higher by 22% at INR30 crore, led by improved margins across verticals.

items.statement: Fertilizer PBDIT at INR 23 crore vs INR 38 crore last year; year-ago quarter had INR 24 crore one-time retention price gain
items.quote: PBDIT stood at INR23 crore versus INR38 crore last year, reflecting better margins from improved energy efficiency, though the year-ago quarter had carried a INR24 crore one-time retention price gain.

items.statement: Bioseed PBDIT negative INR 9 crore vs positive INR 42 crore last year due to lower volumes in corn and paddy and lower margins in cotton
items.quote: PBDIT for Q1 FY27 came in at a negative INR9 crore as against a positive INR42 crore last year, on account of lower volume in corn and paddy, along with lower margins in cotton.

items.statement: Domestic caustic soda market healthy supported by steady demand from alumina, soaps, detergents, and textiles
items.quote: The domestic caustic soda market remained healthy, supported by steady demand from alumina, soaps and detergents, and textile industries.

items.statement: PVC demand subdued due to labor shortages, heatwave, and cautious buying; expected to remain soft in Q2 FY27 with monsoon onset
items.quote: On the demand side, offtake remained subdued through the quarter, weighed down by labor shortages, heatwave conditions, and cautious buying sentiment. With the onset of the monsoon, demand is expected to remain soft in Q2 financial year '27.

items.statement: SFS business impacted by delayed and deficient Southwest monsoon with rainfall significantly below normal across key agriculture regions
items.quote: Performance was impacted by the delayed and deficient onset of the Southwest monsoon, with rainfall remaining significantly below normal across several key agriculture regions

items.statement: Bioseed Kharif season impacted by 15-20% all-India sowing acreage shortfall due to delayed monsoon; much higher in some markets
items.quote: The current season has also marked by delayed monsoon, resulting in an overall shortfall of 15% to 20% sowing acreage in an all-India basis and much higher in some of its markets.

items.statement: ECU prices firmed up by 7% year-on-year in Q1 FY27
items.quote: While caustic soda volumes held steady, realizations improved with ECU prices firming up by 7%.

items.statement: PVC volumes fell 25% year-on-year despite prices rising 22%
items.quote: Revenue moderated 10% versus last year as PVC volumes fell 25% year-on-year, despite prices rising 22%.

items.statement: Sugar realizations improved 2% year-on-year; ethanol prices 4% lower due to sales mix change
items.quote: Domestic sugar volumes fell 8% on lower offtake, even as realizations improved by 2%. Ethanol volumes were flat, while prices were 4% lower, a result of change in sales mix.

items.statement: Fertilizer realizations up 19% year-on-year while volumes stayed flat
items.quote: The Fertilizer revenues for Q1 FY27 rose 11% year-on-year with realizations up 19%, while volumes stayed flat.

items.statement: Sharp increase in natural gas prices following West Asia supply disruptions impacting Urea business
items.quote: The Urea business witnessed a sharp increase in natural gas prices following supply disruptions arising from West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Government granted temporary waiver of basic customs duty on PVC; later reinstated duty and notified minimum import price of US$766/MT on suspension grade PVC for six months
items.quote: Additionally, DGFT has notified minimum import price of US$766 dollar per metric ton on suspension grade PVC for six months.

items.statement: Domestic and leisure demand strong; international business ex-crew flat YoY due to West Asia conflict; air traffic flat Apr-Jun.
items.quote: On the other hand, domestic and leisure witnessed strong demand driven by strength of domestic industry, rising affluence, changing consumer preferences, and growing discretionary spend.

items.statement: Business foreign tourist arrivals will take 60 days to normalize once West Asia conflict nears resolution.
items.quote: As we had mentioned on previous earnings call as well, business foreign tourist arrivals will take 60 days to normalize once the West Asia conflict nears resolution.

items.statement: Leisure portfolio delivered 19% RevPAR growth with healthy mix of occupancy and ADR increase.
items.quote: Leisure portfolio delivered a strong 19% RevPAR growth with a healthy mix of occupancy and ADR increase.

items.statement: Overall RevPAR increased 6.5% YoY, largely driven by 8.5% YoY growth in average daily rates.
items.quote: RevPAR increased by 6.5% year -on-year, largely driven by an 8.5% year -on-year growth in average daily rates.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin improved 231 bps to 46.7% YoY.
items.quote: Excluding the residential business, our revenue grew by 10% year-on-year to INR5,140 million with an EBITDA of INR2,400 million, up 15% year-on-year. Importantly, EBITDA margin improved by 231 bps to 46.7%.

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin improved 92 bps to 42.6% on resilient pricing and efficiency measures.
items.quote: Hospitality revenue grew by 9%, while EBITDA stood at INR1,784 million, up 11% year -on-year, reflecting 92 bps improvement in EBITDA margin on the back of resilient pricing dynamics and efficiency measures.

items.statement: Commercial real estate EBITDA margin expanded 193 bps to 85% YoY.
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR735 million, up 21% year -on-year, with an EBITDA margin of 85%, up 193 bps versus Quarter 1 FY2026.

items.statement: Signed LOI for additional 66,000 sq ft at Bangalore, taking overall CRE occupancy to 91%; Jun'26 rental run rate INR290M/month.
items.quote: During the quarter, we signed an LOI for an additional 66,000 square foot at Bangalore, taking the overall occupancy level to 91%. Our Jun'26 run rate for rentals reached INR290 million per month, slightly higher than Mar'26.

items.statement: Expect monthly CRE rentals to scale up to INR300-320M during FY27; CIGNUS II commissioning to drive step-change growth FY28 onwards.
items.quote: We expect monthly rentals to scale up to INR 300 - 320 million during FY2027. Commissioning of CIGNUS II at Powai will also lead to a step-change in growth FY2028 onwards.

items.statement: Planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY27 to FY29 across hospitality and CRE, largely funded through internal accruals.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have outlined a planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY27 to FY29 across our hospitality and commercial real estate portfolio. This includes committed investments and importantly is expected to be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: CIGNUS II Powai on track for FY27 end substantial completion; Taj Delhi Airport minimum 70 rooms launch Q4 FY27, balance phased within Q1 FY28.
items.quote: Work is in full swing at CIGNUS II Powai, and we are on track for FY27 end substantial completion. We expect to launch a minimum of 70 rooms at Taj project at Delhi International Airport in Q4FY27, with balance inventory to be launched in phased manner thereafter, but within the first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Mindspace excavation begun at Hyderabad and Airoli; evaluating expansion potential at Udaipur resort.
items.quote: Mindspace has begun excavation at Hyderabad and Airoli. Both these projects are well on track. We are evaluating expansion potential at Udaipur resort, and we shall soon be able to give you the details for the same.

items.statement: Vashi property renovation complete, rebranding announcement in coming weeks; Powai porch and Westin Banquet connectivity by end of Q2 FY27.
items.quote: The good news here is that our Vashi property is now completely ready, and we shall be able to announce the rebranding in the coming few weeks. Also, the work at Powai is in full swing, and our porch as well as the connectivity to the Westin Banquet shall be in place by the end of this quarter.

items.statement: South Goa hotel construction to start by end of Q2 FY27 post monsoon; G+1 structure expected to finish faster than typical 200-room hotel.
items.quote: We still hope to start construction by the end of this quarter, essentially once the rainy season is behind us. With that in mind, we know that we can build fast. It's a G+1 structure, and therefore, we would hope to finish this sooner than what a usual 200-room hotel would look like.

items.statement: Average cost of finance declined marginally to 7.4% as of Jun'26 vs 7.5% as of Mar'26.
items.quote: The average cost of finance declined marginally to 7.4% as of June '26 versus 7.5% as of March '26, indicating strength of our treasury practices, leverage mix, ca sh flows, and overall balance sheet strength.

items.statement: Liquidity position comfortable around INR4 billion as of Jun'26.
items.quote: We continue to maintain a comfortable liquidity position around INR4 billion as of June '26.

items.statement: Leisure portfolio target remains 20% of overall portfolio; no strategy change despite strong quarterly performance.
items.quote: As we are in a very long -gestation business, and changing it because of a quarter's performance or two-quarter performance even is not the best strategy. So, we continue to work on the same strategy as we have always had, 20% of our portfolio should be leisur e, and we'll stay in that

items.statement: Resort occupancy currently ~51%, trending towards stabilized 60-65% range.
items.quote: If we look at our resort occupancy for this quarter, it was about 51%, and we expect that to continue to improve and slide upwards.

items.statement: Deloitte contract at Westin Hyderabad Hitec renewed for 1 year; rental growth and extension to be reviewed at fiscal year-end.
items.quote: We have actually renewed it for 1 more year. So it' s been a learning curve for both us and Deloitte, and Deloitte has been monitoring the occupancy on that.

items.statement: Commissions on GDS/OTA channels at bottom end of market; room margins at top end of industry.
items.quote: So the first thing is on the commission side, and with having tied up with really large chains like Marriott or Accor and so on and so forth, we are very confident that the commissions that we pay on any of the channels is at the bottom end of the market, and we are at the lowest end.

items.statement: Supply in MMR absorbed, no major new supply expected in next 1-2 years; market expected to grow back.
items.quote: I can tell you that in general, the supply seems to have been absorbed, and there is no major supply that's coming through at least in the next year or two. So, we do expect that market to sort of now start to grow back again

items.statement: Geopolitical situation (West Asia conflict) makes forecasting difficult; business monitored day-to-day, no guidance given for current quarter.
items.quote: Overall, this quarter, it would be remiss of me to give you any sort of guidance, because we ar e ourselves monitoring the situation on a day-to-day basis.

items.statement: MMR share in hospitality revenue for Q1 FY27 close to 43%.
items.quote: I think it's close to 43%.

items.statement: Achieved 8th rank among mid-sized workplaces by Great Places to Work; focused on attracting and retaining talent.
items.quote: Finally, I am delighted to share that we have achieved 8th rank among mid-sized workplaces by Great Places to Work. This is an important milestone, as we are focused on attracting and retaining best talent in the industry by providing them inclusive growth.

items.statement: EBO same-store sales growth turned positive at 0.6% in Q1 FY27, first positive in several quarters
items.quote: Same-store sales growth for our EBO channel turned positive this quarter at 0.6% and same cluster sales growth was at 1.2%.

items.statement: Larger stores (>700 sq ft) delivered SSSG of 2.5% to 3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: That was the proof in the putting for a, yes so the SSSG growth for 700-plus square feet for quarter 1 was in the range of 2.5% to 3%.

items.statement: Closed 66 stores in Q1 FY27, reducing total retail space by 7,000 sq ft; consolidation to continue through FY27
items.quote: Despite the quarter, during the quarter, we closed 66 stores in the catchments where we already have or we are going to be opening a larger format store nearby. As a result, our total retail space reduced by 7,000 square feet in this quarter, even as we continue to add larger stores elsewhere in the network.

items.statement: Target net retail space addition of 8% to 10% on a year-through basis in FY27
items.quote: From a square feet deployed in the business on a year through basis, Sameer, we should be at around, we should add about 8% to 10% of square feet space.

items.statement: Plan to scale daily wear concept stores to 25-30 by end of FY27
items.quote: We remain committed to our target of scaling our daily wear stores to about 25 stores to 30 stores by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Plan to add 10-12 genuinely new product formats in FY27 targeting younger customers
items.quote: Over Go Fashion ( FY27, we plan to add 10 to 12 new refreshing products for our customers, not just like extension, but genuinely new format that will open up new purchase occasions and consumer cohorts

items.statement: Advertising spend at 2.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27; expected to remain 2-3% for full FY27
items.quote: Our advertising spend as a percentage of revenue stood at 2.3% for Q1 FY27, and we expect it to remain in the same range between 2% and 3% in FY27.

items.statement: Inflated RM prices will impact gross margins in coming quarters; difficult to quantify due to blended inventory
items.quote: But having said that, these inflated RM prices would impact the gross margins in the coming quarter. It's difficult to quantify how much it will impact because we are also having older inventory in the system, we are also adding new inventory in the system.

items.statement: Daily wear concept stores generating ~INR1,000 sales per sq ft per month; 12-13 of 15 stores profitable
items.value: INR1,000 per sq ft per month
items.quote: Currently, based on the size, the stores deployed, we are generating about INR1,000 of sales per square feet per month. And all the stores, I would say, out of the 15 stores operational today, 12 stores to 13 stores are already profitable and doing well.

items.statement: Daily wear store payback period 15-20 months; inventory turns 45-60 days on sales
items.quote: Payback period could range in that range of 15 months to 20 months will be the payback period. The inventory turns would be about, inventory in larger stores would be around, if I'm not wrong, about 45 days to 60 days on sales.

items.statement: LFS channel grew 2% YoY to INR50 crores in Q1 FY27, signaling recovery after FY26 disruptions
items.quote: Our LFS channel grew 2% on a year-on-year basis to INR50 crores, a clear signal of returning to some sort of normalcy after a difficult FY26 that included operational disruptions with a key LFS partner.

items.statement: Working capital days at 139 with inventory days at 100 in Q1 FY27; target 90-100 inventory days by year-end
items.quote: Our working capital days stood at 139 days with inventory days at 100 days. We believe there is room to optimize this further by a few more days, which will contribute to a strong balance sheet and support long-term sustainable growth.

items.statement: Capex for store expansion to be funded entirely through internal operating cash flows
items.quote: Yes, yes. We feel our operating cash flow will be strong enough to take care of all the capex.

items.statement: Full price sales at 94% and average selling price ~INR863 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Full price sales for the quarter stood at a strong 94% and our average selling price came to about INR863.

items.statement: Footfalls increased 1-1.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 at EBO level
items.quote: We would have maybe seen a 1%, 1.5% increase in footfalls on an overall basis compared to last year Q1. And this I'm talking from an EBO level.

items.statement: Evaluating entry into lingerie/innerwear as part of daily wear concept; no timeline yet
items.quote: See, definitely, it is there in one of our contention list because lingerie and ladies innerwear is a very important part of our everyday wear concept of women's what we have just launched, right, our daily wear product, daily wear concept. So we are evaluating it.

items.statement: Management cautious on SSSG sustainability; 0.6% may be one-quarter trend due to favorable base, store migration, or demand
items.quote: We are very conscious that one quarter does not make a trend, and we intend to stay disciplined and measured as we build on this momentum through the rest of the year. But we are encouraged by the direction and we remain confident that in the underlying strength of the business.

items.statement: Onboarded Shraddha Kapoor as brand ambassador from July to strengthen brand resilience and reach younger audience
items.quote: We have onboarded Shraddha Kapoor as our brand ambassador from July. This is intended to strengthen the brand resilience and bring us to a wider younger audience.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue flat YoY at INR223 crores; GP margin 62.9%; EBITDA before exceptionals INR67.4 crores (2% degrowth); PAT INR16 crores
