items.quote: Revenue stood at INR223 crores, flat year-on-year. Gross profit stood at INR140 crores with a GP margin of 62.9%. EBITDA before exceptional expense stood at INR67 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 30.3%. PAT stood at INR16 crores.

items.statement: Exceptional expense of INR6.5 crores in Q1 FY27 from write-off of capex on closed stores
items.quote: I want to flag one specific item in the P&L this quarter, an exceptional expense of INR6.5 crores relating to the write-off of capital expenditure on account of the store closures we did during the quarter.

items.statement: Inventory at end of Q1 FY27 was INR245 crores including raw materials
items.quote: Inventory number at the end of Q1, I'll just tell you. Just give me one second. It is INR245 crores including RM, it is INR245 crores.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents INR202 crores as of 30 June 2026
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR202 crores as on 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Over next five years, aim to significantly expand footprint with potential to double square feet deployed
items.quote: Over the next five years, we aim to significantly expand our footprint with potential to double the square feet deployed in the business.

items.statement: Store closure pace in FY27 will be much lower than recent quarters; exact number depends on large store opportunities
items.quote: It will definitely be a much lower number. But to give a number of stores guidance is very tough for me because it's directly linked with what large store opportunity we get during the year.

items.statement: ROCE and ROE excluding Ind AS impact at 10.8% and 7.9% respectively in Q1 FY27
items.quote: ROCE and ROE excluding Ind AS impact stood at 10.8% and 7.9%, respectively.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Insurance revenue growth expected to reach 15-16% through the year and increase further in FY28
items.quote: So, we will see a 15 -16% growth going forward throughout the year. It will keep on increasing in FY28 as well.

items.statement: Expense ratio improvement target of 30-40 basis points annually from technology and digitization investments
items.quote: the investment that we are doing in tech and digitization, the focus on efficiency and productivity, will ensure that 30 -40 basis points improvement in the expense ratio is something which we'll get consistently over the years

items.statement: Targeting mid- to high-teen ROE on a steady-state basis
items.quote: On a steady-state basis we have articulated clearly that all the efforts that the organisation is taking is to deliver a mid- to high-teen ROE

items.statement: Fresh retail health GWP grew 37% YoY on 1/N basis and 35% on N basis
items.quote: Fresh Retail Health GWP increased 37% YoY to Rs. 730 crore. On N basis, the Fresh Retail Health GWP was Rs. 1,039 crore, an increase of 35% YoY.

items.statement: New-to-insurance mix at 94% of fresh retail business vs 90% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our new-to-insurance mix was 94% on Fresh Retail Business compared to 90% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Non-metro fresh business growth 3.5x metro growth; D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY with 98% new-to-insurance
items.quote: Fresh business growth from non-metro geographies is 3.5 times that of growth in the metro geogr aphies. Digital D2C continues to be our fastest growing profitable channel. Within overall digital business, 74% of the fresh business now originates from our own D2C platform. D2C fresh business grew 142% year-on-year with 98% of customers being new to insurance.

items.statement: Normalised PAT up 44% YoY to Rs 386 crore; annualised ROE improved from 12.2% to 15.6%
items.quote: Under the normalised framework, our profit after tax increased 44% year-on-year to Rs. 386 crore with an annualised ROE increasing from 12.2% in Q1 FY26 to 15.6% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Retail loss ratio in 67.5-68% range; group business now very small component
items.quote: So, retail is closer to 67.5% to 68% kind of a number, right? Amitabh Jain: Yes, in that range

items.statement: Annual pricing strategy continues with actuarial justification; focus on maintenance pricing not knee-jerk; discounts for non-claimants being introduced
items.quote: As far as the pricing strategy is concerned, we continue to focus on an annual price strategy wherever it is required. Obviously, it has to be justified product by product in terms of actuarial evaluation. So, that will continue. And while we do the pricing strategy, we will try to give benefits to non -claimants through some discounts which we are trying to bring in.

items.statement: Reinsurance cost expected to decline to 0.5-0.6% range from 0.9% in FY26 as voluntary quota share treaty fades and obligatory negotiations progress
items.quote: Very difficult to comment at this moment, but it should be in the range of 0.5%, 0.6%.

items.statement: Other expenses rose 23% YoY to Rs 283 crore due to loss of GST input credit on technology and admin expenses plus annual rate hikes
items.quote: On the expenses side, last year GST input credit was available on the operating expenses, especially the technology, admin and all those things. This year the input tax credit is not available and hence you see a 20% year -on increase in this segment.

items.statement: Agency network expanded by 20,000 agents to 8.5 lakh total with 19% YoY productivity improvement
items.quote: We continue to scale our industry -leading agency network, adding around 20,000 new agents during this quarter to take the overall count to 8.5 lakh agents along with 19% YoY improvement in agent productivity.

items.statement: Digital adoption: 97% new applications digitally sourced; customer app at 16M downloads and 1.5M monthly active users
items.quote: 97% of our new applications are now digitally sourced and an 'always-on' work stream continues to enhance the app capabilities. On the customer side, our customer app has scaled to ~16 million downloads and over 1.5 million monthly active users

items.statement: Retail claim settlement ratio improved 1% to 91%; renewal ratio up 3% to 102%; NPS improved 12 points to 65; 80%+ claims cashless
items.quote: Our retail claim settlement ratio increased by 1% over Q1 FY26, which now stands at 91% for Q1 FY27. Our renewal ratio increased by 3% YoY to 102% for Q1 FY27. Our company level NPS improved by 12 points to 65 points at June 2026. We settled over 9.5 lakh claims during this quarter, of which more than 80% of claims were cashless

items.statement: Senior citizens under 5% of overall book; focus on younger cohorts
items.quote: Senior citizens is hardly under 5% now of the overall book. We largely focused on younger cohorts of consumers.

items.statement: Retail market share 29% in Q1 FY27 vs 31% in Q1 FY26; impacted by long-term policy reporting and disciplined focus on preferred segments
items.quote: Our retail market share was 29% in Q1 FY27 compared to 31% in Q1 of last fiscal. This is partly impacted by a share of long-term policies and consequent reporting implications on an N and 1/N basis, and clean like-for-like comparability will be restored only by FY28. More meaningfully, it also reflects our strate gy: a very disciplined focus on preferred segments, prudent underwriting and an avoid

items.statement: Already operating within expense of management limits; will assess strategy after regulatory guidelines on commissions are finalized
items.quote: Star Health is probably the only company in the S AHI space which is already operating within the expense of management limits set out by the regulator and we keep improving that. But we will await and see what the regulatory guidelines are and then we will be able to give you better clarity on our strategy as far as acquisition expense is concerned.

items.statement: Proprietary distribution at 90% positions company advantageously for potential distribution and commission reforms
items.quote: Star Health probably is placed very uniquely with a 90% share of business coming from proprietary channels. So, we believe that we would be at an advantageous position in case of the reforms which comes in.

items.statement: Gross written premium up 19% YoY to Rs 4,287 crore (1/N) and Rs 4,672 crore (N basis)
items.quote: On a 1/N basis, the gross return premium increased 19% YoY to Rs. 4,287 crore. On N basis, the gross return premium was Rs. 4,672 crore, an increase of 19% YoY.

items.statement: Investment income up 10% YoY to Rs 644 crore; profit after tax up 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore
items.quote: The investment income for the quarter increased 10% YoY to Rs. 644 crore. The profit after tax for the quarter increased 25% YoY to Rs. 550 crore.

items.statement: ~19,000 employees; largest employer in general insurance including public sector companies
items.quote: I would like to take this opportunity to thank my team members of ~19,000 employees for their sincerity and hard work over the last 20 years. Star Health is probably also the largest employer in the entire General Insurance space, even while counting public sector companies.

items.statement: Noida expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven earlier than previous expectations
items.quote: Based on the current operating trajectory, we expect Noida to achieve EBITDA breakeven earlier than our previous expectations.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex incurred was INR1,610 million; future expansion pipeline capex estimated at INR4,850 crore
items.quote: In this q uarter, we have done INR1,610 million of our capex. And the capex plan, which we have given in our investor presentation is a future requirement to complete these projects

items.statement: Guwahati hospital expanded to 650 beds with estimated project cost of INR9,700 million; construction underway
items.quote: Following the revised building bylaws and National Building Code 2026, the project has now been expanded to a 650-bed super specialty hospital with an estimated project cost of approximately INR9,700 million.

items.statement: 72 beds added in Q1 FY27 (51 at Noida, 21 at Lucknow); operational bed capacity now 3,737
items.quote: During the quarter, we operationalized 72 additional beds, including 51 beds at Noida and 21 beds at Lucknow, taking our operational bed capacity to 3,737.

items.statement: Announced expansion pipeline represents nearly 3,350 additional beds
items.quote: Together, our announced expansion pipeline now represents nearly 3,350 additional beds, providing a strong runway for sustainable long-term growth.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes grew 28% YoY, outpatient volumes grew 34% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Inpatient volumes increased by 28% year-on-year, while outpatient volumes grew by 34%, reflecting sustained demand across our specialties and the continued scale-up of our new facilities.

items.statement: Network occupancy healthy at 63% on expanded bed capacity; Cluster 1 occupancy stable at 63%
items.quote: Occupied bed days for the quarter increased by 21% with network occupancy remaining h ealthy at 63% on expanded bed

items.statement: EBITDA excluding Noida grew 24% YoY to INR3,201 million with margins improving to 25.8%
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding Noida, witnessed a growth of 24% year-on-year to INR3,201 million, with margins improving to 25.8%, highlighting the continued strength of our core operating portfolio.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA including Noida grew 23% YoY to INR3,153 million with margins of 23.8%
items.quote: Reported EBITDA, including Noida stood at INR3,153 million, registering a healthy 23% year-on-year growth with EBITDA margins of 23.8%.

items.statement: Cluster 1 EBITDA margin improved to 24.1% from 23.4% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR1,858 million, reflecting a strong growth of 13% year-on-year with improved margins of 24.1% compared to 23.4% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Cluster 2 excluding Noida delivered 40% EBITDA growth with strong EBITDA margin of 32%
items.quote: On this basis, excluding Noida, Cluster 2 delivered 28% revenue growth and 40% EBITDA growth with a strong EBITDA margin of 32%, highlighting the robust underlying performance of both Lucknow and Patna.

items.statement: Noida total income grew to INR855 million from INR525 million in Q4 FY26; EBITDA loss narrowed sharply from INR236 million to INR49 million
items.quote: On the fin ancial performance, Noida generated total income of INR855 million compared to INR525 million in Q4 FY26. More importantly, the EBITDA loss declined sharply from INR236 million in Q4 FY26 to only INR49 million in Q1 FY27

items.statement: ARPOB grew 5% YoY to INR70,244 supported by favorable case mix and high acuity specialties
items.quote: Average revenue per occupied bed or ARPOB grew by 5% year-on-year to INR70,244, supported by favorable case mix, increasing contribution from high acuity specialties and improvement in operational efficiency.

items.statement: CGHS rate hike benefit fully factored in Q1 FY27; CGHS share 10-12% of revenue; growth mainly volume-led not tariff
items.quote: And Yogesh is saying, in Medanta, our CG HS business is not very high. I think somewhere in the 10% to 12% range. So for us, it's not moving the needle on the total revenue. But of course, for whatever it is, it's beneficial

items.statement: Oncology share increased from 13.7% to 14.4% YoY; kidney and urology grew from 7.6% to 8.2%
items.quote: Our share of cancer, what we reported in our investor presentation has actually increased from 13.7% to 14.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: International patient revenue grew 23% YoY to INR782 million despite geopolitical tensions
items.quote: International patient revenue witnessed a growth of 23% year-on-year to INR782 million, reflecting strong growth despite current geopolitical tensions.

items.statement: OPD pharmacy revenue grew 51% YoY to INR609 million supported by hospital and retail pharmacy network
items.quote: Our OPD pharmacy business also continued its strong growth trajectory with revenue increasing 51% year-on-year to INR609 million, supported by both hospital pharmacies and our expanding retail pharmacy network.

items.statement: Onboarded over 70 doctors including 50+ senior clinicians across specialties in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we onboarded over 70 doctors, including 50-plus senior clinicians across specialties.

items.statement: Negligible attrition at senior clinical levels; high attrition in nursing and junior doctors consistent with industry
items.quote: So we have seen very negligible to no attrition at any of our senior clinical levels across any of our hospitals. Of course, doctors do come and doctors go. I think in the last probably 6 to 18 months, barring, of course, the additions which we have done, I don't see any very significant changes in the attrition rates across the Board.

items.statement: Guwahati project expanded due to revised National Building Code 2026 and building bylaws allowing doubled floor plate and increased height
items.quote: the changes in the National Building Code and the relev ant bylaws of which Global Health Limited – Medanta July 31, 2026 apply to us in Assam and Guwahati, we have been able to actually significantly increase our square footage of the building which we are making

items.statement: ARPP introduced as new metric; Q1 FY27 ARPP at INR201,891 broadly similar to prior year
items.quote: For Q1 FY27, ARPP stood at INR201,891, broadly similar to the number achieved in the corresponding period last year, reflecting stable realization despite the continued ramp-up of newer and existing facilities.

items.statement: Cash flow generation strong and not declining; will fund future growth along with debt; balance sheet strong with low leverage
items.quote: If you see our overall cash flow has been strong over previous year, and we see continuously happening that way only. And we are not seeing any decline in our cash flow generation.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with very low leverage; no challenge on debt side
items.quote: We have a strong balance sheet with a very low leverage as on today, and we don't see any challenge on that side.

items.statement: Key risk is ability to deliver high-quality ethical supply to meet growing demand; demand tailwinds strong from flight to quality, rising income, awareness
items.quote: I think our real challenge will be, can we deliver the supply and more importantly, the high quality, ethical supply to meet that demand.

items.statement: Target to double revenue from Rs.1,000 cr to Rs.2,000 cr by FY29 with normalized EBITDA of 16-18% as ready-to-cut fabric supplier
items.quote: When we are vertically integrated and have become ready-to-cut fabric, we can expect a normalized EBITDA of about 16% to 18%. And also, our ambition is to double our revenue, right, from Rs.1,000 crores to Rs.2,000 crores by FY29.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY26's ~14% growth, reaching at least Rs.1,450 cr
items.quote: We will be able to maintain similar growth for this year or more. So, our floor is definitely what we have delivered last year. So, based on that, I think in the next three years, similar growth we expect to continue.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 17% driven by inventory gains and better pricing; normalized margin for year seen at 14-15%
items.quote: We think the normalized margin for this year will be about 14%-15%. So, there will be some inventory gain which is there in Q1 will not happen going forward in the quarters as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 spread Rs.155/kg (with packing) vs Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26; benefit from timely cotton procurement
items.quote: Currently, our spreads are about Rs.160 per kilo without the packing cost. We can take the average packing cost of about Rs. 5. So, with packing, it is about Rs. 155 per kilo is what our current spread for the last quarter was.

items.statement: Order book healthy with 1.5-2 months forward booking maintained; good export demand from Europe (Germany, Italy) in Q1
items.quote: The order book is healthy. We usually maintain about one and a half to two months of forward booking, which we are able to maintain as of now as well.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~Rs.100-120 cr for knitting, solar, modernization; Rs.350-400 cr planned for ready-to-cut fabric at PM MITRA Park over 2-3 years
items.quote: This year, our CAPEX, all projects put together, including modernization, replacement of capital equipment, I think will be about Rs.100, 120 crores.

items.statement: PM MITRA Park project commissioning targeted CY28; government infrastructure completion by Dec 2027; 3-year policy timeline from land allotment
items.quote: December '27 is the completion date for the PM MITRA Park and the facilities to be provided by the government. And from the date of allocation, which was in '26, right, we have about three years to complete it.

items.statement: Fabric contribution to reach 30-40% of revenue in 3 years as ready-to-cut fabric supplier; in-house knitting capacity 12-15% of yarn production at 40 machines
items.quote: Fabric will become a significant part of our overall top line, probably in the region of about 30% -40%, which is right now at 15% -16%. But this is after three years is what I am talking about.

items.statement: Cotton prices volatile: domestic Rs.62,000-68,000/candy Apr-Jul '26; NY futures 80 cents/lb end-Jun '26; spreads maintainable at Rs.68-69k cotton but risk if prices rise further
items.quote: Domestically, cotton prices witnessed an upward trend during the quarter, rising from Rs.62,000 per candy in April '26 to Rs.67,000 per candy in May ' 26 and then dropping to Rs.64,000 pe r candy in June '26, prices have since risen again to Rs.68,000 per candy

items.statement: Inventory days maintained till Nov-Dec; future inventory levels depend on monsoon evolution; calculated calls to be taken
items.quote: Going forward, I think we will have to see how the monsoon evolves and the entire situation with respect to rains. Based on that, we will take calculated calls, how much inventory to maintain or whether we sort of maintain similar level of inventory.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet; PM MITRA Park capex may use Tamil Nadu incentive schemes (capital subsidy ~Rs.100-125 cr on Rs.1,000 cr investment); no significant concessional debt from PM MITRA
items.quote: In terms of the total investments of around Rs. 1,000 crores, almost around Rs. 100 crores, Rs.125 crores kind of capital subsidy and other benefits will be there.

items.statement: ESOP scheme for executives/management proposed (subject to shareholder approval) to align incentives for value creation
items.quote: We have also gone for a ESOP Scheme for the executives or the management. I think that will also kind of help in terms of creating that kind of an environment for the management team to kind of pursue a much bigger value creation.

items.statement: ROCE ~12% in Q1 FY27; expected to improve with asset turnover from knitting integration, customer mix, export mix
items.quote: This quarter our ROCE is approximately around 12%. The way the value creation or the way this asset turnover ratio is increasing because of this kni tting machine forward integration and those kinds of things, even the kind of customer selection or the mix of the customers and exports, all these things are adding to the ROCE, this will improve

items.statement: US tariff reset at 10% over MFN (~16.5%) = 26.5% total; potential zero duty if 20%+ US cotton used (details pending); India-UK FTA executed, India-EU FTA upcoming
items.quote: has been set at 10% over and above the MFN duty, which is on an average about 16.5%. MFN is more or less similar across all the countries, except countries where they have gotten LDC benefits and others. So, the total tariff as of now is 26.5

items.statement: Focus on labor availability challenges; team working on solutions; ESOP proposed for management retention and motivation
items.quote: If you look, many industries are facing the problem of the labor availability, but the team is working on those things beautifully, and I am reasonably sure that this year of '26-27 is likely to be much better years of the last two years.

items.statement: India's market share in UK could double from 4-5%; US share may rise from 6% to 7-8%; structural demand shift from China (lower cotton output) and US bans on Asian yarn
items.quote: In a market, which is almost $40 billion, our market share was about 4%-5%. That could itself double, right? So, if we are doing about $1.52 billion business in UK market, it could double to almost $4 billion.

items.statement: Full-year ARR net new money target remains 20-22% of opening assets
items.quote: Our target for the full year still remains at 20 -22% of the opening assets.

items.statement: Asset management cumulative loss expected at INR35-40 crores for FY27, breakeven path starts after
items.quote: So this year, we will end up at a cumulative loss of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores. And subsequent to that, you will see the path to breakeven start.

items.statement: Full-year asset services revenue growth expected at 20-25%
items.quote: But on a full year basis, we are confident that revenue growth will be more than 20 -25% here.

items.statement: Full-year opex to revenue ratio expected at 15-16%
items.quote: If you look at the overall full year opex, I would imagine it will still be in the range of 15-16% for the full year.

items.statement: Consolidated cost-to-income ratio expected around 55% for full year
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our cost-to-income ratio is around 55% and maybe for the full year, this will remain around this level only.

items.statement: Private wealth cost-to-income target 60-62% over next 3 years
items.quote: And overall, as you rightly said that 60% to 62% medium term, that target also remains over the next 3 years.

items.statement: RM addition target 15-16% annually if market allows
items.quote: RM addition essentially our desire always is to basically keep adding 15 -16% every year, provided the market allows us to do that at costs which are not upsetting to the overall business.

items.statement: Capital markets segment full-year cost-to-income expected 36-40%
items.quote: But I think overall full year basis, anywhere between 36% to 40% range is what will remain here.

items.statement: Client assets crossed INR5 lakh crores, now at INR5,36,000 crores
items.quote: So we have crossed the INR5 lakh crores mark on the client assets and now the client assets stood at around INR5,36,000 crores.

items.statement: MPIS assets at INR43,000 crores (32% YoY growth), ARR assets at INR58,000 crores (21% YoY growth)
items.quote: Now MPIS asset stands at around INR43,000 crores and ARR assets stands around INR58,000 crores. This is a strong growth of around 32% and 21%, respectively, for both wealth and private.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth net new money crossed INR3,000 crores, highest quarterly ever
items.quote: Net new money, one of the highest quarters ever. We crossed INR3,000 crores in this.

items.statement: Private ARR net new money INR1,800 crores in Q1
items.quote: Our overall net new money on an ARR has been INR1,800 crores for Q1 for private.

items.statement: PRIME commercial real estate fund closed at INR4,000 crores vs INR3,000 crores target
items.quote: We successfully closed our first commercial real estate fund. It's branded as PRIME (PRIME Offices Fund). We closed at around INR4,000 crores. We had initially launched with a target of INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Crossover 4 private equity fund raised INR300-350 crores, targeting INR700-1,000 crores
items.value: INR300-350 crores raised, target INR700-1,000 crores
items.quote: We've done about INR300 crores to INR350 crores. We are targeting anywhere between INR700 crores to INR1,000 crores there.

items.statement: Lending book crossed INR5,000 crores, NII grew 12% QoQ
items.quote: The book has now crossed INR5,000 crores, lending book and NII growth was also about 12% Q-on-Q.

items.statement: Quarterly PAT crossed INR300 crores, all-time high; ROE near 30%
items.quote: Our quarterly revenues crossed INR900 crores, and our quarterly PAT crossed INR300 crores, an all -time high for us. ROE still stands near 30% and remains to be one of the best in the industry.

items.statement: Lending margins expected 30-40 bps higher than current 3.7-3.8% on period-end basis
items.quote: So basically, blended, if you are asking me from the current level, you can add 40-50 basis points from here.

items.statement: Investing heavily in technology and AI across value chain; launched Nuggets AI chatbot, RM Buddy, AI customer profiler
items.quote: We are deliberate and intentional in investing in technology and AI across the value chain, and this business, I think, will get the most of it. We've introduced concepts like Nuggets. This is an AI -based chatbot which services, RMs and our external wealth managers.

items.statement: Offshore: Dubai broken even, Singapore to breakeven by year-end; revenue contribution 5-7% this year
items.quote: Dubai, we've already broken even and Singapore will breakeven by the end of this year. Overall, revenue contribution from offshore will remain between 5% to 7% at least in this year.

items.statement: Asset management cost run rate INR30-33 crores/quarter, peaking at INR35-36 crores/quarter this year
items.quote: Right now, our cost run rate is between INR30 crores to INR33 crores a quarter. Our assessment is that it will peak at INR35 crores to INR36 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Managed products/ARR asset mix: 30-35% equity, 65% non-equity (fixed income plus alternatives like credit, real estate, infrastructure)
items.quote: broadly for us, it remains in the managed products and ARR segment between 30% to 35% would be equity and 65% will be non -equity. So it's not fixed income. It will be fixed inco me plus alternatives like credit, real estate, infrastructure

items.statement: Launched Pinnacle offering for super ultra HNI bundling multiple services
items.quote: We've launched an offering here for the super ultra HNI called Pinnacle. It's a very, very differentiated offering, bundling multiple things and delivering a lot of value proposition to the client.

items.statement: Tier 2+ cities now contribute >35% of MPIS assets and growing faster
items.quote: I think one of the interesting observations which we are seeing that Tier 2 and beyond is expanding faster. I think now it has started contributing to more than 35% and growing even in the MPIS segment.

items.statement: SEBI PMS-MF consultation: overseas investment allowance and to-be-listed securities inclusion more impactful than MF threshold reduction
items.quote: I think the other measures which they have mentioned, that can have more impact for both our businesses, which is allowing for to-be-listed securities to be incorporate d that makes PMS come at par with MF and AIF allowing for overseas investments to be made as part of PMS.

items.statement: Monitoring derivative regulations (STT, intraday financing, bank guarantee collateral); no significant impact expected
items.quote: There is one key monitorable, which basically on the new regulations which have come around derivatives, which is STT and on intraday financing and bank guarantee collateral around these two. We've seen the numbers. We've ran through the numbers. At least we don't feel that there's going to be a very, very significant impact

items.statement: Offshore allocation in client portfolios expected to reach 15-20% over 3-4 years
items.quote: And our view is that over a 3 -4-year period, you will see maybe around 15 -20% allocation sitting in a lot of client portfolios, which are offshore assets.

items.statement: Asset services collateral shifting from cash to G-Secs may moderate yields
items.quote: The yield will adjust because some amount of collateral may shift from cash to G-Sec.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded rating from AA- to AA stable
items.quote: CRISIL has also upgraded our rating from AA- to AA stable. So that is also being reflected because of the financial strength.

items.statement: MPIS revenue per RM up 17% YoY; net new money per RM up >25% YoY
items.quote: I think all this has led to significant productivity jump across MPIS both revenue and net new money assets, we have seen more than 25% jump per RM year-on-year and overall revenue jump of about 17% per RM year-on-year.

items.statement: Private RM productivity up 17-22% YoY
items.quote: RM productivity here also continues to be strong. We have seen a jump of about 17% to 22% year-on-year.

items.statement: Fixed income IB revenue had INR15-20 crores non-repeatable benefit in Q1 from G-Sec tax changes
items.quote: I think there is some amount of, I would say, income which may not be repeatable in the coming quarters, maybe about INR15-INR20 crores, which we benefited in Q1.

items.statement: Management expects to return to pre-crisis growth profile when Middle East normalizes, but timing uncertain
items.quote: we would absolutely expect to get back to that when things get normal. The when is a big when and we really don't have an answer for it.

items.statement: Classic Vacations full-year EBITDA margin expected around 2.5% on GTV
items.quote: Yes, I think that is a fair assessment.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to be better than Q1 on QoQ basis due to July travel season
items.quote: We continue to aim for that. From that perspective, Q2 should be somewhat better than Q1 given that July, which is the heaviest travel month in the northern hemisphere, falls in Q2.

items.statement: Operating leverage visible in Q1 with EBITDA margins growing faster than GP/revenue margins
items.quote: Our bottom-line EBITDA margins grew significantly faster than our GP or revenue margins.

items.statement: SG&A growth will be significantly slower than GP growth, driving meaningful margin expansion
items.quote: our SG&A growth will be significantly slower than GP growth and hence those margins should expand meaningfully.

items.statement: Steady-state platform businesses normalize at 45-60% EBITDA margins, but TBO not anchoring to that in short-medium term
items.quote: those businesses are starting to normalize anywhere between 45% to 60% EBITDA margins, which we are not at all.

items.statement: Middle East delivered flat 1% constant currency growth despite being epicenter of crisis
items.quote: The final highlight purely on the numbers was that the Middle East, in spite of the massive crisis within the region, delivered flat numbers. It delivered 1% growth in constant currency which is very commendable.

items.statement: Europe delivered 24% YoY growth despite travel disruptions
items.quote: Even in a very tough quarter, travel in Europe was generally impacted as well but we still delivered 24% YoY growth in Europe.

items.statement: North America becoming almost a quarter of hotel GTV after Classic acquisition, providing resilient corridor
items.quote: With the acquisition of Classic Vacation s, North America is starting to be almost a quarter of our hotel GTV, which is substantial and we believe we will be able to create growth plans over there

items.statement: Organic business grew 15% YoY in constant currency terms
items.quote: So, 15% YoY growth on a CC terms is great at a time when the Middle East is affected definitely.

items.statement: India Airlines grew 15% GTV on volume shift to East Asian carriers and proactive customer service
items.quote: I think we kind of are proactive in grabbing the business and I think we did some right things in terms of our customer service, and I think the camps were very aggressive, picking up this business.

items.statement: AI initiatives (VOYA, CX, sales productivity) are lean, in-house, minimal capex, not impacting cost structures
items.quote: It is a lean team as is the modern AI native projects. So, it is not impacting on our cost structures in any way at this point, but it is creating optionality on the other side.

items.statement: Hosting and bandwidth expense fell 14% due to technical optimization and moving from expensive infrastructure to self-managed solutions
items.quote: We had made significant investments in terms of technical investments to make sure that we optimize our traffic. Also, on the infrastructure, we essentially try to move away from expensive solutions, infrastructure solutions to solutions that we manage oursel ves to essentially bring that cost

items.statement: Classic integration three-pronged: North America sales hiring mostly done, CRM/back-office automation underway, platform migration targeted by calendar year-end
items.quote: The third is platform integration, which is the big one and which we are likely to finish by CY end of this current calendar year.

items.statement: Key account managers show 4-6 quarters of increasing growth before exhausting regional potential; growth sticky once customers acquired
items.quote: a key account manager will show at least four to six quarters of increasing growth before they start to exhaust whatever they could have gathered within their region.

items.statement: Working capital has seasonality; performance-linked incentives accrue over year and release in first half of next year; supplier mix changes also impact
items.quote: For example, the performance linked incentives etc., they get accrued from the hotels or the airlines suppliers etc., over the year. Either they would be on the Jan to December calendar or April to March. So, generally those accruals would be more or less highest at the time of margin, but those accruals get released, the payment gets released during the first half of the next year.

items.statement: Cash in bank Rs 1,980+ crore; $70 million loan for Classic and 6 million euro working capital loan for Jumbo
items.value: Rs 1,980+ crore cash; $70M loan; €6M WC loan
items.quote: We have reported Rs. 1,980 plus crore as the cash in bank and we have 70 million USD of loan as well as 6 million euro of a working capital loan for Jumbo.

items.statement: Classic integration cost synergies largely in numbers; revenue synergies to pick up after platform migration completes early next year
items.quote: Yes, I think that is a fair conclusion.

items.statement: TBO clearly taking share in APAC and Europe with high double-digit growth while markets show no organic growth
items.quote: we have clearly taken share because it is hard to imagine that these markets could have grown at this level at all. In fact, they won't have grown at all, but we have high double-digit growth.

items.statement: Take rates slightly lowered in crisis regions to win disproportionate volume; selective margin drops for market share
items.quote: there is the regions were fighting for business in a tough environment and from a dollar value perspective, any growth would be accretive. But they will be selective places in such crisis situations where we do drop margin a little bit to win disproportionately more business.

items.statement: Three distinct GTV types with varying GP profiles: Air ~1% GP, Classic ~11% GP, organic in middle; blended GTV hard to model
items.quote: We have the air GTV which you know is like a 1% kind of GP profile, but on the other hand there is Classic which is 11% GP profile and then there is our organic business which is in the middle.

items.statement: 11% gap between hotel GTV in constant currency vs INR due to steep rupee depreciation YoY; started reporting constant currency numbers
items.quote: There was almost an 11% gap in our hotel GTV when we looked at in constant currency versus INR and which is leading to significantly higher growth numbers if you looked at INR standalone.

items.statement: GTV split broadly 50-50 between retail and B2B/API business, consistent with last quarter
items.quote: GTV numbers would broadly be between 50-50 only as the last quarter.

items.statement: Middle East situation extremely fluid, changes hourly; management given up predicting recovery timeline; treating any growth as optionality
items.quote: situation is extremely fluid, and the fact that the Middle East was flat is quite an achievement in all honesty given that is the eye of the crisis right now. It is also very hard at this point , we have given up on predicting what is going to happen because the situation literally changes every hour

items.statement: AI agentic booking interfaces not yet creating meaningful conversion; frontier labs shifting focus away from cannibalizing OTA models; TBO experimenting but predictable gains from CX and sales AI
items.quote: both Anthropic and OpenAI haven't really tried to create a transaction or a payment framework within their apps which basically means that there isn't a significantly easier way to make a booking via an agentic interface vis-a-vis just going on the website of an OTA.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin guidance of 0 to -100 bps for Q2 FY27, assuming no change in competitive intensity
items.quote: Even the guidance that we've given is highly range-bound. We closed the last quarter at -0.2%, and we're talking about -100 bps is the range. So obviously, we've assumed no change in competitive intensity.

items.statement: Food delivery YoY growth guidance maintained at 18% to 20%
items.quote: But if you've seen the momentum over the last 3-4 years, it's been on an upward trajectory, and we continue to maintain guidance of YoY growth between 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Expect overall cash breakeven in next two quarters while supporting quick commerce EBITDA journey
items.quote: So we expect to, over the next two quarters, be able to break even at the overall cash level, while we continue to support the Quick Commerce business during its EBITDA profitability journey.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin improved to INR 30 per order over last 5 quarters, closed Q1 FY27 at -0.2%
items.quote: When we look at the quality of the business going into the future, we have absolutely moved close to INR30 in contribution over the last 5 quarters.

items.statement: Food delivery margin at 3%, targeting 5% steady state
items.quote: We are currently at about 3%. We have told that we will be getting to 5%, and that steady growth you will continue to see, as well as the treasury income.

items.statement: Quick commerce monetization target of INR 30 per order to reach EBITDA breakeven, split between product margins and advertising
items.quote: Again, INR20 roughly, that is going to come from the monetization side, roughly broken half and half between, say, the product margins that we make from the brands or the mix of our business, as well as roughly, say INR10 from the advertising side of the business.

items.statement: Quick commerce 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% in preceding period, cautiously optimistic on double-digit sequential growth
items.quote: So we are cautiously optimistic of being able to deliver at least on this double-digit growth on a sequential basis, and hopefully more.

items.statement: Quick commerce added more orders in last 4 weeks than previous 6 months
items.quote: So even over the last four weeks, we've added more orders than in the previous 6 months.

items.statement: Quick commerce M1 retention of transacting user base at highest level in many quarters
items.quote: So our first month (M1) retention of the transacting user base has actually been the highest that it has been over the last many, many quarters for us.

items.statement: Quick commerce 1-month retention at 61%, up from 55% last year, but not considered gold standard
items.quote: You said 61% 1-month retention is the best you've had in many quarters. You said 55% was the level last year.

items.statement: Quick commerce to add more stores in Q2 FY27 than in last four quarters combined, focusing on existing top 8 cities
items.quote: Our guidance for the current quarter is that seeing some of this growth, that we are going to add more stores than we have added in the last four quarters, in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Quick commerce network at 40% utilization, some hyperlocal stores hitting 2,500-3,000 orders per day requiring more stores
items.quote: Though as an overall network level, we are obviously 40% utilized. Our guidance for the current quarter is that seeing some of this growth, that we are going to add more stores than we have added in the last four quarters, in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Quick commerce take rate improvement driven by brand margin negotiation, advertising, and user fees; deemed sustainable
items.quote: So the combination of these three levers, we have been able to increase the take rate significantly and a large part of our improvement over the last 4-5 quarters to help us get to the CM break-even was also led by the monetization efforts.

items.statement: Wage hike impact in Q1 FY27 from annual salary revision and minimum wage increases in some states, factored into Q2 guidance
items.quote: One is that our annual salary revision happens in the Q1FY27 cycle, so that's one part which sits below the contribution margin. Also we have seen in certain states where there's been a minimum wage hike, which has impacted certain, say, operations around our picking and packing costs at the warehouse or at the dark store level.

items.statement: Last mile cost impact from West Bengal elections and summer heat partially offset by efficiency gains; 20 bps dip vs 40 bps last year
items.quote: In the previous year, we had a 40 basis point dip, which got reduced to 20 basis point dip in the current year, and we hope to continue doing better on this going forward.

items.statement: Quick commerce differentiated assortment strategy includes proprietary brand Noice, partnerships with large brands (Aashirvaad, ITC) and D2C brands; many SKUs exclusive
items.quote: The way we are working is we work with a mixture of both incumbent and large brands in some of the categories, as well as challengers like D2C brands to create a distinctive value proposition of better quality or great quality at great prices.

items.statement: Private brand strategy is experience-driven with higher margins, not value-driven; no conflict with advertising revenue
items.quote: I think by the inherent nature of some of these private brands means that they come with significantly higher margins. So there's both the supply chain margins and some of the manufacturing margins that you can, as a brand appropriate, which gives enough and more room for you to have higher gross margins than this.

items.statement: Quick commerce has 7-8 players, many expanding rapidly; competitors operating at double-digit negative contribution margins
items.quote: There are lots of folks expanding their networks rapidly. Also, I think as a part of the reset that we did and this whole differentiated assortment that we keep harping on about, at some level, I think you should be rest assured that most of our efforts are to actually fiercely shape the positioning that we want.

items.statement: Food delivery competition likely in affordability segment; premium segment harder to enter; Toing model differentiated on delivery fee, proposition, cuisine, last mile, economics
items.quote: And also it is very likely that any competition of any nature which comes in, is likely to come in more in the affordability segment than the premium segment. The premium segment is much harder to enter for any new competitor.

items.statement: Zero commission model unsustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers, or delivery partners eventually
items.quote: So while you can call something zero commission, there are 3-4 fundamental questions to be answered there. One, if it is zero commission, then who pays for cost of the platform. Somebody has to pay.

items.statement: Quick commerce culled low-value users over last 2-3 quarters, causing soft growth but improving retention quality
items.quote: We have actively culled out a lot of Monthly Transacting Users (MTU) users on the platform. And since these are reported numbers across food delivery as well as quick commerce, there's been an impact because quick commerce has lower frequency compared to food delivery.

items.statement: Toing acquiring 2 out of 3 users new to Swiggy platform; overlapping users either switch entirely or split use cases
items.quote: So one out of three users who are obviously common on Swiggy exhibit one of two behaviors. One, the first behavior is that they just wanted a different alternative. And they find Toing more appealing to them, and which is great because they stay within the same company.

items.statement: Nandita appointed as Instamart CEO; strong merchandising leader with retail experience to build on differentiated assortment and brilliant basics
items.quote: We're starting with these record high retention levels. We're starting with some early success in the differentiated assortment approach and everything in Nandita's experience has also demonstrated that in retail, she's proven to be a strong merchandising leader who's understood consumers better than her competitors in the past.

items.statement: Quick commerce NOV growth 3% QoQ, revenue growth 13% QoQ implying take rate expansion
items.quote: Because when we look at Quick Commerce NOV growth, it's roughly 3% QoQ, QC revenue growth is roughly 13%. Clearly, the implied take rate has moved up.

items.statement: Food delivery growth at adjusted 18% YoY excluding cancellations
items.quote: So while this quarter growth is coming at adjusted about 18%, if you adjust for cancellations.

items.statement: Quick commerce strategy shift to 0 to -100 bps contribution margin assumes no dramatic change in competitive intensity; will moderate if needed
items.quote: Should things change dramatically, you should expect us to also keep moderating the strategy.

items.statement: No capitalization of employee costs, store pre-opening costs, or indirect costs; all expensed in contribution margin
items.quote: Absolutely not. For all the line items that you mentioned, and there are a lot of them, we do not capitalize any of these. All of these are booked as part of the -- especially also new stores when they open, even if there are 30-60-90-day period, all of that gets baked into our contribution margin.

items.statement: No securitization of payables or arrangements with brands for delayed payment with interest
items.quote: No, we are not aware of such practices, Sudheer.

items.statement: Platform innovation losses driven by Snacc closure costs and Toing marketing investment; minimal fixed cost overhead for Toing
items.quote: Part of that was the closure. Since we had closed it last quarter, there were some operating costs that got booked in this current quarter. But a large part of this investment is on Toing. And again, as we have called out, a lot of this is around the marketing investment that we have made to acquire new users on the platform.

items.statement: Target pre-sales of approximately Rs 6,500 crores for FY27, implying ~23% growth over FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we target closing the year with pre -sales of approximately Rs. 6,500 crores which would be a growth of ~23% over

items.statement: Expect net debt levels by end of FY27 to remain around same levels as FY26
items.quote: Keeping in view the capital allocation of upcoming launches and the business development spend, we expect the net debt levels by end for FY27 and to remain around the same levels of FY26.

items.statement: Net debt to equity ratio expected to improve from current ~2.0x due to profit recognition at end of FY27
items.quote: However, the net debt / equity ratio is expected to improve from current levels of ~2.0x due to recognition of profits at the end of FY27.

items.statement: Target completion of 5.5 million square feet in FY27
items.quote: We are well on track to deliver on a target of 5.5 million square feet of completion this year.

items.statement: Company will complete around 15 million square feet of ongoing projects across FY27, FY28 and FY29
items.quote: In closing, I wish to state that company would be completing around 15 million square feet of ongoing projects in FY27, FY28 and FY29 gradually.

items.statement: Pre-sales grew 6% YoY to Rs 1,329 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Pre-sales grew 6% year-on-year to reach Rs 1,329 crores in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 1,249 crores in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Sales collections grew 17% YoY to Rs 1,365 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Sales collections showed a 17% year-on-year growth to Rs 1,365 crores.

items.statement: Pre-sales at Kalpataru Park City Thane surged ~350% YoY in Q1 FY27 on a low base
items.quote: Sales momentum at Kalpataru Parkcity, Thane expanded significantly this quarter, with pre-sales surging ~350% year-on-year compared to Q1 FY26 on a low base.

items.statement: Launched two projects/phases with total potential of 1.25 million square feet of saleable area in Q1 FY27
items.quote: we launched two projects/ phases which have a total potential of 1.25 million square feet of saleable area.

items.statement: Strong pipeline of launches spread over approximately 5 million square feet worth approximately Rs 7,800 crores for FY27
items.quote: We have a strong pipeline of launches spread over approximately 5 million square feet and worth approximately Rs. 7,800 crores this year

items.statement: Secured development agreement for redevelopment of five societies in Ashok Nagar, Kandivali with GDV potential of Rs 1,250 crores on 2.8-acre land parcel
items.quote: I am pleased to share th at we have secured a development agreement for the redevelopment of five societies in Ashok Nagar, Kandivali. This project is situated on approximately 2.8 -acre land parcel and has a GDV potential of Rs. 1,250 crores.

items.statement: Monetized commercial office property Kalpataru Infinia in Pune for ~Rs 119 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we have monetized our commercial office property Kalpataru Infinia located at Shivajinagar Nagar in Pune for a consideration of ~Rs. 119 crores.

items.statement: Received occupation certificate for ~0.79 million square feet across 668 units in Q1 FY27
items.quote: during the quarter we received occupation certificate for ~0.79 million square feet across 668 units

items.statement: Received occupation certificate for Kalpataru Elitus Tower B and Kalpataru Summit Office Complex in Mulund during Q1 FY27
items.quote: We received occupation certific ate for Kalpataru Elitus Tower B and Kalpataru Summit Office Complex in Mulun d during this quarter.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA was Rs 95 crores with margin of ~20% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA during the quarter was Rs. 95 crores with the margin of ~20%.

items.statement: Reported loss of Rs 29 crores in Q1 FY27 due to project completion method of revenue recognition
items.quote: On the profitab ility front, we reported a loss of Rs. 29 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Gross debt stood at Rs 9,189 crores, cash and equivalents at Rs 959 crores, net debt at Rs 8,229 crores as on June 30, 2026
items.quote: as on June 30, 2026, our gross debt stood at Rs. 9,189 crores while our cash and cash equivalents were Rs. 9 59 crores resulting into a net debt of Rs. 8,229 crores.

items.statement: Net debt to equity ratio stands at 2.0x as on June 30, 2026
items.quote: Consequently, our net debt to equity ratio stands at 2 .0x.

items.statement: Refinanced debt of approximately Rs 1,800 crores in Q1 FY27 giving estimated annual savings of Rs 55 crores in finance cost
items.quote: during this quarter, we have refinanced a debt of approximately Rs. 1,800 crores which wi ll give us an estimated annual savings of Rs. 55 crores in a finance cost.

items.statement: Total debt refinanced since IPO is approximately Rs 5,300 crores; weighted average cost of borrowing now ~11% per annum, down ~200 bps since listing
items.quote: since our IPO, the total debt which stands refinanced is approximately Rs. 5,300 crores. Hence, our weighted average cost of borrowing now stands at ~11% per annum down by approximately 200 basis points since the listing.

items.statement: Cumulative optimization of borrowing costs adds to approximately Rs 180 crores annually
items.quote: This cumulative optimization of borrowing costs therefore adds to approximately Rs. 180 crores annually.

items.statement: Seeing positive trend towards walk-ins and conversion; pricing looking stable and strong
items.quote: We are seeing a positive trend towards walk-ins and conversion and also the pricing is looking stable and strong.

items.statement: Pricing generally increases as project progresses; by Q2 will know how much price increase shall be about
items.quote: So the pricing generally as the progress of the project goes, wherever we can see an increase, we are planning to move towards that. By Q2 we will know how much the price increase sha ll be about.

items.statement: Pre-sales growth of 6% YoY despite 48% area sold increase due to project mix; no discounting
items.quote: It is right. It is due to project mix.

items.statement: Most of the Q1 FY27 collections of Rs 1,365 crores came from units sold earlier; bookings during quarter were marginal
items.quote: The booking made during the quarter was marginal only. Most of the collection was due to the units sold earlier.

items.statement: 35% of Q1 FY27 pre-sales came from new launches; full year expectation remains ~25% from new launches
items.quote: In this quarter, 35% was from new sales and as we have said, for the entire year, about 25% will be from new launches.

items.statement: Launches well-spread across next three quarters: Blossom next quarter, Estela 1 Tower and Hari Neketan this quarter, Ardene and Suman Nagar next quarter
items.quote: They are well -spread across the three quarters. Blossom will happen in the next quarter. Estela 1 Tower will happen in this quarter. Hari Neketan will happen this quarter. And Ardene and Suman Nagar will go to next quarter.

items.statement: Debt may increase slightly or marginally within quarters due to spend on ongoing or new projects, but trend is generally on the downside year on year
items.quote: Directionally, it is going to be on the downside, year on year. Periodically, within quarters, it is possible that it may increase slightly or marginally due to the spend or investment or capital allocation on to the ongoing projects or the new projects which are acquired under new BD.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25-30% from earlier 25%, and PAT margin expansion guidance to 0.5-1% from earlier 0.5-0.75%
items.quote: In terms of specific guidance, we would like to revise our revenue guidance from earlier 25% to 30% and at the PAT level margin growth, we would like to increase it from 0.5% to 0.75% -1%.

items.statement: Strong demand across India and international markets (US, Europe, Middle East) driving 32% YoY revenue growth
items.quote: Revenue grew 32% year-on-year to INR412.5 crores, supported by healthy demand across India and our international markets, particularly the United States, Europe, and the Middle East.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 24.65%, up 329 bps YoY and 542 bps QoQ; EBITDA margin 12.8%, up 156 bps YoY; PAT margin 7%, up 108 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross margin expanded to 24.65%, improving by 329 basis points over last year and 542 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Supplies to 49 countries (up from 46), 5,130 customer touchpoints, 773 suppliers, 2,420 employees as of June 2026
items.quote: As of end of Q1 FY27, Electronics Bazaar supplies to 49 countries, up from 46 at the end of FY26. Customer touchpoints have grown to 5,130 and our supplier base now stands at 773, reflecting deeper and more diversified sourcing across geographies.

items.statement: Memory prices rose 5-10% in Q1; 8GB DDR5 at $126, 16GB DDR5 at $231 as of June 30; prices up 5x since Oct 2025; entry laptop price rose from INR40k to INR48k
items.quote: Memory prices have risen a further 5% to 10% in the last quarter alone. 8GB DDR5 now stands at $126 and 16GB DDR5 at $231 as of June 30th. Since October 2025, these prices have more than doubled.

items.statement: Laptop ASP INR30,763 (up 12% YoY, 2.5% QoQ); Desktop ASP INR19,300 (up 10% YoY, 1.5% QoQ); Laptops 81% of revenue, 108k units; Desktops/others 42k units
items.quote: In terms of ASPs, in terms of laptops during the quarter, we have an ASP of about INR30,763. If you were to compare this to the corresponding quarter, it is about it was about INR27,500.

items.statement: Geographic revenue mix: India 36%, Middle East 12%, US 24%, Europe 23%, Others 5%; Deeper penetration in US/Europe driving higher international margins (~30% vs India 21%)
items.quote: 36% is out of India, 12% is from Middle East, US and Europe together account for 47%, US being 24% and Europe being 23%, and others is about 5%.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR406 cr from INR399 cr; Inventory INR700 cr (down from INR740 cr); Strategic inventory holding for margin advantage; 30-40 days finished inventory target
items.quote: The inventory at the end of Q1 is about INR700-odd crores. This has gone down, this has gone down from about INR740-odd crores at the end of the year.

items.statement: Memory prices expected to rise 5-10% quarterly; No meaningful relief before end of 2027; Procurement prices trailing new laptop prices; Securing material at old prices via contracts
items.quote: What I hear from lot of experts is that it will continue to rise 5% to 10% every quarter. And it is not just the memory, it is the processor, SSD, and memory is fundamental to any technological device that we use.

items.statement: No fixed capital investment; Business is working capital heavy; No machinery involved; Focus on operational efficiency
items.quote: Also, in our business, we don't have any fixed capital worth talking about, there are no machinery involved, there are no other things, so the business is working capital heavy.

items.statement: Headcount grew to 2,420 from 2,148; Investing in production, sales, support; Hiring ahead of curve for niche industry training
items.quote: Our teammates, our biggest asset, have grown to 2,420 as of June 2026, up from 2,148, reflecting continued investment in production, sales, and customer support.

items.statement: Negligible competition in served markets; Trust and warranty creating pricing power; Refurbished PC at ~30% of new price vs 50% in phones/cars; Room to move to 50%
items.quote: Due to our deeper penetration in all the markets, we are actually facing negligible competition and that is allowing us to price our products better.

items.statement: Volume growth 18% YoY (150k total units); Revenue growth 32% YoY; Realization growth 12% YoY; IDC projects global PC shipments down 11.3% in 2026, 20% decline in H2
items.quote: In terms of the overall unit numbers, you are right. It is about 18% and the overall growth being 32%.

items.statement: Middle East tensions (500 missiles, 2000 drones fired at UAE) but UAE facilities unaffected; Shipments via air continuing normally; Procurement lumpiness and potential disposition volume decline
items.quote: Around 500 missiles and 2,000 drones have been fired upon UAE, but we see no visible damage anywhere. So, they manage it very well. The interception rate was very high and that has allowed commerce to function.

items.statement: Headcount 2,420 (up 272); Hiring across management, marketing, production; Training curve for production staff; Channel meets and 'Chai Pe Charcha' events expanding reach
items.quote: We have to hire people in advance and obviously, marketing and other expenses are happening. As you would have seen, we are doing channel meets, we are doing other meets to expand our proposition.

items.statement: Net debt INR406 cr (up from INR399 cr); Capital employed marginally down; Working capital similar size; Tax rate 10-12% for FY27
items.quote: The net debt has increased by about INR100-odd crores. This number was about INR399 crores or almost rounding off to INR400 crores at the end of March '26. This has gone to INR406 crores.

items.statement: Other expenses up 68% YoY due to incentivization for better realization and sales; Directionally okay per management
items.quote: This number has gone is increased by about 68% as you rightly observed. But also, this is on account of, I think what we are also doing is there's a lot of incentivization that is going on for better realization and better sales.

items.statement: Industry added 70 lakh new demat accounts in Q1 FY27 vs 67 lakh in Q1 FY26; total industry demat count crossed 23.16 crore, up 16.3% YoY
items.quote: the investor base continued to expand as far as our market is concerned, with nearly 70 lakh new demat accounts getting added in Q1 FY27 versus 67 lakh that got added in the same quarter of the previous year. With this addition, the total demat count for the industry has now crossed 23.16 crore, which is up on a YoY basis by 16.3%.

items.statement: NSDL net demat additions 12.4 lakh in Q1 FY27 vs 10.4 lakh in Q1 FY26; incremental market share 17.6% up from 14% in Q4 and 15.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This improvement reflects a steady pickup in accounts addition and the various works that we've been doing to add new DPs and improve our customer experience and add APIs with 12.4 lakh net additions of accounts during Q1 FY27 compared to 10.4 lakhs that we added last year, same time.

items.statement: Fintech share of incremental demat additions rose from ~2% to ~20% over recent quarters; 6 new DPs added in Q1 FY27, total 317 DPs
items.quote: In fact, just for information, that number few quarters back was about 2% of our total addition was coming from FinTech and 98% was coming from non-FinTech. Now, that number of FinTech too has gone to almost 20%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 57.8% in Q1 FY27; margins moderated due to front-loaded investments in technology, cyber security, automation and talent
items.quote: I wish to highlight that our standalone margins have seen some moderation compared to the previous periods. This is largely on account of the investments that we have been our focus areas which we have been talking to you about which is strengthening technology resilience and cyber security, enhancing customer experiences through greater operational automation and increase in talent pool by addres

items.statement: Capitalized INR 7-8 crore on technology in Q1 FY27 vs INR 106 crore full year FY26
items.quote: On the technology front, we have capitalized INR7 to INR8 crores during Q1 FY27 versus full year capitalization in the previous year of INR106 crores.

items.statement: Net hiring of ~98 employees in FY26; hiring now cautious, peak near; additions mainly in technology and cyber security
items.quote: if you look at our net hiring in the previous year was about 98 employees. With regards to this quarter, and that's why you see there is an uptick and that the cost is now coming in this financial year. As far as the peak is concerned, we are now going to go very cautious in terms of our hiring.

items.statement: Yuva and Women's Demat plans (zero settlement charges for 3 years) together 18-20% of incremental demat additions in Q1 FY27
items.quote: our Yuva, the youth plan, and the Women's Demat plan, where we have made the settlement charges zero for the first 3 years for a new entrant for an NSDL account, continue to gain traction, and together they stand at about 18% to 20% of our incremental demat additions in Q1 of FY27.

items.statement: E-voting events 900 in Q1 FY27 vs 794 in Q1 FY26; e-voting market share 64% vs 61% YoY
items.quote: Our e -voting platform has helped many leading companies to offer e-voting services to their shareholders, empowering them to exercise their voting rights electronically with a number of events conducted during the quarter increasing to 900 compared to 794 that we did same time last year, same period last year. items.statement: SWAGAT-FI framework enabled for FPIs/FVCIs: simplified onboarding, reduced compliance, 10-year registration validity
items.quote: NSDL also enabled a special tagging of SWAGAT-FI, a (Single Window Automatic and Generalized Access for Trusted Foreign Investors) framework for FPIs and FVCIs in NSDL. items.statement: KYC charges cut 20% by regulator/KRA; NSDL KYC revenue declined only 2% due to volume growth and SEZ business offset
items.quote: as we all know that KYC charges on fetch was cut by 20% by regulator or all depositories took that call, KRA agencies took that call to reduce it by 20%. Still, our decline was just 2%.

items.quote: Further, during the quarter, the board approved an investment in IIBH, which is a subsidiary in the GIFT City, which is an associate, I'm sorry, in the GIFT City with NSDL holding 20% stake in that company.

items.quote: the West Asia conflict, as all of us are aware, eased during Q1 of FY27, supporting lower oil prices, stabilization of the rupee, and improved market sentiment. items.quote: The count has also grown in the last year - on-year by about 15% count in terms of the pledge and unpledged. And that is where it is helping us this line of revenue.

items.quote: And in terms of the component of the joining fee, we typically charge INR15,000 per company as a processing charge at the time of joining. So INR15,000, I mean, let me just look at the number here. Yes, that should be in the range of about INR5 to INR6 crores.

items.statement: 40+ APIs launched for DPs in prior quarters; utilization focus in Q1 FY27 improved customer experience and market share
items.quote: The focus during the quarter was also to increase the utilization of the 40 plus APIs that we launched for DPs during the previous quarters. I think we had briefed this to you earlier. This helped us improve our customer experience and increase market share in demat accounts, which I will talk about in a bit.

items.statement: DLT (distributed ledger) revenue line new; 600 issuers on platform; no specific revenue disclosed
items.quote: DLT is a relatively new line of revenue. We are not giving any specific number with regards to the DLT. Overall, we have right now about 600 issuers on our platform. So that's something which I can give you an additional information.

items.statement: Product gaps vs competition largely closed; some APIs not available with competitors; focus on word-of-mouth, relationship building, tactical pricing (Yuva/Women plans) to gain share
items.quote: I think today from what we engage, product gaps are not there really in the market. In fact, many people have said some of the APIs that we have launched are not available with competition. So I don't think product gap is a showstopper anymore. It is about more positive word of mouth endorsement, more positive comfort that the market will get from other players. Our sort of relationship building t

items.quote: NSDL conducted investor awareness programs online, offline and in hybrid formats in association with corporates, defense services, education institutions and women -focused forums, covering a very diverse set of investor segments nationwide.
