items.statement: NDML transferring insurance repository business from SBU to separate subsidiary per IRDAI guidance; transition underway
items.quote: pursuant to IRIDA's guidance, the company is in the process of transferring its insurance repository business from existing SBU to a separate subsidiary dedicated to this activity. The work on this transition is currently underway.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38%-40% from previous 27%-30%
items.quote: We are now revising our FY27 revenue growth guidance from 27% to 30% that we had given earlier to 38% to 40%.

items.statement: Margin trajectory unchanged despite higher growth guidance
items.quote: Having said that, our margin trajectory remains unchanged, suggesting faster growth with the same disciplined path into profitability.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 4.9% in Q1 FY27 from 4.7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crores, with margins expanding to 4.9%, which was 4.7% last quarter.

items.statement: Lost shipment debit cost reduced to 5.5% of revenue from 6.1% last quarter and 7.9% a year ago
items.quote: Our lost shipment debit cost, came down to 5.5% of revenue, which was 7.9% a year ago and 6.1% in the last quarter, Q4.

items.statement: Transportation costs held flat sequentially despite opening 716 new pin codes
items.quote: Transportation costs held flat sequentially in a quarter where we opened 716 new pin codes, and all of them will be running below capacity initially.

items.statement: Delivery partner expense increased only 10 bps quarter-on-quarter despite supply squeeze and hyper-local growth
items.quote: The largest cost line item, delivery partner expense, went up just by 10 bps quarter-on-quarter, despite significant supply squeeze and growth in hyper-local vertical.

items.statement: Order volumes reached nearly 25 crores in Q1 FY27, growing 83% year-on-year
items.quote: Order volumes reached nearly 25 crores, growing 83% year-on-year.

items.statement: Prime business grew 2.7x year-on-year and crossed 400 D2C customers
items.quote: Prime grew almost two and a half times last year. It has accelerated to 2.7 times year-on-year this quarter, even at a much larger base. Along the way, we have crossed more than 400 D2C customers who are using our Prime services across our platform.

items.statement: Shadowfax 360 self-serve platform onboarded over 1,200 transacting sellers within one quarter of launch
items.quote: Within one quarter of the launch, we already have more than 1,200 transacting sellers, and this number is compounding every single week.

items.statement: Prime Large expanded to 10,000 pin codes in Q1 FY27, achieving full-year target; FY27 target raised to 12,000 pin codes
items.quote: We have already expanded to 10,000 pin codes, which was our full year target for FY27. We hit that number within the first quarter. We are now raising our FY27 target for Prime Large to 12,000 pin codes.

items.statement: Prime Large revenue grew close to 170% year-on-year to roughly INR75 crores ARR
items.quote: Revenue has grown close to 170% year-on-year to roughly about INR75 crores ARR in this business line.

items.statement: Hyper-local grew 53% year-on-year and 17% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Hyper-local has grown about 53% year-on-year, and 17% over the last quarter itself.

items.statement: Added 716 pin codes in Q1 FY27, ending at 16,372 pin codes coverage
items.quote: We ended the quarter at about 16,372 pin codes, where we opened about 716 pin codes over the last 90 days, almost 8 pin codes every single day.

items.statement: 47 dark stores live as of June 30, another 20 on the way, against full-year target of 100
items.quote: We are super proud to communicate that out of thos e 100 dark stores, 47 are already live as on 30th June, and another 20 are on the way to go

items.statement: INR60 crores capex in Q1 FY27, 77% allocated to network and automation for middle-mile capacity
items.quote: 77% of the capex that we are talking about has gone into network and automation. To make it simple, network and automation typically means everything which is part of our sortation centers.

items.statement: Chose to lag diesel price pass-through to customers by 5 days to support relationships
items.quote: On diesel price, many of our contracts allow us to pass increases straight to our customers, and we had every right to take that hike on day one, but we chose to lag it by 5 days and carry it on ourselves.

items.statement: Minimum wage hikes in four states causing INR2-2.5 crores monthly impact
items.value: INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores per month
items.quote: We have roughly taken about between INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores a month impact because of minimum wage impact coming from various states.

items.statement: Market share in Express Parcel segment improved to 28%-30% from 27%-29% last quarter
items.quote: What we are seeing in the market today is that the consolidation continues to strengthen between the two large players, and every quarter, the two large companies in the Express Parcel segment are continuing to gain market share.

items.statement: Quick commerce market share in outsourcing segment expected to exceed 50%
items.quote: While in quick commerce industry, we are the single largest 3PL operating today, where now we have a meaningful market share, and we believe our market share will be more than 50% today in the quick commerce outsourcing segment.

items.statement: Vertical quick commerce estimated to grow to 20%-25% of overall quick commerce market
items.quote: We believe vertical quick commerce can grow to 20%-25% of the overall quick commerce market, following exactly the same path that e-commerce took.

items.statement: D2C brands growing significantly faster than rest of business; was virtually non-existent 8 quarters ago
items.quote: 8 quarters back, it was virtually non-existent. 4 quarters back, it became a smaller number. Today, that has grown to almost 2.7 times. So, you can imagine that the D2C brands and the associated smaller businesses are growing significantly faster than the rest of the business.

items.statement: AI co-pilot 'Delivery Partner Buddy' handles 16,000 rider conversations daily with 97% auto-resolution
items.quote: It now handle s around 16,000 rider conversations in a single day, and roughly 97% of queries are all resolved without a human agent ever touching them

items.statement: Vision AI at Pickup catches 40% of bad pickups before losses at 35x lower inference cost than frontier models
items.quote: It is catching roughly 40% of bad pickups before they become losses, and all this is done at about 35 times lower inference cost than what a frontier model would charge us.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from anchor customers possible but mitigated by volume-based rate cards and operational efficiency
items.quote: See, our customers are optimizing their cost and experience literally on every lane that they work on. So, if we are not competitive, we will anyways not get the desired volumes that we are delivering today.

items.statement: New urea plant expected to be commissioned by 2030
items.quote: In my opinion, even with today's situation in terms of stressed timelines for critical equipments, we should be able to deliver it within 2030.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton for new urea plant estimated at INR 12,000
items.quote: I would say we will be still around INR 12,000 a ton.

items.statement: New urea plant capex estimated at INR 10,000 crores
items.quote: projects of this type, almost INR 10,000 crores, they go through several phases in terms of preparation.

items.statement: Financial bids for new urea plant expected by mid-October
items.quote: The financial bids after equalization of the technical requirements should be available to us by may be middle October or so.

items.statement: Gadepan-3 maximum run rate 9.5-10 lakh tons before policy period ends
items.quote: the maximum we can do is about 9.5 to 10, depending on how the circumstances pan out.

items.statement: TAN project production commenced for Weak Nitric Acid and Ammonium Nitrate solutions
items.quote: Our Technical Ammonium Nitrate project progressed well during the quarter with production commencing of Weak Nitric Acid and Ammonium Nitrate solutions, while the high-density Ammonium Nitrate moves closer to commissioning.

items.statement: 8.5 lakh tons of NPK fertilizers tied up with vendors
items.quote: I think till date we have tied up, Ashish, about 8.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crores with margins expanding to 17%
items.quote: EBITDA, however, rose 12% to INR 851 crores, with margins expanding to 17%, roughly from 13%, an improvement of about 350 basis points.

items.statement: Complex fertilizer segment EBIT rose 67% to INR 239 crores
items.quote: On the complex fertilizer segment, revenues stood at INR 1,737 crores, against INR 2,131 crores, lower by 18%, reflecting a measured approach to placement in a season where sowing was delayed. Segment EBIT rose 67% to around INR 239 crores.

items.statement: Crop protection segment EBIT grew 13% to INR 108 crores with margins at 25%
items.quote: The crop protection chemicals, special ity nutrients and seed segment recorded revenues of about INR 430 crores, as against INR 458 crores, lower by 6 %, reflecting deferred farmer purchases. Segment EBIT, however, grew 13 % to INR 108 crores, with margins improving to about 25

items.statement: Gas price for Q1 was USD 17.25 per MMBtu on NCV basis
items.quote: Gas price for Q1 was, because the Government has only declared the provisional price. So, it is on NCV basis, it is USD 17.25 for the quarter.

items.statement: Nutrient-based subsidy rates for Kharif revised up 10% but don't reflect subsequent cost escalations
items.quote: While the nutrient-based subsidy rates for Kharif were revised upwards by around 10%, these were announced prior to the sharp increase in global prices following the geopolitical developments in West Asia and therefore do not fully reflect the subsequent cost escalations.

items.statement: July urea farmer sales at 3.8 lakh tons and NPK at 92-93k tons, pickup of 19-20k tons/day
items.quote: This month itself, we have had almost 3,80,000 tons of farmer sales of urea and almost 92,000-93,000 tons of NPK sales in this month alone. So, that means the pickup is close to 19,000-20,000 tons a day.

items.statement: Kharif sowing caught up to last year levels after July monsoon recovery
items.quote: According to the Ministry of Agriculture, acreage has broadly caught up with last year's levels, while the IMD continues to maintain its forecast of a normal monsoon.

items.quote: This is under the NIP-2012 policy. My understanding is that this is a group other than the NUP-2015. The treatment could likely be different, and we are already in discussions with the government.

items.quote: As of 30th June, total receivables stood at INR 3,300 crores, comprising of market debtors of INR 841 crores and subsidy receivables of INR 2,460 crores.

items.statement: Net borrowing of INR 200 crores as of Q1 FY27
items.quote: We had net borrowing of about INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Dividend policy maintained at 25% of profit, no buyback planned
items.quote: We have a policy in any case. There is a profit number. We have declared that there will be a 25% or so that we will pay for that. So, I don't think that is an issue. items.quote: I would say, my own assessment is that we will be short or slightly long in the market, maybe for not more than a year or so, and which we will have to manage in the situation. But going forth, the market is again going to get short in terms of the demand exceeding supply.

items.statement: India urea consumption 404-405 lakh MT vs production 305-306 lakh MT
items.value: 404-405 lakh MT consumption, 305-306 lakh MT production
items.quote: As you know, we today have a consumption of close to 404, 405 lakh metric tons, while production is only 305, 306 lakh metric tons.

items.quote: Corporate overheads, as you know, we continue to reduce them, and we bought them down by 25%. So we have done a very good job. items.statement: Indonesia installed self-ordering kiosks for first time, increasing average per check by 4-5%
items.quote: We also installed self-ordering kiosks for the first time in Indonesia. which has actually pushed our APC, average per check up by about 4%, 5%.

items.statement: Cash generated will be used for growth of current businesses; no dividend plans indicated
items.quote: As far as the business is concerned, we are very clear that the cash that the business generates will be utilized for the purpose of growth of our businesses. And that's something which is very clearly kind of agreed as a part of our long-term plan.

items.statement: FY27 disbursement target to exceed INR35,000 crore achieved in FY26
items.quote: And the guidance that I've given right in the beginning of the FY that whatever we did last year, we intend to surpass that in this year also.

items.statement: FY27 year-end AUM target around INR5 lakh crore
items.quote: And we'll be hoping to catch around INR5 lakh crores by the end of the year. That guidance remains intact.

items.statement: NIM target of 2% by end of 2030 with ~10 bps annual improvement
items.quote: What we feel that 10 basis points my NIM should grow on an average every year. And that is what we are very meticulously working forward to. And we will reach 2% NIM by the end of 2030.

items.statement: FY27 NIM expected to end above 1.6%
items.quote: This year, we are looking forward to NIM growing. And by the end of the year, when we add more of high-yielding assets in my AUM, we intend to end up more than 1.6%.

items.statement: High-speed rail and DFC pipeline of ~INR20 lakh crore with INR50,000-60,000 crore annual disbursement potential for over a decade
items.quote: Now the total expenses or the planning of the financing is in tune of INR 16 lakh crores for high-speed rail corridor or nearly INR3 lakh crores for DFC coming out to be around INR20 lakh crores. IRFC is actively working for being part of this financial solution. items.statement: Metro and rapid rail expected to bring INR20,000-30,000 crore annual disbursement
items.quote: And apart from that, Metro and rapid rail things should bring around INR20,000 crores to INR30,000 crores every year.

items.statement: Strong demand from high-speed rail corridors, DFC, metro, rapid rail, ports, GenCo and renewable energy linked to railways
items.quote: We are now apart from what we did last year, we are going to proliferate in high-speed and dedicated freight corridor, metro rail, rapid rail, big size port, GenCo, Transcos, any renewable energy projects, which are linked to the railways, these are all on the platter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 NIM at 1.48%; FY26 average NIM improved from 1.40% to 1.50%
items.quote: So what we saw last year is my NIM going from 1.40% average to 1.50% for the whole of FY '26. This year, we are looking forward to NIM growing.

items.statement: New disbursements at ~100 bps margin vs runoff at 35-40 bps, driving NIM expansion
items.quote: And the impact on PAT and NIM will be like this only because whatever we'll be adding will be nearly 100 bps or even more than that kind of margin. And whatever will be deducted from my AUM will be 35 bps or 40 bps margin things.

items.statement: IRFC lending at 8% with >100 bps margin; competitors forced to match efficiency
items.quote: We are very comfortable at 8%. Others were never lending at 8%. So beneficiary is the country, country as a whole. So now onwards, the kind of low overhead cost that IRFC is maintaining and transferring the efficiency to the customers, every other competitor or the sibling in the ecosystem is forced to bring in that efficiency.

items.statement: Fertilizer companies (HURL Gorakhpur, Barauni, Sindri) have direct railway linkage via raw material and finished goods movement on railway sidings
items.quote: So, these are the mega factories which are producing mainly urea and other fertilizers for the country. As you know, we are a urea deficit country. So , government is working very hard on creating indigenous system where we try to produce more and more urea indigenously. S

items.statement: Fertilizer loans refinanced at 40-50 bps lower rate; cost-plus model with government offtake ensures zero risk
items.quote: There was some rate we refinance it by reducing by some 50 or 40 bps I'm giving you a ballpark figure, but obviously, not less than 50 bps reduction that I brought in their cost of borrowing.

items.statement: INR92,799 crore agreements signed in FY26 (greenfield/brownfield); INR37,000 crore disbursed; balance over 1-3 years
items.quote: Now for any greenfield projects, funding is not done in the same year. It takes around 3 to 5 years. So that is how INR92,799 crores, INR37,000 crores we could disburse, and rest are in pipeline where the disbursement will take place in 1 to 3 years.

items.statement: Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 (~125 km, ~INR40,000 crore) under evaluation; Phase 1 refinancing agreement signed
items.quote: Also, we have entered into agreement for refinancing of Phase 1, which is already operational for the last 10 years. And you may be aware that they are coming out with the Phase 2, which is even longer lines of nearly 125 kilometers worth around INR40,000 crores.

items.statement: Zero NPA maintained as business proposition; only lending to best-in-class government-linked entities
items.quote: And one particular thing that we always say that zero NPA is not a kind of status, but a business proposition for us. So, this company going forward, whatever businesses that we look forward to get into a kitty will surely ensure that they are best in the class, probably in whole of government approach, either directly or having some linkage with the government so that our comfort level remains in

items.statement: "Fund in India" model: IRFC as conduit for bilateral/multilateral funds, leveraging to offer bespoke long-tenor solutions
items.quote: Fund in India means that IRFC wants to be a conduit, where the bilaterals or the any multilaterals, if they want to put money in India, they give this money to IRFC. IRFC leverages this money, makes a bigger kitty and it gives a bespoke solution to every customer in the whole of government approach.

items.statement: Q1 other income from yen currency fluctuation (rupee appreciation, yen depreciation) on metro funding; prior quarter had INR7 crore loss
items.quote: That is a normal fluctuation in the currency. So, you can say that we are lucky enough. We have taken some amount in the yen that is part for funding to ongoing metro disbursement for which there is an agreement for metro railway payment, and we are expecting it somewhere in Q2.

items.statement: Q1 AUM dip due to Ind AS accrual of railway repayments received in September; Q1 disbursement ~INR2,000 crore
items.quote: Now disbursement in this quarter is not very high as we did last year also, it is around INR2,000 crores itself. But going forward, as I said it will be picking up.

items.statement: FY26 agreements signed INR75,000+ crore vs INR60,000 crore guidance; disbursement INR35,000+ crore vs INR30,000 crore target
items.quote: As you know, that last year against the guidance of INR60,000 crores, we could sign agreements worth more than INR75,000 crores. And against the target of INR30,000 crores disbursement, we could disburse more than INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: IRFC's low-cost model forcing competitors to improve efficiency; IRFC can lend at 8% with >100 bps margin
items.quote: I am again reiterating everybody is playing on the turf of IRFC now. We are going to be the game changer. If you are following the rates being quoted on the open tender of any of the GenCo and transport, you see what kind of rates are coming now.

items.statement: AUM growth moderation near INR5 lakh crore; focus on margin accretion over balance sheet expansion
items.quote: Obviously, we are already INR5 lakh crores. So, I have given you enough indication when I talk about something on the platter in tune of INR20 lakh crores. It is not that I'm telling you. If you follow my honorable minister, you see what he is talking about, about high-speed rail corridors and these things.

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 80% with EBITDA margin of 24% plus/minus 100 bps, confident of beating guidance
items.quote: I would like to reiterate ou r confidence in achieving the guidance given earlier at 80% revenue growth for the current fiscal year with an EBITDA margin of 24% plus-minus 100 basis points, and we are pretty confident to do better than the guidance given earlier to everyone

items.quote: With the Government of India targeting 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047, we believe the long-term opportunity for the company in this sector is substantial.

items.statement: Bluetile and BestPlay Q1 FY27 revenue INR 518 crores, EBITDA INR 55 crores; consolidation expected from Q2 FY27
items.quote: For reference, the Bluetile and BestPlay business reported INR 518 crores of revenue and INR 55 crores of EBITDA in Q1 FY27. And subject to the final closing, we are expecting to start consolidating this entire business from Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Raymond Stauffer appointed CEO of Nazara Technologies effective 1 September 2026 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: We have also appointed Bluetile CEO and founder - Raymond Stauffer - as CEO of Nazara Technologies, effective 1 September 2026.

items.statement: Nitish Mittersain remains Founder and Managing Director focusing on long-term strategy, portfolio direction and key relationships
items.quote: As Founder and Managing Director, I will continue to shape Nazara's long-term strategy, portfolio direction, and key relationships, working closely with Raymond and the Board.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 429 crores, EBITDA INR 46 crores, PAT loss INR 82 crores in Q1 FY27

EBITDA held flat as UA spend rose from 78% to 85% of revenue, though revenue net of UA spend still increased from INR 73 crores to INR 80 crores.

Transaction sales for Human: Fall Flat and For The King II both increased year-on-year, while more than 60% of the development investment during the quarter was allocated to new signings. items.statement: IronOak Games (For The King) seeing good upside on For The King II; working on new first-party titles for better margins in coming quarters

IronOak Games is also now working on some new titles, which again will be first-party titles and hence, they will deliver better margin as we go along in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Datawrkz revenue INR 126 crores, EBITDA INR 3 crores; Space & Time grew EBITDA YoY showing margin resilience

items.quote: What we keep a look out for is the regulatory environment and the policy decisions, especially in the U.S., which impacts this industry the most.

items.statement: Outcome-based model contracts require customer involvement, signoffs, interim markers as Gen AI needs evolve
items.quote: One other thing that we are looking out for is the performance on our outcome-based model contracts, which we have been operating for a very long time. But in the current age of evolving Gen AI needs, it is also getting the customer involved, getting the signoffs and interim markers being ticked off as we move deeper on those engagements.

items.statement: Margin normalization expected in 6 quarters from Oct 2025 (by Q4 FY27), not 6-8 quarters as earlier guided
items.quote: What we said is 6 to 8. We had got a range over there. We are saying we don't need this range. It's not going to be 6 to 8, it's going to be 6. By March end, we get back to that 19% to 20% range.

items.statement: Confidence in margin recovery based on contracted revenue from signed deals, not future wins
items.quote: The reason we are confident about that this is not resting on some revenue which we'll win in the future. This is resting on revenue which we will, in all probability, be recognizing, contracts which we already have.

items.statement: Constant currency growth approximated at 2.6-2.7% QoQ vs 2.5% USD growth
items.quote: It will be a tad north of our U.S. dollar growth of 2.5%, will be more in the 2.6% to 2.7% range.

items.statement: Revenue per employee grew 25% in last 2 years; cash position strengthened over 30% since listing
items.quote: The revenue per employee grew 25% in the last 2 years to over USD 77,000. And the share of delivery talent with healt hcare expertise has risen to 29% from 22%. Our cash position has strengthened by over 30% in the same period

items.statement: Order book at INR61,500 crores, up from INR50,000 crores a quarter ago, with INR16,000 crores new orders in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crores
items.quote: Taken together, these are proof points across capacity, storage, transmission, EPC and international markets. It is exactly this best of execution that gives us the confidence to reaffirm our operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000 crores to INR7,700 crores of FY27.

items.statement: Announced capex of INR31,500 crores, INR9,450 crores deployed by June 2026, phased 30% FY27, 40% FY28, 30% FY29
items.quote: Our announced capex programs total around INR31,500 crores, of which we have already deployed around INR9,450-odd crores as of 30th of June. It is around 30% in FY27, roughly 40% in '28 and around 30% in FY29.

items.statement: Imported cell price USD0.04-0.045/Wp; local manufacturing cost USD0.07-0.08/Wp; DCR market pricing USD0.12-0.13/Wp
items.quote: If you look at the current import price of around USD0.04 to USD0.045 per watt peak basis in local markets, our manufacturing cost is around USD0.07 to USD0.08 and the market pricing in terms of the DCR market is around USD0.12 to USD0.13 per watt peak.

items.statement: Retail revenue up 130% YoY to INR2,289 crores; targeting INR9,000-10,000 crores for FY27; e-commerce scaling fast
items.quote: Retail grew 130% year-on-year from INR995 crores to INR2,289-odd crores of revenue this quarter. And we are looking at this segment heading towards a range of INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores for the full year FY27.

items.statement: Top 5 customer share down to 27.1% from 33% in FY26; top 10 down to 37.1% from 47%
items.quote: Our top 5 customer share has now come down from 33% in FY26 to around 27.1%. Our top 10 customer sales came down from 47% to around 37.1% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Export realization USD0.25-0.26/Wp; DCR USD0.20-0.25/Wp; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14/Wp; US local manufacturing margin USD0.07-0.08/Wp including IRA
items.value: Export USD0.25-0.26/Wp, DCR USD0.20-0.25/Wp, non-DCR USD0.13-0.14/Wp
items.quote: The export market, whatever we have exported, the realization is between $0.25 to $0.26 cents per watt peak basis. The DCR market continues to stand across $0.20 to $0.25 per watt peak basis on realization terms. And non-DCR markets continue to range between $0.13 to $0.14 per watt.

items.statement: ALMM I, II, III, 20% customs duty, PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM support domestic manufacturing; US IRA, UFLPA, FEOC drive traceable non-China supply chain
items.quote: In India, the PLI incentive the ALMM List ALMM I, II and now III, at 20% custom duty on imports, demand schemes like PM Surya Ghar yojana, PM-KUSUM yojana, all of this support domestic manufacturing and integration. Globally, in our U.S. facilities, the IRA, the UFLPA, FEOC rules combined together are driving traceable non-Chinese supply chain for our U.S. clients.

items.statement: Revenue mix: utility/IPP/C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC/O&M 8.9%; module volumes 3.6 GW, up 89% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, utility IPP, C&I contributed around 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2% and EPC and O&M services 8.9%. Our module volumes sold during the quarter grew 89% over the prior period from 1.9 gigawatts to 3.6 gigawatts.

items.statement: Net cash balance sheet, net debt/equity -0.08x as of June 30, 2026; ROCE 28.5%, ROE 24.8%
items.quote: And on our return ratios, we continue to run a net cash balance sheet with a net debt to equity of minus 0.08x as on 30th of June, an ROCE of 28.5% and ROE of 24.8%.

items.statement: Board and shareholder approval for INR10,000 crores fund raise via equity/QIP; INR7,000 crores cash on hand as of June 30; capex outflow 30% in FY27, 40% FY28, 30% FY29
items.quote: If you look at the approval that we have taken from Board and shareholders to have around INR10,000 crores worth of fund raised through various channels, including equity. Right now, our balance sheet stands at around INR7,000 crores worth of cash available as of 30th of June.

items.statement: WRTL acquired 55% stake in Associated Power Structures for ~INR1,225 crores, extending into T&D
items.quote: WRTL completed the acquisition of an approximately 55% stake in Associated Power Structures for approximately INR1,225 crores, extending our reach decisively into transmission and distribution.

items.statement: Cell production ~400 MW/month in Q1, targeting 420-430 MW/month (1.3-1.4 GW/quarter); 10 GW cell facility to add from Q3
items.quote: As I mentioned just now that from the same facility, we are already starting to see around 400 megawatts of monthly production. Going ahead, this can go between 420 to 430 megawatt of monthly production leading to a quarterly ramp up of around 1.3 to 1.4 gigawatt from the same facility.

items.statement: US IRA incentives ~USD12-13 million on 230 MW in Q1; production to rise to 400-500 MW from Q3; incentives receivable quarterly from Q3/Q4
items.quote: Like this quarter, we have around USD12 million to USD13 million worth of IRA incentives on account of roughly 230-odd megawatts of production. Going ahead, we are looking at the same production go up between 400 to 500 megawatts starting from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: FY27 capex includes 2.6 GW US module, 10 GW India cell, 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformer, 4 GW inverter, 1 GW electrolyzer
items.quote: In FY27, which absorbs around 30% of overall capex. We shall be adding 2.6 gigawatt of module capacity in Waaree Americas. 10 gigawatt solar cell capacities in India, 100 KTPA of T&D EPC is already acquired, 20 GVA of transformer capacity, 4 gigawatt of inverter and 1 gigawatt of electrolyzer capacity.

items.statement: Global solar additions 698 GW (2025) to 993 GW (2035), ~4-5% CAGR; India 38 GW (2025) to ~100 GW (2035), ~10% CAGR; India added 26 GW in H1 CY2026 vs 18 GW prior year
items.quote: Globally, the annual additions are expected to grow from 698 gigawatt in 2025 to 993 gigawatt by 2035, roughly 4% to 5% CAGR. With global capacity having crossed 3 terawatt already in 2026, India additions are growing much faster from 38 gigawatt in '25 to around 100 gigawatt by 2035, are 10% CAGR over next 10 years.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved in Q1 due to controlled inventory; non-DCR offtake picking up from Q2 with 6-month ALMM-II extension
items.quote: In terms of the cash flow, like quarter one itself, our operating cash flow has been far better because of controlled inventory that has continued. Our production also now moving to a scenario wherein the offtake has started happening from the non-DCR community which was a little softer in Q1.

items.statement: BESS: 3.5 GWh cell + 5.15 GWh pack/container in FY27; 90-95% site construction done, equipment at site/ports; cell production starting next 2 quarters; 1,520 MWh EPC order won
items.quote: have done more than 90% -- 95% of site construction. All the equipments have already arrived either at the site or are lying at the ports. So, we have control of all the equipment, which is the BESS news here. We have recently started the container line, which should also follow the pack line over 60 days at the same facility

items.statement: BESS FEOC-compliant cell pricing USD75-80/kWh vs Chinese USD50-55/kWh (25-30% premium); two revenue streams: Make in India for overseas (cell) and Make in India for India/export (pack/container)
items.quote: In terms of the realization per megawatt hour basis for the cell -- for the FEOC compliant, the numbers are around 25% to 30% higher than Chinese cell pricing. Currently, USD50 -- USD55 per kilowatt hour is the price of Chinese cell against it, the non-FEOC market is ranging between USD75 to USD80.

items.statement: FY28 step jump: ~15.4 GW cell operational, ~10 GW cell production, 16-18 GW module production; FY29 BESS 16.5 GWh phase 2
items.quote: '28 is when the entire 15.4 gigawatt will be operational. And we could look at close to 10 gigawatt of production from cell. So close to 16-odd gigawatt of module -- 16 to 18 gigawatt of module and 10-odd gigawatt of cell production is what we are looking at in FY '28 as a very big step jump.

items.statement: Varun Goenka (President, Growth & Strategy) and Abhishek Pareek (CFO) led Q&A; Jignesh Rathod (CEO) gave opening/closing remarks
items.quote: We have from the management, Mr. Jignesh Rathod, Whole-Time Director and CEO; Mr. Abhishek Pareek, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Varun Goenka, President, Growth and Strategy.

items.statement: Targeting near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in 4-5 years; retail + BESS + data center demand (15-20 GW additional) + industry consolidation (ALMM/ALCM) + exports/US manufacturing as growth levers
items.quote: But then more important point is our aspiration, vision and execution towards in less than -- or maybe in 4 years or less than 5 years, the near INR1 lakh crore vision is what Waaree is building towards.

items.statement: Targets full-year PAT profitability for FY27 with INR40 crores PAT and INR75 crores EBITDA
items.quote: We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.

items.statement: Expects lending disbursements to reach INR1,000 crores per quarter in coming quarters
items.quote: We are expecting to grow the disbursements in lending from the current baseline of about INR700 crores to INR1,000 crores every quarter in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Guides net payments take rate at 12-14 bps on gross profit level long-term
items.quote: But we continue to guide in the roughly 12 bps to 14 bps in terms of net payments take rate. That is what we are focused on.

items.statement: Expects mature consumer payments revenue to grow 5-6% quarterly and merchant payments revenue to grow 25% quarterly
items.value: 5% to 6% quarterly for consumer, 25% quarterly for merchant
items.quote: We feel comfortable that the mature consumer payment businesses, we will expect 5% to 6% quarterly growth in terms of revenue. That is our expectation for ourselves. And in the emerging and fast-growing merchant businesses, we expect that we'll be able to grow about 25% in terms of revenue quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Expects long-range financial services net margin between 4.5% to 5.5%
items.quote: On a long-range basis we believe that this will continue to be between 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: UPI transactions grew 5x faster than industry making MobiKwik second fastest-growing TPAP
items.quote: In terms of UPI, the company's UPI transactions grew 5x faster than the overall industry, making MobiKwik the second fastest-growing TPAP, UPI app in the country.

items.statement: Platform GMV reached all-time high of INR587 billion, up 50% YoY, 14th straight quarter of growth
items.quote: In terms of the payments business, the platform GMV of the company reached an all-time high of INR587 billion. This is 50% up YoY. This is also the 14th straight quarter of growth in payments GMV that the company has delivered.

items.statement: Payments gross profit up 31% YoY to INR777 million, financial services gross profit grew 5.6x YoY to INR433 million
items.value: INR777 million payments, INR433 million financial services
items.quote: In terms of the margin expansion story, payments gross profit landed at INR777 million, up 31% YoY, whereas the financial services gross profit grew 5.6x YoY and landed at INR433 million, demonstrating robust credit quality.

items.statement: Contribution profit rose 66% YoY, direct costs down 21% YoY (payments 15%, lending 40%)
items.quote: In terms of the cost, we have been able to do a great job at compressing costs at scale. Direct costs have been brought down 21% YoY. For payments side, the direct cost was down 15%. Lending side, the direct cost was down 40%.

items.statement: Merchant GMV at INR125 billion in Q1, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion
items.quote: We have done about INR125 billion in Q1 in mercha nt GMV. And this number was INR 107 billion last quarter, so that's a 17% Q-o-Q growth in the merchant GMV

items.statement: Targets 10x ramp-up in merchant business revenue over two years
items.quote: What we had said last time is that in two years we expect to do a 10x ramp-up here.

items.statement: INR25 crores available from IPO proceeds for merchant device purchases, expects to utilize fully this year
items.quote: Roughly INR25 crores is what we have available to buy more devices out of the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: Added two new lending partners in Q1, adding more in Q2, currently 9 major partners
items.quote: In Q1 also, we have added two new partners which will further scale up in Q2.

items.statement: Built AI engine to detect and address drop-offs in lending funnel, expects INR100 crores additional quarterly disbursements
items.quote: We have built our own AI engine which will automatically detect the steps at which a user is getting dropped off, and according to the place in the funnel the drop-off is happening, will automatically address that and therefore try to get the user back into the funnel and get the user converted.

items.statement: Cross-sell initiatives target INR150-250 crores incremental quarterly disbursements from 96M engaged users via pre-approved offers
items.value: INR150 crores to INR250 crores per quarter
items.quote: We are looking to tap into them and generate roughly about INR150 crores to INR250 crores of additional disbursement every quarter.

items.statement: Paused card-linked payment categories (rent, education) due to regulatory guardrails, plans to re-launch in Q2
items.quote: And to that extent, we just mentioned that we have also paused one of our products in Q4 as well as in Q1 and we intend to re-launch it in Q2.

items.statement: RBI mandated PPI on UPI MDR but NPCI has not rolled it out despite 2.5 years, causing revenue loss
items.quote: Although RBI had mandated it, but NPCI has still not rolled it out despite 2.5 years. So there again, we are losing revenue.

items.statement: NBFC license approved in April with condition to move digital lending to subsidiary, shareholder approval received July 2, targeting CoR after August migration
items.quote: When we received the approval on NBFC application from RBI in April, one of the conditions of that was that we have to take the digital lending business from the parent company MobiKwik to a wholly-owned subsidiary.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR437 crores as of June 30
items.quote: So, the net cash that the company has is INR437 crores.

items.statement: Repaid all long-term loans by March 2026, only short-term working capital facilities of INR320 crores from two private banks for payment settlements
items.quote: As of financial year 26 end, which is 31st March, we have repaid all our long-term loans. So, the only loans that we have now are short-term working capital facilities which are from two major private banks, the total of value of which is INR320 crores.

items.statement: Credit quality improved 25%, 60% of loans to repeat customers, FLDG mix 68% currently targeting 60% by year-end
items.quote: In terms of the credit quality improvement, we saw 25% improvement and 60% of the loans this time went to repeat customers.

items.statement: UPI GMV INR269 billion, non-UPI GMV INR317 billion (6% QoQ growth), Zaakpay GMV INR25.6 billion
items.quote: For the quarter, it was INR 269 billion in terms of UPI GMV. The remaining roughly INR300-odd billion is non-UPI GMV.

items.statement: Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV only 24% YoY due to lower ticket sizes and Pocket UPI usage
items.quote: One, people are using wallet more and more for lower ticket transactions. More people are using Pocket UPI, which is effectively using wallet and paying on a UPI QR code.

items.statement: Merchant business burn limited to INR50-60 crores annually, employee costs up from INR46 to INR53 crores QoQ
items.quote: We had said that we don't expect for the full year merchant business burn will be more than INR50 crores to INR60 crores and we are running on that timetable only on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Carry forward tax losses of INR900-1,000 crores, no tax payment expected anytime soon
items.quote: Yes, we have substantial losses. I don't have the exact number, but it will be somewhere in the range of INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance of INR520-540 crores
items.quote: We are maintaining the guidance of EBITDA between about INR520 crores to INR540 crores.

items.statement: Plans INR400 crores capex for greenfield cotton plant in MP with 72,500 spindles
items.quote: Yes, so we are trying to put in about INR400 crores of capex there at MP to install that 72,500 spindles of cotton yarn.

items.statement: Technical textile capacity at Silvassa doubled from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA, commercial production expected shortly
items.quote: We have recently completed the installation of the plant and machinery for the expansion of our technical textile capacity at Silvassa, taking the installed capacity from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Punjab polymerization capacity at 700 MTPD with 80% utilization in Q1, targeting 85-90% in Q2 and 95-96% thereafter
items.quote: At Punjab, our polymerization capacity is at 700 metric tons per day, and we have achieved a capacity utilization for the quarter at about 80%.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 2 expansion to 900 MTPD on track for commissioning by Q1 FY28
items.quote: We are on course with that. Coming first quarter next year, we will be fully commissioned with the second phase also. So what we are at 700 tons per day today, we aim to be at 900 tons per day by then.

items.statement: Targets Punjab EBITDA of INR30,000 per ton for filament yarn next year vs Silvassa blended INR11,000 per ton
items.quote: And we are targeting Punjab to give us next year about close to INR30,000 per ton.

items.statement: Expects better demand in July-September quarter, particularly from end of August through September
items.quote: So July, August, September quarter, we expecting a better demand, particularly going onwards from the end of August till the end of September, yes.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through occurred with slight delay as customers deferred purchases during volatility
items.quote: The pass-through happened with a slight delay as customers deferred purchases, waiting for stability through the constant price volatility.

items.statement: Government waived 11% customs duty on raw cotton imports from June 1, 2026 to ease input pressure
items.quote: The rise in cotton was steep enough that the government stepped in and temporarily waived the 11% customs duty on raw cotton imports with effect from June 1st, 2026, to ease input pressure across the value chain.

items.statement: PTA sourcing: Punjab 100% from IOCL Panipat; Silvassa 40% domestic contracted, 60% imported with short-term contracts
items.quote: As far as we are concerned, today's thing, we get all our raw material from the IOCL Panipat plant at Punjab. And for Silvassa, we are 50% / 60% on imported PTA and 40% on domestic PTA.

items.statement: In talks with GAIL and IOCL Paradip for domestic PTA supply once commissioned, but cannot finalize until production starts
items.quote: Yes, we are already in contact and we are already in talks with them, once they come into production, how to get more material from them and what terms and what contractual terms.

items.statement: Raw material inventory at quarter end: 8-10 days; Polyester finished goods inventory: 12-13 days at both sites; Cotton finished goods: ~7 days
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, we were holding about, let's see, about 8, 9 days of inventory, 10 days max.

items.statement: Consolidated yarn sales of 1 lakh metric tons in Q1: 54,000 MT from Silvassa, 46,000 MT from Punjab
items.quote: At a consolidated level, we sold 1 lakh metric tons of yarn. From this, 54,000 metric tonne was sold from the Silvassa facility across all three yarn verticals, and approximately 46,000 tonne were sold from the Punjab facility.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 55.38% YoY to INR108.08 crores; margin stable at 8.10% vs 8.08% QoQ
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR108.08 crores, compared to INR94.43 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR69.56 crores in Q1 FY26, representing a growth of 14.46% quarter-on-quarter and 55.38% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 233 bps YoY to 11.67% driven by disciplined procurement and favorable product mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 11.67% against 10.96% in Q4 FY26 and 9.34% in Q1 FY26, an expansion of 72 basis point sequentially and 233 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Technical textile utilization at Silvassa was 94% on 9,000 MTPA capacity before expansion
items.quote: And the utilization was about 94%.

items.statement: Punjab revenue ~INR550 crores with EBITDA ~INR12 crores in Q1
items.quote: Yes, the revenue was close to INR550 crores and the EBITDA was close to INR12 odd crores.

items.statement: 32 MW hybrid wind-solar captive power project commissioning in phases to meaningfully reduce power costs
items.quote: We are also progressing on the renewable energy front through our captive arrangement of 32 megawatts of hybrid wind-solar power, which will be commissioned in phases and expected to deliver a meaningful reduction of our power costs as it comes online.

items.statement: Spreads improved across all three verticals (polyester, cotton, technical) sequentially from Q4 to Q1
items.quote: It has improved. The spreads have improved across divisions, all three verticals.

items.statement: Geopolitical environment remains fluid; full impact on demand, logistics, energy prices and supply chains difficult to assess precisely
items.quote: The global geopolitical environment remains fluid, and the full impact on demand, logistics, energy prices, and supply chains continues to be difficult to assess with any precision.

items.statement: Depreciation rose from INR11.7 to INR34.7 crores and finance costs from INR4.62 to INR38.6 crores due to Punjab plant commissioning
items.quote: Depreciation rose from INR11.7 crores to INR34.7 crores, and the finance costs from INR4.62 crores to INR38.6 crores. That difference is the entire story.

items.statement: Both facilities operated seamlessly without interruption despite global and local supply chain disruption
items.quote: Both our facilities operated seamlessly and without interruption through a period of significant global and local supply chain disruption.

items.statement: Focus on deepening customer relationships across both markets as operational priority for rest of FY27
items.quote: Overall, our operational priority for the rest of FY27 is to improve our production efficiency and capacity utilization, to improve and tweak our product optimization, especially at Punjab, and bring the expanded technical textiles capacity at Silvassa into commercial production, along with deepening customer relationships across both markets.

items.statement: Cotton import duty waiver temporary; climate-related risk flagged as key monitorable for raw cotton pricing and availability
items.quote: Raw cotton pricing and availability remains a key monitorable factor for the coming season, particularly given the ongoing global disruption emerging from climate-related risk.

items.statement: Management reiterated confidence in delivering double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.
items.quote: we remain very confident on delivering double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

items.statement: Management stated comfort with average net debt to EBITDA of 2.5x in coming years, up and down in some quarters.
items.quote: we have always given the guidance that we are comfortable to an average of 2.5x in the coming years, up and down in some quarters.

items.statement: Management confirmed on track to achieve INR20 billion EBITDA target by FY30.
items.quote: we are on track, we are moving in the right direction to achieve the targets that we have committed.

items.statement: Management expects ROCE to reach mid-to-high teens in coming years as new hotels become operational.
items.quote: This will go to mid-to-high teens ROCE in the coming years in few years when all the new hotels will become operational.

items.statement: International room revenue mix for five owned palace hotels recovered from 10% YoY decline in March to 1% YoY increase by June.
items.quote: the in ternational room revenue mix for our five owned palace hotels recovered progressively through the quarter, moving from a 10% Y-o-Y decline in March to a 1% Y-o-Y increase by June

items.statement: Domestic room revenue increased 25% YoY at five palace hotels driven by event-led business, long stay offers, and digital activations.
items.quote: As a result, domestic room revenue increased by 25% year -on-year at our five palace hotels.

items.statement: Management expects international demand to normalize in H2 FY27 with peak months October to March, creating further inventory compression and pricing power.
items.quote: Typically, the months from October to March are the peak months for international travellers, and being, and from there, November to February are the busiest because that's when the international FTOs and the tourists and the MICE and incentives from international travellers also start happening.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA grew 41% YoY to INR143 crores with record Q1 EBITDA margin of 41%, driven by over 60% flow-through excluding Coorg and disciplined cost management.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew 41% year-on-year to INR143 crores, highlighting the strong operating leverage of our business model and resulting in a record first quarter EBITDA margin of 41%.

items.statement: Management targets maintaining EBITDA margins around 50% with marginal year-on-year growth as RevPAR grows.
items.quote: we already operate a very significant good EBITDA, we are around 50%, and we intend to maintain that and marginally grow it year-on-year as our RevPAR grows.

items.statement: Portfolio expanded to 25 properties with 5,257 keys across 15 operational hotels and 10 in pipeline, maintaining roughly half owned and half managed structure.
items.quote: Following this addition, our portfolio now stands at 25 properties with 5,257 keys across 15 operational hotels and 10 in the pipeline. We are also maint aining a balanced structure with roughly half our keys owned and half managed, enabling us to scale while preserving capital flexibility

items.statement: Signed concession agreement for 30-key luxury resort in Tadoba, Maharashtra, with INR1,200 million investment under 60-year concession extendable by 30 years, targeted for CY30 completion.
items.quote: During the quarter, we signed a concession agreement to develop a premium resort in Tadoba in Maharashtra, an underserved premium wildlife tourism location. The development will comprise 30 luxury keys spread across a 62 -acre site. The INR1,200 million project is to be developed under a 60-year concession agreement with an opportunity to extend for another 30 years and is targeted for completion

items.statement: Tadoba project expected to generate 15-17% yield on cost (YOC).
items.quote: that's a very value accretive deal for us, Karan, and we'll generate 15% to 17% of YOC on that deal, just to give that number.

items.statement: Jaisalmer and Leela Residences Mumbai on track for early CY27 opening; Srinagar and Bandhavgarh targeted for Q4 CY27 (Oct-Dec); Agra, Ayodhya, Sikkim, Ranthambore for CY28; Tadoba for CY30.
items.quote: This year, by the year-end, we'll be opening Jaisalmer and the Leela Residences. We are on track to open Agra, Ayodhya, and Sikkim, and Ranthambore in CY28. And we have added Tadoba to the mix, which will open in CY30.

items.statement: Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary rebranded on 8th July ahead of schedule; ADR nearly doubled post-acquisition and asset broke even operationally in Q1 before rebranding.
items.quote: We unveiled The Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary, the new identity for our recently acquired operational resort, on 8th July ahead of schedule. Notably, the ADR at Coorg has nearly doubled post our acquisition, and the asset broke even operationally in the qua rter even before its rebranding

items.statement: Direct website booking contribution doubled to 16% vs Q1 FY26, reducing reliance on higher-cost third-party channels; direct acquisition cost nearly one-third of OTA cost.
items.quote: During the quarter, the contribution of the Leela brand website booking doubled to 16% versus Q1 FY26, reducing reliance on the higher -cost third-party channels and enhancing distribution economics.

items.statement: Renewable energy share at 67% across five palace hotels, targeting 75%; helps lower fixed costs.
items.quote: Plus our renewable share of energy is around 67%, which we intend to take it to 75%.

items.statement: HMA fees grew 86% YoY to INR262 million driven by managed portfolio ramp-up, performance-linked fees, and past key money investments.
items.quote: HMA fees grew 86% to INR262 million, driven by ramp -up of managed properties, including higher fees in some contracts linked to performance and past key money investment, while other operational service revenues increased by 26%.

items.statement: Net Promoter Score at industry-leading 86, 12 points above APAC luxury average; ranked world's second-best hotel brand in Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2026.
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, our Net Promoter Score stood at an industry -leading 86, remaining 12 points above the luxury hospitality average in the APAC region.

items.statement: RevPAR grew 17% YoY (10% ADR growth, 4pp occupancy improvement) to 1.4x RevPAR index; same-store RevPAR growth 15% excluding Coorg.

items.statement: Resort occupancy target mid-60s over next 3-4 years from current ~59% blended FY26, driven by 12-month programming and multi-generational travel.
items.quote: We would be able to go to mid-60s, but that's our growth trajectory that we intend to go to, and we are confident we'll be on track.

items.statement: City hotel occupancy can cross 75% threshold but focus remains on ADR-driven growth rather than occupancy maximization.
items.quote: obviously a lot of luxury hotel do operate in the market that in close to 80%, we can obviously cross 75% threshold as well, but we are more, target towards driving the ADR, and accordingly the growth from the ADR side rather than occupancy.

items.statement: Dubai JV handover from current operator and renovation start early CY27, 12-month rehab, rebrand to Leela; residential sales plan unchanged (2-3 year period).
items.quote: We'll get the handover from the current operator and start the rehab early next year, and as per our plan, we intend to complete the renovation in the next 12-months and rebrand to Leela.

items.statement: Launched Leela Centre of Excellence (LCOE), 9,600 sq ft learning hub with Le Cordon Bleu, to train 3,000+ associates over 3 years; conducted LEAD program at IIM Ahmedabad for 20 executive committee members.
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched The Leela Centre of Excellence (LCOE), a 9,600 square feet purpose-built learning hub developed in partnership with Le Cordon Bleu. The LCOE will help institutionalize The Leela's service standards at scale, support a future -ready talent pipeline, and is expected to train more than 3,000 associates over the next three years to support our portfolio expansion.

items.statement: Dubai JV impacted by West Asia conflict reducing travel flows, occupancy and ADR; asset operationally break-even but accounting loss due to interest and depreciation; Leela 25% share reflected in share of profit of JV.
items.quote: While the Dubai hotel continues to be operational, reduced travel flows due to the West Asia conflict have impacted both occupancy and ADR for the time being. However, the asset is operationally break-even despite this being an off-peak period on the back of demand from local business and leisure segments, including MICE and staycation. items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR1900-1950 crores, ~30% growth over FY26
items.quote: Because in this financial year 27, we have targeted a revenue of close to INR1900 crores to INR1950 crores which would be almost a growth of 30% over the last financial year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 10.5-11.5%, normalizing from Q2
items.quote: And also going forward, as we have always guided the market, our EBITDA margins from this quarter onwards will be normalized at 10.5 % to 11.5%.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target INR2000 crores, INR580 crores booked in Q1
items.quote: Yes, I think we have guided the market in the month of May that total order in target for us in this financial year is INR2000 crores.

items.statement: Order book INR1380 crores as of June 30, 2026, up 150% YoY, visibility 6-8 months
items.quote: As we speak today, so the total order book for us as on 30th of June 26 was almost INR1380 crores giving us a clear visibility for the next 6 and 8 months, 6 to 8 months and also the run-up for the entire financial year '27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order inflow INR580 crores vs INR240 crores in Q1 FY26, 150% growth
items.quote: So in the order book, there was a growth of 150%. So as compared to INR240 crores orders that we booked in the Quarter 1 of last year, this year, we have been able, in this quarter, last quarter we have been able to book INR580 crores of orders.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.4% vs 10.5% YoY, 100 bps contraction due to steel price spike
items.quote: So EBITDA margin in the first quarter last year was 10.5 which stands at 9.4% and we during our first during our last investor call in the month of May for the entire year '26 have already stressed upon the fact that due to the commodity price increase coming from the war in the Middle East, there was a immediate abrupt steel price increase.

items.statement: Margins expected to normalize to 10.5% from Q2 FY27 as old orders executed and new orders at revised pricing
items.quote: Definitely, yes. The margins will definitely come back to the old level of 10.5%, close to 10.5% from this quarter onwards because, like I think the increase -- the impact of the commodity price increase has now behind us and most of the new orders that we have booked are based on the increased commodity prices.

items.statement: Ghiloth sandwich panel line commissioning end of Q2, commercial production Q3; AP second line Q3; Gujarat 50k ton plant commissioning Q4, production from April 2027
items.quote: Yes. So first of all, the Ghiloth sandwich panel line would be commissioned by the end of this quarter, so commercial production likely to start from the next quarter onwards. items.statement: Prefab division avg capacity utilization 75%+; sandwich panel line at Mambattu 44% in Q1, targeting 70%+ for FY27
items.quote: The total average capacity utilization of the prefab division was almost 75% plus and also the good part has been the ramp up in the capacity utilization of the sandwich panel line that we had put up in our Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh plant. So there also the capacity utilization was almost 45% as compared to the utilization of 25% that was done in the last financial year.

items.statement: Strong capex cycle driving order growth; energy sector (renewables, transformers, wires/cables) major contributor, logistics 24-25%, auto 10% of order book
items.quote: Most of the orders at this time are coming from energy sector, so be it the renewable energy, the transformers, the wires and cable industry, and also our , conventional industries are typically the logistics, so logistics is contributing about 24 % to 25% of the total order book for us. Similarly, auto is contributing about 10% and few other, commodities, like cement and steel.

items.quote: So of the total order book, if we talk about it may not be major, it may be just 4% to 5% of the total order book right now. items.quote: The reason of having this INR75 crores equity plan is basically to set up a manufacturing facility. So we have to get the land in place before we can actually plan for product development and things like that. So with that purpose, like we have earmarked INR75 crores for now.

items.statement: Export start: INR2.5 crores sandwich panels to Africa in Q1; building export team, targeting PEB structures too; no quantified 2-3 year target yet
items.quote: We have export -- we have exported sandwich panels, so insulated sandwich panels we exported to Africa, African nation, and it has been a good start point. items.statement: Existing clients 40-45% of revenue; win rate ~20% overall, higher for existing clients (30-40%); market share ~5-6% in FY26, targeting 7-7.5% by FY27 end
items.quote: Yes, typically for us, existing clients contribute around 40 % to 45% because not every client will have a repeat order or would not make like factory every year. So it is around 40% to 45% for us.

items.statement: Most orders fixed-price; mitigate commodity risk by weekly order booking at current prices; steel prices up 12-15% post war, balance sheet impact only 1%
items.quote: So most of our orders are fixed price mechanism orders only and the pass -through doesn't work because we procure raw material at a different point of time and then the production and the logistics and installation at the site happens. So it creates confu sion with the customer. So it's better to have a fixed price contract.

items.statement: Average order size increased from INR6.5 crores to INR12-13 crores due to large renewable order; median lower due to sandwich panel/modular mix
items.quote: Our last year average order size was around INR6.5 crores, but because last quarter we got this INR165 crores order, so now it would be almost INR12 crores to INR13 crores is the average order size of the total pending order book right now.

items.quote: Yes, the only challenge in this quarter could be the monsoon. So because of monsoons, the civil works get delayed. But as far as our role is concerned, I really don't see any major challenge there.

items.quote: We are just one player in the noodles category, is still around 35, 36. Even in urban, we would be half of biscuits.

items.quote: All our businesses are getting healthy growth. I spoke about coffee, 20 quarters of double-digit growth, so it is not just a confectionery thing.

items.quote: we did run out of capacity , we are putting in more capacity , but the growth we are seeing is equally strong

items.quote: We are not chasing growth at the cost of margin. We will deliver and maintain our margin in line with our past track record.

items.quote: You are aware like close to 80% of the snacking market is still below Rs.20. Consumers are very, they aspire for brands, but it is our job to make it affordable for them.

items.quote: We have one of the best fill rates. And which is why I keep on saying that we have a far more sustainable, collaborative model with the q-commerce platforms.

items.quote: In our business there are two things which are critical, the brands and the people.

items.quote: While we are concerned about some of the rising costs and the challenges, I think the last one year clearly gives me the confidence that my team has the resilience to work around it and while there could be a month of up and down, I believe this growth story, the secular growth story remains in place strongly.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR1,450-1,500 crores with 12% EBITDA margin target
items.quote: We had projected a margin of 12% EBITDA over this INR1,500 crores. So quarter 1 has been 9%. We hope to recover the rest in the 3 quarters that are to come to average out 12%. We are still maintaining that.

items.statement: Garment division targeting INR100 crores per quarter for next 3 quarters
items.quote: So I'm confident that we're looking at possibly a INR100 crores quarter sales from here onwards on the garment side.

items.statement: INR140 crores capex planned and sanctioned for FY27 in fabric, garment and common infrastructure
items.quote: This year, we will be investing another about INR140 crores is planned and already sanctioned. And we will be making these investments in fabric and garment and some in common infrastructure.

items.statement: Planning 20-25% capacity expansion in garment and 20% in fabric for FY28
items.quote: I mean in general, we are looking at an expansion next year of about 20%, 25% in garment and an expansion of about 20%. I'm talking now '27-'28 FY.

items.statement: Garment order book fully booked through December, fabric order book strong through November
items.quote: Our order book continues to be robust and is fully booked through to November and even Decemb er now, providing us with strong revenue visibility and confidence for the coming quarters

items.statement: Demand healthy for fabric and garment for next 2 quarters, meeting or slightly surpassing projections
items.quote: And I think, yes, the demand is definitely looking good for both, I can say, for both fabric and garment, at least for the next 2 quarters is looking very healthy and meeting our projections or somewhat slightly surpassing our projections.

items.statement: India-U.K. FTA effective July 15, 2026 eliminating import duties, benefits to accrue from coming quarters
items.quote: The elimination of import duties on Indian textiles and apparel entering the U.K. is expected to significantly improve the competitiveness of Indian manufacturers and strengthen our position as a preferred sourcing destination.

items.statement: Garment exports to U.K. currently INR20-25 crores, expected to double to INR50 crores next year
items.quote: On the garment, currently, it is pretty moderate. It's about INR20 crores to INR25 crores. But we have now got a good inquiry pipeline, and we expect this to double next year to at least INR50 crores.

items.statement: Added new global brands C&A and NEXT in garment, deepened engagement with Mango, Celio, Walmart, Haggar
items.quote: We continue to deepen our engagement with existing customers with increased business from our global brands such as Mango, Celio and Walmart. At the same time, we have expanded our customer portfolio through the addition of international new brands such as C&A and NEXT.

items.statement: Increasing share of value-added products: bi-stretch fabrics, poly viscose, poly-rich blends, wool blends in fabric; jackets volume rising to 800K-900K annually
items.quote: We have been consciously increasing the share of premium product categories such as our bi-stretch fabrics, both in poly viscose and poly-rich blends, wool blends, in our portfolio.

items.quote: So when we will look at restarting Surat, we would look at it in a way of investing fresh into Surat and completely making a modern plant with new machinery. items.quote: And with garment, at least you'll have the opportunity to earn 10%, 12% EBITDA, and that will be our target. So from a situation of probably coming of low 3%, 4% EBITDA, we will probably move higher to 8%, 10% EBITDA and possibly even push to 12%.
