So you will definitely see volatility linked to raw materials as the raw material softens in future, pricing, of course, will get corrected to some extent. But there is some element which is also linked

items.statement: Working capital expanded due to higher feedstock prices and increased export volumes; debt and finance costs rose
items.quote: Working capital requirements expanded during the quarter, driven by higher feedstock prices and increased export volumes. Consequently, debt levels and finance costs rose to support this requirement.

items.statement: West Asia revenue share fell from 15% to 2% due to conflict; volumes redirected to other markets; export revenue 59% of total
items.quote: The West Asia crisis had a direct impact on our Energy business, temporarily halting exports to the region. The region's share in our revenues declined from about 15% to 2% in this quarter. We successfully redirected a significant portion of these volumes to other markets, limiting the overall business impact.

items.statement: Forex volatility: rupee ranged INR 92-97 in Q1; gains from timing of import purchases and export realizations
items.quote: We saw rupee ranging from a level of INR92 to INR97 in the quarter and hence wherever the opportunities are there, we will look to capitalize on those.

items.statement: Zone 4 product mix diversified across agro, pharma, coatings, polymers; not heavy on single end market
items.quote: The product mix that we are currently starting with is very well diversified. It has a mix of agro, it has a mix of pharma, it has mix of coating, it has mixed of polymers. And we remain to have a different sort of segregated differential end market exposure for the overall Zone IV capabilities. It will not be heavy towards one particular end market.

items.statement: Long-term contracts execution stable, underpinning baseline volume growth and revenue visibility
items.quote: Execution across all our long-term contracts remains stable, continuing to underpin baseline volume growth and safeguard revenue visibility.

items.statement: Fuel additives faces significant competition from 2-3 Indian and 2-3 Chinese players; strategy includes new products, differentiated offerings, global supply chain, unique distribution, top-decile cost structure
items.quote: I would say there is already significant competition in this product. I think there are more than two or three players in India, which have entered this market and there are more than 2 or 3 players in China which are currently playing in this market. We continue to maintain our market leadership position and we will continue to do so. The strategy involves multiple aspects. I would not go into th

items.statement: China suspended export tax rebates creating favourable opportunities for NCB value chain products
items.quote: The suspension of export tax rebates in China has created favourable opportunities for our NCB value chain products.

items.statement: Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/barrel in Q1, healthy for fuel additives demand
items.quote: Overall, at the gasoline naphtha level, the cracks have averaged in the range of $15 to $18 per barrel, which are pretty healthy and this is a global market.

items.statement: Energy volumes down 17% QoQ; non-energy volumes down 7% QoQ; overall volumes down ~12% QoQ
items.quote: So volumes on energy business were down 17% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and on non-energy business, they were down by 7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. On an overall organization level, they were roughly 12% down on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Zone 4 chlorotoluene blocks delayed due to piping/insulation manpower shortages (LPG issue, elections, monsoon); 97% equipment erected, 85% piping complete
items.quote: In terms of piping, 85% of piping is complete. I think this is one area where it requires huge amount of manpower, both piping and the final insulation. And that is where we faced a bit of challenges, as I mentioned majorly in the March-May time frame.

items.statement: Crude-linked raw material volatility risk remains; domestic RM procurement 7-15 days inventory, imported 1-1.5 months; hedging and forward booking strategies in place
items.quote: We typically will not have more than 7 to 15 days inventory, wherever we are purchasing raw material in the domestic market. I think in the imported raw materials, which is where we tend to have 1 to 1.5 months of inventory ideally in stock or over waters, which is where this price fluctuation sometimes could impact us. We have put in strategies in place, including a combination of forward booking

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA guidance of Rs 1,800 crore included Augene JV contribution; other JV not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY27-28
items.quote: So INR1,800 crore guidance included the EBITDA, especially for Augene JV because we expected it to start contributing by that time frame. The other JV, we did not anticipate will start contributing meaningfully before FY27, '28 time frame. So that guidance did include Augene's EBITDA.

items.statement: DCB capacity debottlenecking to 140 KTPA backed by PDCB and downstream demand increase
items.quote: We are also looking to debottleneck our DCB capacity to 140 KTPA backed by volume increase supported by PDCB and downstream demand.

items.statement: SABIC backward integration project in execution phase; civil/building work ongoing; commissioning expected Sep-Oct 2027
items.quote: I think the civil and the building work is currently ongoing. The commissioning of that project is expected around September to October 2027 time frame.

items.statement: Augene JV steady-state revenue projected at Rs 300-400 crore; will maintain range until ramp-up stabilizes
items.quote: We had projected INR300 crore to INR400 crore. I think we will maintain that range for the joint venture to start with. As and when we complete the ramp-up in this quarter and we stabilize the plant operations, we will come back with a firmer estimate.

items.statement: Achieved EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 with score of 87/100, placing company in top 1% globally for sustainability
items.quote: We were pleased to achieve the EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 during the quarter with a score of 87 out of 100, placing Aarti Industries among the top 1% of companies globally for sustainability performance.

items.statement: Management expects 10-15% volume growth over the next two years, with 10% achievable even without salicylic acid ramp-up.
items.quote: So achieving 10% to 15% volume growth in next two years should not be a problem. Only challenge would be how fast we streamline the Salicylic acid and the derivative part.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 14% is already achievable; 15% should be easy once greenfield utilization improves and salicylic acid drag reduces.
items.quote: So 14% is quite doable. We are almost there. Now once the utilization of the two main greenfield projects what we have put up once that improves, then definitely 15% should be very easy.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 120 bps YoY to 13.8%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 13.8%, an expansion of 120 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Backward integration at Sayakha expected to add ~1% to gross contribution at peak utilization.
items.quote: Yes. So, we are hoping that it should add another 1% or so in the gross contribution at the peak level.

items.statement: Demand remained healthy across API and Specialty Chemicals, supported by strong consumption across key therapeutic categories in domestic and international markets.
items.quote: Demand remained healthy across API and Spec Chem portfolio, supported by strong consumption across key therapeutic categories and continued traction in both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: Aggregate volume growth was ~3.5% YoY in Q1 FY27, mostly driven by price increases rather than volume.
items.quote: Overall company level, we still achieved around 3.5% aggregate volume growth both domestic and local markets. But majority of the growth came from the price growth in the June quarter.

items.statement: API prices rose across the industry due to supply tightness from geopolitical conflict, leading to significantly better realizations in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: API prices witnessed an upward movement across the industry. This translated into significantly better realizations for us during the quarter.

items.statement: Metformin pricing up ~20% vs pre-war levels; currently slightly below March-April peak.
items.quote: Yes, pricing movement. Yes, it has gone up by around 15%, 20% compared to before the war, 20% approximately.

items.statement: Aggregate YoY pricing growth ~16-17% in Q1 FY27; management expects prices to ease as raw material costs normalize.
items.quote: In Y-o-Y basis, at the aggregate level, we saw somewhere around 16%, 17% aggregate growth.

items.statement: Phase 1 greenfield asset turnover ~1.5x; Phase 2 brownfield capex at Sayakha and Tarapur expected at 3-4x asset turnover.
items.quote: About Sayakha, around 50% of the capacities are being utilized for captive consumption for our antidiabetic portfolio. So that will add to the gross margins more than the rev enue itself. Having said that the Phase 2 capex, brownfield capex which will come in both these sites, Sayakha as well as G61 in Tarapur, their asset turn will be much higher around 3x, 4x

items.statement: Sayakha facility operated at ~65% utilization in Q1 FY27; methylamine plant at ~65% utilization (~60 tons/day, ~3,500 tons/quarter).
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, our Sayakha facility continued its planned ramp-up and operated at nearly 65% utilization.

items.statement: Metformin capacity to scale from 1,400 to ~2,200 tons/month, including ~500-550 tons/month USFDA block; USFDA supply earliest in 12 months.
items.quote: Our current plan is to scale up Metformin from 1,400 tons per month to roughly around 2,200 tons per month, out of which around 500-550 tons per month would be a USFDA capacity.

items.statement: Baddi brownfield expansion to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity; USFDA-approved oncology and EU-approved oral solid dosage formulation facilities in place.
items.quote: Our brownfield expansion at the Baddi facility in the adjacent land parcel is progressing as planned. Once completed, this project is expected to nearly double our oral solid dosage manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: USFDA API plant at E-22 has 2 main lines + 1 high-value line; planning quasi-greenfield expansion to more than double capacity with 3 new multipurpose lines (~10 tons/month each).
items.quote: So, we are also planning a fresh quasi greenfield project of USFDA in the adjacent plot itself. So, it will have same API number. So that will give us capacity enhancement of slightly more than double our existing capacities.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals revenue INR 82 crores in Q1 FY27 (up 149% YoY) driven by Sayakha facility; run-rate expected to sustain or improve for next 3 quarters.
items.quote: Yes. So, this first quarter's performance will definitely repeat for the next 3 quarters. And in fact, we will be trying to improve it further.

items.statement: API therapeutic mix: antibiotic 35%, antiprotozoal 18.5%, anti-inflammatory 11.9%, antidiabetic 18.2%, antifungal 10.2%, others 6.1%.
items.quote: Within the API business, the antibiotic therapeutic category contributed 35.0%, antiprotozoal around 18.5%, anti-inflammatory 11.9%, antidiabetic 18.2%, antifungal 10.2%, and the rest contributed around 6.1% to the total API sales.

items.statement: Formulations revenue INR 81.6 crores (up 8% YoY), 74% exports; regulated market filings underway for both API and formulations.
items.quote: Revenue from formulations stood at INR81.6 crores compared to INR75.8 cr ores in Q1 FY26, up 8% year -on-year. Exports contributed around 74% to this revenue

items.statement: European metformin clients require both EU and USFDA approval; USFDA approval will unlock US and larger EU markets.
items.quote: Many of the European clients of Metformin are also operating in the US market, so they need a supplier who is both European as well as USFDA approved. And that is the main reason why we are going in for USFDA approval.

items.statement: Salicylic acid anti-dumping duty delayed by ~1 year; company shifting to derivatives (methyl salicylate, 350-400 tons/month capacity) to achieve breakeven.
items.quote: Unfortunately, what has happened to the anti-dumping duty part, it got delayed a little bit. Though the case was okay, but the government asked that the injury period should be a year more. So we'll have to wait most probably 1 more year for anti-dumping duty to come up.

items.statement: Manufacturing facilities hold USFDA and UK regulatory approvals; 9 products have European CEP approvals; USFDA approval for oncology formulations and EU approval for oral solid dosage.
items.quote: Our manufacturing facilities continue to hold approvals from leading global regu latory authorities, including the USFDA and U.K. regulatory agencies. These approvals not only validate our quality systems and manufacturing standards, but also enable us to strengthen our presence in regulated markets over the long-term

items.statement: Standalone exports 32% of revenue (up 12% YoY); domestic 68% (up 25% YoY). Formulations exports 74% of segment revenue.
items.quote: 68% of the stand-alone revenue came from the domestic market and 32% from the exports market. Domestic revenue grew 25% year-on-year, and export revenue grew 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Formulations purchasers reduced buying during sharp price hikes, keeping inventory minimal; demand expected to return as inventory depletes.
items.quote: And because of such sharp increase in the prices, typically what happens is formulations purchasers, they refrain from buying too much. They keep the stock to minimum because the prices are very high. And that definitely impacts the demand.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia causing elevated freight costs, longer procurement cycles, raw material price volatility, and demand uncertainty.
items.quote: Geopolitical developments, particularly the ongoing conflict in West Asia, remained an important factor affecting international trade, logistics, and supply chains. The industry also continued to witness elevated freight costs on certain routes, longer procurement cycles in a few regions, and increased volatility in raw material pricing.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 703.6 crores (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR 96.9 crores (+30% YoY), PAT INR 50.1 crores (Q1 FY26 included INR 15 cr tax refund).
items.quote: Q1 FY27 revenue stood at INR703.6 crores compared to INR590.8 crores in Q1 FY26, reflecting a growth of 19% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at INR96.9 crores versus INR74.4 crores in Q1 FY26, a growth of 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Adhish Patil elevated to COO and CFO; management team includes Joint MD Harshit Savla, WTD Harit Shah, and Pinnacle MD Vishwa Savla.
items.quote: Joining me today are Mr. Harshit Savla, Joint Managing Director; Mr. Harit Shah, Whole-Time Director; Mr. Vishwa Savla, Managing Director of Pinnacle Life Science Private Limited, along with our Investor Relations Advisors SGA.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,500 crore, EBITDA at Rs 525-575 crore, blended ROCE at 16.25-16.5%
items.quote: Our guideline stands as published. So, FY '27 consolidated revenue of roughly Rs. 1,400 crores to Rs. 1,500 crores, EBITDA of 525 to 575 and a blended return on capital of 16.25 to 16.5.

items.statement: FY27 core crane rental EBITDA guidance unchanged at Rs 525-575 crore despite Q1 margin compression
items.quote: Taking all together, we regard this core margin are structurally intact and our guidance for FY'27 is still between Rs. 525 crores to Rs. 575 crores which is unchanged.

items.statement: Core crane rental EBITDA margin dropped 6pp YoY to 47% in Q1 FY27 due to ECL provisions, forex MTM, one-time incentives, and revenue mix shift
items.quote: The core crane rental EBITDA margin moved from 53% in FY'26 to 47% in Q1 FY'27. That is a 6% point drop.

items.statement: Underlying core margin excluding forex and incentives was ~49% in Q1; expected to cross 51% if ECL provisions rationalize
items.quote: So, putting together, excluding this FOREX and incentive item, the underlying core margin for the quarter was approximately 49% and if the credit provision rationalized as we are expecting in during the course of the year, the return crossed 51%.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at Rs 1,250 crore fully executable in FY27; renewables E&C order book at Rs 680 crore
items.quote: Total income of Rs. 393 crores, growth of 40% and order book of almost Rs. 1,250 crores. So, Pradeep has been candid about where margin moved and why.

items.statement: Renewables inquiry pipeline at Rs 4,656 crore; Middle East 0-24 month pipeline at $38 million
items.quote: In addition, we have a healthy project pipeline or inquiry pipeline of almost Rs. 5,600 crores across multiple sectors, giving us the confidence in sustained business momentum.

items.statement: FY27 capex pool of Rs 652 crore approved; Rs 92 crore capitalized in Q1, balance Rs 560 crore to deploy in H2 FY27
items.quote: On CAPEX, FY'27 pool of Rs. 652 crores as approved by the board of directors. Rs. 92 crores already capitalized in Q1 and balance deployment is in second half.

items.statement: Middle East capex of Rs 324 crore (Rs 316 crore revenue-generating) ordered; expected to come online Q3-Q4 FY27
items.quote: We will be doing approximately 300 plus crores or rather 324 crores of which 316 crores is in revenue generating CAPEX in the region. Right now, the entirety of this CAPEX orders have been placed on the equipment manufacturers and it is their responsibility to bring the equipment to Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: Fleet size 492 cranes, gross block ~Rs 3,300 crore; India/Botswana utilization 86% at 2.29% yield, GCC utilization 86% at 4.10% yield
items.quote: Our fleet size is 492 cranes and gross block is approximately Rs. 3,300 crores. The India and Botswana business reported utilization of around 86% at a yield of 2.29% and the GCC business utilization process is 86% at a yield of 4.10%.

items.statement: India investment-led growth across refining, steel, cement, power, renewables, infrastructure, heavy engineering; wind 6GW added, 29GW under construction, thermal 62GW bid/awarded
items.quote: India continues to be the fastest growing major economy, closing the last financial year with 7.7% of GDP growth while Q1 FY'27 is tracking at around 6.6%R. Most importantly, the quality of the growth remains investment led.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia construction activity driven by Vision 2030, FIFA World Cup, World Expo, Aramco spending; zero structural change to investment thesis despite regional tensions
items.quote: Saudi Arabia today is the construction backyard of the world and we see tremendous amount of activity happening across all sectors. Our investment thesis to go to Saudi Arabia was correct because as Pradeep has announced, we are already cumulatively EBITDA positive in the country and we continue to deploy capital in the region.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 60% crane rental, 37% renewable E&C, 3% project EPC; full year target ~2/3 crane rental, 1/3 renewable E&C
items.quote: The crane rental contributes approximately 60% of revenue from operations and 37% renewable E&C and balance 3% from project EPC. Renewable business ran ahead of our full year mix in Q1 on execution phasing and for the full year, we continue to expect roughly two-third revenue from crane rental and one-third from renewable E&C business.

items.statement: Group DSO 116 days (crane rental 124, renewable E&C 98, GCC 201); GCC collections improved significantly in July 2026
items.quote: Group Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) stood at 116 days which includes crane rental 124 days, renewable E&C 98 days and GCC business 201 days. So, this year's collection is very focused and the GCC collection has improved in the month of July after the end of quarter June '26.

items.statement: ECL provision of Rs 6.2 crore in Q1 driven by aged India receivables; expected to normalize during FY27 as collections improve
items.quote: Two points related to a higher expected credit loss provisions driven by aging of receivables that is around Rs. 6.2 crores. We expect it to rationalize over the course of this year as collection improves.

items.statement: Gross debt-to-equity 0.54x vs guided ceiling 0.72x; net debt-to-equity 0.3-0.7x with Rs 300+ crore treasury surplus
items.quote: Our gross debt-to-equity stood at 0.54 times against our guided FY ceiling 0.72 times and group ROCE was around 16% as of March 26.

items.statement: India borrowing at ~8% +/- 0.25%; international at SOFR+spread (5.5-6%); weighted average cost disclosed at half-year
items.quote: India is generally ranging 8% plus minus 0.25 is the difference. And internationally it is SOFR plus spread, which is ranging between 5.5% to 6%.

items.statement: India crane yields improved QoQ, not capped by competition; Saudi yields ~4.1% vs India ~2.29%; Saudi EBITDA margin ~47% vs India higher due to higher operating costs
items.quote: Over the last quarter, we have been able to shift yields. So, yields are not being capped by competition and there is a tremendous demand for cranes that still remains in the country.

items.statement: No material shift in client behavior on contract tenure or rate resets in India; renewables clients include large PE-funded platforms valuing governance and execution track record
items.quote: So, we don't see any material shift in the customer's perspective as of now.

items.statement: India crane rental: yields improving, demand strong, competition not capping yields; Renewables E&C: only organized player, competition unstructured, margins sustainable at 12-15%
items.quote: We are the only organized, well-structured, well-governed company. And this really matters with the clientele that we work with because we work with large PE funds who have platforms like such as which I cannot name in this call.

items.statement: Nuclear sector open to privatization under SHANTI Act; government capex at record Rs 12.2 lakh crore
items.quote: Nuclear: I am sure all of you be aware, is open to privatization under the SHANTI Act. Each one of these require a heavy lift.

items.statement: Middle East revenue Rs 19 crore at 23% EBITDA margin; Saudi operations cumulative EBITDA positive; Botswana commissioned, $1.1M repatriated
items.quote: GCC total income was Rs. 19 crores at an EBITDA margin of 23% and the Saudi operation has now delivered cumulative EBITDA positive performance.

items.statement: MTM forex loss of Rs 1.4 crore on foreign currency loan (non-cash accounting entry)
items.quote: One point is regarding mark-to-market reinstatement of foreign currency loan and that is Rs. 1.4 crores and it is a non-cash accounting entry.

items.statement: One-time incentive paid to frontline and senior management for surpassing Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY26; transferred seasoned Indian operators and safety officers to KSA
items.quote: One point is one-time incentive paid to frontline employees and to senior management teams because Company has rewarded for first time, surpassing Rs. 1,000 crores top line and extraordinary performance by the employee in FY'26.

items.statement: West Asia tensions causing temporary supply chain disruption and higher GCC DSO (201 days); zero working capital draw in KSA despite high DSO
items.quote: I am sure that you are aware that there is a conflict between USA and Israel with Iran. And that has caused a certain amount of disruption in West Asia. So, this DSO that you are seeing is reflective of the situation that is there on ground.

items.quote: the ranking is established by International Cranes, which is an industry recognized and gold standard magazine. items.quote: Do I see that our R&D density will increase in the coming quarters? Absolutely. I think that's a bet, and that's an investment that we must make. Because being a product company, again, we are not services. My investment in people or expanding my workforce does not make sense. I need to go back and invest in technology.

items.statement: Core R&D team is approximately 200 out of total 700 employees
items.quote: Our R&D team, so my overall strength is approximately give or take, 700. Our core R&D teams are about 200 out of that.

items.statement: Contract signing to subscription revenue typically takes four to five quarters with implementation milestones generating revenue during the period
items.quote: Typically, we have seen it can take four or five quarters between when you will sign a contract and you will start seeing the subscription revenue. But that does not mean that we don't have revenue during this wire time, right. Even when we are implementing, we have a lot of milestones.

items.statement: Margins have expanded QoQ and are at a healthy profile; management intends to hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash into R&D
items.quote: Like I was saying, we are looking at expanding the margin from where we closed last year. And this quarter, you have already seen margin expansion. That's one of the big goals that we want to do margin expansion. But, like I was explaining to one of the previous shareholders, Brian, just now, I do not want to continue to expand margins at the cost of reinvesting in the business.

items.statement: FraudZap margins are much higher and investment has already been recovered with ROI achieved
items.quote: I think, see, we have done a few contracts already. We know where our margins will land on FraudZap. I think it's much higher. I think if it gives you any comfort, we have already recovered our investment on this. My ROI is already done.

items.statement: New FraudZap customer signed this quarter after a slight delay of about a month
items.quote: No. This quarter also, like; this is one of the slight delays that I was talking about. It's moving by a month or so. But, yes, is it will be. It will not technically become last quarter. It will become this quarter. But, yes, it's one of the deals.

items.statement: Margin thresholds are confidential and competition-sensitive due to RFP bidding processes where orders above 800k or 1M USD go through competitive bidding
items.quote: Any order that exceeds, you know, 800 k or a million-dollar threshold typically goes through an RFP process. We are competing and bidding against our competitors. If I were to divulge, what our thresholds are, you know, or what my profit margin or what my margin threshold is, this becomes competition-sensitive.

items.statement: Currency gain of approximately INR 3 crores contributed to revenue increase from 72 to 79; revenue predominantly foreign currency denominated
items.quote: I think it's about INR 3 crores, this currency gain, yeah, to answer your question.

items.statement: Actively considering inorganic acquisitions with INR 185 crores cash on balance sheet; pipeline running but no active talks currently
items.quote: We do have cash on the balance sheet, and one of the ways to leverage our balance sheet is obviously, through some of these methods. That's very much on our radar. We are kind of running a pipeline in the back. We are seeing what we can do. But am I actively talking to, someone right now? The answer is no. But are we strongly considering it? items.statement: Middle East subsidiary is self-sufficient and no further capital infusion expected currently
items.quote: Currently, not. It is self-sufficient. The last time which we found the capital more about to support the business. So that remains the same. We don't expect further the infusion right now.

items.quote: We are starting to measure this, and I'm seeing on an average, we are able to gain almost a month to 45 days in our implementation cycle. items.quote: Instead of just doing one Investor Day in a year, I thought that doing quarterly NDRs is a better way, because we will come to your cities. We are thinking Mumbai. We are thinking Ahmedabad, Chennai. We are planning to do a broader coverage of NDRs.

items.statement: Management will articulate long-term vision more clearly next quarter based on shareholder feedback
items.quote: What I will do is I'll take this feedback, and I will probably come back and articulate this much better next quarter. Let me take this as an actual item.

items.statement: Freight business top-line growth guidance 10-12% for FY27 with profitability improvement
items.quote: The guidance for this year, as we have indicated, about 10 -12% on the top line should also apply to this business, and our profitability should improve from the last year.

items.statement: Supply chain business top-line growth guidance 12-15% for FY27
items.quote: So, again, I think this business should grow in the higher teens, 12-15% for the top line.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget 500-600 crore including two new ships, warehouses, trucks, rakes and IT
items.quote: But I am estimating depending upon how things go between 500 and 600 crores for this year.

items.statement: Two new ships expected September-October and October-November; third ship under evaluation
items.quote: The new ship is expected in September end of this year, the next two months. And the next ship should be, well, actually probably September-October and again October-November for the second ship.

items.statement: Freight EBITDA margin slight improvement; supply chain EBITDA margin slightly improved but EBIT flat due to investment lag
items.quote: On the freight business side, the margin has been slight, there has been slight improvement, but top line has also grown by about 10-11%.

items.statement: Seaways EBITDA margin flat at 40%+; may compress to 30-40% if bunker prices remain high
items.quote: The margins at a decent level, I think 40 -ish plus percent EBITDA. So, I think if the prices remain as is in terms of the fuel, it will probably come down a little bit.

items.statement: Transystem margin declined to ~9%; expects ~10% as reasonable long-term level

items.statement: Portfolio yield improved marginally to 9.48%; incremental disbursement yield higher than book yield across all verticals

items.statement: RBI maintained repo rate at 5.25%; revised FY27 GDP forecast to 6.66%; PMAY 2.0 facilitated 7,000+ subsidies

items.statement: Capital adequacy 28.26%, Tier 1 27.87%; net worth INR 19,800 cr; leverage avg 3.75x vs 3.6x prior quarter

items.statement: Disbursement recognition changed from cheque handover to cheque realization; one-time impact on Q1 interest income, no yield impact

items.statement: External risks: geopolitical tension, volatile crude, monsoon uncertainty, US-Iran conflict; RBI flagged higher energy costs and supply chain disruptions
items.quote: The quarter was also characterized by heightened global uncertainty arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to higher crude oil prices, increased market volatility and tighter liquidity conditions.

items.statement: Digital transformation: 100% fresh disbursals via new LOS (SFDC), 70%+ onboarding via Infinity app, 2,600+ e-signs via Legality; Voice AI PoC completed
items.quote: 100% of our fresh disbursals are happening through our new LOS platform, which we call SFDC. More than 70% of our business is now being onboarded through our in-house onboarding app, which is the Infinity app. And more than 2,600 e-sign executed through Legality platform.

items.statement: Acquired loan assets of INR 146 cr via full buyout transactions; launched Emerging Developer Finance (INR 71 cr disbursed)
items.quote: Also, as part of our growth strategy, we have commenced full buyout transactions and acquired loan assets aggregating to INR146 crores during the quarter.
