items.statement: Evaluating 7th hospital to take network beyond 1,000 beds in next 2 years
items.quote: In addition, we continue to evaluate opportunities for our seventh hospital, which will increase our n etwork capacity to over 1,000 beds in the next 2 years and further strengthen our presence across Eastern and Central India

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR126.2 cr, EBITDA INR26.2 cr (20.4% margin), PAT INR12.7 cr (9.9% margin)
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, revenue from operations stood at INR126.2 crores, while EBITDA was INR26.2 crores, translating to an EBITDA margin of 20.4%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR12.7 crores, with a PAT margin of 9.9%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 total income +18.2% YoY, PAT +66% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, our total income increased by 18.2% and PAT increased by 66% compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Network occupancy 45.5%, mature hospitals 58.07%, ARPOB INR42,350
items.quote: The network occupancy stood at 45.5%, while average revenue per occupied bed, or ARPOB, improved to INR42,350.

items.statement: No tariff hikes in Q1; annual inflation-linked increase in October; 50-60% of ARPOB rise from specialty mix shift
items.quote: We have not had any tariff increase in any of our hospitals. Our tariff increase generally happens in the month of October. This is probably an effect of incremental change in case mix. We have been focusing a lot on high -end tertiary care, including cardi ology, oncology, neurosciences, which is giving an impact in the blended ARPOB being increased

items.statement: ARPOB growth driven by specialty mix shift to cardiology, oncology, neurosciences, robotic surgeries
items.quote: of the -- or almost, I would say, 50% to 60% of the ARPOB increase comes from an improved specialty mix and change in case mix

items.statement: ~90% revenue from cash and insurance patients; limited Ayushman Bharat in Raipur lowers ARPOB slightly
items.quote: Approximately 90% of our revenues continue to be g enerated through cash and insurance patients, highlighting the strength of our payer mix and sustained demand for quality health care across our operating

items.statement: Not pursuing government scheme patients in West Bengal due to delayed payments and lower ARPOB
items.quote: Even now, we don't really see a need to change our strategy and focus on these patients because they come with a delay in payments and lower ARPOB numbers for sure.

items.statement: Salt Lake occupancy 62% (up from 60% YoY), ARPOB INR45,300; Dumdum occupancy 65% (up from 60% YoY), ARPOB INR43,041
items.quote: During the quarter, occupancy stood at 62%, up from 60% on a Y-o-Y basis, while ARPOB improved to 45,300, supported by a favorable mix of higher contributing surgeries.

items.statement: Agartala occupancy dipped due to tribal elections and reduced ALOS (3.38 to 3 days); ARPOB grew 70% to INR41,573
items.quote: The hospital saw a slight decrease in occupanc y because of geopolitical reasons, but the overall ARPOB grew by 70% to INR41,573 on account of higher -end tertiary care work

items.statement: Howrah revenue +31% YoY, occupancy +16% YoY; MAKO robotic knee program driving ARPOB
items.quote: At ILS Hospital Howrah, we were able to significantly increase our revenue by 31% compared to last year and increase our occupancy levels by 16%.

items.statement: Raipur occupancy 17% (up from 7% YoY), ARPOB INR42,300 (down from INR44,500 QoQ due to Ayushman Bharat patients); loss INR3 cr in Q1
items.quote: The bed occupancy for this hospital improved to 17% compared to 7% of same period last year. Supported by its strategic location and asse t-light operating model, Raipur remains on track to achieve operational breakeven while steadily expanding its reach across the surrounding catchment area

items.statement: Raipur loss INR3 cr in Q1, expected to taper through year; exit occupancy target 30%
items.quote: Q1 has been minus INR3 crores. We expect it to taper down throughout the year.

items.statement: Jamshedpur initial ARPOB expected INR38,000-40,000, ramping to INR42,000-43,000; breakeven ~24 months
items.quote: So the ARPOB -- initially, the ARPOB level at that hospital should be around the INR38,000 to INR40,000 mark. Slowly, as the hospital establishes, we expect it to catch up with the Calcutta level of around INR42,000, INR43,000 on current terms.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient inflows improving but not yet at pre-disruption levels; expect recovery in 6 months
items.quote: It is definitely an upside over the previous past few quarters, which you were experiencing, but it has still not reached the pre-disruption levels. There have been changes in the policies of both Government of India and Government of Bangladesh, which is impacting this positively, I would say, because now the visa requests are coming with the targeted hospital names and not open access.

items.statement: Doctor attrition single digits in Kolkata (6-7%), ~10% in Agartala/Raipur; nursing college in Agartala aids retention
items.quote: So the attrition rate amongst doctors is not very high. It is in the single digits, especially in our Calcutta markets. It is slightly higher in the Agartala and Raipur because those hospitals come with their own geographic challenges. It would be around 10% in Agartala and Raipur. But in Calcutta, it is around the 6%, 7% mark.

items.statement: Debt unchanged from last year; Jamshedpur to add ~INR25 cr this FY
items.quote: It is the same as last year. Jamshedpur will see an incoming debt, but that will happen in this FY. That will be to the tune of around INR25 crores.

items.statement: Evaluating both greenfield and acquisition for 7th hospital in Tier 1/2 Eastern cities (Cuttack, Ranchi, Patna, Banaras, Prayagraj)
items.quote: We have been focusing on the Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities of Eastern India. These include cities like Cuttack, Ranchi, Patna, Banaras, Prayagraj. We have been evaluating both acquisition opportunities and greenfield opportunities in these areas.

items.statement: Jamshedpur commissioning subject to approvals; may slip to early FY28
items.quote: But in case of any delay in approvals, it might be pushed to first -- the beginning of next year.

items.statement: Asset-light model: Raipur and Jamshedpur on long-term lease (rent mid-30s INR lakh/month); reduces real estate capex
items.quote: So the Raipur rental is in the mid-30s. It is as per the market area, market standard. Similarly, the Jamshedpur rental is around that much only completely based on the market feedback around the mid-30s.

items.statement: Order book full till December; booking for Q4 (January onwards) underway
items.quote: We have closed taking orders for December on 31st July. From 1st August, we've started booking for fourth quarter, that is January onwards, which means my garmenting capacity is full from now till December.

items.statement: Aim to at least double turnover in 5 years and grow EBITDA faster than topline
items.quote: If you ask me directionally, I want to at least double or more than double the turnover and grow EBITDA faster than topline, without doing the project I am telling you.

items.statement: Expect 5-7% ASP hike in apparel and 7-9% in fabric for FY27
items.quote: But my guess is between 5 % to 7% in apparel and between 7 to 8% in fabric. Because fabric will need between 7 % to 9% depending on the quality, because a larger proportion of a fabric business is raw material price.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.6%, up 40 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter rose to INR 135 crores, a 11% year -on-year growth, resulting in an improved EBITDA margin of 8.6%, a 40 basis point expansion over the same period last year.

items.statement: Garmenting EBITDA margin 7.3% vs -4.1% YoY, 1100 bps improvement
items.quote: The segment achieved an EBITDA of INR 22 crores versus negativ e INR8 crores last year same quarter, with an improved EBITDA margin of 7.3% versus minus 4.1% last year, which is a 1100 bps jump.

items.statement: Target mid-teens ROCE for manufacturing-driven business over time
items.quote: But if you ask me, I have done enough businesses in my life to know mid-teens is a good ROCE to have for a manufacturing -driven business, so that will be the endeavor, but that is not the target that I am chasing.

items.statement: New factory in Andhra Pradesh; five garmenting factories total (3 Karnataka, 1 Andhra, 1 Ethiopia)
items.quote: I have clear, full I have three factories in Karnataka, I have set up a new factory in Andhra, we have a factory in Ethiopia. So my five factories, I have no capacity to give till December.

items.statement: Wool prices up ~100% YoY; cotton and flax up ~20%; chemicals up ~30%
items.quote: if you look at wool, it is almost increased 100% over the same quarter last year. Cotton and flax has almost increased by about 20% over last year. Your chemicals have increased by about 30%.

items.statement: Diversified vendor base, reduced Chinese content in dyes/chemicals, consolidated shipping lines to cut freight
items.quote: we have diversified our vendor bases and we have looked for new vendors who are willing to come in and do business with us at more competitive rates. We have taken trials, we have done samples, and without compromising quality, we have introduced a few new vendors. We've also worked on a little bit of "Make in India." A lot of these components, dyes and chemicals, have a lot of Chinese impact on t

items.statement: Premiumization and casualization driving mix shift; suits returning in Western markets
items.quote: Good news is, I was recently in US and UK and Europe meeting some of these big customers because this is a very important SBU for me this year, and the suit usage I felt is coming back. The product mix is changing a little bit from 100% pure wool suits to a little bit of poly-wool to manage the cost, but at least the suit -wearing piece is coming back in Western world, which I think is a welcome n

items.statement: New garmenting clients: Next (UK), El Corte Ingles (Spain), OVS (Italy), Carl Gross (Germany), T.M. Lewin (UK)
items.quote: From UK, new client is next. Next is a big client in UK. From Europe, I'll give you different countries. From Spain, the biggest departmental store El Corte Ingles, from Italy OVS, and from Germany, Carl Gross. These three are new orders that we are already processing in our plant. And Next is from UK, there's another client from UK called T.M. Lewin, which is a shirting client.

items.statement: Geographic mix: US 59-60%, UK 12%, Europe 7-8%; Europe FTA benefits 6-9 months away
items.quote: So we've gone back to 59% -60% in US, but our UK has moved from 10% to 12% and Europe has moved from 6% to 7%-8%. But the Europe orders are yet coming, because the FTA has just been announced and it will take about 6 to 9 months to come into force.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 75 from 90 YoY
items.quote: Net working capital days improved by 15 days, stood at 75 days in Q1 FY27 versus 90 days in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Net cash surplus INR 154 cr in June 2026 vs net debt INR 55 cr in June 2025
items.quote: We sustained our debt -free status with a net cash surplus of INR 154 crores in June '26, a marked improvement from a net debt position of INR55 crores in June '25, which is a INR209 crores swing within the year.

items.statement: Transformation project with Kearney may lead to dropouts, mergers or acquisitions
items.quote: Once they come out with the project, there could be some dropouts in the business, some mergers and acquisitions, I am not talking about that.

items.statement: Transformation project with Kearney India to challenge cost base across media, product, manpower, factory productivity
items.quote: We are going through a transformation project with a big consultancy firm, and we're looking at every cost from media buying cost to product buying cost to manpower cost to factory productivities, and we will find these monies without too much price pass-on to the consumers.

items.statement: Branded Apparel: e-commerce high double-digit growth, LFS >25% growth; casual brands ColorPlus, Parx double-digit
items.quote: In fact, in e -commerce is growing high double digit and LFS is growing upwards of 25%. So that's very, very good. From the casualization point of view, ColorPlus and Parx, which are our casual brands, are growing at double digit.

items.statement: Loyalty program at 12.4 million members
items.quote: Furthermore, our loyalty ecosystem now reached 12.4 million members, providing a data -led consumer insight engine to drive repeat visits and lower marketing acquisition costs.

items.statement: International business unpredictable; Truth Social message can change everything; geopolitical volatility
items.quote: the international headwinds now come without warning. A Truth Social message comes and things change in your life. So it's very, very difficult to predict, but we've hit 7.3 at one change, and if we can keep our combination right, which is the suit versus shirt versus trouser, this combination, the product mix there, then there is no reason why we shouldn't go to double-digit EBITDA actually

items.statement: Consumer sentiment okay across US, UK, Europe, India; premium end off-take strong in Q1
items.quote: I was in UK in July. I was in U.S. in July personally. I have met customers, I have met CEOs of big brands that you think of that you can think of, I have met the CEO of Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Brooks Brothers, Charles Tyrwhitt in UK, I have met Taylor brands, Men's Wearhouse. I have met Tommy Hilfiger in U.S., everybody is bullish about the business, everybody is seeing good off-take growth

items.statement: Store rationalization ongoing; net EBO closures this year; TRS format +6 stores in Q1; Ethnix -17 net
items.quote: We will open, for example, we've opened 8 stores this quarter but we've closed 24, so there's a net of minus 16 in branded EBOs. But if you look at our TRS format, The Raymond Store format where the whole company comes in to retail, we are plus 6 in this quarter. Ethnix, we have opened one store actually, and we've closed 18, so you're seeing minus 17 over there in Ethnix.

items.statement: Commissioned 18 new greenfield facilities in Q1 FY27 including 1 large tertiary in Thane and 15 secondary facilities
items.quote: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we expanded our footprint by commissioning 18 new greenfield facilities, strengthening our reach and capaci ty. Now these facilities included 1 large tertiary facility in Thane and 15 secondary facilities

items.statement: Total network of 285 facilities across 14 states and 5 union territories covering 165 cities as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Now in India, we have a total network of 285 facilities across 14 states and 5 union territories, covering 165 cities.

items.statement: Served over 8.8 lakh patients and performed over 90,000 surgeries in Q1 FY27; nearly 12,000 patients daily
items.quote: During the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we served over 8.8 lakhs patients and performed over 90,000 surgeries. Every day, nearly 12,000 patients come walk into our facilities across our network.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 16.3% YoY for facilities operational prior to FY23 contributing INR465 crores (75.9% of revenue)
items.quote: Our most mature facilities, those which have been operational prior to FY '23 contributed to INR465 crores of revenue, recording a strong 16.3% year -on-year growth and accounting for 75.9% of the overall group revenues.

items.statement: Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores at 28.5% margin, up 30 bps YoY; PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9%
items.quote: quarter delivered a robust Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores, growing 25.2% year -on-year with margins of 28.5%, an improvement of 30 basis points with a PAT margin expanding by 127 basis points to 8.9% despite rising greenfield losses driven by 23 surgical new facilities launched in the 6 months

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~1% YoY due to higher surgery mix; doctor/employee costs at 34% of revenue; other expenses stable at 16.8%
items.quote: Gross margins have improved year-on-year with a higher contribution of surgeries in segment mix. Doctor and employee costs have increased slightly to 34% of total revenues in Q1 FY '27 with the addition of talent across all facilities launched in Q1 FY '27 . Other expenses as a percentage of total revenue have remained stable at 16.8% of total revenues.

items.statement: Premiumization contributed ~7.5% and price hike ~0.5% to value growth on like-to-like basis
items.quote: On the premiumization we are close to around 7.5%. And price hike, so far this year, we have realized around 0.5%. So, overall, closer to 8% is what we have realized from a premiumization and price hike. This is on a like-to-like basis over last year.

items.statement: High-end cataract surgeries 29.3% of 67,000 total cataract surgeries; Femto cataract up 33.4% YoY to 1,548; SMILE up 36.2% YoY; retinal surgeries up 30% YoY to 3,861; 285 corneal transplants
items.quote: For this quarter, high-end cataract surgeries accounted for 29.3% of the 67,000 total cataract surgeries performed. Within the high-end surgeries, robotic cataract surgeries, what we refer to as the Femto Cataract, grew by 33.4% year-on-year, crossing 1,548 procedures for the quarter. Lenticular Procedures, what we call as the SMILE surgeries for refractive surgeries, increased 36.2% year-on-year,

items.statement: Payer mix: 63.6% cash, 27.7% insurance/TPA, 8.6% government schemes
items.quote: payer mix for the quarter Q1 FY '27 stood at 63.6% from cash, 27.7% from insurance and TPA, and 8.6% from government schemes.

items.statement: Paid INR25 crores towards deferred acquisition payable in Q1 FY27 reducing interest on deferred consideration from INR6.8 crores to INR3.6 crores YoY
items.quote: What I had mentioned in the opening remarks was there was a saving from the interest on deferred acquisition payable. The interest on deferred acquisition payable was about close to INR6.8 crores in corresponding quarter of last year, which dropped down to about INR3.6 crores, I think, with the payment of about close to INR25 crores on the d eferred acquisition payable, which was affected in Q1

items.statement: Merger expected to close around mid-November
items.quote: So, we are in the process of closing some of the final items when it comes to the merger, and we expect to close this around mid-November.

items.statement: West region revenue grew 24% YoY to INR91 crores (15% of group); 52 facilities with 5 new greenfield including Thane, Ulhasnagar, Moshi, Wagholi, Ahilyanagar
items.quote: This region contributes to 15% of the overall group revenues and delivered INR91 crores in revenue, up by 24% year-on-year. We currently have 52 facilities here now across the West region, including five new greenfield facilities, which we have launched this quarter, Thane and Ulhasnagar in Mumbai, Moshi and Wagholi in Pune and Ahilyanagar.

items.statement: East region revenue grew 21% YoY to INR16 crores; 14 facilities; new leadership in Kolkata focused on clinical excellence and business development
items.quote: Coming to East region. This region is still a relatively smaller contributor. It delivered INR16 crores of revenue, up 21% year-on-year. We currently have 14 facilities in the Eastern region. In Kolkata, we have put in a new leadership team with a renewed focus on clinical excelle nce and business development, which we expect will deliver strong performance going forward as we have seen in the fir

items.statement: Surgery volumes grew 15.5% YoY to ~91,000; cataract surgeries 74% of total, up 16.5% YoY; refractive surgeries 4.4%
items.quote: For the quarter ended June, we performed close to 91,000 surgeries, marking a 15.5% year-on-year growth. Cataract surgeries remained the largest contributor, accounting for approximately 74% of total surgeries, followed by refractive surgeries at around 4.4%. Volumes for cataract surgeries grew 16.5% year-on-year, while other surgeries on a blended basis recorded a growth of 13.3%.

items.statement: SSSG volume grew ~8% and value grew ~8% for pre-FY23 facilities; OPD growth contributed 6% and conversion 2% to value growth
items.quote: So, overall, on the SSSG front, if I were to breakdown the volume and value, volume grew by around 8% and value grew by around 8%. So , it's a breakup between the two. And on the volume front, the OPD growth which has given us the value growth of 8%, there's a 6% -- the OPD growth value and then there is another 2% which we are getting in from conversion, yes.

items.statement: Expect to sustain growth momentum through deeper penetration, new geographies, and accelerated adoption of innovative surgical procedures
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect to sustain the growth momentum underpinned by deeper penetration of existing micro markets, expansion into new geographies and the accelerated adoption of innovative surgical procedures and advanced technologies across our network.

items.statement: E-two-wheeler penetration up 44% to 11% industry-wide; scooter EV penetration over 25%; Ather inquiries up 95%, preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh in Q1 FY27
items.quote: E-two-wheeler penetration is up by 44% at 11% in the two-wheeler industry, and electric penetration in the scooter industry is upwards of, I believe, 25% now.

items.statement: Ather preorders up 158% YoY to 1.5 lakh in Q1 FY27; monthly preorders now exceed 50,000 despite dealers stopping orders due to 2+ month wait times
items.quote: Ather preorders, these are paid preorders that are captured across the country, they were up 158%, hitting a first-ever seen 1.5 lakh preorders in Q1 FY 2027.

items.statement: Hosur plant at ~100% utilization (35,000 units/month); Aurangabad Phase-1 (5 lakh units/year) go-live later this calendar year, taking total capacity to 9.2 lakh units/year; Phase-2 can add another 5 lakh units
items.quote: Go-live of AURIC will take our total capacity up from 4.2 lakh units to 9.2 lakh units later this calendar year.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,300 crore via QIP; seeking shareholder approval for Rs 1,200 crore preference issue; total Rs 2,500 crore fundraise to fund Aurangabad Phase-1, potential Phase-2 fast-track, and new product launches
items.quote: We are also in the midst of seeking shareholder approval and closing a fundraise of another Rs. 1,200 crores via preference issue, leading to a total fundraise of Rs. 2,500 crores.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin 22.4% in Q1 FY27 (down 5.6% from 25.4% in Q4 FY26) due to commodity inflation; structural gains from price hikes, SKU mix, AtherStack Pro attach (94%) partially offset
items.quote: Net it out, we have landed up at 22.4% AGM for Q1 2027. A fairly respectable place, particularly looking at how strong the commodity hit was.

items.statement: Average sales price increased to Rs 1.61 lakh (from Rs 1.5 lakh) driven by price hikes and improved SKU management; price hikes in April (Rs 1.53L), May (Rs 1.53L), June (Rs 1.61L)
items.quote: The average sales price of Ather has now hit Rs. 1.61 lakh across the country, up from about Rs. 1.5 lakh as of last quarter.

items.statement: Expect commodity headwinds of another 100-200 bps in coming quarters; price hikes already taken should largely mitigate further RM impact in Q2; EL launch to depress ASP slightly but overall margins to look fine
items.quote: There's probably another 100 to 200 bps, which we can probably manage with our already announced price hikes.

items.statement: First ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (0.8% margin) in Q1 FY27; expect ups and downs in coming quarters; AURIC Phase-1 costs to hit P&L from Q4 FY27 but offset by volume
items.quote: Our EBITDA came in at a Rs. 9 crore margin for Q1 2027, which is roughly about 0.8%. It's a small number, but this is the first time ever we have delivered one.

items.statement: EL scooter platform under production, homologation complete, SOP begun at Hosur; brand unveil in days, product launch at Ather Community Day on 29 Aug; target 60,000 units/month capacity across Hosur and Aurangabad
items.quote: We are looking at scaling up our manufacturing capacity for the EL scooter to about 60,000 units per month between Aurangabad and Hosur together.

items.statement: Middle India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha) retail growth 141% YoY; Rest of India 118%; South India 76%; Tier-2/3 cities becoming biggest volume drivers
items.quote: Middle India continues to be our growth driver, driving the highest growth among all zones for us. Middle India are the five zones of Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha, which grew 141% in retail from Q1 last year to Q1 this year.

items.statement: Dealer inventory down from 14 days to 3 days in Q1 FY27; retail outpacing wholesale creating urgency to ramp supply
items.quote: Our dealer stocks are down from 14 days to 3 three days, as of Q1 FY 2027.

items.statement: PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension awaited; ~15-20% of Q1 vehicles sold without subsidy; Delhi EV Policy seen as strong positive; other states like Haryana showing support
items.quote: We have been hearing an intent by the government to find a way to extend PM-E-DRIVE to continue supporting the larger electrification drive that they've been behind.

items.statement: Commodity index up 46% over last 5 quarters; further 100-200 bps margin risk; supply chain constraints from labor crisis and West Asia conflict impacted April production
items.quote: The commodity index in the last 5 quarters has gone up by 46% for us, which is what we had roughly guided by last quarter also.

items.statement: AtherStack Pro attach rate 94% in Q1 FY27; non-vehicle revenue 14% of operating revenue; service revenue long-term target 10-12% of revenue (currently 2-3%)
items.quote: We saw 94% AtherStack Pro attach rates in Q1 2027.

items.statement: Aurangabad Phase-1 equipment installation ending in next couple months; trial production from festive period; reliable daily output from Jan; full 42,000/month ramp in 4-5 months (end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28)
items.quote: Expect reliable daily output all throughout Q4, starting from first Jan itself. It is difficult for me to exactly pin down whether it is end of Q4 or into Q1 that the ramp-up to 42,000 units a month will finish.

items.statement: EL launch to initially target Rest of India, then Middle India, then South India; expect at least 75% AtherStack Pro attach on EL; Rizta likely to see cannibalization, 450X unlikely impacted
items.quote: I would cautiously guide at least 75% attach rates with EL also, but I would hope for even higher.

items.statement: QIP of Rs 1,300 crore closed with strong participation; preference issue of Rs 1,200 crore pending shareholder approval; total Rs 2,500 crore for capacity, supply chain, new products, balance sheet resilience
items.quote: Recently, we finished closure of our Rs. 1,300 crore QIP a few weeks ago with very strong participation from funds, both from India and abroad.

items.statement: Targeting more than 300 gross store additions in FY27
items.quote: We are confident to achieve our targeted expansion of more than 300 stores during this fiscal year.

items.statement: Expect 3-4% cost increase in H2 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and labour
items.quote: For the second half of the year, and particularly between Q2 and Q3, we expect between 3% to 4% cost increase.

items.statement: Q1 revenue typically 21-22% of full-year revenue
items.quote: This quarter is typically about 18, no, slightly higher than 20%, between 21%-22%.

items.statement: Domestic demand broadly consistent with prior trends; consumer traction healthy across categories and channels
items.quote: As we reflect on the quarter, domestic demand condition s remain broadly consistent with the trends witnessed in the same quarter , despite continued global microeconomic uncertainty. Consumer traction remains healthy and well distributed across categories and channels

items.statement: Small-town network delivering double-digit growth for fifth consecutive quarter
items.quote: Our small-town network continued to perform strongly, delivering double-digit growth for the fifth consecutive quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY to 16%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by 14% Y-o-Y to Rs. 327 crores, compared to Rs. 286 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, while EBITDA margin expanded by 50 bps to 16%.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin expanded ~40 bps YoY to 18.5%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 319 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 18.5%, and an expansion of approximately 40 bps over the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Emerging Brands EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps YoY to 4.3%
items.quote: Profitability also improved meaningfully, with EBITDA margin expanding by 240 bps Y-o-Y to 4.3% during the quarter.

items.statement: Expect major part of 3-4% cost increase to be absorbed via productivity and cost rationalisation; no material margin change
items.quote: We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization. So, we don't feel a material change in margin on account of this.

items.statement: Opened 68 gross new stores in Q1; retail footprint at 3,362 stores spanning ~5 million sq ft across 800+ cities
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened more than 65 new stores across the portfolio. At the end of the quarter, our retail footprint stood at 3,362 stores, spanning nearly 5 million square feet across more than 800 cities and towns.

items.statement: Net store additions for FY27 expected at 150-200 (gross 300+, closures 120-140)
items.quote: On a net basis, I think we will close in the year between 120 to 140 odd stores, sometimes a little higher, sometimes a little lower. And therefore, the net number would be function of where we end up with that. So, somewhere, net number between 150 to 200 stores versus the gross number closer to 300 stores.

items.statement: Small-town store count ~500; contributes ~15-16% of retail revenue, growing >15% vs metros ~10%
items.quote: We have of our network more than 500 stores in small-town. We have, as you correctly noted, for almost a year plus we are finding much stronger growth in smaller-town network.

items.statement: Taken small price hikes across brands/categories to offset large part of expected 3-4% cost increase
items.quote: Yes, we have taken smaller priced price hikes. They are not very large, but we have taken price hikes to compensate for that.

items.statement: Marketing spend ~3.5% of sales in Q1 (slightly lower YoY due to IPL shift to digital)
items.quote: On marketing expenditures, it is slightly lower than last year because last year we had invested in IPL. This year we moved primarily to digital advertising, but still about 3% to 4% of sales, about 3.5% in this quarter.

items.statement: Casual wear share increasing 2-3 percentage points per year
items.quote: I think it continues to grow, the share of casual w ear continues to grow. So, I won't say stable. We have seen even in a period of one year, you would find typically between two to three percentage point increase in the share of casual wear

items.statement: Gen-Z focus via brand-specific sub-brands/collections (Reebok, Peter England Vybe, Allen Solly); smaller towns growing faster
items.quote: Of course, some brands are more tuned to it, brands like Reebok, etc. Similarly, Peter England has a sub-brand called Vybe and also there are collections in Allen Solly. So, each of the brand has part of their portfolio, which is dedicated to address these customers.

items.statement: E-commerce profitability now marginally below retail; disciplined approach avoiding deep discounts
items.quote: Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability. It is just marginally lower than our retail profitability. And now that we have got to this level, having exercised a very disciplined and patient approach to building this channel, you are starting to see the growth on that base.

items.statement: Karnataka minimum wage hike stayed at High Court; garmenting excluded; manufacturing diversified across TN, AP, Odisha (40% in-house)
items.quote: As you know, the current increase is with health and it is still at the high court level. We will respond appropriately as we find a decision coming on that.

items.statement: Reebok BIS compliance ongoing; factories require annual renewal; building domestic sourcing base to mitigate regulatory risk
items.quote: So, BIS does remain a problem. As you know, the factories have to get the BIS approval on an ongoing and annual basis, and we are still continuing to operate with a couple of factories outside India. But as a part of our overall long-term strategy, we have built a very strong domestic base so that we are not impacted when the regulatory changes come in.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands retail like-to-like growth 7% (7th consecutive quarter of high single/double-digit LTL)
items.quote: Retail continued its consistent performance, supported by healthy like-to-like growth of 7% across an extensive store network of almost 3,000 stores.

items.statement: Emerging Brands retail like-to-like growth 11%; e-commerce >30%
items.quote: Performance remained healthy across channels, with retail like-to-like growth of 11% and e-commerce growth of over 30%.

items.statement: E-commerce growth 23% consolidated; Lifestyle Brands own digital platform >50%
items.quote: E-commerce continued to build on the strong momentum established in Quarter 3 last year, delivering robust growth of 23% during the quarter.

items.statement: Cautious on H2 demand impact from consumer wallet inflation; no meaningful shift seen yet
items.quote: We are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year. And therefore, we have called out in our commentary. As and when it plays out, we will obviously have to respond to that at that point of time.

items.statement: Reebok revenue doubled from Rs 250 cr at acquisition (2.5 yrs ago) to ~Rs 500 cr; targeting ~20% annual growth to double again in 3-3.5 yrs
items.quote: It is a brand which has a huge potential, but currently the footprint across all channels has been very small. That is why it has allowed us to grow this business from Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 500 crores, and we still feel confident over longer term, closer to 20% growth rate is what is possible for this business.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 35-40% annually for FY27
items.quote: We would like to stick to the same guidance. It's more of a strategic play. The demand is huge. Obviously, our scale is negligible compared to the market size, but we will stick to the guidance that we have shared, about 35-40% annually.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 10.5-11% for next few quarters
items.quote: And we expect this to sustain for the next few quarters.

items.statement: Plan to add 2-3 million tons annual capacity in next two quarters by recycling existing deposits
items.quote: And we look to add about 2- 3 million annual capacity this year , in the next two quarters.

items.statement: Current contract manufacturing capacity at 9 million tons annually with 65-70% utilization
items.quote: Based on the annual capacity that we have in the revenue possibility. We are at a utilization of somewhere around 65-70% as on Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Capacity to increase to ~11 million tons without new capex or deposits
items.quote: So 9 million would typically become around 11 million tons without any CapEx or any kind of deposits.

items.statement: DaaS mandate worth INR 650 crores secured from Wadhwa Group in Mumbai
items.quote: We secured a new DaaS mandate worth INR 650 crores from the Wadhwa Group in Mumbai, significantly strengthening our project pipeline and market presence.

items.statement: Gross development value under execution increased to over INR 1,800 crores across 10 active projects
items.quote: As a result, our GDV under execution increased to INR 1,800 plus crores, compared to INR 1,250 crore at the year-end Q4 FY26, providing strong revenue visibility over the coming years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 191 bps YoY to 10.49% driven by contract manufacturing and DaaS mix shift
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter grew 68 % YoY to INR 31 crores, with EBITDA margins improving by 191 basis points YoY to 10.49%.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing and DaaS combined share moved from 46% to 63% driving margin expansion
items.quote: Their combined share moved from about 46% to 63% as of Q1 FY27, and that's the main lever behind the EBITDA margin expanding.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing revenue grew 84% YoY to 53% of total revenue
items.quote: Our contract manufacturing business maintained strong momentum during the quarter, with revenues growing 84% YoY. Now the contribution from this segment alone increased to 53% of the overall business in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Asphalt revenue increased to INR 53 crores from INR 30 crores QoQ with customers rising to 38 from 28
items.quote: Revenue from the segment increased to INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR 30 crores in Q 4 FY26. The number of customers transacted also increased to 38 from 28 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 56 days from 66 days at March 2026
items.quote: Our net working capital days further improved to 56 days, compared to 66 days as of March 2026, demonstrating our continued focus on efficient working capital management.

items.statement: Steady-state net working capital cycle expected at 60-70 days
items.quote: But I think steady state, look to be somewhere between 60-70 days on a net working capital cycle day.

items.statement: Current net debt at INR 14.5 crores, targeting INR 75-80 crores by end of FY27 with net debt-to-equity at 0.5-0.6x
items.quote: In this financial year, we will like to grow this to about INR 75-80 crores and be conservative in terms of our net debt -to-equity. As we maintained before as well, we would like to keep our net debt-to-equity at par of 0.5 to 0.6, not more than that.

items.statement: Top 10 customer concentration at 45-50%, well diversified across projects and regions
items.quote: The top 10 concentration is about 45-50%.

items.statement: Repeat order contribution improved to 82% from 78% QoQ
items.quote: Customer retention also remained a key strength of our platform. Repeat orders improved to 82% compared to 78% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: DaaS segment expected to contribute 9-11% of total revenue growing at 35-40%
items.quote: Overall, we should be between 9- 11% of the top line of the company. That is what Da aS would be. Number two is 9-11% is what we will be turning for. And given that the revenue would be growing 35-40%, DaaS would be following the same range.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing contribution target of 55-60% in coming months
items.quote: We will look to achieve a 55 over 60% contribution in the coming months.

items.statement: Supply chain financing provides 90-day credit period; interest cost borne by company or vendors negotiable
items.quote: They will pay our vendors on day one, and we get a credit period of around 90 days to make those payments. Now, there are two things here. One is the interest payment that is borne either by us or by the vendors sometimes. That's a point that we continuously negotiate, and that keeps on changing.

items.statement: Expected credit losses at ~0.5% of lifetime revenue (INR 22 crores on INR 3,800-4,000 crores); conservative provisioning to continue
items.quote: So, if you look at the lifetime revenue that we have done, it's close to about INR 3,800-4,000 crores. And the ECL that we have provided for till date is about INR 22 crores. It's just a little over 0.5%.

items.statement: Subsidiary merger process advanced with 3 of 4 regulators cleared; final timeline depends on government procedures
items.quote: The process has already started, and three out of the four regulators have already cleared it. We are at the last leg. However, the timeline obviously de fined on procedures of the government , so that we won't be able to comment on, but we are at a very advanced stage.

items.statement: DaaS model operates with professional deployment only, no capital commitment to projects
items.quote: We do not commit any kind of capital to these companies. We do not lend, our income is only by way of fees. Our investment is by way of the professionals that we deploy in these projects.

items.statement: No direct competition seen for DaaS model currently; focus on South India expansion (Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad)
items.quote: currently, we do not see anyone directly competing with this. But, of course, competition is always welcome. It keeps us on our toes. T he real estate market is huge, and especially the land availability in South, especially Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, that is going to be our main focus

items.statement: H1 typically 40% of sales, H2 60%; Q1 slow due to strategic cash flow management not demand
items.quote: Annually, we continue with our guidance of 35-40% growth. And typically, the first six months is around 40% of our sales, and the next six months are around 60% of us.

items.statement: Strong collections of over INR 1,100 crores in last financial year supporting working capital efficiency
items.quote: In the last financial year, we collected more than about INR 1,100 crores. We've been doing fantastically well on that front, and you can see the result in the reduction in our net working capital days.

items.statement: Delivered ~8.65 lakh metric tons of construction materials in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We delivered approximately 8.65 lakh metric tons of construction materials during Q1 FY27, supported by increasing utilization across our manufacturing partnerships and continued customer demand.

items.statement: FY27 full-year performance expected to remain broadly in line with FY26 levels
items.quote: Taking all these factors into account, our full-year performance for FY27 is expected to remain broadly in line with FY26 levels.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY27 expected in the same 25% to 27% range as previous years
items.quote: Yes, will be in the same range.

items.statement: Structural demand for international education remains intact despite near-term visa policy and currency headwinds
items.quote: What T can say with confidence is, structural demand for international education remains intact, our platform is scaling, our balance sheet is strong and our inorganic pipeline is active

items.statement: PAT margin expanded 152 bps YoY to 22.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: PAT margin expanding by 152 basis points to 22.6%, underscoring the scalability and capital efficiency of our operating model.

items.statement: Investing in technology, AI capabilities and talent with upfront costs; benefits expected to accrue progressively
items.quote: we are also investing in the people and infrastructure required to strengthen our technology and Al capabilities. While these investments involve some upfront cost, we expect the benefit to accrue progressively as the capabilities mature and scale across our operation

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Innova Consultancy in July 2026 via UK subsidiary; adds Netherlands as destination and Mexico as source market
items.quote: Subsequently, in quarter end in July 2026, we acquired 100% of Innova Consultancy Limited through our wholly owned UK subsidiary. This acquisition strengthens our UK partnership across UK and Europe and extends our presence in Mexico and marks our entry into a new destination market, Netherland.

items.statement: Strategic investment in ForeignAdmits in June 2026 for education financing and visa preparation; founder joined as Chief Product and Marketing Officer
items.quote: In June 2026, we made a strategic investment in ForeignAdmits, extending our capabilities to education financing and visa preparation. Its founder, Mr. Nikhil Jain, has joined us as Chief Product and Marketing Officer.

items.statement: Innova Consultancy acquisition less than INR7 crores; integration ongoing; indirect impact via Netherlands student placement
items.quote: With reference to margin expansion and profile, it's a very small acquisition of less than INR7 crores. So there won't be a huge impact — direct impact because of this acquisition, but there will be a big indirect impact because well be able to place students from our ecosystem to Netherlands.

items.statement: Christopher Nagle steps down as UK CEO, becomes Non-Executive Director and Chairman of Crizac Limited; Eric Wijmenga joins as Regional Director UK & Europe
items.quote: Mr. Christopher Nagle, who has led the group UK entity as Chief Executive Officer, will step down from his exccutive role. He will, however, continue to serve as a Director on the Board of the UK entity and assume the role of Non-Executive Director and Chairman of Crizac Limited, our Indian holding company

items.statement: Committed to minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least 3 years; 1 year done, minimum next 2 years committed
items.quote: We have declared in our DRHP that we'll be paying minimum of 40% of PAT of that year as a dividend to our shareholders. And that would be for at least minimum of 3 years. 1 year is already done, so minimum next 2 years we are committed to pay 40% dividend.

items.statement: Revenue per student lower due to unfavorable university mix; missed bonuses and slabs for top-ranked universities
items.quote: As a result, we have missed couple of bonuses and couple of slabs for our top-ranked universities, which has resulted in a lower revenue per student.

items.statement: Currency strength of USD and GBP increases effective cost of education; multi-geography sourcing model provides natural hedge
items.quote: The continued strength of both the US dollar and the pound sterling increases the effective cost of education in those markets, which can affect conversion timelines and student decision-making. We are monitoring these dynamics carefully, and our multi-geography sourcing model provides a natural hedge against single-market concentration risk.

items.statement: Visa policy tightening in US and UK (graduate route shortened, higher maintenance thresholds, stricter compliance) redirecting demand to Ireland, Germany, New Zealand
items.quote: In the United Kingdom, our largest destination market, the shortening of the graduate route, higher maintenance thresholds, and stricter compliance standards for sponsoring institutions have raised the bar on application quality. Importantly, this tightening in the US and elsewhere is redirecting demand towards markets such as Ireland, Germany, and New Zealand.

items.statement: UK student visa market share increased from 3.5% in FY24 to 6% in FY26; US study visa share for Indian students rose from 9% to 13.9%
items.quote: In the United Kingdom, our largest destination market, our share of total student visa granted increased from 3.5% in FY24 to 6% in FY26. From the same period, our share for US study visa granted to Indian student rose even more significantly from 9% to 13.9%.

items.statement: International travel disruption and flight cancellations between Feb-Jun expected to impact Q2 performance; recovery anticipated in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: In particular, intemational travel disruption and widespread flight cancellations between February and June are expected to impact our Q2 performance. However, as mobility normalizes and based on our current application flow, we anticipate a recovery across Quarter 3 and Quarter 4

items.statement: Top 3 universities contributed 41% of Q1 revenue due to seasonal concentration; full-year concentration lower and declining as other universities scale
items.quote: The 41% of top 3 universities which you are seeing is only for quarter 1. Quarter 1 includes April, May, and June, where you don't have a traditional university. Very few modem universities have the intake. Overall, you have around 10 to 15 universities only. That's why this concentration is looking high

items.statement: Deep strategic tie-ups with top 10 universities include defined SLAs, quick offer turnaround, joint events; replicating with others is multi-year process
items.quote: With these top 10 universities, which changes every year, we have a much deep strategic tie-up with them, where which includes defined SLA, quick offer turnaround, and lot of other events which we do with them. We are trying to do replicate the same with other remaining universities as well. These negotiations take time, and is a multi-year process.

items.statement: Platform scale (17,400+ counseling partners, 450+ university relationships, 5+ year partnerships) and compliance focus are key differentiators as universities prioritize quality recruitment
items.quote: As compliance and quality become central to universities' choice of recruitment partners, scale, trust, and execution capabilities have emerged as key differentiators. Our platform brings together more than 17,400 counseling partners and over 450 university relationships, with several of our leading partnerships extending beyond 5 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to be down; pent-up demand recovery in Q3 and Q4 to make full year flat vs FY26
items.quote: We have a negative growth in quarter 1 by 4% in constant currency growth. We expect Quarter 2 also to be a bit down. But considering the overall scenario, we expect the pent-up demand to come in Quarter 3 and Quarter 4. So overall will be same as last year.

items.statement: Acquired companies contributed ~INR 6 crores revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The revenue from the acquired company, all the acquired companics around? Yes. It is around INR6 crores

name: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Ltd

items.statement: FY28 minimum EBITDA guidance of INR3,000 crores, nearly 2.4x FY26 EBITDA of INR1,290 crores
items.quote: we are comfortable providing that new guidance, that we will have a minimum EBITDA of INR3,000 crores in FY28, which is nearly 2.4x the EBITDA in FY26.

items.statement: FY27 minimum new capacity addition guidance of 1.5 gigawatt
items.quote: we will be able to meet or exceed our guidance of 1.5 gigawatt of minimum new capacity addition during this year.

items.statement: Added 500 megawatt new capacity in Q1 FY27 (400 MW RE power sales, 100 MW RE services)
items.quote: in this quarter, we've commissioned about 400 gigawatt in the RE power sales segment and 100 megawatt in the RE services segment, so overall 500 megawatt.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month capacity addition run rate increased to 1,740 megawatt from 450 megawatt a year ago
items.quote: 450 megawatts of capacity addition have increased to about 1,740 megawatts in the trailing 12 months

items.statement: Total contracted capacity 6 gigawatt (3.5 GW operational, 2.5 GW under construction); RE services 682 MW operational, 147 MW under execution
items.quote: total contracted capacity is about 6 gigawatt as of 30th June. Of that 6 gigawatt, 3.5 gigawatt is already operational, and another 2,500 megawatt, therefore, is contracted and currently being executed.

items.statement: RE power sales EBITDA margin improved from 76% to 84% YoY; RE services EBITDA margin improved from 8.7% to 11.2% YoY
items.quote: RE power sales first quarter of last fiscal, our EBITDA margin was 76%, which has increased to about 84% in the first quarter of this fiscal. Secondly, second business segment is RE services, which was 8.7% EBITDA margin in Q1 of last year, which is 11.2% in Q1 of this year.

items.statement: Contracted under-construction tariff stable at INR4/unit vs operational portfolio at INR3.93/unit
items.quote: the tariff of the 2.5 gigawatt , which is contracted, yet to be built, without storage, without value to storage, is about INR4 per unit of power.

items.statement: Net debt INR11,809 crores (up from INR9,684 crores); weighted average interest cost reduced from 9.4% to 8.4% YoY
items.quote: the net debt number is INR11,809 crores compared to the INR9,684 crores last quarter, which is 31st March 2026. And similarly, the equity base also has increased to INR5,831 crores.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA, enabling first domestic corporate bond issuance
items.quote: our credit rating now is AA, which was a A+ for the last quarter same period. So that certainly is a very, very good outcome for us post listing, and that Kuldeep already touched upon that this also opens up a DC M opportunity for us

items.statement: Data & AI segment 42% of contracted capacity, 10x growth in 2 years; 35% market share of hyperscaler business in India
items.quote: We had 42% of our capacity in Data and AI in terms of our contracted capacity, 42% is Data and AI, and we have about 10x growth in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Industrial (non-Data & AI) contracted volumes doubled in 2 years (~46% CAGR); 7% penetration of industrial green power implies 93% headroom
items.quote: We have doubled our contracted volumes in the last 2 years, which means that we are growing at about 46% even in that segment.

items.statement: 80%+ of customers rated AA/AAA or multinational subsidiaries; 80% of new volumes from repeat customers; avg PPA tenure 23 years
items.quote: First is, how much of our customers are rated AA, AAA or multinational subsidiaries in India, and we are glad to report that honestly for the last decade or so, that number has been well above 80% and continues to be.

items.statement: Run rate EBITDA at end of FY26 was INR1,870 crores; minimum 4.6 GW opex capacity by 1st April 2027
items.quote: Our run rate EBITDA has increased. Run rate EBITDA means EBITDA from all operational assets as on that day for the next 12 months. So at the end of last fiscal, it was INR1,870 crores or so.

items.statement: Steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA estimated at INR16,000 crores
items.quote: the steady-state net debt corresponding to this INR3,000 crore s EBITDA will be INR16,000 crores

items.statement: ALMM deferral allows use of cheaper imported-cell modules saving ~INR60 lakh/MW; pulling forward projects to commission by 31st Dec to capture benefit
items.quote: The price difference is about INR60 lakhs per megawatt between Indian-made cells and imported cells. So, the benefit is about INR60 lakhs per megawatt.

items.statement: BESS integration initiated: first STU BESS project in Rajasthan greenlit; 3 MOUs signed in past month; targeting 2-hour storage; BESS-as-a-Service tariff ~INR3-3.5/unit (ex-generation)
items.quote: it would be about 2 hours of storage is what the numbers correspond to. So , that's what we are willing to talk about right now.

items.statement: Bikaner CTU project facing 70% curtailment; impact limited to ~13% of run-rate EBITDA (~INR170 cr annualized if continues full year); assume curtailment persists for rest of fiscal
items.quote: we have a project commissioning in Bikaner at the end of last fiscal, start of this fiscal, where we have about 70% curtailment, and expect that curtailment to actually continue throughout the duration of the current financial year.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu approvals saw 1-2 months flux after government change but now moving; no structural delay expected
items.quote: there was 1 or 2 months of just, I would describe it as flux, I would not call it delay, you know, sometimes when political administration changes, there's just 1 or 2 months of flux

items.statement: Low receivable days maintained; 38% of net debt (INR4,483 cr) against under-construction assets
items.quote: 38% of the total debt, which is INR4,483 crores, is against the under-construction asset.

items.statement: Capex not disclosed quarterly; 500 MW commissioned in Q1; organization demonstrated 1,750 MW/year execution capacity
items.quote: we are adding at the pace of about 1,750 megawatt a year. This is what we've demonstrated in the past 12 months

items.statement: Board discussed 5-6 organizational gap areas in last meeting; NRC subcommittee addressing them to support scaling
items.quote: we did discuss five-six areas of gaps and what we are doing to address them with the NRC subcommittee of the board

items.statement: C&I market highly fragmented; CleanMax market share ~14% (up from 12%); not winner-takes-all; advantages: 600+ customers, 80% repeat, 10-state footprint, wind+solar mix
items.quote: even a market leader like us has 14% or so market share. So, you know, we don't need to win every contract, right ? We are not in every state, we are not in every client discussion, that's fine.

items.statement: Planning first domestic corporate bond issuance enabled by AA rating
items.quote: we'll be coming up with a first domestic bond for CleanMax hopefully soon.

items.statement: Supply-constrained not demand-constrained; Data & AI and industrial pipelines very strong; Data center market could need 30-60 GW new RE over 5 years
items.quote: we are in an almost happy situation to be supply-constrained, not demand-constrained.

items.statement: Mutual fund QAAUM at ₹12.6 trillion, up 11% YoY; market share 15.1%
items.quote: Mutual fund QAAUM for the quarter stood at ₹12.6 trillion, registering Y-o-Y growth of 11%, compared to 11.4 trillion in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Active QAAUM at ₹8.6 trillion, up 10% YoY with 21% three-year CAGR
items.quote: Active QAAUM increased by ₹8.6 trillion, up 10% year-on-year and a robust three year CAGR of 21%, supported by consistent performance and healthy flows.

items.statement: Passive QAAUM rose to ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY
items.quote: Passive QAAUM rose to ₹4 trillion, up to 12% year-on-year, reinforcing our leadership in the segment.

items.statement: Alternate AUM (PMS, advisory, offshore, AIF) reached ₹16.5 trillion; AIF assets at ₹6,800 crores, up 29% YoY
items.quote: Our alternate business continued to scale with total non-mutual fund AUM comprising PMS, advisory, offshore, and AIF assets reaching ₹16.5 trillion.

items.statement: Offshore funds contributed approximately ₹45,000 crores to overall AUM
items.quote: Offshore funds contributed approximately ₹45,000 crores in the overall AUM.

items.statement: Unique investor count expanded 12% to 1.82 crores as of 30th June 2026
items.quote: Our unique investor count expanded by 12% to 1.82 crores as on 30th June '26, compared to 1.63 crores as on 30th June '25.

items.statement: SIP AUM increased by ₹2.1 trillion, up 15% YoY; monthly SIPs grew 14% to nearly ₹4,000 crores
items.quote: SIP AUM increased by ₹2.1 trillion, reflecting 15% year-on-year growth and monthly SIPs grew by 14% to nearly ₹4,000 crores.

items.statement: Distribution franchise: 23,000+ SBI branches, 124,000 IFAs, 10,000 national distributors, 90+ banking partners covering 98% pin codes
items.quote: Our distribution franchise continued to be deepened, supported by over 23,000 + SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, and over 90 banking partners, including State Bank of India, which has enabled us to reach investors at over 98 % pin codes across the country.

items.statement: B30 market share 19% MAAUM; 65% of SIP contribution from B30 locations
items.quote: We continue to remain market leader in B30 locations with an MAAUM market share of 19%.

items.statement: Launching second SIF strategy in Ex-Top 100 long-short category this quarter; NFO underway for SBI Nifty Midcap 150 Momentum 50 ETF FOF; also launching SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund
items.quote: We are further strengthening our SIF offering and will launch our second strategy this quarter, positioned in the Ex-Top 100 long-short category.

items.statement: Gross margins stable across strategies; net margins improved overall despite TER regulation changes
items.quote: Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable during the quarter, while net margins have improved at overall level despite change in regulation around transition to the base expense ratio and removal of exit load

items.statement: Operating margin improvement driven by asset mix shift from low-yield passive to high-yield equity/hybrid; yield up 2 bps
items.quote: You would have seen that has increased our yield by two basis points and this is a trend which has started, and it will continue because of the very high concentration on passive funds, we were making hardly two basis points.

items.statement: Arbitrage fund yield ~30 bps vs liquid ~11 bps; gold/silver ETF spread ~44-45 bps
items.quote: when we talk about the arbitrage fund which has been replace ment of liquid fund, in the arbitrage fund, our yield is around 30 basis points, whereas in the liquid it's around 11 basis points

items.statement: TER reduction impact largely passed to distributors (70-80% of business); net neutral or positive impact from April
items.quote: Majority of the reduction which has happened has been passed on to the distributors in a very calibrated manner so that they also don't feel a pinch and we also get the desired benefit.

items.statement: Opex focused on technology and human resources; quality of fund managers and AI/digital upgrades prioritized
items.quote: Opex, I may not give a guidance because you know, this is a silent period , but I must say our o pex will be mostly focused on technology and human

items.statement: 94% of investor transactions processed digitally via secure hybrid cloud infrastructure
items.quote: Around 94% of the investor transactions are processed digitally through our secure hybrid cloud infrastructure.

items.statement: Fresh SIPs added in Q1: 1.7 million; live SIPs at 16 million; monthly SIP flow maintained at ~₹4,000 crores despite volatility
items.quote: Fresh SIPs added in the last quarter is 1.7 million. Live SIP s have gone up to 16 million

items.statement: SBI YONO integration since Dec-Jan 2026; 2.5 lakh YONO users applied in IPO; KYC 2.0 to enlarge partnership
items.quote: In fact, I must tell you, in the last IPO, around 2.5 lakh YONO users applied through the platform directly in addition to other channels.

items.statement: SBI channel contributes ~33% of SIP flows (~₹1,300 crores of ₹4,000 crores); target to maintain 35% SBI / 65% other mix
items.quote: Out of 4,000 crores which has been talked about, 1,300 odd crore s coming from SBI channel and remaining 2,700 crores is coming from other channel and direct

items.statement: 90-92% of operating revenue from mutual fund business; alternate (PMS, advisory, international) 8%
items.quote: Almost 90-92% of the operating revenue is coming from the mutual fund business only. The PMS, advisory and international is remaining 8%.

items.statement: AIF/PMS more margin-accretive than equity; regulations easier; bullish on SEBI proposal for PMS via MF at ₹25 lakh ticket
items.quote: Yes, it's better than this. The regulations are little more, easier in this. Overall, you can say, it is more attractive than equity.

items.statement: Dividend policy uploaded; will pay per policy subject to board/AGM approval; special dividend paid last year
items.quote: The dividend policy is now, you know uploaded. So, we will continue to, pay as per that and of course, it will be depending on final board and AGM approvals on how we will pay.

items.statement: Employee expense drop in Q1 due to new labour code implementation adjustments; training expenses in Q2/Q3; no change in employee benefits
items.quote: We have fully implemented the new set of labour codes coming into action and that has a kind of impact on the whole cost, but it is not something that in its first quarter is like a little subdued, but our training expenses will come in second, third quarter.

items.statement: Board-approved ESOP policy in place; details internal and per SEBI guidelines; will share when public
items.quote: We have a board-approved ESOP policy and that is what we follow every year and it's basically internal to the organization and the standard policy should be followed and it is in line with the industry and SEBI guidelines.

items.statement: Flow market share aligned with AUM share at 11-12% for equity/hybrid; hybrid funds gaining share in volatile times
items.quote: For equity and hybrid, we are in line with the market share. It's around 11-12%.

items.statement: No QAAUM growth guidance given due to silent period post results; operating profit grew 17% YoY in Q1
