items.quote: This was achieved while maintaining a trading margin of 3.35 paise per unit. Notably, 60% of the trading volume came from exchange-traded products, with the remainder coming from bilateral short-term, long-term and medium-term trades.

items.statement: Signed long-term PPA of 1200 MW for solar power procurement from NTPC Green
items.quote: Recently, we have signed a long-term PPF of 1200 MW for procurement of solar power from NTPC Green.

items.statement: Expect power demand to grow steadily at 4%-6% annually, with short-term volatility from weather
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect power demand to grow steadily at 4%-6% annually, although short-term volatility may arise due to transient weather conditions.

items.statement: National Electricity Policy Draft 2026 targets per capita consumption of 2,000 kWh by 2030 and 4,000 kWh by 2047 with market reforms
items.quote: The National Electricity Policy Draft 2026 has been released by the Government of India, which aims for an increase per capita electricity consumption to 2,000 kWh by 2030 and over 4,000 kWh per person by 2047.

items.statement: Board approved investment up to Rs. 500 crore in JV with NLC India; DPE approval received for JV formation
items.quote: We had sought permission of the Board to invest up to Rs. 500 crore rupees into that JV, but that will unfold over a period of time as to what kind of projects we are deciding to execute.

items.statement: No new long-term contracts expected in FY27-FY28 due to regulatory constraints; NTPC Green 1200 MW solar PPA expected online by FY29
items.quote: Long-term capacity, I think, sir, explained that there is a constraint there from the regulatory side. So, we are not expecting to add any long-term contracts in that duration. However, the other initiatives on battery and those types of seasonals and time of the day differences, those we will be taking advantage of.

items.statement: Exchange markets provide lower margins; future margins depend on evolving portfolio including storage opportunities
items.quote: Exchange markets typically do provide a lower margin, but then that has to be complemented with the medium-terms and possibly going forward, we might be having this storage kind of context wherein possibly you will procure the direct data and charging power during the abundant hours and possibly would look for the opportunities to sell that power during the evening peak.

items.statement: Exploring battery storage opportunities - both asset ownership and rental models under evaluation
items.quote: We are looking both type of opportunities, whichever comes cheaper. There is an opportunity cost of capital if you invest capital and then there is a cost to be paid in the form of rentals for a long-term service provision from any storage device. So, we are evaluating the options.

items.statement: PTC exposure on debtors not more than 60 days; back-to-back billing for change-in-law/compensation items
items.quote: But as far as the PTC exposure is concerned, so that is not more than, I will say not more than 60 days wherein PTC has taken an exposure and that is pending.

items.statement: Provision of Rs. 17.4 crore made for generator dispute; adjudicating authority ordered payment before recovery from counterparty
items.quote: Now, the matter has been decided by the Adjudicating Authority, which has said that you first pay and then you take a stance to recover it from the counterparty. So, for payment, we are creating this provision.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of Rs. 23/share from PEL asset sale proceeds (Rs. 1,185 crore received, Rs. 1,100 crore net); called one-time special dividend
items.quote: This dividend which we declared yesterday has to be seen in the context of the earlier deal from which we earned significant cash when we sold our PEL assets to ONGC. So, based on discussions with various stakeholders, currently Management and the Board decided to for the interim dividend, but that should be seen as a one-time measure.

items.statement: Engaged SBI Caps as transaction advisor for PFS disinvestment; aim to maximize shareholder value; process expected to progress by end of FY27
items.quote: We have engaged the services of SBI case for this purpose. We shall be exploring options regarding what would be the best way to realize the best value for our shareholders.

items.statement: NLC India JV formation approved by DPE; administrative hurdles removed; MOUs also with SECI, ESL and others
items.quote: Regarding NLC India, I am happy to inform that the approval of the Department of Public Enterprises has been received for formation of JV with the NLC. So, the administrative hurdle in creating that JV post our MOU with NLC is now removed.

items.statement: Standalone net cash position of Rs. 2,451 crore as of June 30; interim dividend to be paid from this
items.quote: cash position as on 30th June is, net cash is Rs. 2451 crores. Shivan Sarvaiya: Rs. 2451 crores? Pankaj Goel: Yes. So, now out of this, we will be giving the interim dividend, which we have declared

items.statement: Power exchange associate (HPX) revenue Rs. 13.98 crore, PAT Rs. 5.16 crore in Q1 FY27
items.value: Rs. 13.98 crore revenue, Rs. 5.16 crore PAT
items.quote: Yes. So, the total income for the quarter's revenue from operation for June '26 is Rs. 13.98 crore. The profit after tax was around Rs. 5.16 crore.

items.statement: CERC ruling limits trading member shareholding in HPX to 5%; PTC holds >22% and cannot become trading member unless stake reduced
items.quote: CERC ordered that if you want to become a trading member, then you have to limit your shareholding to the level of 5% only. Since we are currently owning more than 22% of take sales, we cannot become a trading member on that platform.

items.statement: Long-term contracts (15-25 years) face evolving legal/regulatory risks; difficult to price litigation and policy change risks into spreads
items.quote: These are the actual risks of being in this business. You see the contract is for 15 years, 25 years and so. And when we frame the contract, law was entirely different. Now how the law has evolved over a period of time is for everyone to see.

items.statement: Trading license threshold low (Category 5 net worth minimal); competition on reputation, offerings, relationships, balance sheet strength
items.quote: The threshold for entering into the power trading business is really very low. There is categorization of the license from Category 1 to Category 5 and for Category 5, even the net worth requirement is pretty low, I would say.

items.statement: No definitive projections given for consultancy business; described as stable and steadily growing
items.quote: Giving the definitive projections is basically I am bound by the protocol not to give that kind of guidance. But we have been steadily growing, and I would say that that's also a stable piece of business.

items.statement: Standalone: Volume +12% to 25.8 BU, Op income +2% to Rs. 113 cr, PBT -32% to Rs. 96 cr, PAT -33% to Rs. 71 cr, EPS Rs. 2.39
items.quote: Volume has increased by 12% to 25.8 billion units from 23 billion units. The volume has increased mainly due to increase in our exchange trade. Total operational income has increased by 2% to Rs. 113 crore from Rs. 111 crore. Profit before tax has decreased by 32% to Rs. 96 crore from Rs. 141 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated: Volume +12% to 25.8 BU, PBT -48% to Rs. 151 cr (PFS had Rs. 82 cr impairment reversal in base), PAT -54% to Rs. 112 cr, EPS Rs. 3.31
items.quote: Profit before tax has decreased by 48% to Rs. 151 crore from Rs. 289 crore. The decrease in PBT is basically on account that there is a decrease in the profit before tax of PTC India and change in PBT of PTC Financial Services, our subsidiary has also decreased. As there was a reversal of Rs. 82 crore of impairment provision in the corresponding quarter ended June '25.

items.statement: Surcharge and rebate income declined due to improved Discom liquidity; Discoms now availing rebates and paying on time
items.quote: Decrease in profit before tax is mainly on account of lower net surcharge income and rebate income. As has been said earlier, this is due to the improved liquidity of the Discoms.

items.statement: Rebate income decline also from Discom liquidity improvement; PTC previously earned net rebate by paying generators early and collecting later from Discoms
items.quote: That also is actually related with the liquidity of the Discoms. You see, whenever there is a contract, there is a provision for availing rebate. If generator to whom I have to pay, I pay before time, I earn a rebate. And if the distribution company which has procured power from me pays before time, they also earn a rebate.

items.statement: Cross-border operations stable with Bhutan, Nepal, Bangladesh; energy flows to Bangladesh stable with regular payments
items.quote: In the cross-border markets also, our operations continue across all the three grid-connected neighboring countries, which are Bhutan, Nepal and Bangladesh. Energy flows to Bangladesh remain stable under the agreed contextual framework, with regular flow of payments to our accounts.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11% plus/minus 50 bps with bias towards higher end
items.quote: We remain confident in our annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% plus/minus 50 basis points with a bias towards the higher end.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 10.3%, down from prior year due to commodity inflation, pass-through dilution and wage hikes
items.quote: On the profitability front, EBITDA excluding exceptional income in the previous year grew by 21% year-on-year to INR572 crores with EBITDA margins of 10.3%.

items.statement: Commodity price pass-through without markup caused ~40 bps mathematical margin dilution in Q1
items.quote: Second, even as the commodity price increases are systematically recovered over time, pass-throughs occur on an absolute cost basis without any markup, resulting in mathematical margin dilution. In our case, the impact was approx 40 basis points due to this margin dilution.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at INR 1,750 crores; total project pipeline INR 3,800 crores with INR 1,400 crores spent to date
items.quote: In terms of capex plan, it remains the s ame, what we have shared in the last call of around INR1,750 crores for the current fiscal year. For next year, obviously, we will give our in annual guidance. But if you see our total project capex, and if you go to that, there is a slide on project total announced, which is almost INR3,800 crores in pipeline of which INR1,400 is already spent till

items.statement: Sunroof order book crossed INR 500 crores with new panoramic sunroof order INR 130 crores and electric roller shades INR 40 crores
items.quote: Together with these orders, our total sunroof order book have crossed INR500 crores.

items.statement: Seating export orders of INR 390 crores annual peak value from 3 new customers in Europe and North America
items.quote: Exports reached INR72 crores this quarter, growing consistently quarter -after-quarter and will continue to b e a major growth driver, supported by the landmark export orders of approximately INR390 crores of annual peak value from 3 new customers across Europe and North America communicated in last quarter

items.statement: Lighting 2W new order of INR 450 crores annual peak value announced last quarter (~25% of current 2W lighting revenue)
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect meaningful market share gains over the next few years, supported by the significant new order of approximately INR450 crores of annual peak value announced last quarter, equivalent to nearly 25% of the current two-wheeler lighting revenues.

items.statement: Lighting: new global OEM nomination for domestic 4W lighting; interior ambient lighting gaining traction; Indonesia 4W lighting plant secured second customer with SOP Q2 FY28
items.quote: First, we received a business nomination from a global OEM for domestic 4 -wheel lighting supply in India, a strategic entry into a new customer that opens up the door to incremental customer share and cross -selling opportunities. Second, interior ambient lighting is gaining commercial traction with p ositive customer decisions that open an entirely new avenue of growth for our lighting portfolio

items.statement: Seating: anchor customer secured for new 4W seating greenfield at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (INR 320 crores capex, ops by Q2 FY28)
items.quote: To support this new product line, the company's Board of Directors had approved the setting up of state-of- the-art greenfield manuf acturing facility in Chhatrapati, Sambhajinagar with a proposed investment of approximately INR320 crores. The facility is expected to commence operations by Q2 FY28, and we have already secured business from an anchor customer

items.statement: Exports from India INR 228 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR 141 crores in Q1 FY26 (+62%); exports now ~10% of revenue
items.quote: International business contributed around 10% of total revenues during Q1 FY27. This performance was driven by improved export traction, particularly in the two-wheeler switching and seating segments. Exports from India stood at approximately INR228 crores during the quarter, as against INR141 crores in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Target to double/triple export absolute value; export % depends on domestic growth pace
items.quote: So our target absolutely is to double and triple the export in terms of absolute numbers. But in terms of percentage, it all also depends on how much domestic growth market is giving us.

items.statement: Some customers moved to monthly commodity price adjustments; wage hikes partially absorbed via automation/productivity
items.quote: In fact, we have a customer who has also given in 1 or 2 of the commodities in the monthly sort of price, which we have also mentioned in terms of our last ca ll. So that's a very good thing. Customers has been also conscious of this fact. And we have also seen some of the customers already announced some sort of price hikes to absorb these kind of cost increases

items.statement: Press Note 3 approval received for Inovance JV; Chinese regulatory changes tightening tech partnership norms; Inovance reviewing guidelines
items.quote: During the quarter, we had received Press Note 3 approval for our proposed JV with Inovance. However, as was advised earlier, the joint venture will also require approval in their host country China. There have been recent regulatory changes in China, tightening the norms for such technology partnership. Inovance is reviewing the revised guidelines and seeking clarifications for next steps.

items.statement: Finance costs tightly controlled, up only INR 2 crores to INR 46 crores; expansion funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Finance costs remain tightly controlled, rising only INR2 crores to INR46 crores as majority of our expansion program continues to be funded through healthy internal accruals, a reflection of strong cash generation.

items.statement: Revenue growth 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores (excl. prior period income), outpacing industry production growth of 22%
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 5,557 crores, representing a robust 26% year-on-year growth as against INR4,420 crores, excluding prior period income of INR 69 crores in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: PAT attributable to shareholders grew 24% to INR 296 crores vs normalized INR 239 crores
items.quote: PAT attributable to shareholders grew 24% to INR296 crores compared to normalized PAT of INR239 crores in

items.statement: Inovance JV pending Chinese regulatory approval; recent tightening of norms for tech partnerships creates uncertainty
items.quote: There have been recent regulatory changes in China, tightening the norms for such technology partnership. Inovance is reviewing the revised guidelines and seeking clarifications for next steps.

items.statement: Employee cost grew 15% YoY vs 26% revenue growth; absolute cost will rise with new plants but % of revenue not expected to increase
items.quote: In terms of employee cost, whether that will increase with new capacity, and when you have new capacity you will have more sales. and new sales when you have, then obviously, you will have new plants, you will have new people to run those plants. So obviously, in terms of absolute numbers, the cost definitely will go up because if you're setting new plant, you will need people to run those plants.

items.statement: Depreciation Q1 lower than Q4 due to WDV method in casting business; new assets start with lower base
items.quote: In terms of depreciation, quarter -on-quarter dro p Q1 to Q4 largely happens because in our casting business, which is a capital-intensive business, there is a WDV method of depreciation. So once the new starts, you start with a lower base. So that is one of the reasons why your depreciation in Q1 normally is lower in that business from Q4 to Q1

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 is 17-18%; Q1 achieved over 19%
items.quote: EBITDA margins remained strong at over 19%, exceeding a guidance of 17% to 18%, reflecting an efficient operational performance.

items.statement: Long-term growth aspiration accelerated from 15% CAGR to 20% CAGR over next three years
items.quote: As reiterated earlier, our aspiration is to accelerate our long-term growth trajectory from 15% CAGR to a 20% CAGR over the next three years.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth target 15-18%; Q1 achieved 19%
items.quote: Generally, we said that overall, on a consolidated basis, we will be growing from 15% to 18%. That was our revenue target. I think we have crossed our targets and have been able to achieve close to around 19%.

items.statement: Other income estimated at Rs 30 crores for full year
items.quote: The overall estimate for the other income should be at around Rs. 30 crores for the annualized year.

items.statement: Exports expected to remain flattish during the year
items.quote: Looking at the current scenario, I think exports should remain flattish during the year.

items.statement: Goregaon land monetization under exploration for development or outright sale; no deadline
items.quote: When you spoke about the land, that is also in a standstill position and we are exploring opportunities of development as well as outright sale for the land.

items.statement: Net 4 EBOs added in Q1 FY27; total network 670 as of 30 June 2026
items.quote: In line with our strategy of expanding our retail footprint, we have added a net four EBOs during Q1 FY’27, taking our total network to 670 as of 30 th June 2026

items.statement: EBO net addition target 50-70 stores for FY27
items.quote: The current target for our EBO would be around 50 to 70 odd stores for the current year on a net basis.

items.statement: EBO footprint above 4 lakh square feet
items.quote: It should be above 4 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Market remains challenging but portfolio positioned to gain market share
items.quote: The market remains challenging. But we feel that on a KKCL portfolio, as the brands are positioned, we will be able to gain better market share.

items.statement: Summer season booking roadshow traction was encouraging
items.quote: During the period, we have also done a roadshow for booking for the second season, which is summer. And the traction was encouraging.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 29% YoY to Rs 52 crores; margin over 19%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 29% year-on-year to Rs. 52 crores, driven by disciplined execution and operating leverage. EBITDA margins remained strong at over 19%.

items.statement: GP margin increased by 1% in Q1; cotton price increase may impact GP margins ahead
items.quote: We definitely see that there has been an increase in cotton prices. However, for the current quarter, our GP margin had increased by a percent.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain constant for coming quarters
items.quote: Going forward, I think it may have an impact on our GP margins. But we are trying to reducing the discounts or passing it to the consumers. And we feel that the EBITDA margins will remain constant for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 279 crores, up 19% YoY; apparel volumes up 24% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY'27 stood at Rs. 279 crores, registering a healthy 19% year-on-year growth driven by strong growth in both volume as well as value. Consolidated apparel volumes grew by an encouraging 24% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Retail channel grew 29% YoY; non-retail driven by e-commerce
items.quote: The retail channel grew 29% year-on-year, driven by continued expansion of our EBO network and strong contribution from the LFS channels, particularly led by Kraus. Non-retail growth was primarily driven by the e-commerce segment.

items.statement: Jeans contribute ~50% of revenue and grew double digits
items.quote: Jeans almost contributes to more than 50% of the business and it grew by double digits.

items.statement: Other category (accessories) declining; focus on apparel business
items.quote: There is no specific reason. Anyways, other includes generally accessories as a category which is a trading item for us and which contributes to lower GP. Our main focus is apparel business.

items.statement: Competition intensity exists but aligned brand strategies enable market share gains
items.quote: There is competition intensity within this sector. But we feel as we have aligned our strategy, we will be able to gain better market share.

items.statement: Debtors receivable fell quarter-on-quarter; similar on YoY basis
items.quote: The debtor remains almost similar on a quarter-on-quarter basis. In fact, the debtors, in terms of debtors receivable, it has fallen down if you compare on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with Rs 400-500 crores cash; exploring acquisitions for inorganic growth
items.quote: We are still exploring some acquisition in terms of inorganic growth. So, the utilization of such cash availability will help us in while looking at a bigger ticket size acquisition.

items.statement: Acquisition framework in place; deals not uniform each year; three-year roadmap for 20% CAGR
items.quote: While acquisition may not materialize uniformly every year, a three-year strategic roadmap has been designed to deliver this accelerated growth trajectory.

items.statement: Kraus integration successful; brand delivering strong sales growth and EBITDA margins in line with KKCL
items.quote: The continued strong performance of Kraus also validates the successful integration of the brand following its acquisition and reflects our progress in expanding the business across age groups and gender segments.

items.statement: New acquisitions difficult to comment until deal finalized
items.quote: It is difficult to comment till the time the deal goes through.

items.statement: Cotton prices increased; reducing discounts or passing cost to consumers
items.quote: We definitely see that there has been an increase in cotton prices. However, for the current quarter, our GP margin had increased by a percent. Going forward, I think it may have an impact on our GP margins. But we are trying to reducing the discounts or passing it to the consumers.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 15% YoY for FY27, targeting ~INR6,500 crores
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue growth target that we have given of 15% on the last year's top line. So that's close to around INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR8,000-10,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: So currently standing at, say, INR7,000 crores, we have given a target of INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores for this year, which we are quite optimistic that we'll achieve that target for sure.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 14-15% for FY27
items.quote: We'll be doing 14% to 15% of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR7,500 crores shifted to FY28 with 14-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So this thing our target of INR7,500 crores for FY27 is now shifted to FY28. So we will be doing a INR7,500 crores by FY28 now with similar margins of 14% to 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Order book of INR22,246 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Total order book as on 30th June 2026 stood at INR22,246 crores.

items.statement: Order inflows of INR5,500 crores in Q1 FY27 plus INR1,500 crores L1 position for Delhi Metro
items.quote: So currently, as you can see for the Q1, we stand at a number of INR5,500 crores till today and there is an L1 position of INR1,500 crores for Delhi Metro underground project. So that makes it INR7,000 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 14.1% vs 14.6% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 stood at 14.1% as compared to 14.6% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex of INR34 crores; FY27-28 capex of INR150 crores per year including maintenance
items.quote: So INR100 crores maintenance capex will be there. And INR250 crores we have already done part of it last year another INR100 crores for 2 years. So say 150 for each year.

items.statement: GMLR project: first TBM ready for launch, second TBM assembly advanced, targeting launch in 2 months
items.quote: So GMLR project is in full swing. We have -- yesterday, we completed 2,000 links of casting. That's around 4 kilometers of tunnel has been casted in the casting yard. And the first TBM is ready for launch for drilling in the ground physically.

items.statement: Chennai NHAI packages timeline extended to December 2028; state package 65% complete, targeting March 2027 handover
items.quote: The Chennai project, we have four packages of central government and one package of state government. So the state government project was costing INR580 crores, which is like almost 65% completed. So we plan to hand over it by March 2027 the work should be completed.

items.statement: Anand Nagar project 15% complete, targeting October 2028 completion
items.quote: We hav e completed around 15% in Anand Nagar Saket and we intend to complete the same in scheduled date of October 28 this project

items.statement: GMLR internal target June 2029 completion, max December 2029 (vs original November 2028)
items.quote: So by June 29, we intend to complete the project internally. But say, December 29 max is what we'll be going ahead.

items.statement: Vadhvan project mobilization underway, actual excavation to start post-monsoon in October
items.quote: So after rains, the actual excavation and this work will be started only in October.

items.statement: Working capital days at 103 in Q1 FY27 vs 99 in FY26; target range 100-110 days
items.quote: Working capital days for Q1 FY 27 stood at 103 days as compared to 99 days for FY 26.

items.statement: Net debt negative INR45 crores as of June 30, 2026; gross debt-equity 0.24
items.quote: Net debt as on June 30, 2026 stood at negative INR45 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt INR840 crores as of June 2026, expected below INR800 crores by March 2027
items.quote: So we proceed this like less than INR800 crores by the year end, not more.

items.statement: Fund-based limit INR1,300 crores (39% utilized), non-fund-based INR5,000 crores (65% utilized)
items.quote: Fund based limit is INR1,300 crores out of that INR530 crores is term loans and balance INR800 crores is EC. Dhananjay: Okay or non-fund based? Kamal Gupta: Non-fund based is INR5,000 crores

items.statement: BMC water restriction temporarily slowed projects; issue now resolved with monsoon
items.quote: growth during the quarter was tempered by external factors, including the U.S. Iran war and most notably the restrictions imposed by the BMC on water usage at construction sites.

items.statement: Chennai NHAI project delay due to Cooum river restrictions; extension granted with prolongation cost paid
items.quote: Extension was basically due to like the whole project is out of 25 kilometers, 21 kilometer is in the Cooum river. So in Cooum River there are some restrictions by the state department. So that was the reason it has gone ahead. And NHAI has already given us the extension for that.

items.statement: Order book execution delayed by land acquisition, tree-cutting permissions, GAD finalization; now largely resolved
items.quote: But unfortunately, the new orders that we bagged in 2024 by March '24. In that year, it was basically the 2 years that is GMLR, VDCR, Chennai Elevated Corridor these projects which we have bagged, including Orange Gate, which got cancelled. So there were some big ticket size projects which did not take off due to the land acquisition issues, tree-cutting permissions and finalization of GAD.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR50,000 crores to INR1 lakh crore over next 9-12 months from MSRDC, MMRDA, NHAI, DMRC
items.value: INR50,000 crores to INR1 lakh crore
items.quote: And in the near future, there is around INR50,000 crores to INR1 lakh crore job worth of jobs that's coming, which is mainly from MSRDC, the Shaktipeeth corridors, the Uttan-Virar corridor that the MMRD is going to come up around INR15,000 crores, INR16,000 crores and various other NHAI and the other flyovers and DMRC contracts and metro jobs.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration but deferred due to capex needs from new orders
items.quote: So currently we also understand and we know that it's a highly lucrat ive thing to going for you clipping or acquisition or whatever you call it, but currently we are just waiting for some time but yes it's on our cards

items.statement: Tax rate ~29.7% in Q1 FY27, expected to normalize to FY26 levels after TBM capitalization
items.quote: So for the entire year it will be reducing because it is at this point of time based on available information we have damaged and as I said 300 crores TBM once we capitalize it will give shelter to the tax and the rate will automatically come down.

items.statement: Prompt payments from DMRC, MMRDA, MSRDC, BMC, NHAI; no cash flow issues with these clients
items.quote: For us then with DMRC, MMRDA, MSRDC, BMC, NHAI, there is absolutely no issue and we are getting prompt payments from them. So it's quite regular cash flow and absolutely no problem with regards to that.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR1000 crores for FY27 is on track
items.quote: Yes, INR1000 crores is on track.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 28-30% for FY27 to be maintained
items.quote: Yes, this quarter is 33% because of Ind AS impact is there, because we are opening the bigger stores now. So yes, 30 plus percent what we delivered last financial year, it has to be maintained and it will be maintain.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth target of around 5% for FY27
items.quote: So we expect it to be around 5%.

items.statement: Gross margin target of 60% average annual margin on track
items.quote: Absolutely. We are working on our annual target, right? So couple of quarters it may be up and down, but overall target of maintaining the average annual margin of 60% is absolutely on track.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 11-12% going forward
items.quote: And we are going forward expecting is approximately 12% -- 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Long-term SSG target of 5-6%
items.quote: So we have always been focusing on SSG of approximately 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Plan to open 28-30 stores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So we expect to open around 28 to 30 stores in the Q2.

items.statement: Opened 27,000 sq ft in Q1, plan 55,000-60,000 sq ft in Q2
items.quote: So we have opened around 27,000 square feet in Q1 and we expect to open 55,000 to 60,000 square feet in Q2, so that is more than double square feet we are planning to open in Q2.

items.statement: Average store size increased to 1,810 sq ft in Q1, targeting ~1,500 sq ft average by year-end
items.quote: In Q1, our average size of opening store is 1810. And we are expecting more bigger stores opening in Q2 as well. So our size is continuously increasing. So average size by the end of this financial year, we are expecting approximately 1500 square feet per store.

items.statement: Q2 volume growth expected to be muted, stronger growth expected in H2 driven by winter season and late Diwali
items.quote: This time the Diwali is late. Last year we had Diwali in the mid-October and this time Diwali is around on 10th November. So we expect Q3 the volume growth will be seen. In Q2, I don't think there will be much volume growth.

items.statement: July had moderate numbers, festive sales postponed due to late Raksha Bandhan
items.quote: So right now the July was having moderate numbers, not great numbers. But this time the Raksha Bandhan is on 30th or 28th August and last year Raksha Bandhan was on 10th August. So definitely the festive sale has got postponed.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by product mix and inflation correction

items.quote: If you take the Q1 average realization, realization it should be the same what you are saying is that same, it should be in the region of around INR850 crores to INR900 crores.

items.quote: If you look at the current Q1 levels, I think it is more or less the same, but there may be an incremental growth of 0.5%–1%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capacity utilization at 90-95% for new 4,500 MT capacity, overall 100% utilization with 15 days annual maintenance

items.quote: As per the current price levels, because now I am not doing any FDC right, but as per the current market prices and all, if I take that into consideration, it is around 28% to 32% difference is there between SDC and FDC.

items.quote: Now Q1, we did around 45-55 ratio. 45% bulk and 55% consumer packs.

items.quote: Out of this Rs. 500 crores, the CAPEX will be around Rs. 220 crores – Rs. 240 crores, roughly, in a full year basis.

items.statement: Annual free cash flow estimated at Rs. 480-500 crores
items.quote: On a full year basis, definitely, this will be in the range of around Rs. 480 crores-Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 20-21% maintainable for next 3-4 years

items.statement: Volume growth of 7-8% expected for next 3-4 years based on current activities
items.quote: Even for the next three to four years, we can expect the volume growth in the range of around 7% to 8% based on the activities what we are carrying today.

items.quote: July, we already performed around 10% growth in the tonnage and we are expecting simi lar growth, at least around, on a full quarter basis, 9% growth is possible

items.quote: The EBITDA margin is improved by 36 basis points from 21.4% to 21.8% mainly driven by increasing in the freight realization.

items.statement: If fuel prices decline, freight rates may reduce 2-3%
items.quote: Effectively, the reduction will be in the range of around 2% to 3%, not beyond that.

items.statement: Fuel procurement cost per liter increased from Rs. 83 to Rs. 94

items.quote: The growth in revenue is also on account of growth in volumes by 90% from Rs. 9,35,000 metric tons to Rs. 10,19,000 metric tons.

items.quote: The cash flow of have been effectively utili zed for the purpose of capital expenditure to the tune of Rs. 76 crores in the current quarter mainly for the purpose of addition of commercial vehicles of Rs. 18 crores and Rs. 49 crores is utilized for the purchase of land and building facilities in the critical locations of our operations

items.statement: Full-year property CAPEX of Rs. 150-160 crores, vehicle CAPEX of ~Rs. 100 crores
items.quote: On the properties, we may invest around Rs. 150 crores – Rs. 160 crores. And on the vehicles, remaining around Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: Existing fleet capacity fully utilized, new volume growth requires additional CAPEX or hired vehicles

items.statement: Net debt reduced from Rs. 440 crores to Rs. 391 crores in Q1
items.quote: The remaining surplus cash flow resulted into reduction in net debt from Rs. 440 crores as of 31st March to Rs. 391 crores as of quarter end.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.3x, year-end debt expected to remain at current levels despite buyback and CAPEX
items.quote: It's hardly around 0.3x of the debt equity ratio. So, this kind of a debt level has to be continued considering the growth and other aspects of the company.

items.quote: The board had approved the buyback of shares by the company to the tune of Rs. 280 crores with a per share value of Rs. 320 which is much higher than the current market price. The promoters of the company are not participating in this buy back.

items.statement: Shareholder rewards to continue annually via buyback or dividend
items.quote: No, but the reward to the shareholder will continue every year, either in a way of buyback or dividend.

items.statement: Bulk diesel purchase stopped as bulk price Rs. 15/liter above retail; will resume if crude falls making bulk 2-3 cheaper than retail
items.quote: The bulk purchase price is at least around Rs. 15 more than the normal price. In this scenario, we cannot buy the bulk purchase or buying from the refinery.

items.statement: Unorganized operators hold ~70% market share in areas VRL operates
items.quote: So, even today, the area where we are operating, at least around 70% of the contribution is coming from unorganized operators.

items.statement: No acquisition plans; inorganic growth difficult due to operational mismatch
items.quote: We don't have good opportunities which will match with our business operations. We did that exercise, but unfortunately, the matching is very difficult.

items.statement: Lower monsoon may slightly impact agriculture sector volumes (10-11% of total) in coming quarters
items.quote: Considering the lower monsoon, it may little bit impact in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Freight realization per ton increased 9% YoY to Rs. 8,546, 5% QoQ
items.quote: The growth in revenue is mainly on account of increase in freight rates across all the commodi ties and geographies due to which the realization of freight per ton increased by 9% from Rs. 7,852 per ton to Rs. 8,546 per ton

items.statement: Footfalls grew due to high-end procedures, robotics, and clinic network driving referrals; strong general healthcare demand across regions
items.quote: We've been off late doing a lot of high-end procedures and also the robotics has gone up substantially. So, if you see the margin improvement over the last two, three quarters, they are essentially on account of high volume of high -end procedures and also increased use of technology and robotics.

items.statement: Clinics contribute ~30% of total OPD footfalls, strengthening brand and driving hospital footfall growth
items.quote: If you look at the data of clinics, clinics we do more or less, the total footfalls of patients in clinics is approximately 30% of the total OPD footfalls in the hospital.

items.statement: Core operating margin expansion expected from leverage benefit as no meaningful bed addition for 2-3 years; will balance cash flows, growth investment, and customer pricing
items.quote: This will continue because we don't have any meaningful bed addition coming in for the next two to three years. Having said that, we have to make a choice on the leverage benefit.

items.statement: Insurance loss ratio spiked due to small book volatility and few large claims; expense ratio fell substantially; AI solutions, in-housing claims, and portfolio focus on SME/retail to improve loss ratio over time
items.quote: It is still a relatively small book, and so a few large claims sometimes can have a disproportionate impact when you look at loss ratios. But at the same time, when you look at the growth, there are other benefits.

items.statement: Loss ratio expected to moderate to acceptable levels as book scales and initiatives deliver; short-term volatility may persist until scale achieved
items.quote: And as these measures start to deliver benefits and the book size grows, which is important, I feel confident the loss ratio will moderate to acceptable levels over a period of time.

items.statement: Retail insurance customers largely choose NH hospitals; group policy customers improving but still offered choice; focus on service and engagement to drive NH preference
items.quote: On the retail side, a lot of our customers come to our come to our hospitals by choice. And on the group side, we are seeing those numbers improving.

items.statement: Most projects within acceptable 6-month timeline; partner model projects delayed by licensing issues, expected to resolve in a month; Southwest Bangalore 100-bed project to start by end of Q2
items.quote: There are a couple of asset-light partner model projects, which are running a bit slower, specifically because from the partner side in terms of certain licensing issues, the delays, licensing, which obviously we are in constant discussion with them, and i t should get sorted in t he next month or so.

items.statement: Southwest Bangalore project at end stage of construction, expected to operationalize by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: And when it comes to the project in Southwest Bangalore, as I said, we are at the end stage of th is construction and we are hopeful to start it by the end of Q2.

items.statement: INR 3,000 crores committed for projects over next two years; part own contribution, part borrowing; cash from India and Cayman operating performance
items.quote: So, this will get deployed into the projects that we've committed over the next two years. We've committed INR 3,000 crores. A part of that will be our own contribution and a part of it will be borrowing in nature.

items.statement: ALOS target 3.9-4.0 days; currently 4.3 in Q1 FY27; balancing complex cases and medical patients
items.quote: Our intention is to get it down somewhere between 3.9 and 4. That's a journey, because that's one of the areas of efficiencies we've been working on for the last couple of quarters, and we want to do that.

items.statement: Clinic OP consultations grew ~30% YoY to ~66,000 in Q1 FY27; high member revenue share; opening 2 more clinics this quarter
items.quote: In terms of ove rall transactions in terms of OP consults, these have grown to about grown by about 30% year-on-year. And in the quarter, we did about 66,000 consultations across our clinic network.

items.statement: Focus on existing strong clusters for current expansion phase; Phase 2 will consider underpenetrated states like UP, Bihar after progress on Phase 1
items.quote: We have outlined over the next 3 financial years or so, how that capital deployment will look like. And once we start Phase 2, following some progress on Phase 1, we will consider newer markets and newer geographies.

items.statement: India business net margin expanded 400 bps YoY including clinic losses; Cayman hospital back to optimal margins; UK, India Insurance, Cayman Insurance causing margin dilution but on improving trajectory
items.quote: If you look at the India business per se, including combining the losses from the clinic business, even if you set that off, the net margin has expanded by 400 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated margin trajectory expected upward in medium term as insurance losses recoup and UK transformation progresses
items.quote: In all, overall, we are positive that the margin trajectory will be in the upward direction from here, given that all the efforts that we are taking will start to bear fruit in the medium term for us.

items.statement: Cayman insurance July renewals 100% acceptance at higher prices; similar expectation for January cycle; worst losses likely behind barring abnormal large claims
items.quote: So on the exercise of renewals in July, we're very happy to note that we had a 100% acceptance and renewal rate, which is quite unusual for a for a new insurer.

items.statement: Cayman hospital volumes show healthy double-digit YoY growth in discharges and outpatient footfalls; Q1 seasonally slower; insurance book at USD 60M annualized should drive hospital growth
items.quote: Having said that, we do look forward to the growth being a little more in the hospital, and as you said, it should result from the insurance company growing. The insurance company is not small anymore. I mean, it's looking at a USD60 million annualized book of business.

items.statement: UK Q1 revenue down sequentially (seasonal) but up ~5% YoY; heat wave caused chiller failures and lost operating days; worst likely behind by mid-Q2
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, which we'll have to compare to the period prior to acquisition, there is about a 5% year-on-year revenue growth. It would have been higher, however, as you would have read in the media, there was a widespread heat wave.

items.statement: UK cost optimization: standardizing implants/consumables/drugs, consolidating purchasing, procedure standardization, consultant productivity alignment, non-clinical automation via software modules
items.quote: So on the cost side pretty much what we started in NH in India about, I would say, 15 years ago, so, standardizing the variation in implants, consumables, drugs consolidating purchasing power to a few global vendors and getting those benefits.

items.statement: UK payer mix shifting from 95% NHS toward private (self-pay/PMI); private contribution at historical high but still low vs peers; private insurers encouraged by cost-control focus
items.quote: The business's private contribution, while still low, very low compared to peers, compared to the business itself is at an historical all-time high. It's never had this proportion of private revenue sources.

items.statement: UK software deployment delayed 4-6 months due to regulatory classification as software as medical device; one-time effort; few products at this scale have UK medical device certification
items.quote: Having said that, I think it adds about, I'm going to be approximate here, about 4 to 6 months in terms of timeline to what we initially anticipate d.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA <1x; debt to rise as project construction peaks over next 2-3 years; expected to decline to even lower levels by FY30
items.quote: See, the debt -equity ratio and debt -EBITDA ratio are not very high even now. Net debt -EBITDA is still less than 1. This number, still debt numbers still go up as the project construction picks up the pace, which will be for the next 2 -3 years, but by FY30, you would expect these numbers to come down to even lower levels than that what it is currently.

items.statement: No plans for new European/US/Canada markets in next 2-3 years; focused on current UK, Cayman, India expansion
items.quote: We have a we have a handful with what we've started, yes.

items.statement: India clinic business loss ~INR 15 crores in Q1 FY27; margins reported with and without clinics in IR deck
items.quote: That number is approximately INR 15 crores for this first quarter of FY27 for the clinic business alone.
