items.statement: UK heat wave caused infrastructure failures (chillers/AC) leading to lost operating days; will strengthen HVAC systems using India/Cayman experience; resilience improvements will take time
items.quote: Critical infrastructure, not only hospitals, but railway operators and other infrastructure, was significantly impacted. For us, what that meant is the chillers and air conditioning units in the hospitals conking off quite often, and we lost several days of operating capacity.

items.statement: Insurance strategy reassessed every few quarters on timeline and cumulative investment; clinics ahead of plan, insurance slightly behind; early ecosystem results encouraging
items.quote: Things are on track, especially ahead of plan with the clinics, slightly behind with the insurance, but every few quarters or so, we'll continue to reassess if the ecosystem benefits do materialize.

items.statement: Mid-teens revenue growth outlook maintained for existing and new centers
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering a mid-teens growth from the existing centers and including the new ones that we are building through the greenfield and brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Target 21-22% EBITDA margin in next 2 years, 24-25% in 4-5 years
items.quote: So I said in the next 2 years, we are looking at a 21%, 22% EBITDA margin. For the next 4 to 5 years, we are confident of clocking the 25% margin number.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 19.4% in Q1 FY27 from 18.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA increased by 20% year-on-year to INR1,339 million, with EBITDA margins improving to 19.4% from 18.2% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: North Bangalore hospital expected to reach peak EBITDA loss in Q1 FY27, losses to reduce in coming quarters
items.quote: I feel we have reached the peak EBITDA loss in this quarter. So from here on, we feel as we ramp up clinician practices, insurance empanelment happens and revenue goes up meaningfully, I think the losses will come down quite reasonably in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Revenue grew 13% YoY to INR6,951 million, driven by 11% volume growth and 2% ARPP growth
items.quote: During the quarter, HCG delivered revenue of INR6,951 million, representing approximately 13% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: 16 of 25 centers (excl. North Bangalore) delivered highest ever quarterly revenues
items.quote: More importantly, growth was broad-based with 16 out of our 25 centers, excluding North Bangalore, delivering their highest ever quarterly revenues, reflecting sustained patient demand and improving execution across our hospitals.

items.statement: Non-institutional revenue grew 17% YoY, payor mix improved from 67% to 69% non-institutional
items.quote: During the quarter, non-institutional business revenue grew by 17% year-on-year. As a result, our payor mix improved with non-institutional contribution increasing from 67% in Q1 FY'26 to 69% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Discontinued low-margin chemo drugs caused 1.5% top-line impact but was margin-accretive
items.quote: The impact in Q1 has been about 1.5% on our top line. And that is why I think if we were to plow that back, the top line would have been around 15%. But having said that, we have discontinued those drugs because while they were high value, they were low margin.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex INR750 million (INR350 million growth, INR400 million maintenance); full-year maintenance capex ~INR1,000 million
items.quote: We have incurred a capex of approximately INR750 million. And as far as the split is concerned, we have incurred almost INR35 crore on account of growth capex and almost INR40 crore in terms of the maintenance capex.

items.statement: Full-year maintenance capex likely ~INR100 crore
items.quote: So, the maintenance capex is likely to be approximately INR100 crore.

items.statement: Added 121 operational beds in Q1 FY27 across clusters; plan 65 more in FY27, 520 in FY28-29, 230 in FY30
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 121 operational beds across the network, including 61 beds in the South cluster, 27 beds in West and 26 beds in East cluster and 7 beds in our Kenya unit.

items.statement: Two greenfield projects: Whitefield (South) and Maharashtra (West), first operational by end FY28, second in FY29
items.quote: So these 180 beds will obviously come from 2 greenfield projects. One of them is in our South cluster in Whitefield. The other one is in Maharashtra in our West cluster. So I think the likelihood of the first one to operationalize is somewhere at the end of FY28 and the other one in the subsequent year.

items.statement: Existing facilities can handle 75-80% utilization; North Bangalore optimal utilization 60-65% by year 3-4
items.quote: So, the existing facilities can manage utilization level up to 75%, 80%. So, there is ample headroom for both in our clusters across the board.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds used to repay INR170 crore debt; interest cost expected to moderate vs last year
items.quote: As you see that the interest cost has come down during this quarter because of the proceeds that we have raised from the right issue that has been used for the purpose of repayment of some of the debt almost amounting to INR170 crore.

items.statement: New CFO Sanjeev Kumar joined with 3+ decades experience; onboarded ~20 oncologists in last 4-5 months
items.quote: I would like to warmly welcome our new Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, who has recently joined HCG. Sanjeev brings more than 3 decades of experience across finance, strategy and business transformation.

items.statement: Onboarded about 20 oncologists in last 4-5 months to improve clinical capabilities
items.quote: In the last quarters, in the last 4, 5 months, we have onboarded about 20 oncologists.

items.statement: M&A remains a focus for value-accretive opportunities in new or existing markets
items.quote: Whenever we get a value-accretive opportunity which aligns with our values and helps to expand our presence in the new market or existing market, we will definitely go for it.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds: INR170 crore debt repayment, INR150 crore for Vizag stake increase to 85%, INR50 crore and INR95 crore general corporate purposes
items.value: INR170 crore / INR150 crore / INR50 crore / INR95 crore
items.quote: We have used INR170 crore for the purpose of debt repayment which is INR170 crore. We also increased our shareholding in our Vizag hospital from 51% to 85% and have used INR150 crore and almost INR50 crore and INR95 crore were used for the purpose of general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Marketing spend increased >20% YoY to 2.9% of sales; target long-term 2.5-2.6%
items.quote: It is gone up by 20% vis-a-vis last year quarter, it is today at 2.9% of our sales. And we want to kind of keep it around that mark given the nature of our specialty and the competitive intensity in several markets that we operate in.

items.statement: Hospitals in >INR10 crore/month revenue bucket increased from 4 to 7; INR5-10 crore bucket decreased from 14 to 11
items.quote: The bucket with more than INR10 crore per month revenue we have got from last year 4 hospitals, we moved to 7 hospitals. So we have added 3 new hospitals to that. And the bucket with INR5 crore to INR10 crore per month revenue, that number has gone down from 14 to 11.

items.statement: North Bangalore hospital: 550+ new patient registrations, 300+ admissions in first quarter
items.quote: In the very first quarter, the hospital recorded over 550 new patient registrations, more than 300 admissions.

items.statement: ESOP policy in final approval stages; P&L impact to be assessed and reported in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The ESOP policy is undergoing final stages of approval, and that charge will be evaluated basis the grand and its impact on company's P&L will be assessed and reported in quarter 2.

items.statement: Depreciation ~9% of asset base in Q1 FY27, includes North Bangalore facility
items.quote: So today it will be in the region of 9% of our asset prices.

items.statement: Target to become net zero debt company in next 36 months
items.quote: in the next 36 months we again wish to become a net zero debt company, and we are working towards that.

items.statement: Acquisition loan reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹174 crore
items.quote: we had taken a ₹ 210 crore loan for the acquisition financing of DEXIT. That quantum is now down to ₹ 174 crores, after our repayments are going as per schedule.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 218 bps to 16.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This translates into roughly a 218 basis point increase in our EBITDA margin, to about 16.6%.

items.statement: DEX won 9 new contracts worth ₹34 crore TCV, ₹22 crore to execute in current year
items.quote: we have won about nine new contracts with a total contract value of about ₹ 34 crore during the course of the first quarter, of which abou t ₹ 22 crores will get executed during the current year

items.statement: EasyApply saw extremely positive traction in first 15 days of new admission cycle
items.quote: in the first 15 days I think we have seen an extremely positive traction, and we are extremely bullish and positive about the scale-up of this line over the next 12 months.

items.statement: VIRSA targeting 45-50% revenue growth for full year
items.quote: I think we should be able to achieve 45 to 50% overall revenue growth for this business during the whole of the year.

items.statement: 60-70% of FY26-27 technology projects for DEX completed
items.quote: almost 60 to 70% of the projects that as a team for FY26-27 we had undertaken are almost complete.

items.statement: DEX expanding network nodes across India and rewriting exam engine
items.quote: expanding the nodes across the country, are the very high -level strategic meaty projects that we are undertaking in the current financial year.

items.statement: MarTech tech revenue share expected to rise from 10% to 13-15% in FY27
items.quote: The contribution of the technology business, which was roughly around 10% last year in the overall revenue — we are expecting that to clip up to roughly around 13 to 15% in the current year

items.statement: VIRSA pilots scaled with Salesforce, Dell; Infosys expanding to APAC and US
items.quote: VIRSA, our AI-driven agentic tool for an account -based marketing approach, has found — we have already successfully completed pilots and are now scaling it up for corporates like Salesforce, Dell and Infosys.

items.statement: Nilekani task force driving exam rationalization and digital shift
items.quote: the direction of assessments is going to be digital, number one. Number two, from an examination's point of view, there is going to be a significant amount of rationalization of exams which is likely to happen.

items.statement: NTA may develop in-house assessment capabilities posing competitive risk
items.quote: how do we counter the risk that the NTA might develop in-house software and hardware to mitigate risks of malpractice?

items.statement: 74% of coding now AI-enabled driving cost rationalization
items.quote: almost 74% of our coding now is AI -enabled, AI-driven. And as you move in and see, we have done a lot of cost rationalizations.

items.statement: DEX revenue recognition at exam conduct or post-result declaration milestones
items.quote: revenue recognition in DEXIT happens — A, as I said, it is on a per seat, per candidate basis. B, it is on an exam -to-exam basis, contract-to-contract basis. C, it is divided typically into two or three milestones.

items.statement: Ongoing strategic discussions with large global and Indian players
items.quote: there are certain ongoing strategic discussions right now with large gl obal and Indian players, and we would share whenever there is an appropriate development and it is worthy of sharing.

items.statement: Capital reduction scheme for RPS approved by NCLT, redemption by August end
items.quote: the NCLT approval came in the second week of July. The necessary ROC approvals have also been received, and we are hopeful that we should be able to wind up that transaction and complete the redemption of those preference shares within the month of August.

items.statement: PhysicsWallah targets lower end; CL focuses middle to upper segment
items.quote: PhysicsWallah by nature, from a business perspective, has been targeting the lower end of the market. And while we are in the middle to top — while we are offering programmes at the lower end also, the focus by and large has been on the middle and the upper end of the segment.

items.statement: MarTech adding blue-chip customers in Singapore and Indonesia
items.quote: We continue to add and sign up reasonably newer blue -chip customers in Singapore and Indonesia.

items.statement: Finance cost declined from ₹12.8 crore to ₹10.6 crore
items.quote: The finance cost has also declined, with the interest cost declining from ₹ 12.8 crores to about ₹ 10.6 crores.

items.statement: BBA/IPM segment growing with more institutes offering 5-year MBA programs
items.quote: BBA and IPM — the segment is doing fairly well. It has been a growth segment for us, and we expect this to grow further, given that a larger number of institutes have started offering five-year MBA kind of programmes

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 40-45% for FY27 on consolidated and standalone basis
items.quote: Somewhere in between 40% to 45% is the continued growth that we will continue to demonstrate, in this financial year onwards.

items.statement: No EBITDA margin guidance given but momentum expected to continue
items.quote: Sir, we are not giving EBITDA guidance anytime, sir. But the momentum will continue to be same.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR1,704 crores as of August 8 including INR480 crores from Ideal Explosives
items.quote: As of August 8, our standalone order book stood at INR1,224 crores, while our consolidated order book stood at INR1,704 crores, which includes an order book of INR480 crores at Ideal Explosives Limited.

items.statement: Expect single order of INR2,500-3,000 crores by end FY27 bringing consolidated order book to INR3,500-4,000 crores
items.quote: by end of this financial year, we are expecting a single order more than INR2,500 crores, INR3,000 crores, which will cumulatively bring, could bring our order book to INR3,500 crores to INR4,000-odd crores is on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Acquired 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives for INR1,550 crores all-cash transaction
items.quote: We have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives Limited for approximately INR1,550 crores through an all-cash transaction.

items.statement: Planning to acquire 2-3 more companies, will announce after signing MOUs
items.quote: Yes, the 2-3 companies we are planning to acquire. I think maybe this is not right time to tell you -- like once we sign MOU with these companies, then we are going to announce in the this thing.

items.statement: Unit III facility first phase production started, full commissioning expected before March 2027
items.quote: First phase, in fact, we have already started the production. Maybe the final production as a complete production activity, I think before March '27, we are going to start.

items.statement: Planning production plants at Ideal and Premier for integration, will announce plans in 2-3 months
items.quote: I think next 2-3 months' time, we'll be coming out with our plan, actually. So, the now the plan is changed, you know. Before, our plan was different. Now, the after the completion of this Premier acquisition, we are going to come out with the -- our future plans.

items.statement: Received Make-II prototype sanction order from Indian Navy for SAVIOR Anti-Submarine Warfare system
items.quote: We have received a Make-II prototype sanction order from Indian Navy for the development of SAVIOR Anti-Submarine Warfare system, our semi-submersible autonomous vessel designed for intelligence operations and reconnaissance.

items.statement: Selected as prime development agency for IPREC program under Make-II category by Indian Air Force
items.quote: We are also encouraged by the Indian Air Force as a prime development agency for IPREC program under the Make-II category of DPP 2020.

items.statement: Successfully handed over indigenously designed Safety and Detonation Device to Indian Navy with 100% indigenous content
items.quote: Another significant milestone was the successful handover of our indigenously designed and developed Safety and Detonation Device to the Indian Navy, marking an important step in translating our in-house technology into operational defence capability.

items.statement: QRSAM order expected from BEL/BDL worth INR11,000-12,000 crores for 1,000 missiles, Apollo component value >INR1 crore per missile
items.quote: BDL order value is something around I'm expecting INR11,000 to INR12,000 crores kind of thing. And the first phase actually, they are releasing for only 1,000 numbers QRSAM, this thing. So, each missile INR1 crores plus component will be there.

items.statement: MIGM order expected by Dec/Jan from INR3,500 crores budget, Apollo expects 70% share with 20% advance payment
items.quote: Like order, we are expecting by December or January, we are expecting the purchase order. And the I think as you know, the this total budget is INR3,500 crores kind of thing. And it is good that, you know, they are also accepting, you know, 20% advance payment also is there in this.

items.statement: Pinaka order for 2,000 rockets expected, Apollo component value INR85 lakhs per rocket
items.quote: Pinaka 2,000 number, Army is negotiating, already negotiation has completed. I think anytime these three companies are going to take the orders. And our component size is something like INR85 lakhs for each Pinaka we are supplying.

items.statement: Expect meaningful export breakthrough orders in FY27, sizable export orders from FY28
items.quote: This financial year, we are likely to get some meaningfully good breakthrough orders is what I can broadly say, but I'll not be able to give a firm commitment and guidance, but for next financial year for sure, there will be a sizable orders, which will be pulled in terms of the export opportunities.

items.statement: In-house explosive production from Premier to improve margins vs outsourcing for MIGM and rocket programs from FY28
items.quote: definitely in terms compared to the outsourcing as how MD sir has already told there will be improvement because it is an in-house, production for us, actually.

items.statement: R&D spend at 9.5% of revenue in FY26 (INR72.53 crores on INR764 crores revenue)
items.quote: the last year revenue stood at INR764 crores and the investment in R&D at INR72.53 crores, which translates to close to 9.5% on R&D.

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduction on track, expects to close all pledges in 1 year (by Q1 FY28)
items.quote: I think next 1 year I think we'll reduce. I think, it is going to take another 1 year to close all the pledge part.

items.statement: INR3,300 crores raised: INR2,500 crores for Premier acquisition, INR500 crores for working capital/debt, rest for general corporate purposes
items.quote: Already we have given a breakup of it, actually. Then out of which, the proceeds INR2,500 crores is going for the acquisition, around INR500 crores, is actually going for the, working capital debt, and some for the general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Moored mines combat trials completed, handover to Indian Navy expected this month, DCP signing in 2 weeks
items.quote: moored mine, combat trials already we have completed. Anytime this month, we are going to hand over to Indian Navy. In fact, we are expecting anytime call from Indian Navy. We are going to have one celebration. That is one part. Moored mine also, I think, I'm sure next 2 weeks time, we are going to announce. I think we are going to sign DCP.

items.statement: Limpet mines completed, orders expected from Q4 FY27; moored mine orders from FY28
items.quote: Limpet mine, we have already completed, limpet mine we have completed, and limpet mine, we maybe start getting orders, maybe 4th quarter onwards, maybe we are expecting orders. At moored mine next financial year only we are expecting.

items.statement: Aerial bombs 1-25kg with 9 variants tested and accepted, drone tie-ups planned
items.quote: And aerial bombs we have already established, 1 kg to 25 kg, some 9 variants already testing we have completed, and we received acceptance also recently. The other things, drones and all, we are going to have tie-up with some of the companies.

items.statement: HAL orders currently INR100-150 crores, expecting another INR150 crores order
items.quote: In case of HAL, HAL we are doing not big orders, I think some INR100 crores, INR150 crores order only we are doing right now. We are expecting another INR150 crores order we are expecting from HAL.

items.statement: Open offer timeline for Premier acquisition uncertain, depends on regulator
items.quote: No, it's in the regulator's hand it's very tough to comment. As and when it comes, we'll have to tell, actually. I cannot give you a guidance on that particular thing.

items.statement: Revised FY28 revenue target to more than Rs. 1,600 crores
items.quote: our company has revised our FY28 revenue target to more than Rs. 1,600 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 30% to 40% annual revenue growth over the next few years
items.quote: Based on current market conditions, customer inquiries and commitments, we are targeting 30% to 40% annual revenue growth over the next few years.

items.statement: Increased FY27 capex plan from Rs. 125 crores to Rs. 250 crores for two new production buildings at Pakhajan facility
items.quote: Accordingly, we have decided to enhance our planned capital expenditure for FY27 from Rs. 125 crores to Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Capex phased: Rs. 100 crores in Phase 1 (operational Q1 FY28) and Rs. 150 crores in Phase 2 (operational Q4 FY28)
items.quote: In the 1st Phase about Rs. 100 crores and 2nd Phase will be Rs. 150 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 17% to 24% in Q1 FY27 driven by volume growth, product mix, and capacity utilization
items.quote: This increased utilization of our facilities as well as improved product mix helped increase our EBITDA margin from 17% to 24%.

items.statement: Management confident to sustain current EBITDA margin going forward due to improved product mix, capacity utilization, and customer commitments
items.quote: The Management is confident to sustain the EBITDA margin of its current quarter going forward on account of improved product mix and better capacity utilization which is backed by commitment from key customers.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to over 65% in Q1 FY27, targeting 75% utilization for FY27
items.quote: Capacity utilization at our facilities improved to over 65%, supported by the successful ramp-up of capacities commissioned at our Pakhajan plant.

items.statement: Long-term agreement project on track with commercialization expected in Q1 FY28
items.quote: We also continue to make good progress on our long-term agreement, and the project remains on track with commercialization expected in Q1 FY28, in line with the planned execution schedule.

items.statement: Exports contribute approximately 69% of total revenue; management expects export mix to remain in 70%-75% range
items.quote: Export continues to remain a key pillar of our business, contributing approximately 69% of total revenue.

items.statement: Top customer contributes about 7% of revenue; long-term contractual customers now over 50% vs 30-40% previously
items.quote: Well, top most customer will have a contribution of about 7% of the revenue.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved from 190 days to 143 days due to better inventory planning and receivables management
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved from 190 days to 143 days, supported by better inventory planning, improved receivables management, and tighter control over cash deployment.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.86x from 3.75x; CRISIL and ICRA upgraded bank loan ratings from BBB+ to A-
items.quote: Our net debt to EBITDA ratio improved to 1.86 x as of June 30, 2026, compared with 3.75 x at the end of Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Company expects to raise approximately Rs. 100 crores through borrowings in FY27 to fund capex expansion
items.quote: To fund this expansion, the company expects to raise approximately Rs. 100 crores through borrowings during FY27.

items.statement: Pricing is formula-driven based on raw material costs with quarterly or half-yearly revisions; EBITDA percentage remains constant
items.quote: Generally our prices are based on raw material costing with our long -term suppliers or the marquee customers. It's not a market -driven price, but it's a formula -driven

items.statement: Asset turnover target of 2.5x on capex; new molecules initially expected to contribute Rs. 50-100 crores revenue each
items.quote: I think, yes, we will like to keep it 2.5x of the CAPEX. So, we should get the revenue.

items.statement: Facing supply chain challenges: raw material procurement issues and container booking delays of 3-4 weeks
items.quote: We are facing a genuine supply issue on our raw material side. Also, we are facing an issue on our export side where we don't get the booking of our containers.

items.statement: R&D team has more than 50 scientists; pilot facility started at Pakhajan to support R&D scale-up
items.quote: The company continues to invest in R&D, which today has more than 50 scientists.

items.statement: Not concerned about Chinese capacity additions; addressable market of $12-15 billion vs $200-300 million target
items.quote: That's of 12 billion to 15 billion addressable market, we are aspire to become $200-$300 million. I don't see that as a challenge.

items.statement: Volume grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY27; management expects sequential quarter-on-quarter volume growth to continue
items.quote: The company achieved its highest quarterly revenue of Rs. 308 crores driven by a 42% increase in volume on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: US tariff issues resolved; USA subsidiary picking up well on sales side
items.quote: In USA, we started at the wrong time. We had a tariff issue, tariff is gone. So, USA subsidiary is also picking up quite well on the sales side.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 14%-15% for FY27, primarily volume-driven
items.quote: We believe this is a good start to our year and that we can sustain revenue growth outlook of 14%-15% for the year, which we expect to be primarily driven by volume growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement of 100-150 bps in FY27, targeting 27%-28% over this year and next
items.quote: Supported by ongoing operational efficiencies and cost optimization initiatives, we expect an improvement of 100-150 basis points on EBITDA during the current financial year and over this year and the next year, we remain focused on achieving an EBITDA margin of 27%-28%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~17% YoY to INR 450 cr, driven by 10% patient volume and 11% test volume growth
items.quote: Revenue grew by about 17% year -on-year to INR 450 crores, ahead of our stated guidance, while EBITDA margin expanded by 210 basis points to 25.2%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 210 bps YoY to 25.2%, PAT margin up 90 bps to 12.6%
items.quote: Q1 EBITDA stood at INR 113 crores, growing 27% year-on-year. EBITDA margin expanded by 210 basis points to 25.2%. Q1 PA T stood at INR 57 crores, growing at 26% year -on-year. PAT margin expanded by 90 basis points to 12.6%.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to be similar to FY26's INR 65 cr for the group including acquisitions
items.quote: I think last year we did INR 65 crores of CAPEX and I think our CAPEX requirement for this year will also be in the similar lines. I am saying for the Group, including all the acquired entities, everything put together.

items.statement: Specialty Diagnostics grew 17% in Q1, now 40% of revenue; target to increase contribution to 45%
items.quote: We aim to increase contribution of this portfolio to 45% from the current 40%.

items.statement: TruHealth grew 22% in Q1, now 18% of revenue; radiology wellness packages grew >40%, premium packages >50%
items.quote: TruHealth revenues grew 22%, supported by integrated preventive healthcare offerings and targeted digital customer acquisition initiatives. Radiology integrated wellness packages grew by more than 40%, while premium TruHealth packages grew by more than 50%.

items.statement: No price increase in last 18 months (since Jan 2025); CGHS price hike benefit minimal (<1% of revenue); may pass on inflation at appropriate time
items.quote: No, there is absolutely no price increase during this quarter. In fact, last time we increased the prices was January 2025. There's no price increase after that. We just talked about the CGHS price increase, which is a very insignificant part of our busine ss. That really didn't help us too much.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics integration in final leg; genomics portfolio doubled, North India revenue now 18% (from single-digit); acquired at <2x revenue, effective multiple ~10x EBITDA in FY27
items.quote: Based on the EBITDA that Core Diagnostics is expected to generate in FY 2027, which is just the second year as part of Metropolis, our effective acquisition multiple would be approximately 10x EBITDA. This demonstrates the value that disciplined acquisitions and successful integration can create for our shareholders.

items.statement: Agra and Dehradun acquisitions performing ahead of revenue growth and EBITDA targets
items.quote: Our recent acquisitions in Agra and Dehradun are also performing very well, with both business tracking ahead of the revenue growth and EBITDA.

items.statement: Leadership team strengthened over past 12-18 months; annual employee increments advanced from July to April
items.quote: Lastly, over the past 12 to 18 months, we have strengthened our leadership team, completed the integration of acquisitions, expanded our network, and significantly enhanced our operational capabilities.

items.statement: Medium-term CAGR guidance 14%-15%, with 9%-10% from patient volume growth and 5%-6% from mix improvement
items.quote: We continue to maintain that our medium-term CAGR guidance is about 14%-15%. Out of this 14%-15%, about 9%-10% will come from patient volume growth, and the remaining will come from the product mix.

items.statement: Weather unpredictability due to climate change makes quarterly forecasting difficult; business heavily influenced by weather conditions
items.quote: The reality is climate change is changing everything for everybody. Weathers are unpredictable and our business is heavily influenced by weather. Conditions which then impact and create diseases and then require testing. It's quite difficult to predict.

items.statement: Competitive intensity normal; irrational pricing not seen; scaling profitably remains key challenge; many entrants stagnate at INR 50-75 cr
items.quote: So, on the competitive dynamic space, we have seen nothing irrational happening. The normal competitive intensity in the diagnostics industry, which we have seen for 10 -15 years, continues to be there where obviously everybody is jostling for their piece of the pie.

items.statement: GST benefits passed to consumers instead of price hike; lab transformation program standardizing platforms, consolidating vendors, increasing automation
items.quote: This is a year we have not taken a price increase. That's largely because of the GST benefits that has come into the industry, and we thought it's passing on to the consumer is the right thing to do.

items.statement: Rationalized 300 low-productivity centers after ~2 years; rationalization done without revenue impact; occurs once in 12-18 months
items.quote: This time, we knocked it off after almost two years, we knocked off these 300 centers. The number that we are talking about, 500 center expansion, is a net number that we are talking about.

items.statement: International business delivered healthy revenue and EBITDA growth; market leader in 2 of 5 countries, top 3 in all; specialized testing offshored to India reference labs
items.quote: Our international business continued to perform well, delivering healthy growth in both revenue and EBITDA. We are the market leaders in two of the five countries in which we operate and rank amongst the top three players in all the markets.

items.statement: Strengthening data governance and ensuring DPDP-compliant handling of patient data with focus on privacy, security, responsible use
items.quote: Across these initiatives, we are strengthening data governance and ensuring DPDP-compliant handling of patient data with a clear focus on privacy, security, and responsible use of information.

items.statement: Company-wide automation and digital transformation across labs, customer engagement, vendor consolidation, commercial ops, finance, procurement, support functions
items.quote: We are executing a company-wide automation and digital transformation program spanning labs, customer engagement, vendor consolidation, commercial operations, finance, procurement and support functions.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 international patient mix expected closer to or better than 30%
items.quote: And in Q2, we are again hopeful to see it closer to, if not better than 30%, is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Raipur hospital break-even in 15-18 months with INR 20 crores operating loss
items.quote: we are going to be looking at around 15 to 18 months of break -even, around INR 20 crores of overall operating loss

items.statement: Gurgaon Tower IV operational in 18-22 months
items.quote: the timeline we are looking here is between around 18 to 22 months to be able to fully operationalize this

items.statement: Gurgaon Tower IV break-even in 8-10 months
items.quote: I would say it would do in 8 to 10 months' time. If not earlier.

items.statement: Gurgaon Tower IV to reach 50% occupancy in first six months
items.quote: See, in my opinion, it should reach 50% in first six months.

items.statement: Gurgaon standalone revenue potential INR 2,000 crores at 900-950 beds, 85% census, 70% occupancy, 4-5% ARPOB growth
items.quote: we can essentially get to a INR 2,000 crores top line. Is that a valid assumption only from the Gurgaon facility? Devlina Chakravarty: Yes, it is possible

items.statement: Gurgaon standalone EBITDA margin upwards of 23% at scale
items.quote: Upwards of 23%, I would say.

The geography mix with approximately 78% of the revenue has been generated from the export during the quarter.

items.statement: Targeting geographic diversification: North America to reduce to 55-60%, Middle East and Europe growing to 10-20%
items.quote: And in terms of the geography -wise, yes, North America is still around 55 % to 60%. So, that will be around, we are working on the -- as per our strategies, we are working on the balancing that our geographical risk, that so for that our Middle East and our Europe regions, that is growing in the good way.

items.statement: Approved with major customers including Oshkosh, BLY, ABB, Siemens; large order conversions from motion control customers expected in 6-15 months
items.quote: So, many of our loose compound FA has been completed, and now moving towards the more approval stage. So, probably it can you can say another 6 to 12 months or 15 months, it will be done.

items.statement: ROCE annualized improved to 17.8% from 13.7%; ROE annualized 16.8% from 11.7%
items.quote: Our return on capital employed annualized improved to 17.8% compared to 13.7% at the year-end of FY26.

items.statement: Asset turnover 2.25-2.5x; targeting ROCE >20% at peak capacity utilization
items.quote: See, if you see our asset turnover ratios and similar like that, so it is around 2.25 around 2 to 2.5 in between. And in terms of ROCE it should be more than 20 and similar like that.

items.statement: Raw material mix: stainless steel, Inconel (<15%), carbon steel, low alloy steel, aluminum, titanium capability
items.quote: Exact quarter-on-quarter little bit it gets changed, but you can say high level we operate into stainless steel to Inconel, to carbon steel, low alloy steel, and aluminum. So, probably presently our Inconel level probably it will be I don't have exact numbers, but it may be a less than 15% in the stainless steel categories.

items.statement: 1.2 MW solar plant from IPO capex operational and contributing to P&L
items.quote: But one more thing from the IPO capex, our solar of roughly around 1.2 megawatt has been already start working and that has been already started producing the units for us. So, that is already start coming into our P&Ls.

items.statement: Nadcap certification process in progress for defense/aerospace qualifications
items.quote: In addition, the Nadcap certification process is also in progress, and the development orders from the defense and aerospace segment are also progressing well.

items.statement: Management cautious on accepting larger orders despite strong order book to ensure execution capability
items.quote: But we have to be a more careful before accepting the order, because at the end of a day, we have to execute the orders. So, we are having a very strong order book as of now, and we are skeptical to taking the more bigger orders also.

items.statement: Investing in talent for new verticals (aerospace, defense, energy) with costs already in P&L
items.quote: So, it is like we have we should have a equal talent on board to project our growth which is more than like 1 or 2 years beyond that also, because aerospace, defense and new some of energy verticals we are working, there we have already invested and start invested on the talent side.

items.statement: Management reiterated 11% as center of gravity for jewellery EBIT margin, not changing guidance
items.quote: In the Investor Day and prior, we have said that more of 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin, we would be around that plus/minus something can happen.

items.statement: Normalized Tanishq Mia Zoya EBIT margin for Q1 FY27 is 10.9% after adjusting for customs duty and MTM gains
items.quote: The normalized margin considering both custom duty gain and MTM gain, the normalized EBIT margin for our Tanishq Mia Zoya business would be 10.9%, the number for this quarter.

items.statement: Customs duty gain of ₹407 crores realized in Q1, with ₹386 crores in Tanishq Mia Zoya and ₹21 crores in CaratLane
items.quote: We had during this quarter, gains on account of customs duty rate increase from 6% to 15%. items.statement: MTM inventory gain of 75-80 bps in jewellery division EBIT expected to reverse over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So on account of those price divergence, we have accounting MTM in the inventory, which is -- which caused 75 to 80 basis point jewellery division EBIT upward. So jewellery division has the benefit of that. And we believe that these are likely to reverse in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment softened for ~3 weeks in May due to PM announcement, customs duty change, and Adhik Maas, but recovered in June
items.quote: As a consequence, we did see a softness in consumer sentiment for about 3 weeks' time till the end of May. But by the beginning of June, things started picking up. Weddings also restarted post the end of Adhik Maas. So we believe that it was a deferment and we saw things pick up in June.

items.statement: Studded jewellery growth momentum from Q4 FY26 continued in Q1 FY27 despite brief lull in May
items.quote: We have - we began seeing a resurgence of studded in Quarter 4 of last year, and we are seeing that continue to play out in Quarter 1. And in a sense, it's the momentum that we had in Quarter 4 continued during Akshaya Tritiya.

items.quote: Color stone jewellery, which was earlier clubbed under the studded category, we have reclassified that into the gold jewellery, so that studded reflects to more diamond jewellery and not any other Colorstone or Polki jewellery, etcetera.

items.statement: Normalized Watch EBIT margin 17.8% in Q1 FY27 vs 18.6% in Q1 FY26 due to lower standard costing revaluation benefit
items.quote: Last year, we had called out, if you refer to that earning s that about ₹50 crores was the benefit to Watch division. This quarter, that benefit was far less. items.statement: International business (ex-Damas) making 5-6% EBIT margin; Damas loss-making due to war impact on footfall and ticket sizes
items.quote: I would think that our rest of the portfolio of international business, except Damas is making profit mid-single-digit EBIT margin, 5% - 6%, which they will continue to make. And overall, Damas contribution in international business will not be very high.

items.statement: Cash-for-gold program rolled out in all stores from June as customer solution, not revenue stream; margin neutral due to deductions
items.quote: We have rolled out what we had called as cash for gold in all our stores from the month of June. And we are not seeing significant traction here, but that option is available for customers to bring their own gold and exchange that f or cash. Not exchange, but convert that into cash

items.statement: Gross margin expansion initiatives include lower caratage, GC Max program, and sourcing strategies; details not disclosed
items.quote: Suffice to say whatever has been spoken about lower Caratage, there is a GC Max program, there are sourcing strategies, etcetera. It's a mix of various things. We certainly don't want to give more detail on this.

items.statement: Buyer growth 5% in Q1; stable gold prices support positive sentiment and buyer growth
items.quote: On the buyer growth, like we -- like I said earlier to the first question, we had a good period in April and a good period in June. And there was a bit of sentiment that was dampened in the month of May. So this is an average for the entire quarter.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit aggressive growth in jewellery; FY30 goals unchanged
items.quote: If you're looking for what is that we are targeting, we are targeting, as always, a double-digit aggressive growth, and that's something which we shared even in the Investor Day. Those targets and our ambitions don't go away.

items.statement: TEAL normalized margin gravitating towards 12-16% long-term; CaratLane targeting double-digit EBIT margin (~10%)
items.quote: Overall, long term, growth is on a very strong wicket, but the normalized margin would be gradually gravitating towards 12% to 15%, 16%. This year, full year basis, they can be higher. As far as CaratLane is concerned, we have always said they will gradually go towards double-digit EBIT margin, more

items.statement: No easing of competitive intensity in plain gold jewellery despite gold price stabilization; regional variations persist
items.quote: We're not seeing any easing up of competitive intensity. We are seeing it more of the same. Obviously, the intensity in certain geographies is much higher and has been much higher in the last 2 to 3 years, for example, in Gujarat, right?

items.statement: Gold price volatility creates demand uncertainty; softness seen in plain gold in late July due to bearish sentiment
items.quote: Towards the end of July, perhaps we did see some softness in -- on the plain gold side, okay? And it does happen sometimes when the price is range bound or the price and people also hear news from various sources that bears have taken hold of gold and gold is likely to go down.

items.statement: Exchange share exceeds 50% of business; spiked during May overdrive but normalized since
items.quote: Like we have said in the past, the sale that comes from exchange, both the exchange of old gold bought elsewhere and the gold bought at Tanishq exceeds 50% of our -- of the business. So that's a trend that is sustaining.

items.statement: Customs duty increased from 6% to 15%; gains realized as inventory sells over next couple of quarters
items.quote: We had during this quarter, gains on account of customs duty rate increase from 6% to 15%. While these gains will be realized as the inventory gets sold over the next couple of quarters, but in this quarter, we had overall at a consolidated level realization of ₹407 crores.

items.statement: Prioritizing top-line growth over margins in TEAL and CaratLane; both on significant growth path
items.quote: Both these subsidiaries are still on a significant growth path, okay? And the opportunity to grow is significant and substantial, and we will continue to prioritize top line growth in both of them.

items.statement: Coin demand growth moderating from previous high levels; expected to help mix and margins
items.quote: the kind of growth Y -o-Y coin was showing, it should start moderating fro m here

items.statement: Focus on lightweight jewellery, lower karatages, and exchange programs to keep jewellery accessible across town classes
items.quote: And accessibility comes from keeping it lightweight, looking at a variety of karatages, looking at an exchange program that is strong to get them to recycle. So all these are different levers that we are using to keep consumers -- to keep jewellery accessible to a wide set of consumers across the different town classes that we are present.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit healthy value growth in jewellery to achieve FY30 goals; not carried away by quarterly volatility
items.quote: I think overall, we are committed to -- I'm just reiterating, we are committed to a double-digit healthy growth in value in the jewellery business. So that's the only way we'll get to our committed FY 30 goals that we've said.

items.statement: Product mix shift to studded, gross margin programs, and stable gold prices to drive margin improvement in H2
items.quote: The product mix swinging upwards towards more studded scale is a very important driver, and that's a focus area also for the division. items.statement: Gold price trajectory uncertain; geopolitical normalization could push prices up again
items.quote: Gold prices continue to remain on a very uncertain trajectory. You would have seen softening then all of a sudden in a day, $100, $200 going up and down. So given the circumstances, we will stick with our previous guidance.

items.statement: Golden Harvest customers shifting preference to Rivaah Golden Advantage for rupee cost averaging
items.quote: What's really happening is the dynamic between the 2 where we are seeing most customers prefer Rivaah Golden Advantage because it helps in the rupee cost averaging. And we are -- we're seeing a shift of preference from Golden Harvest to Rivaah Golden Advantage.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14% to 16%

items.quote: 2-wheeler industry volumes grew 14% year-on-year in terms of VAHAN or retail sales, of which 11% was growth in ICE and 67% was in EV.

items.quote: This top line expansion was driven by premiumization across our portfolio, driven by a shift in mix towards EV, scooters and premium variants, contributing a mix benefit of 8%.

items.quote: In May, we had talked about a new CTO who joined us, Sachin Agrawal. He joined us as the new CTO in May.

items.quote: The conflict in West Asia triggered inflationary spikes across oil and gas, freight, foreign exchange and core raw materials, including steel, aluminum and precious metals.

So, the prices for polyester fiber went up as high as to the tune of 30%. So, thereby, uncertainty did prevail in terms of buying from customers.

items.statement: Focus on value-added products, sustainable textiles, specialized yarns, functional fabrics; graphene fiber development with Birla Cellulose progressing
items.quote: Innovation also remains a key differentiator as we steadily expand our portfolio of specialized yarns, functional fabrics and sustainable textile solutions. Our diversified manufacturing base allows us to clear the multiple end-use industries, reducing dependence on a single product category or market.

items.statement: India-UK FTA and India-EU FTA discussions creating opportunities for competitive Indian textile manufacturers in value-added segments
items.quote: Structured developments including recently concluded India-UK free trade agreement, ongoing discussions on India-EU free trade agreement and increasing diversification of global sourcing from concentrated manufacturing hubs are expected to create meaningful opportunities for Indian textile exporters over the medium to long term, particularly for the value-added and forward-integrated products.

items.statement: Export revenue ₹336 Cr, lower than Q4 FY26; diversified customer base across international markets maintained
items.quote: Export revenue stood at ₹336 crores lower than the immediately preceding quarter through the business maintained diversified customer base across multiple international markets.

items.statement: Finance costs increased to ₹31 Cr from ₹30 Cr QoQ primarily due to higher working capital requirements
items.quote: Finance costs for the quarter stood at ₹31 crores compared with ₹30 crores in the preceding quarter, primarily attributable to the increase in working capital requirements.

items.statement: Board approved principal approval for denim garmenting JV; RSWM to be majority shareholder; Phase 1: 5 lakh pieces/month; further phases planned
items.quote: Today is the first day we discussed this in board, and we have got the principal approval from board for this JV. The stake percentage sharing is still under discussion, but RSWM will be a major majority shareholder in this. So, we will be able to work on this. So, the vision for garmenting will be in phases. In the first phase, we may go up to 5 lakh pieces per month, which may further be added i

items.statement: Strong demand across key end markets; power generation demand strong in CPCB IV+ and higher ranges; mining tenders improving; railways strong; construction flat with no new national highway tenders
items.quote: From a demand side, I'm presuming you're asking me a question about power generation, but I will give you answer for power generation perspective. So, from a power generation perspective, demand, we continue to see strong in the market, both CPCB IV+ range and in the higher range, different segments, but still continue to see demand coming in.

items.statement: Demand outpacing supply in high horsepower; adding capacity at specific nodes but demand outpacing capacity additions; not losing orders solely due to supply constraints
items.quote: From a supply perspective, capacity on the higher end, there are a few players in the market, and everybody is facing the same situation as we are. Demand is outpacing supply for everyone. And we have been putting in efforts to increase capacity at those s pecific nodes

items.statement: Commodity costs (steel, pig iron, aluminum, copper) up significantly; freight costs increasing; took one price increase at start of Q2; price realization lags cost by at least a quarter; working on cost control and value engineering
items.quote: Major commodities, steel, pig iron, aluminum, copper significant increases. And commodity-related cost inflation also has been impacting the West Asia crisis, labor shortages at our supplier, all of those ha ve impacted us in the quarter. Now yes, we have taken some price increases and price is quite dependent on market conditions and how market accepts some of the price

items.statement: Gross margins under pressure from unprecedented commodity inflation and freight; unable to confirm return to historic 36-37% levels; endeavour to improve margins through cost management and pricing
items.quote: I think the commodity increases at this point, in time are very unprecedented than ever in the past. And freight, by the way, as well has also been a challenge. Freight costs have been increasing. There are continuous supply chain issues that we see and continue to manage. So some of these issues will continue.

items.statement: Strong order velocity in domestic power generation across manufacturing, data centers, residential, commercial realty; data center inquiries strong for current and next two years; data centers 40% of power gen revenue in Q1 FY27 vs 23% in Q
items.quote: And data centers out of this, in this particular quarter, was 40% of overall power generation revenue.

items.statement: Exports flat YoY, up 16% QoQ; high horsepower exports up 16% YoY, 37% QoQ; low horsepower exports down 20% YoY; Middle East exports weak due to West Asia crisis; Europe and Asia Pacific doing well
items.quote: Exports at INR521 crores are flat.

items.statement: Utilization at 70-75% and consistently going up; capital investment in line with last few years in existing plants
items.quote: Our utilization level is between 70% to 75%. So it has been consistently going up. And the capital investment is in line with what we have been doing in the last few years in our existing plants.

items.statement: Domestic power gen: low HP INR77 cr, medium INR248 cr, heavy duty INR125 cr, high HP remainder; Industrial: construction INR148 cr, rail INR145 cr, compressor INR52 cr, marine INR50 cr, rest mining/defense/others
items.quote: So for power generation domestic, the low horsepower sales in this quarter was INR77 crores. The medium range is INR248 crores. The heavy duty is INR125 crores, and the high horsepower, the range after that is the remaining.

items.statement: Data center customers prioritize lead times and site readiness over price; no delivery postponements seen; customers want prepone deliveries; strong relationships with end customers
items.quote: And price increases as far as data center goes, I think, for data centers, it is really important to work on lead times and ability to supply when they have the site readiness, those are more critical, more important for data centers than the price.

items.statement: High horsepower market has few players all facing supply constraints; market very competitive with 10-12 competitors in non-HHP segment; market share not disclosed
items.quote: This is a highly competitive market with more than 10 or 12 competitors in the market. Extremely difficult to say what the growth could be.

items.statement: Retrofit opportunities exist for emission control and long-life assets; CPCB IV+ range driving demand
items.quote: Distribution business is retrofit and opportunity, absolutely, because some of our assets do have a long life. Sometimes also retrofitting when we want to control emissions. So yes, there are opportunities around both rebuilding our own engines and retrofitting our assets for managing emissions and things like that.

items.statement: Price realization lags cost increases by at least a quarter due to backlogs in power generation business
items.quote: Ankur, there's always a lag when the cost hits us and when the price realization actually starts happening. So price realization will start happening a few months down the line because we do run backlogs in our power generation business.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to annual merit increase effective April 1, variable comp true-up, and actuarial credit reversal from prior quarter; headcount flat
items.quote: First is the annual merit increase that gets effective April 1, 2026. So there is an impact of that. Then we do true-up of our variable comp factor, based on which direction the company is going and where it is expected to land at. So we do a true-up in this quarter, which has been done and there is an impact of that.

items.statement: Related party transaction approvals for current fiscal year only; purely anticipatory for export flexibility; no specific order book from UK subsidiary
items.quote: This is purely in anticipation, Jonas, just as a prudent governance practice and order books don't get built this early in the year, they get built 2 to 3 months in advance only and the geopolitical situation is not as stable to be able to predict a year down.

items.statement: Distribution business has 3,500 trained engineers and 450 touchpoints; 2-hour service guarantee for critical customers, 4-hour for others
items.quote: We have, between us and our dealerships, 3,500 trained engineers and 450 touchpoints in the country. At this point in time, our distribution business promises to all o ur customers, specifically critical customers. Critical customers are the likes of, say, hospitals that a service engineer will reach them within 2 hours of logging a complaint

items.statement: Inflationary pressures and supply chain constraints likely to continue; geopolitical instability affecting exports; commodity inflation unprecedented; freight costs rising
items.quote: As we look ahead, we believe that strong demand in various end markets will sustain. At this time, inflationary pressures and supply chain constraints are like ly to continue and are sha ping our operating environment

items.statement: Domestic power generation growth strong; mining tenders improving; railways strong; construction flat; exports difficult due to geopolitics; distribution business potential for 20% growth this year and next few years
items.quote: DBU business absolutely has the potential to grow at 20% growth over this year and the next few years as well.

items.statement: BESS installed at Phaltan rebuild center as demonstrator; very close to getting orders but nothing to share yet
items.quote: We have already installed the BESS at one of our own plants, our own rebuild center in Phaltan. We have installed this BESS as a demonstrator and we are getting our customers to see and experience that. Very close to getting some orders, but nothing more to share yet on that.

items.statement: No incremental data center component exports to US; global integrated supply chain manufacturing components for various plants is business as usual
items.quote: We are catering to the data center market in India domestically and since we are a global integrated supply chain, we do manufacture components and engines which go into our different plants. Now this was not specific to the data center. This is not specific to U.S. And this is nothing new. We have been doing this for a long period of time.

items.statement: Royalty rates standardized to 4% from previous 1-8% range across services
items.quote: Actually, we had some different royalty percentages for different services, which used to range between 1% to 8%. We have standardized it to 4%. That's all.

items.statement: Management looking to appoint rightful successor for Managing Director
items.quote: Cummins management is involved and they are absolutely looking to appoint a rightful successor for me.

items.statement: India data center market still largely QSK60; seeing momentum for QSK78 and QSK95 but not reached capacity establishment point; continuing to evaluate
items.quote: India market is still largely QSK60. We are seeing momentum and ask of some more QSK78 and some QSK95, but still largely the India volume is QSK60. So we haven't reached the point where we would need to establish capacities yet of 78 and 95 liters and we continue to evaluate that.

items.statement: Non-HHP power gen volume growth has scope to improve but difficult to quantify due to high competition
items.quote: I absolutely agree that this volume growth has scope to grow.

items.statement: Only one price rise taken at beginning of Q2; yet to see market absorption; percentage not disclosed
items.quote: Prathmesh, we have only taken one price rise at the beginning of quarter 2. So we are yet to see how it gets accepted in the market, and that's what I have been mentioning. We have to wait and see how that gets absorbed in the market.

items.statement: Rail orders for power cars and diesel-electric tower cars growing; hotel load converter acceptance good; working on other Indian Railways products
items.quote: Rail has been growing good order board and good execution from our end. So largely, the applications where we have been getting orders are power cars and diesel electric tower cars.

items.statement: High horsepower exports INR296 crores in Q1 FY27; low horsepower exports INR180 crores
items.quote: Yes, that is correct. INR296 crores.

items.statement: Data center inquiry momentum continues very strong; generating inquiries for this year, next year and year after; execution strong but big gensets take time for delivery
items.quote: Sure. Yes, the data center inquiries as they had picked up in the last few quarters, the momentum continues, very strong momentum on the data center side. And our execution has also been strong.

items.statement: Management does not provide earnings guidance or market forecasts
items.quote: We are not forecasting the market. We don't give earnings guidance either.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated profit was INR 1,309 crores, the most profitable quarter ever
items.quote: We've had our most profitable quarter ever by a significant margin. The consolidated profit is INR 1,309 crores, while the stand-alone profit is INR 1,157 crores.

items.statement: 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share announced, highest ever quarterly dividend
items.quote: We also announced our 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, again, our highest ever quarterly dividend.

items.statement: Strait of Hormuz disruption caused trade pattern shifts, longer voyages, and surging ton-mile demand for tankers
items.quote: As a result of that, the trade patterns went completely askew and therefore, ton-mile demand picked up hugely.

items.statement: Order book percentages: crude tankers 27%, VLGCs 35%, product tankers 20-21%, bulk carriers 14%
items.quote: The order book now for crude tankers is at 27%. The order book for VLGCs is currently at 35%, which is a huge number for product tankers continues to be at about 20%, 21%, while bulk carriers are at about 14%.

items.statement: Fleet strategy is to replace, not expand; willing to wait for prices enabling long-term returns
items.quote: Our fleet strategy is to replace, not expand. So for capacity expansion, we will wait for prices which we think will enable us to make a good return in the long term.

items.statement: Invested INR 1,200 crores last year and INR 300 crores in Q1 FY27 on fleet modernization; INR 250-300 crores in July
items.quote: last year, we invested about INR 1,200 crores in changing the fleet mix. So, we have invested INR 1,200 crores. This year, in the first quarter, we invested INR 300 crores in doing those transactions. Last month, already, we have invested between INR 250 crores and INR 300 crores

items.statement: Buyback treated as capital allocation decision; no fixed policy, target price, or multiple; board will evaluate vs other options
items.quote: The way we look at buyback is as another capital allocation. And we will treat it exactly the same way. So this will be discussed. We don't have a policy as such, which is on a target or a target price or a target multiple.

items.quote: second is a time charter, which is coming off now and where we've already got the repricing done, which is at about 25% to 30% higher than the previous charter rate. Repricings have got done. There's one third VLGC, which we have, which comes off charter early 2027, first quarter

items.statement: Crude tanker TCE $90,000/day, product tanker $45,000/day for Q2 coverage (40% through quarter)
items.quote: And you can see the TC-wise, so crude tankers have produced a TC $90,000 a day, product tankers, $45,000. This is a coverage of the operating days for Q2. Of course, we are almost 40% through the quarter.

items.statement: Jack-up rig utilization stable globally; Saudi Aramco suspended rigs returning to work; 3 rigs up for repricing in H2, 1 awarded 3-year contract
items.quote: the utilization of jack-up rigs is a global number, remains where it was 3 to 6 months ago. The headline news is that rigs which were temporarily suspended during these hostilities by Saudi Aramco are slowly coming back on contract and going back to work. Coming to what's happening with our fleet. We have mentioned here that 3 rigs are up for repricing in the second half. We have just received a l

items.statement: Sold 2 MR tankers, replaced with 1 MR; bought 1 Kamsarmax bulker; sold LR2 Jag Lokesh, replaced with younger eco LR2 Jag Lakshya in July
items.quote: So, we've sold 2 MR tankers replaced with 1 MR tanker, and we also bought a Kamsarmax dry bulk carrier. In the month of July, we sold the Jag Lokesh, which is an LR2 tanker and replaced with the Jag Lakshya, which is also an LR2 tanker, but is 6 years younger and is an eco-ship as well.

items.statement: Newer eco-ships (post-2013) offer 20-25% fuel savings vs pre-2013 vessels, translating to $1,000-$2,500/day earnings improvement
items.quote: If you compare the ship built in the 2020s compared to what was built prior to 2013, fuel savings could be up to maybe 20%, 25%. And then depending on the size of the ship, it can translate from $1,000 to maybe even $2,000, $2,500 per day on the earnings.

items.statement: Revenue spillover from Q4 to Q1 was INR 50 crores last quarter; not significant this quarter
items.quote: Last quarter, we had a INR 50 crores spillover from Q4 to Q1. This time, it's not really significant.

items.statement: Order book delivery schedule: ~7% product tanker, ~4% bulk carrier expected next year
items.quote: Yes, probably have 7%. Yes, 4% of bulk, 7% of product tanker.

items.statement: No fixed annual capex budget; replacement driven by ship age and tradability concerns; decisions ship-specific and market-dependent
items.quote: No, we look at it more ship specific. We have a guiding idea because we know the ships, how they're aging and where we would ideally like to do certain things. But as you can imagine, if the markets change, we do change the way we stick to that plan.

items.statement: Government's Samudra Manthan offshore program announced but no on-ground tenders yet; too early for capex plans
items.quote: Firstly, I think it is too soon to decide on a capex plan based on what the government is going to do. While they have showed intention, we have not seen on the ground any more further tenders coming from the government for rigs or offshore vessels.

items.statement: Current freight rates: product tankers significantly lower than Q1; Suezmax similar/slightly lower; Aframax significantly lower; bulk carriers marginally higher
items.quote: for product tankers, they are probably significantly lower than they were in Q1, the current freight rates. For crude tankers, Suezmaxes are probably around the same or sli ghtly lower. Aframaxes are significantly lower than they were in Q1. Bulk carriers are marginally

items.statement: Treasury strategy: no US treasury exposure; dollar balances in bank, rupee balances in debt funds/bank deposits
items.quote: We don't hold any cash in U.S. treasuries. Our money sits in the bank. We have some dollar balances, which just sit in the bank. Our rupee balances are invested in debt funds or bank deposits typically.

items.statement: Panama Canal transit restrictions due to low water levels; Suez Canal unaffected; El Nino impact mainly on Panama Canal and LPG/dry bulk trades
items.quote: In the Panama Canal, while it's not been a large impact, we have seen certain water levels starting to drop off. G. Shivakumar: And the number of transits actually being restricted because of that in the Panama Canal. The Suez Canal has not had this problem, never had this problem

items.statement: Strategic petroleum reserves: US SPR down to ~300M barrels from 750M; China reserves opaque; prolonged conflict may strain inventories and boost demand
items.quote: In the U.S., they do publish the data. So we know that the SPRs, they used to be at 750 million barrels, they have fallen to about 450 million barrels before the Iran war. And now they're down to about 300-odd million.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of over INR2,500 crores and EBITDA margin range of 25% plus/minus 2%
items.quote: Accordingly, we reaffirm our guidance of achieving over INR2,500 crores in revenue for FY27 while maintaining EBITDA margin in the range of 25% plus/minus 2%.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 15-20% revenue CAGR and reaching INR3,500 crores in 3-4 years
items.quote: Over the medium term, we continue to target 15% to 20% revenue CAGR, supported by capacity expansion, increasing contribution from value-added products and backward integration through the TPU project, the new project introductions and continuous expansion of our direct-to-consumer platform and disciplined execution.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 544 bps to record 30.3%, crossing 30% milestone for first time
items.quote: EBITDA increased 56% year-on-year to INR192 crores with EBITDA margin expanding by 544 basis points to a record of 30.30%, crossing the 30% milestone for the first time in company's history and significantly exceeding the upper end of our long-term guidance

items.statement: Gross margins around 60% in Q1 driven by product mix shift to high-end Sun Control and architectural films, not exceptional items
items.quote: Even on the gross margin, there is nothing exceptional. I mean this has come purely from the performance of the company, right? There is no, I would say, any item which is exceptional like refunds for tariff or something. It is purely from the performance of the company.

items.statement: TPU backward integration expected to add 1.5-2% EBITDA margin in FY28
items.quote: Yes. So we have given a guidance of 1.5% to 2% after this line comes into stream, of course, for FY28. So the guidance is already given to that.

items.statement: PPF old line at ~100% utilization, new PPF line at ~60% (impacted by shipping delays from Jebel Ali)
items.quote: Yes. So PPF old line is running almost 100% and the new one is running at the rate of roughly 60%. We lost some volume last quarter because of some delays in the shipping because, I would say, ship got stuck in Jebel Ali because of the war.

items.statement: New Sun Control line peak revenue potential INR500-550 crores
items.quote: That will be roughly INR500 crores, INR550 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR633 crores (+28% YoY), highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: Revenue from operations for the quarter stood at INR633 crores, growing 28% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Architectural films now >25% of revenue (up from 5%), Sun Control 55% and PPF 20% in Q1 vs 48-50% and 25% last year
items.quote: If you really see like from 5% revenue percentage of architectural today stands more than 25%. So such kind of high-end products always lead to good margins. And we have been very consistent in saying that our aim is to go towards the products which gives more value to the consumer.

items.statement: New Sun Control line capacity allocation ~30% to architectural films
items.quote: So I can say whatever the number we say, like 25%, 30%, now this will go to 35% architectural. So all new lines will take 30% of that because this is how the products are manufactured in our company.

items.statement: US e-commerce sales for PPF rising continuously; dealer/distributor order flow strong in Q1
items.quote: In U.S. the sales through e-commerce is continuously rising for PPF. And for our dealer, distributor and order flow is really strong that we have seen in Q1.

items.statement: 5 OEM partnerships for PPF; sole supplier for some; preferred due to Make in India
items.quote: See, we have like five OEMs with us. And some of them, we are the only one. And some of them, like some companies have a policy that they do not have one vendor. So for that, they have another one. But we proudly say that we are the only official high-quality producers in India.

items.statement: Garware Application Studios network expanded to 250+ locations in India; Garware Home Solutions at 9 studios, targeting 50 by end FY27
items.quote: In India, our Garware Application Studios network has now expanded to over 250 locations, while Garware Home Solutions continues to scale steadily with 9 studios currently operational. We remain firmly on track to expand this network to 50 studios by end of FY27.

items.statement: DGTR recommended antidumping duty on TPU-based PPF imports from China, creating level playing field
items.quote: Another important development during the quarter has been DGTR's recommendation for antidumping duty on TPU-based paint protection film imports from China. We believe this represents an important step towards creating a more level playing field for domestic manufacturers.

items.statement: Tariff refunds: 30-40% received by July-August; expect full refund in Q2 FY27; net ~INR50 crores+ to be retained after sharing with US customers
items.quote: See, the thing is whatever refund we will get, we need to share with our customers in U.S., some of them. So if you talk of net number, I expect anywhere around INR50 crores plus should be with us.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with INR850 crores cash and liquid investments despite INR700+ crores invested in expansions
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain one of our greatest strength despite investing over INR700 crores towards strategic expansions over the past few years, the company remains debt-free with a healthy cash and liquid investment balance of INR850 crores.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; cash generation funding capex and potential inorganic growth
items.quote: We are working on some inorganic growth where we have evaluated in the past. We are still evaluating if something makes sense for us. That's number one. Number two is we also want to make this system much more reliable in terms of our manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic growth opportunities; no deals announced
items.quote: We are working on some inorganic growth where we have evaluated in the past. We are still evaluating if something makes sense for us.

items.statement: Capital allocation priority: inorganic growth, manufacturing capex for backward/forward integration, then shareholder returns
items.quote: I think in a couple of months' time, first of all, we are working on some inorganic growth where we have evaluated in the past. We are still evaluating if something makes sense for us. That's number one. Number two is we also want to make this system much more reliable in terms of our manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: R&D expense 3-5% of revenue (variable as some R&D capitalized into manufacturing)
items.quote: So the thing is this expense, R&D expense, if we talk of our revenues, it's like in the range of, I can say, 3% to 5%. And yes, but that is very variable. We are continuously monitoring that in a way because some of our R&D comes into manufacturing as well.

items.statement: TPU addressable market estimated INR1,000+ crores in India (market creation phase)
items.quote: I won't be surprised if I say like this is easily INR1,000 crores, but we need to really get there with our products and the time line, right? and that will grow because it's not something -- as I said, we do not do anything.

items.statement: Middle East supply chain disruptions due to war causing shipping delays (ship stuck in Jebel Ali)
items.quote: Unfortunately, one of our ship got stuck in Jebel Ali. So we received some of the consignments late, and that's why some of the products were delayed from Q1 to Q2.

items.statement: Raw material cost correlation only 10-12% for consumer products due to backward integration; crude-linked increases passed through to customers
items.quote: See, raw material on our consumer products, there is like the real impact. If I say correlation, if I talk, it's only 10% to 12%, direct correlation with the top end raw material, right? Because there are 10 components which we manufacture on our own, right? So their raw material to the end product ultimately reaches only to 10%.

items.statement: Expect raw material inflation of about 8% sequentially into Q2
items.quote: Based on the current outlook, we expect raw material inflation of about 8% sequentially into Q2.

items.statement: Expect financial and operational benefits of Enschede restructuring to start materialising from H2 FY27
items.quote: The Netherlands plant stopped production as planned in June 2026, and we expect the financial and ope rational benefits of the restructuring to start materialising from H2 of the current fiscal

items.statement: Expect Europe Operations to deliver high teens EBITDA on full year basis after footprint change
items.quote: on a full year basis in E urope, with this change, we would look to deliver high teens EBITDA

items.statement: Anticipate net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to go up slightly in current year; will be a net borrower
items.quote: We anticipate that our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio will go up slightly in the current year. We will be a net borrower.

items.statement: Demand remains healthy across categories and channels; July delivered strong start
items.quote: Looking ahead, demand remains healthy across categories and channels. July already delivered a strong start, providing confidence that the momentum will carry into Q2.

items.statement: India replacement volume growth 13%, OEM 10%, exports 15% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Replacement was 13% OEM was 10% and exports was 15%. So fairly in a narrow range, but all in double digits.

items.statement: Europe PCR replacement growth in double digits, well ahead of market
items.quote: Even in this quarter, Raghu, the PCR replacement growth was in double digit, well ahead of the market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 11.7%, down 150 bps YoY due to RM cost pressures
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at INR 74 billion with an EBITDA margin of 11.7%, down about 150 basis points year-on-year, primarily on account of RM cost pressures.

items.statement: India Operations EBITDA margin 12% vs 13.6% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 6.5 billion, a margin of 12% compared to 13.6% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin 8.9% vs 10.8% YoY, impacted by Enschede transition costs
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR13 million, a margin of 8.9%, lower than the previous year 10.8%.

items.statement: Europe margin would have been ~11% without Enschede-Hungary overlap costs
items.quote: I would say if those overlaps were not there, we would have been at about 11% odd margin levels, okay?

items.statement: Raw material costs escalated ~17% in Q1; India needs 15-16% price increase, currently at 11%+
items.quote: Raw material costs escalated sharply during Q1 by the magnitude of nearly 17%. Despite this, we largely successfully defended margins through a combination of calibrated price increases and disciplined cost control.

items.statement: India Q1 price increases implemented 7-9% staggered; further hikes announced for Q2 (1% in July, ~2% expected in August)
items.quote: What was implemented and that also in a staggered manner through the quarter was about 7% to 9%. Further price increases into Q2 have already been announced.
