items.quote: The business mix remains well diversified with water, transport and tunneling contribution 41%, 35% and 24% of revenue, respectively.

items.statement: WMEL micro tunnel fleet 100% occupied, focusing on domestic market
items.quote: Right now, we are quite busy with the domestic market simply because our fleet of machines are 100% occupied.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and commodity availability could impact execution timelines
items.quote: We remain mindful of the evolving external environment, including geopolitical developments, which could influence execution time lines.

items.statement: Q1 execution impacted by Mumbai construction stoppage, geopolitical supply chain disruptions, and election-related labor migration
items.quote: Firstly, we experienced supply chain disruptions arising from the ongoing ge opolitical develo pments, resulting in a volatil e and uncertain operating environment. Secondly, execution across a significant portion of our project portfolio was affected by the temporary construction stoppage in Mumbai, which lasted for several weeks. Finally, labor availability at proj ect sites was impacted by migr

items.statement: Smart Ops revenue estimated at INR50-100 crores range for current year, no formal guidance
items.quote: I think it can range anywhere from INR50 crores to INR100 crores, but we are not able to give you a guidance, yes.

items.statement: Strengthening talent practices and digitizing process systems
items.quote: Beyond our financial and operational performance, we continue to strengthen our talent practices and digitize our process systems.

items.statement: FY27 copper revenue contribution expected at ~45% as capacity ramps up
items.quote: Copper is expected to contribute approximately 45% of our overall revenue in FY27 as capacity ramp-up progresses.

items.statement: 2030 roadmap targets >15% volume growth, 20%+ revenue/profit CAGR, EBITDA margin >8%, ROCE >20%, >60% revenue from value-added products
items.quote: Our target 2030 road map is focused on delivering over 15% volume growth, 20% plus CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margins above 8%, Pondy Oxides and ROCE exceeding 20% and deriving over 60% of our revenue from value-added

items.statement: Lead volume guidance of 1.25-1.3 lakh tons for FY27 maintained despite Q1 supply constraints
items.quote: we are confident at least we will be able to close up to the numbers that we had committed over the last quarter.

items.statement: Copper cathode EBITDA per ton guided above INR40,000 (previously INR35,000-40,000) driven by capacity efficiencies
items.quote: we should be able to do in excess of 40,000, which mainly is driven through the efficiencies that we have gotten through our increased capacities

items.statement: Copper cathode plant blended EBITDA per ton guided at INR60,000-65,000; recycled copper sold externally above INR40,000/ton
items.quote: What we had guided was a blended margin profile on this should be in the range of around 60,000, 65,000.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR175 crores: INR20-25 crores maintenance, INR140-150 crores for copper cathode plant
items.quote: Out of approximately that INR175 crores, the maintenance capex will be in the range of INR20 crores, INR25 crores and balance INR140 crores to INR150 crores would be for the copper new plant division.

items.statement: Copper cathode project: INR200 crores total, INR25 crores spent, Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) commissioning by Dec 2026, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) by Q3 FY28
items.quote: We are establishing a 36,000 metric ton per annum copper cathode facility at our Thervoy kandigai plant in Tamil Nadu with a total investment of approximately INR200 crores, fully funded through our internal accruals.

items.statement: New 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity (Q4 FY26) at ~75% utilization in FY27; lead TKD plant (pure lead) below 50% utilization in Q1
items.quote: The incremental 6,000 metric tons per annum copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 has ramped up well and is expected to achieve capacity utilization of approximately 75% through FY 2027.

items.statement: FY28 copper cathode capacity utilization targeted at 80-90% of 36,000 tpa
items.quote: In FY28, I mean, we are confident we'll be able to utilize over 80%, 90% of the capacity of 36,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Q1 FY27: Revenue INR931 crores (+56% YoY), EBITDA INR56 crores (+30%), PAT INR36 crores (+32%); domestic/export mix 55/45
items.quote: Revenue growth remained robust during Q1 FY27 with revenue increasing to INR931 crores, registering 56% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 6%, PAT margin 3.9%; lead EBITDA/ton INR21,595 (highest ever), copper EBITDA/ton INR48,488 (+66% YoY)
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, EBITDA and PAT margins remained strong at 6% and 3.9% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Lead value-added mix 85% in Q1 (vs ~55% YoY, ~63% FY26); sustainable annual target 65-70%
items.quote: Annually, we are looking at around 65% to 70% on the value-added mix. Last year was at about 63%.

items.statement: No demand softness in lead; volumes lower due to supply chain delays (shipping via Hormuz); demand intact
items.quote: Like I said, there is no softness in demand. There is a gap in supply because of delay in shipments and the supply chain disruptions. But overall, the demand is intact.

items.statement: Other expenses up due to fuel prices and additive costs (not just logistics); Middle East sourcing <5% but shipping route delays via Hormuz cause disruptions
items.quote: The major part is contributed by the fuel prices and a couple of additives prices that have shot up in the last 3 months.

items.statement: Alternative sourcing from Southeast Asia and South America being pursued; pricing similar but depends on inward freight
items.quote: We are looking at alternative sourcing as we have, and we have already started working on it from our Southeast Asian and other South American and other region suppliers.

items.statement: Domestic lead sourcing not pursued in Q1 due to high price delta wiping out profitability; domestic copper sourcing target 25-30% going forward
items.quote: we are also looking at copper from domestic sourcing, which would contribute about 25% to 30% going forward.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 46 days (from 53 days); positive cash flow; April receivables of INR110-115 crores received April 5
items.quote: Currently, we are at 46 days... Versus 53 days earlier. And we have a positive cash flow as well, yes.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded outlook to A Positive from A Stable, reaffirming credit rating; strong balance sheet noted
items.quote: CRISIL has upgraded POCL's outlook Pondy Oxides and to A positive from A stable while reaffirming its credit rating, recognizing its strong balance sheet and sustained financial performance

items.statement: Lead value-added products 85% of segment revenue in Q1; copper value-added focus with cathode production upcoming
items.quote: Within the lead vertical, value-added products accounted for 85% of the segment revenue reinforcing our strategic focus on increasing the share of higher-margin products.

items.statement: Lead value-added customers are supplier-specific; pure lead volumes reduced to prioritize value-added during supply constraints
items.quote: We requested our customers to take the basic pure lead product from any other supplier because Pondy Oxides and that's more easy to procure, wherein value -added products are supplier specific

items.statement: Lead volume decline 25% vs competitor ~10%; management declines to comment on competitor specifics
items.quote: I won't be able to specifically comment on the competitor. But regarding our reasons, we have already given you the reasons in terms of why the volumes were lower.

items.statement: EPR credits not yet monetized; domestic procurement may yield EPR benefits in Q2; margins compensated through pricing
items.quote: Probably in the second quarter, we look on it if the domestic procurement improves, then we can have the benefit of EPR in the second quarter.

items.statement: Copper production/sales volumes up >3x YoY in Q1; highest ever quarterly production and sales
items.quote: achieving the highest ever quarterly production and sales with both Pondy Oxides and volumes increasing by more than 3 times on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions (Hormuz shipping route) may persist; working capital not stretched as payment cycle tied to material arrival
items.quote: Our payment cycle is when the material arrives closer to the port, that's about a week before the arrival of the material. So that still stays in place.

items.statement: Lithium-ion recycling at pilot stage; monitoring LFP chemistry (1.5-2% recovery), technology evolution, and feedstock availability
items.quote: We are still contemplating and working with some strategic technical partners predominantly in India, only the LFP chemistry is available and wherein the recovery extraction is about 1.5% to 2%.

items.statement: Plastics division turned profitable (INR15 lakhs net profit, ~800 tons); aluminium at ~200 tons; preparing value additions
items.quote: Plastic division for this quarter, it has turned profitable. We have achieved about INR15 lakhs in terms of profit -- net profit.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking guidance but expects continued traction from pipeline conversion
items.quote: Looking at the overall outlook, as you know, we do not provide guidance, but if our trailing 12 month numbers are an indication, then we are positively stepping into a zone where we feel comfortable that we will continue to create traction.

items.statement: Targeting sustainable adjusted EBITDA margin of 18-19% while investing in AI and sales
items.quote: But from a margin perspective, like I have guided in the past also, we continue to stay focused to stay in that 18 to 19 percentage adjusted EBITDA on a sustainable basis, beyond which we will obviously continue to invest in our AI initiatives, sales and marketing efforts and continue to build for the future in terms of capturing the whole AI-led growth.

items.statement: AI-led transformation driving larger deal sizes and better pipeline quality across geographies
items.quote: The quality of pipeline is better, meaning average deal sizes is better, the kind of work that the customer is asking us to do is better.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month ACV bookings at $82.9 million, up from $82.3 million previous quarter
items.quote: reporting the trailing 12-month ACV bookings in Q2, we recorded $82.9 million of ACV bookings compared to $82.3 million in Q1.

items.statement: Data, AI and cloud services now exceed 50% of revenue and continue to grow
items.quote: So, data , AI and cloud taken together while we don't share an explicit percentage, but it is something that we are quite focused on and happy about, that as an organization, we have now significantly data AI and cloud services-driven organization, revenue numbers have crossed 50% and continues to go up.

items.statement: Top client contribution increased to 6% from 5.8%, top 10 clients at 24.4% from 24%
items.quote: Our client concentration has shown a positive uptick both on the top client and the top 10 client basis, where top client contributes now 6% instead of 5.8%, top 10 clients leading to 24.4% instead of 24%.

items.statement: Deliberate increase in sales and marketing spend including new brand identity and AI studio launch
items.quote: We have been invited to several conferences, etc., where we participated and talked about EXIQO, the AI studio and how it makes a difference. All of that is in the direction of both building the market, having more feet on the ground, and being able to create more positive traction.

items.statement: Utilization at 80.5-81% within target band, sweating AI bench investments made over last 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Utilization percentage has slightly ticked up to reach 80.5% to 81% which is our standard and accepted band of between 80% to 81% which is where we want to operate.

items.statement: AI productivity gains enabling premium pricing without deflationary pressure on project revenue
items.quote: For us, the AI -based productivity is an inbuilt part of our AI -first delivery methodology. So, what we bid for and what we win in the market is AI -led and already contains the elements of productivity gains that the customer is looking for and a project revenue which we have already won then does not have deflationary pressures.

items.statement: Billed DSO at 55-56 days, billed plus unbilled at 75 days, in line or better than industry
items.quote: Our DSO remains largely in the band with b illed DSO staying at about 55 -56 days and b illed plus unbilled coming to about 75 days, which is very much in line or better than the industry averages.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisition opportunities with focus on differentiated capabilities and margin accretion
items.quote: we as an organization have an organic plus inorganic growth ambition and thesis. So, we continue to be on the lookout, we continue to stay vigilant and actively receiving inbounds in terms of where interesting opportunities may lie, we evaluate those.

items.statement: Revenue per employee and margin per employee showing green shoots from AI-compounded growth
items.quote: the whole AI -compounded growth story, which is beginning to kick in and starting to show green shoots of better revenue per employee and a margin per employee story.

items.statement: Novigo facing geopolitical challenges in Middle East but continuing strong deal wins across markets
items.quote: Novigo, of course, has an ongoing geopolitical challenge that they are dealing with, which is due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East. But despite that, they continue to show strong deal wins all across the markets, including in the Middle East.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 370 bps YoY to 46.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin came at 46.8%, an expansion of approximately 370 basis points over the same last quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reached 6.7% in Q1 FY27, fifth consecutive quarter of expansion
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR47.2 crores against INR5 crores in Q1 FY26 with EBITDA margins at 6.7% against 0.8% a year ago and 5.3% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain or better Q1 FY27 numbers in subsequent quarters
items.quote: I think at this point of time, what we are saying is that let's maintain -- I mean, rather than giving a very clear outlook, I mean, what we are saying is we will maintain or we'll better the numbers what we have done for Q1.

items.statement: Value-added yarn currently 10-15% of portfolio, targeting 30-35%
items.quote: At this point of time, possibly 10% to 15% of our products in yarn is on that category.

items.statement: Capex funded from internal accruals and existing facilities, no equity requirement
items.quote: Everything we have described is funded from existing facilities with no equity requirement and no dependence on market conditions because we are mostly upgrading assets we already own rather than building new capacity.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to rise to ~INR75 crores in FY27 from INR67 crores in FY26 due to capex
items.quote: And I think this year, we should be at about -- we'll be about INR75 crores.

items.statement: Export demand steady across 60 destinations; new markets in Far East, Africa, SE Asia, LatAm contributing
items.quote: Our export growth this quarter came from disproportionately from these markets we did not serve 18 months ago, and our exposure to any single geography is lower than what it was 2 years ago.

items.statement: Home textile business targeting doubling in 2 years
items.quote: Currently, we -- I mean, we are looking at doubling this in about 2 years, the home textile business.

items.statement: Yarn segment EBITDA grew 5x to INR34.4 crores on 16% revenue growth
items.quote: Segment revenue of INR640 crores grew 16%, but the more important number is the segment EBITDA of INR34.4 crores against INR6.5 crores a year ago, almost a fivefold improvement on 16% more revenue.

items.statement: Home textile revenue grew 22% YoY and turned profitable
items.quote: Home textiles grew revenue 22% and held profitability against the loss a year ago.

items.statement: Sutlej Green Fibre gross sales ~INR400 crores, 70-75% captively consumed
items.quote: On the green fiber, which is basically the recycled polyester, if you were to look at the gross margin, I mean, the gross sales, it will be roughly about INR400 crores. However, almost 70%, 75% of this gets consumed into our own units.

items.statement: Working capital utilization comfortable; inventory calibrated, receivables steady
items.quote: Working capital utilization remains comfortable against sanction limits. Inventory is calibrated to demand and receivable cycles are steady.

items.statement: Employee cost at 16.6% of revenue; management acknowledges need to reduce further
items.quote: Employee cost stood at 16.6% of the revenue against 17.7% a year ago. This quarter absorbed the annual wage revision, which takes effect in Q1.

items.statement: Raw material prices, geopolitics, global demand outside control; execution risk remains
items.quote: Raw material prices, geopolitics and global demand are outside our control, and we take nothing for granted.

items.statement: Home textile order phasing softer sequentially but H1 visibility healthy
items.quote: The quarter was softer sequentially on order phasing, not on demand. Visibility through the first half remains healthy.

items.statement: Raw material to sales ratio improved 2.5%; 60% from product mix upgrade, 40% operational efficiency
items.quote: I would say that almost 60% is coming -- of that improvement is coming because we are moving the product categories up. And balance is obviously the change in the bottom line is because of the operational efficiency.

items.statement: Design-led home textiles insulated from tariff noise affecting commodity segment
items.quote: Tariff noise affects commodity home textiles, it has not dented ours because complex design-led product is not easily resourced.

items.statement: SGF demand structural, driven by European regulation on sustainable materials
items.quote: The demand behind it is structural, written into European regulation, not a cycle that will reverse.

items.statement: Technical textiles (Protech) progressing to schedule; FY28 revenue contributor
items.quote: Protech business has moved from qualification into sampling and trials are advancing. I'll be measured though that these are FY28 contributors not FY27.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned in transcript
items.quote: Our objective is not to maximize the quarter. It is to build a business that consistently delivers stronger margins, better returns on capital and improved cash generation and to create durable value for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 constant currency revenue growth guidance of 10% to 13% and EBIT margin band of 12.25% to 12.75%
items.quote: We are reaffirming the full-year guidance we set out at the start of the year. On revenue, we continue to expect constant currency growth of 10% to 13% for FY27. On margins, we continue to guide to an EBIT margin band of 12.25% to 12.75%.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to reach EBIT margin of 14% to 15% over next two to three years
items.quote: We see our constant currency revenue growth for FY27 in the 10% to 13% range, and we remain laser-focused on taking our EBIT margin to 14% to 15% band over the next two to three years.

items.statement: EBIT margin 12.4%, up 110 bps YoY and 20 bps QoQ; seventh straight quarter of margin expansion
items.quote: EBIT margin for the quarter was 12.4%, up 110 basis points and 20 basis points on a year -on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively.

items.statement: Top 5 and top 10 client revenue share declined over last eight quarters despite top 5 growing at industry rates; broad-basing deliberate
items.quote: Over the last eight quarters, the revenue share of our top 5 and top 10 clients has come down. And importantly, that has happened even as our top five clients continue to grow at industry rates, despite a significant onshor e-to-nearshore shift in at least a couple of them.

items.statement: Headcount 36,875, net increase of 670; voluntary attrition 27.5%; offshore/nearshore hiring 80% of gross additions
items.quote: We closed Q1 FY27 with a headcount of 36,875 Firstsourcers, a net increase of 670 associates over Q4 FY26, with strategic client demand driving growth across our core delivery geographies. Our voluntary attrition was 27.5% for the quarter.

items.statement: Exceptional charge of INR717 million (INR563M net of tax) including INR357M for healthcare BPaaS program termination, INR284M for regulatory penalty indemnification, INR76M for Ascensos contingent consideration
items.quote: During the quarter, we also recognized onetime exceptional charge of INR717 million or INR563 million net of taxes. This comprises of the three items.

items.statement: Normalized DSO 67-69 days; normalized FCF to PAT at ~94%
items.quote: Normalized DSO continue to be in the range of 67 to 69 days. Our FCF to PAT normalized for subsequent collection - related to exceptional item we talked about, continue to be at around 94%.

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP61.6M for next 12 months at avg 118-120; USD119M at avg INR92.7; option products on 25-30% of portfolio for upside
items.quote: Our hedge book as of June 30 , 2026 was as follows. We had a coverage of GBP61.6 million for the next 12 months with an average rate between 118 to 120, and coverage of US$119 million with an average rate of INR92.7 to a dollar.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances INR3 billion; net debt INR17.1 billion vs INR16.3 billion at March 2026
items.quote: Turning to the balance sheet, our cash and bank balances stood at INR3 billion and net debt was INR17.1 billion versus INR16.3 billion at the end of March 2026.

items.statement: Healthcare payer clients recalibrating scope due to CMS rate adjustments and utilization management requirements; regulatory friction making outcome-accountable partnerships more valuable
items.quote: On the Healthcare Payer side, Q1 revenue reflected program timing effects as several Medicare Advantage clients recalibrated operational program scope in response to CMS rate adjustments and evolving utilization management requirements.

items.statement: AI platforms live at scale: 14 of top 20 US mortgage lenders, 10 of top 15 US health plans, top US/UK card issuers; Kairos Intelligent Context Framework enabling AI in regulated environments
items.quote: The same model is already in production at scale, where our AI platforms run for 14 of the top 20 US mortgage lenders, 10 of the top 15 US health plans, and top US and UK card issuers.

items.statement: South Africa fastest-growing geography; new UK delivery office in Glasgow for financial services regulatory work; expanding sales presence in Canada
items.quote: Also, our pitch for transformational programs and nearshore delivery from South Africa has been resonating strongly with clients, and South Africa is our fastest -growing geography today. We also expanded our UK delivery footprint for regulatory work with a new office in Glasgow supporting financial services clients on the financial assistance and anti -fraud services.

items.statement: Partner ecosystem expanded with Zendesk, Cresta, and Silicon Valley startups; dedicated partnerships team deepening hyperscaler collaboration on AWS and Google Cloud
items.quote: We have expanded our dedicated partnerships team and deepened collaboration with leading hyperscalers, building momentum on AWS -based AI and automation, and also taking similar opportunities to clients on Google Cloud. Beyond the hyperscalers, we announced three key relationships as well.

items.statement: Healthcare BPaaS engagement wound down due to client leadership change; 1-1.5% FY27 growth impact absorbed; charge of INR357M taken prudently but recovery expected
items.quote: Importantly, our original guidance had factored in roughly about 1% to 1.5% of growth from the healthcare BPaaS engagement that is now being wound down because of a leadership change and an intent to continue with the same technology platform that they earlier had.

items.statement: Healthcare provider clients facing flat reimbursement, rising labor costs, regulatory uncertainty from HR1 accelerating shift to AI/automation-led RCM delivery
items.quote: In Healthcare Provider, our clients are contending with flat reimbursement, rising labour costs, and regulatory uncertainty from H R1. This is accelerating a structural shift towards AI and automation -led RCM delivery.

items.quote: See, right now in Q1, there is, I t hink maybe around 1% is from the railway, less than 1%. But this is increasing, and we constantly now started participating in the tender. And number 2, on the fire product, it will start in Q3

items.statement: UAE capex funding 50-50 debt-equity; AED7M bank debt being tied up
items.quote: So, we are right now it is whatever the funding is done is from the internal accruals, and apart from that, now we are tying up with the fund from a bank, which is around AED7 million we are proposing to take us in long-term debt over there.

items.statement: Q2 revenue guidance INR140-145 crore (15-20% QoQ growth from Q1 INR118 crore)
items.quote: So, Q1 is around 118, so mostly we are seeing in between 140 to 145, Q2.

items.statement: FY27 production guidance toned down to ~380,000 tons from earlier 400,000 tons due to transformer and gas cleaning plant constraints at KNR-2
items.quote: We had indicated 400,000 tons, but we going to tone it down a little bit because while we were able to switch on all furnaces at KNR-2 in the month of March and, in fact, got a little bit of production, but some of the transformers we have, we feel should not be loaded beyond a certain point.

items.statement: FY28 production target maintained at 475,000-500,000 tons
items.quote: We are still maintaining 475,000 to 500,000 tons for FY '28.

items.statement: KNR-1 first furnace heating refractory lining, first tapping expected around third week of July 2026; second furnace by end September/early October
items.quote: We are also looking to commission the KNR-1 greenfield project, where the first furnace we have already initiated the process of heating the refractory lining, so we expect first tapping around the third week of this month.

items.statement: Full capacity of ~120,000-125,000 tons/month expected by Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027) when all furnaces stabilized
items.quote: By the end of the financial year, that is, so the fourth quarter, which is January to March 2027, we will be looking at a full 50% higher volume at roughly about 120,000, 125,000 tons per month.

items.statement: Ordered 2 sets of transformers plus a spare for KNR-2; replacement planned in Q2/Q3 FY27; additional INR15-20 crores approved for 50,000 ton furnace at KNR-2 pending environmental clearance
items.quote: We have already ordered 2 sets of transformers plus a spare. Sometimes in Q2 or Q3, we will be looking to replace the 2 sets of transformers where we have a little bit of concern.

items.statement: Global stainless steel production growing ~2.5-3%; ferrochrome prices supported by chrome ore cost pressures; captive chrome ore insulates IMFA
items.quote: Stainless steel production has grown. I mean it may not be very aggressive growth, but about 2.5% to 3% growth is there globally if you look at it.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 blended selling price just shy of INR120,000/ton; Q2 expected similar with slight correction; volumes to offset price dips
items.quote: On a per ton basis, if you look at for Q1, obviously, the number is a lot higher because what we are seeing is our selling price being just shy of INR120,000, blended selling price.

items.statement: KNR-1 and KNR-2 more competitive than Therubali; full margin benefit of INR1,500-2,000/ton expected from Q4 FY27 when 500,000 tons stabilized
items.quote: Once KNR-1 and KNR-2 all stabilize and we get to that 500,000 tons production in a smooth manner, then we will see our margins improve by about INR1,500 to INR2,000.

items.statement: Met coke prices moved up slightly due to Colombian currency depreciation; impact may be seen in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Actually, met coke prices have moved up a little bit. I don't know about coking coal, but as far as metallurgical coke is concerned, it's moved up a little bit on account of Colombia, etc., their currency depreciation.

items.statement: Chrome ore stock ~6 lakh tons to meet additional capacity needs for next year; ferrochrome stock building from ~17,000-18,000 tons to support higher output across three locations
items.quote: On the chrome ore, we have stacked up to meet whatever is our additional capacity requirement for next 1 year. So approximately chrome ore stock of 6 lakh tons is there with us.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 other expenses included INR32 crore MTM forex loss on hedged exports; Q1 FY27 currencies stable, forex gain realized, lowering other expenses
items.quote: As you know, in quarter 4, we had said that since the forex USD had gone up from Q3 to Q4 range from INR89.9 to INR94.65, the exports proceeds are hedged. MTM, that is a mark-to-market impact of INR32 crores had reflected in our financials as a negative for Q4.

items.statement: ~19% domestic sales in Q1 FY27; balance exported mainly to Far East; domestic and export prices at parity due to low duty protection (2-3%)
items.quote: Yes, around 19% we have sold in domestic.

items.statement: South African producers (Glencore, Samancor) restarting furnaces with Eskom special tariff ($0.62/lb); Glencore Line 1 ~700,000-800,000 tons; may create short-term glut but chrome ore supply to China should reduce
items.quote: I don't think the number of 4.5 million is right because at the moment, only Glencore has switched on, I believe, Line 1, and Suresh might have the numbers, but I thin k it's something like 700,000, 800,000 tons expectation, including others

items.statement: Environmental clearance pending for 50,000 ton furnace at KNR-2; clarity expected in 3-4 months; operational by mid-2027 if approved
items.quote: Not at the moment. We are hoping that somewhere around middle of next year is when we can do that.

items.statement: Coke consumption 0.65 kg/ton ferrochrome; chrome ore consumption 2.5 tons/ton ferrochrome
items.value: 0.65 kg coke, 2.5 tons chrome ore per ton ferrochrome
items.quote: So broadly, that's 0.65 kilograms of coke and broadly 2.5 tons of chrome ore.

items.statement: No impact from West Asia crisis as no imports/sales there; freight costs up slightly but prices more than compensate
items.quote: Fortunately, for us, no impact of the West Asia crisis because we don't import anything from West Asia or sell anything to West Asia.

items.statement: Critical minerals remain area of interest; bid on blocks unsuccessful so far but will keep trying
items.quote: Critical minerals are something we are interested in because it's certainly adjacent to our skill set. We have looked at a couple of blocks but have unfortunately not been successful in the bid.

items.statement: Management expects to announce at least one new park before end of FY27
items.quote: Before the end of the financial year, we will have something to announce.

items.statement: Maintenance capex at 6-7% of revenue; expansion capex at ~10% of revenue
items.quote: Generally, we keep about 10% of our top line for the expansion purpose or maybe for adding new attraction to the existing park. 6%, 7% of my top line will be for the maintenance capital.

items.statement: Large parks can handle 1.2-1.3M visitors; small parks ~500-550K visitors at structural limit
items.quote: We can handle maybe up to 1.2 million, 1.3 million visitors for a large park. And then, maybe the small park can handle like Bhubaneswar can handle maybe like 5 lakhs or something like that.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 footfall grew 33% YoY to 12.25 lakh; existing parks footfall up 7%
items.quote: Our footfall crossed 12.25 lakh visitors, up 33% over the same period last year, reflecting the continued strength of our brand and growing demand for quality leisure experiences.

items.statement: Chennai Park EBITDA margin tracking at mature park levels for Q1; long-term expected at par with other parks
items.quote: For now, it is. But then, we don't have a full picture until we finish a year because every quarter is different, and the footfalls can vary.

items.statement: Average ticket price up 2% YoY to INR1,310; non-ticket spend up 20% YoY to INR591; ARPU up 7% to INR1,901
items.quote: Our average ticket price for the quarter stood at INR1,310, registering a 2% Y -o-Y increase. Average non -ticket spend per guest increased by 20% Y -o-Y basis to INR591, reflecting a continued strength in our in-park spending initiatives.

items.statement: Targeting 40-50% non-ticket revenue mix; currently ~30%
items.quote: Yes, your assumption is correct. That's it.

items.statement: Hyderabad Park growth driven by marketing investments and brand building in AP-Telangana region
items.quote: We made some disproportionate investments like our CFO earlier also said in terms of marketing and building the brand and further penetrating more footfall for the AP -Telangana, and we've been seeing early results.

items.statement: Management believes paying for foreign IP doesn't work financially in India; prefers proprietary IP
items.quote: See, paying foreign money for IP and then getting that to India, I don't think it works financially. So we believe in creating our own IP.

items.statement: No government directives on water usage currently; rainfall strong recently
items.quote: As of now, there is no issue. I think rainfall has been actually very strong in the last few days.

items.statement: Corporate overhead increased INR6.5 crores YoY due to digital transformation (INR1.5 cr) and marketing
items.quote: This is mainly the digital transformation expenses compared to the previous quarter because we started the new POS in our parks only from July month. So all those digital transformations has costed us about some INR1.5 crores incrementally.

items.statement: Net cash position INR400+ crores on balance sheet
items.quote: Now we have crossed INR400-plus crores of net cash on balance sheet, and now we will have the financial ability to open more parks in quick succession.

items.statement: Planning 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small parks over next 3-4 years; exploring asset-light models
items.quote: We'll definitely work on 1 or 2 parks large parks, and then maybe 1 or 2 small ones as well.

items.statement: Chennai Park revenue INR45 crores, footfall 2.42 lakh, EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our new asset, Chennai Park, contributed INR45 crores in revenue during the quarter with a footfall of 2.42 lakhs.

items.statement: Heavy rainfall in Kerala causing some disruption to Kochi Park footfall
items.quote: Whenever there is heavy rainfall and landslide, some disruption will be there. We are not -- in our area, there is not much issues. But of course, there are disruptions in the state, and definitely, that will have some effect on footfall also.

items.statement: Resort business (ISLE and Terrea) delivered best ever quarter; majority guests are park visitors
items.quote: Both our resort offerings delivered their best and along with Hyderabad Park, delivered their best ever quarter.

items.statement: New roller coaster in Bangalore driving higher dwell time, experience scores, and repeat visits
items.quote: The new roller coaster has been received extremely well. The customer dwelling time, customer experience scores are really up. And when we add such global-standard rides, it definitely becomes a star attraction for people to come and visit the park again.

items.statement: Targets substantial revenue growth for FY27 vs FY26 with red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT margins on consolidated basis
items.quote: We will ensure that we don't go below these red lines. Specifically, to answer your question, yes, these 22 and 17, which are there currently on a consol basis, while they may fluctuate a bit here and there on a particular quarter. But on an annual basis, we will definitely not allow them to go below the red lines.

items.statement: Expects at least INR 300 crore export revenue in FY27
items.quote: Our assessment is that this year, export, we should try and achieve at least INR 300 crores plus.

items.statement: Targets one export order per quarter in FY27
items.quote: We are aiming that we continue to get fresh orders also, one export order per quarter, which we are trying this year.

items.statement: Total order book at INR 9,450 crore as of Q1 FY27 with 50% Turnkey and 50% consultancy/export
items.quote: We are now at INR 9,450 crore. Our target of achieving INR 10,000 crore, and the interesting thing is that about 70% of these fresh orders are on a competitive basis.

items.statement: Export order book (RITES Videsh) at INR 2,100 crore including INR 1,775 crore rolling stock export and INR 900 crore Bangladesh coach order
items.quote: We have an total RITES' order book, let me include both the export and consultancy (foreign), is INR 2,100 crores. Out of that, about INR 1,775 is the export of rolling stock and out of that, about INR 900 odd crores is the order from Bangladesh, which is about 200 coaches.

items.statement: Received 128 orders worth INR 670 crore in Q1 FY27 at strike rate of 1.4 orders per day
items.quote: You see, this quarter also, we have got 128 orders totaling INR 670 crores. We've maintained the strike rate of one plus, which is nearly 1.4 orders a day.

items.statement: New export order for 9 locomotives to South Africa worth ~35 million received in July, pending formal agreement signing
items.quote: This quarter also, in July, we have got an order for about 35 million for nine locomotives to South Africa. 9 RITES Limited Q1 FY27 Post Earnings Conference Call 05.08.2026 While we declared it to the stock exchange, we haven't yet accounted for it in our order book, because we're waiting for the

items.statement: Turnkey projects carry 1.5-2% margins due to accounting method where full project value flows through P&L vs only fees in consultancy
items.quote: Basically, they always remain in the range of about 1.5-2% margins. We are very clear. As we have said earlier, we are not a construction company. We are a consultancy company.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin at 22% and PAT margin at 17%, held sequentially from Q4 FY26
items.quote: Even this quarter, we've been able to hold on to 22%. Sequentially, also, we've held on to 22% Q4, Q1. PAT margins, we've held on to about 17% sequentially also.

items.statement: Margin pressure from 70%+ competitive orders, travel costs, and impending pay revision
items.quote: There are broadly three elements, which are definitely contributing to the overall stress in the margin. The first is definitely, as you see, that since about 70% plus are on competitive mode, as they generate revenue in the coming quarters, these have been taken definitely at a much tougher margin.

items.statement: Mozambique locomotive deliveries targeted to begin by end of FY27 with clarity by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: As far as the locomotives are concerned, the Mozambique, yes, we are trying that maybe by the end of this FY, we could aim for beginning of the deliveries. But again, a little more clarity would happen maybe by end of Q2 in terms of the exact visibility.

items.statement: Vande Bharat export initiative started with standard gauge prototype development discussions underway with Indian Railways
items.quote: We have already initiated the possibility of exporting Vande Bharat on the standard gauge platform to certain geographies. We have reached out to certain possible countries, which have even some interests in it.

items.statement: Employee count increased by ~450 YoY to 3,125 in Q1 FY27 to build bench strength for order execution
items.quote: If you compare YoY Q1 to Q1, there has been a net increase in our employee strength of about 450 numbers, which is a huge jump from about 2,675. It has gone up to about 3,125.

items.statement: Employee cost expected to increase 8-10% in FY28 due to pay revision and headcount growth
items.quote: Not really 20%. I would put it more in the range of about 8-10%.

items.statement: QA (Quality Assurance) revenue at ~INR 70 crore in Q1 FY27, targeting double-digit growth for FY27
items.quote: QA has been again a good steady growth and if you recall last FY, we touched the levels which we had touched about before the competitive were enough up about 2 years back. We are on track again. It's about in the same range of about INR 70 odd crores.

items.statement: Dividend payout policy to continue at 90%+ with no major changes expected given low capex, minimal working capital, and debt-free status
items.quote: We are always 90% plus. We'll not give you any surprise in the change in our basic business model. Once there is no major change, we can with the low CapEx and hardly any working capital requirement, debt free, we don't see any major shift in the dividend payout policy.

items.statement: REMCL contributed INR 22 crore PAT (50%+ margins) and INR 10 crore dividend (91% payout) in Q1 FY27
items.quote: REMCL has been steadily giving a good PAT and dividend to us. It's about 50% plus PAT margins. This quarter also, it gave a profit of about INR 22 crores. That's a good dividend payout ratio of about 91%. We've got a good dividend of about INR 10 crores from REMCL.

items.statement: Low capex requirement cited as supporting continued high dividend payout
items.quote: Once there is no major change, we can with the low CapEx and hardly any working capital requirement, debt free, we don't see any major shift in the dividend payout policy.

items.statement: Turnkey share of order book at ~50% but not expected to exceed 50% long-term as consultancy and export grow in parallel
items.quote: I don't think over a period of time, I see the Turnkey being more than 50 odd percent on an average basis of the total order book.

items.statement: Clients prefer Turnkey model for single-point compliance and GST handling, driving strategic acceptance despite lower margins
items.quote: More and more, many clients are preferring to give us on a turnkey mode in terms of dealing with a single point of contact for compliances, GST provisions, etc.

items.statement: Margin red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT on consolidated basis will be defended through execution prioritization of higher-margin orders
items.quote: Our red lines of 20% EBITDA margins and 15% PAT margin on a consol basis, we will definitely strategically pushing on the execution of some higher margin orders out of the 700 plus order that we are executing. We will ensure that we don't go below these red lines.

items.statement: Focus on sequential execution improvement to achieve double-digit revenue growth and incremental quarterly growth in FY27
items.quote: Just to reiterate that the focus on increased execution sequentially to be able to achieve the targets that we had set ourselves for this FY. That's the key focus in the coming quarters, while definitely not compromising on the red lines of margins that we have set.

items.statement: Revenue recognition for Next Generation Corvette project to start in FY28 if contract signed this quarter
items.quote: The first revenue recognition will commence next year, that is the Financial Year 2028. Revenue recognition will commence in Financial Year 2 028 when we will be utilizing the activities involved in design, then the binding data information which we need to progress with the preparation of compartment design and equipment layout

items.statement: Current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore comprising 11 projects and 44 marine platforms
items.quote: Our current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore and this comprises mostly of shipbuilding orders with shipbuilding divisions contributing to ₹13,296 crore and the other two divisions, the engineering and the engine divisions, contribute to the balance of the order book.

items.quote: And there the capital infusion is expected to be just about ₹200 crore and this will be completed within a year and half (18 months). items.quote: In the last quarter, we had three of the ships which were commissioned. So, the last phase of commissioning, a certain amount of expenditure was incurred for these activities. So, in the current quarter, we did not have such occasions. So, that has resulted in a drop in the other expenses.

items.quote: MR Tanker, we are collaborating with one of our sister shipyards, and so are we doing so for the VLGC. So, we, along with our partnership here i

items.quote: not gone in for any export orders after the multipurpose contract. It is a very conscious act. When we went in for multipurpose vessel, obtaining the multipurpose vessel export order, at that point of time, our government had not aggregated the demand of the Indian non- defense requirements. So, now that demand has been aggregated and the opportunities are fantastic. About 200 plus platforms are r

items.quote: This is one of the projects which, as we are given to understand, this is in their prospective plan.
