So, I do not expect, in my appreciation again, that I do not expect th

items.statement: Water metro projects: ₹200-300 crore per metro, potential ₹1,500 crore for 5 states, 30-40 platforms; actively engaging with state governments, RFPs expected in 1 year
items.quote: The water metro project, as an earlier speaker, an analyst or an investor mentioned, many of the states are now looking at setting up a water metro. Kochi has already a facility and here we are doing one for the government of West Bengal. So, these are not very high-value projects. The order value could be to the tune of around ₹200 to 300 crore per metro. They are small platforms, but that but is

items.statement: Bonus/stock split decision rests with Administrative Ministry and DIPAM; awaiting government directives
items.quote: We are fully aware that this is controlled by the government department. We are waiting for t heir instructions on this. And whatever instructions come from the Administrative Ministry and DIPAM, we will abide by that. Let us wait for their directives

items.statement: PVC resin prices corrected sharply from early April after temporary suspension of import duty till June 2026, causing destocking across channel partners.
items.quote: While PVC resin prices witnessed a recovery during the March quarter, prices saw a sharp correction from early April following the temporary susp ension of import duty on PVC resin till June '26, which introduced fresh uncertainty into the market and resulted in destocking across channel partners across the industry

items.statement: Added many new channel partners in June quarter by identifying white spaces at district and taluka level; will continue aggressively in September quarter.
items.quote: At the beginning of this fiscal year, we have identified white spaces at a district and taluka level across India. In the June quarter, we have been able to add many new channel partners , and we will continue to do so aggressively in the September quarter.

items.statement: DMS fully in place with complete visibility of secondary sales at retailer level; scheme spends now directly targeted to retailers enabling pull-based demand model.
items.quote: DMS, which is Distributor Management Systems, are now fully in place, and now we have complete visibility and tracking of secondary sales at a retailer level. Our scheme spends ar e now directly targeted to retailers across the country, which has helped us move from a -- move to a pull-based demand model rather than the legacy push-based way of selling.

items.statement: Reaffirmed full-year volume growth guidance of 12%-15% and EBITDA margin guidance of 11%-13%.
items.quote: No. We will stick to our guidance on growth going forward.

items.statement: Revenue from operations stood at INR 609 crores, up 5% YoY.
items.quote: Revenue from operation in this quarter stood at INR 609 crores, a growth of 5% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Volumes degrew 7% YoY to 40,729 metric tons.
items.quote: Our volumes for the quarter stood at 40,729 metric tons , degrew by 7% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 93% YoY to INR 77 crores; EBITDA margin expanded 600 bps to 13%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 77 crores, a growth of 93% Y -o-Y, while margins stood at 13%, registering a 600 basis point growth.

items.statement: PAT grew 580% YoY to INR 34 crores; PAT margin at 6%.
items.quote: Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR 34 crores, a growth of 580% Y-o-Y. PAT margin for the quarter stood at 6%.

items.statement: Working capital days at 71 days; receivable days 40 days; inventory days 100 days as of 30 June 2026.
items.quote: Working capital days stood at 71 days in Q1 FY '27. Receivable days stood at 40 days, whereas inventory days stood at 100 days as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Capex plan unchanged; spent INR 40-42 crores in Q1 mainly on Bhuj plant second tranche completion; rest to flow in next 9 months.
items.quote: For this quarter, around INR 40 crores, INR 42 crores has been spent, and that has primarily been on the completion of second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover. So that is the only thing which has happened. Rest of the capex will flow in next 9 months.

items.statement: Net cash nearly neutral as of 30 June; gross debt around INR 120 crores including long-term and short-term.
items.quote: So net cash is almost neutral on 30th June. I think the gross debt is around INR 120 crores, kind of, including long-term and short-term both.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by better product mix: plumbing/drainage share increased vs agri; CPVC, PPR, PP contribution improved vs PVC.
items.quote: So one is product mix has improved relative to what it usually is from a segmental point of view. That is point #1. And second point is, from a polymer mix as well, CPVC, PPR, PP, these kind of product contribution has improved compared to what it was in the past.

items.statement: CPVC price hikes being passed on in phased manner, typically 1-2 weeks to channel.
items.quote: I think we are passing it on in a phase -wise manner. So usually, we give 1 to 2 weeks to the channel. So we have -- accordingly, we have done it this time as well.

items.statement: April volume washout due to high channel inventory and PVC price correction; strong recovery in May, June and July.
items.quote: April was a blip because of the one -way decrease in PVC prices and high level of channel inventory as of March 31. But if I look at June, July, again, we are back on the growth trajectory.

items.statement: Channel partners resumed normal buying behavior in June-July; MIP provides price floor eliminating uncertainty for distributors.
items.quote: I think in June and July, we saw better stocking from channel partners, which is more reflective of the secondary demand or the last mile demand. And especially now with the MIP in place that really -- that there is no uncertainty of what is the bottom anymore.

items.statement: Larger players consolidating market share; smaller players face raw material insecurity and supply security challenges.
items.quote: My view is that larger players continue to consolidate because in the volatility, a lot of the raw material -- a lot of the smaller players face raw material insecurity. And in our kind of industry, unless your machines are running 365 days, it's very toug h to survive.

items.statement: Added channel partners from both organized and unorganized players driven by stronger demand engine, DMS/SFA enabling faster inventory rotation, not price-driven.
items.quote: I think more is just stronger relationship and a stronger demand engine. Today, more than margin, I think what is important for a distributor is how fa st you can rotate their material, the amount of inventory turns you can offer them in the retail market and because we now have DMS and SFA in place, and a direct control on retailers across the country.

items.statement: Current utilization at 52%-53%; guided 12%-15% volume growth would take utilization to ~60% if capacity static.
items.quote: So as of now, we are at around 52% - 53% kind of utilization. And what we have guided is 13% to 15% of growth in this year, which translates to, if the capacity is static, then we will reach to around 60% of utilization.

items.statement: Inventory days at 100 days vs guidance 65-75 days due to supply insecurity during war and unexpected 7% volume degrowth; expects correction by end of September quarter.
items.quote: Yes. It was 2 parts. One is, of course, we stick to our guidance of 65 to 75 days for inventory. Two things. One, there was supply insecurity during the war time. And second, we did not expect 7% kind of a degrowth. So obviously, there was a sales loss.

items.statement: Debtor days at 40 days in June; target to reduce to 30 days in next couple of years via channel finance and pull-based demand model.
items.quote: So if you see June end, we are at 40 days of debtor days. This is key for us. And as the brand becomes stronger, this has to reduce. Compared to my peers, my debtor days is still higher, and we recognize and acknowledge that.

items.statement: Bathware revenue INR 13 crores, EBITDA loss INR 5 crores in Q1; expects significantly better performance in Q2, INR 25 crores quarterly run rate by Q3 near breakeven.
items.quote: I think in Q2, we should have a much better performance than in Q1. So yes, Q3, I think INR 25 crores is an achievable number if I look at the monthly run rate. So in the December quarter, we should be doing INR 25 crores, which will be very close to break even.

items.statement: Medium-term focus on 11%-13% EBITDA margin with industry-leading growth; long-term margin improvement driven by value-added products like CPVC and new products like DECILO.
items.quote: I think for now, if I look at medium term, I think 11% to 13% kind of operating margin with industry-leading growth should be the focus. Any improvement in margins has to be driven from value-added products like CPVC coming in as well as new products like DECILO.

items.statement: Project vs retail mix broadly similar: 25%-30% project, balance retail.
items.quote: Yes. It would be broadly similar where 25% to 30% would be project and balance would be retail.

items.statement: Sustainable ROCE target 15%-20% historically achieved; expects to reach with volumes, stricter capital allocation.
items.quote: See, it is historically seen, apart from the past few years, 15% to 20%, sometimes even higher than that has been done. And of course, for us, that has to be the -- that is the rule.

items.statement: Internal utilization target 60%-65% on production capacity; above that suggests delayed capex.
items.quote: I mean, typically, 60% to 65% is where we'll hit it. Anything more than that, I fear that we have been late with our capex cycle because at Prince, while, of course, utilization levels are important, one of the reasons why we have been able to reach the scale that we have is that we have been ahead of the curve in adding capacity.

items.statement: No significant inventory gain or loss expected in Q2 due to MIP floor and higher cost cargo from previous month's correction.
items.quote: Actually I would not like to comment on inventory gain or loss right now because we also have -- while the MIP is in place, you also have a higher cost cargo coming in because we did see a correction in month before this month. So I would -- I don't think there will be a significant inventory gain or loss in second quarter.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement in Q2 FY27 and return to year-on-year growth from H2 FY27
items.quote: From here onwards, we expect improvement in Q2FY27 and the return to year-on-year growth from the second half.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expected closer to previous year level in FY27, then accelerate from FY28
items.quote: So Foram we should be looking at a number which will be closer to previous year margin percentage for the current year. And we should thereafter start accelerating from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Restocking order received for commercial molecule providing delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28
items.quote: For one commercial molecule that faced destocking last year, we have now received the restocking order, providing meaningful delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: RFQ pipeline strengthening with Phase 3 KSM commercial supply inquiries from large pharma and Western CDMOs
items.quote: Our RFQ pipeline continued to strengthen during the quarter, supported by many Phase 3 KSM commercial supply inquiries from a large pharma company, along with additional commercial and late-stage inquiries from all the large pharmaceutical customers and Western CDMOs.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 71.5% in Q1 FY27 vs 73% in Q1 FY26 due to mix and lower Pharma CDMO contribution
items.quote: Consolidated gross margin was at 71.5% compared with 73% in Q1 FY26. The decline primarily reflected the product mix and the lower contribution from the high-margin Pharma CDMO business.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 92 million at 2.2% margin in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA was at INR92 million, representing a margin of 2.2%.

items.statement: Standalone business generated INR 3,599 million revenue and INR 332 million adjusted EBITDA at 9.2% margin in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The standalone business generated a revenue of INR3,599 million and adjusted EBITDA of INR332 million, representing a margin of 9.2%.

items.statement: Robust API order book supporting outlook for the year
items.quote: These were largely timing-related factors, and importantly, the underlying demand remains healthy, with a robust API order book supporting our outlook for the year.

items.statement: 10 molecules in Phase 3 pipeline with expectation that more than 50% will get approval
items.quote: On Phase 3, we are in, as indicated, 10 molecules, and we have reloads that are coming on a regular basis. So, of course, some of those molecules may not make it to the market, because they will not get the approval at the end, but, at least, we can expect that more than 50% should get the approval at the end.

items.statement: Capital expenditure approximately INR 598 million in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter was approximately INR598 million as we continue to invest in capabilities required for future growth.

items.statement: Commercial flow reactor at Jaggayyapet site expected ready by next quarter
items.quote: We have recently invested in a commercial flow reactor at our Jaggayyapet site, and it is expected to be ready by next quarter.

items.statement: Operationalized additional GMP manufacturing laboratory at Princeton expanding ability to support small molecule and biologic programs
items.quote: The team also operationalized an additional GMP manufacturing laboratory at Princeton, expanding its ability to support small molecule and biologic programs through Phase 1 and Phase 2 clinical development.

items.statement: Passed on major chunk of raw material cost escalation to customers in API+ business
items.quote: The price increase which happened during the last quarter, largely due to the larger raw material price escalations which we witnessed because of the geopolitical situation, we tried our level best in terms of transferring a decent portion of that increase to our customers.

items.statement: API+ portfolio increasingly focused on niche CNS and controlled substances assets with value chain play across intermediates, APIs, pellets, formulations
items.quote: The portfolio is increasingly focused on niche assets in CNS and controlled substances space, while targeting value maximization through our value chain play across intermediate, APIs, pellets, and formulations.

items.statement: Multiple audits by large innovator partners across Pharma CDMO platform completed without critical findings
items.quote: During Q1FY27, we had multiple audits by large innovator partners across the pharma CDMO platform, including our API manufacturing sites. These audits were completed without any critical findings, reinforcing customer confidence in our operating systems.

items.statement: Secured supply agreement covering selected Middle Eastern markets in formulation business
items.quote: We finalized a supply agreement covering selected Middle Eastern markets.

items.statement: MMAE and Exatecan payload products receiving good traction as market welcomes alternative to Chinese suppliers
items.quote: The recent products added to our portfolio, namely MMAE and Exatecan, are receiving good traction from a market welcoming alternative to Chinese suppliers.

items.statement: USFDA inspection of Pashamylaram facility completed July 27 to August 5, 2026; received Form 483 with five observations, none related to data integrity
items.quote: I also want to add that we have just announced that USFDA has completed an inspection of our Pashamylaram facility, which was conducted from 27th July to 5th August, 2026. Following this, we received a Form 483 with five observations. None of them relate to data integrity.

items.statement: Nacharam remediation and operational stabilization progressing with CAPA implementation in line with plan
items.quote: At Nacharam, the remediation and operational stabilization remains our immediate priority. CAPA implementation continues to progress in line with plan, supported by ongoing engagements with the regulator.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash approximately INR 2,512 million as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains resilient with consolidated net cash of approximately INR2,512 million as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Agreed clear path to full ownership of Sapala by FY30 with Dr. P.Y. Reddy continuing to lead
items.quote: Alongside this, we have also agreed to a clear path to ownership of Sapala, fast-growing and highly profitable business by FY30. Dr. P.Y. Reddy remains invested and will continue to lead the business through this period.

items.statement: CFO Himanshu Agarwal to remain in role until September 13, 2026; succession process underway
items.quote: As you are all aware, Himanshu will remain in his role until 13th September 2026, and we will update you on succession process as it progresses.

items.statement: Commercial OTIF remained at almost 100% year-to-date in Pharma CDMO
items.quote: Our commercial OTIF remained at a very high rate of almost close to 100%.

items.statement: Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As a result, Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1.

items.statement: Biotech funding environment continues to influence timing of customer decisions and FTE renewals at NJ Bio
items.quote: We remain watchful of the biotech funding environment, which continues to influence the timing of customer decisions and FTE renewals.

items.statement: NJ Bio expected to continue affecting consolidated performance until revenue conversion improves
items.quote: Until revenue conversion improves, NJ Bio is expected to continue affecting the consolidated performance in the near term.

items.statement: Expects gross margin to improve by at least 1% year-on-year and settle between 40-42% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are confident of increasing our gross margin at least a percentage year-on-year. Ideally, we would want to get, of course, we want to be above 40%, and we, I think the gross margin should settle between 40% and 42% on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 14-15% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: We believe that we'll be able to grow at least a percentage even on the margin side year-on-year, which will ultimately in the range, in the next two to three years, we should be in the range of 14-15%.

items.statement: Expects export contribution to reach 15% of revenue in next two years
items.quote: As the company grows, we believe even in spite of the growth overall as a company, our export contribution in the next two years, that is the current and the next year, should get to 15%.

items.statement: Targets 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by end of 2027
items.quote: Further, we added 17 new stores under franchise model during the quarter, reinforcing our retail expansion strategy and advancing our long-term objective of establishing 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by the year end 2027.

items.statement: Expects non-induction growth of nearly 20% in coming quarters
items.quote: And our endeavor is to actually take the non-induction growth to nearly 20% if possible, if you are able to do everything right.

items.statement: Expects consistent 15%+ growth across operating categories
items.quote: We are looking at 15% plus going, going across consistently in the categories we are operating in. Given the kind of product development and innovations that we have lined up.

items.statement: Expects Induction Cooktop contribution to be at least 20% of full year revenue
items.quote: We are confident of this, contribution from Induction Cooktop to be in the range of, at least 20% and a little above that as we progress over the year.

items.statement: Induction Cooktop demand remains structurally higher than pre-war levels
items.quote: While the category witnessed extraordinary growth last year, demand continues to remain substantially above pre-war level, indicating a structural shift in consumer adoption rather than a temporary spike.

items.statement: Sees strong consumption across product categories for upcoming festive season
items.quote: We are seeing strong, kind of consumption in various of our product categories, and all the manufacturing facilities that we have set up in the last few quarters are all now up and running.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 127 bps YoY to 39.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR190.4 crores versus INR130.4 crores in Q1 FY26, a growth of 46% year-on-year. Despite ongoing supply chain challenges and elevated raw material costs. Also, gross margins expanded by 127 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 71 bps YoY to 11.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR53.8 crore s in Q1 FY27 compared to INR35.6 crore s in Q1 FY26, registering a robust 50.9% year-on-year. Consequently, EBITDA margins improved to 11.2% from 10.5% in the corresponding period last year, expanding by 71 basis points

items.statement: PAT margin at 3.5% in Q1 FY27, up from 3.1% YoY
items.quote: PAT for Q1 FY27 stood at INR17.1 crore s versus INR10.4 crores in Q1 FY26. Showing exceptional growth of 63.5% year-on-year. The PAT margins for the current quarter stood at 3

items.statement: Triply cookware manufacturing JV in China to be commercially operational by end of calendar year
items.quote: We believe by the end of this calendar year or before December, we'll be able to produc e commercially the circles that are, I mean, triply circles that are required for manufacturing the pressure cookers and cookware

items.statement: Setting up completely automated line for pressure cookers
items.quote: We are setting up a completely automated line for pressure cookers. For triply, we have not even started this. This will be ready, up and ready in the end of third quarter.

items.statement: Augmenting capacity for pressure cookers and small appliances to meet unmet demand
items.quote: But then there is still unmet demand, and so we are addressing it by additional capacities. On the small appliances, we have capacity. In the first quarter, we had to let go some of our, I mean, capacity is being used for some other, when used for Induction and other Infrared products. But we have now augmented those capacities as well.

items.statement: Increased domestic prices and export realizations to pass on input cost inflation
items.quote: We have increased our prices for the domestic market. We also are, there's a favorable situation even in our exports. They have corrected their buying prices upwards to address the input cost.

items.statement: Operates on cost-plus model; passes on input cost increases and targets additional margin
items.quote: Generally, our procurement is linked to the cost for a quarter and our prices to the market are also for a quarter. Other than the exports, we are able to play that very safely. Though we are a brand company, we still are a cost plus. If there is a pressure on i nput cost, we pass it on. But there is also an endeavor to now improve our margins

items.statement: Premiumization driving growth; stainless steel pressure cookers growing faster than aluminium
items.quote: We are seeing a lot of premiumization into various category of products that we are example is our pressure cooker. We have grown higher in our stainless steel pressure cooker versus our aluminium pressure cooker, which also means, I mean, it's the product mix which is contributing.

items.statement: Net working capital at 45 days in Q1 FY27, up from Q4 FY26 due to strategic inventory buildup for festive season
items.quote: From a working capital perspective, the net working capital increased to 45 days in Q1 FY27, which is much better than Q1 FY26 and FY25, but is higher than quarter 4 of FY26. Primarily driven by strat egic inventory buildup undertaken to ensure adequate quality availability, product availability ahead of the upcoming festive season and anticipated demand

items.statement: Targets straight-line production to optimize working capital and supply chain
items.quote: And also we are now going to a straight-line production plan. So irrespective of the cycles that we have over Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, we would want to have uniform p roduction around the year. This optimizes our cost and better supply chain

items.statement: ROCE improved to 13.9% from 12.6% YoY; ROE increased to 9.3% from 8.3% YoY
items.quote: ROCE improved to 13.9% from 12.6%, while ROE increased to 9.3% from 8.3% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Average sales per store at INR4.3 lakhs/month; target INR5 lakhs/month
items.quote: For us, anything beyond the 2.5 lakhs per store is profitable. We are currently trending at about 4.3 lakhs, and ultimately our target is to at least stabilize at 5 lakhs per store per month.

items.statement: Input cost pressures continue; managed through price hikes and efficiency
items.quote: So yes, while, there has been input cost pressure continuing, we have also addressed this by correcting our realization. We have increased our prices for the domestic market. We also are, there's a favorable situation even in our exports. They have corrected their buying prices upwards to address the input cost.

items.statement: Chimney category revamped with BLDC motors; expects substantial growth
items.quote: What we have done is actually revamped the entire range from normal AC motors to BLDC motors, all but one. So that makes us extremely, current and in fact ahead of many of our competitors. And given that we've got our own retail also to drive this, we are very confident that the Chimney business is going to grow quite substantially.

items.statement: Target to reach 300 restaurants by FY27
items.quote: We are committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27, and we'll build our portfolio from there.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR140 crores with INR120 crores for new outlets and INR20 crores for maintenance and ancillary
items.quote: We guided previously capex for full year would be around INR140 crores of which INR120 crores to the new outlet openings and INR20 crores towards the maintenance capex and our ancillary capex.

items.statement: 15 restaurants under construction to operationalize through Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: As of today, we have 15 restaurants that are under construction, and these will operationalize through Q2 and Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Barbeque Nation India TAM increased to around 600 restaurants from earlier 400-450
items.quote: I think at the current scale, the brand, which is Barbeque Nation India can take it up to around 600-odd restaurants.

items.statement: Consolidated same-store sales growth 28.7% in Q1 FY27, entirely volume-led with no price increases
items.quote: Consolidated same-store sales growth was 28.7% on top of the 14.4% we delivered in Q4 FY26. Our growth continues to be entirely volume led. We have not taken any price increase during Q1.

items.statement: Dine-in transaction volumes grew 63.5% year-on-year in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consolidated dine-in transaction volumes grew 63.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin improved to 8.1% in Q1 FY27, up 350 bps year-on-year
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin for Q1 came in at 8.1%, which was around 350 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Mature restaurant operating margin reached 16.2% in Q1 FY27, up 290 bps year-on-year
items.quote: Q1 FY27 matured portfolio Pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin came in at 16.2%. This was again around 290 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Back-end cost as percentage of sales reduced from 7.1% in Q4 FY26 to 6.5% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our back-end cost as a percentage of sales have reduced from 7.1% in Q4 FY26 to 6.5% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: No price increases taken in Q1 FY27; average per cover spend reflects mix changes and value-led initiatives
items.quote: We have not taken any price increase during Q1, and our average per coverage spend continues to reflect changes in business segment mix, daypart and session mix and value-led initiatives that we started from Q2 FY26.

items.statement: International gross margin impacted by 30-40% commodity price inflation due to Middle East geopolitical crisis
items.quote: In some cases, we are seeing commodity prices going up by almost 30% -40%.

items.statement: Barbeque India growing faster than International and Premium CDR, creating mix drag on consolidated gross margin
items.quote: Barbeque India, which is at a lower gross margin than, let's say, International and premium CDR is today growing faster than the other 2 segments and it is bringing the consolidated gross margin down.

items.statement: Monthly active users on digital platform grew ~60% year-on-year to ~1.4 million; captive channels contribute 65% of Barbeque India dine-in transactions
items.quote: Our monthly active users on our digital platform have grown to approximately 1.4 million, which is up by almost 60% year-on-year. Our captive digital ecosystem contributes to 65% of overall Barbeque India dine-in transactions, up from around 61% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Repeat rate ~45-47%; new vs repeat customer ratio shifting slightly in favor of new customers
items.quote: Typically, on any particular period, our repeat business is approximately 45% to 47% and the balance is new customers. And during this period of intervention, we're also seeing that our ratio of new versus repeat is actually shifting slightly in favor of new customers.

items.statement: Delivery business grew 62% year-on-year in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our delivery business also continued its excellent trajectory growing 62% year-on-year.

items.statement: Net debt increased marginally from INR102 crores at end FY26 to INR106 crores at end Q1 FY27 due to capex investment
items.quote: Our net debt position has moved marginally up from INR102 crores at the end of FY26 to INR106 crores at the end of Q1 FY27. This is marginally higher due to the investment that we have made in our capex and also the ongoing pipeline that we have.

items.statement: Average revenue per mature restaurant increased to around INR7 crores
items.quote: Our average revenue per mature restaurants have now increased to around INR7 crores.

items.statement: International restaurant operating margin 18.7% in Q1 FY27, up 22% year-on-year despite food inflation
items.quote: Gross profit grew 40.3% and pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margins grew year-on-year by 22% with restaurant operating margins of 18.7%.

items.statement: Premium CDR mature restaurants delivering operating margins upwards of 20%
items.quote: Our mature prem ium CDR restaurant continue to deliver restaurant operating margins of upwards of 20

items.statement: Invested in back-end capabilities: added culinary team from 5-star hotels, beefed up marketing, brand, digital, tech teams
items.quote: We ha ve beefed up our culinary team. We have a new Chief Culinary Officer joining. Under them, we have created regional spocs for our culinary heads. We earlier had spots for operations, but not entirely for culinary. We have built in approximately 4 senior people all joining us from 5 -star h otels with good culinary backgrounds with an experience of around 20 years

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected to moderate in FY27 due to higher comparable base, not demand change
items.quote: We are conscious that the same-store sales growth will moderate as we move through FY27. This again, is more mathematics than our comment on demand. Our comparable base tightens meaningfully as we move through the year with Q3 FY27 and Q4 lapping on to our strongest quarter of FY26.

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical crisis causing food inflation impacting International gross margin
items.quote: This is mainly due to the impact of higher food inflation for a large part of our input categories. While this is linked to the ongoing and uncertain geopolitical crisis, we're taking 5 | United Foodbrands Limited United Foodbrands Limited Earnings Call Transcript Q1 FY27 efforts to reduc e the impact of this in

items.statement: Expansion funded largely through internal accruals; borrowings kept at prudent levels
items.quote: We'll continue to fund expansion largely from internal accruals, and we'll keep the borrowings at prudent levels related to the underlying business profile that we have.

items.statement: Expects to outperform underlying automotive industry by 1.5x to 2x in FY27
items.quote: Given our current b usiness visibility, healthy order pipeline, and execution capabilities, we continue to expect SJS to outperform the underlying automotive industry by 1.5x to 2x in FY27

items.statement: Targets export contribution of 14%-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28
items.quote: We continue to focus on scaling our export business and remain committed to achieving export contribution of 14 %-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28

items.statement: Aims to double SJS Decoplast sales in next 3-4 years
items.quote: So, what we mentioned was that we hope to double sales in the next 3 to 4 years. So, that is the plan that we have internally in the company.

items.statement: Aspires to capture at least 10% of Indian display market by 2030
items.quote: Our aspiration is to be at least 10% of the market by 2030. That is our internal wish list, which we are working towards.

items.statement: Indian automotive industry grew 21.7% YoY in Q1FY27; SJS automotive business grew 32.4% YoY
items.quote: In Q1FY27, the combined passenger vehicle and two-wheeler industry recorded a year-on-year growth of 21.7%, while SJS automotive business grew by 32.4%, outperforming the industry by approximately 1.5 times.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 239 bps YoY to 30% in Q1FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 799.6 mn, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 36.2%, with EBITDA margin expanding by 239 bps to 30%.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 0.1% QoQ to 56.7% in Q1FY27
items.quote: So, the gross margin on quarter-on-quarter, I mean, Quarter 4 was 56.6%. And now we are 56.7%. If you see it, it is actually increasing by 0.1%.

items.statement: Higher input costs impacted profitability by 0.5%-0.6% this quarter
items.quote: That would be somewhere between 0.5% to 0.6%.

items.statement: Secured new orders from Mahindra, Tata Motors, TVS, Autoliv, Royal Enfield, Skoda, John Deere, Hero MotoCorp in Q1FY27
items.quote: The company also secured new orders from leading customers, including Mahindra and Mahindra, Tata Motors, TVS, Aut oliv, Royal Enfield, Skoda, John Deere, Hero MotoCorp, amongst others, during the quarter

items.statement: New SJS Decoplast facility in Pune commenced commercial operations in August 2026
items.quote: In August 2026, we also commenced commercial operations of the new SJS Decoplast manufacturing facility in Pune, further expanding our manufacturing capacity and creating additional capacity to support future customer programs and business growth.

items.statement: New Decoplast facility adds Rs. 200-250 crore additional revenue capacity
items.quote: And B - this new capacity will add close to about 200 crs to 250 crs of additional revenue.

items.statement: Expects 85-90% utilization at new Decoplast facility within 3 years
items.quote: Regarding utilization ratio, we already have explained in the current call that in a period of three years, one can expect to reach at a level of 85%-90%.

items.statement: Walter Pack India operating at ~75% utilization; no immediate capex planned
items.quote: As of now, the Walter Pack is operating around 75%. We are developing a couple of business there. So, we have the capacity available there. So, as of immediate basis, there is no further capex.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases typically passed through to customers with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: Somewhere we have a lag for one quarter, or maybe two quarters. But we were able to maintain our gross margin with the lot of operational efficiency and the export and also the richer product mix.

items.statement: New generation products contributed ~24% of consolidated revenue in Q1FY27
items.quote: New generation products contributed approximately 24% of consolidated revenue during Q1FY27.

items.statement: Revenue mix: PV 44.6%, 2W 36.6%, Consumer Appliances & Others 18.8% in Q1FY27
items.quote: Our revenue mix remained well diversified, with passenger vehicle contributing 44.6%, two-wheelers 36.6% and consumer appliances and others forming 18.8% of consolidated revenue.

items.statement: SDPL won new business with Tata Motors; Walter Pack won new business with Mahindra
items.quote: SDPL won new businesses with Tata Motors, while Walter Pack won new businesses with Mahindra, underlining our strategy of increasing cross-selling opportunities going ahead.

items.statement: Exclusivity with BOE for four-wheeler displays; Pricol-BOE tie-up limited to two-wheelers
items.quote: They are only for two-wheelers. We have exclusivity for four-wheelers.

items.statement: In-house R&D Centre received DSIR recognition from Government of India
items.quote: Further reinforcing our commitment to innovation, our in-house R&D Centre received recognition from the Department of Science and Industrial Research, DSIR, the Government of India.

items.statement: Exports grew 83.2% YoY to Rs. 255.8 mn, contributing 9.8% of consolidated revenue in Q1FY27
items.quote: Exports continued to gain traction during the quarter, growing by 83.2% year-on-year to Rs. 255.8 mn and contributing 9.8% of consolidated revenue.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations at Rs. 809 mn (101.2% of EBITDA); free cash flow Rs. 838 mn in Q1FY27
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for the quarter stood at Rs. 809 mn, which is 101.2% of EBITDA, and we generated free cash flow of Rs. 838 mn.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs. 3,287.7 mn as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026 stood at Rs. 3,380.8 mn, resulting in a net cash position of Rs. 3,287.7 mn.

items.statement: Board approved wholly-owned subsidiary for cover glass and display business
items.quote: The Board has approved setting up a wholly-owned subsidiary for the cover glass and display business.

items.statement: Acquired remaining stake in Walter Pack India, making it 100% wholly-owned subsidiary
items.quote: Furthermore, the acquisition of the remaining stake in Walter Pack India, making it a 100% wholly-owned subsidiary, will enable greater operational alignment, enhanced technology integration with improved execution capabilities.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE at 37.2% and annualized ROE at 20.3% in Q1FY27
items.quote: Despite continued investments, we have maintained a robust returns ratio, with annualized ROCE at 37.2% and annualized ROE at 20.3%.

items.statement: Non-compete with Walter Pack Spain expires January 2027; may enable global competition
items.quote: We have an agreement with Walter Pack Spain on non-compete till January of 2027. At that point in time, we will take a call what we need to do.

items.statement: Cover glass and display plant equipment on order; supplies expected from Q2 FY28
items.quote: Equipment is on order. It will be shipped and installed. And sales out of this new plant will come in Q2 of next year. This is what is for FY28.

items.statement: Paisabazaar EBITDA expected at ~₹50 Cr for FY27 vs earlier ₹100 Cr estimate
items.quote: I don't think it'll be ₹100 Cr. I think we'll be, maybe, at about half of that.

items.statement: Insurance premium grew 41% YoY to ₹8,372 Cr; new health and term grew 53% YoY
items.quote: The overall insurance premium, is now at ₹8,372 Cr, it's grown at 41% year -on-year. Importantly, this growth continues to be led by the protection categories, which is our focus. New health and term insurance grew at 53%.

items.statement: Renewal revenue grew 55% to ₹1,003 Cr LTM; renewals growth expected >50% for some time
items.quote: While our renewal revenue has grown at 55% to ₹1,003 Cr for the last 12 months, but now we're getting to a stage when you will see higher and higher growth in renewals.

items.statement: Core credit disbursals grew 33% YoY to ₹4,366 Cr; credit revenue grew 25%
items.quote: The total credit disbursa l is now at ₹4,366 Cr for the quarter. The business continues to focus on customers with all different credit profiles

items.statement: Top 100 partners contribute 16% of PB Partners premium; aim to reduce concentration
items.quote: Our top 100 partners' share of premium is 16%. We will furth er work actively in reducing this

items.statement: Hired 5,000 people gross in Q1; expanding marketing (Amitabh Bachchan tie-up)
items.quote: We hired, at a gross level, 5,000 people in Q1. That explains to you how much we are trying to reduce cost. Because most of those 5,000 will not be productive in Q1, for sure.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense 15% of PB Partners revenue (12% in Q4 due to seasonality)
items.quote: The share of employee benefit expenses was about 15% of the revenue for the quarter. It was 12% in the previous quarter, but that is because it was seasonally a bigger quarter.

items.statement: Waiver of Premium (WOP) >60% of savings business in some centers in July; GIFT City dollar plans growing
items.quote: In domestic business, in some centers, it has crossed 60% n ow in July. I think WOP is the dominant story, and we are quite encouraged by that

items.statement: Online B2C: 65-70% from Tier 2/3 cities (ex-top 10); South growing faster than North/West
items.quote: Tier 2, Tier 3 now, depending on the business, on the direct side, account for somewhere between 65% and 70% of the business, and this part is growing faster than the bigger cities.

items.statement: COR model aligned with quality over volume; well received by insurers and platform
items.quote: The COR model is really around that stuff, and I think directionally, I would say it is well received, and so far, it's going in the right direction.

items.statement: Regulator defines broker as highest effort channel; effort visible in marketing, conversion, claims support
items.quote: Legally, as defined by the regulator, the largest amount of effort in any sale needs to be put by a broker, more than any other channel. And that is as legally defined, in terms of tasks to be undertaken, by the regulator.

items.statement: Dark patterns allegation: mobile number collection not deceptive; global comparators also collect numbers

items.statement: Paisabazaar contribution margin 41%; operating break-even achieved in Q1
items.quote: Paisabazaar business has just broken even on the operating basis. On the contribution side, it's 41%. So it's pretty much as high as Policybazaar on the contribution side.

items.statement: AI touches 30-40% of 10 Cr monthly customer interactions; 20-30% auto-handled in service
items.quote: Roughly we handle 10 Cr customer interactions in a month, calls, emails, etc, etc. Of those 10 Cr, 30-40% are now being touched by AI, and that number is growing.

items.statement: Supreme Court TP extension: brand new ticket sizes up; enforcement could drive meaningful jump

items.quote: Our UAE insurance premium grew 31% year-on-year for this quarter. Most of what we do is health and life insurance, similar to evolution of our India business.

items.statement: Targets mid-double-digit revenue growth for FY27, split between ASP and volume; confident of 17-19% EBITDA margin band

items.statement: Targets 90-100 new EBO store openings in FY27 after accelerated Q1 pace

items.statement: Q1 volume growth 11.7% despite price hikes; expects high single-digit volume growth for full year
items.quote: we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right?

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin stable at 15.9%; confident of delivering 17-19% full-year margin band
items.quote: Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.

items.statement: Shut 4-5 million pairs of DIP capacity; Stuck-On capacity strong; new Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar facilities commissioned
items.quote: So, we had basically 4 million to 5 million capacity of DIP that we sort of shut down because it is a very old, archaic technology and very like cheaper economical price points, wh ich were not viable for us

items.quote: We have moved this entire business from DIP to Stuck-On, which has a much better ASP and is a margin-accretive category versus DIP.

items.statement: Launched Elan by Campus in neo-casual segment (Rs 1,899-2,599); selling in 100-110 own stores plus online; initial response extremely positive
items.quote: Elan is almost a two-month-old launch now, and it is doing extremely well. It is selling currently in about 100 or 110 of our own stores, as well as actively selling on Amazon, Myntra, and our own brand.com.

items.statement: Transitioned 158 franchise stores from outright to SOR model; added 8-9 new master franchise partners; franchise ROI 18-30%
items.quote: We have also transitioned over the last three months our entire franchise business from an outright business based model to an SOR model where we control the entire inventory and discounting of these products.

items.statement: Proactively built inventory ahead of festive season; inventory under control; distributor meet provided strong production visibility
items.quote: we have been able to build the right sort of products. We already had the indication of the distributor meet, which gave a very strong visibility on what we need to produce ahead of the curve.

items.statement: Unorganized players facing production constraints due to working capital stress; industry-wide price hikes make new pricing the norm
items.quote: there were production constraints that we are able to find that happen to some smaller or unorganized places as well because, of course, the cost of the working capital gets under stress.

items.statement: Sneaker portfolio targeting ~30% volume growth in FY27; women and kids portfolio showing exceptional momentum
items.quote: We are looking, since the scale is now getting bigger, this year we are looking at a close to 30% growth on this category.

items.quote: there has also been a proportionate increase in costs with respect to HR like employee cost and the other SG&A which Neeraj just called out. So, HR also like there is actually an element of like 10%.

items.quote: Around 8% that's a -- I mean 7.5% to 8% is easily achievable, looking at the current trend.

items.statement: Plan to open 25-30 stores in FY27 across existing clusters and West Bengal
items.quote: we plan to open around 25-30 stores in existing geographies as well as in Bengal for that matter.

items.quote: we're looking at anywhere between 8 to 10 stores. Two are opening this week only. One in Saket and one in Gurgaon, 3 to 4 stores are getting constructed as we talk.

items.statement: Short-term debt reduced drastically; expansion funded through internal accruals

items.quote: Yes, we probably start adding from Q4 of this financial year. It is already under commissioning right now, and our trials will start from Q3 onwards.

items.quote: Commercial vehicle is around 7% . Passenger vehicle is around 8 % of our revenues. Farm equipment is around 5%. Off-highway is again 5%, and industrial is 9%.

items.statement: Container freight costs increased from $2,000 to ~$6,000; company absorbs ~15-20% incremental cost despite 75% pass-through
items.quote: You're right, the cost of, you know, container has gone up from roughly from USD2,000 to almost USD6,000, and a large part of it, the contract that we have, it's kind of a pass-through, or it is around 75% pass -through.
