Despite these headwinds, we remained focused on protecting customer relationships, ensuring continuity of supply, and effectively passing on the price increase, which will largely offset the input cost impact in Q2.

items.statement: SAM customer qualification funnel: 21 at lab validation, 16 at pilot-scale, 7 at pre-commercial/commercial validation with active off-take discussions
items.quote: Today, 21 customers are at the laboratory validation stage, 16 customers have progressed to pilot-scale evaluation, and 7 customers have successfully completed pre-commercial or commercial validation and are currently engaging in active off-take discussions.

items.statement: Signed two additional strategic MOUs with leading South Korean cathode active material manufacturers and their cell manufacturing partners
items.quote: During the quarter, we also signed two additional strategic MOUs with leading South Korean cathode active material manufacturers and their respective cell manufacturing partners, further strengthening our commercial pipeline.

items.statement: SAM Phase 1 construction on schedule; all major long-lead equipment deliveries expected by October; statutory approvals progressing per schedule
items.quote: Construction remains on schedule, and we continue to target commissioning of Phase 1 by April 2027. Deliveries of all major long-lead equipment are expected to be completed this October, while statutory approvals continue to progress in line with our project schedule.

items.statement: Greenfield facility at Navsari approved for food and nutrition; FDA approval expected this quarter; five food nutra customers approving site; supplies expected from Q3
items.quote: The facility has already been approved to supply into the food and nutrition category, and is currently under also undergoing FDA approval, which we expect in this quarter itself. And we have also received five customers of – five, food nutra customers are also currently approving the facility, three of which are from India, and two are global MNCs that are currently approving the site. We expect

items.statement: Specialty ingredients facilities operated at significantly lower utilization in April and first half of May due to LPG shortage; production now normalized
items.quote: During this period, our facilities operated at significantly lower utilization levels with production affected by the limited availability of LPG. We subsequently secured supplies, albeit at higher costs, enabling us to progressively restore normal operating levels.

items.statement: Optimum capacity utilization for business between 70% and 75% depending on product mix
items.quote: Optimum utilization is between 70% and 75% depending on the product mix that we are running.

items.statement: Phosphate price pass-through largely happening in Q2; marginal benefit in Q1
items.quote: So, I think a lot of the pass-through has happened later in Q1, so I would say marginal benefit or kind of we would have received in Q1, but in Q2, majority of the sales would happen with the pass-through.

items.statement: Pharma and food nutrition segment 69% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 66% in Q1 FY26; specialty ingredients 31%
items.quote: The pharma and food nutrition segment continued to be primary revenue contributor for this quarter, accounting for 69% of Q1 FY '27 revenue compared to 66% in Q1 FY '26. Specialty ingredient contributed 31%, indicating a balanced and diverse product portfolio.

items.statement: NSS new business head initiated approvals with five customers across infant nutrition and dairy segments; active pipeline of 12 customer projects
items.quote: Since our new business head joined in June, we have initiated approvals with five customers across the infant nutrition and dairy segments and have built an active pipeline of 12 customer projects.

items.statement: Two large North American customer approvals received for bisglycinate; scaling up supplies behind schedule
items.quote: we are currently seeing or we have received two very important approvals from two large -- two very large customers in the North American market. Currently, we are scaling up our supplies to them. We are behind schedule in terms of

items.statement: Chinese Decree No. 837 increases complexity for Chinese companies establishing manufacturing outside China; reinforces strategic importance of non-China suppliers
items.quote: Recent regulatory developments in China, including Decree No. 837, are expected to further increase the complexity for Chinese companies seeking to establish manufacturing presence outside China and achieve FEOC compliance, as such structures now require g overnment approval for any divestment or reduction of equity in overseas Chinese -owned plants. This further reinforces the strategic importanc

items.statement: Europe, North America, and MENA region meaningfully contributed to growth; international markets carry stronger margin profile from value-added products
items.quote: From a geographic perspective, Europe, North America, and the MENA region meaningfully contributed to growth this quarter. Importantly, these international markets continue to carry a stronger margin profile, supported by an increasing contribution from differentiated and value-added products.

items.statement: Asset turns for battery at scale and greenfield at scale expected between 2.7x and 3x
items.quote: I would say for battery at scale and greenfield at scale, I would say closer to between 2.7 x and closer to 3x is where we would be the asset turns would sit.

items.statement: NSS facing challenging European environment due to energy crisis impacting key infant formula customer in Ireland; expect flattish FY27 with single-digit growth
items.quote: Due to the current energy crisis, that customer has scaled down operation significantly in Ireland, which is kind of -- while we have POs, they've delayed the buying. I would say FY'27 continues to -- they may have a more like a flattish year with, I would say, maybe single-digit growth.

items.statement: Welcomed Mr. Milin Mehta to Board of Directors with experience in business strategy, finance, and corporate governance
items.quote: We are also delighted to welcome Mr. Milin Mehta to our Board of Directors. Mr. Mehta brings with him extensive experience in business strategy, finance, and corporate governance.

items.statement: Conservative FY30 targets of Rs 500 crore revenue and Rs 65 crore PAT, with hope to surpass
items.quote: By FY30, you have guided or you are saying that project FY30 revenue and PAT to be 500 crores and 65 crores respectively. Right? Ashutosh Goenka: That is a conservative figure. We should be able to achieve this

items.statement: Core garment EBITDA margin turned positive at 3.4% in Q1 FY27 vs negative last year; targeting pre-tariff levels
items.quote: Our core EBITDA margin i.e. the garment business alone excluding our other income, turned positive at about 3.4% against a marginally negative number in the same quarter last year and we see further room for normalization towards our historical level.

items.statement: Top 5 clients contribute ~70% of revenue; top 10 above 95%; total 12-20 active customers
items.quote: think it will be about 70% concentrated in the top 5 clients. Rhea Patel: Top 5. Okay. And what about the top 10? Ashutosh Goenka: The rest would be above 95%. Because we have, I think at any point of time, anywhere between 12 to 20 customers at the

items.statement: Geopolitical risk mitigated via Sri Lanka MOU for contract manufacturing and potential own plants in Nepal/Vietnam/Sri Lanka for country-of-origin flexibility
items.quote: We are also looking to put up our own plants outside India to hedge geopolitical risks against one single country. We can give the customers an option of producing in different countries with different country of origin products.

items.statement: Effectively debt-free with borrowings under Rs 1 crore; cash, bank balances and investments ~Rs 80 crore
items.quote: We are effectively debt-free with borrowings of under Rs. 1 crore and we held cash bank balances and investments of approximately Rs. 80 crores at the last balance sheet day.

items.statement: Shifting small portion of business to Landed Duty Paid (LDP) model for higher realization; accepting higher working capital for margin premium
items.quote: This is just to give the customers an additional service. And like you said, we will get a reasonably good margin because it gives the customer a lot of flexibility in their inventory. So, people are willing to pay. Of course, that is a very small portion of our business

items.statement: D2C brand launch put on hold due to patent issues with SHORTSTOP; was in test marketing phase
items.quote: We have already entered it as a test marketing phase. And unfortunately, we ran into some patent issues with SHORTSTOP. So, for the time being, since we have not invested much in the brand and our test marketing was not very far ahead, we put that on hold as of now until we are able to sort out this patent issue.

items.statement: Awaiting India-UK and India-EU FTAs operationalization (expected Q1 CY27); India-US FTA uncertain; conservative guidance reflects this
items.quote: The European FTA will hopefully get operational in the 1st Quarter of calendar year 27. The US, we have been hearing contradicting reports for the past two months on a daily basis. So, we have actually kept these things in mind and kept a conservative target.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; family-led with Ashutosh Goenka (CMD), Shubhang Goenka (WTD), Vivek Bahety (CFO)
items.quote: We have with us today Mr. Ashutosh Goenka – Chairman and Managing Director of the company. Also joining us today is Mr. Shubhang Goenka – Executive Non-Independent Whole- Time Director. Ms. Kanchan Rathi – Company Secretary. Mr. Vivek Bahety – Chief Financial Officer

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and aims to maintain margins at ~14% standalone and 12-13% consolidated
items.quote: And in terms of overall margins for FY27, we should do despite with all the changes and volatility, we remain fairly confident to maintain at about, I think, 14% on standalone, and approximately 12%-13% on con sole basis

items.statement: July revenue showed significant growth vs April-June; August-September also look good with surplus demand from institutional pipe negotiations
items.quote: We have registered already positive revenue growth in July as against April to June, significant revenue growth here. And August and September also seem to be good, but especially we think with the kind of negotiations we are doing also with the institutional customers for larger diameter pipes, we see a lot m ore kind of surplus demand coming through

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin down ~2% YoY to ~11% consolidated due to unabsorbed fixed costs from lower volumes; Hi-Tech margin fell from 16.6% to 14.4%
items.quote: EBITDA margins are down by about 2% or so, but mostly linked to unabsorbed fixed costs, which can be captured in the second half, and adjusted PAT has remained profitable.

items.statement: Project billing was ~Rs 24 cr in Q1; one large Pune water supply project has triple-digit billing remaining; other projects have ~Rs 40-50 cr left
items.quote: In the other projects apart from the one project in Pune, I think total billing left is about approximately closer to Rs. 40-50 crores only.

items.statement: Rs 690 cr NCDs due this fiscal (Rs 230 cr in Sep, rest in Mar); management confident of repayment via internal accruals, legacy receivable collections, asset monetization, and refinancing
items.quote: This year, with about Rs. 690 crores of debt of the NCDs falling due in the current fiscal, partly in September, par tly in March, approximately Rs. 230 crores in September, and rema inder in March of that Rs. 690 crores

items.statement: Food business IPO delayed due to market valuation decline; PE investor is patient; may be seriously looked at by September as market improves
items.quote: And I think as we go along, as we move forward for September, as the market improves, that something would be seriously looked at.

items.statement: Majority of polymer price increases passed to customers; demand expected to spur when polymer prices decline further
items.quote: In terms of structurally speaking, while the polyme r prices went up, we have been able to pass on majority of the increases to the customers. And if and when prices of polymers do come back, we think that would spur overall demand into the

items.statement: Chose to forgo Rs 50-60 cr of government-subsidized micro-irrigation sales to avoid long receivables and protect cash flow
items.quote: Otherwise, I think this revenue negative growth, what you see would have been actually covered, because e asily we could have sold 50-60 crores rupees more of micro-irrigation, but that would have meant many more longer receivables

items.statement: No material write-offs expected on project receivables; provisions already made; targeting minimum Rs 380 cr collection from legacy govt receivables in remaining 9 months
items.quote: I think our target this year was about Rs. 422 cror es to be received. Rs. 60 crores we already received in the 1st Quarter. And so, remainder of nine months minimum, and this I am talking minimum, target is Rs. 380 crores will come from that in total

items.statement: Biochar plant recently started using agri waste (corn cob, cotton stalk, mango stones) to create soil conditioner and carbon credits; revenue impact from next fiscal
items.quote: You will start seeing because project has recently started any impact on numbers from the next fiscal.

items.statement: Hi-Tech retail business de-grew 17% YoY (MIS -16%, tissue culture -10%); solar pump seasonality to drive growth from September
items.quote: So, if I break up that 22% reduction in revenue, the re tail business, which would cover the MIS, the tissue culture, solar, etc., that de- grew by about 17

items.statement: Tamil Nadu land monetization delayed by elections; expected to close in current quarter with lender coordination
items.quote: In terms of the Tamil Nadu land, it got delayed somewhat. And I think maybe I referred to it, it was also ele ctions there in April, May, which took place. But it is certainly h appening. Again, we are working with lenders, and I think that should get hopefully delivered in the current quarter

items.statement: Beverage business added ~Rs 60 cr revenue in Q1; overseas plastic business grew ~40% YoY
items.quote: The beverage, your qu estion was that we did approximately Rs. 60 crores into the fo od business in April to June quarter into that business

items.statement: Geopolitical stability and oil/polymer price stability needed to trigger full demand recovery; monsoon progress positive for Rabi and next summer
items.quote: Now, subject to a little bit more stability on the geopolitical events, where oil sta bilizes and the polymer prices come down a little bit more than whe re they are, I think that would give that trigger momentum for the growth into the

items.statement: Dividend expected from FY28 once NCDs repaid and standalone India business becomes debt-free except working capital
items.quote: I think from next year, you will start seeing the dividend, which will come from positive cash flow, which will go into the growth of the company.

items.statement: Targets 8-10% top-line growth per quarter for next couple of years, assuming industry grows 6-7%
items.quote: you can assume from all the businesses put together, we are looking at between 8% to 10% growth, quarter-on-quarter. That is the number we are looking.

items.statement: Consumer products EBIT margin improved to 3.9% from -1.7% YoY driven by gross margin expansion and operating leverage
items.quote: Our EBIT margin has expanded to 3.9% versus negative 1.7% on a year-to-year basis. This is primarily driven by expansion in our gross margin and efficiency generated on account of operating leverage.

items.statement: Overall EBIT margin improved to 6.6% from 2.5% YoY reflecting cost discipline, value engineering and agile pricing
items.quote: The 6.6% EBIT margin is very satisfying for us. It reflects that the growth we delivered this quarter was earned through cost discipline, value engineering, and agile pricing, actions that we have taken to offset commodity inflation.

items.statement: Lighting solutions margin temporarily impacted by legacy professional lighting contracts; expects return to double-digit margins in a quarter or two
items.quote: So, that is getting reflected in the overall lighting business margin. But we believe in a quarter or two as we exit some of these legacy contracts, we will build back our margins. So, we see it a temporary blip in our margin journey.

items.statement: Consumer products EBIT margin expected to stabilize at 6-7% for next two years, then steady improvement toward 10%
items.quote: so we do see our margins for next two years to stabilize between six to 7%. Because we would like to, at the same time, invest a bit more behind our brands. But once we have strengthen ed our brands and the scale is coming, we will then build our margins further

items.statement: Consumer products grew 1.7% YoY after multiple quarters of decline; non-summer categories and Morphy Richards grew double-digit while cooling contracted
items.quote: consumer products growing at 1.7% after a decline for multiple quarters, and lighting solutions grew at 4.4%.

items.statement: Lighting solutions grew 4.4% YoY on strong base, fueled by double-digit growth in consumer lighting
items.quote: Lighting solutions continue to be the vertical carrying momentum for us. Following a year in which it delivered one of the strongest growth in the industry, a 4.4% growth in this quarter on the top of that stronger base is a credible continuation.

items.statement: BLDC fan contribution growing faster than industry; company slightly under-indexed at 30-35% industry estimate but gaining share
items.quote: So, the estimates which we have on BLDC vary between 30% to 35%. We are slightly under-indexed versus the industry, but it is growing much faster and we will be in our rightful share as we progress.

items.statement: Premiumization progressing well with increasing BLDC and premium portfolio contribution in fans
items.quote: Over a period of time, the BLDC contribution has continued to increase and so has the premium contribution. I am happy to say that from a premiumization point of view, our journey is going well.

items.statement: Market share stable or growing in most categories except fans where share loss is being addressed with corrective actions to claw back in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: The one category which is large where we have, as we explained earlier, we have not done as well as we want to is fans. This is where we are losing share. We know why we are losing share and we have corrective actions in place. So, we intend to claw back on our share loss in next two or three quarters.

items.statement: E-commerce contributes ~15% of sales (15-18% range), grew double-digit; alternate channels (e-com, modern trade, exports) together ~45%
items.quote: E-commerce contributes to approximately 15%. And again, depends on quarter-to-quarter, depending on the festive or the sale events, which the e-commerce players do. But on an average, it is around 15%, which is in line with the industry. Alternate business contributes in all put together around 45%.

items.statement: Quick commerce is 8-10% of e-commerce business and growing rapidly though still small
items.quote: Within that, the quick commerce space within e-commerce is growing rapidly and is approximately 8% to 10% of the total e-commerce business. But it is growing rapidly, but it is early days.

items.statement: Direct distribution model being accelerated in parts of South and West; bulk of business still through distributor channel
items.quote: In certain markets, we have already started kicking off our direct model where it is required. So, we have direct dealers, which we are now reaching out to in parts of South, in parts of West. And going forward, we will probably accelerate, depending on the geography, our direct distribution model.

items.statement: Cost inflation 6-10% across categories (up to 13% in coolers); managed through selective price hikes and savings, no major price increases needed for rest of year at this stage
items.quote: See, across the categories, we have seen around, depends on each category, but let us say ranging from 6% to 10%, this is the kind of number we have seen. And where raw material inflation has been significant, we have taken selective price correction depending on category elasticity and competitive intensity.

items.statement: Working capital improved on debtors side; inventories slightly up due to seasonal stocking, overall hovering around 50-60 days
items.quote: On the overall inventories, however, slightly up. And the reason for that is because we have locked ourselves in some good inventories. This is a seasonal period, so we have increased slightly over there. But normally, broadly, it is in the range. And it is largely hovering around between 50-60 days.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative in Q1 due to tax compliances on Morphy Richards acquisition (TDS and GST); otherwise healthy
items.quote: So, see, overall cash flow has been negative. The larger reason for that is because of some of the tax compliances we had to make on the Morphy acquisitions to the TDS, as well as on the GST. So, hence, it has been negative. But other than that, it has largely been healthy.

items.statement: Wires business (part of lighting segment) progressing better than expected, giving confidence for significant future role
items.quote: All that I can say that in wires, our progress is better than what we were expecting. And that gives us confidence that it can play a significant role moving forward to our business.

items.statement: New CGO hired to drive expansion into new categories like solar, cables and beyond current consumer products and lighting portfolio over 3-5 years
items.quote: And there are more areas when we see around, and we see that there are possibilities, we as a company to expand. For obvious reason, it is still at a very early stage to share. But this is exactly the job the person who will come will do.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility remains a risk; pricing decisions will be assessed based on commodity movements
items.quote: As regards to future, see, the external environment continues to remain volatile. And we will assess the impacts before taking any pricing decisions. But at this point in time, we are assessing, we will have to see how the commodity prices move.

items.statement: Competition intensifying but market expanding; not expected to impact medium-to-long-term share except in fans where corrective actions underway
items.quote: While we have one brand Bajaj, but we have another brand Morphy Richards, which is the right space in terms of when the people premiumize, this is one of the brands which we gain. So, therefore, we do see many levers coming in as we get our act together. And we don't think and that is not our play, that our share will be questioned.

items.statement: Overall revenue grew 2.3% YoY in Q1 FY27 with consumer products at 1.7% and lighting solutions at 4.4%
items.quote: We have started delivering top-line growth with meaningful margin expansion. As the Chairman mentioned, our overall revenue grew by 2.3% year-on-year in Quarter 1, with consumer products growing at 1.7% after a decline for multiple quarters, and lighting solutions grew at 4.4%.

items.statement: Supply chain challenges in fans due to gas shortages and PCB constraints from war; gas restored, PCB planning extended for BLDC demand
items.quote: So, that was more induced due to external factors like war and we had challenges both in terms of gas shortages and to some extent PCBs.

items.statement: Geographically weak in South markets, strongest in East; focusing on both numeric reach and counter share expansion
items.quote: So, from a geographical point of view, we are a little weak in the South markets and we are the strongest in East.

items.statement: FY27 DI pipe volume guidance lowered to ~575,000 tons from earlier 650,000-700,000 tons due to slower JJM fund release
items.quote: So, Sir, we had erstwhile indicated the volume of I think 650,000 tons to 700,000 tons. But due to the slower initial release of JJM, we are expecting to reach a quantity of around 575,000 tons.

items.statement: Export share expected at 22-25% of total volumes in FY27
items.quote: And we are expecting that at the end of the year, we will be exporting around between 22% to 25% of our total volumes.

items.statement: T.I.S. Services revenue target EUR 42-45 million in FY27 with EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT ~8%
items.quote: Sir, by the end of this financial year, we are expecting, as mentioned, it was going to be 20% above last year's average of around EUR 38 million. So, we should be, hopefully, we'll reach a number of EUR 42 million to 45 million in revenue. The EBITDA margin of similarly the 14%-15% level with the PAT of 8% or so.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to reach 12-13% in Q3-Q4 FY27
items.quote: Going forward, I think Q3 FY'27, Q4FY'27, we should be hitting EBITDA number of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Industrial paints revenue target Rs 800-1,000 crore in 5 years with phased capex of Rs 250-300 crore
items.quote: We aim to establish a meaningful presence in this segment and target annual revenues of around Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 1,000 crores in the next five years. To su pport this growth, we plan to incur CAPEX in a phased manner of around Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores

items.statement: Valve segment revenue target to double from ~Rs 400 crore to Rs 800-1,000 crore in 4 years including inorganic growth
items.quote: And hence, we are even more aggressive where we, so far, we have only been manufacturing for internal consumption, but we expect to go out into the market and get around Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 1000 crores of re venue. This would include, hopefully, some inorganic growth also

items.statement: Long-term revenue target Rs 7,000-8,000 crore with EBITDA 13-13.5% by FY30-31
items.quote: So, without that in the picture, I am very certain that we can look at a growth of revenue to around Rs. 7,000-8,000 crores with EBITDA level of 13%-13.5% by FY30 & FY31.

items.statement: JJM 2.0 approved with Rs 8.69 lakh crore outlay (Centre Rs 3.59 lakh crore); Rs 67,670 crore allocated in FY27 budget, Rs 10,344 crore already sanctioned vs Rs 1,560 crore last year
items.quote: Central Government has allocated Rs. 67,670 crore towards JJM in the union budget for FY '27. Out of this, approximately Rs. 10,344 crore has already been sanctioned to various states during the current financial year till date compared to meagre Rs. 1,560 crore released under JJ M in previous financial year

items.statement: River linking projects Ken-Betwa (Rs 44,000 crore) and Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal (Rs 90,000 crore) expected to drive long-term DI pipe demand
items.quote: In case of river linking projects, we are hopeful to see demand coming in from the Ken-Betwa project involving a total project cost of Rs. 44,000 crores and the Pa rbati-Kalisindh-Chambal Link project bet ween Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, which is also expected to commence shortly with project value being around Rs. 90,000

items.statement: MCAD scheme with Rs 1,300 crore outlay for pressurized pipeline networks to boost irrigation demand
items.quote: Further momentum is expected from the recently approved Modernization of Command Area and Development and Water Management or in short MCAD scheme with an initial outlay of Rs. 1,300 crores for the modernization of irrigation water distribution systems through underground pressurized pipeline networks.

items.statement: Current executable order book ~300,000 tons (~5 months), ~50% from JJM
items.quote: So, we have a total order book of around 3 lakh tons, which works out to around five months. So, JJM, this order book, JJM would be around close to 50%.

items.statement: Order booking momentum expected to pick up substantially in next 1-2 months as JJM funds flow
items.quote: But in the next month or two, we are finding that speed of order booking is going to pick up substantially.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 9.5% (Rs 139 crore on Rs 1,465 crore income); standalone 6.3%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 139 crore with an EBITDA margin of 9.5%.

items.statement: DI pipe net realization improved to ~Rs 55,000/ton in Q1 FY27 from ~Rs 50,500/ton in Q4 FY26
items.quote: These are net realizations of around Rs. 50,500 per ton for Q4 FY'26and in Q1 FY'27 is around Rs. 55,000 per ton.

items.statement: Management sees DI pipe pricing at rock bottom; expects firming trend
items.quote: Sir, of course, as you might have seen, the last one, one and a half years has been extremely muted, especially the last particular financial year was probably rock bottom for the industry. Since it's been there since '1994, I think, at least from my understanding is the worst year Ductile Iron has seen in India. So, most definitely this is rock bottom.

items.statement: Industrial paints: Phase 1 capex Rs 100 crore for 17,000 KL capacity (brownfield, West Bengal); commercial production post Q1 FY28
items.quote: So, Sir, initial investment will be to the tune of Rs. 100 crores, wherein we will add capacity by 17,000 kiloliters. We already have a small facility on which we will have to do a brownfield expansion in West Bengal. So, that allows us a quicker return on inve stment and it will also allow us to better learn the nitty-gritties of the business

items.statement: Valve manufacturing facility in India to commence operations by end of FY27
items.quote: We also expect our valves manufacturing facility in India to commence operations by the end of this financial year, supporting future growth and improving profitability.

items.statement: Railway rubber components: additional equipment under installation, ready in 3 months; railway registration 4-6 months
items.quote: The bulk of the equipment is the same. Some additional equipment are required for which we have already taken procurement steps. They are under installation now. In the next three months, we are expecting those to be installed.

items.statement: Ferroalloy expansion planned as brownfield at existing West Bengal unit
items.quote: Our expansion in ferro alloy is also going to be in our existing unit. We already have one ferro alloy plant and we have found that with certain investments, we can utilize additional energy, etc. to put up another plant right next to it. So, that is what we are doing.

items.statement: Odisha greenfield site deferred; focus on brownfield efficiency investments
items.quote: Sir, because of the downfall in the market, we realized that it is better to hold back and utilize this capital for these more efficient brownfield expansions and to work on efficiency rather than just expansion in capacity.

items.statement: Structural cost optimization program implemented across operations to strengthen cost base and operating leverage
items.quote: During this year, we implemented a broad-based structural cost optimization program across our operations, strengthening operating efficiencies and creating a more competitive cost base that will support profitability and operating leverage as volumes recover.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia anti-dumping duty impact minimal (2-3% of sales); volumes easily diverted to other GCC/Africa markets
items.quote: The total sales of Electrosteel Castings to Saudi Arabia was to a total of, it is about 2% to 3% of our sales. So, that is a quantity that can be diverted to other markets pretty easily. It is not going to be such a problem.

items.statement: Export focus: 60-70% Western markets (Europe, UK), 30-40% Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia
items.quote: So, Europe, the U.K. have been our strong markets since we started exporting. Around 60% to 70% of our exports are focused on the Western markets. The remaining 40% is to the Middle East, Africa, and we have recently also started expanding into the Southeast Asian markets.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt Rs 1,658 crore, net debt Rs 876 crore (Jun 2026); term debt Rs 340 crore to reduce to Rs 230 crore via scheduled repayments
items.quote: At consolidated level, gross debt and net debt as on 30th June 2026 stood at Rs. 1,658 crore and Rs. 876 crore respectively. During the last fi nancial year, the net debt had reduced by nearly Rs. 1,100 crore and we are focusing on optimization, utilization of the funds

items.statement: Term debt Rs 340 crore to reduce to Rs 230 crore with scheduled repayments; working capital debt depends on business volume
items.quote: So, we have our term debt right now stands at around Rs. 340 crores, which will eventually go down to around Rs. 230 crores with the scheduled repayments that we have.

items.statement: Acquired T.I.S. Service S.p.A. Italy; Q1 FY27 revenue EUR 10 million (+18.4% QoQ), EBITDA margin mid-teens
items.quote: During the quarter, T.I.S. delivered EUR 10 million in revenue, representing a sequential growth of 18.4% over the previous quarter with EBITDA margins improving to the mid-teens.

items.statement: Actively seeking bolt-on acquisitions in adjacencies; Rs 700 crore capital available for deployment
items.quote: Sir, we have around Rs. 700 crores of capital on our books which we are ready to invest. So, if some opportunity comes, we will be more than happy to look at it. Of course, it is always best to expand within your adjacency. So, that is our first priority.

items.statement: Rajesh Daga appointed CFO (joined 1989, headed domestic marketing 25 years); Ashutosh Agarwal stepped down
items.quote: I would like to now hand over the call to Mr. Rajesh Daga, CFO, who has recently taken over from Mr. Ashutosh Agarwal. Mr. Daga has been with us at Electrosteel since 1989. Throughout his tenure, he has held key positions across diverse functions, including finance, accounts, purchase and sales.

items.statement: JJM market share estimated at 12-13% of ductile iron industry outlay
items.quote: So, we can say that approximately from Jal Jeevan we will be getting close to probably 12%-13% of this outlay.

items.statement: River linking projects: 5-7% of project volumes translate to DI pipe demand

items.statement: Focus on ABS expansion as priority; PS expansion to be evaluated when business case clear; both businesses important.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,014.2 cr; EBITDA INR 223.6 cr; PAT INR 138.3 cr; consolidated volume 50.8 KT.
items.quote: total income for quarter 1 FY27 stood at INR1,014.2 crores. EBITDA for quarter 1 FY27 stood at INR223.6 crores and EBITDA margin stood at 22%. Profit after tax for Q1 FY27 stood at INR138.3 crores and profit margin stood at 13.6%. Consolidated sales volume, which includes both India and Thailand, for Q1 FY27 stood at 50.8 KT.

items.statement: Parador revenue expected to grow by EUR 20-30 million over next couple of years on last year's base
items.quote: But overall, there is now emerging line of sight for adding about at least 20 million to 30 million over the next couple of years on the revenue side to that base.

items.statement: Parador EBITDA margin expected to improve by 300-400 basis points from BCG cost-out program
items.quote: Our expectation is, at a conservative level that should deliver at least 300 to 400 basis point uplift on the EBITDA side.

items.statement: BCG cost-out program first results visible by end of Q2, full impact by Q4 FY27
items.quote: So Q4 of this year should have visible impact on the P&L. But many of those will start building gradually over the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Pipes business expects moderate growth in seasonally weak Q2 FY27 as PVC resin prices stabilize
items.quote: With government interventions facilitating stabilization in PVC resin price, we expect demand conditions to improve and anticipate moderate growth during the seasonally weak quarter 2.

items.statement: Parador expected to achieve more than break-even in FY27
items.quote: And yes, this year, the outlook is strong. We are looking at growth overall from a rev enue perspective, and we are looking at more than breaking even this

items.statement: Board approved new greenfield designer board plant near Hyderabad with Rs. 167 crores capital outlay
items.quote: During the quarter, the Board has approved the establishment of a greenfield designer board manufacturing facilities in Hyderabad with an estimated capital outlay of Rs. 167 crores.

items.statement: Nellore Boards plant on track for commissioning by Q4 FY27, OPVC capex completed
items.quote: So that project is on in full swing, we are on track as far as timelines are concerned and as I mentioned, Q4 we should look to commission the plant.

items.statement: Total capex of ~Rs. 500 crores allocated to known programs over next couple of years
items.quote: I think what we know at this moment is, over the next couple of years, there is close to INR 500 crores of capex that have been allocated to known named programs and projects.

items.statement: Boards & Panels industry sized Rs. 1,500-2,000 crores growing 10-14% YoY, BirlaNu operating at 80-90% capacity
items.quote: We have been operating at nearly 80% to 90% of our capacity. So, we are chock-a-block.

items.statement: New Boards capacity additions expected to add Rs. 300-350 crores revenue and Rs. 75-85 crores EBITDA over next couple of years
items.value: INR 300-350 crores revenue, INR 75-85 crores EBITDA
items.quote: By the time these capacities come in, and we are able to ramp it up, it will inject close to a revenue upside of about INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores and hopefully an EBITDA uplift north of INR 75 crores to INR 85 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 35% to Rs. 80 crores, margins improved significantly
items.quote: At a consolidated level, the revenue for quarter 1 grew by just short of 12% to Rs. 1,174 crores, and the EBITDA improved significantly to INR 80 crores, which is about 35% higher compared to previous year.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose ~70% to Rs. 97 crores, margins expanded 420+ bps
items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue increased by 10% year-on-year to Rs. 824 crores, while EBITDA rose by nearly 70% to Rs. 97 crores. EBITDA margins expanded by over 420 basis points.

items.statement: Roofs segment EBITDA margin improved 390 bps to 18.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 390 basis points to 18.2%, supported by stronger realization, improved volume sales and favourable operating leverage.

items.statement: Pipes segment EBITDA margins expanded 660 bps despite 11% revenue decline and 27% volume drop
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, EBITDA margins expanded by 660 basis points, driven by an improved product mix, procurement efficiencies and disciplined pricing actions.

items.statement: Parador Q1 FY27 EBITDA loss of Rs. 13 crores vs profit of Rs. 5 crores last year due to raw material costs, SAP migration, plant maintenance
items.quote: EBITDA stood at a loss of Rs. 13 crores BIRLANU LTD’S Q1 FY27 EARNINGS CALL TRANSCRIPT compared with a profit of Rs. 5 crores in the corresponding quarter last year

items.statement: Parador order book up over 10% YoY, pipeline indicates strong recovery in H2 FY27
items.quote: The order book is healthy. It is up over 10% over last year, and the pipeline indicates a strong recovery in H2.

items.statement: India business revenue grew ~11% to Rs. 833 crores in Q1 FY27, EBITDA grew 71% to Rs. 98 crores
items.quote: The India business has been off to a great start in FY27. We grew our revenue base by about 11% to Rs. 833 crores, while EBITDA grew by 71% to reach Rs. 98 crores.

items.statement: Roofs segment revenue grew 17% to Rs. 517 crores, market share up ~1%
items.quote: In the Roofs segment, we broke all previous records, crossing the Rs. 500 crores mark for the quarter. In fact, we did Rs. 517 crores to be precise, which represents a growth of 17% over last year.

items.statement: Walls business revenue grew >14% led by robust demand across panels and blocks
items.quote: The Walls business continued its strong momentum with revenue growth of over 14%, led by robust demand across both panels and blocks.

items.statement: Construction Chemicals revenue grew 11% despite 50%+ raw material inflation and Middle East conflict impact
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, we delivered 11% revenue growth, supported by focused sales acceleration initiatives and a significant expansion in our portfolio.

items.statement: PVC resin prices rose ~60% in March then fell ~30% in April, causing sharp demand decline in April
items.quote: You recall, in March, there was a price rise of nearly 60%. This was followed by a decline of about 30% in April, which resulted in sharp decline in demand, particularly in the month of April.

items.statement: Construction Chemicals key raw material prices increased over 50% due to Middle East conflict
items.quote: Our key raw material prices increased by over 50%, while disruptions across customer industries, for instance, tile industry was badly impacted and project execution led to a temporary slowdown in demand across several application segments.

items.statement: Reduced ~Rs. 100 crores working capital YoY through inventory and receivables management
items.quote: Through targeted initiatives across receivable, inventories and sourcing, we reduced approximately Rs. 100 crores of working capital on a year-on-year basis, resulting in improved operating cash flows.

items.statement: Substantially reduced fibre stock in last 6-8 months, ~30% reduction in receivables
items.quote: We used to carry a large stock of fibre . We have substantially reduced our fibre stock in last 6 to 8 months. The other side on receivable side, we have tightened our controls on giving the credits, and that has resulted into close to 30% reduction in our receivable numbers.

items.statement: Gross borrowings reduced ~Rs. 100 crores in Q1 FY27 from Rs. 852 crores (Mar'26) to Rs. 758 crores (Jun'26)
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that gross borrowings reduced by nearly Rs. 100 crores during the quarter from Rs. 852 crores as of March '26 to Rs. 758 crores as of June '26.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio 0.68x as of June 30, well within manageable range
items.quote: So, debt to equity, our debt-to-equity ratio as on 30th June is 0.68x, which is well within our manageable range.

items.statement: Telangana Boards plant targeting 0.9x asset turn, Rs. 140 crores revenue on ~Rs. 145-150 crores investment (ex-land)
items.quote: So, asset turn will be 0.9x. We are targeting to generate INR 140 crores revenue. This INR 166 crores also includes the land cost, so other than land, it will be around INR 145 crores to INR 150 crores in investment.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties persist, raw material, freight, currency markets volatile, labour costs trending upward
items.quote: Geopolitical uncertainties continue to persist. Raw material, freight and currency market remain volatile and in addition, labour costs are showing an upward trend.

items.statement: Open orders of Rs 365 crore pending dispatch, mostly to be executed in current financial year
items.quote: We have open orders of 365 crores, that is the orders which we have received, and the open part of that amount which is yet pending for dispatch. It should be dispatched during this year, or in the near future, over one or two years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 78% YoY to Rs 48.98 crore driven by product launches, import substitution and certifications
items.quote: Year on year, for the first quarter, the comparison is that last year the revenue was 27.48 crores, where in the current year it is 48.98 crores. That is a 78% plus year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted: automation & digitalisation 15%, water 26%, industrial engineering & systems 59% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Revenue from automation and digitalisation in the current year is almost 15%. Last year, it was almost the same at 15.6%. From water, in the current year we earned 26%, and in last year it was 55.8%. From industrial engineering and systems, in the current year it is 59%, where last year it was 28.6%.

items.statement: Current Ahmedabad facility (140,000 sq ft) can support double current turnover; new facilities planned in near future
items.quote: We are in a business where all the products have different space requirements, because we are not on a job manufacturing basis. But even then, we can say that if we double the current turnover, even then new facilities would not be required. But yes, in the near future, we will need new facilities, and we will work on that.

items.statement: Recurring MRO/AMC revenue currently 5-6% of total, expected to increase significantly in 1-2 years
items.quote: On MRO, AMC or warranty-related recurring revenue, we can say that it varies on a year-on-year basis. But around 5% to 6% of the total revenue is in MRO, and it is gradually increasing. Given the type of orders we are receiving, within a very short span of time, during one or two years, you will find a really very good amount of increase in MRO.

items.statement: Receivables ageing high due to Q4 concentration; normal payment terms 30-60 days or LC

items.quote: Right now, whether we have to go for NSE or not will be decided by the management, but first of all we need to comply with MPS, the minimum public shareholding requirement. For MPS compliance also, we have enough time right now.

items.quote: We cannot right now declare anything confirmed right now, because we are trying for the commercialise this. Once we can confirm anything, you will receive the orders. So, it is early to declare anything yet. But yes, we are planning on this, and we hope for the best this.

items.statement: Company does not compromise on price for competition; growth driven by product quality, certifications and import substitution
items.quote: We have an in-house R&D centre, and we launch many products year on year, and we do not compromise on price for competition. A good industry, good products, good product life cycles and good registrations; all of this mix is driving the good growth of Axis Solutions.

items.statement: ATEX and IECEx certifications enable supply to Middle East, Southeast Asia and Europe; import substitution for European and Chinese products

But this will not restrict us on the top line

items.statement: Subsidiary details disclosed on BSE under Regulation 30; management declined detailed discussion on call

items.quote: Yes, of course. You're absolutely right.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing 10.14% (-41 bps YoY), 7th consecutive quarterly improvement; incremental long-term borrowing at ~9.8%

Our total debt stood at INR 10,793 crores. I'm happy to inform you that about 66% of borrowings are now beyond 3 years tenure and our incremental long-term borrowing also came at about 9.8% in this quarter.

items.statement: GNPA 2.6% vs 2.5% in Mar '26 (denominator effect); focused book 2.1% GNPA, defocused 3.1%; Stage 1 92.5%, Stage 2 4.9%, Stage 3 coverage 45%; Net NPA 1.9%

Defocused book carrying 3.1% GNPA is fast running down, while incremental focused book sits at 2.1% GNPA. Stage 1 on the book is 92.5% of exposure. Stage 2 is 4.9% and our provision coverage on Stage 3 is 45%. Net NPA is accordingly at 1.9%.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 98% in Q1

items.statement: Branch network build-out complete at 317 branches; focus shifted to productivity and operating leverage
items.quote: With the branch built-out complete, our operating focus has now shifted from branch expansion to productivity, throughput and operating leverage.

Encouraging to note that despite prevailing macro headwinds, the non -digital business improved profitability, delivering EBITDA growth of 7.4% and PAT growth of 85% during the quarter.

items.statement: International operations contributed INR3 crores revenue despite West Asia conflict impact.
items.quote: Our international operations, though impacted by the West Asia conflict, contributed INR3 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Radio FCT Advertising revenue was INR62.2 crores with soft advertiser demand due to macroeconomic uncertainties.
items.quote: The Radio FCT Advertising segment delivered reported revenues of INR62.2 crores on the back of ongoing macroeconomic scenario. The challenging conditions witnessed in FY26 extended into Q1 FY27 with advertiser demand remaining soft due to the uncertainties.

items.statement: Non-FCT segment revenue was INR17.5 crores, impacted by event cancellations and artist travel disruptions.
items.quote: The non-FCT segment stood at INR17.5 crores, impacted by event cancellations and artist travel disruptions across markets weighed on our business activity.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 43.3% YoY to INR31.1 crores, contributing 30.2% of total revenue, driven by Gaana's user traction.
items.quote: In this quarter, Digital revenue stood at INR31.1 crores, up 43.3% year-on-year, contributing to 30.2% of our total revenue, up from last year of 23%. This growth was largely powered by Gaana's strong user traction and consumer engagement on the platform.

items.statement: Digital business investment declined to INR8.3 crores from INR9.8 crores YoY, reflecting operational efficiency efforts.
items.quote: I'm happy to report that investment in Digital business declined to INR8.3 crores from INR9.8 crores in the same quarter last year, reflecting the results of our ongoing operational efforts.

items.statement: Advertising revenues across traditional media (radio, TV, print, outdoor) are under pressure due to media fragmentation and content abundance.
items.quote: Media, as I've been telling in other earnings calls also, is going through a major transition phase where the subscription numbers or a dvertising revenues are under pressure where there is a lot of content available. There is media fragmentation happening and which is leading to pressure on overall the advertising landscape. It's not just radio, but be it television, be it print, be it outdoor, a

items.statement: Three business verticals: Radio, Digital (Gaana), and Events; Events business growing quarter-on-quarter but Q1 impacted by cancellations.
items.quote: we have 3 businesses we put as verticals. One is radio. The second is Digital, which you rightly said. The third is our Events business, which has been growing really quarter-on-quarter every quarter. This quarter has been marked by a lot of cancellation because of artists couldn't travel.

items.statement: Cost rationalization includes station networking, AI usage, and new broadcasting tools to minimize broadcasting costs across cost structure.
items.quote: there are networking of stations, usage of new tech of AI, usage of new broadcasting tools helps us minimize the cost of broadcasting really drastically. So that helps a lot, which impacts line items across the cost base.

items.statement: Radio EBITDA margins 35-40%, Events EBITDA margins 25-30%.
items.quote: our radio margins have always been in the range of 35% to 40%. Events have been in the range of 25% to 30% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Gaana subscription price increased to INR799; annual pack has headroom vs competitors, monthly pack ~10% lower; focus on profitable subscribers (~70% margin).
items.quote: We have increased our price to INR799, and it's a balance what we keep creating. As I said, our endeavour for us is to make it breakeven as soon as possible and not gun unnecessarily for subscriber growth, which comes at a lower cost or a lower LTV.

items.statement: Inventory utilization down ~8%, but pricing improved ~4%; volume utilization down 8%.
items.quote: So inventory utilization has gone down by about 8%, but the price has improved by almost 4%.

items.statement: Market share on volume 27-28%; Gaana is only pure subscription service in India; competitors have free tiers; industry moving toward subscription-only models.
items.quote: Market share on volume has been about 27% to 28%.

items.statement: Events business is H2-heavy (35%/65% H1/H2 split); some cancelled events moved to Q2; remain positive on Events growth from Q2 onward.
items.quote: Having said that, the Events business has always been H2 heavy. Q1 and Q2 are always subdued. Other than that media is like 45%, 55% H1, H2. Events is almost 35%, 65%, if not more. So that's the way it looks like. So we remain very positive on our Events business, and we believe our quarter 2 onwards, the business will remain in good shape only.

items.statement: Buyback/dividend decisions are Board matters; management takes feedback but no commitment made.
items.quote: So that's a Board discussion. We keep discussing. As and when it comes, I think we will come back to you.

items.statement: Cash balance INR390 crores as of June 30, 2026.
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a robust balance sheet with a cash balance of INR390 crores as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Company experimenting with AI internally but sector focus remains media; no diversification plans outside media.
items.quote: So Suresh, so far, we have concentrated on the Media business, but with new tech of AI and all, we do delve on that, and we keep experimenting on and do internal investments on usage of AI, but largely, our overall sector will remain media.

items.statement: Express Logistics EBITDA margin target 7.5% for FY27 and 10% over 3 years
items.quote: we had said it will be 7.5% on the Express margin so that we are looking at in this year. And if you see 10% is the target in that plan, so we are inching up towards that direction.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA target 5-6% for FY27
items.quote: We are sticking to that plan. This year, the trajectory on this front is to be in the level of 5% to 6% and improve from there on.

items.statement: Aim to grow faster than logistics industry by a percentage point
items.quote: whatever logistics industry growth is, we will be at a percentage point above the logistics industry. That's the strive we have for growth.

items.statement: Express Logistics gross margin improved to 26.3% in Q1 FY27 from 25.3% a year ago
items.quote: If you see this quarter, both the yield effort and the volume growth has shored up the gross margin from the last year number of 25.3% to 26.3%.

items.statement: Express Logistics EBITDA margin at 6.2% in Q1 FY27; Consultative Logistics at 29.56%
items.quote: Express is at 6.2% and at CL, we are at Consultative Logistics, we are at 29.56%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 39.2% YoY to INR71 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the same period stood at INR71 crores, registering a growth of 39.2% over Q1 FY '26 and 18.9% over Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Express volumes grew 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Volumes increased 6.7% year-on-year to 312,000 tonnes, while realization per tonne improved by 6.4%.

items.statement: Express realization per tonne improved 6.4% YoY; 80% from natural escalation, 20% from diesel pass-through
items.quote: the natural escalation is a larger pie, which would be, let's say, 80% and 20% would be around on the pass-through of diesel impact.

items.statement: Diesel price hike fully passed through via transparent DPH mechanism on website
items.quote: all the impact from the diesel is passed through to the customer because we have a transparent DPH, diesel price hike mechanism that is also available on our website.

items.statement: Express revenue mix: KEA ~60%, retail ~20%, balance strategic; reclassified from prior 80:20 split
items.quote: the KEA that we account for here are at about 60% of our revenue, retail at about 20% and the balance is strategic.

items.statement: Express business 95% road, 5% air
items.quote: About 95% of our business is road and about 5% is air.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics revenue per sq ft increased 3% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This quarter, that discipline has delivered a 3% increase in revenue per square foot.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics customer retention rate 98%; service quality adherence over 99%
items.quote: We closed the quarter with service quality adherence of over 99%, and that consistency has led to a 98% customer retention rate.

items.statement: Other income INR14 crores includes INR8 crores lease closure, INR2 crores interest, INR4 crores refunds
items.quote: One exceptional is the lease closure, which has happened in this quarter. So that's one INR8 crore amount, which is the other income component sitting here, plus we have received some income refunds and there's an interest component of INR2 crores.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; focus on profitable growth and cost efficiency
items.quote: We will continue to invest in initiatives that enhance customer value and operational capabilities, maintain a disciplined approach to costs and focus on delivering sustainable profitable growth.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics serves all major e-commerce and quick commerce players; growing strongly
items.quote: On the consultative logistics side, we run a lot of sort centers, fulfillment centers for e-commerce and quick commerce companies, and it continues to be a very large vertical on the CL side of the business, growing very, very strongly.

items.statement: Fuel and labor cost inflation persist; minimum wage hikes passed through via GPI exercise
items.quote: fuel that is a transparent DPH mechanism. The people cost with minimum wages going across the country, that is also a pass-through mechanism. We deploy the annual GPI exercise.

items.statement: Strengthening leadership team with capabilities in technology, digitization, infrastructure, automation
items.quote: Equally important is the investment we continue to make in strengthening our leadership team with organization capabilities, not just in people but in technology, in digitization, in infrastructure and in automation.

items.statement: Oil production target of 1 MMT per quarter from now on, aiming for 3.9-4 MMT in FY27 and up to 4.2 MMT by FY29
items.quote: If everything remains ceteris paribus, then given everything going good and nothing adverse happens in the field, we expect that we will be reaching 1 MMT every quarter from now onwards.

items.statement: Gas production target of 3.8 BCM in FY28, reaching 5 BCM by FY29 first quarter with pipeline completion
items.quote: Yes next year it will be 3.8 BCM. So now on an averaging we are shutting down some wells at least 30 wells we are always shutting down. When we will be opening all those well. On an average if there is low consumption we will shut in up to 60 well. See the situation is like this. So it becomes a issue. So these wells are already there.

The natural gas production on quarter-to-quarter has increased by 0.4%.

items.value: INR 9,146 cr revenue (+45% YoY); 105% utilization; 87% distillate yield; USD 35.95/bbl GRM; INR 1,843 cr EBITDA; INR 1,305 cr PAT

items.quote: Our per barrel operating cost hovers around USD4.5 to USD5 today. It will come down to a level of USD3.5. That's what our expectation is because we will be rationalizing on the facilities and our throughput will be high, so that therefore the operating cost will come to around 3.5.

items.statement: No impact from recent floods on operations in Sivasagar and Charaideo areas
items.quote: No. In our areas there was no impact. We have operations in Sivasagar and also in Charaideo, but these are in the Western part of the – means Eastern part of Sivasagar and Charaideo. So our place like not much of flood, but definitely the nearby areas got submerged and a lot of things not much impact on our side.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 12 percentage points to 18% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: total revenue grew by 15%, coming at INR 497 crore, with EBITDA going up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore with a margin expansion of 12 points.

items.statement: Print segment operating EBITDA margin was 13% in Q1 FY27 despite high newsprint costs
items.quote: Operating revenue, at INR 376 crore, which is a 16% increase, and operating EBITDA improved substantially to INR 50 crore with a margin at 13%.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 15% year-on-year to INR 295 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: ad. revenue grew 15% to INR 295 crore and circ. revenue was virtually flat at INR 52 crore.

items.statement: Newsprint prices peaked at $650-700 per metric ton and are expected to plateau before declining
items.quote: this is the highest peak that we have seen at about $650 to $700 a metric ton. We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down.

items.statement: Print advertising growth driven substantially by yield improvement and pricing increases
items.quote: a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing . Of course, Government gave a price increase in November last year, but that was after seven years.

items.statement: Preferential issue proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt in HT Media and Digicontent Limited
items.quote: Once the preferential capital comes in, the money will be used to retire the debt. At least 30 % to 50% of the debt will be retired, which will definitely be accretive to the EPS and long-term interest coverage ratio, our credit rating and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Preferential issue priced at SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP) with no premium
items.quote: the pricing of the preferential issue has been done strictly on the basis of a SEBI formula and the higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP prices and we have not put any premium on that number.

items.statement: HMVL other income includes treasury gains from yield curve movement and realized profit on asset sales
items.quote: In HMVL, in the other income there is a substantial portion which is on treasury and this time there is also profit on sale of assets which we have got.

items.statement: Employee costs reduced year-on-year due to organizational right-sizing across HT Media and HMVL
items.quote: We've been driving efficiency. I think that's something that we've been saying for the past sometime. We've been right-sizing the organization and that's basically what it is.

items.statement: Preferential issue chosen over rights issue for faster execution (2-3 months) and fundraising certainty
items.quote: The rights issue would have meant a longer process. Preferential issue is a slightly shorter process. There is greater certainty of fundraising because there was a quantum that was being targeted to reduce the debt.

items.statement: No forward guidance given on revenue or earnings projections as per usual practice
items.quote: We would not, as per usual practice, be giving any specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Digital revenue declined 28% year-on-year due to deliberate portfolio reset toward leaner, profitable offerings
items.quote: Digital revenue moderated during the quarter as we deliberately reset the portfolio around leaner, more focused offerings with the intent of driving sustainable and profitable growth.

items.statement: Radio segment operating on leaner footprint after surrendering non-viable station licenses
items.quote: The segment is now operating on a leaner and more sustainable footprint following the surrender of licenses for certain non-viable stations.

items.statement: HT Media and Digicontent Limited hold net debt positions while HMVL holds net cash of INR 922 crore consolidated
items.quote: HT Media Limited and Digi content Limited - which is not here - where the preferential issue is being done, are both indebted companies and are running a net debt position.

items.statement: Management aspires to reach ~8% operating EBITDA margin for full year FY27, up from 7.3% in Q1, but explicitly states this is not formal guidance
items.quote: initially, at the beginning of this year, we had guided that we should be probably close to 8% kind of a margin for the whole year, at least at the operating level, which is this quarter about 7.3%.

items.statement: Industry RAC primary sales grew ~20-25% YoY in Q1 FY27 (10-15% volume + 10-12% ASP); secondary sales better than primary; channel inventory near normal levels
items.quote: overall industry has done around 10% to 15% better, 15% better as compared to last year. And on the couple of that, if you combine that with around 10% to 12% value growth in the ASP, so the combined is around 20%, 25% is the growth in the -- at the primary level for the RAC.

items.statement: Company expects ~20%+ volume growth for full year FY27 on low base; prepared for higher volumes if opportunity arises
items.quote: We think that should be a possibility for us, given the fact that for us, for the next 9 months, barring December, base is pretty low. And yes, if industry is even normal in the sense that we see industry normalizing and unlike last year, the channel inventory is not high, etcetera. So we think that we should be having close to 20% plus kind of a volume growth for the full year.

items.quote: RAC at a volume level has grown around 20%, 22% for us in this quarter. And rest of the value has come from the price increases. ASP has increased by around 10% to 12%.
