items.quote: Some of these large orders, the margins were offset by a rise in forex and commodity prices. But due to large volumes, we were able to offset some of these cost increases.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions in semiconductors, plastics, copper impacting material availability and costs; team resolving most issues
items.quote: Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption. So those disruptions impact availability of material, and that's why sometimes don't allow us to fully use our capacity.

items.statement: Temporary inventory build-up at both Hyderabad and Gurgaon plants by design for transition; receivables elevated due to 57% YoY revenue growth but collections quality healthy
items.quote: Inventory with Hyderabad and Gurgaon plant running in parallel, we have a temporary built-up inventory both -- in both the facilities. This is by design. items.statement: Secured 100% share of business for leading international brand for wallbox home chargers; renewed agreement with leading truck OEM for portable chargers

items.quote: we've added 15 new network operators in terms of order intake in Q1 and have an order book of almost close to 180 DC chargers, which will continue until October '26, right? items.statement: BESS commercial/industrial segment: 15 MWh orders in hand (~INR20 crores) plus 34 MWh advanced pipeline (~INR45 crores)
items.quote: Today, we have about 15 megawatt hours of orders in hand, which are worth roughly INR20 crores and another INR45 crores or 34 megawatt hours of orders in advanced pipeline.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at low to mid-teens; EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps committed
items.quote: I would like to reiterate my confidence in Emcure to deliver low to mid -teen revenue growth in FY27. As I have said, we expect to see positive movement quarter after quarter, and as we discussed in the past we are committed to give 70 to 100 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin expected around 59% due to stronger international mix
items.quote: I think '27 will probably be around the 59%.

items.statement: FY27 R&D spend guided at 4-5% of revenue
items.quote: R&D, I for the full year will be between that 4% to 5% range. So, I think we continue to maintain that outlook.

items.statement: Net cash position targeted by end of FY28
items.quote: Probably by the end of FY28, we should be net cash.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 50 bps YoY to 19.7% on operating leverage and cost control
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 19.7%, up 50 bps, supported by operating efficiencies and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin declined to 58.4% due to export mix and product mix
items.quote: Gross margin was 58.4%. Margins declined year-over-year, led by increased exports and a function of product and business mix.

items.statement: India business grew 10.2% YoY to INR 1,095 crore, returning to double-digit growth
items.quote: On a year -on-year basis, it has grown by 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore, returning to double -digit growth compared with Q1 of previous year.

items.statement: International business grew 34.2% YoY to INR 1,485 crore with all regions contributing
items.quote: The international business delivered very strong and robust growth during the quarter with revenue of INR 1,485 crore, a growth of 34.2%.

items.statement: Rest of World grew 44.8% driven by ARV segment; ARV ~2/3 of ROW in Q1, expected 50-55% for full year
items.quote: Rest of the World grew by 44.8% to INR 522 crore, led by very strong performance in the ARV business.

items.statement: Liposomal amphotericin B introduced across Europe with order book ramping up in line with supplies
items.quote: It's pretty much in all the countries and there also, we are ramping up supplies. So , the order book across the different countries should also go up in line with the supplies.

items.statement: Net debt to increase by INR 450-500 crore next quarter for Mantra and Gennova minority stake payouts
items.quote: We have made these payments for acquisition of Mantra and also the Gennova minority stake. So that will take us by debt by close to around INR 450 crore to INR 500 crore.

items.statement: Net debt INR 1,103 crore as of June 30; expected to rise to ~INR 1,450 crore by end of next quarter after payouts
items.quote: by the end of next quarter, we should have a net debt of close to around INR 1,450 crore. From what today, I see at INR 1,560 crore.

items.statement: Acquired 12.05% minority stake in Gennova, making it a 100% owned subsidiary
items.quote: The third important thing that has happened is we have just recently acquired 12.05% minority stake in Gennova, making it a 100% owned subsidiary of Emcure.

items.statement: Chairman Berjis Desai to retire at AGM; CEO Satish Mehta to assume Chairman role in addition to MD & CEO
items.quote: With the recommendation of the Board, I wil l now take on the role of Chairman in addition to my existing role as Managing Director and CEO of the Company post the conclusion of the upcoming Annual General Meeting

items.statement: Samit Mehta appointed COO of Emcure and CEO of Gennova, overseeing R&D, manufacturing, licensing and strategy
items.quote: The second important announcement I would like to make is that Samit Mehta now takes over as Chief Operating Officer of Emcure . As far as Samit is concerned, he is extremely passionat e about science and technology.

items.statement: In-licensed products (Sanofi, Roche, Poviztra) growing in line with industry; own brands in women's health, cardio, CNS, oncology driving faster growth
items.quote: So, I think most of the in -licensed are growing in line with the industry. I think that's what we talked about even when we've taken over the portfolio, they will continue growing in line with the industry growth. But where we're talking about faster industry growth, that will be driven more by our own brands across women's health, cardio, CNS, oncology, those segments.

items.statement: India organic growth (ex-Sanofi OAD, Roche) ~6-7% in Q1; Poviztra is a new launch
items.quote: I think if I strip out the Sanofi OAD and the Roche, we'll probably be about 6%, 7% growth in the quarter. Poviztra effectively is a new brand that we are launching out. .

items.statement: Semaglutide (Poviztra) priced competitively; month-over-month growth seen; MASH indication recently approved for innovator
items.quote: And since the innovator, Novo Nordisk and of course, Emcure , we took a decision to make the pricing very competitive. I have every reason to believe that, over time, we will emerge as one of the stronger players and perform better than most brands.

items.statement: ICMR licensed novel anti-HPV candidate for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia to Emcure in July
items.quote: part of government technology transfer initiative, ICMR licensed a novel anti -HPV candidate for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia to Emcure

items.statement: Signed royalty-free voluntary license with MSD for generic alimatravir (once-monthly oral HIV PrEP) across 129 low/lower-middle income countries
items.quote: Also in July, we signed a royalty-free, non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreement with Merck Sharp & Dohme to make and sell a generic version of experimental once a monthly oral HIV pill across 129 low and lower -middle income countries.

items.statement: Received 15+ product approvals across developed and emerging markets in Q1
items.quote: During the quarter that ended, we received 15 -plus product approvals across developed and emerging markets.

items.statement: Semaglutide filing for Canada planned in next few months (second wave)
items.quote: We'll be filing in the current quarter in the next few months

items.statement: Working capital increased slightly in Q1 but stabilized in July; expected to normalize in Q2
items.quote: yes, my working capital went up a little bit, but that's now stabilized in this month. So that will come to normal in this quarter.

items.statement: Global uncertainty (West Asia, Russia-Ukraine) noted; management highlights resilience of team
items.quote: If you look at the global environment, what's happening in West Asia, Middle East or even for that matter, what's happening with Russia a nd Ukraine, there continues to be significant uncertainty, Emcureans have shown a lot of resilience

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20% over a three-to-five-year period and EBITDA margin range of 28% to 30%
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR 1,100 crores to INR 1,300 crores; no guidance provided for FY28 yet
items.quote: So, we have given a FY27 capex guidance of INR1,100 crores to INR1,300 crores. That still stands. We haven't provided a guidance on fiscal '28.

items.statement: Targeting 1,150 kilolitre capacity by FY27; on track for capacity additions including Bidar production blocks and formulation facility
items.quote: Just to confirm, we are in line with our capacity building to reach 1150 kilolitre by FY27, right

items.statement: Peptide manufacturing facility at greenfield site near Hyderabad expected operational in 2028; clinical capacity coming online sooner
items.quote: In addition, we plan to break ground for a peptide manufacturing facility at our new greenfield site near Hyderabad, which is expected to be operational in 2028.

items.statement: Total spend on peptide side towards end of 2028 expected to be less than INR 300 crores
items.quote: Dhaval, it's probably going to be less than INR300 crores.

items.statement: 33 active commercial molecules and 14 molecules in late phase; added six late phase molecules over last 15 months, five from large pharma FTE engagements
items.value: 33 active commercial molecules and 14 molecules in late phase
items.quote: the underlying health of the CMC business continues to be strong with 33 active commercial molecules and 14 molecules in late phase

items.statement: Three of four commercial contracts to be added this year are commercial supplies; primary supplier for two of three; decently sized products by value
items.quote: Three of the four that we will be working on this year, as we had mentioned during the last call, will be commercial supplies. Primary - Secondary, as we've discussed before right, they are, I think we probably are primary in two out of th is three

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and IP concerns strengthening India's role in customer diversification strategies; biotech funding expected to support healthy demand
items.quote: From a customer s' standpoint, geopolitical uncertainty and concerns around intellectual property have made India an increasingly important part of their diversification strategies. I would say this trend has not only continued but strengthened.

items.statement: Expanding into peptides beyond GLP-1s including macrocyclic peptides, peptide-drug conjugates, and radiochemistry; building broad-based peptide capabilities across discovery, development, and commercial manufacturing
items.quote: We are not solely focused on just the GLP-1 space. We are taking a very big position built to support peptides across the therapeutic window. That is the comment we are making. So that we are not just chasing a single modality, we are really building broad-based capabilities in peptides and built a significant technology platform for peptides.

items.statement: Entering formulation capabilities for small molecule oral solids up to Phase 1 and Phase 2; driven by China+1 strategy and existing development relationships
items.quote: As of now, we're building small molecules, primarily oral solids of different forms up to phase 1 and phase 2. We have significant interest from multiple of our large pharma partners already who are working with on the chemistry side to be able to support them on their early clinical formulation.

items.statement: XDC Center of Excellence opening soon to support payloads, linkers, and conjugation across antibodies, peptides, PROTACs, and oligonucleotides
items.quote: We are close to opening our XDC Center of Excellence , which will support both discovery and development teams in the synthesis of payloads, linkers, and conjugation across antibodies, peptides, PROTACs, and oligonucleotides

items.statement: Returning customers accounted for over 90% of revenue in FY25 and FY26; working with 19 of top 25 pharma companies; aiming to transition at least two large pharma customers to integrated discovery models this year
items.quote: We continue to add new customers, but returning customers accounted for over 90% of our revenue in FY25 and FY26. We believe this is a strong reflection of customer satisfaction and the value we are creating for customers over the course of their programs.

items.statement: Converted pilot collaboration with large pharma into long-term, high-volume discovery chemistry partnership; multiple customers expanding collaborations this quarter
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully converted a pilot collaboration with a large pharmaceutical company into a long-term, high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. This is exactly the kind of progression we were looking for, starting with a focused engagement, demonstrating value, and expanding the relationship over time.

items.statement: Supported 5 FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 and 17 launches over past 5 years, demonstrating ability to supply launch quantities and support commercialization
items.value: 5 FDA-approved molecules in 2025, 17 launches over 5 years
items.quote: In calendar 2025, Sai contributed to five FDA-approved molecules, meaning we were part of either discovery or development or commercial manufacturing for the product. Over the past five years, we have supported 17 launches, demonstrating our ability to supply launch quantities and play a meaningful role in commercialization.

items.statement: Launched campus strategy program led by former board member to establish Sai as employer of choice; structured management development programs and intensifying Sai Academy for capability building
items.quote: We have kick-started a campus strategy program led by a former board member , with the objective of establishing Sai as an employer of choice for life sciences talent. We are putting in place a more structured approach to how we attract, develop, and retain scientific and technical talent.

items.statement: Successfully scaled up late-stage GMP intermediate for large pharma customer using flow chemistry; experimenting with continuous downstream operations for commercial manufacturing
items.quote: Recently, we successfully scaled up a late-stage GMP intermediate for a large pharmaceutical customer at our manufacturing facility using flow chemistry. We are experimenting with continuous downstream operations, including extraction, distillation, and crystallization, with a long-term objective to developing more flow applications in our commercial manufacturing.

items.statement: Inherent lumpiness in business due to shipment timing and purchase orders; growth should be viewed over 3-5 year horizon rather than quarterly
items.quote: Given the inherent lumpiness in the industry and the way the business operates, we believe it is more appropriate to look at the direction of the business over a three-to-five-year period.

items.statement: Secured EcoVadis Platinum rating 2026, placing company in top 1% worldwide for sustainability performance
items.quote: I am also pleased to report that we secured the prestigious EcoVadis Platinum rating 2026, placing us among the top 1% of the companies assessed worldwide for sustainability performance.

items.statement: Boston and Manchester offshore facilities acting as satellite centers to cultivate early relationships and bring larger business back to India; Boston P&L accretive; discovery revenue grown at 30-35% CAGR over last 4-5 years
items.quote: if you look at the discovery revenue it is probably in the last four, five years has grown at a CAGR of close around 30%-35%.

items.statement: Evolution from small molecule CRDMO to technology-led multi-modality partner; following Wuxi model of integrated discovery, FTE development, and commercial manufacturing; India currently in early stages of this opportunity
items.quote: We believe Sai is at an important point in evolution from being a strong small molecule CRDMO to becoming a technology-led, multi-modality partner with capabilities spanning discovery through commercial manufacturing.

items.statement: One customer received approval in FY26, two more have regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected in Q2 FY28
items.quote: With respect to the phase 3 pipeline, one of our customers received an approval during FY26, two more have regulatory milestones during this financial year, and one is expected in Q2 of FY28.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains healthy with financial flexibility to invest in growth opportunities while maintaining disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains healthy, and we continue to maintain the financial flexibility required to invest behind the opportunities we see across the business. We will continue to balance investments in future growth with disciplined capital allocation and returns.

items.statement: Biotech acquisitions and ~18 IPOs observed; expect capital to flow back into funding new biotech companies with leaner in-house capabilities supporting demand for CRDMO services
items.quote: In the biotech environment, we have seen several large acquisitions and about 18 IPOs in the As investors cash out, we expect capital to flow back into funding new biotech companies. The clear message we are picking up is that these new companies will be built with even leaner in-house capabilities, which should continue to support healthy demand for our sector.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% year-on-year for FY27 maintained
items.quote: We maintain our guidance of 20% revenue growth for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 11% plus maintained for FY27
items.quote: we maintain our 11% guidance for the year, which is one of the best in the industry.

items.statement: Order intake guidance of INR10,000+ crores for FY27 maintained
items.quote: And our overall order intake guidance remains the same. We will look at INR10,000 plus crores of new orders this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.7%, above the 11% guidance
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR203 crores, resulting in a healthy EBITDA margin of 11.7%, which is more than the guidance of 11% given at the start of the year.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of INR16,035 crores as of June 30, 2026, including L1 orders of INR400 crores
items.quote: As of June 30th, 2026, our unexecuted order book was INR16,035 crores, including L1 orders of INR400 crores.

items.statement: Quoted tenders worth more than INR20,000 crores expected to be declared in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: It is also noteworthy to note that we have quoted tenders worth more than INR20,000 crores, which will be declared in the coming quarter, that is Q2 and maybe part of Q3.

items.statement: Conductor brownfield expansion phase 1 ready, awaiting approvals, expected to start in Q2 FY27
items.quote: the factory phase 1 is ready and we have calibrated all the equipment. There are certain approvals required from the various approving authorities, and we are confident in Q2, we will start this.

items.statement: Greenfield tower factory at Butibori, Nagpur commenced commercial production on April 24, 2026
items.quote: Greenfield has already started the tower factory in Butibori, Nagpur, as I read out in my opening statement, has already started on April 24.

items.statement: INR200 crores capex plan for tools and plants, 70% to be utilized in FY27, balance in FY28
items.quote: this INR200 crores is predominantly for tools and plants to execute our projects, both in domestic and international, and it is going to be used in a staggered manner quarter-on-quarter. So, I would say 70-odd percent would be utilized this year and the balance will go to next year.

items.statement: Expanded manufacturing capabilities with new eco-friendly tower facility and ongoing tower and conductor plant expansions
items.quote: Together with our ongoing expansion across our tower and conductor plants, this significantly strengthens our manufacturing capabilities as well as to execute our robust order book and capitalize on future growth opportunities.

items.statement: Global electricity demand expected to nearly double by 2050; India's National Electricity Plan envisages 1,91,000 circuit km of transmission lines by 2032
items.quote: Global electricity demand is expected nearly double by 2050, driven by electrification, renewable energy adoption, AI, data centers, and rising energy consumption.

items.statement: Acquired Gactel turnkey projects to expand cooling tower EPC offering from NDCT to include IDCT tower solutions
items.quote: We also strengthened our diversified EPC platform through acquisition of Gactel turnkey projects, enhancing our capability on cooling tower EPC business.

items.statement: Evaluating strategic opportunities in BESS, data centers, and drones for mapping and survey
items.quote: BESS and data centers, we are keen to go ahead. If you see our investor presentation, it is already mentioned that it is something we are looking at in terms of seed marketing in the next few months.

items.statement: Entered Australian market for first supply of monopoles; global footprint now reaches 6 continents
items.quote: Additionally, we entered Australian market for the first supply of monopoles. With this, our global footprint has now reached 6 continents.

items.statement: Received 500 kV HVDC order from reputed developer in India
items.quote: Further, we received a 500 kV HVDC order from a reputed developer in India.

items.statement: Working capital days were 81 in FY26; targeting same level or sub-81 in FY27 despite Q1 collection delays
items.quote: working capital days, we were 81 last year. As CFO just mentioned, there have been some delays in collections, obviously, because of the disruptions globally and locally. So, we feel that we will be the same level or improve from 81 and will be sub-81 below.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA increased in Q1 due to delayed collections; expected to normalize to 0.33x by year-end
items.quote: net debt has increased on account of some delayed collections and working capital has been deployed more in the business, which is going to be normalized in Q2, and we are expecting all those to be realized in Q2.

items.statement: INR80 crores loan to related party Burberry, INR30 crores repaid last year, balance plus interest to be repaid by September 30, 2026
items.quote: It is INR80 crores loan, and it will be repaid before September 2026. That is the agreement.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to AA- Stable from India Ratings; now AA- from both CRISIL and India Ratings covering ~INR7,500 crores
items.quote: an upgrade of our long-term credit facility India Rating AA- Stable from India Ratings. So, this upgrade now, the company has long-term credit facility of AA- both from CRISIL and India Ratings, covering limit approximately INR7,500 crores.

items.statement: Board approved proposal to raise up to INR600 crores via QIP or other eligible securities, subject to approvals
items.quote: Board has approved a proposal to raise up to INR600 crores through a qualified institutional placement, QIP, or other eligible securities, subject to the necessary shareholders and regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR3 per equity share (150%) declared for FY27
items.quote: the board has declared an interim dividend of INR3 per equity share for the year '27.

items.statement: Granted 1,89,000 stock options under ESOP 2023 post quarter-end
items.quote: the Board has also approved the grant of 1,89,000 stock options under Transrail Lighting Employee Stock Option Plan 2023

items.statement: Won ET Edge Best Organisations to Work for 2026 Award and RoSPA Silver Award for transmission line projects in Africa
items.quote: we were honored by ET Edge Best Organisations to Work for 2026 Award in recognition of our growth rate, training and development, industry reputation, workplace culture, and business ethics.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 5% year-on-year to INR1,736 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Revenue from operations in Q1 FY2027 was INR1,736 crores Indian rupees, an increase of 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Profit after tax increased 3% year-on-year to INR108 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Profit after tax was INR108 crores, an increase of 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions including diesel, LDO, and procurement delays impacted Q1 manufacturing and revenue
items.quote: There were supply chain disruptions in our factory. As you know, diesel, LDO, and certain amount of delays have happened for procurement.

items.statement: Aspiration to achieve revenue of INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores by FY30
items.quote: Our objective remains unchanged: to build a stronger and more diversified and more profitable business while creating value for all stakeholders. We remain confident in our long -term growth roadmap and our aspiration of achieving revenue of INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores by FY’30.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth up to 10% YoY in FY27 if situation stabilizes
items.quote: we believe that in terms of top line, we will do quite well and we will be back on track and we will be able to deliver a growth year-on-year in the range of maybe up to 10%.

items.statement: Target to recover full price increments over full financial year for zero loss
items.quote: when we look at the entire financial year, the target is to recover in full all the price increments.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 10.4%, affected by higher energy, raw material costs and labour availability constraints
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 10.4% and was affected by higher energy and raw material costs along with labour availability constraints.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin improvement of about half a percentage point YoY in FY27 if price increments fully recovered
items.quote: if we do that, we will be able to for sure increase our overall EBITDA versus last year, probably by half a point, I would say it's something realistic but we will try for sure to do more than that.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient across agriculture, construction equipment and off-highway segments supported by infrastructure investments and mechanization trends
items.quote: On one hand, domestic demand remained resilient across the agriculture, construction equipment and broader off -highway segments, supported by continued infrastructure investments, healthy mechanization trends and sustained demand for higher performance equipment.

items.statement: Export markets face headwinds from geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and softer demand in certain markets
items.quote: On the other hand, global markets continued to face headwinds from geopolitical uncertainties, particularly the ongoing situation in West Asia, which resulted in supply chain disruptions, logistical challenges and softer demand in certain export markets.

items.statement: Order book encouraging, capacity expansion underway to meet market demand toward INR3,500-4,000 crore target
items.quote: we are seeing order book which is quite encouraging for us. So, for the capacity to meet the market demand, we are doing the debottlenecking and expansion of wherever we need capacities to meet the market demand in the direction towards INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: New paint shop construction commenced, additional investments in portal axle capacity and sub-assembly operations commissioned
items.quote: Construction of our new paint shop facility commenced during the quarter, while additional investments in portal axle capacity and sub -assembly operations were successfully commissioned.

items.statement: Expanding capacity for four-wheel drive axle solutions and tele boom handler programs, capacity additions linear with demand growth
items.quote: We continue to work closely with our customers and are expanding capacity to address anticipated demand growth.

items.statement: Commodity cost pass-through agreed in principle with customers, but time lag creates temporary margin gaps; transportation cost inflation also expected to be passed through
items.quote: It's a pass-through. That is what has been agreed and customers have been told that it has to be a pass-through. In principle, many of them have also agreed, but still there are certain wait-and-watch situations.

items.statement: Raw material localization at 74% in Q1, down from ~78% due to temporary imports for supply shortages; target to return to 86-88% as local supply chain normalizes
items.quote: During the quarter, raw material localization stood at approximately 74% and we remain committed to increasing this further over the next few months and years.

items.statement: Domestic agriculture revenue grew 32% YoY, construction grew 20% YoY in Q1; four-wheel drive tractor penetration increasing, targeting 30-40% by FY30
items.quote: In agri business there is 32% growth, Q1 versus Q1. On the construction business domestic, there is a 20% growth.

items.statement: Supplying to all major Indian tractor OEMs (36 customers); new projects indicated by two prototypes under development
items.quote: We already have 36 customers, right from Mahindra to Kartar or Captain, we have covered almost all tractor manufacturers in India.

items.statement: Exports declined 14% YoY in Q1 due to geopolitical disruptions; expect recovery from Q2 back to FY25-26 levels; export mix ~33-35% of revenue long-term
items.quote: This robust domestic performance helped offset the temporary weakness in exports, which declined by approximately 14% year -on-year due to geopolitical disruptions and supply chain challenges in certain international markets.

items.statement: Turkey higher horsepower transmission serial production started; market volatile due to inflation, volumes growing steadily quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: This is achieved as an important milestone during the quarter, with the commencement of serial production for a Turkish customer.

items.statement: Focus on ensuring profitable growth to generate healthy cash flow and avoid working capital tension during capex phase
items.quote: We have to make sure that the growth is profitable to generate healthy cash flow. We have to make sure that we do get unbalanced and avoid it to create tension in terms of working capital.

items.statement: Funding growth and expansion while ensuring profitable growth and adequate returns on capex
items.quote: We have to make sure that our growth is sustainable because we are going ahead for some relevant amount of capex that needs adequate returns.

items.statement: Backhoe loader market grew 14% YoY in Q1; Carraro driveline sales to OEMs grew 18% YoY, outperforming market
items.quote: Overall, backhoe loader sales by Indian OEMs, including domestic sales and exports, grew by approximately 14% year -on-year during the quarter. During the same period, Carraro's sales of drivelines to OEMs increased by approximately 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Four-wheel drive tractor penetration gaining large-scale acceptance, no change in 30-40% target by FY30
items.quote: There is no change in the pattern of growth in the four-wheel drive. That segment is growing and that is gaining momentum. More than that, that is gaining large -scale acceptance in the market as well.

items.statement: Near-term uncertainty from geopolitical developments, global demand conditions, inflation, supply chain disruptions; labour shortages at supplier tier impacting deliveries
items.quote: Looking ahead, while geopolitical developments and global demand conditions may continue to create near-term uncertainty, we remain constructive on the outlook for our business.

items.statement: Biggest risk is demand stability and funding profitable growth; monitoring order book sustainability and inflation pass-through
items.quote: first of all, is that our order book, our demand remains stable. We want to make sure that whatever we see ahead is something which is really there, something that we can sustain and something in which we can invest for.

items.statement: Labour availability constraints at supplier level (migrant labour for casting/fettling), not at Carraro India; using overtime to manage
items.quote: Shortages are for migrant labour. So, to answer your question, within Ca rraro India, we are not facing any hurdle or constraint because of manpower in our

items.statement: Engineering services business gaining momentum; INR33 million assignments completed in July 2026; discussions with another prospective customer progressing
items.quote: Assignments worth approximately INR33 million that were under execution at quarter-end were completed in July 2026. Discussions with another prospective customer are also progressing, supporting further growth in this business.

items.statement: Recognized by Mahindra & Mahindra for performance and partnership
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that during the quarter, Carraro India was recognized by Mahindra & Mahindra for our performance and partnership, which reflects our team's commitment to quality, delivery and customer satisfaction.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin expected to increase 4-5% from solar plant commissioning in Q4 FY27
items.quote: with our capex of about INR60 crores with a 3-year payback, I think that itself will increase the margin to maybe translate into 4% to 5% increase in my view.

items.statement: Invested INR60 crores in captive solar plant with battery storage for Pune hotels targeting Q4 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: We have now invested around INR60 crores in captive solar plant with battery storage for our Pune hotels targeting commissioning in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Solar capacity expansion at Raaya to 80% by April 2027 with further capacity at Conrad and Anantara
items.quote: At Raaya, we are i ncreasing solar capacity, taking the resort to about 80% solar with battery backup by April 2027, with further capacity being added at Conrad and Anantara

items.statement: India EBITDA margin expanded to 36% from 35% YoY despite higher power and wage costs
items.quote: India EBITDA grew 16% to INR74 crores. And most importantly, our India margin expanded 36% from 35% even after absorbing higher power and wage costs during this quarter.

items.statement: Maldives EBITDA declined 32% YoY to INR32 crores due to diesel price spike
items.quote: EBITDA was INR32 crores, down 32%, almost entirely due to fuel.

items.statement: Maldives solar program expected to save USD1.5 million annually, roughly 2.5% of Maldives EBITDA
items.quote: Together, we expect this to save us around $1.5 million a year, roughly 2.5 percentage of Maldives EBITDA and to protect the portfolio against exactly this kind of diesel shocks in the future.

items.statement: India hospitality revenue grew 13% YoY to INR203 crores driven by corporate demand, MICE, and premium leisure
items.quote: In India, business delivered strong quarter yet again. Revenue grew 13% to INR203 crores supported by resilient corporate demand, strong MICE activity, and premium leisure.

items.statement: Maldives revenue grew 5% YoY to INR218 crores despite war-related cancellations in April
items.quote: In Maldives, revenue grew 5%, INR218 crores, a resilient outcome given the war-related cancellations early in the quarter and the sharp recovery that followed.

items.statement: India occupancy grew to 67%, up 7% YoY with ADR up 8% driving 20% RevPAR growth
items.quote: Our occupancy grew to 67%, up about 7% is reflecting very, very strong demand both in Pune, Bengaluru, and Goa. Most importantly, the important point is we added occupancy and rate at the same time.

items.statement: July Maldives tourist arrivals recovered to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights vs 170 previously
items.quote: July tourist arrivals have actually recovered to 2025 levels. And this is with only 27 disrupted flights. This indicates that travel disruption seems to be easing.

items.statement: Acquired Sahyadri Hills Wellness Estate (Ritz-Carlton Reserve) for INR281 crores equity, EV INR466 crores, targeting >12% yield-on-cost
items.quote: We have acquired it 100% at an equity consideration of around INR281 crores and enterprise value of around INR466 crores, targeting a yield-on-cost above 12%.

items.statement: Promoter group ROFO pipeline of 1,114 keys provides long-term visibility toward 4,000+ keys ambition
items.quote: Alongside these, our promoter group ROFO pipeline of 1,114 keys spanning JW Marriott, Navi Mumbai and 3 Moxy hotels gives us long-term visibility towards our ambition of 4,000-plus keys.

items.statement: Diesel prices reached 2.1x pre-war levels, driving fuel and ancillary cost increase of INR19 crores in Maldives
items.quote: Diesel prices reached roughly 2.1x pre-war levels, driving a fuel and ancillary costs increase of around INR19 crores.

items.statement: Pune solar plant expected to reduce energy bill by ~45%, positive impact of 5-6% on India EBITDA with 3-year payback
items.quote: We expect this to reduce our Pune energy bill by close to 45%, a positive impact of 5% to 6% on India EBITDA with a payback of roughly 3 years.

items.statement: 70% of Pune hotels' electricity already from green sources, targeting 85% after solar plant commissioning
items.quote: Around 70% of electricity used by our Pune hotels portfolio already comes from green sources, which insulates us from tariff increase. We have now invested around INR60 crores in captive solar plant with battery storage for our Pune hotels targeting commissioning in Q4 FY27, which will raise our green energy contribution to around 85%.

items.statement: Raaya Maldives to generate 17 hours of solar capacity daily, first resort in Maldives to do so
items.quote: Raaya will be able to generate and operate around 17 hours of solar capacity and will be the first resort in Maldives to do so.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced to 7.2% for India portfolio and 6.1% for Maldives portfolio
items.quote: I'm pleased to report a continuous improvement in our debt profile, with the cost of funds for Indian portfolio reducing to 7.2%, while the cost of funds for our Maldivian asset declined to 6.1%, an improvement of 12 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.quote: The passenger vehicle demand remained strong during quarter under review despite geopolitical tensions in West Asia, elevated inflation within the RBI's target band, and heat waves across select regions.

items.quote: LCV demand remained robust, driven by healthy last mile logistics, sustained e-commerce and FMCG demand and a low base effect that supported growth momentum.

items.quote: We've gained market share, yes. There are some new products introduced to new OEMs. So we've gained market share.

items.quote: the Chassis Systems business, which we've acquired was a Bosch sister company. And in terms of synergy effects, we see very minimal improvements in costs and synergy effects. items.quote: We anticipate closing financial year '27 on a stronger note compared to financial year '26, supported by the partial contribution from the new capacities in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Capex plan includes fabric capacity expansion of 35 million meters and spinning capacity addition of 74,000 spindles, progressing as per schedule.
items.quote: Going forward, our -- one of our future growth driver will be our capacity addition, which is going -- progressing as schedule with the expansion of our fabric capacity by another 35 million meters and spinning capacity by additional 74,000 spindles.

items.statement: Spinning capacity utilization at 98% and woven fabric over 92% in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: In FY27, our spinning capacity was operating at 98% utilization and woven fabric over 92% utilization.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 17.78% in Q1 FY27, up 376 bps YoY and 261 bps QoQ, driven by higher realizations and cost savings.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for this quarter stood at 17.78% against Q1 FY26 margins of 14.02% is an increase of 376 bps on a year-on-year basis and 261 bps on quarter-on-quarter basis. That is due to improved realization and cost saving initiatives.

items.statement: Yarn spreads improved from INR110 in Q4 FY26 to INR130 in Q1 FY27 and are sustaining in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: In the first quarter, I think in the last quarter of the last financial year, the spreads were in the range of about INR110. And now it is in the range of or INR130.

items.statement: Cotton prices increased 8-10% in Q1 FY27 due to lower global production and supply chain challenges; Indian cotton parity with international prices improved.
items.quote: Cotton prices increased during quarter 1 by about 8% to 10%, primarily driven by overall lower global production, global supply chain and logistics challenges due to West Asia war.

items.statement: New fabric capacity will focus on solid dyed and yarn dyed fabrics; no capacity addition in printing segment.
items.quote: The capacity which we are adding is both in the weaving as well as finishing. So we are adding both weaving capacity as well as finishing capacity. And this new capacity will be for solid dyes, solid dyed fabrics, also the yarn dyed fabrics as well.

items.statement: Demand improved due to removal of US tariffs, China importing more cotton yarn, and domestic demand growth; expect continued better demand for fabric and yarn.
items.quote: We anticipate that the demand for fabric and yarn will continue to be better, supported by demand coming from growth across the downstream sector and the consolidation of the spinning industry.

items.statement: Exports contributed 65% of revenue in Q1 FY27; India-UK FTA and potential EU FTA expected to support exports.
items.quote: In terms of geographical split of revenue, export contributed nearly 65% and domestic 35% of the total revenues during the quarter.

items.statement: Working capital cycle remained similar to previous quarters with no major change.
items.quote: There is no major change as such. The cycle has more or less remained similar as compared to the last quarters or the financial year.

items.statement: Company is deploying internal accruals and taking loans for growth capex; no buyback planned.
items.quote: We are deploying our capital for the growth purposes, internal accruals as well as we are also taking some loans as well.

items.statement: Buyback not prudent at this stage as company is in growth phase deploying capital for expansion.
items.quote: I think at this point of time we are in a growth phase. We are deploying our capital for the growth purposes, internal accruals as well as we are also taking some loans as well. So it would not be some it would not be prudent for us to go for buyback at this point of time.

items.statement: Renewable power expansion expected operational by end of Q3 FY27; already contributed INR1.2-1.5 crore in Q1 FY27, annual EBITDA savings expected ~INR50 crore.
items.quote: The renewable power expansion plan is also going as per schedule and expected to be operational by the end of Q3 '27.

items.statement: New spinning capacity to ramp up by March 31, 2027; fabric capacity full ramp-up may take 1-2 quarters into FY28.
items.quote: I think we would have ramped up all our capacities by 31st of March of this financial year. So that will be there and fabric 100% ramp up may take a quarter or two more in FY28.

items.statement: Incremental revenue from new capacity estimated at INR200-300 crore plus existing revenue slightly higher than FY26; fabric revenue expected to reach INR1,200 crore in FY28 from INR700+ crore in FY26.
items.quote: We should be already with our new expansion should add another 200 crores to 300 crores to our revenues going forward -- going in this whatever capacity we add. Plus the existing revenue should be slightly higher than the last year.

items.statement: Management maintains EBITDA margin guidance range of 16-20%; expects to remain in this band with product mix improvement and power savings.
items.quote: I guided or have informed that the kind of product mix which our company has, we should be in the range of 16% to 20%. I still maintain the same, that we should be -- kind of product profile as well as the kind of cost metrics we have, we should be still remain in this range.

items.statement: Fabric share of revenue to increase from 20-21% to ~30%, adding 100-150 bps to overall margins.
items.quote: At this point of time our top line consists about 20% to 21% of our fabric, which you should go up to about 30% going forward. And this should add about 100 to 150 bps to our margins.

items.statement: Weaving capacity to start in couple of months, processing by Diwali, spinning by December; most capacities up in 4-5 months.
items.quote: We will start our weaving capacities in couple of month's time. We should be starting the same. Processing capacities will take then further one and a half more month to start which is around Diwali and spinning capacity should be on stream by around December.

items.statement: India-UK FTA implemented; EU FTA expected to create level playing field for Indian textile exports.
items.quote: The recently implemented India U.K. FTA is also expected to support India's exports by opening up new sourcing and export opportunities for the Indian textile sector.

items.statement: Knitted fabric utilization at 55-60% due to US market uncertainties and tariff changes; pre-tariff utilization was 60-65%.
items.quote: This is in the range of about 55% to 60% at this point of time. We have not yet reached the 65% level the usual utilization pre this US tariff regime used to be around 60% to 65%.

items.statement: Indian cotton now at -1 to -2% vs Cotlook Index, improved from +5-7% premium in 2023-24; delta change of 7-8%.
items.quote: So in '23, '24 our cotton prices were about five to even 7% higher than the Cotlook Index and now it is at this point of time at a similar level minus 1 or 2% the Cotlook Index level. So the overall delta change has been in the range of 7% to 8%.

items.statement: China cotton yarn imports from India increased from 90-100 mn kg in 2025 to 110-115 mn kg in 2026; expected to continue due to lower Chinese crop.
items.quote: We used -- we were India was exporting in the range of 90 to 100 million kgs during the whole of year '25. In '26 in the calendar year '26 China started to import and it went up to 110 to 115 million.

items.statement: No new capex planned until after FY28; evaluating options for next growth phase including garmenting and home textiles.
items.quote: As of now, whatever capex we have announced, we are not considering any new capex in the next FY28 this is all done, till FY28.

items.statement: Company evaluating garmenting entry organically or inorganically; waiting for right opportunity and conditions.
items.quote: Definitely, we have to look to -- if we have to, as I've highlighted here that the future will be dependent on how our garmenting industry performs. Definitely we have to look for that particular field as well.

items.statement: Cotton crop size expected at 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26 season, similar to previous year; next season acreage ~same, quality currently good but dependent on rains.
items.quote: Last year I think the we have closed at about 320 lakh bales . Nearly we will close it over, normal pressing bales I am talking about, which is more or less equal to what we had in the previous year.

items.statement: Blended power cost expected at INR5.50/unit once solar capacity fully operational (covering ~60% of requirement).
items.quote: This should be once we have our complete capacity up and running, which would be constituting about 65% of our -- 60 to 60 -- about 60% of our overall requirements our blended cost should be in the range of about INR5.50.

items.statement: Fabric business passing only raw material cost increases, not improving margins like yarn business; expects improvement with settling cotton prices and global demand.
items.quote: In the case of fabric business only whatever raw material increase actually has happened in the cotton that is only getting passed on. We are not able to improve upon the margins as we are able to improve upon the margins in the yarn business.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volumes achieved 16-29% of full-year guidance; FY27 mining guidance of 3.4 million tons maintained
items.quote: We remain on track to deliver our FY '27 guidance, with Q1 volume achieving between 16% to 29% of full year guidance.

items.statement: Pellet production guidance of 4.0 million tons for FY27 likely to be slightly lower due to plant shutdown
items.quote: Although we haven't revised, we are still evaluating but you can expect the volumes to be slightly on the lower side.

items.statement: Beneficiation plant capex of INR218 crores incurred till June 2026; CRM project capex revised to INR1,100 crores (INR550 crores debt, balance internal accruals)
items.quote: The project is now targeted to be, commissioned by December '27, with planned capex of INR1,100 crores to be funded through INR550 crores of debt and balance through internal accruals.

items.statement: BESS project capex of INR501 crores incurred till date; remaining INR700-800 crores to be spent in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: On the battery storage side, we've already spent about close to INR500 crores. The remaining CapEx of close to INR700 crores, INR800 crores will be spent in this year and next year.

items.statement: Total remaining capex for FY27 and FY28 estimated at close to INR2,000 crores excluding steel plant
items.quote: Overall we envisage a CapEx of close to about INR2,000 crores for remaining FY'27 and entire FY'28.

items.statement: 4.7 million ton expanded pellet capacity operated at 77% utilization in Q1 FY27; expected to ramp to 80-85% in FY27
items.quote: The 4.7 million ton expanded pellet capacity operated at 77% utilization in Q1 and is expected to ramp up to around 80%-85% in FY '27 as the operations scale up.

items.statement: Beneficiation plant commissioning expected in Q3 FY27; Ari Dongri mine ramp-up from Q3, full scale from FY28
items.quote: The Ari Dongri iron ore mine expansion is progressing as planned, with ramp-up expected from Q3, following commissioning of beneficiation plant, and full scale operation targeted from FY '28.

items.statement: CRM complex relocation to Maharashtra; land allotment expected by end August 2026, construction start October 2026, commissioning by December 2027
items.quote: We expect the land allotment approval by end of August '26. The project construction activities are expected to start from October 2026. The project is now targeted to be, commissioned by December '27.

items.statement: BESS project scheduled for commissioning in Q1 FY28; soil testing done, compound wall construction underway
items.quote: The 20 gigawatt base project is progressing well and is scheduled for commissioning in Q1 '28.

items.statement: 25 MW solar plant commissioned May 2026; 100 MW under construction targeting September 2026 commissioning; 45 MW storage targeted for Q3 FY26
items.quote: The 25 megawatt solar plant has been commissioned in May 2026, and 100 megawatt project is under construction, targeted for commissioning by September '26.

items.statement: Exported two vessels of pellets in June-July 2026 at ~INR9,000 ex-plant; open to exports based on domestic demand and pricing
items.quote: We did export two vessels in July -- in June and July, and then we had to stop exports because of shutting of our another pellet plant.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7%; margins softened sequentially due to higher iron ore and coal costs
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margin stood at 19.1% and 12.7%, respectively. Except margin improvement, we expect margin improvement from Q4 FY '27, following commissioning of beneficiation plant.

items.statement: CRM complex margin expected to improve to 10-11% with Maharashtra incentives (vs earlier 7-8%)
items.quote: Yes, we should, Yes, exactly. We should touch 10%-11% with incentives.

items.statement: Iron ore cost increase: 75% from market purchases, 25% from imported coal (coal up from INR10,500 to INR13,000)
items.quote: Iron ore contributes about 75% of the increase cost and 25% was the imported coal. Just to be very specific in terms of the number, our imported coal cost was about INR10,500 for Q4 and early Q1. Now, it's almost touched INR13,000.

items.statement: Gas price up 40-45% due to PNGRB guidelines; pellet plant commercially unviable at current pellet prices (~INR8,700)
items.quote: the value -- the purchase value of the gas has gone up drastically. It's almost up by 40%-45%. So, purchasing iron ore from the market and also getting gas at higher price, that makes pellet plant operation commercially unviable

items.statement: Pellet prices expected to hover INR9,000-10,000 ex-Raipur long-term; currently ~INR10,000
items.quote: I still feel in the longer term, the prices will keep hovering between INR9,000 to INR10,000 ex-Raipur.

items.statement: Iron ore mining volume declined due to overburden dumping constraints from delayed tree-cutting permission on government land
items.quote: Our iron ore mining volume declined primarily due to space constraints for dumping of overburden, in view of delay in obtaining tree-cutting permission in the additional allotted land.

items.statement: Mining cost currently INR3,000-3,500/ton; target below INR2,700/ton from FY28 via beneficiation and EV deployment
items.quote: Currently our mining costs stand about, you know, between INR3,000 to INR3,500, depending on the production. So, our target is to bring down the mining cost below INR2,700 from FY28.

items.statement: Market iron ore purchase to reduce from 25-30% in Q3 to <10% in Q4 FY27; 100% captive by FY28
items.quote: Q3, you can say we'll still -- so we'll be running at pellet plant at full capacity. The purchase of market will be still about 25%-30%. And from Q4 gradually, it should come down below 10%, and finally in FY28, it should be 100% captive.

items.statement: Value-added products (sponge iron, billet, rolled) recorded healthy YoY growth in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our value-added product also recorded healthy YoY growth in Q1, led by sponge iron, billet, and rolled production.

items.statement: Galvanized product volumes lower in Q1 due to monsoon seasonality; expected to recover post-monsoon
items.quote: Usually, being a monsoon, the delivery is on the lower side, the projects get delayed. So that is why the galvanizing products you can see is on the lower side.

items.statement: CRM relocation to Maharashtra driven by automobile hub demand and better industrial policy incentives (SGST benefits)
items.quote: Maharashtra being an automobile hub, right? And a lot of our products will be consumed in automobile. So, we expect a -- you know, a demand growth local in Maharashtra, which will add to the benefit of CRM.

items.statement: Global iron ore prices resilient at $95-105/ton; Simandou project presents downside risk but Indian prices stable ~INR5,500 ex-mine
items.quote: Globally, iron ore prices remain resilient, close to about $95 tons to $105 tons, supported by healthy mill margin and inventory restocking, despite peaking Chinese steel consumption.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant (1 MTPA) kept in abeyance due to water allocation delays (9.4 MCM) and EC/consent delays; treat as optional for medium term
items.quote: The company has decided to keep the proposed 1 million ton integrated steel project in abeyance due to on-ground challenges and delays in approval, especially the approval for water allocation.

items.statement: Boria Tibbu mine expansion TOFR filing planned; capacity to increase from 0.7 MTPA to 4 MTPA by FY31 with 40% yield beneficiation
items.quote: We expect Boria Tibbu expansion to happen somewhere in probably April '30, you know, FY31. That is the plan. The current mining capacity is 0.7 million. From next year onwards, Boria Tibbu will be running at full capacity of 0.7 million, currently is running at about 0.2 million, 0.3 million. And eventually in FY31, we will be taking the mining capacity from 0.7 million to 4 million tons.

items.statement: No new debt needed for current projects (CRM, BESS, mining) as steel plant on hold; sufficient free cash flows to fund capex
items.quote: Since it's on hold now, so we don't need to borrow any money for funding our current projects. We are very much -- we have sufficient free cash flows to fund the entire projects now.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed credit rating at AA- Stable for long-term facilities
items.quote: The CRISIL has reaffirmed the credit rating of the company at AA- Stable for long-term facilities.

items.statement: CO2 emission intensity: 3.180 tCO2/ton steel (CBAM) in Q1 FY27, down 1.9% QoQ and 4.2% YoY; 2.485 tCO2/ton (WSA) stable vs 2.492 target
items.quote: Under CBAM technology based on the total carbon basis, emission intensity stood at 3.180 CO2 ton in Q1 FY27, improving 1.9% quarter-on-quarter and 4.2% Y-o-Y from 3.244 ton fixed carbon.

items.statement: EV fleet expanded: 15 dumpers, 24 loaders, 15 excavators; reduced operating cost ~75%, CO2 emissions ~88% vs diesel
items.quote: The adoption electricity transportation has reduced operating cost by nearly 75%, CO2 emission by around 88% as compared to the conventional diesel vehicle.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining double-digit EBITDA margin on full-year basis
items.quote: We remain confident of sustaining the double-digit EBITDA margin on a full year basis as well.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% EBITDA margin by FY28
items.quote: As we have guided earlier, our first aim is to really target between 10% to 12% by FY28.

items.statement: Aim to accelerate FY28 revenue target of INR6,000 crores
items.quote: Our endeavor is to accelerate the milestone revenue which you specified for FY28, and we keep working towards that.

items.statement: CAGR target of 12-14% but current traction suggests better
items.quote: In terms of top line, we have been always saying that our CAGR would be in the range of 12% to 14%. But if you look at better years, we have done more than that.

items.statement: Capex commitment of INR200-250 crores for FY27 across geographies
items.quote: Further, we are in the process of outlining capex commitment of approximately INR200 to INR250 crores for FY27 across geographies.

items.statement: Bangladesh expansion adds 6-7 million pieces, taking group capacity to ~108 million pieces
items.quote: These projects expected to give us almost about 6 to 7 million pieces of additional capacity in Bangladesh, and that will take our total group installed capacity to almost 108 million pieces.

items.statement: India Bihar second shed (450 machines) operational by September-October
items.quote: Construction for the second shed, manufacturing shed in Bihar has already commenced. We are expecting completion in next couple of months.

items.statement: Vietnam land acquisition completed for future greenfield expansion
items.quote: The land acquisition in Vietnam is also completed in line with what we have communicated earlier.

items.statement: Group installed capacity target of 125-130 million pieces by 2028
items.quote: By 2028, we had forecasted that we should be having around 125 to 130 million pieces capacity.

items.statement: US consumer behaviour remains healthy despite geopolitical tensions
items.quote: On the brighter side, what we find is that despite all these war and inflation, the US consumer behaviour remained healthy.

items.statement: Retailers placing shorter-term orders due to logistics disruptions
items.quote: So, they are more in terms of what is selling, and read the sales and then place the business, that's the kind of trend that we see.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 10.7% in Q1 FY27, up 140 bps YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 10.7%, up by 140 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin dropped to 6.6% due to Haryana wage hikes of 38% and 21%
items.quote: The drop in EBITDA margin despite revenue growth is because of higher wage cost in all factories in Haryana post wage revision by state government.

items.statement: India standalone EBITDA margin target of high single-digit to double-digit
items.quote: So, yes, the target is to really have high single-digit and double-digit EBITDA in Indian operations as well.

items.statement: Healthy order book with better capacity utilization in India vs last year
items.quote: At Pearl, we are having a healthy order book and have better utilization of capacity in India as compared to last year.

items.statement: US Section 301 tariff: 10% additional on India/Bangladesh/Indonesia, 12.5% on Vietnam
items.quote: Now we have an additional 10% for India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, and a 12.5% on top of the MFN tariff for Vietnam.

items.statement: Haryana and Noida minimum wages raised 38% and 21% respectively
items.quote: Haryana and Noida both raised the minimum wage significantly, 38% and 21% respectively, which caused another ripple into our cost structure.

items.statement: Container shortages and high spot freight rates before peak shipping season
items.quote: Even before the peak shipping season, we are seeing a shortage of containers and the shipping lines capacity shortages resulting in delays and high spot prices of freight.

items.statement: Q1 realization INR735/piece driven by outerwear seasonality; full-year FY26 average INR643
items.quote: Last year, we closed an average realization of INR643 per piece. And so, if you're comparing an average of full year with the quarter 1, that's maybe not the right comparison.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 51.5% from 46% YoY due to high value-added product mix
items.quote: There is actual improvement in terms of the volume growth led by the high value-added margin products, which we had in overseas location, which has led to improvement in the gross profit.

items.statement: Growth driven by wallet share expansion with existing customers across 7 product categories
items.quote: Our strategy as Pearl Global, we are doing almost about 7 different category of product. So, that means you can say almost about 70%, 75% of our apparel store, all the product that is selling, Pearl can give them that.

items.statement: UK FTA driving significant jump in UK business by end of FY27
items.quote: In terms of UK business, yes, you will -- by end of this year, you will see a significant jump in the UK business that we do as a group.

items.statement: India-UK FTA effective July 15, 2026; EU FTA targeted for early 2027
items.quote: The implementation of India-UK free trade agreement which went effective 15th of July 2026 is a significant positive development for Indian exports. Now the focus will be on the implementation of European Union FTA by the beginning of 2027.

items.statement: Board approved 1:1 bonus share issue subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board of Directors have approved, subject to shareholder approval, the issue of 1 fully paid-up bonus equity share for every 1 fully paid-up equity share.

items.statement: Japan apparel imports from China fell from 65% to 49%; Vietnam at 17.4%, Bangladesh at 4.3%
items.quote: Clothing import from China to Japan, which used to be around 65% plus, has now fallen down to 50%. So, it's a 15% drop that has happened, and this is the first time in 31 years.

items.statement: Targets 10x revenue growth over 10 years (~20% CAGR)
items.quote: So, we are seeing 10x growth in 10 years, which turns out to be about 20% a year is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Pipeline healthy; procurement cycles longer but demand intact
items.quote: Our opportunity pipeline remains healthy. Customer engagement is robust, and we are increasingly participating in larger and more strategic transformation programs.

items.statement: Booked Rs 120+ crore new wins and renewals in Q1
items.quote: During the quarter, ADSL has booked orders for Rs. 120-plus crore towards new wins as well as renewals for multiyear contracts.

items.statement: Leadership changes: Nehal Shah to Joint MD, Paresh Shah to Chief Innovation Officer, Arun Pathak hired as CEO Cloud Infrastructure India & Middle East
items.quote: the new role, I have been entrusted with the responsibility o f Joint Managing Director. Paresh Shah has transitioned into a newly created role of Chief Innovation Officer to lead our AI and technology transformation agenda. And we are delighted to welcome Arun Pathak as CEO of Cloud Infrastructure Services for India and Middle East

items.statement: Trailing 12-month revenue crossed Rs 1,000 crore (Rs 1,009 crore)
items.quote: Our trailing 12 months revenue have now crossed the Rs. 1,000 crore mark, reaching to Rs. 1,009 crore.

items.statement: Audit report unmodified with no qualifications for first time since comprehensive review
items.quote: For the first time since the comprehensive review commenced, the audit report carries no qualifications or observations.

items.statement: Investing in AI, talent, leadership and sales engine for next growth phase
items.quote: We are investing on people. We are investing on technology where we are doing a lot of investments on AI to make sure that our service portfolio is AI ready.

items.statement: Margin pressure from customer discounting in anticipation of AI automation; competitive intensity in US market
items.quote: Every large company is also facing the cost pressure because every customer wants in anticipation of the automation norm, they are trying to discount the pricin g from the now itself. So, margins are definitely under pressure for everybody

items.statement: Finance costs rose modestly due to higher working capital deployment and large projects entering execution
items.quote: Finance costs also increased modestly due to higher working capital deployment and as large projects moved into the execution phase.

items.statement: US subsidiary funds reclassified from debt to equity in FY26, eliminating quarterly FX revaluation
items.quote: As part of the governance and accounting measures completed during FY26, funds deployed in our U.S. subsidiary were reclassified from debt to equity.

items.statement: Embedding AI across service portfolio to create outcome-driven offerings
items.quote: As we continue to embed AI across our services and solutions, we are not only enhancing operational efficiency but also creating differentiated outcome-driven offerings that will define the next phase of Allied Digital's growth.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crores D2C revenue by FY29 with at least 15% operating margin from that segment
items.quote: We remain committed to achieving INR1,000 crores of direct-to-consumer revenue by FY29 with an operating margin of at least 15% from this segment.

items.statement: Expects working capital improvements of approximately INR250 crores and operating cash flow over INR300 crores in FY27
items.quote: The initiatives currently underway are expected to deliver working capital improvements of approximately INR250 crores in the current financial year and generate cash flow from operations of more than INR300 crores during the year.

items.statement: Projects bottom line growth greater than 30% for FY27 despite muted revenue growth due to exiting unprofitable lines
items.quote: Our expectation is to -- that bottom line should grow more than 30% for the year. Revenue growth may be muted because as stated earlier, we are exiting certain unprofitable lines of businesses.

items.statement: Expects customer brand revenue reduction of INR300-400 crores on annualized basis from exiting low-quality businesses
items.quote: on an annualized basis, this will result in an approx imately INR300 crores to INR400 crores reduction in revenue. The customers that we are exiting would result in INR300 crores to INR400 crores reduction in revenue

items.statement: Plans to add 4 Jean Dousset retail stores in FY27, reaching 7 total stores by year-end
items.quote: Following the encouraging response to our New York store and the opening of our San Francisco store location in July 2026, we currently operate 3 Jean Dousset retail stores. And during FY27, we intend to add 4 more locations.

items.statement: Jean Dousset store payback period less than 1 year, profitable from month 2-3
items.quote: And currently, based on the unit economics, we see a payback of less than 1 year for the JD stores. So very optimistic. And obviously, we're watching the numbers very carefully as we ramp up the store rollout of Jean Dousset meaningfully.

items.statement: Plans to add 6 more Jean Dousset stores in FY28 after reaching 7 stores in FY27
items.quote: Currently, our business plan is to get to 7 stores by the end of the current financial year. And then the plan would be to add 6 more stores in the following year. Currently, that's the plan for '27 and '28.

items.statement: Owned brand revenue grew 29% YoY to INR89 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR69 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Coming specifically to our owned brand. Revenue increased by 29% year-on-year to reach INR89 crores from INR69 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 22% YoY to INR50 crores in Q1 FY27; owned brand EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 10%
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 22% year-on-year to reach INR50 crores, compared with INR41 crores in Q1 FY26. EBITDA from owned brands grew to 11.5% from 10% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated margins dipped from 7.7% to 7.2% due to strategic exit of low-margin businesses and bullion sales
items.quote: And I think this would be comp arable. And like -for-like this reduction is on account of the strategic choices that we've made to exit certain businesses which we've communicated earlier

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 220 from 253 days YoY, a 33-day reduction in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our working capital efficiency improved meaningfully during the quarter with working capital days reducing to 220 days from 253 days in Q1 FY26, representing an improvement of 33 days year-on-year.

items.statement: Exiting customer brand relationships with high consignment/receivable days where cost of capital exceeds EBITDA
items.quote: we made a s trategic decision to exit certain customers, which would actually lead to meaningful reduction in working capital. While doing that, we've sort of ensured that this should not have any impact on our bottom line

items.statement: Rationalized licensed brand portfolio to focus primarily on Disney license; exited NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter licenses
items.quote: So on the licensed brand segment, we were operating a very wide portfolio of brands and even within this portfolio, what we've done is we've rationalized some of the licenses and the focus going forward is going to be primarily on the Disney relationship, and the Disney license.

items.statement: Owned brand focus narrowed to 3 power brands: Jean Dousset, WithClarity, and Disney licensed brand
items.quote: The 3 brands that will be most meaningful will be Jean Dousset, WithClarity and in the licensing segment, Disney. And these and the renewed strategic focus on these brands will allow us to expand profitability and grow profitability going forward.

items.statement: Customer brand segment operates across value spectrum USD50 to USD3,000; owned brands target 3 tiers: Disney ~USD400, WithClarity ~USD3,000, Jean Dousset ~USD8,000 AOV
items.quote: For our owned brands, we sort of have a 3-tiered approach, right? The license brands have an average order value of around USD400, for WithClarity, it's about USD3,000, and for Jean Dousset, it's USD8,000.

items.statement: Applying for tariff refunds on US exports; expects to share refunds with customers; details in coming quarters
items.quote: We are in the process of applying for tariff refunds and we do expect to get some refunds for tariffs. I think we will have to obviously share some of those refunds with our customers as well. So we will -- I think we should know more in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Forex loss of ~INR13 crores in Q1 due to currency appreciation; hedged on rupee expenditures but working capital is dollar-denominated
