items.statement: No capital allocation for wires manufacturing; using outsourced model; greenfield plant planned for next-gen capability.
items.quote: as of now, we are not putting up a plan for manufacturing wires, so it's not really a capital allocation issue

items.statement: Monsoon impacts solar execution (installation delays) but not demand; government payments on track and accelerating.
items.quote: The monsoon impacts insofar as execution is concerned. So far as solar pumps is concerned, if it's raining very heavily in an area, obviously you can't go and install a solar pump because the place would be wet.

items.statement: Solar rooftop revenue recognition on installation basis; dispatches ongoing but revenue expected in Q2 as installations complete.
items.quote: The revenue recognition for solar rooftop, we follow a methodology on installation basis. So, dispatches from our end are ongoing. It's been moving in the right trend, but revenue is recognised when the installation gets completed, which we're expecting to happen in Q2.

items.statement: Renewable business EBITDA margin similar to company EBITDA margin; gross margin lower but installation partner model keeps EBITDA in line.
items.quote: On the EBITDA line, it is similar.

items.statement: Government pays 40% upfront on solar rooftop orders upon product demonstration; balance paid by MNRE after installation.
items.quote: The payment characteristics of this are that when we demonstrate to the government that we have the product; the government upfront pays us 40%.

items.statement: BEE regulatory changes expected to help Crompton consolidate entry segment fan market as competitors may struggle to absorb incremental costs.
items.quote: We see Crompton is positively poised to consolidate the industry at the entry segment and gain market share, considering that it may not be competitively possible for people to absorb the incremental cost and pass back.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 revenue growth to exceed 10%, breaking the prior 10% growth band, driven by festive season demand in Q2 and Q3.
items.quote: So I would say that certainly, it will be more than 10% because normally the quarter 1 is quite, not that great any year. And as Akshali told that it is the best quarter we had in Q1, having 10% growth. So obviously, the second quarter and third quarter with a lot of festive season and demand, certainly, we are going to grow more than 10%.

items.statement: Cheese production capacity will double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over the next 1.5 years, targeting completion by March 2028.
items.quote: We are doubling our cheese production capacity from 60 metric tons per day to 120 metric tons per day over the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Gross margin remained stable at 27.3% in Q1 FY27 as 11% gross profit growth matched 11% revenue growth, demonstrating full cost pass-through.
items.quote: On a weighted average portfolio level, if you look at Y-o-Y, if the sales growth is 11%, gross margin growth is 11%, this clearly demonstrates that the entire cost push has been passed on as a blended portfolio.

items.statement: Milk prices were INR42 per litre in Q1 FY27, up 13% year-on-year and flat sequentially; management expects slight further increases due to monsoon and festive demand.
items.quote: The milk prices at INR42 per litre during the quarter, 13% higher year-on-year and flat sequentially.

items.statement: Monsoon progress should improve milk availability, and the festive period will support demand for value-added categories in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: Milk availability should benefit from the progress of monsoon, and the festive period should provide a supportive demand environment for the value-added categories.

items.statement: New age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar) grew 59% year-on-year to 13% of revenue from 9% last year, with strong volume growth across new formats like ready-to-drink and protein bars.
items.quote: The new age business, that is Pride of Cows and Avvatar, grew by 59% year-on-year in this quarter and now contributes to around 13% of our overall revenue versus 9% in the Q1 last year.

items.statement: B2B volumes in flagship categories declined modestly as the company foregoes low-margin volumes to protect profitability; this transient slowdown may continue.
items.quote: Though B2B, we have to maintain our profitability and all these things. So sometimes we forego some volumes from the few customers, which are negotiating very hard and we don't go to that kind of pricing to maintain our profitability.

items.statement: Avvatar distribution is 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce, and website; 25% via traditional retail and specialized protein outlets.
items.quote: Our revenues from quick-com, e-com and our website is 75% and 25% is coming from the traditional retail or specialized protein outlets.

items.statement: FDA ban on analogue paneer (vegetable fat-based) is positive for Parag as it sells 100% milk-fat paneer, supporting organized dairy players.
items.quote: So just to eliminate that confusion, they have banned any paneer, which is basically not made out of the milk fat, which is not a case with us because we make 100% with milk fat. So in that case, it's good for us

items.statement: Renewable energy investments include a Tata Solar collaboration, biogas from 5,000 cattle, and planned solar panels on cattle sheds; total investment is INR4.6 crores, not INR50 crores.
items.quote: We have a collaboration with Tata Solar Power, where we have some contribution with the joint venture. And then we produce some biogas power for the uses in our farm.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin improvement over next two to three quarters from current ~8%
items.quote: With Q1 FY'27 at around 8%, we are further targeting to improve EBITDA over the next two to three quarters.

items.statement: Expect debt reduction of Rs 25-30 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: I think by the end of this financial year, our debt should reduce by almost Rs. 25 crores to Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Target commercial production at MP plant in FY28
items.quote: And we begin to, we target to start commercial production at that plant in FY'28.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 AAC block capacity utilization at ~69%
items.quote: It is approximately 69% for Q1 of FY'27.

items.statement: Construction chemicals plant utilization at 20-25% in Q1, to scale up over next couple of quarters
items.quote: The construction chemicals plant recently began in May. And for that, for this quarter, the capacity utilization is in the range of almost 20%, 25%. It will be gradually scaled up over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Fungible AAC block/panel plant utilization at ~40%
items.quote: For that plant, the capacity utilization is approximately at around 40%.

items.statement: Optimum utilization for AAC plants is 80-85% due to fly ash supply constraints
items.quote: Since our raw materials are fly ash, which is a waste from the thermal power plants, there are some other issues or challenges while operating a plant. So, the optimum capacity which we have achieved in any particular quarter is around 80% to 83%.

items.statement: MP plant construction to begin post-monsoon, targeting FY28 commercial production
items.quote: And hopefully post-monsoon we will be looking at beginning construction at this site.

items.statement: Demand supported by real estate, infrastructure and structural shift to green building materials
items.quote: The demand continues to be supported by healthy activity in the real estate and infrastructure sectors along with the increasing adoption of lighter, faster, more efficient and sustainable construction materials.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin ~8%, up from 1% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA improved significantly to approximately INR 6 crores compared with INR 1 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. This represents a substantial improvement in operating performance with EBITDA margins expanding to 8% approximately.

items.statement: Margin improvement to come from operating leverage and price hikes
items.quote: So, from a combination of both, from operating leverage as well as improvement in realizations.

items.statement: AAC panels target 30-35% EBITDA margin at higher utilization
items.quote: So, AAC panels will have almost 30%, 35% EBITDA margin possibility as the utilization levels keep on improving.

items.statement: Already implemented price hikes in some markets, will extend to others
items.quote: Now that we have reached the volume growth that we are targeting to reach, we will be now able to pass the price increase to the market. And across some markets and some segments, over the last one or two quarters, we have already done some price hikes and passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Fly ash prices up 5-10% over 6-12 months, driven by diesel cost increase
items.quote: Over the past six to 12 months, I think there has been a normal increase, maybe between 5% to 10% in the fly-ash prices. But apart from that is majorly because of transportation cost and not because of the material cost.

items.statement: Coal cost up 50-60% but hedged for monsoon period; expect decline post-monsoon
items.quote: The cost for coal has grown up drastically by almost 50% to 60%. But since we had booked the coal in advance for the monsoon period for a period of almost three, three and a half months, we are quite, I mean, settled over there.

items.statement: AAC panels contributed ~5% of Q1 FY27 revenue
items.quote: So, AAC panel had a sales contribution of approximately 5% in the total revenues of the company for Q1 FY'27.

items.statement: Mortar plant operational, expanding into construction chemicals
items.quote: Our mortar plant is now operational, further expanding our product portfolio and enabling us to participate in the growing opportunity in the construction chemicals and allied building material solutions.

items.statement: Sales mix: 50-60% dealers, 20-25% builders, 15-20% large corporates (Adani, L&T, Runwal, etc.)
items.quote: We are selling almost 50% to 60% of our materials through a dealer network. Almost 20%, 25% material is being sold to a builder. And 15%, 20% is sold to large corporates, the likes of, Adani, L&T, Runwal, Suntech, PSP Projects, etc.

items.statement: Executing bullet train stations for L&T with AAC wall panels; talks for more stations and data centers
items.quote: We are also executing the upcoming bullet train stations on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad route. And are in the process of executing work orders for two bullet train stations and are in talks for a few more with the AAC wall panels.

items.statement: AAC block competitors: Magicrete, BirlaNu (Hyderabad Industries), plus small regional players
items.quote: So, in terms of the other competitors, one of them is Magicrete and another would be Hyderabad Industries Limited, which is BirlaNu Now. And apart from that, lots of small regional players which are multiple partners or small players.

items.statement: Competition intensity matured, no significant increase expected
items.quote: So, the competition had increased over the last two years but with the increase in those competitions as well, as of today, that competition level has matured and going forward, we do not see much of an increase in competition.

items.statement: ~52% of power from solar; 3.3 MW rooftop solar across four plants
items.quote: During the quarter, approximately 52% of our power requirement was met through solar energy.

items.statement: Introducing electric forklifts to reduce diesel and maintenance costs
items.quote: Secondly, over the next one or two quarters, we are looking at introducing electric forklifts at our plant level, thereby saving on the diesel as well as the maintenance costs or the rental costs of the forklifts that we are running.

items.statement: Finance cost decreased sequentially; expect further reduction
items.quote: So, sequentially the finance cost has not increased, it has gone down, I think. So, maybe there is some error. And as I mentioned, we have done a lot of CAPEX and are in the process of continuously reducing our bad debts as well. So, I think the finance cost should keep on going down over the next few quarters.

items.statement: AAC block market share ~8-10% in Western India (9-10M cu m capacity)
items.quote: In western India, the total installed capacity would be at around 9 million cubic meters to 10 million cubic meters per annum. So, we consider about 8% to 10% of the total market size for the western India AAC block space.

items.statement: Labor shortage seasonal (mid-Mar to early Jul) but currently resolved
items.quote: Generally, in every year post Holi, from mid-March up to mid-June or first, second week of July, there are labor shortages because of, you know, the harvesting season as well as the marriage season, in the small towns, rural villages, etc. But yes, today we are totally sorted with labors at plants as well as in the market side.

items.statement: FY27 operating revenue growth target 10%-15%
items.quote: Firstly, we are looking to grow Operating revenues by 10%-15% for the year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance band 17%-19%
items.quote: Secondly, we are giving an EBITDA margin band guidance of 17%-19%.

items.statement: Content licensing revenue target over Rs400m and client count 5 to 10 in FY27
items.quote: Fifth, We are looking to target revenues in excess of Rs400m in the Content Licensing opportunities of our text, images, audio, videos and non-academic datasets and growing the number of clients from 5 to 10 this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin improved year-on-year
items.quote: we reported consolidated revenues of Rs1,145 million (up 12% YOY), Improved Gross Margin, EBITDA Loss of Rs97 million and a PAT Loss of Rs187 million.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance factors in 10%-12% paper price increase
items.quote: We factored in about 10% -12% price increase.

items.statement: Advanced paper purchases to pre-empt higher prices and supply disruptions; dollar at Rs95 vs Rs85 last year
items.quote: We took a conscious decision to advance Paper purchases since we are pre-empting higher paper prices, supply disruptions and elongated shipping timelines for imported paper.

items.statement: Paper prices may firm up next quarter; only 20%-25% of annual requirement purchased so far
items.quote: We've barely taken 20%-25% of our annual requirements.

items.statement: Receivable days stable; Middle East geopolitical issues hamper collections; higher inventory from early paper buying raised net working capital days
items.quote: Our Receivable days were stable during the quarter. Geo-political instability in the Middle East continues to hamper our collections from the region.

items.statement: Cash surplus with highest ever Q1 net cash balance of Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend payout
items.quote: We continued our strong cash flow generation and remained Cash Surplus at the end of the quarter with the highest net cash balance at the end of Q1 in the company's history of Rs1,182m (Vs. Q4FY26: Rs1,160m) after distribution of dividend of Rs141m.

items.statement: Evaluating M&A opportunities in test prep and school space; total investment size around Rs40-50 crore
items.quote: One is in the test prep space, and one is in the school space. And once we have more details, we'll come back to you. The total size of these investments is not much. I think they should be around Rs40 crore toRs50 crores at max

items.statement: CPD Singapore acquisition contributed ~Rs1 crore in Q1; targeting SGD 1 million (~Rs7.5 cr) revenue by year-end
items.quote: It's just started. It's a very small company. I think contribution in the first quarter is around only Rs 1 crore, but the main business is Q3 and Q4. So, we are developing additional content there, and of course currently we've ramped up the marketing team, so we expect it to at least give us a decent revenue by the end of this year. We're looking at crossing SGD 1 million (Approx Rs 7.5 cr) at t

items.statement: Actively considering a market buyback; decision expected by October after acquisition clarity
items.quote: Yes, so we are considering a market buyback. I think we should be able to once these acquisition opportunities, really, fructify over the next 2 months. I think by October we should be in a space to decide on where we are on this.

items.statement: New printing and binding facility partially operational from September-October; full completion next year; built for 10-15 year capacity
items.quote: Half of it will get done this year. The complete process will complete next year. So partially the binding and some printing will start moving from next week onwards. We'll start operation there probably in September and October, and the rest of it will go next year.

items.statement: Refreshed curriculum products (Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK, Solid Steps) got multiple repeat adoptions; new partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin, Speedlabs
items.quote: Our refreshed curriculum businesses including Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps got multiple repeat adoptions from across the country. Along with this our new partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin and Speedlabs further strengthened our product offering helping us offer more to our customers.

items.statement: Content licensing generated Rs91 million in Q1; expect growth acceleration in coming quarters; diversifying into non-academic data licensing
items.quote: We generated Rs91 million revenues from content licensing during the quarter. We expect growth acceleration in this segment in the coming quarters. We are also diversifying the dataset base to include non-academic data licensing.

items.statement: Full adoption of new NCERT syllabus books expected in FY27
items.quote: We look forward to NCERT releasing the remaining books on the new syllabus over the course of the year. We expect the full adoption of the new syllabus books in FY27.

items.statement: Mylestone and My Zen curricula revenue Rs55-60 crore in FY26; on uptrend
items.quote: The current revenues from both of these is around Rs55 crores to Rs60 crores.

items.statement: Content licensing at Rs14 crore as of date (Q1 Rs9 crore); confident of crossing Rs40 crore target
items.quote: As on date, we're sitting on Rs14 crores revenues, where in Q1 we did Rs9 crore. Our expectation is definitely we'll cross Rs40 crores, but there is some positive development that is happening, so hopefully we'll do more.

items.statement: New West Bengal syllabus expected to provide growth leg-up for two years from next year
items.quote: the new syllabus is expected in West Bengal, so that should give us a good leg up for 2 years from next year onwards.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment deferred; may consider if exceptional income event occurs (e.g., real estate sale or Smartivity IPO)
items.quote: In case we have an event where there is an exceptional income, which may happen in a couple of years' time, then that is the time that we probably look at impairing the goodwill.

items.statement: Hiring marketing team in India for CPD Singapore content; hired in two cities with more to follow
items.quote: We have started hiring people for this particular segment in India. So that is where we are. We have hired people in two cities, and we have more hiring to follow.

items.statement: IIT Madras Pravartak partnership for future-ready skills programs (Class 7-12); revenue not material but strengthens school connect
items.quote: So in terms of revenue it's not much. It's more about the branding and, you know, the schools, how they perceive you as a brand since you are enabling them with upskilling.

items.statement: CPD Singapore brand known in Singapore/Malaysia; India and Middle East rollout will take 1-2 academic cycles to scale
items.quote: The brand is more known in the Singapore markets. So to bring it here and to promote it and make it known in the education space, it takes time. And we are very patient in that regard, and we are waiting for it.

items.statement: Steady-state core business growth 10%-12% (3%-4% student growth, 4%-5% volume, 4%-5% pricing); acquisitions needed to exceed
items.quote: The steady state is again 10% to 12%, for the core business. In case there are acquisitions, then even more. Because see, the number of students that increase every year is about 3% to 4%, and volume growth another 4%-5% that you can take, pricing growth again 4%-5% you can take. So that's the limitation in this, and, unless you're doing new segments or acquiring, you really can't, going beyond th

items.statement: FY27 cement volume growth revised to 8-9% from earlier 11-12%
items.quote: And on the overall year, I think we expect to probably revise the numbers. A bit from 11% to 12% to about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: FY27 clinker sales expected to be stagnant or degrow 5-10% vs FY26
items.quote: I think the clinker sale in FY27 would probably be stagnant or may degrow by about 5% to 10% compared to FY26

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA per ton target of INR1,500-1,600 maintained
items.quote: Yes. I mean, over the entire year, yes, it can be doable. I think INR1,500, INR1,600 is still a good estimate.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA per ton expected around INR1,400 due to shutdown costs and lower volumes
items.quote: Only for quarter 2 because the shutdown cost also gets added in the cost in quarter 2 and also because in Northeast, the rain is more so of course, the fixed costs are getting absorbed by a lower volume. So it may be about INR1,400 for quarter 2

items.statement: FY27 subsidy income expected at INR115 crores vs earlier INR145 crores
items.quote: So what I expect for this year is not about INR145 crores, but about INR115 crores.

items.statement: Non-cement revenue target of INR150 crores from Building Solutions division by Q4 FY27
items.quote: And I think we should be able to reach that ballpark figure. At least on an ARR basis, we should be able to reach that 150 number by the quarter 4.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex spend of INR93 crores; FY27 capex plan maintained at INR500 crores
items.quote: This quarter, we have spent around INR93-odd crores. And our planning what we have given INR500 crores for this quarter this year, that will continue. That will still holding on the same.

items.statement: Total North expansion capex estimated at INR2,600-2,700 crores (ex-GST) for 3.3mt clinker, 3mt grinding in Rajasthan and 2mt grinding in Haryana
items.quote: The overall capex of this thing is about INR2,600 crores to INR2,700 crores is that what we are expecting. And I think we are focusing in the next 2 years to primarily get this capex going in North.

items.statement: West Bengal industrial policy expected mid-August; decision on 2mt grinding unit in Siliguri vs Bihar after policy review
items.quote: I think about 15th of August is when the West Bengal is supposed to come up with their industrial policy. So looking at the industrial policy and looking at the potential benefits that one can accrue, I think we wi ll take a

items.statement: Northeast demand muted in Q1-Q2 due to elections and floods; pent-up demand expected to drive higher growth in H2 FY27
items.quote: I think that when the floods subside, which is basically quarter 3 and 4, I think there should be some pent -up demand which gets released in those 2 quarters in the second half of the year. So I would expect a bit higher than usual growth in thos e 2 quarters

items.statement: FY27 Northeast industry growth estimated at 7%; Star Cement targeting 8-9% growth in Northeast
items.quote: For the industry, I would say that the growth rate should be about 7%. For us, I hope that we can do about 8% to 9% in Northeast.

items.statement: Fuel cost per ton increased to INR1.55 in Q1 from INR1.33 in Q4 FY26; expected to decline to INR1.45 in Q2 and further in H2
items.quote: So in the fuel cost in F Y26, quarter 4 was about INR1.33, which has gone up to INR1.55. We expect in Q2 onwards, the cost should come down to about INR1.45 -- and hopefully, in Q3 and Q4, we can hopefully reduce the cost further on

items.statement: Cement prices broadly stable in Northeast and outside markets (Bihar, West Bengal) in Q2; Bihar prices ~INR10 higher, Northeast/West Bengal up ~INR3
items.quote: I think the prices are broadly stable in Northeast as well as in outside Northeast markets of Bihar and West Bengal, even in the quarter 2.

items.statement: Q1 fuel mix: 45% FSA coal, 30% spot coal, balance biomass/AFR; Coal India supply diverted to power plants forcing spot purchases
items.quote: So fuel mix for FSA would be about -- would be about 45% and from FSA and the other source spot contracts. What has happened in quarter 1 is that all the coal has been directed to the power plant by because I think there was a surge of power requirement. So all the Coal India coal was diverted.

items.statement: PP bag prices elevated due to international turmoil/war; difficult to predict trajectory
items.quote: The PP bag prices are completely related to the international turmoil and war situation, which is going on and thereafter prices are up. So that, I think, really is hard to predict of how will it play out.

items.statement: Not actively considering QIP; targeting 1.5-1.6x net debt/EBITDA to fund North capex over next 2 years
items.quote: So we are not at the moment actively thinking of QIP. We will do it at the opportune time in case there's opportunities available for which we need to further raise money that may be organic or inorganic.

items.statement: Q1 FY27: Clinker production 9.10 lakh tons, cement production 13.08 lakh tons, cement sales 13.02 lakh tons, clinker sales 0.52 lakh tons
items.quote: ended June 26, we have produced 9.10 lakh tons of clinker as against 8.90 lakh tons same quarter last year. So far as cement production is concerned, we have produced 13.08 lakh tons this quarter as against 12.31 lakh tons same quarter last year. Now I will take you through the sales volume. During the quarter, we have sold 13.02 lakh tons of cement and 0.52 lakh ton of

items.statement: Q1 FY27: Northeast cement sales 8.71 lakh tons, outside Northeast 4.31 lakh tons; blend mix ~15% OPC, rest PPC
items.quote: In Northeast, we have sold around 8.71 lakh tons as against 8.67 lakh tons during same quarter last year. And as far as outside Northeast is concerned, we have sold 4.31 lakh tons of cement this quarter as against 3.55 lakh tons same quarter last year. In terms of blend mix, it is almost 15% of OPC and the rest is PPC.

items.statement: Assam government changed subsidy payout to equal annual installments over 12 years, reducing annual accrual by INR20-30 crores
items.quote: But now what we've done is that they have divided the number of -- the amount of subsidy by 12 years, right? items.quote: So yes, I think we have already gotten the standa rd approved package in Rajasthan for the Nimbol clinker plant that we plan to set up. I think I will share a slide of those benefits in the next presentation. It involves a degree of capital subsidy along with SGST

items.quote: in quarter 2 and July , of course, the volume degrowth was about 12% -- the reason was because July was completely flooded in Assam and Assam was completely shut down in many areas. This year, September, we expect to be without m

items.quote: Green shares for this quarter was about 3%. This, of course, includes the WHRS as well. Shravan Shah: Tushar Bhajanka: And this we are planning to introduce solar some group captive opportunities that we're evaluating. I think in quarter 3 or quarter 4, we will also share the details of those contracts

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores, meaningfully higher than outlook communicated 9 months ago
items.quote: Our current FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores is meaningfully higher than the outlook we had communicated 9 months ago.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores revenue by FY30
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our aspiration of INR8,100 crores by FY27 and INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores by FY30.

items.statement: Will revise revenue target after Diwali, analyzing one more quarter before giving new guidance
items.quote: We will revise our target after Diwali. We'll analyze one more quarter, and we will give our new guidance post Diwali. That's our plan.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin increased to 9.3% in Q1 FY27 vs 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by Advance Gold and non-22 KT jewelry mix shift
items.quote: Our consolidated gross margin increased to 9.3% in Q1 FY27 versus 9.1% in Q4 FY26, an improvement of 27 basis points.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance maintained at 8.5% to 9% despite mix improvement due to volume discounts on 22 KT jewelry
items.quote: The guidance of 8.5% to 9% gross margin we are giving, because, in the journey of business, you can see if 22 karat is somebody is taking volume, we have to pass on some 0.25% to 0.5% discount also to the customers.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance of 5.25% maintained, with aim to reach INR1,000 crores PAT
items.quote: From the overall guidance to the Street, 5.25% of the PAT margin still holds, while we plan and aimed at how we can reach the magical number of INR1,000 crores of PAT going forward.

items.statement: Advance Gold sales at 17% in Q1 FY27, significantly ahead of 15% expectation for FY27
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have achieved 17% sales on the Advance Gold model, significantly ahead of our expectation of 15% of the Advance Gold model for FY27.

items.statement: Non-22 KT jewelry share increased from 10.5% to 14% of volume, studded jewelry from 1.65% to 2.1% of revenue
items.quote: the share of non-22 KT jewelry has increased from 10.5%in Q4FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27 due to structural shift in customer preference towards lower Karatage jewelry. Sky Gold & The share of studded jewelry has also increased from 1.65% in Q4 '26 to 2.1% in Q1 '27

items.statement: CEO target: Advance Gold 15% average this year, 20% next year, 25% third year, 30% by 2030
items.quote: We have achieved 18% Advance Gold business, and we have given him the target for this year to be average of 15%, next year 20%, and the third year of 25%. In 2030, we will achieve 30% of the Advance Gold business.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 55%-60%, sufficient until 2028; future expansion via leased model with INR80-100 crores capex (12%-20% of PAT)
items.quote: Currently, the capacity utilization is close to 55%- 57%. And looking at the current projection numbers, we are good till 2028. And post that, we may look at a new facility, but that we will continue on the leased model, and capex will not be very big. It will be close to INR80 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Q2 better than Q1 due to Navratri-Diwali orders, Q3 better due to marriage season, Q4 strong with Akshaya Tritiya deliveries
items.quote: So, we follow Q2 is better than Q1, and then Q3 is better. And again, the fourth quarter, March is better than that because Akshaya Tritiya's major delivery goes in March.

items.statement: International expo generated prospective order pipeline of INR30-45 crores across U.K. and European markets
items.quote: The response was highly encouraging, resulting in strong initial interest and helping us to build a prospective order pipeline of approximately INR30 crores to INR45 crores across the U.K. and European markets.

items.statement: Cyber fraud incident involving INR10.7 crores; INR3.5 crores recovered, legal proceedings ongoing for balance
items.quote: Out of that, INR10.7 crores was the total amount involved, but such incidents have unfortunately become increasingly prevalent across many organizations which are listed on the BSE and NSE.

items.statement: Generated INR30 crores operating cash flow in Q1 FY27, marking milestone towards cash flow positive model

items.statement: Net working capital cycle at ~60 days, targeting 2 days improvement YoY to reach 52 days by 2030

items.statement: Target mid-teens revenue growth for FY27

items.statement: Target 14% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27
items.quote: our target still remains that by quarter 4 of this financial year, we get to our 14% EBITDA target. So that's the journey plan we have

items.statement: Target 15-16% EBITDA margin by FY30
items.quote: over a period of next 3 to 4 years, say, by 2030 financial year, we want to hit EBITDA closer to 16%. That's the aim as of now. So somewhere between 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Target INR4,000 crores revenue by FY30
items.quote: we want to hit the next milestone of INR4,000 crores, right? So there's a fair amount of investment, which will also go in expanding our distribution

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 13.1%, up 80 bps YoY

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 47.2% in Q1 FY27 from 45.6% YoY

items.statement: Bakery EBITDA above company average, Biscuit EBITDA slightly below

items.statement: Price increases of 2-2.5% in consumer business taken during Q1

items.statement: Input cost inflation impact ~1.5% in Q1, higher in Q2
items.quote: About 1.5% approximately was the inflationary impact for this quarter, the next quarter is higher. So, the quarter 2 is much higher.

items.statement: Project IMPACT expected to deliver 0.4-0.5% cost savings in FY27
items.quote: we expect this year to deliver almost close to 0.4% to 0.5% coming out of our cost impact program.

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy across retail and institutional channels
items.quote: Domestic demand remained healthy across both retail and institutional channels, and our export order book strengthened materially despite vessel availability yet to normalize fully after the disruption in this quarter.

items.statement: Domestic biscuit sales growth at high-single digits
items.quote: It has been high-single digits.

items.statement: Quick commerce grew 58% YoY
items.quote: Quick commerce continues to be of strategic significance for us and grew 58% year-on-year.

items.statement: Export business delivered high-double-digit growth despite shipping challenges
items.quote: Despite this, our export business delivered healthy high-double-digit growth. Importantly, the U.S. market is back on a growth trajectory for us.

items.statement: B2B bakery (QSR) returned to double-digit growth
items.quote: in this quarter, there has been a good double-digit growth in the B2B segment, and we are very confident this trend to continue in the coming quarters

items.statement: Export orders are month-to-month, no long order book
items.quote: we don't have any long order book. We get orders on a month-to-month basis, right? So it's not that like projects and other things where you get 6 months or 9 months orders, it's nothing like that.

items.statement: Kolkata bakery unit commissioned in Q4 FY26, servicing East markets
items.quote: Our Kolkata bakery unit commissioned in quarter 4 of financial year 2026 is now servicing East markets, and the market has responded encouragingly.

items.statement: Khopoli plant commissioned March 2026, stabilizing and scaling toward full capacity

items.statement: Bangalore plant location shortlisted, capex under finalization

items.statement: Current capacity supports INR3,400-3,500 crores revenue at current prices
items.quote: in terms of capex, which we have invested or investing this year can -- on current price levels, can cover us up to approximately INR3,400 crores, INR3,500 crores, right?

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR200 crores excluding last year spillover
items.quote: this year, our approximate investment should be -- other than the spillover of last year, this should be close to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Kolkata plant investment ~INR20 crores
items.quote: Calcutta was a small investment, which plant was commissioned last year. So, it was a small investment approximately, which I remember around INR20-odd crores, right?

items.statement: Capex funding 60% internal, 40% borrowed in FY27
items.quote: the additional capex, which we are planning to do in this particular year, it will be almost 60% -- 60% coming out of our own funds and 40% would be borrowed funds.

items.statement: Naturbaked crossed INR1 crore monthly revenue run rate
items.quote: With our focused efforts, Naturbaked has crossed a monthly revenue rate of INR1 crore.

items.statement: Premium creams and cookies driving premiumization in biscuits
items.quote: we are investing behind our premium creams and premium cookies, right, to drive our premium contribution in the business.

items.statement: Export business 95-98% from existing customers, adding SKUs
items.quote: more than 95% or 98% business would be the existing. But the thing is that the existing customers, we are consistently and continuously adding newer SKUs to them in the form of innovation to grow their share in the market.

items.statement: General trade revenue split 50% Upper North, 50% Rest of India

items.quote: We are setting our full year services revenue goal at INR2,650 crores to INR2,750 crores against the INR2,700 crores to INR2,800 crores earlier.

items.quote: The total revenue, including product revenue, is estimated accordingly at INR2,750 crores to INR2,850 crores.

items.statement: Track record of converting 65-70% of EBITDA to operating cash flows over last 5 years

items.statement: Will Poole appointed to Board; co-founded Capria Ventures with 60+ AI investments; previously built platform businesses at Microsoft
items.quote: It is also why I'm pleased to welcome Will Poole to our Board. Will has co-founded and leads Capria Ventures with more than 60 investments in companies putting AI to work in the real economy.

items.quote: And if the currency supply and the transaction levels do not improve, we will prune the persistently underperforming ATMs out of our BLA estate.

items.statement: No plans to enter merchant acquiring/payment aggregator space; finds it very competitive and difficult to make money
items.quote: As of now, we don't have any plans to be in the merchant acquiring space. We find that space to be very competitive and very difficult to make any money.

items.statement: Express volume growth tracking towards upper end of 20-30% YoY range for FY27
items.quote: Broadly looking at where we are at the start of Q1 and the early part of Q2, we're towards the mid or upper side of the range that I spoke about, which is a 20-30% range.

items.statement: Automation investments in transportation facilities and fulfilment centres (in-facility movement, ASRS) brought forward to sustain market share growth amid labor shortages

items.quote: Our original plan was to reach a GMV of close to Rs. 250 Cr in FY27. As things stand, we are currently at a GMV ahead of plan at close to about Rs.150 Cr GMV and expect that we will close the year higher than originally planned.

items.statement: Chronic labor shortages across industry in April-June; significant disruptions from elections and weather; geopolitical uncertainty driving inflation in fuel and input costs
items.quote: There have been chronic labor shortages across the industry throughout the period of April, May and June. We also had significant disruptions due to both elections as well as weather in this quarter.

items.statement: Supply chain services revenue ~Rs 200 Cr in Q1; profitability affected by start of two large contracts expected to stabilize over Q2 and early Q3
items.quote: Our supply chain services business came in at nearly Rs.200 Cr of revenue for Q1. Profitability was affected by the start of two new large contracts, which we expect will stabilize over a combination of Q2 and early Q3.

items.quote: Overall our growth so far in Q1 is 55% YoY, but of course that also has the base effect due to the fact that the Ecom Express acquisition was fully reported from Q2 onwards in the last financial year.

items.statement: Express service EBITDA margin target 16-18% for FY27, confident to reach higher end in H2
items.quote: In Express, our target has been in that 16-18% service EBITDA range. We continue to maintain that and we remain confident that in the second half of this financial year, we will be in that range, in fact, closer to the higher end of that range.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin target to exit FY27 at 15-15.5%, up from 13.4% exit FY26
items.quote: The long-term target there also is 16-18%. We exited last financial year at 13.4%. This financial year, our internal objective will be to exit closer to 15-15.5% service EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 normalized EBITDA impact from fuel and wage inflation estimated at 35 Cr, with 30-35 Cr delay in fuel pass-through to Q2
items.quote: So normalised, it would have been at least probably about 30-35 Cr higher compared to where we ended up.

items.statement: Strong volume growth across Q3, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; gained share versus in-house logistics

items.statement: Fuel and labour cost inflation passed through to customers; discussions smooth as industry-wide issue
items.quote: These increases in labour costs, these increases in fuel are obviously passed through to customers. And frankly, our discussions with customers on this are fairly smooth, because most customers do realise that, it's not just a Delhivery problem, this is an industry wide problem.

items.statement: Yield decline from Q1 FY26 to Q1 FY27 due to Ecom Express acquisition adding small parcel volume without heavy delivery
items.quote: Ecom Express did not provide heavy delivery services at all. So essentially, our acquisition was of a small parcel delivery network. In Q1 of last financial year, we were a standalone network. So the proportion of heavy consignments in the combined volumes of Delhivery and Ecom Express, which is in Q1FY27 or Delhivery consolidated effectively now is lower than it was in Q1FY26

items.statement: Two large new supply chain services contracts (industrials and consumer durables) in ramp-up phase causing temporary margin drag
items.quote: The major change is the start of two new big contracts. At the start of the contract, what typically tends to happen is that we will commission the fulfilment centers across multiple sites. Inventory starts rolling in. There's a period where there's a mismatch between inventory inbound and inventory outbound

items.statement: Supply chain services new contracts expected to reach full margin potential 45-60 days after inventory roll-in
items.quote: What typically tends to happen is about 45 to 60 days after the inventory starts rolling in is when you start moving to high potential, the full potential outbound volumes. And at that stage, the margins start quickly scaling up and reaching their full potential.

items.statement: New initiatives investment budget 160-175 Cr for FY27, mostly for Delhivery Local; financial services just received NBFC approval in July
items.quote: The amount that we had earmarked, up to about 160-175 Cr for the financial year, at least looking at current trajectory, we should be well within that.

items.statement: Delhivery Local ARR at 150 Cr in July, ahead of 250 Cr FY27 exit target; contribution margins better than expected
items.quote: We were expecting to exit the financial year at a 250 Cr ARR. But, here we are, we're sitting in August and we're already hitting, sorry, in July, and we're hitting a 150 Cr ARR.

items.statement: Network structural changes as freight service centers activated: heavy loads withdrawn to gateways, reducing average delivery center size and costs
items.quote: When you activate a freight service station in Patna, which now has the ability to do PTL freight as well as heavies, what's happening is you're withdrawing the average weights from the DC network back into a gateway or a service center. And when you do that, the average size of delivery centers that you need in that specific city suddenly crashes.

items.statement: Delhivery avoids quick commerce dark store operations and last-mile delivery; focuses on PTL supply to mother warehouses and dark stores
items.quote: We do not run dark stores for Quick Commerce players. As of now, there isn't a multiplayer dark store model that has emerged because every Quick Commerce player wants to have dedicated dark stores. And we do not do delivery from dark stores to consumers.

items.statement: Senior management focus shifting to technology, engineering, network structure to mitigate labour availability, wage inflation, climate risks
items.quote: More of the time, across the senior management team, and certainly more of my time is going to go into the fundamental competitive advantages that delivery has, which are around network structure, technology, product and engineering.

items.statement: Business development teams expanded for part-truck and full-truck freight across 100 cities, increasing wage costs in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Essentially, moving to a different, much wider cross-sale structure, which would allow us to penetrate, I think we now have 100 cities all over India, much more deeply compared to where we were earlier, which was really, the top 3 cities plus some.

items.statement: Record volumes on express and high volumes on PTL in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Hopefully from here on, as we look forward, this decent start to Q1 with record volumes on express and high volumes on PTL continues.

items.statement: Corporate overheads stable at ~9.3-9.4% of sales in FY25, FY26, and Q1 FY27; operating leverage not yet visible.
items.quote: What we see is that in FY25, in FY26 and even in 1QFY27, the corporate overheads as a percentage of sales has been stable at around 9.3, 9.4%.

items.statement: Contractual manpower expense rose to 12.8% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 12.2% a year ago, impacting EBITDA margin by ~0.6%.
items.quote: Last year, in a similar quarter, we were having 12.2%, the contractual manpower expense as a percentage of revenue. This quarter, with all this wage raising across the states, this is at 12.8%.

items.statement: Fuel and oil-price linked costs (linehaul, consumables, air movement, last-mile partner payouts) increased materially in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Now, the linehaul impact would be larger than 30%. Now, that's all just fuel, but linked to oil price, you also have the cost of consumables going up. You also have the cost of air movement of parcels going up.

items.statement: Annual increments and network expansion in H1 FY27 increased fixed cost base.
items.quote: Even in a more normalised environment, the first quarter would have had the annual increments coming in. So your employee benefits costs would have gone up. And your first quarter onwards, we would also have our network expansions coming in.

items.statement: Delhivery Local (new services) contribution margin significantly ahead of plan in Q1 FY27; expected to improve further in Q2 and Q3.
items.quote: And contribution margin also actually significantly ahead of where we anticipated we would be in Q1 itself. And we continue to see some improvement in Q2 and anticipate that that will improve further in Q3.

items.statement: Cash integration cost for Ecom Express at 17 Cr in Q1 FY27; total cash guidance 300 Cr.
items.quote: The more relevant number is the 17 Cr, because our initial guidance of 300 Cr was a cash integration cost guidance.

items.statement: Depreciation on unused assets awaiting disposal increases statutory PAT impact but not cash cost.
items.quote: There are certain unused assets which are awaiting disposal, and they are also being depreciated. So that's while we are not really incurring any cash cost on it, but the depreciation for that is part of our statutory P&L.

items.statement: Contractual manpower expense was 371 Cr in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: That number would be 371 Cr for this quarter, this first quarter of FY27.

items.statement: Supervisory span 1:15-1:20 in distribution centres; 6-8% of field executives promoted to supervisory roles within 1-2 years.
items.quote: Ultimately, we have a supervisory span in the distribution centres of maybe, 1:15, 1:20. So, if you join us as a field executive, 6-8% of those people are going to make it to a supervisory level within, call it a year or a year and a half or two.

items.statement: Heavy freight loads (>200 kg) withdrawn from forward service stations into gateways, reducing average service centre size and rental, supervisory, and storage costs.
items.quote: Loads that weigh over 200 kgs have now been withdrawn wherever possible into gateways as opposed to being delivered from forward service stations. items.statement: Software-driven serviceability rules optimise node selection by load form factor, utilisation, and parcel gross margin (e.g., 140g parcel at 21% vs 370g at 27%).
items.quote: A 140 g parcel which yields, let's call it 21% gross margin versus a 370 g parcel which yields a 27% gross margin are not the same. A lot of the focus of the company therefore has, even from a software standpoint, has been on establishing these kinds of serviceability rules and making them more intelligent over time.

items.statement: Reverse logistics share lower than forward logistics share due to profitability screening per parcel and claims uncertainty.
items.quote: Our relative share in reverse logistics is certainly lower than our relative share in forward logistics. But the reason it is lower is fundamentally because we have the ability to examine the profitability of every parcel that we are taking.

items.statement: Gig worker wage regulations and incentive structures favour full-time dedicated riders; Delhivery prioritises stable 5-day workweeks over multiplexing.
items.quote: The directionality of the conversation, when you look at the changes to statutory wages, or when you look at things that are coming into effect on the gig worker laws, as well as regulators are looking at this and saying if somebody ultimately, and look at how gig worker contracts are really structured, right?

items.statement: External environment challenging at start of FY27 but appears to be easing.

items.statement: Management targets healthy project-level margins of 20-30% across redevelopment projects.
items.quote: But a healthy margins of around 20% to 30% should be expected in every project.

items.statement: Pricing trends stable across micro-markets; no significant volatility observed.

items.statement: Customer confidence driven by timely delivery and word-of-mouth; 200 families per completed project become brand advocates.

items.quote: One number I want to specifically mention is the area sold, which in Q1 FY27, we have sold around 44,000 square feet.

items.statement: War-related cost spikes in April-May 2026 impacted Q1 margins but have stabilized; Govind Dalvi project delayed by government stay order.
items.quote: The war, thing which has now subsided, initially during the first quarter in April:May, there were few challenges, but now everything has subsided.

items.statement: Demand exists for both luxury and economical segments; project positioning determines buyer profile.
items.quote: Every market is different. So, in Kandivali, Borivali also larger homes, you have to make the project, you have to matket the project that way, so the demand is as such that if you market the project in a lwuxury segment, you will be getting clicnts in the luxury segment

items.statement: No expansion planned outside Mumbai/Maharashtra currently; focus remains on Mumbai redevelopment.
items.quote: We are going to be around Bombay only as of now. Then, we are obviously open to expand into other cities of India.

items.statement: No comment on dividend or buyback; stock liquidity attributed to market factors.
items.quote: I've o idea. That is purely the -~ what do you say, the market side. I don't sce the market side or anything, so Il not be the one

items.quote: we partner with socictics rather than competing for lands in open market. This keeps our land cost low and puts owr capital where it belongs, into construction and into families waiting for their homes

items.statement: Brand building initiatives include digital presence, channel partner meets, broker meets, and sales lounges.
items.quote: We are positioning our, we ate spending our brand in digital presence as well in terms of making expericnces.
