items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 utilization 50-60% in FY28, 70-80% in FY29; Phase 2 expansion to start in FY29
items.quote: This year if you assume about 3-4 months of utilization, obviously the utilization numbers would not be very high vis-a-vis the capacity. But I would say when we talk about next financial year, which is the first full year of operations, we should be looking at minimum 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 14-15% with higher value-added product share
items.quote: So, going forward, our target would be to get to an EBITDA margin level of about 14% to 15% with the higher share of value-added products that we are foraying into now.

items.statement: Dahej greenfield investment ~INR100 cr for 40,000+ MTA zinc chemical facility; Phase 1 15,000-17,000 MTA zinc oxide
items.quote: With an investment of about INR100 crores, the estimated revenue potential will be INR900 crores.

items.statement: Naidupeta brownfield expansion adding ~5,000 MTA; capex figure not disclosed as utilities built over years
items.quote: So, the total capacity being added is about 5,000 tons. On the exact capex figure, I'll need to check because a lot of utilities, etcetera, have been already been created beforehand.

items.statement: Current installed capacity ~70,000 MTA; combined capacity to exceed 115,000 MTA after Dahej both phases
items.quote: Our manufacturing is anchored at our facilities in West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, which together today command an installed capacity of close to 70,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Current utilization in early 80s of achievable capacity; room to reach 100% via debottlenecking
items.quote: So, the utilization levels are in early 80s right now as we speak.

items.statement: Strong demand across tire/rubber (largest pillar) and non-rubber segments; ATMA reports Q1 FY27 volume growth: PV 26.6%, 2W 16.5%, CV 16.48%, 3W 11%+ YoY
items.quote: As per ATMA, the Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: passenger vehicles growing up to 26.6%, two-wheelers 16.5%, commercial vehicles 16.48%, and three-wheelers more than 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Tire industry capex ~INR25,000 cr announced; 25% of India tire production exported; customers at high utilization
items.quote: Indian tire majors are expanding their capacities to cater to this demand, with approximately INR25,000 crores of capex already announced by leading tire manufacturers.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 10.64% YoY; driven by operating leverage, higher-priced specialized orders, small inventory gains
items.quote: The EBITDA for the current quarter was INR36.3 crores with a margin of 11.5% as compared to 10.64% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Structural EBITDA margin range 10-12%; cost optimization initiatives yielding sustainable margin improvement
items.quote: So, you see, we have always maintained that in our industry, the EBITDA margins would be in the range of 10% to 12%, and going forward, we will have higher margins because of higher value-added products.

items.statement: Non-rubber share ~18% in Q1 FY27, inching up YoY; Dahej to accelerate non-rubber (pharma, ceramics, specialty chemicals, agri)
items.quote: This quarter, the share of non-rubber would be close to 18% or so. I don't have the exact number available for the previous quarter, but as we've guided earlier, gradually this number is inching up.

items.statement: New grades launched: LabPure (high-purity analytical reagent) and JG-ZRA (rubber activator for non-tire); patent pending for jointly developed chemical
items.quote: During this quarter, we introduced a new grade, which is called the LabPure zinc oxide, a high-purity grade for analytical reagent application. We also introduced JG-ZRA, a zinc oxide rubber activator designed for specific non-tire customer requirements with strong demand and export potential.

items.statement: 200+ domestic, 50+ international customers; supply all Indian major tire makers and 9 of top 10 global tire companies
items.quote: Today, our customer franchise extends to more than 200 domestic customers and over 50 international customers. And we are proud today to supply to every Indian major tire manufacturer and also to 9 out of the top world's 10 global tire companies.

items.statement: Ceramic market seeding for ~1 year; approvals 1-3 months vs 5 years for tire; Dahej well-positioned for Western India non-rubber demand
items.quote: So, as we mentioned earlier also, we have already started to seed the market. So, customers are aware of us. Relationships have already been established. And as far as your specific question, which relates to the difference in the approval process between say, a tire and a ceramic approval process is fairly quicker. It should be roughly in the range of 1 to 3 months.

items.statement: Exports 10-15% of sales; target ~15% in FY28-29; Dubai subsidiary BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO for sourcing and global distribution
items.quote: Today, it would be between 10% and 15%.

items.statement: Zinc dross supply uninterrupted despite geopolitical disruption; scale, financial strength, supplier relationships ensure raw material security
items.quote: However, JGC's scale, financial strength, and the long-standing supplier relationships have ensured that your company has had uninterrupted supply of raw material, enabling us to maintain a continuous supply to our extremely wide customer base.

items.statement: Neutral to zinc price volatility (3,000-3,600 range); higher commodity prices reflect new normal for realizations
items.quote: We are neutral to zinc prices, if you ask me honestly. So, whether zinc is at 3,000 or 3,500 or 3,600, it really doesn't matter to us.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiatives over last 3 months yielding sustainable margin improvement beyond short-term gains
items.quote: So, those efforts have also yielded results, and the inch up in the margins that you see in the current quarter, a good part of that is also due to the cost initiatives that the company has taken

items.statement: Proposed Dubai subsidiary BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO (step-down WOS) for raw material sourcing and global finished goods distribution
items.quote: Recently, the company has also proposed to incorporate BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO in Dubai, UAE, which upon incorporation will become a wholly owned subsidiary of BDJ Oxides Private Limited, a material subsidiary of JG Chemicals, and consequently a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary of JG Chemicals Limited.

items.statement: Zinc sulphate revenue <5-6% of sales; growing in South India; Dahej to enable Western India expansion using zinc oxide byproduct
items.quote: So, the revenue for zinc sulphate is less than 5%. I don't have the exact number with me, but it's less than about 5 to 6% of the overall sales.

items.statement: Recycled rubber project JG TUR pilot trials positive; commercial launch target within 12 months; supports tire industry ESG/recyclable content goals
items.quote: And we hope that in the next 12 months, we should be able to commercially start this project, and then the ramp up should be good, because there is an eminent need for the tire business and the tire industry in general to look for recycling alternatives.

items.statement: Condolences on demise of Independent Director Shri Ashok Bhandari (3 Aug 2026); valued contributor to Board
items.quote: However, before I begin, I would like to take a moment to express our deepest condolences on the sad and very untimely demise of Shri Ashok Bhandari-ji, Independent Director of our company, who passed away on 3rd August 2026.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict causing global supply chain disruption for zinc dross; managed via strong supplier relationships
items.quote: As we had mentioned earlier, the ongoing geopolitical conflict had impacted global supply chains for Zinc Dross, which is our primary raw material.

items.statement: Naidupeta facility: only IATF certified zinc oxide plant with WHO GMP and Pharmacopoeia certifications; structural differentiator for tire and pharma
items.quote: Our Naidupeta facility continues to be a structural differentiator, being the only IATF certified zinc oxide facility and also holding WHO GMP accreditation along with several Pharmacopoeia certifications.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 EBITDA margin 11-12%; Phase 2 expansion to start once utilization reaches late 70s/early 80s
items.quote: And the EBITDA margins that we expect to generate from that project would be in the 11% to 12% range.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of minimum 20% YoY growth for FY27
items.quote: we strongly stand by our earlier guidance given of, you know, minimum 20% growth in this financial year over last year.

items.statement: Full-year revenue target of INR 1,800-1,900 crores for FY27
items.quote: for the full financial year, in terms of top line increase, we said we would be ending somewhere between INR 1,800 crores to 1,900 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% for FY27 with exit run rate near double-digit
items.quote: as far as EBITDA margin is concerned, it's between full year average between 8% to 9% with an exit run rate close to double-digit.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 11-11.5% over medium term
items.quote: The sustainable EBITDA margins which we are targeting is somewhere around 11% to 11.5%, that's what is sustainable EBITDA margins we are targeting.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR target of minimum 20% beyond FY27
items.quote: subsequently also we continue to maintain our stand of delivering minimum 20% CAGR on revenue front.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin at 27% despite raw material inflation
items.quote: Gross profit increased to INR 114 crores, with gross margin remaining healthy at 27%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 7.4% from 4.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin improving to 7.4% as compared to 4.7% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: FY28-29 EBITDA margin target of 10-11% with exit near 11%
items.quote: next year, which would be next it would be FY27-28, somewhere around 10% to 11% with an exit to near to 11%.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 7-7.5% for FY28
items.quote: in terms of PAT margin, it would be around 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: 5% raw material inflation in Q1, passed on 4.2% via price hikes and grammage reduction, 0.8% absorbed
items.quote: total inflation which hit us in terms of raw material, it was 5%, out of which 4.2% we have passed on to the consumers and 0.8% sit as an hit to our P&L in the current quarter.

items.statement: Further 0.2-0.3% raw material inflation impact to be passed on in coming quarters
items.quote: considering the current raw material prices, another 0.2 %, 0.3% still there is an hit, which we will definitely pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: Trade discounts reduced from 3.5% to 2.5% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Current quarter it is 2.5%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR 422.3 crores, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: We delivered highest-ever quarterly revenue from the operations of INR 422.3 crores during the quarter, reflecting a growth of 31.1% year -on-year and 3.1% sequentially.

items.statement: Current monthly run rate of INR 150+ crores after April disruption
items.quote: our current run rate is INR 150 crores plus. So, there was a small hiccup in the month of April owing to, you know, our Gondal facility was gas -based and we shifted our Gondal facility to Rajkot.

items.statement: Core market Gujarat run rate target of INR 100+ crores per month
items.quote: See from here onwards, we are targeting INR 100-plus crores per month.

items.statement: Wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets
items.quote: Wafers have grown by YoY is 15% in core markets.

items.statement: Rajkot main facility recommenced operations, production consolidated from Gondal
items.quote: The successful recommencement of operations at our Rajkot main facility together with continued contributions from our Modasa and Nagpur plant has further enhanced our manufacturing capability.

items.statement: Rajkot consolidation expected to lower power, fuel, transportation and operating costs as utilization improves
items.quote: the recommencement of Rajkot main manufacturing facility and the consolidation of production from the Gondal facility expected to improve manufacturing efficiencies through lower power and fuel, transportation, and operatin g costs. These benefits will reflect as the utilization improve over the coming quarters

items.statement: Nagpur plant capacity utilization under 30%, 60 distributors remapped to Modasa for logistics savings
items.quote: When we look at operational efficiencies, so we identified 159 distributors who were mapped to our Nagpur plant, out of which roughly 60 distributors we already mapped to our Modasa plant because that gives us benefit in terms of logistics costs. So that continues to put pressure on Nagpur plant in terms of lower utilization, lower capacity utilization.

items.statement: Distributor base expanded to over 1,000 distributors nationally
items.quote: We expanded our distributor base to over 1,000 distributors while continuing to deepen our presence across core and focus markets.

items.statement: Retail touchpoints at 5.25-5.5 lakh outlets nationally, targeting 6 lakh by end of FY27
items.quote: as on date, as a brand, we are a vailable somewhere between 5.25 lakhs to 5.5 lakhs outlets. And going forward, since we already are working on footprint expansion as well as distribution automation, so by end of this year, we'll definitely be present at 6 lakh outlets

items.statement: Focus state distributors grew from 440 in Q1 FY26 to 567 in Q1 FY27; other states from 110 to 129
items.quote: distributor count in focus states, it was 440 in Q1 FY26, it went up to 530 in Q4 FY26, and in just concluded quarter, which is Q1 FY27, it was 567. It did not drop. And in other states as well, it went up from 110 to 129

items.statement: 5 of 7 new product launches in H2 FY27 are non-palm oil based with healthier margins
items.quote: out of 7 NPIs which are in pipeline, 5 NPIs are non-palm oil based with healthier margin and which have synergies with our existing product category.

items.statement: Other products category (Shot Go Noodles, rusks, wafers, washing bar) grew to INR 24 crores monthly run rate
items.quote: last year we did INR 10 crores, now we're doing INR 24 crores, INR 23 crores.

items.statement: Chana inventory stored till Q3 end, potato stored, palm oil and laminate purchased at spot prices
items.quote: chana we have stored almost till Q3 end, so there also there has been inflation, but that is not hitting our P&L. Potato we have stored it. Palm oil and laminate prices, we are continuously buy from the market.

items.statement: Insurance claim of INR 30-40 crores expected in Q2 FY27, documents submitted to PSU insurers
items.quote: We are expecting those things to fall in Q2. However, since this is coming from the insurance company, from the PSUs, but we are quite confident enough because whatever necessary documents were required already submitted to the insurance company and the pr ocess is going very strongly

items.statement: No major churn in regional brands in Gujarat; two national brands (Miraj, Star) shut but Miraj restarted
items.quote: we don't see any major impact as such, whatever brands were operating, those are operating, name it our Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari, all the brands are present, and we don't see any churning as such. And coming to the national level, we noticed two brands got shut. One was based out of Rajasthan, Nathdwara, called Miraj brand. Another was Ghodawat Group brand Star brand, based out of Kolhapur. But no

items.statement: Gujarat market still 65% unorganized, gradual shift to organized continuing for decades
items.quote: To my estimate, still in Gujarat, roughly 65% market is unorganized, Saurabh-bhai. And it has been happening for last 3 decades-4 decades now that market is getting shifted from unorganized to organized, and it will continue to happen.

items.statement: Management does not give quarterly brand marketing spend guidance but targets overall customer inducement cost (brand, performance, discounts) around 4% of GTV when possible
items.quote: we don't typically give guidance on the brand marketing spend, but what I can tell you is that if you look at the overall customer inducement cost that we have, right, which is brand performance and discounts put together, we try to stay in the 4% of the GTV range, right, whenever we can.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA declined 7% YoY to Rs 29.24 cr as operating leverage from core businesses is reinvested into hotels and AI
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding other income and ESOP costs, was INR 29.24 crores, compared to INR 31.34 crores, a decline of 7%.

items.statement: Contribution margin grew 13% YoY to Rs 144.94 cr with margin percentage stable at 40.6%
items.quote: Contribution margin grew to 144.94 crores, up 13%, with contribution margin percentage at 40.6% against 40.5% last year.

items.statement: GTV reached all-time high of Rs 5,524.33 cr, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Gross transaction value, or GTV reached INR 5,524.33 crores, a 19% increase over 4,644.66 crores in Q1 last year.

items.statement: Bus passenger segments grew 33% YoY to 0.89 cr; GTV up 39% to Rs 947.43 cr
items.quote: On buses, passenger segments grew 33% to 0.89 crores. GTV grew 39% to Rs. 947.43 crores.

items.statement: Flight segments grew 4% YoY to 0.29 cr; flight GTV up 27% to Rs 2,341.84 cr
items.quote: In flights, we booked 0.29 crore flight segments, up 4%, with a GTV of Rs. 2,341.84 crores, up 27%.

items.statement: Train segments declined 8% YoY to 2.44 cr; train GTV up 4% to Rs 2,138.86 cr
items.quote: For trains, we booked 2.44 crore train segment, down 8%. GTV was Rs. 2,138.86 crores, up 4%.

items.statement: Bus business is now largest contributor to group contribution margin at 37%, followed by trains at 36% and flights at 28%
items.quote: Buses are now the largest contributor to contribution margin, accounting for 37% of the group.

items.statement: Hotel business (in Others segment) contribution margin was negative Rs 3.06 cr vs positive Rs 1.86 cr last year, reflecting deliberate investment
items.quote: Others had a contribution margin of negative INR 3.06 crore against a positive INR 1.86 crore last year. That is a meaningful part of where this year's investment in hotel is showing up above the contribution margin, and this is a choice that we are making with our eyes open.

items.statement: 90% of hotel bookings come from existing registered users on ixigo platform, not new acquisitions
items.quote: 90% of the bookings we are seeing are coming from users who are already registered on our platform, right, which means they were already our users and not people who came and registered for the explicit purpose of buying a hotel.

items.statement: Monthly active users 8.5 cr, monthly transacting users 0.42 cr, MTU/MAU ratio nearly 5%
items.quote: monthly active users were 8.5 crore, monthly transacting users were 0.42 crore, with our MTU to MAU ratio up to nearly 5%.

items.statement: Train OTA market share increased from ~60% to 63% this quarter
items.quote: Our share of the OTA train market has increased from approximately 60% a few quarters ago to 63% this quarter.

items.statement: Bus GDP growth 39% YoY, exceeding 60% in 17 states including Delhi, Odisha, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh and several Northeastern states
items.quote: Our year-on-year GDP growth came in at 39%, much higher than that of the market, and it even exceeded 60% in 17 of the states we operate in, including large markets such as Delhi, Odisha, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Himachal Pradesh, as well as in several states in the Northeast

items.statement: Investing in AI infrastructure, model development, token usage, orchestration, engineering talent; costs front-loaded but expected to moderate as productivity benefits scale
items.quote: Building this capability requires investment today. That investment is currently visible through higher expenditure on engineering talent, AI infrastructure, model development, token usage, and orchestration. Some of these costs are front-loaded.

items.statement: Acquired 54.66% stake in Brevistay to accelerate hotel supply, direct relationships, flexible stay inventory and Peace of Mind products
items.quote: The acquisition of a 54.66% stake in Brevistay accelerates this journey. Brevistay adds direct hotel relationships, feet on the street, supply capabilities and expertise in flexible stay inventory.

items.statement: Direct hotel partnerships now exceed 10,000 hotels across nearly 700 towns, signing up several thousand more each quarter
items.quote: We now have direct partnerships with more than 10,000 hotels across nearly 700 towns, including thousands of independent properties, and we are signing up several thousand more every quarter.

items.statement: Bus roadside assistance program now covers ~95% of bookings across 20 states with AC taxi typically arriving within 45-60 minutes
items.quote: Our roadside assistance progr am, for instance, provides eligible travelers with a replacement taxi to their destination in the event of a bus breakdown or accident. It is now available across 20 states and covers approximately 95% of our bookings, with an AC taxi typically showing up within 45 to 60 minutes of a breakdown even in the middle of a highway

items.statement: Domestic flight average transaction value up 22% YoY and 13% QoQ; international ATV up 38% YoY and nearly 30% QoQ due to capacity constraints and oil prices
items.quote: Domestic average transaction values or fares on our platform increased 22% year-on-year and 13% sequentially. International average transaction values increased 38% year-on-year and nearly 30% sequentially.

items.statement: Bus net take rate sequentially lower at 10.8% due to peak season discounting; gross take rate 11-11.5%, discounting range-bound over last 6-8 quarters
items.quote: No. So, 11%-11.5% is the gross take rate, and then there are discounts which lead to the net take rate. But if you look at the discounting levels we have operated at in the last 6-8 quarters, right, we have been range-bound on that.

items.statement: ixigo continues to be fastest-growing flight OTA in India and gaining market share across all categories despite challenging environment
items.quote: We have continued to be the fastest-growing flight OT in India and have continued gaining market share; however, the current environment affects an important part of our growth funnel.

items.statement: Aviation capacity cuts by Air India (~20%) and IndiGo (~10%) in JAS quarter leading to YoY decline in flown passengers; meaningful capacity restoration may begin only in festive Q3
items.quote: Right now, I can tell you that for Air India, we have seen close to 20% cut. Indigo, we have seen like a 10-ish% cut, right. So, on the supply side, if that continues, it's going to be a very tough situation for everyone who's in the air OTA business.

items.statement: High airfares widening price gap with train/bus deferring next-billion-user upgrade to air travel, especially in Tier-2/3 markets
items.quote: When the price gap between a flight and a train or bus journey expands so sharply, these users are more likely to defer or reconsider their upgrade to air travel. That effect is especially visible in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets.

items.statement: Hiring focus shifting to judgment, taste, empathy, agency, resilience, curiosity, ambition as AI makes execution more accessible
items.quote: We believe seven of these qualities will become especially important: Judgment. Taste. Empathy. Agency. Resilience. Curiosity. Ambition.

items.statement: Food on trains crossed 17 lakh meals in quarter, touching 20,000+ on many days; metro bookings growing month-on-month, live in 5 cities
items.quote: Food on trains crossed 17 lakh meals during the quarter, touching 20,000 plus on many days. Metro bookings are growing month on month, and we are now live in five cities.

items.statement: Launched Bharat Darshan Rail Packages on train apps offering all-inclusive tourist train experiences with IRCTC and tour operator partners
items.quote: We have gone live with Bharat Darshan Rail Packages on our train apps, offering affordable all-inclusive tourist train experiences that encompass the journey, hotel, sightseeing or darshan at destinations in partnership with IRCTC and its tour operator partners.

items.statement: AI chatbot resolved 92% of customer queries this quarter, up from 88%
items.quote: 92% of our customer queries were solved by the AI chatbot this quarter, up from 88%.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins to remain in the 14% to 15% range, inclining towards the upper bracket given strong Q1.
items.quote: Margins are expected to remain at similar levels, right? So we have always guided for a 14% to 15% margin. And obviously, quarter -- as we've always discussed, it's difficult to rate the business quarterly. But overall, at an annual level, we expect that the margins should remain in the 14% to 15%.

items.statement: API segment targets monthly EBITDA positivity by end of FY27 (Feb-Mar) and positive profit contribution in FY28.
items.quote: Absolutely right, Abdul. So the whole target is on a monthly level, at least by the end of February, March, we should be monthly EBITDA positive in this business. And then next year, we should start positively contributing to the profit from this segment.

items.statement: Zambia order revenue of ~$25 million (~INR240 crores) expected in H2 FY27 and similar in FY28; European business to kickstart in FY28.
items.quote: Zambia is something we expect in the H2 that we deliver for this fiscal, the $25 million, which will roughly translate to almost INR240-odd crores in our revenue. And similar in the next financial year as well. And within the next financial year, we will kickstart our European business as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 15% (up 238 bps YoY, 187 bps QoQ); gross margins above 40% driven by high-value product mix and API price rebound.
items.quote: Margins were robust at 15%, improving 238 basis points year-on-year. Quarter 1 FY26, we were at 12.6%, and 187 basis points quarter-on-quarter or Q4 FY26, we were at 13.1%.

items.statement: Zambia order: agreed volumes and prices for 100+ products; revenue recognition in FY27. European business launch in FY28.
items.quote: As we speak, we are already in advanced stages where we have agreed upon the volumes and the prices with the government over there of almost 100-plus products that we would be supplying in Zambia. So that is completely on track. And this fiscal, we'll recognize the revenue.

items.statement: New oral manufacturing facility in Baddi to go live by end of FY27; capex amount still under discussion.
items.quote: the process of setting up one more facility in Baddi, which will go live in the -- almost at the end of this financial year itself, which will significantly boost our oral manufacturing capabilities, right? Praveen Jayaraman: Right. What could be the capex...? Sahil Maheshwari: So we are still discussing. As we go live, we'll update you with it

items.statement: CDMO operates on cost-plus model; API price increases passed through at every purchase order.
items.quote: So the model has always remained a cost plus, right? So it is at every purchase order or whatever is the prevailing price of the input materials that gets passed through.

items.statement: Domestic branded (Akumentis) added ~200 field force (15% increase) to expand into adjacent HQs/cities; focus on gynaecology, cardiology, paediatrics.
items.quote: As mentioned in the initial note, we have added almost 200 people in our field force to tap adjacent headquarters, which are important where we can tap some growth, right? So the focus here remains how do we expand our presence into prescription business?

items.statement: Acquired Oriflame India manufacturing (Roorkee, Noida plants + warehouse) to expand skin care/cosmetics capacity and enter color cosmetics.
items.quote: On 23rd of July, we announced the acquisition of Oriflame India's manufacturing business. The transaction covers two manufacturing facilities, one at Roorkee, Uttarakhand and other one at Noida, Uttar Pradesh, along with a leased warehouse situated at Noida, Uttar Pradesh. With the acquisition, we expand our manufacturing footprint in skin care cosmetics and wellness products.

items.statement: Zero debt; net worth >INR3,400 crores; cash surplus INR1,616 crores net of debt.
items.quote: So Abdul, I'll answer the first part of the question. Most of the money, in fact, 98% of the money is parked in fixed deposits with nationalized banks, right? And the money is safely with these banks. There was another question on inorganic. So our net worth sits at more than INR3,400 crores and there is no debt on the company.

items.statement: Domestic branded (Akumentis) revenue INR115 crores (+7.3% YoY, +12.9% QoQ); EBITDA INR12 crores (-25.4% YoY, -46.5% QoQ) due to field force expansion.
items.quote: Domestic branded formulation stood at INR115 crores, an increase of 7.3% year-on-year and an increase of 12.9% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA for the quarter was INR12 crores, a decline of 25.4% year-on-year and a decrease of 46.5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: International branded (Unosource) revenue INR35 crores (-1.5% YoY, -3.6% QoQ); EBITDA INR6.9 crores (-14.4% YoY, -31.4% QoQ).
items.quote: For the international branded formulation business, the revenue stood at INR35 crores, a decline of 1.5%, at Q1 of '26, we were at INR35 crores and a decline of 3.6% quarter-on-quarter, Q4 FY26, the revenue stood at INR36 crores. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR6.9 crores, a decline of 14.4% year-on-year and a decline of 31.4% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: API revenue INR32 crores (-29.7% YoY, -22.3% QoQ); EBITDA loss INR4 crores (improved from -INR6 crores YoY, -INR12 crores QoQ).
items.quote: API revenue stood at INR32 crores, a decline of 29.7% year-on-year, Q1 FY26, it was INR45 crores, a decline of 22.3% quarter-on-quarter, Q4 '26, the revenue stood at INR41 crores. EBITDA for the quarter was at minus INR4 crores. The losses were lower than Q1 FY26, which stood at minus INR6 crores, as well as Q4 FY26, which stood at minus INR12 crores.

items.statement: Trade generics revenue INR21 crores (-9.5% YoY, -23.4% QoQ); EBITDA breakeven at INR0.1 crores (2nd consecutive quarter).
items.quote: Trade generic business stood at INR21 crores, a decrease of 9.5% year-on-year and a decrease of 23.4% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA continued to remain at breakeven for the second quarter in a row. It was -- it is generally higher than the breakeven of INR0.1 crores compared to minus INR5 crores quarter 1 FY26 and INR1.4 crores in quarter 4 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR1,167 crores (+13.9% YoY, +0.8% QoQ); EBITDA INR175 crores (+35.4% YoY, +15.1% QoQ); PAT INR101 crores (+56.1% YoY, +24.1% QoQ).
items.quote: Our operating revenue stood at INR1,167 crores, an increase of 13.9% year-on-year. Quarter 1 FY26, the revenue was INR1,024 crores and increasing 0.8% quarter-on-quarter. Quarter 4 FY26, our revenue was INR1,158 crores. The operating EBITDA for the quarter was INR175 crores, an increase of 35.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin target around 30-32% and opex target ₹300-325 crore per quarter
items.quote: Our gross-margin target is around 30-32%, which is where we want it to be, and opex continues to improve structurally.

items.statement: Expect gross margins to remain steady to slightly growing and volumes steady to slightly growing
items.quote: While doing this, we intend to keep gross margins steady to slightly growing and volumes also steady to slightly growing.

items.statement: Service revenue roadmap targeting ₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28
items.quote: Our roadmap targeting service revenue of approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY 2027-28.

items.statement: ASP expected to remain broadly around ₹1.25 lakh plus or minus 5%
items.quote: Overall I would say ASP should remain broadly around 1.25L, plus or minus 5%.

items.statement: Capex beyond Cell project completion around ₹30-50 crore for the year
items.quote: Except for the Cell project that is now being completed, capex beyond that will be around ₹30-50 crore. You can use ₹50 crore as a target number.

items.statement: Cell factory expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh planned in FY27 with separate equity raise
items.quote: At that point, we will aim to scale from 6 GWh to 20 GWh, but only by bringing equity into the Cell company. We will not use equity from the parent entity for that expansion; we will raise separate equity at the right time.

items.statement: Most vehicles expected to be on in-house cells by end of this year
items.quote: As an assumption, by the end of this year most of our vehicles should be on our own cells.

items.statement: Deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units; orders increased to ~44,000
items.quote: Deliveries increased to approximately 39,200 units, nearly doubling quarter-on-quarter, while orders increased to approximately 44,000.

items.statement: Market share grew from 5.1% to 8.4% with registrations up 97% QoQ vs industry 17%
items.quote: The broader electric two-wheeler market grew approximately 17% quarter-on-quarter, while Ola registrations grew 97%, taking our market share from 5.1% to 8.4%.

items.statement: Auto gross margin sustained at 30.5% despite commodity upcycle
items.quote: Despite a challenging commodity environment, we sustained Auto gross margin at 30.5%, reflecting the underlying strength of our product economics.

items.statement: Expect margins to remain above 30% over next quarter or two and improve as commodity prices ease
items.quote: Margins remained steady and industry-leading at above 30%, despite the commodity upcycle. We expect margins to remain in this range over the next quarter or two and to improve further as commodity prices ease.

items.statement: Cell factory completing 6 GWh capacity this quarter; remaining capex funded through debt
items.quote: Our Cell factory is also completing its capex cycle this quarter with 6 GWh installed. We do not foresee material capex after that, and the remaining Cell capex is funded through debt; the equity contribution is largely complete.

items.statement: Auto portfolio: ~20% to remain NMC for high-end; rest moving to LFP; all energy storage LFP-based
items.quote: Ola Electric's Auto business will move to LFP over time. Please wait until later this month, when we will have some announcements on that. Within Auto, about 20% of our portfolio will remain NMC -based for higher -performance and top -end products. Everything else will move to LFP. All of Shakti and Mahashakti - the energy- storage business - will be LFP-based

items.statement: Dealer model shifts parts inventory to dealers on cash-and-carry basis, reducing supply chain challenges
items.quote: Going forward, under the dealer model, dealers will stock parts and buy them from us on a cash-and-carry basis. That should materially reduce this challenge across the dealer-led sales and service network.

items.statement: ₹780 crore QIP completed strengthening balance sheet; Cell capex funded through debt
items.quote: The balance sheet strengthened during the quarter through the successful completion of a ₹780 crore QIP, giving us greater financial flexibility as we pursue the next phase of our growth.

items.statement: Electric two-wheeler penetration in India crossed 10% for first time in June
items.quote: The external environment remains supportive, with electric two-wheeler penetration in India crossing 10% for the first time in June this year.

items.statement: Cell yields in high-70s to ~80% when paused; roadmap to >90% within a quarter of restart
items.quote: Yields were in the high-70s to around 80% range when we paused production. There is a clear roadmap to move from there to above 90% within a quarter of restarting.

items.statement: Parts supply chain had vendor challenges linked to macro geopolitical situation; couple of items still monitored closely
items.quote: Whenever parts were required, some were in short supply, particularly a few critical parts where we faced vendor challenges, including issues linked to the macro geopolitical situation. We are navigating that. There are no material challenges in the parts supply chain, although there are a couple of items that we monitor very closely.

items.statement: Depreciation policy aligned to industry norms; delta ~₹10-20 crore
items.quote: On depreciation, we have evolved parts of our depreciation policy to align with industry standards. There were some areas where we were depreciating assets very aggressively, and we have brought those to industry norms. The resulting delta is about ₹10-20 crore.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margins of 29-30% (+/- 100-150 bps) over the next 2-3 years driven by backward integration and scale.
items.quote: we have consistently, you know, informed that the margins of 29%, 30%, plus-minus 100, 150 basis points, we will be maintaining.

items.statement: Transformer business revenue expected to more than triple over the next three years from ~INR400 crores base.
items.quote: Over the next three years, we expect this to be more than triple of that level.

items.statement: Depreciation expected to reach INR240-250 crores quarterly by Q3/Q4 FY27 as new capacities commission.
items.quote: we will see roughly about INR240 crores to INR250 crores of depreciation quarterly.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was INR1,500 crores, with INR1,250 crores on solar (Seetharampur and Naidupeta) and INR250 crores on Transcon.
items.quote: So the total capex in the quarter was about INR1,500 crores. Bulk of the capex was incurred on solar, on solar projects, basically both Seetharampur and Naidupeta. And then the remaining was incurred on Transcon, INR250 crores.

items.statement: 5.6 GW fully automated solar module plant at Seetharampur is operational; 7 GW TOPCon cell line in advanced commissioning with trial runs starting this month.
items.quote: Our 5.6 gigawatt fully automated solar module plant at Seetharampur is operational. The 7 gigawatt TOPCon cell line is in advanced stages of commissioning, with trial runs expected to start later this month.

items.statement: Existing Telangana cell plants delivered record 92% capacity utilization in Q1.
items.quote: Our operational cell plants in Telangana delivered a record capacity utilization of 92%, showcasing our all-round excellence in plant operations.

items.statement: Transformer capacity growing from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28 with shift to HV/EHV segments and export focus.
items.quote: our transformer capacity is growing almost from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28

items.statement: New orders of INR3,011 crores for cells and modules in Q1, taking total order book to INR15,000 crores including transformers.
items.quote: We won new orders totalling INR3,011 crores for cells and modules, taking our total order book to INR15,000 crores, including transformers.

items.statement: DCR module order book sold out for FY27, now booking for FY28; cell orders spread over FY28-FY29.
items.quote: DCR is, we are sold out. So, you know, we are selling now only for FY28 now.

items.statement: 40-45% of INR15,000 crores order book expected to execute in FY28.
items.quote: a substantial portion of this order book, at least about 40% to 45% of this order book, would go into FY28.

items.statement: Solar demand strong with ~12 GW capacity addition in Q1; PM Surya Ghar and KUSUM schemes driving momentum.
items.quote: Solar demand has been strong, too, with nearly 12 gigawatt of capacity addition in quarter one itself, with great momentum in the PM Surya Ghar Yojana and KUSUM schemes.

items.statement: KUSUM installations expected at 6-8 GW AC (higher in DC) over next 9 months; Surya Ghar at 1.2-1.3 GW/month average.
items.quote: I would expect the installation over the next nine months to be something between 6 to 8, possibly higher than 8 gigawatts.

items.statement: C&I DCR demand to pick up from Q4 FY27 (Oct-Dec) as ALMM Phase 2 mandates DCR modules for projects commissioned from Jan 1.
items.quote: the demand will start arising from the last quarter of this year, which is basically October, November, December.

items.statement: Cell pricing stable on mono-PERC; TOPCon cells used internally, not sold externally currently.
items.quote: Pricing is more or less been stable on the solar cell side, that is the mono-PERC cell. TOPCon cell, we don't sell. We use it for our own consumption.

items.statement: DCR module pricing stable across segments (Surya Ghar 24-24.5 cents, KUSUM ~22 cents, C&I slightly lower); no material change in spreads despite rupee depreciation.
items.quote: most of the order book is already in place, particularly for DCR modules as well as for cells, and those are all booked at the current prices. So there is no change that we see, I would say, even over the next 12 to 15 month kind of trajectory.

items.statement: Europe market opening up with tenders in Italy, France, Germany excluding Chinese modules; advanced stages of opening European office and hiring sales team.
items.quote: Europe actually is in a take off stage. In fact, we are in advanced stages of opening our European office and even hiring a sales team over there.

items.statement: ALMM Phase 2 extension to December 2025 triggered influx of non-DCR orders; DCR mandate from Jan 2026 for new projects.
items.quote: the government has said that any projects commissioned from 1st January onwards will have to use DCR modules.

items.statement: BESS plan of 12 GW (6 GW Phase 1) underway with land acquired and construction started; technology partner for containerized solution to be finalized in 2-3 months.
items.quote: our BESS plan of 12 gigawatt, 6 gigawatt Phase 1 is already underway, construction has started, and technology partner would be, I think, finalized in the next two to three months.

items.statement: New capacity expansions largely funded by equity; finance expense increase expected to be relatively small in Q3/Q4.
items.quote: bulk of the increase in capacity for the new lines has been actually funded by equity. So the increase in expenses will be actually relatively quite small.

items.statement: Industry consolidation inevitable as smaller non-integrated module manufacturers face vanishing margins; profitability shifted upstream to cell/ingot-wafer.
items.quote: consolidation in our mind is inevitable in the sector.

items.statement: No concrete plan to raise primary capital in near future; enabling resolutions taken annually for flexibility.
items.quote: As we speak, I can confirm that there is no concrete plan to raise any primary capital in the near future.

items.statement: Commissioned 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi, taking total distillery capacity to 800 KLPD
items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the successful commissioning of our 200 kilolitres per day grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi, taking our total distillery capacity to 800 kilolitres per day.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR25 crores in debottlenecking bio-based specialty chemical capacity
items.quote: We have, therefore, decided to invest a further INR25 crores in debottlenecking our capacity to be able to further meet the growing demand for our bio-based specialty chemical business.

items.statement: Evaluating addition of 160 KLPD fungible capacity within existing 800 KLPD for grain-to-ethanol conversion
items.quote: In this context, we are evaluating the addition of 160 kilolitres per day fungible capacity within the existing 800 kilolitres per day capacity.

items.statement: Expects bio-based chemical revenue of INR190 crores in Q2 FY27 and INR240 crores per quarter after debottlenecking completion in early FY28
items.quote: In the first quarter of this past compared to the quarter before, we have seen a good increase from about INR141 crores to INR169 crores, and we are anticipating in this coming quarter INR190 crores of business.

items.statement: Bio-based chemicals EBITDA margin expanded to 11.4% from 8.9% YoY, supported by favorable product mix and debottlenecking benefits
items.quote: The bio-based chemicals business delivered a strong performance with revenue growing 19.4% year-on-year to INR168.7 crores, and EBITDA increasing 53% to INR19.2 crores. EBITDA margin expanded to 11.4% from 8.9%, supported by favorable product mix and the benefits of the debottlenecking initiatives.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin declined to 0.5% from 1.2% YoY due to elevated inventory carrying cost and higher raw material prices
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR2.6 crores compared to INR6.5 crores in Q1 FY26, with margin at 0.5% against 1.2% last year. Profitability was impacted by elevated inventory carrying cost and higher raw material prices.

items.statement: Government issued draft guidelines for E85 and E100 fuels; auto companies launched flex-fuel engines
items.quote: The government has come out with new draft guidelines for E85 and E100 to be used as a fuel. This will lead to these fuels coming out in the market sooner rather than later and reflect the government's direction for the country to be more self-reliant in energy.

items.statement: Monitoring climate effects including El Niño, rainfall and dam levels in Maharashtra and Karnataka; recent weeks have improved dam levels and rainfall
items.quote: We were and we remain very focused on looking at climate effects, because there was a prediction of El Niño. So, we are very focused. Our areas are Maharashtra, Karnataka that we examine, and we look at rainfall in our area of operation as well as dam levels

items.statement: DME pilot trials progressing as planned; final results expected by March 2027
items.quote: The pilot trials are proceeding as planned. Final results of how the pilot trials have done will come latest by March of 2027.

items.statement: Filed CDSCO application for preliminary efficacy trials of triple-negative breast cancer molecule; expects permissions by end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have filed the application the CDSCO, which itself is one milestone. The next milestone we expect will be the permission from the CDSCO to start these preliminary trials. We are hoping for we get these permissions by the end of this third quarter FY27.

items.statement: No capital raise needed for R&D; estimates INR20 crores over 2-3 years for preliminary efficacy trials, funded internally
items.quote: Our estimate of taking it to preliminary efficacy is about INR20 crores over the next 2 to 3 years. So, we do believe that we have the resources for this purpose within the system.

items.statement: Expects to keep debt levels similar with slight changes, no major changes in overall debt-equity structure despite ongoing investments
items.quote: We are looking at broadly keeping debt levels similar or a margin or a slight change, not major changes in the overall debt-equity structure.

items.statement: Seeing greater customer interest in bio-based chemicals abroad and at home due to supply chain reliability and narrowing fossil-green price gap
items.quote: We are definitely seeing greater interest, which is reflecting in our greater business in this last quarter and the business that will happen in this quarter, and which is what is encouraging us to make this debottlenecking so that by next year, we have further increase in business.

items.statement: Sugar prices increased in recent weeks; ethanol prices from sugarcane juice remained same over past years; will optimize diversion based on economics
items.quote: The prices of sugar have increased in the past few weeks. The prices of ethanol from sugarcane juice have remained the same over the past few years. So, we will continue to look at the economics of sugar and ethanol as we make our choices of diversion.

items.statement: Expects higher ethanol demand going forward due to E20 rollout, growing fuel consumption, and draft E85/E100 guidelines
items.quote: India is a rapidly growing large economy of the world. The economy is growing, and this consumption for mobility across the nation, whether it be petrol or diesel, is also growing at equal to or higher than the country's GDP growth rate. So, we definitely look at a ethanol in at the same levels of blending, that means even with E20 with the growth in fuel consumption, there will be an increase.

items.statement: Full-year order inflow guidance of INR30,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving our full-year order inflow guidance of INR30,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR43,290 crores at end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: With these orders, our order book stood at INR43,290 crores at the end of the quarter, providing strong visibility for future revenues.

items.statement: Orders booked for FY27 to date stand at INR15,700 crores
items.quote: As on date, our orders booked for the year stands at INR15,700 crores, including orders received up to date.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 9.6% in Q1 FY27, down from 13% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Coming to profitability, we reported an EBITDA margin of 9.6% during the quarter.

items.statement: Overseas projects have 200-300 bps higher margins than domestic projects
items.quote: the delta in, say, domestic versus overseas is around 200 to 300 basis points, which is higher in overseas market.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR1.5 lakh crores for remaining 9 months of FY27 and INR3.96 lakh crores for next 2 years
items.quote: This is supported by our healthy bid pipeline of approximately INR1.5 lakh crores for the remaining 9 months of financial '27, and INR3.96 lakh crores for the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY28 capex expected in range of INR600-650 crores
items.quote: So, in FY28, we are looking at capex in the range of say INR600 crores to INR650 crores.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity at 0.68x; targeting net debt of INR2,700-2,800 crores by year-end
items.quote: Net debt will be somewhere around INR2,700 to INR2,800 crores kind of a number.

items.statement: Working capital elevated due to funding projects and slow collections; net working capital at elevated level
items.quote: Specifically, the net working capital is at an elevated level because of funding to the projects and no material movement in collection of the blocked-up asset.

items.statement: Working capital days marginally increased from March levels
items.quote: It has marginally increased from the March number.

items.statement: Energy, transport, and logistics costs increased, partially offsetting cost reduction efforts
items.quote: We have put lot of efforts towards reducing cost on the possible revenue, but that has been partially offset by increase in energy, transport, and logistics cost.

items.statement: Interest-bearing advances at 38% of total advances; expect interest cost to decrease as new orders have interest-free or low-interest advances
items.quote: Currently, 62% of our advances are interest-free and 38% of the advances are interest-bearing.

items.statement: Both TBMs for Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 package commenced initial tunneling drives; main tunneling drives expected to start in coming months
items.quote: both tunnel boring machines for our Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail C2 package successfully commenced their initial tunneling drives as per schedule.

items.statement: UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments remain problematic with INR400 crores receivable; Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan payments partly coming
items.quote: in UP, we were having close to INR400 crores of receivable. From there, we have received a very small fraction.

items.statement: Overseas revenue share dropped to 16% in Q1 from 30% in March; order book mix now at 25% overseas, targeting return to 30%
items.quote: In Q1, we are we are having overseas revenue around 16% from overseas market, domestic is 84%.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties weighing on infrastructure investments and project award activity across regions
items.quote: For some time now, geopolitical developments have weighed on infrastructure investments and project award activity across several regions.

items.statement: Execution challenges from land handover delays, labor shortages, pending clearances, and adverse weather expected to ease over coming quarters
items.quote: We expect these issues to gradually ease, enabling stronger execution momentum over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Bid pipeline for next 9 months: Urban infra 34%, Marine 32%, Hydro/Underground 20%, Surface transport 14%
items.quote: major chunk is from urban infrastructure, which for us comprises of metro and elevated bridges and elevated roads, that is around 34%. Marine is 32%. Hydro and underground is 20%. It includes our water business as well. Surface, which is road and railway business, that is 14

items.statement: Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link project inaugurated on 1st May 2026; cable-stayed bridge is India's tallest road cable bridge
items.quote: I'm delighted to share that the Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link project was inaugurated on 1st May 2026, marking yet another defining milestone in Afcons' journey.

items.statement: Croatia railway project is largest single order ever secured by Afcons; Vadhvan Port project involves world's second largest breakwater
items.quote: The Croatia railway project represents the largest single order ever secured by Afcons, while the Vadhvan Port project provides us with the opportunity to construct the world's second largest breakwater.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations negative in Q1 as typical due to government budget cycles; collections slow in Q1
items.quote: cash flow from operations generally in Q1 remains to be negative, because in past also we have explained that customers, what they try to do is, they will try to release all the payment in -- up to date payment in March quarter.

items.statement: Other income for full year FY27 expected around INR400 crores
items.quote: this year also, we'll be in the range of say, for the year somewhere around INR400 or so.

items.statement: Depreciation lower in Q1 at INR83.52 crores due to minimal TBM activity; expected to increase in H2 as TBM operations ramp up
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA, the depreciation is at INR83.52 crores, which is 3.06% of the turnover. This quarter, the TBM operations were virtually not there, so the accelerated depreciation what we charge was not there in the quarter.

items.statement: Tax rate elevated at ~40% in Q1 due to losses in JV/subsidiary entities and turnover-based taxes in overseas locations
items.quote: The tax rate is working out almost 40%. This is primarily because on Afcons' profit what we are paying, Afcons' standalone profit what we are paying 25% tax. However, in consolidated profit, this has decreased due to some of the closed projects which is in JVs and subsidiary where minor administrative expenses and provisions leading to small losses.

items.statement: Ketan Pendse joined as CFO in June 2026 with over two decades of experience
items.quote: I'm delighted to welcome Mr. Ketan Pendse, who joined AJAX as our Chief Financial Officer in June 2026. Ketan brings over two decades of industry experience and we're confident that his expertise and leadership will play a valuable role in driving AJAX's growth and success.

items.statement: Infrastructure sector faces near-term challenges with government spending below budgeted allocations and contractor payment delays
items.quote: the road bumps encountered over the last year or so in terms of actual government spending on infrastructure projects remaining well below the budgeted allocations, resulting in the slower -than-expected pace of project execution across the country, have br oadly remained in place during Q1 of this year as well

items.statement: Industry registrations down 27% in Q1 FY27, AJAX volumes down 21%, market share expanded to 75.1%
items.quote: the industry registrations in this quarter came down by 27% and AJAX was down 21%. So clearly speaking, the registration levels have been lower in the quarter.

items.statement: Q2 expected to remain seasonally soft, demand momentum to improve in H2 with 60% revenue typically in H2
items.quote: While Q2 is expected to remain seasonally soft, we expect customer sentiment and demand momentum to improve as we head into the second half of the year. As we highlighted previously, nearly 60% of our revenue is typically generated in H2.

items.statement: Direct material costs inching up due to fuel and steel price increases, cost optimization measures accelerated
items.quote: Towards the latter part of Q1, we saw direct material costs inching upwards owing to increase in fuel and steel prices. In anticipation of these cost pressures, we had initiated several internal cost optimization measures that were originally planned for implementation in the latter part of the year.

items.statement: Evaluating another price hike after 2% increase in Q4 FY26, to be implemented in calibrated manner
items.quote: Following the price increases of about 2% that we took in Q4 FY26, we are also evaluating another price hike which will be implemented in a calibrated manner, with the timing and quantum to be determined based on the prevailing market environment.

items.statement: UDAAN series scaling well with 121 units in Q1 FY27 and 35-40 units in July, ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The UDAAN series is scaling up reasonably well. We have seen some good traction for UDAAN in Q1. We plan to drive market activation initiatives such as demos and customer meetings to drive ho me the value proposition of UDAAN in its targeted application segment

items.statement: ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27 to fill portfolio gap
items.quote: We are planning to launch the new ARGO 4000 in Q2 FY27, which fills an important gap in our portfolio and further strengthens our product offering and value proposition.

items.statement: Key customer wins with Ultratech, JSW, ACC, J. Kumar in non-SLCM segment
items.quote: there are some key customer wins which we did not see as much coming in the past and the B2B team has been able to open some doors. For example, large players like Ultratech, JSW, ACC, J. Kumar, where either where we were not present or not present for quite a long period of time.

items.statement: Non-SLCM revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48 crores led by pumps, concrete pumps delivered strong growth
items.quote: Non-SLCM revenue in Q1 FY27 stood at around INR48 crores, growing by 6.4% year-on-year led by healthy growth in the pumps segment.

items.statement: Expect non-SLCM business to grow 10-15% YoY for full year FY27
items.quote: we would be happy if we are able to drive the non-SLCM business on a lower base to a decent number of about 10% -15% growth over the previous year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.5% in Q1 FY27, down 70 bps YoY, Q2 expected to be challenging, long-term target 13-15% corridor
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter dropped by 70 basis points and came in at 12.5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 margins challenging, 12.5% looks difficult, hope to return to 12.5% corridor by Q3 with volume improvement
items.quote: Definitely 12.5%, looks challenging at this point in time from a second quarter perspective. As we move into the third quarter and hopefully as the volumes see some improvement, I think some of that will start playing out and we'll get back to the corridors of about 12.5%.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target 13-15% corridor as demand improves
items.quote: On a general basis, I think we've called this out that for the longer term, the 13% to 15% corridor is something that we are very clear about that we will endeavor to make sure that as demand comes back to the economy, that should play.

items.statement: Strong emphasis on cash flow generation and disciplined working capital management, cash balance exceeding INR1,100 crores as of June 2026
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be a key source of strength with cash balance exceeding INR1,100 crores as of June 2026, providing us with ample flexibility to pursue future growth opportunities, including inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities with cash balance, committed to prudent utilization with guardrails
items.quote: we're aggressively pursuing the same, and we would be in a position to come back to you as and when I'm very clear about where we've gone. So, we remain committed to making sure that the cash gets utilized in a prudent manner and that giv es us good returns

items.statement: Streamlined org structure with all manufacturing under single leader, Obadenahalli plant head now oversees procurement and supply chain
items.quote: To drive greater operational agility and execution, we streamlined our org structure by bringing all manufacturing under a single leader. The head of our Obadenahalli plant now oversees procurement and supply chain.

items.statement: SLCM market share expanded to 75.1% in Q1 FY27 from 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% in FY26
items.quote: Our SLCM and retail market share expanded to 75.1% during Q1 FY27, increasing from about 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% during the full year FY26.

items.statement: Decadal mid-to-high teens CAGR trajectory, revenue CAGR 16-17% from 2014-2026
items.quote: AJAX has consistently demonstrated its resilience and ability to successfully navigate transitions, emerging stronger each time. This is reflected in our track record with a decadal mid-to-high teens CAGR trajectory.

items.statement: Geopolitical environment and commodity costs, currency implications not going away soon, steel prices E250/E350 increased
items.quote: there are challenges that are there on the horizon, particularly on the margin front given the fact that the geopolitical environment around us and the implication of that in terms of commodity costs, in terms of currency, I think they are not going to go away anytime soon.

items.statement: Urban infra and building applications now 35-40% of business vs 15-20% previously, offsetting muted government sectors
items.quote: urban infra and building-related work, which is both commercial and residential and some part government, are largely private sector led and we've seen some decent movement upwards, particularly in the urban infra, which currently in terms of application constitutes anywhere in the range of about 15% to 20%. Similarly in the case of buildings, in the range of about 10% to15%. So this number, which

items.statement: Other expenses up due to freight outward cost increase from diesel prices and export business, plus INR16 million SAP HANA migration cost
items.quote: There is increase in the freight outward cost which comes on account of two reasons. Overall, due to the increase in diesel prices as well as export business, we see an increase in marginal freight outward cost. At the same time, we are also undergoing migration from SAP ECC 6 to SAP HANA. So that's the cost which is coming in the books for this year to the tune of INR16 million.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 2,500 million for FY27 and Rs 2,000 million for FY28
items.quote: Our capex guidance remains at 2,500 million or 250 crores for FY27 and 2,000 million or 200 crores for FY28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 40% or higher over the longer term
items.quote: We expect this business to stabilize at 40% or higher EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Structural demand growth supported by manufacturing, infrastructure, steel, chemicals, pharma, healthcare, engineering, defence and emerging applications
items.quote: The long-term opportunity continues to be supported by India's manufacturing growth, infrastructure build-out, higher steel production, expansion in chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and the gradual increase in demand from healthcare, engineering, defence and emerging industrial applications.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 39% vs 38% YoY and 30% QoQ; improvement from higher operating efficiency, cost control, production and argon benefit
items.quote: On the margin front, the EBITDA margin stood at 39% compared to 38% in Q1 of FY26 and 30% in Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by newer energy-efficient plants, higher production, cost rationalization and renewable energy savings
