items.statement: Machine tool division order inflow was INR59 crores in Q1 FY27 with total order backlog of INR183 crores (30% of company backlog).
items.quote: The machine tool division recorded an order inflow of INR59 crores in FY26 quarter 1, with a total order backlog for this division reaching INR183 crores as of June 26, accounting for 30% of the company's overall order backlog.

items.statement: Quickmill recorded turnover of INR45 crores in Q1 FY27 and expects consistent performance based on pending orders.
items.quote: Quickmill recorded a turnover of INR45 crores in FY27 quarter 1, and based on the pending orders as of Q1 end, Quickmill will be delivering a consistent performance in upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Air Engineering group reported revenue of INR21 crores and order inflow of INR21 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The Air Engineering group reported revenue of INR21 crores in the quarter and for Q1 FY27, accompanied by an increase order inflow of INR21 crore s in the same quarter

items.statement: Textile machinery group had order inflow of INR79 crores, order backlog of INR201 crores, and revenue of INR12 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The textile machinery group had an order inflow of INR79 crores in Q1 FY27. Order backlog stood at INR201 crores. Textile machinery group reported a revenue of INR12 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering division reported order inflow of INR76 crores, revenue of INR27 crores, and order backlog of almost INR134 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The Environmental Engineering division reported order inflow of INR76 crores and a revenue of INR27 crores in the quarter, with healthy order backlog of almost INR134 crores.

items.statement: Investment in machine tool division capex has increased production capacity by around 30% over the last year.
items.quote: Based on the customer feedback and competitive benchmarking, our investment in capex is in machine tool divisions has started yielding results in terms of increasing production capacity around by around 30% over the last year.

items.statement: Planning one or two quick investments including in machine tool space and a solar plant to make energy cost revenue neutral.
items.quote: Yes, Shaishav, we are looking at some -- one or two quick investments, one maybe in our machine tool space its elf and we are also probably looking at the idea of putting one more solar plant in our factory to bring our overall operational cost lower and make the energy value almost revenue neutral

items.statement: Currently have 65-70% of power commissioned as solar, with 30-40% spare capacity available for augmentation this fiscal year.
items.quote: Right now, we have almost 65%-70% of the power commission solar power commissioned on our factory, and another 30%-40% of spare capacity available that we are definitely looking at augmenting that capacity by in this fiscal end.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 80% YoY to INR125 crores with stable EBITDA margin of 4% and PAT of INR49 lakhs vs loss of INR2.4 crores YoY.
items.quote: In Q1 FY26, our top-line revenue grew by 80% year-on-year to rupees INR125 crores, thereby beating our earlier guidance, while we successfully maintained a stable E BITDA margin of 4%. Despite meaningful headwinds from global supply chain disruptions and broader macroeconomic uncertainty, we recorded a PAT of INR49 lakhs against a loss of INR2.4 crores on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA improvement to 7-8% in next 1-2 years from current 4-6% level.
items.quote: See, look, today we are at let's say 4% of our -- 6% of EBITDA. Going forward in next t wo, 3 years, definitely any company would look at improving the EBITDA by having operational efficiency coming in and we are working towards that. We are looking at something around 7% to 8% in next 1 year or 2 years to reach that operating level

items.statement: Absorbing part of raw material cost increases (copper, steel) and passing on part to customers; also working on productivity improvements.
items.quote: So, for manufacturing space, of course, whatever the raw material cost increase comes up, like any other manufacturer, we are now trying to absorb part of it, trying to pass on to the customer, especially the copper, steel prices and there is an overall increase with all the manufacturers on terms of the raw material increase that are coming in.

items.statement: Demand for machine tools picking up due to government push for private industry participation in defense, aerospace and power sectors.
items.quote: Demand for machine tool is picking up, primarily due to government push for private industry participation in defense, aerospace and power industries.

items.statement: Textile industry expected to improve with new incentive policies and FTAs with UK and EU; focus on retrofit segments, export markets (Africa, South Asia) and Bangladesh recovery.
items.quote: Regarding textile industry, we expect this industry to do better with introduction of a new textile incentive policies announced by the government. FT As with UK and EU in the offing would also help. Going forward, our focus will be to generate business on retrofit segments, export markets like Africa and South Asia market, and also we expect the Bangladesh market to pick up as the situation stabi

items.statement: Mandatory zero liquid discharge implementation in high pollution industries creating sustained demand for advanced treatment systems; Bioconserve outlook robust with growth prospects from food, chemical, pharma industries.
items.quote: Mandatory zero liquid discharge implementation in high pollution industries is creating sustained demand for advanced treatment systems. Outlook for Bioconserve Renewable Envirotech Private Limited remains robust. Apart from this market, the growth prospects will be there from food, chemical, pharma industries going forward.

items.statement: Trading division seeing large orders from defense and aerospace sector clients with delivery timelines of 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: this year we are looking exceedingly well in t hat division where we are representing a lot of , you know, overseas principals because, you know, with the investment that is coming by the government sector in defense and aerospace, we have a large orders from a very big clients of us and all that is going to get, you know, these all basically machines are anywhere delivered between 1 year to 1.5 y

items.statement: Penta Automation did INR25 crores turnover last year; expecting 25-30% growth this year and average 25-30% growth for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Okay. So, Shaishav, last year they did a turnover of, I believe, INR25 crores and going forward, this year we may be ending over almost 25% to 30% growth and for next two, three years, we are looking at an average growth of 25%-30% for Penta.

items.statement: Performance subject to no further adverse impact from prolonged Middle East conflict or tariff-related headwinds.
items.quote: This is subject, of course, to not having any further adverse impact, if any, on the global and Indian economy in the event of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East and any tariff-related headwinds for the balance year.

items.statement: Continuing to look for buyer for land bank at Surat factory; one team working on it.
items.quote: Yes, sir. We continue to look for a buyer for this. And there is a one set of team who is working on this. And we are hopeful that if something very attractive comes across, we will go ahead and do the deal.

items.statement: Q1 order intake was INR11.4 billion, down 30% year-on-year due to lower TBCB realization in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Coming to financial performance during the first quarter, we saw order book at INR11.4 billion, down 30% year-on-year compared to INR16.2 billion in the quarter ended June '26. The primary reason for the lower order intake was due to lower realization of TBCB in market in Q4 '25-'26.

items.statement: Order backlog moderated 2.5% quarter-on-quarter to INR209.3 billion as of June 2026, representing over 3 years of FY26 revenue
items.quote: Execution outpaced new orders because of which the order backlog moderated to INR209.3 billion as of June '26 versus INR214.6 billion as of March '26, down by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter. The order backlog stands at more than 3 years of our revenue for FY25, '26.

items.statement: Management maintains full-year EBITDA margin guidance in the mid-20s band
items.quote: We maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA for the year. There is no reason that we should deviate from that right now.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin declined to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26 due to lower export mix, commodity costs, and HV business ramp-up; EBITDA margin was 25.1%
items.quote: Gross margins moderated to 41.3% from 48.4% a year ago and 47% in the last quarter. However, in our business, comparison with annual margin is a better reference point. So during financial year '25-'26, we achieved a gross margin of 45.3%. This quarter, gross margins are lower at 41.3%, representing a delta of 4%.

items.statement: Q1 revenue grew 38% year-on-year to INR18.4 billion driven by execution of high backlog
items.quote: Our Q1 revenue stood at INR18.4 billion versus INR13.3 billion, a growth of 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: Profit before tax grew over 1.25x year-on-year to INR4.9 billion with negligible finance costs and zero debt
items.quote: Our profit before tax and exceptional items for the quarter ended June 26 was at INR4.9 billion compared to around INR3.9 billion in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, growing by more than 1.25x.

items.statement: INR10 billion capacity expansion program announced last year is on track; INR2.5 billion dividend planned for Q2 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: Out of this cash balance, company has announced utilization plan of approximately INR13 billion, which includes INR10 billion of capacity expansion program announced in the last financial year and approximately INR2.5 billion of dividend in Q2, subject to the approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Generated INR4.3 billion cash in Q1; total available cash including cash pool lending stands at INR29.3 billion
items.quote: On the balance sheet and capital allocation side, we generated INR4.3 billion of cash during the quarter, taking our total available cash, including funds that we lend to the cash pool, to INR29.3 billion.

items.statement: Export orders constituted 46% of Q1 order intake driven by GE Vernova entities in North America, Spain, Morocco and data center customers
items.quote: This export diversification, which now stands at 46% of our Q1 orders is a trend, we have been building forward and had flagged in our earlier calls.

items.statement: Order backlog composition: 77% private customers, 21% central utilities/PSUs, 2% state utilities reflecting continued counter-party derisking
items.quote: I would also like to highlight the continued quality of our order book. Private customers now account for 77% of our backlog with central utilities and PSUs contributing another 21% and state utilities exposure just down to 2%.

items.statement: Chinese GIS suppliers approved for Indian market with 60-70% local content requirement; impact on pricing and competition to be assessed during negotiations
items.quote: But we'll also have to understand one thing that the government has approved. So, if you look at Chinese before they were restricted from participating in the Indian market, -- the Make in India clause of like 60%, 65% local content was not there.

items.statement: Domestic TBCB pipeline softened in Jan-Mar but improved from June onwards; full-year market expected to grow 6-7% on TBCB side
items.quote: If you look at January to March for TBCB, pipeline was soft. And because of that, you see the order intake, which is impacting the April to June order intake. But we are seeing now the TBCB pipeline or decisions are getting much better.

items.statement: Confident of achieving INR7,000-8,000 crore base order inflow for full year despite soft Q1
items.quote: No, we remain confident on.

items.statement: Transformer business has price escalation clauses linked to IEEMA formula; non-transformer business builds in commodity cost expectations at tendering with 18-24 month execution lag
items.quote: In that scope, we get a price escalation. So all the commodities like CRGO steel, etcetera, there is a formula embedded in the contract with which we get the compensation. So that part of the business is not impacted.

items.statement: Capacity utilization mixed: some factories well loaded, others have room to grow; Vallam project partial capacity expected Q1 FY28, balance by end FY28
items.quote: I would say it is consistent with whatever we have been explaining in the last few calls that a few of the factories, we are loaded pretty well and a few factories, we still have opportunity to grow.

items.statement: Competitive advantages cited as technology, lean manufacturing, and localization; Tier 2 competition varies by product segment
items.quote: So, of course, technology, Lean and localization. So, these three, we feel are the distinct advantages that we have.

items.statement: HVDC pipeline remains strong but pace slightly delayed; Lakadia on hold, Begunia converted to EHVAC, South Kalamb not yet awarded; developer selection expected Aug-Sep
items.quote: The HVDC pipeline remains strong. Of course, the pace at which we would like it to come, it's slightly getting delayed, but it's not going away.

items.statement: RPT approvals: INR1,300 crore for US data center order (timeline Q2-Q3 FY27), INR3,000 crore project on hold by customer and expiring at September AGM
items.quote: Yes. But out of that INR3,000 crores is going to expire by this AGM. So then it will be only INR1,300 crores, which will be left.

items.statement: Management evaluating options for INR16 billion surplus cash beyond announced INR10 billion capex and INR2.5 billion dividend
items.quote: So we have roughly another INR16 billion of surplus cash over and above the announced plan. So as I said in the beginning, management and the Board continuously evaluates what are the options available for the company for maximizing the returns to the shareholders.

items.statement: HV business ramp-up contributing to revenue growth but with lower gross margin; effect largely offset at EBITDA level due to operating leverage
items.quote: About 2 to 2.5 percentage points reduction is on account of ramping up of revenues for a part of our HV business, which has lower gross margin compared to the rest of the business, but overall beneficial at the EBITDA level due to better operating leverage.

items.statement: Elevated commodity prices (CRGO steel, copper) reducing execution savings versus plan; disciplined costing policy maintained for new tenders
items.quote: And the third reason I mentio ned is the elevated commodity prices resulting into the lower execution savings tha n we anticipated compared to our initial plan

items.statement: Company maintains zero debt position with negligible finance costs
items.quote: Profit before tax for the quarter was INR4.9 billion, up from INR3.9 billion in the Q1 FY 26 with finance costs remaining negligible, and with continuous zero debt position.

items.statement: Data center orders currently not significant in order book; larger capacities at higher voltages on drawing board but timing uncertain
items.quote: in the present order intake, the data center ordering is not significant, I would say, that it's a few product orders which are there in the data center. Of course, what we are seeing is that now on the drawing board, we are seeing much larger data center capacities being planned, which will be at higher

items.statement: Export share in total order backlog estimated at 10-15% range
items.quote: So the export in the total orders in hand or backlog should be about 10%-15% range.

items.statement: No concrete capex plans beyond announced INR10 billion; surplus cash deployed in cash pool and fixed deposits while evaluating options
items.quote: As of now, there are different options under evaluation but nothing is concrete. And as per the requirement also, we need to inform the stock exchange in case of such decision. So it is difficult to call out a number in this call because nothing is firmed up as of now.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20%, tracking towards upper band of margin guidance
items.quote: As we said, we continue to maintain our revenue guidance of 15% and the upper side of the 18% to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 175 bps YoY to 21.2% driven by operating leverage, product mix, efficiency and scale
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 stood at INR56 crores as compared to INR44.1 crores in last year corresponding quarter, growth of 27%. With EBITDA margin expanding by 175 basis points to 21.2% from last year 19.4%.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR80-90 crores with INR40-50 crores for quartz sinks expansion, INR20 crores for stainless steel, INR20 crores for faucets and appliances
items.quote: So we are doing approximately INR80 to INR90 crores capex in the current financial year. Where about 40 to 50 crores is going for the expansion of the granite sinks. 20 crores is approximately stainless steel.

items.statement: Strongest ever export order booking position with new SKUs added with Lowe's, Home Depot and Amazon; factory running at full capacity with 7-day weeks
items.quote: We have been able to break through wit h adding a lot of SKUs with Lowe's, Home Depot, and with Amazon. So I think we are probably sitting on the highest ever export order booking right

items.statement: Domestic sales grew 39.8% YoY to INR56 crores in Q1 FY27 driven by 25% volume growth and 12% price realization growth; all four categories grew 28-60%
items.quote: India is increasingly becoming a key growth engine with domestic sales at around INR56 crores, up to almost 40% Y-o-Y, driven by 25% volume growth and 12% average price realization growth.

items.statement: Extended partnership with Home Depot US and Canada, collaborative agreement with Hafele Australia and New Zealand, first orders into Amazon USA; new UK customers Bodel, Barwick, JJO for project segment
items.quote: We would also like to announce that we have extended our partnership with Home Depot US and Canada. We have also entered into a collaborative agreement with Hafele Australia and New Zealand one of the biggest chain retail in Australia.

items.statement: Premium product mix driving margin improvement with full line of premium stainless steel and granite sinks; 90% discount rollback completed in US market
items.quote: We have launched a full line of premium products in stainless steel and in the granite. So, there's a big product mix change and that has led to the higher margins.

items.statement: ASP increased due to operating leverage, discount rollback in US, and premium product mix; no material supply challenges
items.quote: See, one thing is very clear that we have definitely got a big operating leverage, that that's one, Second is that the rollback of the discounts in the United States has also come back.

items.statement: Quartz sink volume grew 6% YoY to 2.01 lakh units; Stainless steel sink volume grew 16% to 49.4 thousand units; Faucet volume grew 43% to 12.5 thousand units
items.quote: Quartz sink volume in Q1 FY27 increased by 6% Y-o-Y basis to 2.01 lakh units compared to 1.89 lakh units in Q1 FY26. Stainless steel sink volume increased by 16% to 49.4 thousand units compared to 42.5 thousand units in last year.

items.statement: Acquired UK tap company primarily for RO water system technology; technology launched in India with 60-day backlog; export faucet manufacturing not yet started
items.quote: We acquired this company primarily to get the technology of the RO water system. And that RO water system is launched in India has been tremendous, been successful.

items.statement: Planning 40-50 galleries, 11 brand stores, 34 committed in Q2, 180 stores in next two years; Carysil Blue brand stores targeting 10 by end of calendar year or March 2027
items.quote: We are increasing our reach by opening 40 to 50 galleries, 11 brand stores, 34 are committed in quarter 2, 180 stores coming in the next two years' time.

items.statement: Logistics disruptions causing container delays impacted Q1 quartz sink dispatches; UK market in tight phase but new customer wins expected to improve momentum
items.quote: There is a lot of disruption happening in the logistics side. So while we had a very strong order booking and I think we did well, we could not dispatch a lot of things because of the delay in containers.

items.statement: New CFO Milind Wadekar joined with 30+ years finance experience, 20+ in hospitality including Leela Group, Chalet Hotels, Ventive Hospitality
items.quote: I would like to welcome our new Chief Finance Officer – Mr. Milind Wadekar, who has joined us this quarter. He has extensive experience of more than 30 years in finance and in that particularly 20 plus years in the hospitality field, right from the Leela Group to the Chalet Hotels where he was the CFO and last he was EVP Finance and Investment Relations at Ventive Hospitality.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew over 10% to Rs. 91 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, consolidated revenue grew over 10% to Rs. 91 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA rose 36% to Rs. 25 crores, margins expanded to 27% from 22% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Driven by again efficiency and I must appreciate our team for their pricing discipline and their operational efficiency, which translated into a phenomenal improvement in our EBITDA rising to 36% high, Rs. 25 crores from the previous quarter in the same year. So, our EBITDA margins have also expanded towards 27% compared to earlier year's same Q1, 22%.

items.statement: Target is net zero debt; consolidated debt Rs. 105 crores, cash Rs. 65 crores, net debt Rs. 38 crores
items.quote: Our target which was and is to be absolutely zero and we are on the target to make net zero and eventually zero on our balance sheet towards that.

items.statement: Orchid Dwarka (63 rooms) to open by December 2024; Gwalior by Diwali 2024; Dehradun delayed 6 months; Nashik before Kumbh; Rishikesh expansion and Mandvi on track
items.quote: We also have expansion which we have signed for our second property in Dwarka. This is the Orchid Dwarka is a 63-room hotel, and which should be starting operations by latest December this year. So, I think that will further strengthen our presence both in the pilgrimage market and in the overall Gujarat market. Previously we also guided that our hotels are there coming up in Gwalior, Dehradun, Na

items.statement: Planning ~400 keys addition over next 12-15 months across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh, Mandvi Kutch
items.quote: So, we are looking at around 400 keys addition, maybe next one year or 15 months from now. That is Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi Kutch. Okay. So, I am saying 12 to 15 months from now. Assuming there will be some delays. It could be earlier also.

items.statement: Domestic tourism CAGR 10-12% over next 3-4 years; Tier-2/3 cities driving 60%+ new branded supply; domestic travel boosted by restricted outbound travel
items.quote: According to industry estimates, India's domestic tourism is expected to grow, with a CAGR of around 10-12% over the next 3-4 years, supported by growth in business travel. And Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are emerging as key growth drivers where we are expanding, contributing to over 60% of new branded hotel supply in the coming years.

items.statement: RevPAR for Orchid and Lotus brands grew 18% and 17% YoY in Q1 FY27; same-store revenue up 17%, EBITDA up 21% YoY
items.quote: Now, if you look at RevPAR at portfolio level, RevPAR for our two brands that is Orchid and Lotus grew 18% and 17% respectively in Q1 FY27. This is high teen RevPAR growth which is much higher than hospitality industry which they have shown in the current quarter.

items.statement: Flow-through (incremental EBITDA/incremental revenue) >75% in Q1 FY27 despite 4 new properties scaling up
items.quote: If you look at flow through for the quarter, what is flow through is incremental EBITDA as a percentage of incremental revenue. It was more than 75% despite four new properties added in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Internal target to reach 30% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years on higher revenue base
items.quote: Pranav, this is long-term. I mean, our target is to take EBITDA margins up to 30% and it comes from both. I mean, higher revenue as well as cost. So, we are looking at various options to control or to rationalize our costs. One of it is moving to renewable energy for some of the properties. So, this is a continuous process and I think this is not one of EBITDA margins. This will remain stable or i

items.statement: Cost rationalization includes moving to renewable energy for some properties
items.quote: One of it is moving to renewable energy for some of the properties. So, this is a continuous process and I think this is not one of EBITDA margins. This will remain stable or improve further.

items.statement: Direct booking traction improving on brand.com (orchidhotel.com, irahotels.com) and loyalty program
items.quote: Our brand.com which is orchidhotel.com and irahotels.com basically have been improving in its direct booking tractions due to various benefits being given additionally to our customers. So, that also has been showing very good traction in general.

items.statement: PAT grew 126% to Rs. 9.7 crores from Rs. 4.3 crores YoY
items.quote: This combined with strong operating KPIs and stringent cost control drove a 126% growth impact to INR 9.7 crores against INR 4.3 crores last year.

items.statement: Comfortable leverage; net debt Rs. 38-40 crores; can raise up to Rs. 300 crores debt at 3x forward EBITDA
items.quote: Even if I take three times multiple of my forward EBITDA, we can raise debt comfortably up to INR 300 crore on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Evaluating growth options: mix of asset-light (lease/revenue share) and owned hotels (brownfield refurbishment or land development)
items.quote: So, we will look at combination of both. I mean, asset-light model where we take properties on lease or revenue share. And we look at our own hotels as well. I mean, we may look at some brownfield hotels, which can be refurbished and put into operations immediately. Or we will look at some land parcels in deep market and develop our own hotels. So, we will look at both.

items.statement: Near-term capex limited to normal repair & maintenance; Mumbai/Pune refurbishment plans being finalized, guidance next quarter
items.quote: So, I mean, just to give you guidance, it will be normal repair and maintenance CAPEX for next two years

items.statement: No formal guidance given; expect quarter-on-quarter growth driven by strong tailwinds
items.quote: So, Gunit, we don't want to give any guidance as such. But what we can tell you is the tailwinds or growth drivers are very strong, and we are expected to show growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Outbound travel restrictions from war boosted domestic leisure; trend expected to continue with rising disposable income and connectivity
items.quote: So, yes, one of the reasons was outbound foreign travel was restricted or limited on account of war. But generally, with higher disposable income and improved connectivity, the leisure travel is increasing year-on-year basis. So, I mean, we feel the trend will continue.

items.statement: Business hotels (Mumbai, Pune) driven by corporate travel; leisure hotels (Goa, Rishikesh) driven by weekend/MICE; no leisure in business hotels
items.quote: So, normally, these are two distinct hotels. I mean, business hotels, we don't get leisure business. If you look at our Mumbai or Pune, mostly it is business travel. There is no leisure. And there are identified, I mean, Goa, it is leisure. In Rishikesh, it will be leisure.

items.statement: New properties take 2-3 years to mature and become EBITDA positive; all hotels scaling up, corrective action taken where needed
items.quote: See, any hotel, whether owned or taken on lease, I mean, it normally takes two to three years for them to scale up and stabilize. So, first year of operation, there could be losses at EBITDA level, but you have to look at long-term trade. And our hotels are scaling up, all hotels are scaling up and wherever we see any loss at operating level, we take corrective action there and there and try to co

items.statement: No hotels opened before FY26 are loss-making after lease charges; new hotels (Bhavnagar, etc.) in first-year investment phase
items.quote: No, no, not really, not really. I mean, all are making profit after lease charges.

items.statement: Dynamic pricing strategy: drive both ARR and occupancy based on micro-market demand; Mumbai at 91% occupancy, RevPAR up ~40%
items.quote: Ideally, hotel performance should be judged by REVPAR, that is revenue per available room. So, I mean, where we think there will be resistance to further improvement in ARR, we go through occupancy route. Now, as I already covered in my opening remarks, my Mumbai property occupancy went up to 91% and RevPAR went up to almost 40%.

items.statement: Occupancy trajectory: Q1/Q2 soft, Q3/Q4 strong; business hotels target 75-80%+ occupancy; leisure seasonal by micro-market
items.quote: See, typically, hospitality industry, Q1 and Q2 are soft, and business picks up. It is business travel as well as leisure in second half of the year, right? So, Q1 occupancy growth has shown good trend, and we expect this trend to continue for the remaining three quarters. Typically, business hotels cross more than 75-80% occupancy. Leisure properties are seasonal, depending on the micro market, o

items.statement: Growth-driven capital deployment; surplus cash to fund managed/owned property expansion, not deleveraging or shareholder returns
items.quote: So, this is growth-driven company and we would like to grow, right? And we will judiciously deploy this capital for growth, whether it is managed properties or our own property. So, we look at growth options.

items.statement: Expects full-year FY27 operating margin in range of 10% to 11%
items.quote: For the whole year, this will be dependent on the raw material prices, of course, but we are trying to maximize it. It may not be to the extent of what we have seen in the last financial year FY26 because of this first quarter. But yes, in the range of about 10% to 11%, if I have to make a guess.

items.statement: Expects overall double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: We are therefore expecting good double -digit growth on the back of the price increase s and the demand led increased volume, everything put together.

items.statement: Expects net debt to increase by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27
items.quote: So broadly, we are expecting an increase of Rs.500-700 crores overall in this financial year.

items.statement: Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin at 6.8% vs 10.9% in Q1FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins (Consolidated) in Q1 were recorded at 6.8% v/s 10.9% in Q1FY26.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve progressively from Q2 and return to normal 11-13% range in H2 FY27
items.quote: And once these costs are stabilized, we will be able to see a good margin improvement from at least 2nd half of this financial year . So, we are expecting all the 3 quarters now onwards should be on a progressive basis, improving in terms of margins.

items.statement: Took ~5% price increase in Q1FY27; expects further 8-9% hikes going forward
items.quote: In the first quarter, we took price increase of nearly about 5%. And going forward , we are expecting to take price increases in the range of about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Cumulative replacement market price hikes of ~11% taken till date
items.quote: Yes, and till now, we have already taken about 11% cumulative in replacement market.

items.statement: Average raw material costs up ~20% sequentially in Q1FY27 due to West Asia crisis
items.quote: Average raw material costs in Q1 were up by ~20% on sequential basis.

items.statement: Natural rubber prices softening; expected to move in range-bound manner
items.quote: Natural rubber prices, we have seen some softening happening. And we see that probably going forward it will move in range-bound manner only.

items.statement: Expects RM cost increase of 8-10% in Q2 due to high-cost inventory
items.quote: And we are hoping that these raw material prices stabilize barring some increase of between 8 - 10% in our RM cost in next quarter as we have been noticing because of the higher cost inventory which we have accumulated.

items.statement: Domestic sales volumes grew 25% YoY in Q1FY27 across replacement and OE
items.quote: Our domestic volumes which includes replacement and OEM, grew by 25% on a year-on-year basis from the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: OEM volumes grew 42% YoY in Q1FY27
items.quote: And just to add, the OEM volumes growth was 42% on YoY basis .

items.statement: Sequential domestic volume growth in mid-single digits
items.quote: Sequential growth was roughly in mid-single digits.

items.statement: Total price increases of 4-4.5% taken since start of war; 3% flowed through Q1, remainder visible in Q2.

items.quote: Rural demand stayed relatively resilient, while urban markets after showing signs of recovery in the second half of FY26 remained subdued during the quarter.

items.statement: Margin recovery expected to be progressive and closely linked to top line growth; benefit from lower crude-linked inputs likely visible only gradually and more meaningfully from October if commodity prices remain stable.
items.quote: Any benefit from lower crude -linked inputs is likely to be visible only gradually and more meaningfully from October, provided commodity prices remain stable. Margin recovery is therefore expected to be progressive and closely linked to top line growth.

items.quote: Having said that, we understand that the heavy dependence on crude -linked material is a risk. And accordingly, we have been working on it for the last 1, 1.5 years. There is a lot of work which is happening in diversification and reducing the dependence on crude-linked raw material.

items.statement: Exo Liquid launched 3-4 months ago, ramping up as per expectations; Maxo incense sticks launched in July, priced at par with competition.

items.statement: Endeavor to deliver double-digit revenue growth from current quarter itself; high single-digit volume growth expected through the year.
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to deliver double -digit revenue growth from current quarter itself. This is what we are aiming for. But of course, 3%, 4% price increase will be sitting over there. So high single digit is the volume growth that we are expecting throug h the year

items.statement: Pharma business development resources already on ground in Europe and Japan; senior level hires to support diversification beyond agchem

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 13% for FY27 with 15% volume growth assumption

items.quote: This quarter, we have reported close to INR300-plus crores of export revenue. Some part of it is contributed by the previous quarter's export quantities.

items.quote: EBITDA grew by 27% year-on-year with margins at 10%, representing a commendable performance in the context of multiple industry headwinds.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased by ~INR3 in Q1 due to export pricing premium from freight/raw material uncertainty

items.quote: Now once the war and the Hormuz situation is clear, then we expect the prices to slowly gradually come down. It may not happen overnight, but it will take 3 to 6 months of time for price to gradually come down to the earlier levels.

items.statement: Bhiwadi capacity to serve existing customers expanding in North (e.g., KEI at Sanand), no new approvals needed

items.quote: Despite geopolitical disruptions in recent years with many wars, our exports has still grown at a CAGR of 16% between FY22 and FY26.

items.statement: India power generation capacity to double from 442 GW to 900 GW by FY32 with INR9 trillion transmission investment

items.quote: we've been able to pass on about 30-40% of the increase in cost to most of our customers who have been very cooperative in absorbing the increase during the last quarter.

items.statement: Company has a strong order book supporting expected utilization improvement

items.quote: Close to 50% of our deals, which is 26 out of 52, the number of deals that we are tracking in the pipeline are more than a single product.

items.quote: Our CAPEX cycle this year is much lower than last year. However, we still require these working capital funds.

items.statement: ESOP expense Rs. 6 million in Q1 FY27; full year guidance revised to Rs. 10-12 crore from earlier Rs. 12 crore due to senior hiring delays
items.quote: ESOP expenses may be a little lesser number than our earlier guidance. However, we are still figuring out because there are some delays. If you look at the quarter expense, it has only been 6 million. Earlier we gave the guidance of around Rs. 12 crores. It may range anywhere between Rs. 10-12 crores is what we anticipate.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin 9.1% in Q1 FY27 (up from ~7.5% steady state); targets steady state operating EBITDA margin of 16-17% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Firstly, those are reported EBITDA. I think our operational EBITDA would be somewhere around 9% for this quarter. But we have always guided that last year we were at about 7.5% as a percentage terms. We should aspire for the same number this year given the huge volatility in all of the things.

items.statement: Store payback period ~10-11 months for recent mini-stores; 2-3 months longer than mega-stores; catchment area revenue grows 2.7-3x after store opening
items.quote: Given that context, the payback period is now somewhere around 10- 11 months, from what we saw. Bu t it's still very early because mini-stores itself, the ramp-up has happened now. It is definitely longer than the original mega-stores, when we had the advantage of selling both mattresses and furniture. It is about 2-3 months longer than that

items.statement: Raw material supply disruption risk from Middle East conflict; prices volatile with shortages; monitoring weekly
items.quote: However, immediately after that, the flare-up happened again with more attacks, etc. And again, Strait of Hormuz being closed, opened, etc. More importantly, with all of these, the shortage itself happened in the industry. So, the raw material suppliers finally said, even if you pay a higher price, there is a shortage.

items.statement: Furniture growth expected to return to mid-teens over next two quarters; step-jump of 25-30% when Jumbo stores open (target June-Sept 2025 for first two stores in Bangalore)
items.quote: So, we should get back to mid-teens to late-teens furniture category growth over the next two quarters steadily. But it will not probably go to 30% that was there last year because of these two conscious reasons. But it will see a step-jump of more than 25%-30% when we open up the jumbo stores.

items.statement: A&P spend guidance 7-8% of revenue for FY27 including festive season
items.quote: Yes, please because the festive season will also come up now so in that range, it should be this.

items.statement: No further price hikes planned barring unforeseen raw material increases
items.quote: Barring any unforeseen increases, we will not be touching the prices as of now.

items.statement: Retail revenue grew 20.5% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As a result of our continuous expansion efforts, retail revenue during the quarter grew 20.5% YoY.

items.statement: Corporate overhead at 7-8% of revenue; expected to remain in same range at steady state, potentially lower as Jumbo stores scale
items.quote: to last year. But overall, percentage wise, we should always remain in the same range at steady state. In fact, as growth of the Jumbo stores and others come up, it might be even lower as a percentage. It might go down from the current 7% to 8

items.statement: Management expects to sustain EBITDA per ton of approximately INR75,000 for FY27, depending on product mix, exports, and currency.
items.quote: We therefore believe that we should be able to sustain approximately INR75,000 per ton for FY27, though the actual performance will depend on the product mix, exports, and currency.

items.statement: Management targets export revenue to return to historical peak of around 40% of total revenue over time.
items.quote: And what we have said is over time, so not specifically in this period of this year, the target is to increase it back to its historical peak of around 40% of total revenue.

items.statement: Management aims to reduce net working capital days to 30-35 days, in line with industry standards.
items.quote: But we feel that 30, 35 days is something that is fairly achievable, and that is what our aim in the going forward will be to do better than that also if possible.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion at Supa has an overall project cost of INR150-160 crores, largely funded by IPO proceeds, with significant spend remaining in FY27.
items.quote: See the overall project cost for phase two like we had mentioned, part funded through the IPO funds, was around INR150 crores to INR160 crores.

items.statement: Installed capacity was 43,445 metric tons at June 30, 2026; Phase 2 expansion to ~59,000 metric tons on track for completion by March 2027, with next wave in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Once phase two of our Super expansion is complete by the end of this year, this financial year, we would have an installed capacity of roughly 59,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Board authorized evaluation of acquiring additional 10 acres in Supa MIDC for long-term expansion needs.
items.quote: Our board last night authorized management to evaluate acquiring an additional 10 acres of land within Supa MIDC for its long-term expansion requirements.

items.statement: Consolidated utilization improved to 73.5% in Q1 FY27 from 70% in Q4 FY26 on unchanged capacity of 43,445 metric tons.
items.quote: With capacity unchanged, consolidated company utilization improved to about 73.5% in Q1, up from 70% in Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Signed five-year supply framework agreement with Hitachi Energy Global for winding wires to Indian and global plants; details being finalized.
items.quote: We are very pleased to announce that we have entered into a five-year supply framework agreement with Hitachi Energy Global to supply winding wires to their Indian plants as well as their some of their global plants.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 76% YoY and 12% QoQ in Q1 FY27, driven by wallet share gains and new OEM customers across all key geographies.
items.quote: Looking at our export performance in Q1 of FY27, our export revenue increased 76% year-over-year and 12% higher than Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Sales volume reached nearly 8,000 metric tons in Q1 FY27, up 30% YoY and 5% QoQ; specialized wire volume significantly outpaced standard wire growth.
items.quote: Overall, sales volume was a little under 8,000 metric tons in Q1, up from roughly 7,600 metric tons in Q4 and 6,100 metric tons a year ago.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month volume growth was 26%; management expects to sustain this rate for full FY27 as Phase 1 capacity available for full year.
items.quote: First, for the trailing 12 months, volume growth was 26%. The higher phase one capacity will be available for the full year FY27 as opposed to only for a part of FY26, and therefore, we feel that we should be able to sustain this rate of volume growth for the full year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton was ~INR93,000, up from INR74,000 in Q4 FY26 and INR66,000 YoY, driven by record CTC mix, higher exports, favorable new customer pricing, higher utilization, and weaker rupee.
items.quote: In Q1 of FY27, we reported EBITDA per ton of approximately INR93,000 per metric ton, up from roughly INR74,000 in Q4 and INR66,000 a year ago.

items.statement: Standard wire EBITDA per ton improved marginally as utilization increased; higher kV class (765 kV/HVDC) CTC volume trended above 25% of CTC volume.
items.quote: As the round wire or standard winding wire capacity utilization has gone up, the EBITDA per metric ton of standard also has improved marginally from earlier quarters.

items.statement: CTC contribution to total revenue reached record levels in Q1 FY27; CTC represents 50-75% of specialized wire segment; higher kV classes ~25% of CTC volume.
items.quote: In fact, in Q1, CTC's contribution to the total revenue reached record levels in the last several years.

items.statement: Peak insulated wire capacity for EV traction motors is under installation as part of Phase 2; not yet operational.
items.quote: Yes, it's still under installation. That whole I mean, we've still not installed the capacity, and we will report it when we've installed that capacity and made it operationalized that capacity.

items.statement: Added new standard wire clients in EVs, AC compressors, motors, alternators for DG sets; new OEM customers onboarded at market-driven value addition rates higher than long-term customers.
items.quote: Some of the new OEM customers have been more favorable and market-driven value addition rates compared to our established long-term customers on a like-for-like basis.

items.statement: Average working capital days improved to 60 days in Q1 FY27 from 65 days in Q4 FY26 and 71 days YoY; payables improved 5 days, receivables 2 days, inventory flat.
items.quote: Working capital days calculated on an average balance basis improved to 60 days from 65 days in Q4 and 71 days in Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Interest cost increased to ~INR17 crores in Q1 FY27 due to higher working capital borrowings from increased turnover; effective borrowing cost ranges 6-9.5% depending on product mix.
items.quote: The overall interest expense is higher because the working capital finance is higher.

items.statement: Commissioned upcast backward integration facility at Chakan (5,000 MT capacity) to recycle own copper scrap; modest operating efficiency and sustainability benefit expected.
items.quote: Last week, we completed yet another one of our IPO objectives on time by commissioning our upcast backward integration facility in Chakan. This facility will have a capacity of 5,000 metric tons and be used to recycle our own copper scrap.

items.statement: Copper price and exchange rate are direct pass-through via make-to-order model; value addition contracts with 80-85% of customers set annually; no inventory gain/loss on copper.
items.quote: Thus, LME copper price and exchange rate is a direct pass-through.

items.statement: Realization per ton ~INR14 lakh includes copper value; gross profit level better reflects value addition as copper fluctuates with LME ($10,000-$14,000/MT) and FX.
items.quote: The realization is, if I understand correctly, you are dividing the revenue per metric ton. And revenue per metric ton, a large, large part of the revenue is the copper part, which fluctuates based on the LME and the exchange rate.

items.statement: Some transformer OEMs delayed order pickups by weeks due to capacity expansion bottlenecks; expected to normalize as new facilities become operational.
items.quote: We have seen a few of the transformer OEM customers who are in active capacity expansion mode, delay picking up their orders by a few weeks.

items.statement: BIS implementation driving localization of standard winding wire supply base from imports to Indian companies.
items.quote: And there are some other factors also like BIS which is being implemented. So there's a lot of localization of the winding wire that's happening, which was earlier being imported from -- imported into the country, but now because of BIS, the standard wires are necessarily being -- the supply base is shifting to Indian companies.

items.statement: Export revenue 27% of operating revenue in Q1 FY27; Middle East, Europe, US each 8-11% of total revenue annually; weaker rupee benefits EBITDA per ton.
items.quote: So on that basis, I think it was 27%, around 27%. Yes, this quarter it was 27%.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned; focus on utilizing and expanding capacity with existing team.
items.quote: I would now like to ask Amod, our CFO, to go over some of the financial and operational details. Over to you, Amod.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR1,164 crores (+108% YoY); EBITDA INR74.4 crores; PAT INR42.2 crores (+86% YoY, +22% QoQ).
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, our revenue from operations was INR1,164 crores, which is 108% higher compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27
items.quote: For FY27, we reiterate our double-digit revenue growth guidance.

items.statement: DG set order book at INR1,700 crores as of 31st July 2026, including INR900 crores data center orders
items.quote: Within our DG set business powered by Cummins, the order book as of 31st July 2026 stood at INR1,700 crores, providing strong visibility for future growth. Out of this, data center -specific orders within this business stood at INR900 crores.

items.statement: Data center order book increased to INR1,100 crores by August 7th from INR900 crores on July 31st
items.quote: as on July 31st, the data center order book stood at INR900, but literally just in the past week, that order book now, like if you would take August 7th as the timestamp, that number would be 1,100.

items.statement: Order book grew 15% to 19% year-on-year as of July 31st
items.quote: We can share those datas as well, but we can consider a 15% to 19% increase in the order book vis-a-vis same quarter last year, as of July 31st itself, depending on the product mix.

items.statement: Genset EBITDA margin impacted in Q1 and part of Q2 due to West Asia crisis, expected to improve from Q3 onward
items.quote: Mohit, as we mentioned in our earlier call as well that due to West Asia crisis, this will be -- the margin will be impacted for Q1 and part of the Q2. So, so this is the period that where the margin will be subdued, but we believe that from Q3 onward, it is going to improve.

items.statement: Took two-phase price hike in Q1 and start of Q2 to pass on commodity cost increases
items.quote: we took a two-phase approach. We based on the market conditions and, you kno w, acceptance, feedback from our sales team, etc., we took a small price increase in the middle of Q1, and the balance in the start of Q2

items.statement: Price hikes mapped to genset level and passed on gradually to customers
items.quote: Yes. We map all price increases to the genset level and then subsequently pass it on to the customers gradually.

items.statement: Data center is fastest-growing segment; manufacturing remains top market segment followed by real estate; rental is second fastest growing
items.quote: Yes. So, data center, of course, is our fastest-growing segment, but manufacturing still continues to be our top market segment in terms of percentage, and that's followed by real estate. The second fastest growing is the rental segment.

items.statement: DG set capacity utilization at 75% to 80% on single shift; no immediate expansion needed
items.quote: It's capacity utilization is about between 75% to 80%.

items.statement: Wind IPP portfolio to grow from 330 MW to 633.55 MW (corrected to 638.35 MW); 50 MW in FY27, 150 MW in FY28, 100 MW in FY29
items.quote: Including above projects, we have clear visibility to take our IPP portfolio to 634 megawatt, or to be more precise, it is 633.55 megawatt. (Wrongly said on call. The correct number is 638.35 megawatt)

items.quote: So you can say approximately the top line would be around INR400 crores of the this EPC business.

items.statement: Data center orders received directly from operators, not through Cummins
items.quote: So, the complete customer engagement scope is with Powerica, so we interact with the data center directly to receive the order.

items.statement: Competition increasing in data center space but confident in execution reputation and trust
items.quote: So, competition continues to increase, right, but we are confident in our product and not just the product, but also the reputation and the trust that Powerica has in the execution of these orders, right.

items.quote: Recently, we have won one tender of INR41 crores, which is to be executed between 12 months to 15 months. The others are in pipeline. As soon as that is been materialized, we will pass on the information to all of you.

So, generally after LoA, it takes 90 days for

items.quote: So, retrofit emission control devices business, it is strong enough, but this time we have we have about 17 crores, 16 crores of a revenue during the quarter, primarily because of one is the crisis, second is on the GRAP implementation, which was there in the Northern Capital.

items.statement: Net cash of INR193 crores; capital allocated to 300 MW wind projects under construction; open to acquisitions
items.quote: So, we already mentioned about the 300 megawatt, which is under construction, including 50 will go live this year and 250 new project that we won. So, one is that the capital will be allocated towards that. Further, the we always open to any of the idea that comes into fore. So as soon as something is been there, definitely we'll look forward to deploy.

items.statement: Acquired 49% stake in Fuji-Kailash Energy Private Limited for solar and bioenergy; incorporated two wholly-owned wind subsidiaries
items.quote: Additionally, we have acquired a 49% stake in Fuji-Kailash Energy Private Limited, a company engaged in the generation and distribution of renewable power across solar and bioenergy solutions. This strategic investment will further strengthen our renewable energy platform and broaden our presence across multiple clean energy technologies.

items.statement: Commodity price inflation weighed on margins with time lag in cost pass-through
items.quote: Commodity price inflation weighed on our margins this quarter as there is typically a certain time lag before we can pass rising input costs through to our customers.

items.statement: Incorporated two wholly-owned subsidiaries (Windfusion Renewable and Whisper wind Renewable) for wind portfolio expansion
items.quote: As part of strengthening our project execution capabilities, we incorporated two wh olly-owned subsidiaries, Windfusion Renewable Private Limited and Whisper wind Renewable Private Limited, by acquiring 100% ownership in both entities

items.statement: Management declines to provide specific FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA margin guidance, stating numbers will go up and they will not let them go down.
items.quote: We are really working hard. We will not let the numbers go down anyway. Numbers will be going up as our first quarter you can see.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 demand was strong across both B2B and B2C, with 78% B2B and 22% B2C mix, driven by bridal season.
items.quote: So, we had around 78% of B2B in this Q1 as I have come to know, 22% we have done B2C and both the demands were connected to bridals.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 33.12% and PAT margin was 23.12%.
items.quote: EBITDA increased 33.02 to INR11.72 crores with a healthy margin of 33.12%, while PAT grew 37.86 to INR8.19 crores with a PAT margin of 23.12%.

items.statement: Flagship store in Jaipur requires approximately INR24-25 crores total investment; company-owned boutique stores outside Jaipur estimated at INR5 crores each excluding inventory.
items.quote: I think approximately we wer e counting around INR24 to INR25 crores invested into that in total

items.statement: Jaipur flagship store (30,000 sq ft) targeting operational by November 2025, with interior work ongoing.
items.quote: Trying to get it done by November, but interior is going on. Let's see what happens. Jaipur is getting good rains. So, the work is getting delayed, but I feel we will be able to get it done by November.

items.statement: Franchise store inventory requirement estimated at INR6-8 crores per store depending on geography and product mix.
items.quote: But approximately, I feel around INR6 crores to INR8 crores is a requirement for a franchise to operate a good franchise store.

items.statement: Gold price locked at order booking with advance; hedging done immediately to protect margins; procurement matched to sold stock.
items.quote: Most of the time, it is order booking and when if we get a good advance from the client, we just immediately hedge the gold so that we don't get any kind of fluctuation in our margins and prices.

items.statement: Expanding beyond bridal into contemporary men's jewellery and lightweight pret jewellery for Gen Z and millennials.
items.quote: We are introducing new collections across emerging categories, including contemporary men's jewellery and lightweight pret jewellery.

items.statement: B2C channels include Jaipur experience center, Instagram (110k followers), LinkedIn, website, and 105-year family brand reputation in Jaipur.
items.quote: We have a we have an experience center in Jaipur. We have our Instagram page. You must have seen the House of Rambhajo . I think 110,000 followers are already there.

items.statement: USP is end-to-end organized manufacturing, trendsetting innovation, 105-year legacy, and fourth-generation expertise in procurement and design.
items.quote: Advit's USP is it's the it's organized to the level where we have end-to-end solutions to every piece we make. We have innovations, we are trendsetters.

items.statement: Prioritizing US as biggest export market, also exploring Middle East and UK; working on exhibitions and private shows for awareness.
items.quote: US is anyway a big market, actually. If we talk about UK yes, it's a good market, but I feel US is a bigger market and we are working on some new shows, we are working on some new partners who can do some exhibitions there.

items.statement: Working capital needs may increase with retail expansion but current capital sufficient for planned expansion; inventory rotation across own stores possible.
items.quote: So, Yes, it is there, because we always work in ready jewellery. Kundan jewellery is always appreciated and being bought when it is ready. So, working capital requirement may increase, but at this moment, we have ample capital to do the current kind of expansion we are looking for.

items.statement: Company is now debt-free after utilizing IPO proceeds to repay loans; balance IPO funds held for working capital and future expansion.
items.quote: So, we have paid our debts. We are totally debt -free now as one of the portion was to be paid for our loans. So, that was paid immediately as we got the funds.

items.statement: IPO proceeds partially deployed: debt repaid, some used for inventory, balance held for strategic expansion based on market demand.
items.quote: We have not invested the whole amount yet. We are just seeing the movement and the needs of the market and for our further expansion. So, the balance funds, we are still holding the bunch of it.

items.statement: Artisan base increased in Q1 with new skilled artisans joining; focusing on training artisans' daughters to build generational ecosystem.
items.quote: I think so it has increased because few very nice new artisans have come. Like one of them, I know well because here I was just thinking him to join us.

items.statement: Average ticket size maintained despite gold price rise by reducing gold weight and increasing stone/Polki content to fit customer budgets.
items.quote: We are trying to make lighter weight gold jewellery . We are trying to get more stones and Polkies and all to make it more grander and more impressive, and more attractive with lesser gold weights.

items.statement: Franchise model protocols not yet finalized; delaying franchise invitations until strong protocols established for Polki jewellery specifics.
items.quote: We are really working hard, I think by a month, we will be ready with our franchise models. What because at this moment, we are not even inviting franchises till the time we are not ready with the strong protocols on that.

items.statement: Brand ambassador planned to be unveiled at Jaipur flagship store inauguration.
items.quote: There is a plan but we want to come up with that with our new store. I want this new store, that flagship store of Jaipur, the day it will be inaugurated, you will be seeing a face joining us.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow at 15-16% CAGR consistent with last 5 years; EBITDA margins to remain stable
items.quote: We expect this growth to continue in that same manner.

items.statement: Order book at INR27,884 million as of June 2026 comprising INR14,327 million manufacturing and INR13,557 million EPC orders
items.quote: Our order book stood at approximately INR27,884 million as of June '26. This comprises of INR14,327 million of manufacturing order and INR13,557 million of EPC order.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.6% in Q1 FY27 from 11.5% in Q1 FY26; management expects margins to remain stable with new products supporting improved realizations
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 12.6% from 11.5% in Quarter 1 of FY26.

items.statement: Installed capacity of 85,000 metric tons across three units; focus on improving utilization and productivity; future capex phased based on demand; land available for expansion
items.quote: Having expanded installed capacity meaningfully over last 3 years, our immediate focus is on improving utilization, increasing the productivity of our existing assets, and growing the contribution from higher value-added products.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity utilization at 62% overall; cable utilization ~80%; can reach 90-95% utilization; capacity expanded from 62,000 to 85,400 metric tons over 3 years
items.quote: so I can what we are reporting is actually the when we say 85,000 metric ton capacity we have, it is actually a optimized one only. So, we are not, so we can go up to utilization of 90%, 95% of the capacity

items.statement: High-voltage cable share increased from 9% to 29% of revenue over last 9 quarters; manufacturing split 90% cables, 10% conductors; HTLS/advanced conductors expected to increase technology content and margins
items.quote: In last nine quarters, we have increased our high-voltage cable sales from 9% of our total revenue to almost 29% of our total revenue in last nine quarters.

items.statement: India conductor market grew from INR102B in FY20 to INR185B in FY25, expected to reach INR230-250B by FY30; HTLS tender pipeline ~INR3,500 crores over last year; company bid INR1,250 crores
items.quote: According to CRISIL's Intelligence, India's conductor market increased from approximately 102 billion in FY20 to approximately 185 billion in FY25, and this is expected to reach 230 to 250 billion by FY30.

items.statement: INR4,900 million IPO proceeds used for debt repayment; gross debt now ~INR3,600 million; net debt negligible after INR2,400 million fixed deposits; finance cost expected to decline progressively
items.quote: Approximately INR4,900 million of IPO proceed was utilized towards the repayment of loan outstanding. Gross debt currently stand at approximately INR3,600 million.

items.statement: Working capital days typically 100-120 days; Q1 spike due to EPC project mobilization and FG/WIP inventory increase of INR90 crores; expected to moderate as projects progress
items.quote: Our working capital typically range between 110 to 120 days, 100 to 120 days, actually. And there could be some spike in a particular reporting date because of various reason, the EPC project at what stage it is.

items.statement: HT cables carry 2-3% higher EBITDA margin vs conventional cables; HTLS/advanced conductors expected to fetch higher margins; conventional conductors lowest margin in portfolio
items.quote: So, it's roughly like 2%, 3% of margin difference between the normal cable and HT cables at EBITDA level.

items.statement: EPC revenue 100% from government utilities; manufacturing revenue split 50-50 between government and private sector; strategy to maintain this mix
items.quote: In manufacturing side, usually it's 50-50, between government and private sector, and that's how we will continue.

items.statement: TS Conductors AECC technology patented; company first Indian partner; participated in INR1,250 crores tenders; other players use CTC Global tech; some tenders have multiple bidders
items.quote: In some of the tenders, there are multiple bidders. In some of the tenders, there may be lower number of bidders, but single bids would not be something that I would really stress upon.

items.statement: EPC EBITDA margins typically 15-20% but vary by project stage and milestone timing; not representative of steady run-rate
items.quote: EPC margin roughly stands between somewhere 15% to 20%, but EPC margin can't be look at a particular quarter or at a particular moment, because that will depend on a single project milestone.

items.statement: IPO completed July 2026; INR4,900 million proceeds used for debt repayment; strengthened balance sheet for larger orders and projects
items.quote: The completion of our IPO has strengthened the foundation of our next phase of growth. A substantial portion of the fresh issue proceeds was allocated towards reduction of our borrowings.

items.statement: Government plans to increase power generation capacity from 500GW to 900GW in 5-7 years; right-of-way constraints driving re-conductoring demand; railway electrification and renewable evacuation supporting growth
items.quote: If you look at our country, the kind of power generation requirement that has come up, we are planning to increase our power generation capacity from almost 500 gigawatt to 900 gigawatt in next 5 or 7 years.

items.statement: Carbon fiber composite core for AECC conductors imported from TS Conductors in US; aluminum encapsulation used instead of glass for easier installation; other raw materials sourced from primary producers
items.quote: The technology provider is a US-based company called TS Conductors, and that is the company which manufactures the carbon core, and it is a patented technology, and they produce this carbon core from U.S. and export it to India.

items.statement: Finance cost absorbed 55% of Q1 EBITDA; working capital spikes during early EPC project stages; EPC margin variability; PAT comparison affected by one-time INR32 crore gain in prior year
items.quote: Finance cost absorbed approximately 55% of quarterly EBITDA and remained a principal factor moderating the conversion of operating profitability into PAT.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target 45-50% YoY on INR9,125 cr order book
items.quote: And we will be doing a revenue growth of about 45% to 50% Y -o-Y. This is driven by full -year execution of orders which we have won recently.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA growth target 35%+ YoY subject to fuel cost normalization
items.quote: Apart from that, we are targeting to have an EBITDA growth of 35% plus year -on-year subject to fuel cost spikes which we are expecting to normalize.

items.statement: FY27 PAT growth target 35%+ YoY reflecting interest cost savings
items.quote: PAT growth we are again expecting to be in the range of 35% plus year-on-year reflecting a margin which will be having because of savings in interest cost as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported EBITDA margin 16.80%, adjusted 20.02% after diesel escalation revenue
items.quote: However, our revenue for the quarter includes a revenue of INR10.57 crores related to diesel escalation which has been given to us by Coal India. So if we report that, our EBITDA margin stands at 20.02% for this quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin 22-25%, Q1 hit due to diesel spike and mine transition costs

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA INR 28 crores at 21% margin; PAT INR 10 crores at 7.4% margin

items.statement: Residential EBITDA margins expected to gradually move up to 30%-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely
items.quote: Given the real estate sector, sell product of residentials and construct, build, and sell, the EBITDA margins would gradually move up around, 30% - 35% once Town Villas and the villa projects contribute largely.

items.statement: Hospitality segment expected to contribute INR 50 crores+ PAT per year from third or fourth year
items.period: third or fourth year from now
items.quote: And it would in terms of value, the hospitality sector would contribute say third or fourth year from now to an average of INR 50 crores of PAT per year. This represents an annuity income model, with both hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crores+.

items.statement: INR 500 crores total investment program for club and hospitality business over three years
items.quote: For three years the company will deploy INR 500 crores of capital, by debt or by internal resources for these projects.

items.statement: Net debt INR 818 crores, net worth INR 460 crores as of 30 June 2026; focused on reducing debt next year onwards

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio expected to gradually come down as projects mature and equity builds up
items.quote: Though the intentions are there, yes, there is a plan for it. The debt-to-equity ratio will gradually come down because once the projects get matured the equity gets on, the reserves and capital reserves get on adding up to every quarter-to-quarter or year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Aspire to maintain 40%-45% premium, 30%-35% middle income, 20% affordable housing mix

items.statement: Collections for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 161 crores, up 28% YoY

items.quote: It's a general behaviour that for an ongoing project, we are into percentage completion method. Hence, all the pre-sales which happen, it takes around 90 days on an average for them to get into the mode of revenue recognition.

items.quote: Going forward for this financial year, we don't have any program for new capital investments for the business development as there is a good handsome size of projects in hand worth INR 14,000 crores and given the scalability possible at our end, it still is in cycle of six to seven years to complete up this INR 14,000 crores.

items.quote: Sector scalability is still increasing overall, which also shows up that implementation is the core key and that is where , there is a shortage of man resources at skill development right from the workers at the labour at the site as well as the monitoring engineering team as well as the sales people and that becomes the key factor.

items.quote: Our GDV (Gross Development Value) has increased from INR 6,000 crore s to INR 14,000 crores in the last five years without any significant fundraise. The only fundraise which we did in the past was INR 36 crores via preferential

items.quote: We are happy to share that ASL is already transacting and emerging as an diversified developer rather than only pure residential. items.quote: I think the next quarter is going to be much bigger than this. But however, the mo st significant part of this June quarter, again, it is the contribution from Geomysore
