items.quote: Our Thriveni Sainik operations retained a 5 -star rating from the Ministry of Coal and the number 1 position among open cast mines in India for the second consecutive year.

items.statement: Thriveni margins impacted by higher fuel costs from Gulf crisis; actively pursuing pass-through to clients
items.quote: Our margins this quarter were marginally impacted by higher fuel costs due to this gulf crisis. We are actively pursuing pass -through of these costs to our clients, and those negotiations are currently underway.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline saves INR550/ton on pellet costing; annualized savings confirmed
items.quote: Rajeshji has mentioned it around INR500 to INR550 per ton on the -- because of the slurry line -- slurry project. That is the saving what we are getting on the pellet costing.

items.statement: Opening iron ore stock of 1.5 million tons to be sold this year; sales expected >26 million tons
items.quote: We had around 1.5 million tons of stock -- opening stock of iron ore, which we would be selling out in this year. So this year, the sales would be more than 26 million with this 1.5 million tons.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR5,616 crores as of June 30; consolidated net debt ~INR19,000 crores including Chemaf acquisition
items.value: INR5,616 crores standalone, INR19,000 crores consolidated
items.quote: Stand -alone net debt as of 30th June stood at INR5,616 crores, very comfortable relative to the EBITDA, and business is now -- the EBITDA, the business is now generating. Let me add one point at the consolidated level. Our consolidated debt -- net debt remains around INR19,000 crores.

items.statement: Chemaf debt restructuring expected next quarter; 40-50% reduction in overall debt anticipated
items.quote: Yes. Once we complete the complete final closure, it depends upon how actually we are refinancing because we are still looking at complete financial closure. So that includes taking some of the debt, which is there. So some of the new debt may replace the older debt, which is there. So yes, but there will be a significant reduction in the overall debt because that debt does include some of the acc

items.statement: Thriveni raising INR650 crores to replace high-cost debt, fund capex and overseas subsidiary investments
items.quote: In fact, we just wanted to reduce our high -cost debt. And at the same time, we are going for capex, capital investment, and we have to invest in our outside subsidiaries also for doing the MDO contract. So for these purposes, as I said in my opening remarks that we are converting a few of our conventional equipment to the electrical equipment. For that, we need funds. We just wanted to replace so

items.statement: DRC copper export ban on concentrate does not impact Chemaf as both assets will produce final cathodes
items.quote: So yes, I mean, DRC government has announced that. But just to give a perspective, actually, DRC has mostly been exporting cathode. There has been very little concentrate which goes out of DRC, and it is limited to mostly some of the players with Chinese s hareholders. So in our case, both the assets will be producing final cathodes. So it does not impact us.

items.statement: NTPC wage receivable ~INR300 crores not provided for; arbitration won, matter subjudice, expecting resolution in 2-3 months
items.quote: No, no. We don't intend to make any provision for that. We are in negotiation with NTPC and the higher authorities, not only for this, but for our escalation on fuel cost and all these things also. So negotiations with NTPC are on. And hopefully, for these wages also, this matter would be sorted out because this is what they had to pay, and they have not yet paid. In arbitration, we had won this a

items.statement: Iron ore production 6.05 million tons (+53% YoY), sales 5.46 million tons (+58% YoY), realization INR6,068/ton
items.quote: Iron ore production for the quarter was 6.05 million tons, up 53% year-on-year, and sales was 5.46 million tons, up 58% year -on-year. Realization stood at INR6,068 per ton with an EBITDA of 2,230 per ton.

items.statement: DRI sales 183,920 tons (+133% YoY) at INR27,376/ton realization, EBITDA INR6,273/ton
items.quote: DRI sales volume stood at 1,83,920 tons, up 133% year-on-year at a realization of INR27,376 per ton and EBITDA of INR6,273 per ton.

items.statement: Thriveni iron ore volumes 19.09 million tons (+93% YoY); coal volumes 26.02 million cubic meters domestic, 5.93 million overseas
items.quote: Iron ore volumes, including BHQ, stood at 19.09 million tons for the quarter, that's nearly doubling from 9.87 million tons in Q1 last year. Coal volumes from Indian operations, including overburden, were 26.02 million cubic meters with overseas operations at 5.93 million cubic meters and baryte at 2.14 million cubic meters.

items.statement: Logistics fleet adding 200 green vehicles (50 LNG, 150 EV) targeting 30-40% cost savings and EBITDA improvement from 32% to 40%
items.quote: At present, we have around 150 electric and LNG vehicles, and we propose to add another 200 vehicles, of which 50 will be LNG and 150 will be EV, to our fleet, aiming to make the fleet of green vehicles. Already 20 charging stations are installed, and in the process -- we are in the process of installing another 30 charging stations. It will give us 30% to 40% cost savings and increase in EBITDA o

items.statement: Geomysore gold mine inaugurated July 2026; delivered 0.17 million tons ROM and 14,000m drilling in first quarter
items.quote: Geomysore, which is India's first privately integrated gold mining and processing operation, this was formally inaugurated in July '26, and it delivered ROM production of 0.17 million tons and drilling of over 14,000 meters in its first quarter.

items.statement: PNG Panguna copper project at early study stage; no investment figures or timelines available yet
items.quote: Like both Siddharth and Hemankur have mentioned, sir, the PNG ABG project is still under study. It's very, very pipeline stage, and it will be very difficult to hazard any guess at the moment.

items.statement: Revised FY27 Lamination volume target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons
items.quote: Therefore, we are revising our annual target to 82,000 tons for Lamination from 78,000 tons, as previously stated in Q4 Conference Call.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target roughly ₹370 crores based on current outlook
items.quote: If I start from current year, I would look at an EBITDA of roughly ₹ 370-odd crores based on current outlook.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target above ₹2,500 crores at 90,000 ton operating level with EBITDA margin 17%-17.2%
items.quote: For the next year, we should be looking at a turnover above about ₹ 2,500 crores if we don't do the Capex. I am obviously going to talk ex of the incremental Capex on Lamination. So, at a 90,000 ton operating level, we should be looking at a ₹ 2,500 crores turnover and an EBITDA margin of about 17%-17.2%.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target 18%-18.5% as Casting and Machining Capex comes online
items.quote: No, for sure it will be upwards of 18% for sure. With the Capex on the Casting and Machining coming online and the value-added products increasing as well as the co-drop products increasing, your margins should be closer to 18%-18.5%.

items.statement: ₹150 crore Capex completed, increasing sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting Casting and Machining
items.quote: We have recently commenced operations of the previously announced ₹ 150 crores Capex, which was announced last year, increasing our sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting our Casting and Machining capacity.

items.statement: ₹290 crore Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad underway, ₹60 crore spent so far, commissioning by Q1 FY30
items.quote: We are now progressing with the ₹ 290 crores investment for our Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad. This facility will help consolidate our foundry operations and provide the infrastructure required for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: ₹290 crore Capex split: 30% infrastructure, 70% plant and equipment; Machining capacity to reach 1,080,000 machine hours
items.quote: Infrastructure investment is about 30% and 70% is going towards plant and equipment. I will not have a year-by-year expenditure plan, but the capacity is expected for commissioning by Q1 FY30 as we had mentioned in the previous call.

items.statement: Potential Bangalore facility ~₹200 crore plus equipment ~₹200 crore could take revenue to ₹3,000-3,300 crore
items.quote: If I were to assume that we go ahead and make a facility in Bangalore, that would entail a Capex of roughly about ₹ 200-odd crores. Then in terms of another equipment, about ₹ 200-odd crores. So, ₹ 400 crores plus the ₹ 290 crores, which we have announced, would be capable of taking us to a top-line of closer to about ₹ 3,000 crores to ₹ 3,300 crores.

items.statement: Sheet metal utilization 73% in Q1 FY27 vs 70% prior; Machining utilization 86% vs 82%; Casting and fabrication 72%
items.quote: We witnessed meaningful improvement across our operations during the quarter. Sheet metal utilization increased to 73% Q1 FY27 compared to 70%. Machining utilization also improved to 86% compared to 82%. Casting and fabrication utilization stood at 72%.

items.statement: Current Lamination capacity 108,000 tons; headroom ~8,000 tons at 80% efficiency; incremental Capex needed for FY28
items.quote: If I look at the capacity side, with this 82,000 tons being the target for current year and 108,000 tons being the capacity, we only have a headroom to grow about 8,000 tons with the current facility, assuming the 80% operating efficiency. definitely, for FY28, there will be some incremental Capex to increase the capacity.

items.statement: Casting capacity increased to 24,000 tons; volume target revised up to 17,000 tons
items.quote: Casting capacity has gone to 24,000 tons. We would be upward guiding the Casting numbers to about 17,000 tons as well.

items.statement: Mining segment revenue share grew from 5% to 10% in Q1; strong order visibility in Mining, Railways, Off-Highway, Special Applications
items.quote: You can see in Quarter 1 already, Mining as a segment has grown substantially for us from 5% of revenue to about 10% of revenue.

items.statement: Broad-based demand across Data Centers, Railways, Mining, Off-Highway, Specialty Industrial; Data Center near-term opportunity strong but measured
items.quote: Speaking of sectoral demand and growth opportunity is broad-based. Our Data Centers have emerged as a strong near-term opportunity given the significant power requirements for both primary and backup power generation.

items.statement: Direct exports steady, indirect exports growing via local operations of global customers; exports to pick up Q2-Q4
items.quote: Exports will again pick up in Q3-Q4. The direct exports are remaining steady, registering nominal growth. What is a bigger opportunity for us is the indirect exports.

items.statement: High value-added Lamination assemblies (Integrated Rotor Shaft, Stator) grew faster than loose Lamination; driven by Data Centers, Mining, Off-Highway, Wind
items.quote: Importantly, within Lamination, Higher Value-Added Assemblies, including Integrated Rotor Shaft and Stator Assemblies, grew faster than loose Lamination. This reflects a continued improvement in the product mix and increasing contribution from value-added offerings.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 tax rate expected ~25% (Q1 lower due to deferred tax on right-of-use assets)
items.quote: No, it will be about 25%, not 33%. This effective tax rate is about 25%. Quarter 1, we have a lot of right of use assets for our lease assets, and that has incurred the deferred tax, and therefore we have a lower tax rate on the P&L for Quarter 1.

items.statement: LPG supply steady; incremental cost passed through to customers; electrification of LPG largely done
items.quote: We are currently doing the electrification. A lot of it is already done. Right now, there is no LPG issue. We have steady supplies of LPG coming in. Whatever is the incremental cost obviously is being incurred by the company, and it is being compensated by the customers as well.

items.statement: Net debt ₹491 crore; potential to rationalize working capital by ₹25-30 crore
items.quote: Right now, the net debt is somewhere around ₹ 491 crores as of last quarter end. We have already incurred, like I said, about ₹ 60 odd crores of expenditure out of the ₹ 290 crores. Despite that, we have been able to meaningfully reduce the net debt, and I think there is still potential to further rationalize our working capital to the tune of about ₹ 25 crores to ₹ 30 crores.

items.statement: Finance cost ₹19.6 crore plus ₹3 crore forex impact from West Asia crisis; interest cost rationalized but forex masks reduction
items.quote: Actually, this quarter if you see, the dollar has moved quite sharply due to the West Asia crisis, and there is a Forex impact of about ₹ 3-odd crores, which is accounted in the finance cost. The interest and bank charges are about ₹ 19.6 crores and the Forex impact is about ₹ 3 crores.

items.statement: State incentive on ₹400 crore Capex (~₹40 crore/year) deferred to maximize cash recovery; decision pending on 9-year plan
items.quote: We are evaluating whether to start claiming the incentive from current year or next year so as to maximize the net cash flow. We are more or less coming to a conclusion that this year we would not be taking the incentive income because we would not be able to recover a large chunk of the money that we can recover next year.

items.statement: Green hydrogen anode/cathode plates for European customer (~EUR 2M); marine propulsion components for electric ships
items.quote: In the green hydrogen space, we make anode and cathode plates for hydrogen electrolyzers for a customer in Europe. These are basically stainless-steel components which are machined and supplied to that customer. It is not a very large business. If I am not mistaken, it is about EUR 2-odd million kind of a business.

items.statement: Data Center growth may not be sustainable indefinitely; Mining and Oil & Gas can correct quickly; cautious on investing ahead of demand
items.quote: If I just look at the outlook and the demand forecast from the customers, we do see that kind of growth over the next three years. But it is coming from segments which, I would say, can change very quickly. So, like Mining and Oil & Gas are segments which go up very fast and can correct very fast. And Data Center is obviously a very new segment, and it is growing very fast. So, it is something we

items.statement: Revenue ₹529 crore (+16% YoY); Adjusted EBITDA ₹89 crore (+14% YoY); Adjusted PAT ₹32 crore
items.quote: from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at ₹ 529 crores compared to ₹ 457 crores in Q1 FY26, a growth of 16% YOY . Adjusted EBITDA stood at ₹ 89 crores compared to ₹ 78 crores for Q1, representing a growth of 14%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.8% for the quarter. Adjusted PAT was ₹ 32 crores compared to ₹ 26 crores in

items.statement: Revenue target for Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions verticals at full capacity
items.quote: the overall revenues we are looking at from the Yarn Solutions vertical and the Fabric Solutions vertical are in the region of INR1,000 crores each at full capacities.

items.statement: Net debt expected to reduce by end of fiscal year
items.quote: So therefore, all in all, we will see a reduction in net debt by the end of fiscal.

items.statement: Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements using existing infrastructure
items.quote: We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.

items.statement: Combined Sheeting and knitting fabric processing capacity to reach 90 million meters by year end
items.quote: The combined capacities of our Sheeting and our knitting fabrics processing capacity is approximately, by the end of the year should stand at about 90 million meters

items.statement: Yarn Solutions spinning capacity of 211,584 spindles, world's largest under one roof
items.quote: Do keep in mind that it's the world's largest plant under one roof where we have a capacity of 211,584 spindles.

items.statement: Transitioning to four verticals: Home Textile Solutions, Yarn Solutions, Fabric Solutions, Apparel Solutions
items.quote: So in a sense, we are going to be adding 3 new product verticals to our port folio and in addition to Home Textile Solutions. And the 3 product verticals will be Yarn Solutions, Fabric Solutions and Apparel Solutions.

items.statement: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions verticals have begun operations; Apparel Solutions to start in a couple of quarters
items.quote: as we speak, the company now operates in 3 verticals: the Home Textile Solutions verti cal, the Yarn Solutions vertical and the Fabric Solutions vertical, of which the Yarn and Fabric Solutions verticals are nascent and are being ramped up as we speak

items.statement: U.S. demand affected by policy uncertainty and tariffs creating inflationary environment
items.quote: We have also seen some flip-flop on policies and therefore, the uncertainty. It's created an inflationary environment as far as our products are concerned, and therefore, the demand, let's just say, scenarios has been slightly altered

items.statement: U.K. and EU FTAs expected to offer opportunities in medium term; U.K. FTA to kick in soon
items.quote: On the other side, the FTAs that the country has signed with jurisdictions like the U.K. and EU will all go well for us in the medium term. The U.K. piece will kick in.

items.statement: Reducing U.S. and client concentration; broadening jurisdictions, India presence, and product categories
items.quote: We believe this will accelerate utilization levels and diversify revenue streams, tap new opportunities in the wake of new global regulatory frameworks and geopolitical realities.

items.statement: Over 90% of Yarn Solutions capacity to be sold externally; currently buy yarn for internal needs
items.quote: So I believe that over 90% of our capacities will be placed externally because even today, we are not able to fulfill our internal requirements just by our captive plant.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 16% driven by lower revenues, product mix tweaks, and raw material inflation
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA came in at INR101 crores. The EBITDA margin came in at about 16%, again, primarily driven by slightly lower revenues, some tweaks in product mix and some inflationary headwinds on the raw material front.

items.statement: Home textile Sheeting facing pricing challenges; new verticals expected to offer better pricing power
items.quote: We believe the home textile space will see pricing challenges going forward, especially on the Sheeting front. And we also believe that our new product verticals will offer better pricing power and market opportunities for us going forward.

items.statement: U.S. tariff situation stabilized at current levels; U.K. and EU FTAs to benefit in medium term
items.quote: So in a sense, the tariff piece has stabilized and the FTA piece should offer some opportunities.

items.statement: Leverage range-bound at INR2,550 crores; NCDs raised for debt tenor balancing, not additional capital
items.quote: In addition to this, we have our overall leverage, which has remained range bound for the quarter at about INR2,550 crores.

items.statement: NCDs raised to balance debt maturity profiles; no incremental leverage expected
items.quote: On the fundraising side, we have just raised some NCDs to make sure that our debt tenors are balanced and our maturity profiles are balanced. So it's not really additional capital as such at this point.

items.statement: Sheeting division capacity utilization at 52%; Terry division at 63% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The capacity utilizations at our facilities stood at 99%. Our Sheeting division came in at 52% and our Terry division stood at 63% as was the case during the last quarter.

items.statement: Transition period may cause revenue volatility over next couple of quarters while stabilizing new platforms
items.quote: this period for us, be it Q2 or whatever it is, in the short term for a couple of quarters, our focus is on transition. We will see some volatility in numbers while we go through this transition and stabilize on the new platforms.

items.statement: Consolidated total income Q1 FY27 at INR634 crores vs INR661 crores previous period
items.quote: So the consolidated total income for Q1 FY27 stood at INR634 crores versus INR661 crores, which was a range-bound number

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Q1 FY27 at INR101 crores
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA came in at INR101 crores.

items.statement: India expected to become largest or top 2 jurisdiction for company revenues in medium term
items.quote: in the medium term, India will probably become the largest jurisdiction for the company going forward, if not the largest, amongst the top 2.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income grew 16% YoY to INR 495 crore; EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore with margins at 18%; cash profit up 56% to INR 76 crore; PAT up 79% to INR 40 crore
items.quote: During the first quarter, we delivered a record quarterly performance, with consolidated total income increasing by 16% year-on-year to INR 495 crore, while EBITDA grew by 17% to INR 88 crore with margins improving to 18%.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across Folding Cartons and Flexible Packaging; export business recorded steady YoY growth but cautious near-term outlook due to global uncertainty
items.quote: This performance was driven by strong demand, particularly in the domestic market, with both of our Folding Cartons and Flexible Packaging business performing very well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 18% in Q1 FY27; management expects margins to follow top line and maintain good profile, but no structural margin expansion or contraction signaled
items.quote: While EBITDA grew by 17% to INR 88 crore with margins improving to 18%.

items.statement: FY27 non-separator capex budget ~INR 100 crore; separator project ~INR 125 crore over 18 months (INR 30-40 crore in FY27); flexible packaging expansion ~INR 50-60 crore for 30% capacity increase
items.quote: In FY27, we have about INR 100 crore budget and this does not include the separator. The separator spend will be over the course of the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Flexible packaging facility at optimal utilization; adding high-speed line for ~30% capacity increase, operational by Jan-Feb 2026; folding cartons at ~70% utilization with headroom varying by plant; Chennai plant ramp-up on track
items.quote: We will be adding about a 30% increase to our existing capacity. You can say that the capacity will increase by about 30%.

items.statement: Broad-based growth across domestic and export; flexible packaging growing faster; Chennai plant utilization improving toward 70%
items.quote: Overall, it is a broad-based growth. I think everything has grown, but our flexible business has grown a little faster.

items.statement: Flexible packaging is lower EBITDA margin but similar return profile; overall mix healthy; mono-material recyclable packaging (Innofilms) technology issues resolved, adoption slower than expected but long-term bet
items.quote: So see, the flexible packaging is a lower-margin business generally speaking. The returns are similar profile-wise, return on capital and all, which is really what matters

items.statement: Diversified customer portfolio; strong relationships; gaining share across key segments; flexible packaging expansion to serve existing and new customers in same sectors
items.quote: We continue to grow ahead of the market and gain share across key segments, supported by strong customer relationships, disciplined execution and continued investments in capacity, technology and value-added solutions.

items.statement: No current domestic lithium-ion separator manufacturers; international market fragmented with majority in China, Korea, Japan; first-mover advantage in India for lithium-ion separator film
items.quote: Right now, nobody, but Vidur, why don't you answer. But I think there is nobody today in India who's manufacturing this material and nobody who has announced any plan to manufacture either.

items.statement: PLI scheme for battery materials not yet formalized; no application opened; plastic ban on pan masala not new, minimal impact as not major supplier
items.quote: So far the government has not formalized any scheme and they have not opened any application. Beyond that, then we will have to discuss when the time for that comes.

items.statement: Export growth steady YoY but cautious near-term; UK/EU FTA positive sentiment for India sourcing; flexible packaging benefits from slight duty reduction
items.quote: Our export business also recorded steady year-on-year growth; however, we remain cautious on the near-term outlook given the continuing uncertainty in the global operating environment.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed through with ~1 quarter lag; EBITDA margin maintenance indicates effective pass-through
items.quote: There is typically like something of a lag when it comes to price increases being passed on. It is a bit of a difficult calculation because we always have some stocks and stocks on order and everything, whenever a price increase is initiated, it takes like over a quarter for it to get passed through.

items.statement: Entry into lithium-ion battery separator film via 100% subsidiary; ~INR 125 crore investment over 18 months; commercial production targeted Q4 FY28; initial capacity 70M sqm/annum (~6-8 GWh); long-term target 500M sqm/annum (~50 GWh)
items.quote: The project will be established through a subsidiary with a proposed investment of approximately INR 125 crore, to be deployed over the next 18 months, with commercial production targeted during Q4 FY28.

items.statement: Phase 1 separator film revenue target INR 150-200 crore; full scale (500M sqm) revenue estimate INR 1,100-1,300 crore; expected good double-digit margins and ROCE above 20% threshold
items.quote: For Phase 1, the thing is that we are building infrastructure, so that, in future when we expand, as we have indicated, our vision is to make 500 million square meter. So we are buying a big land parcel, which we w ill do in Phase 1. So it is not fair to actually compare the asset turn, but still we expect pretty good margin and a topline of between INR 150 crore to INR 200 crore on this first pha

items.statement: Global uncertainty impacts export outlook; battery separator qualification timeline ~1 year; dependent on domestic cell manufacturers' scale-up; geopolitical environment affects export potential
items.quote: We remain cautious on the near-term outlook given the continuing uncertainty in the global operating environment.

items.statement: Interest costs normalized in Q1 FY27 vs prior year forex hit; no specific debt outstanding disclosed
items.quote: This is a more normal cost this quarter. The last year that same quarter, there was a one-time large hit that we had to take on the mark-to-market loss.

items.statement: Building top-class team for battery separator venture; leveraging 30-year engineering and manufacturing expertise; no management changes mentioned
items.quote: We understand these materials very well. And over the years, TCPL has got into many new fields and I would say that almost in every field we have got into, we are easily amongst the best in terms of the technology.

items.statement: FY27 presales target of INR2,200 crores; H1 exit expected at INR1,050-1,100 crores
items.quote: I think INR2,200 crores is what we are targeting. Rohit: Sorry. INR2,200. Varun Gupta: INR2,200 we are confident of holding it this year. At this moment in time, it looks good. We should exit H1 at about INR1,100 crores, as I indicated, between INR1,050 crores, INR1,100 crores, given that we hit INR860 crores by

items.statement: FY27 revenue target around INR2,000 crores
items.quote: And this year is expected around about INR2,000 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Long-term ROE floor of 15%; FY27 expected to hit 20% ROE
items.quote: So when I say 15%, the goal of the company is to make 15% ROE the floor ROE on a long-term basis. And have years higher than that. So the first was to get to 15%, but the strategic objective is to make that the floor, and figure out how do we do that.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 bookings INR358 crores, 3.6 lakh sq ft, 234 units; collections INR409 crores (+6% YoY)
items.quote: The company recorded a booking value of INR358 crores during the quarter gone by, with 3.6 lakh square feet of area sold across 234 units. While bookings moderated compared to the exceptionally strong preceding quarter, our collections remained healthy at INR409 crores, registering a 6% year-on-year growth, reflecting sustained customer confidence and strong collection efficiency.

items.statement: July presales INR859 crores YTD; H1 exit target INR1,050-1,100 crores
items.quote: In July, we took out an operational update. So in July, we had a great launch of a project called Ashiana Oma. So as of 31st July, our full year sales had reached to about INR859-odd crores. So if you look at the July month was better than actually the entire first quarter.

items.statement: Average realization improved 37% YoY to INR9,923/sq ft driven by favorable product mix and pricing resilience
items.quote: Average realization also improved significantly to INR9,923 per square foot, representing a 37% year-on-year increase, driven by a favorable product mix and continued pricing resilience across our portfolio.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget INR800 crores including INR180 crores deployed in Q1
items.quote: Yes. So we have a total budget of deploying about INR800 crores in this financial year, including about INR180 crores that got deployed in the last quarter. So we are looking to deploy INR800 crores for the year total.

items.statement: Acquired 28.55 acres at Vadgaon, Pune for Senior Living; ~20 lakh sq ft saleable, ~INR1,800 crores potential sales value; launch in H2 FY28
items.quote: During the quarter, we made a significant investment towards our future growth pipeline through acquisition of 28.55 acres of land at Vadgaon, Maval in Pune. This is the largest ever land acquisition undertaken by the company for a Senior Living project with an estimated saleable area of approximately 20 lakh square feet and a potential sales value of around INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Vadgaon project underwriting: INR9,000-10,000/sq ft, 2 lakh sq ft/year absorption, 10-year development timeline
items.quote: So it's a 20 lakh square foot project. So we are estimating about INR9,000 to INR10,000 of revenue per square foot on saleable area. So that translates into about INR1,800 crores to INR2,000 crores. So that is our estimated at underwriting. Yes, and we expect to sell about 2 lakh square foot a year. So that takes about a 10-year development time frame.

items.statement: Target 30% gross margin, 12% SG&A, 18% PBT, 12-13% PAT margin at project level to sustain ROE in teens
items.quote: So, as we generally target about a 30% gross profit margin at the project level, about a 12% SG&A and 18% PBT margin and 12-13% PAT margin. If we are able to sustain that whenever whicheveryear, I think overall, generally, our ROEs should translate into the teens.

items.statement: Senior Living presales target INR1,500 crores by FY29-30; 25% CAGR long-term from INR570 crores base
items.quote: So let's say, FY 29-30 target is actually to look at INR1,500 crores of presales from Senior Living itself. And once that kicks in, I think then presales growth will happen.

items.statement: Senior Living GDV target INR10,000 crores; medium-term presales target INR3,000-4,000 crores
items.quote: think maybe get to a first place would be to get to about INR10,000 crores of GDV in Senior Living. Once we have that, I think then we can see just Senior Living driving the momentum of the company going forward. I think that's the basic key. So I think we will need to INR3,000 crores, INR4,000 crores of GDV of presales, probably closer to INR4,000 crores in the medium term to be able to sustain t

items.statement: Bengaluru Kanakapura Road project CPs progressing; final documentation expected soon; team deployed for launch readiness

During this quarter, concreting work of Unit-7 commenced, while execution across the remaining units continues to progress steadily. We remain on track for all eight units to become operational during this financial year.

items.statement: Sleemanabad Tunnel (11.95 km) achieved TBM breakthrough; longest irrigation tunnel in India
items.quote: Another significant milestone was achieved recently at our Sl eemanabad Tunnel in Madhya Pradesh, where we successfully completed the tunnel boring breakthrough. The 11.95 km Irrigation tunnel is currently the longest Irrigation tunnel in India

items.statement: Bidding for large Arunachal Pradesh hydro packages (Kalai-II, Kamla); majority of Rs 9,000 cr bids in Northeast; outcomes expected by Diwali
items.quote: So, 9,000 what we have bid so far is overall. I think majority of that would be in Arunachal and the northeast only

items.statement: Promoter pledge 85-90% currently; expects 15-20% reduction this year but no exact timeline
items.quote: Right now, if I am not mistaken, around 85% to 90% of the shares are pledged. So, we expect that to come down by at least 15%-20%.

items.statement: No exceptional items expected in FY27; prior year exceptionals from Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and investment write-downs
items.quote: We don't anticipate exceptional items coming this year. That was mostly on account of last year for Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and some write-down of investments.

items.statement: Patel Smondo real estate: OC expected in FY27 pending litigation closure; Tower 3 (service apartments) ready for occupancy post-OC
items.quote: OC is expected. There is some litigation which is still pending. So, that we are expecting a closure very soon. And after that, the OC will be received. The third tower was a service apartment tower. As soon as the OC is received, that can be occupied. That is ready to be done and just to be occupied once the OC is received. Rajiv Rupani: So, sir, by when can we expect the OC to come? Approximatel

items.statement: ESOP trust exists; management will consider ESOPs for senior team; buybacks only after major debt reduction (2-3 years)
items.quote: Buybacks, we will consider once we close the debt. So, it may take another maybe two years, three years to reduce the major debt. ESOP, we have an ESOP trust. So, management will consider on that.

items.statement: Implementing IoT and AI-enabled equipment across projects to control diesel consumption and track execution; hard to quantify savings
items.quote: We are implementing IoT at various projects, which is helping us in controlling the consumption of diesel and other costs. So, that is one. And we are also looking at various new equipment's which comes with AI enabled and IoT enabled things so we can track the execution, improve wherever processes can.

items.statement: Dredging (land and water) being evaluated for entry, possibly via JV; leveraging tunneling expertise
items.quote: So, we are dredging work, we are looking for those works whether alone or with other people.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guidance for FY27 is 25%-30%
items.quote: Our expectation for growth of gold loan this year is around 30%, because some quarters are as per season, some quarters are off seasons. We expect that to be some between 25%-30%.

items.statement: Gold loan yield expected to stabilise around 18% with +/- 25 bps range
items.quote: We expect the yield to be somewhere around 18%. It may go down by 25 basis points or go up by 25 basis. Beyond that, we do not expect anything. It will be around 18%.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursement guidance of INR400-500 crores for FY27
items.quote: The growth will remain at a level of, I feel like INR400 crores to INR500 crores, as a disbursement in MFI.

items.statement: Branch expansion focused 60% in South and Central India, 25% in Eastern states
items.quote: The branch opening, we have accessed where the growth possibility is higher. I can say yes, around 60% will be in South and Central India. That is five states of South India plus Maharashtra. And some 25% will be in eastern states like Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha, et cetera, where we are seeing good potential. And the balance in rest of India.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM INR69,635 crores, up 9% QoQ and 57% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consolidated AUM for Q1 '27 was at INR69,635 crores, up by 9% QOQ and up by 57% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone gold loan AUM INR54,655 crores, up 12% QoQ and 97% YoY
items.quote: Stand-alone gold loan AUM for Q1 FY27 was at INR54,655 crores, up by 12% quarter-on-quarter and up by 97% year-on-year.

items.statement: Vehicle finance AUM INR2,562 crores, down 14.3% QoQ and 43% YoY
items.quote: In the vehicle finance business, we have reported an AUM of INR2,562 crores, down 14.3% quarter-on-quarter and 43% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone borrowing cost increased ~10 bps in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The stand-alone borrowing cost has gone up by about 10 bps in the first quarter of FY27.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds expected at 8.8%-9%
items.quote: On an incremental basis, I would say, we will be around the 8.8 to 9 handle, is what I would look at.

items.statement: Income-generating gold loan pricing at 14%-16%
items.quote: The interest rate on this scheme, it ranges from 14%-16%.

items.statement: Income-generating loans yield 50-75 bps higher than consumer gold loans
items.quote: It's higher once it's a consumer loan, up to 50 to 75 basis points.

items.statement: Gold loan share of consolidated AUM rose to 82% from 80% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated gold loan AUM for Q1 FY'27 was at INR57,006 crores. It is 82% of our consolidated AUM versus 80% for Q4 FY'26.

items.statement: Gold loan ticket size mix: up to 1 lakh 21%, 1-3 lakh 30%, above 3 lakh 49%
items.quote: Up to one lakh, it is 21%. One to three lakh, it is 30%. Above three lakh, it is 49%.

items.statement: Income-generating gold loans capped at 85% LTV internally
items.quote: Yes, as per the regulation, there is no LTV cap. But internally, we have fixed up the cap to be 85% maximum. That is the maximum.

items.statement: Added 3.2 lakh new gold loan customers in Q1 FY27; total outstanding customers 26.5 lakh
items.quote: During the quarter, we were able to add about 3.2 lakh new customers and outstanding number of customers was 26.5 lakhs.

items.statement: Pricing at lowest range in NBFC industry; will maintain balance between margins and growth
items.quote: See, we will maintain a balance. So currently, our pricing is at the lowest range in the NBFC industry. So with the market, we cannot be totally away from the market. So we have to move according to the market. But I hope we'll be reasonably balanced in that.

items.statement: Implemented new RBI LTV circular from April 1, 2026 including interest in LTV calculation and ticket-size buckets
items.quote: From the recent RBI circular guideline issued from April 1st onwards, we implemented it across in the recent period by considering the interest also while calculating that. There is a major change happened and also the ticket size also came in the picture, up to INR2.5 lakh, 2.5 to 5 lakh and above INR5 lakh. That is implemented from 1st onwards.

items.statement: Launched monthly interest payment and EMI scheme products per new RBI guidelines
items.quote: According to the new circular guideline and given some options or some different kind of product offering options also given. According to the customer requirement and request some of the products like monthly interest payment or monthly EMI scheme category products also we launched as a part of that.

items.statement: New MD & CEO Ashish Singh to join by January 1, 2027; 25 years retail banking experience
items.quote: Mr. Ashish Singh has been appointed as the MD and CEO and expected to join by January 1st of 2027. He is a seasoned banker with over 25 years of experience in the retail banking space and his latest experience at the IDFC First Bank has set off retail liabilities.

items.statement: Monthly attrition at branch level 2%-2.5%, not rising
items.quote: Our attrition level remained around 2% to 2.5% per month. Yes. It is not rising even now.

items.statement: Standalone GNPA 1.56% vs 1.8% prior quarter; credit cost 1%
items.quote: Stand-alone GNPA was at 1.56% versus 1.8% in prior quarter and credit cost in stand-alone entity for the quarter was 1%.

items.statement: Asirvad net NPA 1.4%, CRAR 31%
items.quote: Net NPA stands at 1.4% and Asirvad's CRAR as of quarter end was at 31%.

items.statement: Vehicle finance GNPA elevated at 13.3% vs 10.4% prior quarter; focus on collections
items.quote: Focus is now on collections as GNPA continues to be elevated at 13.3% versus 10.4% in prior quarter.

items.statement: MSME GNPA improved to 5.9% from 7.1% prior quarter
items.quote: Loans to MSME and allied was at INR3,303 crores with a disbursement of INR191 crores, and GNPA was at 5.9% versus 7.1% in the prior quarter.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR1 per share for Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Online gold loan book 86% of total gold loan book
items.quote: Online gold loan book accounts for about 86% of the total gold loan book.

items.statement: Temporarily stopped vehicle lending for FY27; may reconsider in FY28
items.quote: We do not want to disburse any more vehicle loans during this year. After one year, that probably in FY 2028, we may consider whether to restart or not.

items.statement: Microfinance to be contained below 10% of consolidated AUM
items.quote: I will tell at the group level, we want to contain microfinance at below 10% at a consolidated level. We want to grow that along with our overall growth, but in a stable manner where the asset quality is the prime concern.

items.statement: Management targets mid-single-digit volume growth and aims to maintain or improve Q1 EBITDA margin of 11.6% for FY27, with a goal to reach 12%+
items.quote: We remain positive for the entire year for both the single-digit margin -- single-digit volume growth and also a double-digit margin or the margins which we've given today. We'll only better that going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps YoY to 11.6% driven by higher capacity utilization and JV turnaround
items.quote: As a result of capacity utilization, our EBITDA margins have gone up on operational efficiencies, both on capacity utilization in our plants and also on the JV performances. So EBITDA margins go up by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization rose from 72% in Q1 FY26 to 83% in Q1 FY27; JVs also improved significantly
items.quote: So if you see same time last quarter, which is Q1 last year, it was 72%. We are at 83%, and that's an 11% increase in -- sorry stand-alone, yes. On a stand-alone basis from 72% capacity utilization to 83%.

items.statement: Total capex of ~INR275 crores planned through FY27 end, including INR220 crores for a 9+ million sqm greenfield plant in South (operational by Q3/Q4 FY28) and balancing equipment across plants
items.quote: So from now to '27 end, we have already looked at approximately INR275 crores outlay, which includes the INR220 crores plant plus balancing equipment in various other plants and some more balancing equipment in the Bathware, sanitaryware plant.

items.statement: Adding 4-5 million sqm capacity via balancing equipment in existing lines (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) ready by mid-Q3 to Q4 FY27; new 9+ million sqm South plant by Q3/Q4 FY28 with INR350 cr revenue potential
items.quote: We are taking many more steps, which are all work in progress to augment further capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in our existing lines in Bahadurgarh in -- which is in Haryana and in Gujarat and in Morbi and also in the South. All put together, we will be adding another 4 million to 5 million for the mid -- this will be ready from mid-quarter 3 and would be completely in place in quarter

items.statement: Implemented 16-17% average price hike in Q1 FY27 to pass through gas cost increases; blended natural gas cost at INR68/MMBTU (North INR68-69, South/Morbi mid-70s)
items.quote: We took a price hike of -- you can take an average of about 16%, 17%.

items.statement: Gas prices remain volatile with marginal increases in July and August; Morbi now buying expensive gas from GEL (formerly GSPCL) at significantly higher rates
items.quote: The prices of June and July, in fact, July is a little higher, marginally higher, but a little higher than what it was in May and June. And so is August. August is again slightly more marginally higher.

items.statement: May and June demand decent; July resilient despite rains; Morbi operating at 100% since May-end; export demand down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitics/freight
items.quote: Other than that, the demand of May and June has been pretty decent. July also has been not bad considering that there's been rains in many parts of the country. Morbi operations have completely started. They have resumed 100% production on very expensive gas.

items.statement: Project sales (currently 7-8% retail, 10-11% government) expected to grow 3-4% points; channel inventory normalized post-May but remains lean due to gas price volatility
items.quote: The second question on project is that, yes, project is going to go up. Our total project was about 7%, 8% in retail and about 10%, 11% in government. This in totality will go up by about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 17 to 12 days; receivables improved, inventory reduced significantly due to Morbi shutdown
items.quote: Our debtor days, inventory days, creditor days are all healthy. Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

items.statement: JV losses of INR24-25 crores in FY26 swung to profit in FY27 (Q1: INR3 cr profit vs INR10 cr loss YoY); Somany Max loss narrowed from INR7 cr to ~INR1 cr
items.quote: Last year, we had a loss of about INR24 crores, INR25 crores in our JV. This year, we will be in a net profit. So the swing will be more than INR30 crores from last year.

items.statement: Value-added mix improving via balancing equipment in JVs and subsidiaries; Bathware/construction chemicals margins ~1% above tile margins
items.quote: We've taken a significant value-add increase by balancing equipment. It doesn't come at a large cost, but that will further value add our products.

items.statement: Price gap with Morbi narrowed as Morbi doubled price hikes (from lower base) and shifted to cleaner gas procurement; industry leader Kajaria benefited from higher in-house polished vitrified capacity
items.quote: Morbi was just double of that because they were selling that much cheaper than us. So, obviously, when they have increased prices by more than double of what they were selling, the price gap between us and Morbi has reduced.

items.statement: Current revenue run-rate ~INR3,700 crores at today's prices with existing capacity; balancing equipment could add ~INR300 crores by year-end
items.quote: Approximately INR3,700 crores, yes, more or less, give or take, INR50 crores at today's price.

items.statement: Export weakness (down 50-60%) to persist until freight/geopolitics settle; channel inventory lean due to gas price volatility expectations; Morbi 15-17% capacity permanently offline
items.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak. That's been a little bit of a downer for the quarter, and this would continue probably for this quarter until it starts settling, until the freight starts settling.

items.statement: Targeting top line growth of more than 15% YoY, resulting in about INR1,350 crores revenue for FY27, maintaining healthy bottom line
items.quote: We are targeting a top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, resulting into about INR1,350 crores for this financial year, maintaining a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 is INR1,350 crores plus/minus INR25 crores; FY28 revenue expected at INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores
items.quote: I would seriously insist that we look at our ability to deliver our year-end revenue targets to you, INR1,350 crores for the current year, plus/minus INR25 crores. Next year, you're looking at about INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR2,156 crores as of Q1 FY27 end (66% defense, 34% space/metrology/hydrology); consolidated order book at INR2,849 crores including INR244 crores service orders
items.value: INR2,156 crores standalone; INR2,849 crores consolidated
items.quote: Our stand-alone order book as of quarter end stands at INR2,156 crores, providing strong visibility for the upcoming period. Around 66% of this order book is from defense and the rest that is 34% is from space, metrology and hydrology sectors. Our consolidated order book stands at INR2,849 crores, which includes service orders of about INR244 crores.

items.statement: Order intake guidance of INR8,000-9,000 crores over next 3-4 years to be executed over 5-6 years, including INR4,300 crores current book, QRSAM (INR700-800 crores), ARC (INR500-750 crores), Su-30/Virupaksha/Angad (INR3,000 crores)
items.quote: Our order intake over the next 3 to 4 years, I think should be in the region of at least INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores to be executed over the next 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: Full year order booking guidance of INR1,600 crores for FY27 (excluding Uttam order)
items.quote: See, apart from the Uttam, the order, we have guided to have an order book of about -- booking of order book of worth about INR1,600 crores for the entire financial year. We stand by that.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to be similar to last year with potential for positive delta increase
items.quote: Definitely, definitely, the margins are going to be similar to last year. You can expect a delta increase on that -- positive increase in that margins.

items.statement: Solution product pricing competitive globally at nice margins; expect healthier profitability across product life including AMCs and upgrades, though initial margins may trade off with order size
items.quote: Solution product pricing will be a function of the market, okay? I think the feedback from global markets, which we have received -- actually from not markets, one global market is that we are fairly competitive and that's at a very nice margin, okay? So that gives us the confidence that we should be able to maintain more or less our current margin trajectory.

items.statement: Invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure; production lines and team fully ready for seamless large-scale execution
items.quote: To support this rapidly growing volume and complexity of work, we have invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure. Our production lines and our team are fully ready in all aspects for seamless large-scale execution.

items.statement: Uttam Radar order execution period about 5 years (complete before FY32); Phase 1 (12 units) by September 2027; thereafter ~25 units/year average, potentially completing by FY31
items.quote: The overall, the execution period is about 5 years, as we have mentioned in the press release. Before FY '32, we must complete the total order. And the first Phase 1, the 12 numbers, which we are supposed to complete by September '27. exactly about 14 months from the date of order. And thereafter, almost every year on the average of 25 numbers plus, we should execute.

items.statement: Emerging as key player in airborne segment across platforms: Uttam Radar (HAL), AEW&C Mk-2, Su-30 upgrades (radar Tier 1, EW Tier 2), AMCA (L1/L2 for AAAU with BEL), LCH subsystems
items.quote: Astra is emerging as a significant player in the aircraft -- in the airborne segment. There are various airborne platforms, which are in the works and Astra happens to be a key part of many of these, be it where Uttam Radar is Astra's and the recent INR2,200 crores order. Actually, it's around INR1,870 crores without GST. So we have to keep that distinction in mind or AEW&C Mk-2, where we are part

items.statement: Secured INR45 crores order from BEL for MMIC chipsets; won significant contracts from BDL and Space Application Center in Q1
items.quote: During this quarter, we secured one good order from Bharat Electronics about INR45 crores worth of contract for all MMIC chipsets, proving our strong capabilities in radar core components. We also won significant contracts from key defense and space entities, including BDL and Space Application Center.

items.statement: Export focus shifting from offset/BTP to BTS and own solutions; pursuing MMIC component leads from US/Europe (sizable orders in 2+ years); comprehensive solutions for foreign OEMs in 1-2 years
items.quote: We did not have anything to -- we did not have any solutions to export. It is only now that we have built products, which are -- which can stand in the market along neck to neck with others. So as and when they play out, that's an incremental revenue stream and order stream, which will add to our business.

items.statement: Inducted new leaders in last 18 months: CTO, Head of HR/Admin, Quality Head, Purchase Head, R&D domain heads, Head of Sales & Marketing; resource rejuvenation focus
items.quote: In the last 18 months or so, we have inducted many new leaders into our company to supplement the continuous influx at the middle levels, new resources as well as replacements for folks who have moved on. Resource rejuvenation has become the order of the day. Just to elaborate, we've had a new CTO, a new Head of HR and Admin, a new quality head. We strengthened our purchase department with a new h

items.statement: Working capital cycle typically improves in Q1-Q2 due to prior year execution comfort, then pressure builds in Q3-Q4; expect similar position to FY26, no significant change
items.quote: No, I don't think so. I think normally the Q1 and part of Q2, generally, the working capital cycle looks much better because of the comfort being derived from the execution made in the previous financial year. As we move forward in Q3 and Q4, again, the pressure builds up on working capital. Therefore, I'm not expecting any significant change in the working capital position as compared with the pr

items.statement: Interest cost down substantially in Q1 due to minimal overdraft utilization from positive cash at end of FY26
items.quote: If you recall, at the end of last financial year, there is a significant amount of positive cash available in the books of accounts. So because of that, the utilization of the overdraft during Q1 is very minimal. So that is one of the significant reasons why the overall interest cost is down compared to the previous period.

items.statement: No equity dilution for working capital; equity respected as expensive capital; focus on positive operating cash flow and ROE improvement
items.quote: Till we have accretive nonorganic opportunities, we will not dilute for working capital. We are fairly comfortable on that part, which goes on to increase our return on equity, which is already has moved up substantially. And as execution happen, will move up even better. And more importantly, the positive operating cash flow, which was our focus and has been achieved.

items.statement: Supply chain stretch risk across borders as countries restock inventory; beefing up purchase department to ensure supply chain integrity and timely delivery
items.quote: We are beefing up our purchase departments and other departments as the risk, which I also want to highlight is stretch supply chains across the border, across every country because everybody is restocking on their ornaments inventory. So we've got to make sure that our supply chains remain intact and stuff comes in within the defined time lines.

items.statement: Competitive globally on solution pricing at nice margins; emerging as significant player in airborne segment across multiple platforms
items.quote: Solution product pricing will be a function of the market, okay? I think the feedback from global markets, which we have received -- actually from not markets, one global market is that we are fairly competitive and that's at a very nice margin, okay?

items.statement: Astra Rafael Comsys (ARC) JV order book at INR836 crores; planning INR360 crores sales in current year; execution within guided figures
items.value: INR836 crores order book; INR360 crores sales target
items.quote: As on date, ARC, that is Astra Rafael Comsys has an order book of INR836 crores. In the current year, we are planning to book sales of INR360 crores. We continue to strengthen our positioning across the defense, space and semiconductor segments.

items.statement: BrahMos program: supplying gimbal-based RF seeker components and telemetry for existing missiles; proactive development for BrahMos-NG seeker in development stage (few months to complete); new program numbers not factored in order inflow gu
items.quote: The existing BrahMos missiles, we are there as a part of supply chain for the gimbal-based RF seekers. In that, we are supplying a critical RF component to the OEM. Apart from that, we also supply telemetry products to BrahMos missiles. And also, we have taken up a proactive development for BrahMos new generation that NG missile. There, I think that seeker, whatever we have taken it up, it is in t

items.statement: S.G. Reddy stepping down as Managing Director; passing baton to M.V. Reddy and Atim Kabra; this was his last interaction as MD
items.quote: This is my last interaction with you as a Managing Director of the company. I am passing on the baton to Mr. M.V. Reddy and Atim who are more energetic. I'm sure that they will be able to deliver much more than what has happened in the last couple of years.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,200-2,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 10-11% (INR220-230 crores)
items.quote: So basically, what we are guiding is INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores top line and EBITDA margin in the range of 10% to 11%. So, it will be in that range between INR220 crores, INR230 crores kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: FY28 normalized EBITDA margin target of 12-14%
items.quote: In fiscal '28, I think it's in the region of 12% to 14% is what we can look at.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin dropped to 4% from 45% in Q4 FY26 due to raw material cost increases
items.quote: You would have seen the details of our financial statements and you would have seen that our margins, which were plus 45% last quarter, has come down to 4%, and that's what has percolated down to our EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients segment EBITDA at 6.35% in Q1 FY27, down from normalized 10%+ due to raw material costs and trade finance
items.quote: The EBITDA is 6.35% here. Predominantly, it has come down basically because of raw material prices being high.

items.statement: Aroma segment negative EBITDA of INR4-4.5 crores in Q1 FY27 due to low ethyl vanillin capacity utilization (~25%)
items.quote: So that's why this INR4 crores -- INR4 crores to INR4.5 crores of negative burn has come and hit us.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals segment EBITDA at 2.5% in Q1 FY27 due to diphenol plant shutdown
items.quote: Naturally, the closure of diphenol plant is weighing down on Performance Chemicals, and that's why we have seen a 2.5% EBITDA there.

items.statement: Expect all three segments to be EBITDA positive in Q2 FY27 with Specialty Ingredients improving due to Brazil correction and price pass-through
items.quote: So, all in all, versus Q1, all 3 of the verticals will be significantly better than they were in Q1.

items.statement: Target double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Q3, Q3 could be there.

items.statement: Vanillin demand picking up; channel stocks cleared; estimating 3,000-4,000 tons demand for FY27 but production limited to ~3,000 tons due to campaign changeovers
items.quote: So, in terms of demand pickup, 3,000 to 4,000 tons is what we are estimating for this year, but we may not be able to produce that much because of the campaign that we are doing.

items.statement: U.S. and Europe vanillin supply gap of 5,000-6,000 tons due to antidumping duties; Camlin targeting this opportunity
items.quote: And there seems to be a gap of about 5,000 to 6,000 tons of material, which will have to be imported because the local production capacities are fully occupied at that level.

items.statement: Vanillin plant capacity 6,000 tons (achievable 5,000); FY27 production estimated at 3,000 tons due to 4 campaign changeovers losing ~4 months production
items.quote: So every time we switch a campaig n, we lose about a month of production. And we are going to -- in this year, we are going to do 4 campaigns. So we'll be losing 4 months of production

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin 750-ton campaign completing mid-August; switching to methyl vanillin; Q2 FY27 sales target 500-600 tons combined
items.quote: We'll be taking a shutdown after the 750 ton ethyl vanillin campaigns over in mid of August, and then we switch to methyl vanillin. Naturally, we will be doing around 500 to 600 metric tons in the next quarter of ethyl vanillin and methyl vanillin.

items.statement: 95% of customers have approved ethyl vanillin; targeting 70-80% capacity utilization in subsequent quarters to absorb fixed costs
items.quote: As the capacity utilization crosses 70%, 80% in the subsequent quarters, we will absorb almost all the fixed costs.

items.statement: Vanillin selling prices stable at $13-14/kg in U.S. and Europe; ethyl vanillin cost higher than methyl vanillin; trade finance reducing net realization
items.quote: On the prices, U.S. and European prices are remaining same on the sales side as we have discussed in the earlier period, and it will remain in $13 to $14.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures continuing in Q2 FY27 due to war/conflict; only partial pass-through possible (estimated half of cost increase)
items.quote: In Q2, it will remain with us because I don't see so much of a difference in raw material prices because with the war situation and the conflict, it keeps moving in directions which we don't understand sometimes.

items.statement: Diphenol plant shutdown due to high phenol and raw material prices; sourcing hydroquinone from China at competitive prices for next two quarters
items.quote: We have been procuring the intermediates from Chinese market b ecause the prices are very comparable and competitive as compared to our prices, and we are relying on that

items.statement: Working capital cycle elongated to ~100 days due to Red Sea shipping rerouting and slower customer collections; may need INR100-200 crores additional credit lines
items.quote: We will try to use the internal cash, but it looks like as the year progresses, we may have to go and go and take credit lines from the market in the range of INR100 crores to INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Using supplier and dealer financing to manage working capital; this adds 1-1.5% to raw material costs impacting gross margins
items.quote: In other words, the interest which I paid by b orrowing, I'm paying it to the cost of raw material. So that 1%, 1.5% has impacted me because of this bit of a working capital need has impacted my gross margin

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR670 crores (Mar 31) to INR640 crores due to IFC and EXIM loan prepayments for vanillin plant
items.quote: We were around INR670 crores of debt on 31st of March, the gross debt, which is now INR640 crores. This is on mainly the reduction is on account of prepayments which happened for my long-term loans on IFC and EXIM for the vanillin plant.

items.statement: Evaluating capital raise options for balance sheet strengthening; decision timing depends on market conditions, rating, interest rates
items.quote: But at the appropriate time, what is better, there will be a lot of consideration, the market price and all those things, what is the rate of interest, my rating and other things. So, we will -- we have been closely working on it.

items.statement: CFS Europe in liquidation (no major cash burn); China entity liquidation in progress with INR10-20 million expenditure this quarter
items.quote: CFS Europe is concerned, it has been already gone into liquidation, no more cash burn. Of course, there is a small cash burn because this is a liquidation we require legal help until the entire process is over.

items.statement: Brazil fire insurance claim settled at INR400 million with 20% haircut; exceptional item recorded
items.quote: We have now tried to settle the insurance claim because cash is the requirement, now it's around INR400 million insurance claim. We said that let's not haggle with the insurance people taken a 20% haircut and we have settled.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients: Straights sales INR927 million, Blends INR3,000+ million (total >INR4,000 million); Blends targeting 20-30% growth in FY27
items.quote: We have been saying that we should grow at least 20% as a minimum this year. And in the budgets, we are talking about 25% to 30% of the growth this year.

items.statement: Vanillin EBITDA margin at 7% on total revenue at $13/kg pricing with 3,000 tons annual production (60-70% utilization)
items.quote: We will be making around 7% of EBITDA on the total, if the prices are at $13.

items.statement: Antidumping duties in U.S. and Europe creating supply gap; Solvay pricing strategy limits price increases despite duties
items.quote: If they sell at $18, the Chinese has to bear 250% duty, which comes to $7, $8. And that is how they have kept Chinese out. If they make the sale price to $21, the Chinese price becomes 8%, 8.5%, -- 5%. So, despite 250%, they will start competing.

items.statement: Diphenol plant shutdown; evaluating alternative uses for the asset; decision by Q3 FY27
items.quote: By third quarter, we will take a decision to either have an alternate use for that or maybe if the situation is right, we may shift back to the diphenol production.

items.statement: Changed financial disclosures from lakhs/crores to millions; introduced segmental reporting (Specialty Ingredients, Aroma, Performance Chemicals)
items.quote: From this year, we have also started disclosing the segmental information. There is internal restructuring will happen and the management has started looking at the business in a more structured manner.

items.statement: Delayed and uneven monsoon with high temperatures impacted sowing and delayed demand for crop protection products in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: A delayed and uneven monsoon, coupled with high temperatures across several regions, impacted sowing activity and delayed demand for crop protection products.

items.statement: Rainfall improving, acreage picking up, agriculture activity expected to gain momentum in coming months.
items.quote: With rainfall improving and acreage picking up, we expect agriculture activity to gain momentum in the coming months.

items.statement: Premium Maharatna and Focus Maharatna portfolio contributed around 64% of B2C business in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Within the core business, premiumization continues to gain traction with our Maharatna and Focus Maharatna portfolio contributing around 64% of business.

items.statement: Target to reach 70% premium product contribution in next three to four years.
items.period: next three years to four years time
items.quote: Now we have reached to 60-plus percentage already and the target is to reach to 70% in next three years to four years time.

items.statement: GRANUVIA and Spinoace launched with Corteva; GRANUVIA crossed INR5 crores in Q1, Spinoace INR25 lakhs; FY27 target INR30-35 crores gross for both.
items.quote: Granuvia has crossed about 5 in Q1. Spinoace is just the beginning. I think a small fee in retailsINR25 lakhs were generated in Q1 because the launch was almost in July end. I believe Granuvia can touch about INR20 crores in this fiscal and Spinoace can go INR10 crores plus, so both products put together INR30 crores to INR35 crores range is possible in this fiscal, gross level

items.statement: Revenue from in-licensing products increased from INR36 crores to INR46 crores YoY in Q1.
items.quote: Revenue from in-licensing products, last year first quarter it was around INR36 crores, this year first quarter it is around INR 46 crores.

items.statement: Revenue from patented products decreased from INR97 crores to INR70 crores YoY in Q1.
items.quote: Revenue from patented products has come down from INR97 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: Revenue from combination products decreased from INR134 crores to INR98 crores YoY in Q1.
items.quote: Contribution from combination product has come down from INR134 crores to INR98 crores.

items.statement: Sotanala project total investment ~INR200 crores (INR50 crores formulation, INR150 crores technical); INR70 crores invested so far.
items.quote: It will be a project total investment. These total investment will go roughly about INR200 crores, out of which I think about INR50 crores will be going in the formulations and INR150 crores will be for the technical. And the total investment made so far is to the tune of about INR70 crores.

items.statement: Sotanala formulation facility expected to commence around April-May next year, technical production by Diwali next year.
items.quote: The formulation facility at Sotanala is expected to commence around April-May next year, followed by technical products-- production by Diwali, subject to the project schedule.

items.statement: Dahej facility 50-60% equipment utilized for new plant; further expansion with new power connection and boiler upcoming.
items.quote: There are -- there is about 50%-60% equipment utilized for the new plant which we have made. So, there is further expansion of power, we have taken a new power connection and started this.

items.statement: Target to double company size in next 4-5 years through capacity expansion and product mix.
items.quote: The idea is to double ourselves. In the past, we used to double in 3 to 4 years. Now I believe that we should be able to double in 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Crude and petroleum-linked raw material costs remain pressure; addressed through calibrated pricing, better product mix, differentiated products.
items.quote: On the operating side, crude and petroleum-linked raw material costs remain an area of pressure during the quarter, impacting parts of crop protection value chain. We continue to address this through calibrated pricing, better product mix and increasing contribution from the differentiated products while remaining competitive.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in March, April, May but rolled back due to weak market sentiment; no extraordinary hike possible.
items.quote: We had taken one hike in March, two hikes in April, and I believe in May also we tried to take one hike, but somehow we had to roll it back because the market was very much delayed and the sentiment of the network was very weak.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 240 bps to 31.6% in Q1 FY27 despite revenue decline; driven by premium mix and some inventory advantage.
items.quote: If we compare the value year-on-year results, the revenue from operations has degrown by 12%, INR691 crores to INR612 crores, and the gross profit has decreased from 202 crores to 193.16 crores by 4% though the gross profit percentage has increased from 29% to 31.6%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined from 12.2% to 11.1% YoY in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: If we see the EBITDA, so there is a degrowth of around 20% and percentage-wise, it has come down from 12.2% to 11.1%.

items.statement: PAT margin declined from 8.4% to 7.2% YoY in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The PAT margin has also come down from 8.4% to 7.2%.

items.statement: Focus Maharatna margins 35%+ (30-40% range), Maharatna ~30% (20-35% range), generics 10-15% (up to 20-25% with price advantage).
items.quote: generally I always tell that FMs are the products which have higher profitability, Maharatna have reas onable profitability, say in between, and generics are sales that are low profitability. If you have the price advantage over any generic, you can make some good profits than the normal, because normally generic end up selling the generic at 10% to 15% gross margins. So, there can be cases where

items.statement: June inventory slightly elevated due to slower season start; focused on improving inventory turns, collections, alignment; aim to reduce working capital cycle as season normalizes.
items.quote: Working capital discipline also remained a priority. June inventory was slightly elevated due to the slower start of the agricultural season, and we are focused on improving inventory turns, collections and alignment between placement and underlying demand. Our objective remains to reduce working capital cycle as the season normalizes.

items.statement: Big inventory from June tumbling down; substantial improvement expected in Q2.
items.quote: Already the big inventory which has come in the month of June is tumbling down actually and you'll see a substantial improvement in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Annual capex to normalize around INR30-40 crores maintenance capex after current projects completed; focus on utilization, cash generation, returns.
items.quote: Once the current projects are completed, we expect annual capex to normalize around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of maintenance capex, allowing us to increasingly focus on utilization, cash generation and returns.

items.statement: Volume degrowth ~13% in Q1 FY27; small value growth ~2%.
items.quote: Yes, the volume degrowth is about 13%. There is a small value growth of about 2% actually, which is visible in Q1 results.

items.statement: B2C sales 64%, B2B 34%, exports 2% in Q1 FY27 vs 75%/23%/2% last year.
items.quote: If we see the segment-wise sales, the B2C sales in this quarter is 64%, B2B is 34% and export is 2%, whereas last year B2C was 75%, B2B was 23% and export was 2%.

items.statement: Herbicide 59%, insecticide 33%, fungicide 5%, PGR 3% of B2C sales in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The insecticide percentage in B2C is around 33%, herbicide is around 59%, fungicide is 5% and PGR is 3% in this first quarter.

items.statement: Kaeros Research targeting 100% CAGR initially, then 50-60%; currently on 100% CAGR path.
items.quote: Kaeros is a new company which we had launched and the target is to grow at a CAGR of 100% initially and then it will come down to 50%-60%. So, at this juncture, I can say it is on the path of growing by CAGR of 100%.

items.statement: Kaeros normalized margins expected around single digit currently; not expected to cross double digits until scale achieved.
items.quote: The normalized margin also you can believe should be around single digit at the moment. When it goes up then I'll give my comments. I will not say that it will cross double digits now, till I achieve something big.

items.statement: Sales returns possible but expected to be at least half of previous year's INR200 crores due to cautious placement strategy.
items.quote: I think that we should be able to reduce the sales return numbers to at least half what was there in the previous year.

items.statement: Positive sales growth expected from Q2 FY27; difficult to give exact number.
items.quote: Difficult to give the number, but we should be positive and that positive impact should be visible from Q2 itself, I believe.

items.statement: Operating leverage and efficiency initiatives (renewable energy, AI) to support ROCE/ROE improvement from Q3 (September-October) onwards.
items.quote: As utilization improves, we expect operating leverage and efficiency initiatives to support improvement of ROCE and ROE with renewable initiatives, lower electricity and fuel consumption Insecticides ( and increasing use of AI and other advanced technologies provide additional efficiency benefits for -- from Q3 onwards, I can say from September-October

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of at least 50% for FY27
items.quote: So I think revenue guidance remains the same. It will be at least 50%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance to maintain current levels despite new store additions
items.quote: And we will try to maintain the EBITDA margins even after opening so much new area.

items.statement: SSSG guidance of 8% to 10% for FY27
items.quote: And the guidance for SSSG has always been 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Store opening guidance of 170 to 200 stores for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 170 to 200 stores this year.

items.statement: Per store capex increased 10% to INR1.2-1.22 crores from INR1.1 crores
items.quote: So earlier, the capex used to be about INR1.1 crores. So I think it is up because of the prices rising, it has moved up to INR1.2 crores, INR1.22 crores.

items.statement: Added 56 net stores in Q1 FY27, total 381 stores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: We added 56 stores on a net basis during the first quarter, taking our store count to 381 as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Crossed 400 stores milestone after Q1 FY27
items.quote: Subsequently, we crossed the milestone of 400 stores nationwide.

items.statement: Expect 4-5% garment cost increase from Q3 FY27 due to raw material price rise, will pass on to consumers
items.quote: So I think we'll start seeing that impact from the third quarter onwards, and it will be an increase of about, I would say, 4% to 5% increase in the overall garment cost, which we'll have to pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: Historically price increases offset by ASP growth, minimal impact on value growth
items.quote: Historically, what we have seen is it might impact the volumes a little bit, but it is completely offset by the increase in the ASP. So in terms of value growth, it doesn't have a huge impact.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 SSSG 7.5%, volume growth 56%, full price sales 90%
items.quote: The SSSG for the first quarter stood at approximately 7.5%. We delivered robust volume growth of 56% during the quarter. Full price sales contributed approximately 90% of sales in the first quarter.

items.statement: Adhik Maas and fewer wedding dates caused demand slowness in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So I think both are related because of the Adhik Maas, we saw a slowness in the market. And also, there were less wedding dates.

items.statement: Target inventory 90-100 days, creditors 45-50 days; currently inflated due to vendor prepayments
