items.quote: We are looking to target inventory of 90 to 100 days and creditor cycle of 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Prepaying vendors releases INR150-200 crores capital when creditor days normalize
items.quote: So once we want to use that money for expansion plans, we just get the creditor days back to normal. So I think that releases almost INR150 crores to INR200 crores of capital.

items.statement: Low debt-to-equity ratio provides headroom; in talks with banks to increase limits
items.quote: And we are in talks with the bank to increase the limits also because our debt-to-equity ratio is still pretty low. So we have some headroom there also.

items.statement: Internal accruals sufficient for expansion; no QIP needed
items.quote: No, I think the internal accruals will be enough.

items.statement: Kids wear 25% of sales; demand considered inelastic as necessity-driven
items.quote: For example, kids wear is 25% of our sales. So you have to buy new clothes for your kids every year.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate within first year improved from 40% to 55% over last 3 years
items.quote: So in fact, in the last 3 years, people who came back to us within the first year has moved up from 40% to almost 55%.

items.statement: 80% of stores have 3-4 value fashion competitors; growth achieved despite competition
items.quote: Even today, I would say 80% of our stores already have at least 3 to 4 other value fashion retailers operating in exactly the same space.

items.statement: Announced two president-level hirings to support 50% CAGR target for 2-3 years
items.quote: And we have just, in fact, an nounced two president -level hirings -- and that is one of our areas of focus, getting the team in place because we want to grow at 50% CAGR for the next 2 to 3 years at least

items.statement: Mature stores (2+ years) at INR1,070-1,100 SPSF; new stores at INR730-740 SPSF (34% lower)
items.quote: So more than 2 years old stores are already performing at a very high level of almost INR1,070 to INR1,100 per square feet of sale. So I think in 3 to 4 years, we will see the jo urney of the maturity, and then we'll be able to comment better. But it's at a very respectable level, all the new stores that we have opened, they are already operating more than INR730, INR740 per square feet of sale

items.statement: New store cohort SPSF INR730-740; 10-12 stores below INR600 SPSF being monitored
items.quote: But there are about 10, 12 stores that are performing below INR600 per square feet of sale. But again, it's too short a time to conclude on those stores. So we are doing some measures in terms of marketing, in terms of better assortment, in terms of more freshness. But overall, if you look at new stores cohort, they are at a very respectable level of about INR730 to INR740 per square feet of sale.

items.statement: New store payback period 2.5-3 years; profitable from first month
items.quote: So they are breaking even and profitable from the first month itself. But if you talk about payback period, it's about 2.5 to 3 years.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension led to higher safety stock; will normalize inventory to 100 days
items.quote: Lastly, due to geopolitical tension, we have increased our safety stock in the warehouse for seamless availability of stock, which has resulted in higher inventory levels. Once the situation normalizes, we will reduce our safety stock. We are looking to maintain inventory at around 100 days.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 16-18% by year-end FY27
items.quote: On our EBITDA margins, I should say that even if things go along the way they are, we should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.

items.statement: Revenue target INR 1,300 crore plus for FY27
items.quote: This year will be INR1,300 crores plus.

items.statement: Revenue target INR 1,400-1,500 crore for FY28
items.quote: Next year, for sure, INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Conservative revenue target INR 1,500 crore and EBITDA INR 300-350 crore for FY30
items.value: INR 1,500 crore revenue, INR 300-350 crore EBITDA
items.quote: I think a good conservative figure would be about INR1,500 crores top line and INR300 crores to INR350 crores EBITDA.

items.statement: PM3 major rebuild underway, commissioning within a week
items.quote: Further, Paper Machine 3 has been shut for the time being for a major rebuild, which will lead to enhanced production capabilities and improved quality in the final product.

items.statement: Major capex program completed with PM3 commissioning
items.quote: I think the guidance clearly is positive. We are upbeat that with the commissioning of our last machine on our upgradation program, which is our PM3 that is going to be coming on stream within this month in about a week or so.

items.statement: Pulping capacity at 200 TPD each for agro and wood, sufficient for 4 machines
items.quote: So our pulping capacities, we are at a level of about 200 tons each of agro and wood. And that is consistent with our even paper production capacity.

items.statement: Pulp capacity to increase to 410-415 TPD to support full paper capacity
items.quote: So pulp capacity should -- will increase to about 410, 415 tons per day, and that's all that we will require to produce the relevant quantities of paper.

items.statement: Full plant at peak capacity post PM3 commissioning this month
items.quote: Yes. So post the commissioning of our fourth machine, which is now happening in the -- within this month, we will be running our entire plant at peak capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA INR 40 crore, margin 13.2%
items.quote: As a result, EBITDA stood at INR40 crores, broadly stable year -on-year basis with EBITDA margin at 13.2%.

items.statement: Including other income, effective EBITDA margin 14.4% in Q1
items.quote: And if we add that to our EBITDA margin, which it should, we actually get an EBITDA margin of 14.4%.

items.statement: Targeting 20%+ EBITDA on specialty grades like OGR paper
items.quote: We already have taken the commercial runs also, like initially, I was told that we have produced OGR also, and we are looking on the specialty grade where we can get plus 20% EBITDA on the particular quality.

items.statement: Blended NSR up ~INR 3,400/ton QoQ, but cost up ~INR 4,200/ton QoQ
items.quote: However, the improvement in blended NSR by approximately INR3,400 per ton was more than offset by an increase in cost of around INR4,200 per ton on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: ~50% of cost increase due to West Asia conflict, rest local raw material inflation
items.quote: So I would say about 50-odd percent of the increased cost is due to the West Asia crisis. Rest of it is more local depending on the state in which we are operating and the cost of raw materials that we are procuring that has seen a price rise in this quarter.

items.statement: INR 3,400/ton of INR 4,200/ton cost increase passed through in pricing QoQ
items.quote: But yes, the fact is that out of the INR4,200, which has increased as cost, INR3,400 has been passed on by way of increase in our pricing if you see quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Current NSR at INR 68,000-69,000/ton, targeting INR 72,000-75,000/ton in 4-6 months
items.quote: Currently, we are at about INR68,000, INR69,000 per ton level. Ideally, going forward, sensing of how the market is growing and the kind of positivity that -- positive sentiment that we are getting, our price increase is likely to touch and reach about INR72,000 to INR75,000 level in the next 4, 6 months.

items.statement: Imported copier/Maplitho paper priced at $610-620/ton at port
items.quote: So imported price, we are currently seeing trending between $610 and $620 per ton. Volumes are not large enough to create any kind of negative impact.

items.statement: Chemical/input prices stabilized at higher levels after West Asia conflict volatility
items.quote: As it currently stands, they are higher than they were in Q4. And -- but I guess they've kind of stabilized at these levels, and we don't see any further rise in the prices of these chemicals and inputs going forward.

items.statement: Wheat straw prices coming down, reduction seen in Q2 vs Q1 procurement
items.quote: No, they have come down. We are engaging with our suppliers and aggregators to see how we can moderate these pricing, and we have been successful. And we are seeing a reduction in wheat straw procurement prices for ourselves in Q2 versus Q1.

items.statement: Timber prices stable to down 5-6%, but handling/transport/labor costs rising
items.quote: I think, yes, this is the kind of price line, give or take a few percentage points here or there. This is the kind of price line that we see going forward because handling costs, labor costs, transportation costs, that is something which is increasing.

items.statement: Specialty paper contribution ~18-19% of revenue, targeting 30%
items.quote: Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%. It's about 18%, 19%, but we will surely be making our efforts to reach that level of 30%.

items.statement: Successfully produced OGR paper on PM2 for food wrapping applications
items.quote: On the product development front, we successfully produced oil and grease resistant paper OGR, for food wrapping and application on our PM2, adding another high -value specialty and sustainable product to our portfolio.

items.statement: Targeting 5-6% incremental topline from specialty grades initially
items.quote: We target around 5% to 6% initially moving forward for the next years. And that will be a base creation for this year. And then we will be more moving into specialty grades of paper.

items.statement: Healthy demand in Q1 FY27 supported by education, publishing, office consumption
items.quote: The paper industry saw a healthy demand suppo rted by education, publishing, office consumption and broader economic activity in the first quarter of the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Expect demand to remain supportive going forward
items.quote: While some near-term volatility may persist, we expect demand to remain supp ortive.

items.statement: Dealer inventory minimal, pipelines empty, suggesting demand surge ahead
items.quote: The volumes as being stored by dealers is minimal now. Pipelines are relatively empty and which suggests that there is likely going to be a surge towards a surge of demand in paper and which is likely to impact our pricing also positively.

items.statement: Imports diminishing due to shipping costs and container availability issues
items.quote: So what we are observing is a diminishing trend in imports, which is a good positive for the industry. And largely, it's the challenge that the world is witnessing in terms of shipping costs, container availability and logistic costs.

items.statement: Import pricing stable, not reducing, limited competitive threat from imports
items.quote: Pricing is again, very stable. They are not reducing from last periods. So that, again, is a positive. And I don't see too much competition staring at us from imports of material in the future.

items.statement: Antidumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing/printing paper (40-140 GSM)
items.quote: We have already done that. We are already in close coordination with the government, where our applications for antidumping duty and anti -subsidy duty has already been filed, and it is being keenly being looked at by the government.

items.statement: Expect ADD to stay for 5 years if implemented
items.quote: That's yes. That's what we are expecting.

items.statement: EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed, awaiting shortly
items.quote: No, that's already been filed, and we are awaiting that very, very shortly.

items.statement: GST inverted duty on notebook paper unlikely to be rectified; reducing notebook exposure
items.quote: No, I'm afraid. The government is quite strong in their conviction by sort of having implemented that. I think the industry has to move forward. The fact is that this implication is only and only if you are producing and selling paper for notebook segment. So we have -- we at Kuantum, we've taken a conscious call to reduce, if not eliminate over a period of time, our foray and marketing of noteboo

items.statement: Peak debt INR 760-770 crore, repaying INR 170-175 crore/year for 2-3 years
items.value: INR 760-770 crore peak, INR 170-175 crore/year repayment
items.quote: Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum. And we have repayments of about INR170 crores, INR175 crores for the next 2 to 3 years. And by the next 3 years, we will be at very, very manageable levels of debt under INR300 crores.

items.statement: Debt to reduce to under INR 300 crore in 3 years, possibly INR 300-350 crore
items.quote: And by the next 3 years, we will be at very, very manageable levels of debt under INR300 crores.

items.statement: Possibility of prepayment if profits exceed expectations
items.quote: There is a possibility of even prepaying if we are able to generate higher -than-expected profits for which the situation is positive, we can prepay and get our debt level reduced earlier than later.

items.statement: Paper sales volume 42,922 MT in Q1 FY27, up 35% YoY
items.quote: The paper sales volume for the quarter stood at 42,922 metric tons. During the quarter, we were able to command higher NSR in both the domestic and export markets, supported by improved demand.

items.statement: Operational income INR 304 crore in Q1 FY27, up 36% YoY
items.quote: Despite the macroeconomic challenges, operational income for the quarter stood at INR304 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 36%.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly clonal sapling production 17.28 lakh in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the sustainability front, the company achieved its highest ever quarterly production of 17.28 lakh clonal saplings in our in-house clonal propagation center during the quarter.

items.statement: Social farm forestry area increased by 1,300 acres to ~19,650 acres total
items.quote: We also added almost 1,300 acres of social farm forestry, taking the total area under plantation to about 19,650 acres.

items.statement: Targeting 1 crore saplings/year in 3-4 years from current ~40 lakh
items.quote: In fact, our target is from the current level of about 40 -odd lakh saplings every year, we are planning to achieve 1 crore saplings every year in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: AI integration in manufacturing targeted for completion by March 2028, expecting 4-5% cost reduction
items.quote: We could target between 4% to 5% additions in -- or reductions in costs.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving fuel, chemical, raw material, freight cost inflation
items.quote: However, the West Asia conflict intensified cost pressures, particularly across fuel, chemicals and other raw materials, while also affe cting freight and logistics cost.

items.statement: Input costs still rising, not bottomed out; selling prices may have bottomed out
items.quote: Well, input costs actually are on a rise, so they haven't really bottomed out. Price line, I would say, has bottomed out.

items.statement: Commissioned DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping to optimize yield and reduce costs
items.quote: We successfully commissioned the DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping, which will help optimize pulp quality and yield while reducing utility chemical and overall pulp costs.

items.statement: Installed advanced native starch system on PM2 and PM3 to improve paper properties and reduce losses
items.quote: We also commissioned an advanced native starch system on Paper Machine 2 and Paper Machine 3 aimed at improving paper properties and reducing uncooked starch losses.

items.statement: Installed Folio Ream Wrapping Machine to automate packaging and improve finishing efficiency
items.quote: During the quarter, we installed a state -of-the-art Folio Ream Wrapping Machine to automate the wrapping and packaging of high folio sheets. The system has integrated labeling and stacking capabilities, which will enhance packaging efficiency, streamline material handling and improve the overall operational process of our finishing house.

items.statement: Management expects post-monsoon recovery in DI pipe dispatches and payments from Q3 FY27
items.quote: So, we would be looking at a post-monsoon recovery in the dispatches and the payments, and from the third quarter things should improve now.

items.statement: Management declines to provide volume guidance for DI pipes and ferroalloys for FY27 due to uncertainty in state-level ordering
items.quote: For giving any numbers, I think it will be speculative right now because there are a lot of moving parts.

items.statement: Management targets 80-90% capacity utilization for expanded ferroalloy capacity after commissioning by Dec-Jan
items.quote: As we commission the new module by December-January, capacity utilization in ferroalloys will remain at around 80% to 90%.

items.statement: Management estimates revenue of INR7,000-7,500 crores with current capacity in a normal market by FY28
items.quote: With the given capacity it should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.

items.statement: Management provides long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 15-20% for specialized ferroalloys
items.quote: By and large, 15% to 20% can be a long-term guidance.

items.statement: Management expects DI pipe capacity utilization to reach 50-60% as market improves
items.quote: First target is to achieve 50% to 60% capacity utilization and we'll see as per the orders are coming.

items.statement: Total project outlay revised to INR1,112 crores from INR1,000 crores; INR1,076 crores already invested; balance INR35-40 crores by end of 2026
items.quote: The overall project outlay has been revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores, primarily due to technical upgrades, additional ancillaries, some inflation, and some time overruns also.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity increased to 5.5 lakh TPA; specialized ferroalloy capacity to 1.9 lakh TPA; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh TPA; sinter to 12.08 lakh TPA; all expected by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Our DI pipe capacity has increased from 5 lakh tons to 5.5 lakh tons per annum, positioning us well to ramp up utilization as the demand revives and market conditions improve.

items.statement: Current DI pipe order book equivalent to around four months of dispatch
items.quote: As per the current dispatch position, it is the equivalent of say, the current capacity utilization, it is around four months' order book.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA up 46% YoY to INR154 crores; PAT up 21% YoY to INR85 crores; EBITDA margin 9%, PAT margin 5%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA and PAT increased by 46% and 21% year-on-year to INR154 crores and INR85 crores respectively, driven by price normalization and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Conventional steel products margins 5-7%; specialized ferroalloys margins 15-18%
items.quote: So, for conventional steel products, the margins vary between 5% to 7%, and for specialized ferroalloys it's around 15% to 18%.

items.statement: DI pipe margins currently at rock bottom, similar to pig iron; could improve to 18% if prices recover
items.quote: Whatever we have achieved in first quarter around 12%, that is good enough and it should go up to 18% if the prices improve.

items.statement: Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY; pig iron prices up 16% YoY; sponge iron and billets stable; DI pipe prices down 25-30% from 1.5 years ago
items.quote: Realizations improved across key products during the quarter, led by a strong 46% year-on-year increase in ferroalloy prices and a 16% year-on-year improvement in pig iron prices.

items.statement: DI pipe prices have fallen 25-30% compared to 1.5 years ago and are at rock bottom
items.quote: Prices have dropped by 25% to 30% compared to where they stood a year and a half ago. Prices have fallen by 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Value-added products accounted for 42% of total sales in Q1 FY27; specialized ferroalloys contributed 27% of revenue
items.quote: Importantly, value-added products accounted for 42% of the total sales in Q1 FY27, highlighting the continued progress in our product mix.

items.statement: DI pipe market subdued near-term due to slow government ordering; medium-term outlook strong driven by Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (INR8.69 lakh crore outlay) and AMRUT 2.0
items.quote: The ductile iron pipes market continues to remain subdued in the near term, primarily due to the slow government ordering and project execution.

items.statement: Ferroalloy segment seeing strong momentum with improving realizations over last 5 quarters supported by healthy steel demand
items.quote: On the ferroalloy industry front, the segment continues to witness strong momentum with realizations improving consistently over the last five quarters.

items.statement: Specialized ferroalloys exported to more than 42 countries with repeat orders and constant customer base
items.quote: We are exporting to more than 42 countries today.

items.statement: Outstanding receivables from Jal Jeevan Mission: 25-35% released in last month; expect full liquidation over next 2-4 months
items.quote: Around out of the outstanding, around 25%, 30%, 35% of the money has been released and the balance we expect that now the flow has started to a little more, I will say, thicker in the last one month.

items.statement: Net term debt reduced from INR3,408 crores in FY21 to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27; debt-equity ratio 0.07; working capital sanctioned limit INR550 crores with net utilization below INR500 crores
items.quote: Our net term debt reducing significantly from INR3,408 crores in FY21 to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27. Our net term debt to debt-equity ratio stands at a healthy 0.07 in FY26 end.

items.statement: Management expects further significant debt reduction by March 2027 year-end
items.quote: By the year-end March, it should again see a big dip.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extended to Dec 2028 with INR8.69 lakh crore outlay including INR3.5 lakh crore central assistance; INR10,344 crores released by center in current year
items.quote: The Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, which has been extended up to December 2028 with a total outlay enhanced to INR8.69 lakh crores, including INR3.5 lakh crores of central assistance.

items.statement: DI pipe industry capacity utilization low (25-35% range); competitive intensity to persist until utilization crosses 65-70%
items.quote: Currently the industry with our pipe capacity utilization this particular quarter was only 30% on the enhanced capacity. Similarly, competitors, they also are operating somebody in 25% range, somebody in 30%, 35% range.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity utilization at 30% of enhanced 5.5 lakh TPA capacity in Q1 FY27; production 41,000 tons
items.quote: Right now, in the first quarter, the capacity utilization was 30% of the enhanced capacity. Around 100 and going forward as per the orders improve, we are ready to encash this. Production in the first quarter was 41,000.

items.statement: DI pipe demand recovery dependent on government fund releases and contractor payments; backlog from last year's low budget release (INR1,560 crores) remains constraint
items.quote: It is coming from the government's backlog because there was a big backlog happened last year as the last year from the budget only INR1,560 crores was released by the center. So that backlog remains the constraint.

items.statement: West Bengal government change driving development activity; TMT bar sales in Bengal expected to rise from 15-20% to 50-70% of production
items.quote: Going forward in the next year, we are foreseeing that probably we'll be able to sell around 50% to 60%, 70% of our TMT bars in West Bengal.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 to be the best year in company history and July revenue was INR150 crores monthly ARR
items.quote: July, we ended with INR150 crores plus revenue. So you look into the growth, you can now extrapolate the revenue projection for this year and next year.

items.statement: RetailerShakti EBITDA expected to turn positive in Q3 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA number we are closer to break even and expect to make positive EBITDA in Q3 this financial year end.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin target of 8%+ for FY27 and 12% long-term
items.quote: Entire year we will be maintaining 8% plus gross margin.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin improved to 7.8% from 7.3% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Gross profit increased by 64% year-on-year to INR34 crores and 24% quarter-on-quarter, while gross margin improved to 7.8% from 7.3% in quarter four of FY26.

items.statement: JITO private label gross margin above 50%
items.quote: And the gross margin is above 50%. So this Jito revenue ramp up will increase the gross margin.

items.statement: SastaSundar gross margin around 9.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For the gross margin, I think we were at 9.1% this quarter.

items.statement: RetailerShakti grew 48% YoY and SastaSundar grew 44% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: RetailerShakti grew 48% Y-o-Y, continuing to remain our principal growth engine. While SastaSundar grew 44% Y-o-Y, reflecting a strong B2C business.

items.statement: JITO private label revenue grew from INR25 lakhs in Q4 FY26 to INR79 lakhs in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We launched in the last quarter of financial year '26 and we sold product of Jito around 25 lakhs. And this quarter we sold around 79 lakhs.

items.statement: Existing fulfillment infrastructure can support 100% growth to INR2,500-3,000 crores annual revenue
items.quote: Our existing warehouse infrastructure or fulfilment center infrastructure are ready to take up around 100% growth from the current level. So INR2500 crores to INR3000 crores it means next year 2028 we don't have any issue for the existing infrastructure.

items.statement: Current warehouse capacity utilization at 90% with sideway extension covering another 50-100% revenue growth
items.quote: Existing we are running about 90% of the capacity, but you save the existing plus sideway extension that will cover another 50% to 100% of our revenue.

items.statement: New warehouses under construction in Guwahati (75,000 sq ft), Udaipur, Patna, Lucknow; Noida warehouse started Aug 17
items.quote: Guwahati, we have expanded existing capacity by taking new warehouse on rent, and 75,000 sq. ft. this we are starting the construction in next 6 months’ time. Others are Udaipur we have started the construction, Patna and Guwahati we will -- Patna and Lucknow we will start in next 2 months, 3 months

items.statement: JITO private label targets 60% lower prices than branded alternatives with >50% gross margin
items.quote: JITO private label, through which we aim to make quality healthcare significantly more affordable by offering medicines at prices up to 60% lower than leading branded alternatives.

items.statement: 40,000 pharmacies active in last 30 days out of 75,000 registered; average wallet share ~2%
items.quote: Active, I mean, almost all registered do some transactions in a period of one year. But if you say last 30 days, pure super active, then 40,000 pharmacies are active in last 30 days.

items.statement: 67% of RetailerShakti and 78% of SastaSundar business from tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: Approximately 67% of RetailerShakti business and 78% of SastaSundar business comes from tier 2 and tier 3 markets.

items.statement: Working capital cycle approximately 28 days, equivalent to ~8% of revenue
items.quote: Our working capital cycle is approximately 28 days, equivalent to roughly 8% of revenue.

items.statement: No interest cost; focus on eliminating depreciation and interest through digital distribution
items.quote: We through digital distribution system, we want to eliminate the depreciation cost and interest cost. And straight away come to the functions whereby from the gross margin to the administrative cost it goes directly to the shareholders' kitty.

items.statement: Treasury income from Flipkart sale proceeds funding growth; no paid acquisition of revenue
items.quote: We sold the revenue, built our capital base, and out of the treasury income building business, and we bought the capital rather than expanding and diluting the capital.

items.statement: 3,500 employees and 350+ health buddies; all last-mile riders on company payroll with full benefits
items.quote: We currently serve approximately 75,000 retail pharmacies with more than 50,000 SKUs sourced from over 1,000 vendors, supported by more than 350 health buddies and 3,500 employees.

items.statement: SEBI approval for merger/demerger scheme on track; responding to stock exchange queries
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are absolutely on track. We have started taking questions from stock exchange and replying them. We don't find any problem into anything so far.

items.statement: AI-monitored RetailAir SaaS for retailers scheduled to launch next quarter
items.quote: We are continuously working to launch our AI-monitored RetailAir product for our retailers, and we are scheduled to launch in this quarter. Hopefully in the next quarter we will confirm the success of the project.

items.statement: Tech burn split: 40-45% technology, 25-30% marketing, 30% acquisition/expansion
items.quote: So, breakup of this burning is somewhere around 25% to 30% is towards marketing and advertisement, while the 40% to 45% goes towards tech related cost.

items.statement: Northeast region highest growth; Jharkhand highest growth rate per IPM data
items.quote: I must tell you that the Northeast is the highest growing entity. This shows that this Tier-2, Tier-3 geography and where -- as per IPM, if you see the Jharkhand is having the highest growth rate.

items.statement: Management not prioritizing EBITDA for next 2-3 years; focus on cash flow and capital efficiency
items.quote: We are not an EBITDA positive company for the next two, three years and we neither look the EBITDA from perspective. So EBITDA is not our priority, our priority is building a very, very large company without looking hurriedly EBITDA in SastaSundar business and we will build a solid business with a straight cash flow without killing any money in depreciation.

items.statement: HealthX gross margin performance better than competitors at current scale; industry B2B/B2C gross margin ~12%
items.quote: So at this level, if you compare other companies what they were doing then you will find that the Health X performance is better than any of the competitors. That is number one.

items.statement: 95%+ purchases sourced directly from pharma companies without purchase rights; purchase returns <1%
items.quote: Importantly, more than 95% of our purchases are sourced directly from pharmaceutical companies without paying any purchase rights, while our purchase return remains below 1%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR440 crores (+58% YoY, +16% QoQ); PAT INR2 crores vs loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Health X delivered a strong top line momentum in Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations growing more than 58% at year-on-year level to INR440 crores and registering a growth of over 16% on quarter-on-quarter basis from INR378 crores.

items.statement: Management reiterated prior guidance without providing new numbers for FY27 revenue.
items.quote: So I would just say one thing that as we have given the guidance earlier, we are on it, and we will be proving our best out of the business what we are currently doing.

items.statement: No major capex planned for FY27 beyond INR 5-10 crore maintenance capex.
items.quote: And as mentioned in the speech also, for this particular financial year, we are not planning for any additional capex, except a small operational capex to the extent of INR 5 crores to INR 10 crores.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate capacity utilization at 29% in Q1 FY27; target 55-60% for FY27 and 70-75% next year.
items.quote: So currently, our utilization is 29%, just to correct you because this has a different product mix. And the capacity what we give you is on the basis of 1 mm thicknesses. And the production which we have is of the average 6mm to 12mm. So this way, we consider our capacity utilization is 29% and aspiration of utilizing this year is somewhere around 55% to 60%.

items.statement: MDF capacity utilization was 66% in Q1 FY27 due to planned April shutdown; expected to improve for full year.
items.quote: Following the resumption of operations after the planned annual maintenance shutdown, production gradually normalized with MDF capacity utilization at 66% during Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate revenue target INR 75 crore at 60% utilization; full potential INR 140 crore at 90% utilization.
items.quote: Again, I would like to say here that this year, our aspiration, again, is to take it to somewhere around 60% of utilization, which will take us to somewhere around INR 75 crores. And going ahead, if we utilize the capacity at somewhere around 90%, the potential revenue we can generate from this press would be somewhere around INR 140 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 10-12% expected in 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: If you ask me about, again, aspiration, I want to go this quarter. But realistically, yes, we may take 1 or 2 quarters more to reach up to that level.

items.statement: Older laminate business EBITDA margin normally 9-10%; Q1 hit by shutdown, chemical costs, and war impact.
items.quote: As you rightly pointed, laminate with older laminate, excluding this jumbo has got normal margin for the last couple of years is around in the range of 9% to 10%. So this particular quarter, we have got shutdown. So that has affected. Secondly, the chemical prices has also a negative impact as of now. Third, the war situation has also affected.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate EBITDA margin 20.6% in Q1 FY27; management expects to maintain similar margins through the year.
items.quote: See, it is very earlier in this situation to say because of the fluctuating raw material prices. But we would say our expectation is we would maintain such margins across the year.

items.statement: Resin prices up 35-40% QoQ; wood prices flat. Only marginal correction in July.
items.quote: Wood pricing has remained flat this quarter, but the resin prices have gone substantially high like somewhere around close to 35% to 40%.

items.statement: MDF 15% price hike sustained; no further hikes expected as market won't accept. Laminate 10% hike covering inflation.
items.quote: No. So currently, the 15% hike is what we are sustaining at. And we are not passing any kind of discounts or anything. So we are maintaining our given price hike.

items.statement: MDF industry growing at 20% CAGR; additional 800 CBM/day capacity absorbable but new factories increasing competition.
items.quote: See, as we have mentioned earlier, MDF as an industry is growing at a 20% CAGR. And when we talk about 20% CAGR, that means an additional capacity of 800 cubic meters a day can be absorbed in the market easily. But as you see, there are too many new factories coming into the market, maybe it is organized or unorganized.

items.statement: Added 15 direct distributors and 46 retailers/dealers in Q1 FY27; entered Honduras and Greece markets.
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, we further strengthened our domestic distribution network by adding direct 15 distributors and 46 retailers and dealers. We're also expanding our international presence by entering into two new markets, Honduras and Greece.

items.statement: MDF domestic sales mix 35-40% OEM, balance retail/distribution; export strategy 4,000-5,000 CBM/month.
items.quote: So when we speak about domestic sales pattern, our pattern is 35% to 40% of volume has been sold to OEM and balance is done through distribution and retail channels. Talking about the export, our strategy is really clear that we'll be exporting somewhere around 4,000 to 5,000 cubic meters a month.

items.statement: MDF exports low at 255 CBM in Q1 due to container shortage; July run rate 3,200 CBM. Freight costs remain high.
items.quote: No, not a big volume somewhere around 255 CBM export.

items.statement: Total debt INR 260 crore; scheduled repayment INR 55 crore/year; reduced INR 18 crore in Q1; target debt-free by FY29.
items.quote: As of now, if you see the debt, including working capital is around INR 260 crores. Now we have got a scheduled repayment. And as per the schedule, every year, we are making a repayment of almost INR 55 crores. So if you see the current quarter, we have reduced debt to the extent of INR 18 crores in this quarter only. So considering the schedule which we have been given by the banks and the financ

items.statement: Focus on improving working capital and reducing debt; no major capex beyond maintenance.
items.quote: Additionally, we continue to focus on improving our working capital and reducing debt. With no major capital expenditure plan beyond the maintenance capex, we remain focused on strengthening our cash flow, improving operational efficiency and creating long-term value for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: MDF value-added share 45% volume, 54% revenue in Q1; target 50% volume and 60% revenue.
items.quote: And last year, but the actual scenario for Q1 FY27 was 45% of value addition. And in terms of revenue, it was 54% of revenue addition. So this way, if we consider ourselves, then we are not in difference of 10% to 15%. Our margins are like 2% or 3%, maybe plus or minus to other competitors.

items.statement: Laminate blended realization up 29.3% YoY to INR 836/sheet driven by improved product mix.
items.quote: Blended realization also improved by 29.3% year -over-year to INR 836 per sheet, supported by an improved product mix.

items.statement: BIS licenses: all Indian manufacturers have them; 8-10 foreign factories (Vietnam, Thailand) licensed; minimal imports so far.
items.quote: Export, like all Indian manufacturers has got the BIS license. Pranav Marjan: Sorry, importers. Rushil Thakkar: And as per the information, 8 to 10 factories have already got the BIS licenses. Few are from Vietnam, few are from Thailand. But there is no subsequent amount of import in India as of now

items.statement: MDF pricing sustainable; took hike accepted by market. Vietnam/Thailand have raw material cost advantage offsetting India's freight advantage.
items.quote: So yes, going ahead, we see the good amount of competition in domestic market. And yes, we have taken some hike, which was acceptable to the market and the raw material prices have been included in that. So yes, we don't see any negative side of pricing going at this point of time. The prices, you can say, is more sustainable at this point of time.

items.statement: MDF India sales volume up 16.1% YoY to 52,162 CBM; realization up 14.4% to INR 27,736/CBM.
items.quote: India sales volume increased by 16.1% to 52,162 CBM, while India realization impr oved by 14.4% year-on-year to INR 27,736 per CBM

items.statement: Laminate total volume up 27.9% YoY to 8.8 lakh sheets; India volume up 6.1%, export volume up 43.4%.
items.quote: Total sales volume increased 27.9% year -over-year to approximately 8.8 lakh

items.statement: Jumbo laminate volume 1.13 lakh sheets in Q1; revenue INR 110 million; EBITDA margin 20.6%.
items.quote: Revenue from Jumbo laminates stood at INR 110 million during Q1 FY27 with sales volume of approximately 1.13 lakh sheets. EBITDA was INR 23 million, translating into a strong EBITDA margin of 20.6%.

items.statement: Optimistic on growth of profit and revenue for full-year FY 2027, backended.
items.quote: We remain optimistic on growth s of both profit as well as revenue for the full -year FY 2027, which will of course be backended as suggested by the note.

items.statement: Confident to exhibit top line and bottom line growth for full-year FY 2027.
items.quote: And as we look at the full -year FY 2027, we are confident to exhibit top line and bottom line growth.

items.statement: Optimistic on growth in margins and absolute and percentage in second half of this year.
items.quote: But suffice to say that the company is optimistic on the growth, both in margins and absolute and on a percentage basis in the second half of this year.

items.statement: Believe PBT margin over 20% can be maintained in medium and long-term.
items.quote: as a company, we believe that a PBT margin of over 20% is something that we can maintain in the medium and long -term.

items.statement: Closing order book ₹21.8 billion as of June 30, up 5.1% YoY.
items.quote: The closing order book stood at ₹21.8 billion as of the 30th of June as compared to ₹20.74 billion a year ago, reflecting a 5.1% year -on-year increase.

items.statement: Aftermarket closing orders increased 115% YoY to ₹6.24 billion, 29% of closing order book.
items.quote: The aftermarket business also continu ed to gain strong momentum, with closing orders increasing 115% year -over-year to ₹6.24 billion on the back of contract wins in the geothermal and utility segments, and continued traction in the refurbishment and performance optimi sation solutions, which c ontributed 29% to the closing order book.

items.statement: Order booking for quarter ₹5.68 billion, up 6.1% YoY, led by exports and aftermarket.
items.quote: On the order booking front, the order booking for the quarter stood at ₹5.68 billion as compared to ₹5.36 billion in Q1 FY 2026, a growth of 6.1% year -over-year, an increase led entirely by exports and aftermarket.

items.statement: Export order booking grew 53.4% YoY, 68% of total order booking.
items.quote: Export order booking grew 53.4% yea r-over-year, accounting for 68% of the total order booking as against 47% in Q1 FY 2026.

items.statement: Domestic and product order booking lower by 35.4% and 11.6% respectively YoY.
items.quote: Domestic and product order booking witnessed a slowdown during the quarter, lower by 35.4% and 11.6% respectively on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: International enquiry generation improved; domestic market seen weakness.
items.quote: Having said that, as we look forward, the enquiry generation in the international market has improved while the domestic market has seen weakness.

items.statement: Optimistic domestic market will show some signs of recovery in coming months.
items.quote: While we can internally see weakness, we are optimistic that the domestic market will show some signs of recovery in the coming months as well.

items.statement: Export orders deferred by clients due to freight rates up 3-4x, pushed from Q1 to Q2/Q3.
items.quote: execution of certain orders, especially on the export side, have gotten deferred by clients because freight rates have gone up between 3x to 4x, and those have gotten pushed from Q1 to Q2 to maybe Q3 even.

items.statement: NTPC CO2-based energy storage project taken at negligible and near zero margins.
items.quote: a strategic order that we 've taken on the NTPC CO2 -based energy storage project, which was essentiall y meant to validate technology and to prove a use case for our equipment. This of course, was taken at negligible and near zero margins.

items.statement: NTPC project due for commissioning in Q2, with certain revenue in Q2.
items.quote: But you will have to know that the NTPC project is due for commissioning in Q2, and so we will have certain revenue in Q2 as well.

items.statement: U.S. subsidiary expected to break even this year.
items.quote: We are also targeting to make this year as a break-even for U.S.

items.statement: U.S. product execution possibly in FY 2028; current year facility utilisation adequate, not high.
items.quote: the product will only get executed possibly in FY 2028. When we look at this current year, the utilisation of the facility will be adequate. It will obvio usly not be at a high utili sation level.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR 15,000-17,000 crore
items.quote: INR 15,000 to 17,000, I already committed. Same thing still we are adhering. We will try to.

items.statement: FY28 consolidated revenue target around INR 21,000 crore
items.quote: FY28 around INR 21,000 crores, and FY29, INR 25,000 crore. We are expecting INR 24,000 to 25,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue target INR 13,000-14,000 crore
items.quote: Around INR 13,000 to 14,000 crores on standalone.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated PAT target INR 1,100-1,200 crore
items.quote: And the PAT will be around INR 1,100 to 1,200, during this year.

items.statement: FY28 consolidated PAT target INR 1,300-1,400 crore
items.quote: Next year, INR 1,300 to 1,400, and, of course, FY29 around INR 2,000 CR, we are expecting a PAT.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin 6-6.5% and EBITDA margin 6.5-7% minimum going forward
items.quote: 6-6.5% PAT, and the EBITDA, 6.5-7% minimum.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR 1,12,000 crore, consolidated INR 1,27,000 crore
items.quote: Order book position: NBCC's standalone order book stands INR 1 ,12,000 crores and consolidated order book INR 1,27,000 crores.

items.statement: Secured INR 1,600 crore new business on consolidated basis in Q1
items.quote: Business secured: NBCC secured INR 1,600 crores on consolidated basis in Q1.

items.statement: Awarded INR 1,700 crore new tenders in Q1; expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore awards in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: In Q1, we have awarded INR 1,700 CR new tenders on consolidated level. In the next 2-3 quarters, we are expecting INR 18,000 to 20,000 CR new works will be awarded.

items.statement: Expects INR 50,000-60,000 crore total new order inflow in FY27 including 5 GPRA (~INR 30,000 crore) and other state projects
items.quote: Total. Only GPRA around INR 30,000 crores we may get. Apart from GPRA, we are expecting two, three big orders. So that altogether, INR 50,000 to 60,000 crores we are expecting.

items.statement: 5 GPRA colonies redevelopment order ~INR 30,000 crore cleared by PIB, awaiting Cabinet approval
items.quote: That is 5 GPRA colonies, new development in New Delhi, five colonies. So Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj and DIZ Connught place Area, that will come around INR 30,000 crores order we're going to get shortly.

items.statement: J&K project: five tenders worth ~INR 3,500 crore to be published this month
items.quote: Another five tenders, we're going to publish during this month valuing nearly INR 3,500 CR.

items.statement: Naveen Nagpur: 400-450 acre land acquired out of 1000 acre; DPR in final stage, infrastructure tender expected this or next quarter
items.quote: Naveen Nagpur, good news is already they have acquired 400-450-acre land out of 1000-acre land. So, consultant already appointed, preparation of DPR in final stage. We're going to get the approval of the Cabinet of the DPR. Once the DPR is approved, then we will start the infrastructure tender at the earliest. Hopefully, during this quarter, if not, next quarter, definitely.

items.statement: MAHAPREIT delayed, expected to mature in Q3 FY27
items.quote: MAHAPREIT is still not matured. So, hopefully, like, the next quarter, it is going to start. MAHAPREIT, of course, it got delayed.

items.statement: Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, two more tenders to be done; site mobilized and work started
items.quote: Goa, already, we have ordered four packages. O n two packages, tender is to be done. So , Goa, also, we are through. Goa already is in, the site mobilized and work also started

items.statement: Supertech: 16 projects in Noida/Greater Noida; consultancy awarded, tenders to be called this quarter, revenue from next quarter
items.quote: For Supertech project for all the projects, already, we are awarded the consultancy. So, they are preparing their balance work quantity. So, hopefully, during this quarter, we'll going to call a tender, and we'll going to finalize the tender also. So , next quarter onwards, I think we're going to get the turnover also from Supertech.

items.statement: Awarding target for FY27: INR 20,000-25,000 crore (Supertech ~10,000 cr, J&K ~3,500 cr, Rajasthan Mandapam ~3,500 cr)
