items.quote: If I look for like -for-like, margins are steady at 19%.

items.statement: Nature's Basket margins flat, EBITDA negative Rs. 2.5 crores vs negative Rs. 4.5 crores QoQ
items.quote: Margins were flat. Expenses were marginally lower. And therefore, the financial EBITDA was -- negative Rs. 2.5 crores versus negative Rs. 4.5 crores in quarter 4.

items.statement: No new store openings for Nature's Basket; capex focused on refurbishing existing stores
items.quote: We will spend our limited capex on renovating stores, driving a higher level of throughput. We will not see too many additional stores.

items.statement: No large store addition plan for Spencer's in FY27; only relocations and few stores in existing clusters
items.quote: No, not in this fiscal, we are not ad ding. I mean it's not a large plan. I mean we are opening -- so what we are doing is we are opening stores where we have to kind of relocate a few stores, plus we are trying a couple of stores within existing clusters.

items.statement: Spencer's sales per square foot reached Rs. 1,850, typical of festive quarter levels
items.quote: our sales per square foot is Rs. 1,850 a square foot, which is typically what we get in a festive quarter. We don't get that in quarter 1.

items.statement: Spencer's category mix stable; staples up 100 bps, liquor up 100 bps, non-food down 100 bps, fresh flat
items.quote: Staples has gone up by 100 basis points. Fresh has been the same level. So, it's neither gone up or down. Our contribution, we sell liquor. Liquor has gone up by 100 basis points. And our non -food portfolio which is apparel, E&E and GM has kind of gone down by 100 basis points.

items.statement: Membership program has 125,000+ members (25% of active base), contributing 1/3 of monthly sales
items.quote: Our membership program, which we launched in July of last year, has now -- we've got more than 125,000 members, which is roughly 25% of our active monthly customer base. So, one in four customers are reward members, and they contribute 1/3 of our monthly sales.

items.statement: Members have 2x retention, 3x average monthly spend, and ~5x frequency vs non-members
items.quote: These members have a much higher retention rate. And when I say retention is what percentage of people come back and shop in the next mont h. That's about 2x of what is there for non -members. The average monthly spend by members is also roughly 3x what a non -member would spend. So overall -- and the frequency is almost touching 5, which is, again, 2x of what non-members have.

items.statement: Target 200,000 members shopping at least 5 times a month
items.quote: I would love to have 200,000 members who shop with us at least 5 times a month. That's the number.

items.statement: Focus on continued discipline in working capital allocation and inventory optimization
items.value: discipline in working capital allocation and inventory optimization
items.quote: We are looking at continued discipline when it comes to our working capital allocation and inventory optimization, focusing on availability of the right SKUs.

items.statement: Consolidated debt Rs. 1,266 crores (SRL Rs. 1,019 crores, NBL Rs. 237 crores)
items.quote: So, at a consol level, we have a total debt of Rs. 1,266 crores, SRL is Rs. 1,019 and NBL is Rs. 237.

items.statement: Debt refinancing process started, expected to conclude this month
items.quote: The process has started and it will kind of in the next -- in this month itself, we will get some.

items.statement: Nature's Basket management changed ~45 days ago; complete reset plan initiated
items.quote: We've had a change in management at Nature s Basket about 45 days ago, and we've kind of drawn u p a complete reset plan.

items.statement: Online unit order economics turned positive: Rs. 18 contribution per order vs loss of Rs. 18 YoY
items.quote: Last year, quarter 1, we were making approximately, we were losing Rs. 18 on every order. And now we have actually turned the tide where in quarter 4, we were around Rs.12, now we're making Rs. 18 per order.

items.statement: Online ABV sustained at 780+
items.quote: Our ABVs continue to be 780 plus, which is pretty good.

items.statement: Nature's Basket turnaround depends on execution of inventory availability, assortment focus, and category optimization
items.quote: I would be more focused on what was the year-on-year growth, which was negative. I think we are in the process, like I said, in terms of just resetting a few fundamental basics and those few fundamental basics are more around our own execution.

items.statement: Targets INR 20,000 crore new work orders for FY27, with INR 5,000 crore already received in Q1
items.quote: The company is targeting work orders of around INR 20,000 crore during this year , in addition to the existing order book , out of which approximately INR 5,000 crore has already been received during Q1.

items.statement: Expects top line growth of around 15% and bottom line growth of 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company expects its top line to grow by around 15%, while the bottom line is projected to increase by approximately 15 -20%, reflecting continued business momentu m and a positive growth outlook.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 5,417 crore in Q1 FY27; total order book stands at INR 93,492 crore as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: During the quarter ended April to June 2026, the order inflow stood at INR 5,417 crore. As on June 30, 2026, the company's total order book is stood at an impressive INR 93,492 crore.

items.statement: Order book composition: Railways INR 58,000 crore, S&P INR 12,000 crore, Ports/Roads/Highways INR 3,651 crore, Metros INR 5,700 crore, Power/Transmission INR 4,000 crore, Hydro/Irrigation INR 1,626 crore
items.quote: Order book is primarily driven by railways with INR 58,000 crore, followed by S&P at INR 12,000 crores, ports, roads and highways at INR 3,651 crores, metros at INR 5,700 crores, power and transmission at INR 4,000 crores, and hydro and irrigation projects at INR 1,626 crore.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 3.99% in Q1 FY27 from 2.08% in Q1 FY26; consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.41% from 1.66%
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA stood at INR 171 crore as compared to INR 81 crore in Q1 FY26, which is higher by almost 110% on a YoY basis, while EBITDA margin also improved to 3.99% from 2.08% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Management work margins 8-10%, PMC work ~7%, domestic bidding 5-6%, overseas bidding targeting 15-20%
items.quote: For the last two quarters, we are focusing on the works which give us better margins, and those margins are more than 5-6% for the bidding works. And for management, it is from 8-10%. For PMC work, which we have got from PSU is almost 7%. And we are trying with other state governments and PSUs to get the same PMC margins, fixed margins. For bidding, I will again repeat that our margins will vary f

items.statement: Focusing on port, hydro, highway, and green energy sectors for new orders; targeting INR 20,000-25,000 crore business development for FY27
items.quote: Our target for business development or increasing the order book is almost INR 20,000-25,000 crore for this year, out of which already INR 5,500 crore of works have been entrusted to us. And we are trying in all the sectors. Right now, we are focusing heavily on port sector, hydro, and highway. So, these are the three sectors , and plus green energy also.

items.statement: 42% of railway work awarded on management fee basis; INR 6,500 crore PMC work from NMDC; discussions ongoing with other PSUs
items.quote: It is almost 40%. 42% to be precise , is the railway work, which has been awarded on a management fee basis. And we are also trying with other state government and PSUs to get the work on nomination basis for PMC. And we have already got almost INR 6,500 crore works from a PSU called NMDC.

items.statement: Contracts generally covered by price variation clauses; inflation impact limited though some impact always exists
items.quote: Vishal, generally, all the contracts are covered by price variation, which generally covers the price inflation. So, I think it does not have a very big impact, though some impact is always there.

items.statement: International focus on Central Asia, Middle East, Eastern Europe, Southeast Asia, Africa; bidding for power transmission, railway, road, hydro, metro projects in Africa, Nepal, Israel, Georgia, Serbia
items.quote: RVNL is focused on many parts of the world, and our primary focus is in Central Asia, the Middle East, and Eastern European countries, and Southeast Asia also, in Africa also, and we are in process of bidding in all these areas. And we have submitted bids in parts of Africa for power transmission lines for railway projects, and road projects.

items.statement: Railway receivables outstanding ~INR 2,500 crore; payments received within 30 days of billing; regular follow-up with Railways
items.quote: No. This is actually railway receivable or outstanding is a dynamic process. And presently, our outstanding railway is almost INR 2,500 crores. And we keep on receiving the payment on a monthly basis. We raise our bill to them, and within 30 days, the payment is received.

items.statement: No external debt currently; internal resources sufficient for next 2-3 quarters; working capital lines at 5.5-5.9% if needed
items.quote: Currently, we are not looking for any debt from other sources. We are able to maintain from our internal resources only, but we have our working arrangement s with some banks for working capital if required. So, in next two, three quarters, we are not looking for any assistance on part of that.

items.statement: Dividend policy follows DIPAM guidelines: 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher
items.quote: We generally follow DIPAM guidelines, which is 30% of the PAT or 4% of the net worth, whichever is higher. So, we'll give that dividend.

items.statement: Key risks: geopolitical situation, labor availability, client payment delays; risk assessment done before quoting overseas projects
items.quote: Definitely. As you know, the present geopolitical situation is a challenge that we faced during Q1 also. And if the similar situation persists, this is a big challenge for us. And definitely, we are facing some challenge of labor availability from the market. Labor is not available for works, we have to make extra effort to get the labor for execution of our works. Payment from the client is also

items.statement: All provisioning for onerous projects completed; no further loss provisions anticipated
items.quote: So, we have already provisioned for the onerous project, and we are not anticipating any further provision of the losses.

items.statement: Revenue per employee increased from INR 4.29 crore to INR 4.97 crore QoQ, reflecting improved operational efficiency
items.quote: During the quarter, employee productivity also showed improvement, with revenue from operations per employee increasing from INR 4.29 crore to INR 4.97 crore on a QoQ basis. This growth reflects enhanced operational efficiency and better utilization of human resources.

items.statement: Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project at 78% overall progress, 97% tunnel excavation completed, targeted completion December 2029
items.quote: The Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project is also project of national importan ce in Uttarakhand, being developed at a cost of INR 37,000 crore. The 125-kilometer project has achieved 78% overall progress , with around 97% tunnel excavation completed. Targeted for completion by December 2029.

items.statement: Execution to pick up speed as weather improves; priority to convert L1 positions and LOAs into active projects
items.quote: As weather conditions improves over the coming months, our priority will be to pick up execution speed, maintain margin discipline, and convert our healthy pipeline of L1 positions and LOAs into active projects.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at lower single-digit
items.quote: We are expecting that Q3 and Q4 will be better , so it will be lower single-digit kind of growth this year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 15-18%
items.quote: Sir, we feel that we should be able to get around 18%. 18% if things go alright otherwise at least 15%, 16% we should be able to continue on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.4% vs 18.4% YoY
items.quote: We registered EBITDA of INR 39 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.4% compared with EBITDA of INR 52 crores and EBITDA margin of 18.4% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: One-time export receivable write-off INR 2.5 cr and higher job work charges INR 6 cr impacted operating margin
items.quote: Other expenses included onetime write-off of export receivables of INR 2.5 crores. And secondly, our other expenses also included increased job work charges paid for conversion of raw material that is also higher by around INR 6 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued due to erratic monsoon impacting paddy herbicide Pretilachlor
items.quote: During the quarter, the industry continued to experience subdued demand conditions, particularly in paddy and other crop protection segments.

items.statement: Pretilachlor demand subdued due to irregular rains damaging crops and delaying sowing
items.quote: Pretilachlor is the key molecule of course is right. But this year the demand has bee n slightly subdued because of the irregular rains across the country

items.statement: EU Technical Equivalence approval for fungicide to add INR 30-40 cr revenue
items.quote: at least we feel that we should be able to get another INR 30 crores, INR 40 crores of revenue from this molecule in European Union in addition to what we are already doing.

items.statement: Hamirpur facility expected INR 50-60 cr revenue in FY27
items.quote: Maybe it's not INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores, but it will be somewhere around INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores. It will be there, no doubt about it.

items.statement: Hamirpur facility long-term potential INR 1,000 cr in 3-4 years
items.quote: Overall potential, sir, when we put up roughly 8 to 10 blocks, we comfortably should get almost INR 1,000 crores from our Hamirpur facility. It will take three to four years from now.

items.statement: Annual capex INR 100 cr across Sandila and Hamirpur
items.quote: Every year we are doing a capex of about INR 100 crores at Sandila and Hamirpur together.

items.statement: Hamirpur capex INR 70-100 cr per year, Sandila INR 25-30 cr for add-up systems
items.value: INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores at Hamirpur and INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores at Sandila
items.quote: The capex we already told that we are doing a capex of INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores per year at Hamirpur facility and we are doing some capex at our Sandila about INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores for our add up systems there.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 70%
items.quote: Our capacity utilization currently is around 70%.

items.statement: Hamirpur 2 of 10 blocks operational, adding herbicide and fungicide blocks
items.quote: Development at our Hamirpur facility continues to progress as planned with 2 out of 10 blocks currently operational. The facility provides a clear pathway for future capacity expansion and will support incremental growth opportunities across specialty products.

items.statement: New fungicide production at Sandila using existing plant with INR 2-3 cr balancing equipment
items.quote: We are trying to adjust it in the existing with some balancing equipment. We will not put a whole new plant for this. In the existing plant, we will have to put a little balancing of INR 2 crores, INR 3 crores and with that we will be able to produce this so that our overall capacity utilization will improve.

items.statement: Plan to launch 3 new products in FY27 including fungicide and herbicides
items.quote: Yes, 3. Including what we already produced, 3 products.

items.statement: New fungicide import substitution targeting 2,000 tons of 4,000-5,000 ton market at INR 500-600/kg
items.value: 2,000 tons capacity, INR 500 to INR 600 per kg
items.quote: we are trying our best. And the import what we saw from the data last year, it is around 4,000 tons to 5,000 tons and we should be able to get from this at least 2,000 tons of our capacity. Yogansh Jeswani: And what would be the price of this molecule, sir? D. K. Jain: Price is about INR 500 to INR 600 per

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume down 13%, price up 4% YoY
items.quote: Volume decline was around 13% and price rise was around 4%.

items.statement: Raw material prices moderated, finished goods prices also moderated
items.quote: Currently, the raw material prices has gone down as well as finished goods prices have moderated. So we are confident that we will be able to make reasonable margins in this quarter.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 200 from 170, expected to normalize to 170 by Q3
items.quote: Inventory days have gone up from 170 days to around 200 days. They will come down in Q3 to around 170 days.

items.statement: Receivable days stable at 120 days
items.quote: Our receivable days has been around 120 days. So that will remain at 120 days.

items.statement: No term loans planned, capex funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Our object has been not to take any term loan in India Pesticide for its expansion and we have already a very healthy cash balance . So we will be funding our capex through internal accruals only.

items.statement: Received EU Technical Equivalence approval for fungicide product
items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the receipt of Technical Equivalence approval from the European Union for one of our fu ngicide products

items.statement: Export revenue INR 89 cr (35% of total), slightly higher YoY
items.quote: Export revenue during FY27 quarter 1 was at INR 89 crores contributing approximately 35% of total revenue.

items.statement: EU approval sales expected to commence from November
items.quote: Sales should commence most probably from November onwards because they will take some time because what happens once, we get equivalent, they have to add that as a source.

items.statement: Facing Chinese import price pressure, improving operational efficiency and R&D to compete
items.quote: Of course we know that the market has become very competitive and Chinese products are coming at relatively much lower prices. So we are trying to improve our operational efficiency and trying to compete with Chinese imports and that is where our R&D team is working regularly to optimize further the process conditions and we are also optimizing in engineering to reduce the overall project cost.

items.statement: Erratic monsoon creating demand uncertainty, but long-term strategy intact
items.quote: Sir, as of today, it is going on like this. very well the overall situation of the monsoon and erratic monsoon is there, but it is very erratic. So that's why it is disturbing a lot. Maybe this quarter can be a bit subdued but I think there should be some improvement in the future. But long term strategy point of view, we are intact.

items.statement: Expect to submit SFB operational readiness to RBI by end of Q4 FY27 within 18-month timeline from Dec 2025
items.quote: We continue to expect that all required milestones will be completed within the prescribed 18-month timeline, and we remain on course to submit our readiness to the Reserve Bank of India by end of Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Technology stack for end-to-end customer loan journey expected ready by Feb 2027
items.quote: Technology stack for the end-to-end customer loan journey is under development and is expected to be ready by Feb '27.

items.statement: B2B UPI P2M segment relaunch tentatively in Q4 FY27 depending on ecosystem developments
items.quote: We are preparing to relaunch our high-growth B2B UPI P2M segment. However, this would depend on the ecosystem and other developments, which could result in the relaunch tentatively in Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Expect blended portfolio yield of around 14% for SFB secured lending portfolio
items.quote: And second, what we are looking at is 90% secured book of lending for our SFB portfolio with an average portfolio yield of around 14%.

items.statement: Expect NIMs in range of 8% to 9% for SFB, highest in industry
items.quote: So from an SFB perspective, with the kind of asset products which we are looking at, we expect our NIMs, and that may not answer your ROE question fully, but at least NIMs, which is highest in the industry, which we are looking at anywhere in the range of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Anticipate INR 10 crores SFB-related opex impact on FY27 P&L
items.quote: So, in terms of the burden on opex this year, we are anticipating anything around INR10 crores on this year's P&L in terms of the SFB opex which includes hiring, which includes all the other related opex for the bank.

items.statement: Plan to open 40 new branches in year 1 of SFB operations
items.quote: So we intend to open in year 1, 40 new branches as well, and that is part of our plan as well.

items.statement: Target credit-deposit ratio of around 70% and CASA ratio of around 65% for SFB
items.quote: One is the credit deposit ratio, we are looking at around 70%. So we are not looking at aggressive lending book right now as per the plan for the first 3 years. That is one. Second, we are looking at, as Ketan mentioned, our core book is stable. So 90% of our current CASA is the core. So we are looking at a CASA ratio of around 65%.

items.statement: Referral loan disbursements surged 214% YoY to INR 628 crores in Q1 FY27, nearly 50% of FY26 total
items.quote: Referral loan disbursals surged 214% on year-on-year to INR 628 crores, nearly 50% of the total disbursals in FY26, indicating growing demand for credit in our banking ecosystem and our target customer segment.

items.statement: Digitally active customers increased 22% YoY to 64.6 lakhs, FinoPay app customers grew 38% to 8.4 lakhs
items.quote: Digitally active customer s increased by 22% year -on-year to 64.6 lakhs, while active FinoPay, which is our app customers, grew even faster at 38% to 8.4 lakhs

items.statement: UPI throughput grew 14% YoY to INR 60,000 crores, digitally active customers for June 2026 at 65 lakhs
items.value: INR 60,000 crores UPI throughput, 65 lakhs digitally active
items.quote: UPI throughput grew 14% year-on-year to INR 60,000 crores and digitally active customers for the month of June '26 stood at 65 lakhs, a significant growth of 22% year-on-year compared to June '25.

items.statement: Net revenue margin expanded to highest quarterly value of 42.8%, up 275 bps sequentially and 925 bps YoY
items.quote: One of the key highlights for the quarter was a continued improvement in our net revenue margin. Despite lower revenues, our net revenue margin expanded to its highest quarterly value of 42.8%, improving 275 basis points sequentially and 925 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Added 8.4 lakh new accounts in Q1 FY27, total account base 1.83 crore, merchant network ~20 lakh
items.quote: Customer acquisition remained healthy, and we added 8.4 lakh new accounts in this quarter, taking our total account base to 1.83 crore. Our merchant network, which is close to around 20 lakh continues to be one of the biggest competitive strengths.

items.statement: Large part of technology investment done with Finacle core banking migration, adding lending modules (LOS, LMS) for SFB
items.quote: In terms of the investment, yes, a large part of investment is already done by moving the core banking from FIS Global to Finacle. We have to add a few modules relating to our lending business, which is like LOS, LMS other related modules in terms of the technology.

items.statement: Technology transition for SFB first 3 phases expected complete by end of FY27
items.quote: And as you rightly said, after FY27, we should be completed by our entire technology transition in terms of the SFB as well, at least for the first 3 phases of our SFB.

items.statement: Appointed PwC for SFB implementation and operational readiness, onboarded technology partners for LOS, LMS and lending applications
items.quote: We have appointed PricewaterhouseCoopers to support the implementation and overall operational readiness of SFB. We have also onboarded technology partners for our loan origination system, loan management system and other lending applications that will for m the backbone of our lending platform

items.statement: RBI stipulated 18-month timeline from Dec 5, 2025 (ends June 5, 2027) for SFB transition, must submit operational readiness before that
items.quote: RBI has given us 18 months on 5th December 2025, which ends on 5th June 2027. Before that, we need to submit an application to RBI showing that we are operationally ready to launch the SFB.

items.statement: Current FY30 plan is organic, but will evaluate inorganic opportunities to accelerate lending and digital capabilities if they arise
items.quote: As regards to the inorganic opportunities in terms of acquisition, etc., with our kind of a liability franchise, we will keep our eyes and ears open. And if anything interesting comes across, we will be looking at it as and when it comes and if at all, it comes through. So at current stage, our plan, which we have put for our FY30 is an organic plan.

items.statement: B2B UPI P2M business paused since Feb 2026 event, will take at least couple of quarters for relaunch
items.quote: Besides the event of Feb '26, one of our most profitable B2B business has been paused for recalibration, and it will take at least next couple of quarters for the relaunch.

items.statement: Traditional transaction business (remittance, micro ATM, AePS) saw 13% sequential revenue decline due to digital adoption headwinds
items.quote: Our traditional transaction business, which forms of remittance, micro ATM, AePS saw 13% sequential revenue decline as it continued to face industry headwinds due to grow ing digital adoption in Bharat

items.statement: Fee-based income contributes over 75% of revenue, stood at INR 234 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our USP, the existing fee-based income, which contributes over 75% of the revenue stood at INR 234 crores in Q1 FY27, and it remains our distinct advantage over other SFBs once we transit.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs. 1,000 crores for FY27 and EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% reiterated
items.quote: In summary, we would like to reiterate that our trajectory towards the Rs. 1,000 crores revenue by FY '27 remains firmly on track, supported by a robust product pipeline and a sustained demand across key therapeutic segments including anesthetics, anti-diabetics, anti-anxiety, vitamins, and ADHD. We remain confident of our guidance of EBITDA margins in the range of 33% to 35%.

items.statement: CAGR of about 20% year-on-year expected to continue beyond FY27
items.quote: So, we have already said that we would be growing at a CAGR of about 20% year-on-year. I think the same trend would continue.

items.statement: Strong demand in Q1 but water shortage deferred Rs. 35 crores of sales
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 190 crores, reflecting a 31% year-on-year growth. Demand remained strong during the quarter, but water shortages led to a deferment of sales of around Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 25% in Q1 FY27, down 8.1% YoY due to water shortage and solar policy change impacting Rs. 8 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, EBITDA stood at Rs. 47 crores, a decline of 8.1% year -on-year with EBITDA margins at 25%. Before we move forward, let me explain the reasons for the decline in margins during the quarter. It was a combination of factors that coincided during the period and are mostly temporary in nature.

items.statement: Excluding one-off impacts, margins would have been within guided 33-35% range
items.quote: Excluding these one-off impacts, margins would have remained within our guided range. We believe these are temporary disruptions and with operations stabilizing, we expect performance to improve in the coming quarters while remaining firmly on track to achieve our FY '27 growth and margin objectives.

items.statement: Solar policy change increased fuel and power costs by Rs. 8 crores at EBITDA level in Q1
items.quote: Second, Maharashtra government changed the solar power policy, which led to increased fuel and power costs during the quarter. This alone had an impact of Rs. 8 crores at EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Retrospective solar subsidy payment of Rs. 4.5-5 crores is one-time; ongoing power cost increases will be passed to customers
items.quote: See, this would be somewhere around Rs. 4.5 crores - Rs. 5 crores at this stage. So, in fact, the matter is also sub judice. There is a case which is running on around in that wherein all the Solar Power Association members have come around, and they have filed a case against the MSEDCL.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex of Rs. 16.58 crores for maintenance, smaller projects, formulation plan and Isambe project
items.quote: Our CapEx for Q1 FY '27 stood at Rs. 16.58 crores driven by spend on maintenance CapEx, smaller projects, formulation plan requirements and Isambe project.

items.statement: Patalganga Phase-1 capex earmarked at Rs. 200 crores for two API advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks
items.quote: On Patalganga land, as our Joint MD has updated, we have received all necessary clearances and will be developing the facility in phases. The project will include two API but advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks. The total CapEx earmarked for this facility is around Rs. 200 crores for Phase-1.

items.statement: Boundary wall construction started at Patalganga; API blocks with utilities to be built first, targeting 40% completion in ~2.5 years per MIDC norms
items.quote: We would be looking at the API block to start with. That would be the first thing which we would be building along with the utility blocks. I think these would be the ones which would be coming up for Rs. 200 crores. I don't think formulation can start immediately. Say, right from the acquisition, around 2.5 years, we should have a 40% completion as per MIDC.

items.statement: Block F at Lote not started yet; will begin in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We haven't started it yet. We will be starting it in next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Launched two anesthetic liquid inhalation products from Ambernath in Q2 FY27; two ADHD products and contrast media (Iohexol) in pipeline for H2 FY27
items.quote: We launched two new anesthetic liquid inhalation products in Q2 FY '27 from our Ambernath facility and we expect them to scale up over the coming quarters. In addition, we have two ADHD product launches in the pipeline which will further strengthen our portfolio and support future growth. On the contrast media opportunity, we remain on track with development and continue to progress as planned. We

items.statement: Cardiovascular product launched Q3 FY26 ramping well; ADHD product scaling with LATAM/Europe demand; liquid anesthetic steady monthly supplies
items.quote: Our cardiovascular product launched in Q3 FY '26 has ramped up well. The ADHD product continues to scale up, supported by healthy demand from LATAM and Europe and we expect the momentum to continue. Our liquid anesthetic product remains on track with steady monthly supplies.

items.statement: EU audit for Ambernath facility scheduled for second half of November
items.quote: So, we have already received the dates for audit from EU at Ambernath facility. The audit is scheduled for the second half of November.

items.statement: Close to signing term sheet for large anesthetic CDMO contract; qualification and quality approvals completed
items.quote: We have made good progress specifically on one of the large anesthetic CDMO contract that we are looking at. We are very close to signing a term sheet. So, hopefully in the next quarter, we will be able to announce something good. But at the back end, a lot of qualification work is now completed. Quality has been approved.

items.statement: DSM vitamin project at stable peak volumes; pharma validation completed; dedicated facility operational
items.quote: Yes, we have. So, I think DSM has now reached a very stable state where we are very close to their peak volumes. Pharma validation is completed. Like I mentioned in the previous calls, we have set up now a dedicated facility for DSM. So, that is now up and running. So, things are moving very positively in the DSM project.

items.statement: Exports 81% of revenue in Q1 FY27; Asia 39%, Europe 35%, LATAM 20%

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 141.8 crores (85% YoY, 25% QoQ); EBITDA Rs 41.6 crores (118% YoY, 50% QoQ); PAT Rs 25.2 crores (183% YoY, 63% QoQ).

items.statement: US market programs running into tens of thousands of dollars; one live program ~USD30 million; rapid defense adoption pace

items.statement: Quarterly results can vary due to opportunity cycles, product mix, delivery schedules, supply disruptions, working capital requirements, customer acceptance

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%+ (20%-25% range), implying revenue above INR10,000 crores vs INR8,430 crores in FY26; guidance to be revisited after Q3

items.statement: Long-term target of INR20,000 crores+ revenue and 300+ stores over 4-5 years; EBITDA margin target toward 8%, PAT margin 4.5%-5%, ROE/ROCE approaching 20%
items.quote: Looking beyond individual quarters, our long-term vision is to build on the INR8,430 crores of revenue achieved in the previous financial year and, over the next 4-5 years, grow the company to INR20,000 crores-plus of revenue.

items.statement: Q1 consolidated revenue grew 67% YoY; retail sales grew 50% YoY broad-based across zones; same-store sales growth ~39%
items.quote: If you look at revenue on a consolidated basis, we have grown by almost 67%. This reflects continued and renewed customer trust in the brand. At the retail level, we have grown by more than 50%, which has been a wonderful performance.

items.statement: April sales INR1,500-1,600 crores (55% of quarter); May-June averaged INR500-600 crores/month due to elections, Adhik Maas, heat wave
items.quote: April was a wonderful month, in which we clocked sales of almost INR1,500-1,600 crores. In May and June, despite these headwinds, monthly sales moderated to an average of around INR500-600 crores in each month.

items.statement: July-August sales tracking ~25% YoY growth, 8-10% above May-June run rate
items.quote: Compared with June, we have seen stronger traction in July and August. At present, July and August are up by around 8%-10% compared with the May-June level, and we expect the build-up to become much stronger in October and November.

items.statement: Diamond jewellery sales +43% value, +18% volume; shift to lightweight, design-led, lower-ticket jewellery; 9-carat, 14-carat, lower-carat assortment expanded; old gold exchange 43% of sales quantity
items.quote: We must mention that diamond jewellery sales increased by almost 43% in value and 18% in volume. This gives a strong signal about design development, the shift in consumer preferences and the long -term impact these trends could have on margins as we work t o increase the stud

items.statement: Launched Aham men's jewellery collection combining titanium with gold and diamonds, priced INR20,000 to INR1 lakh
items.quote: I would also like to announce that, alongside our women-focused lightweight jewellery designs, including 9-carat jewellery and new Everlite collections, we have recently launched a new men's jewellery collection under Aham. The range combines titanium with gold and diamonds.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 7% (INR213 crores); PAT INR101 crores (3.3% margin); sustainable EBITDA 7.5%-7.8% assumes neutral gold price environment
items.quote: When we look at EBITDA in the 7% range, it is important to remember that every quarter has its own unique characteristics, particularly in the jewellery industry.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 reported 10.1% EBITDA included 1.5-2% inventory gains; adjusted PAT ~INR70-75 crores vs INR101 crores this quarter
items.quote: Q1 last year benefited from a price rise, and we clarified at the time that although the reported EBITDA margin was 10.1%, our sustainable EBITDA margin was between 7.5% and 7.8%.

items.statement: Customs duty gain estimated INR12-15 crores in Q1 (45 days impact); further benefit expected over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We estimate that the customs-duty gain in Q1 was around INR12-15 crores. This benefit will be partly offset by customer schemes, discounts and other promotional measures, but INR12-15 crores is the estimated gross range for the quarter.

items.statement: Other expenses rose from ~INR80 crores to ~INR195 crores due to store renovations, customer schemes, brand building; marketing spend declined 19%; run rate expected to subside
items.quote: I would attribute the increase in other expenses to the efforts we have made to grow the business. These include marketing-related expenses, store renovations undertaken during the lean season, and customer offers and schemes.

items.statement: Added 3 COCO stores, 4 franchise stores, 1 Sennes showroom in Q1; 12-15 more stores planned for rest of FY27, majority franchise, focus East and North India
items.quote: In terms of new stores added during the quarter, we added 3 company-owned, company-operated stores, 4 franchise stores and 1 Sennes showroom focused on lab-grown diamonds. The company remains on track to open another 12 to 15 stores during the remainder of the financial year.

items.statement: Inventory days at ~152; improved inventory turnover and reduced inventory in kg and value terms; gold-rate-based software implemented for store performance evaluation
items.quote: Inventory days are currently around 152, as stated in the presentation. We will continue to work on improving this further.

items.statement: GML availability constrained in March-April due to bank uncertainty, duty changes, geopolitical situation; procured more from local market; GML now more easily available, rebuilding portfolio
items.quote: Banks were not able to provide GML as freely, gold imports were constrained, and there was considerable uncertainty. This happened during the peak season, ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, when we needed to ensure that raw material was available.

items.statement: Average gold price +61% YoY, +1% QoQ; ASP +40% YoY, ATV +38% YoY; grammage flat on mixed-purity basis, -1% on 24-carat equivalent
items.quote: We have seen average gold prices rise by 61% year-on-year and by just 1% quarter-on-quarter. This has also been one of the drivers of value growth in sales, which has been partly led by the increase in gold prices.

items.statement: Old gold exchange accounted for 43% of total sales quantity (blended), >55% at owned stores; ready-made/traded jewellery ~20%; balance via GML or bullion vendors
items.quote: Old-gold procurement accounted for 43% on a blended basis across owned and franchise stores, while it was above 55% for our own stores. We also purchase ready-made or traded jewellery, which accounts for around 20%.

items.statement: Hedging maintained at ~50% under Board policy; intent to move toward 75-80% as volatility eases; 100% hedge idealised, practical target 75-80% with 20% buffer
items.quote: At present, we are maintaining hedging at approximately 50% because the last financial year saw extreme volatility. We need to balance liquidity risk with the risk of gold-price movements.

items.statement: Sustainable operational EBITDA margin 7.5%-7.8% assumes normalised gold price environment and appropriate hedging; reported margin varies with hedge ratio (50%, 80%, 100%)
items.quote: The 7.5%-7.8% range assumes a normalised situation in which there is no material gold-price rise or fall, and the business is appropriately hedged. In other words, it assumes a broadly neutral price environment.

items.statement: Lower-ticket-size items in greater demand; consumers buying within budgets; continuous data analysis and trend-based offerings
items.quote: Another aspect is that lower-ticket-size items were in greater demand. Consumers remained inclined to buy jewellery despite the headwinds, but they wanted products within their budgets.

items.statement: Competitive intensity and discounting after customs duty increase affected margins; old gold exchange scheme also has margin impact
items.quote: As noted in our comments, this quarter's margins were affected by the fall in gold prices, competitive intensity and discounting, partly offset by the customs-duty impact.

items.statement: PM appeal to reduce gold imports drove industry-wide old gold exchange efforts; customs duty increase benefit accruing over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Following the appeal by our Honourable Prime Minister to reduce gold imports into the country, I believe the industry collectively made strong efforts to encourage consumers to exchange their old gold.

items.statement: Quarterly margin volatility due to gold price movements, hedging (50%), inventory dynamics, discounting; shareholder concern over unpredictability vs peers
items.quote: Margins can be 13% in one quarter, 5% in another and 8% in another. I understand the hedging policies and inventory dynamics, but this degree of unpredictability appears unusual compared with other listed jewellery companies.

items.statement: Factory subsidiary supports ~100 new designs/day; Sennes Fashion and Dubai entity in start-up phase, weighed on consolidated PAT
items.quote: Of these, the factory subsidiary, which is a captive design and jewellery-supply hub, is doing very well and enables us to launch almost 100 designs per day.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations to be disclosed with H1 results; may appear negative due to lower GML borrowing (accounting optics), business generating sales and profit
items.quote: We will share cash flow from operations with the H1 results. As you would have seen last year, the accounting presentation can be affected by the level of GML. I would not call it an anomaly; it is more a matter of accounting optics.

items.statement: Q2 is planning and inventory-building quarter ahead of festive season; inventory build-up from September onward
items.quote: Q2 is the quarter in which we focus on planning and building inventory so that we are well prepared for the festive season.

items.quote: Faridabad Sector 20 is already break even, but EBITDA drag is there, right, because I think the EBITDA margins, there would be around 4% to 5%, so it will take some time to catch up to the, let's say, 20% EBITDA margin. Model town, we are expecting it to break even, somewhere around, between Q3, Q4 this year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target upwards of 24% for FY27; not targeting 28% at group level due to continuous new hospital additions
items.quote: I think upwards of 24% is what we're ta rgeting for the EBITDA margin this year, and I think going forward, yes, a percentage up or so in few years is expected, but we're not targeting a 28% EBITDA margin anytime soon, even at the consolidated group level

items.statement: Existing hospitals (Noida, Jhansi-Orchha) revenue grew 22% YoY; occupancy at Noida and Jhansi-Orchha 90%+; Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56%
items.quote: Our existing 3 hospitals in Noida and Jhansi-Orchha, collectively contributed INR2,862 million, growing 22% year-over-year. Our existing hospital occupancy reached approximately 75% as inpatient volume improved 15% year-over-year. As far as hospital-wise occupancy is concerned, Noida and Jhansi-Orchha Hospital achieved 90% plus occupancy.

items.statement: Group ARPOB all-time high INR 34,758 (up 7% YoY); Noida Extension and New Delhi crossed INR 50,000; Greater Noida INR 43,000; Faridabad Sec 20 approaching INR 40,000
items.quote: The group's ARPOB reached an all-time high of INR34,758 in quarter 1, up 7% year-on-year. Importantly, our premium NCR hospitals at Noida Extension and New Delhi crossed INR50,000 ARPOB mark for the first time in quarter 1, which is a strong indication of the improving case mix.

items.statement: Oncology contributing close to 10% of group revenue with one LINAC at Noida Extension; adding LINAC at Faridabad Sec 20 and New Delhi to strengthen oncology
items.quote: Oncology has already started contributing close to 10% to the group's revenue with only one LINAC machine currently at Noida Extension Hospital. We are in the process of adding another LINAC at our Faridabad Sector 20 hospital soon, followed by the New Delhi facility, which will meaningfully strengthen the oncology sales at the group level in the coming years.

items.statement: Government payer mix ~40% for overall company; newer hospitals <10% government business; 90%+ cash and private insurance at New Delhi and Faridabad Sec 20
items.quote: The payer mix is, government payer mix is close to 40% for the overall company for this quarter, obviously, as I said, in newer hospitals, it is close to not more than 10% of the government business there.

items.statement: ALOS fallen below 4 days for first time, driven by lower government patient share in new hospitals and shift to surgical mix
items.quote: I think it is reflecting in the overall strategy of, first, when the new hospitals are ramping up. The ALOS in those new hospitals is lower than the group ALOS we used to have earlier. But the pure fact that there is very less percentage of government pati ents in these new hospitals

items.statement: Debt increased from INR 210 cr to INR 300 cr (INR 80 cr for acquisition funding); comfortable with up to 2x trailing 12-month EBITDA
items.quote: If you see that we have a debt in our books in March of nearly around INR210 crores which is now being increased to around INR300 crores. Basically, it has increased because we have partly taken the acquisition fund from the debts around INR80 crores.

items.statement: Board approved maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value; launched ESOP Scheme 2026 for talent attraction and retention
items.quote: In recognition to the above performance, the Board today approved a maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value for all our shareholders, ensuring that shareholders benefit from the growth and investments being done by the group.

items.statement: Overall attrition ~7%; senior doctor attrition <3-4%; DNB programs helping reduce junior doctor attrition
items.quote: So, we have attrition rate of nearly 7% overall at a group level. Nitin Gupta: At the senior level I think the attrition as far as senior doctors is concerned is even lesser than this because , yes there is certain movement of doctors especially within the NCR which is happening but in terms of the total number within a unit of the hospital that's very less that moves so I think attrition within t

items.statement: In talks for one new premium asset acquisition in FY27 targeting capital cities in nearby states with high ARPOB potential
items.quote: We are in talks for certain good and premium assets with good and high ARPOB potential. We've always maintained that it's not just the geographies that we want to stay in, but also typically in the cities where we operate, we tend to have largest capacities in those cities.

items.statement: Opened Yatharth Information Center in Uzbekistan; planning 5 OPD/information centres in CIS and African countries; senior marketing person posted in Africa
items.quote: Expanding our global outreach, we opened the Yatharth Information Center in Uzbekistan and have also leveraged our partnerships with health care institutions as well as und ertook many OPD initiatives across key market s like Asia, Africa and Middle East

items.statement: No concern on panel recommendation to cap room rents at 3-star hotel rates; government has historically supported private hospitals; CGHS rates recently revised upward
items.quote: Also see, it's something not for the first time a certain recommendation has been discussed. There have been multiple incidents in the past where center or certain petitions have said to look at the room rents and the rates of the private hospitals. So far, we have always seen that government, in fact, has always supported the growth of private hospitals.

items.statement: Agra hospital at 20%+ EBITDA margin in first full quarter; revenue run rate INR 9-10 cr/month
items.quote: Our Agra Hospital, which was integrated last quarter, achieved a revenue run rate of INR9 crores to INR10 crores and delivered a strong 20% plus EBITDA within its first full quarter of integration.

items.statement: Faridabad Sec 20 monthly revenue run rate INR 12-13 cr, ARPOB ~INR 40,000 (potential INR 45,000-50,000); New Delhi run rate INR 8 cr, ARPOB ~INR 50,000
items.quote: The hospital is now contributing to a monthly revenue rate of INR 12 crores to INR 13 crores with an ARPOB closer to INR 40,000 and the potential to reach INR 45,000 to INR 50,000 as we move ahead. Our New Delhi hospital has already approached the INR50,000 ARPOB mark, positioning us among the premium hospitals in NCR. The hospital is currently operating at a monthly revenue run rate of INR 8 cror

items.statement: Gurugram hospital expected to go live Q1 FY28 with potential ARPOB INR 50,000+
items.quote: The Gurugram construction is progressing as per expectations and we expect the hospital to go live by quarter 1 of the next fiscal with a potential to achieve an ARPOB of INR50,000 plus.

items.statement: New hospitals expected to reach 25-27% EBITDA margin within 2 years (by FY29), similar to mature units
items.quote: Yes, so I think within two years from today, I think new hospitals should be even upwards of 25% of EBITDA margin, somewhere around 27%, just like our existing mature units. And we are quite confident achieving it with the performances that we've already seen from the recent quarters in these new hospitals.

items.statement: Depreciation projected at INR 20-30 cr per quarter for FY27; INR 29 cr/quarter trend; Gurugram addition will increase depreciation from FY28
items.quote: If you see around INR20 crores to INR30 crores okay and the same trend will maintain so as and when we add in the Gurugram facility the then there is a margin increase in the at a group level group, consolidate level the trend we are projecting right now is around INR29 crores for a quarter.

items.statement: Interest cost Q1 FY27 INR 6.6 cr vs INR 5 cr previous quarter; expected to remain stable as no fresh loans planned
items.quote: So, if you see, so we have reported around the interest cost of last quarter is INR5 crores. This quarter we have reported around INR6.6 crores. The same will continue as we are not going to take any fresh loan further.

items.statement: EBITDA per TEU expected around INR2,400 level going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we expect EBITDA per TEU to remain around INR2,400 level.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750 in 3-year plan including Farukhnagar ICD
items.quote: In our 3 years plan, we have targeted EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750. That's including Farukhnagar project.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain EBITDA per TEU in range of INR2,400 to INR2,500 per TEU
items.quote: We will endeavor to maintain profitability, EBITDA per TEU numbers in the range of INR2,400 to INR2,500 per TEU.

items.statement: Capex plan of close to INR400 crores over 3-year Plan 2030
items.quote: So overall, there is a requirement of close to INR400 crores of capex.

items.statement: INR100 crores capex to be incurred in FY27
items.quote: Close to INR100 crores of that capex we should incur in the current financial year, '26-27.

items.statement: Capex funding: INR200 crores from accruals, INR90 crores from equity raised, INR100-150 crores debt
items.quote: So INR200 crores would come from my INR200 crores would come from the existing accruals. As I told you, close to INR90 crores would be used out of the equity, which we have already raised in the past. And the debt requirement would be in the range of INR100 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Annual handling capacity increased ~20% to ~1.03 million TEUs in FY26
items.quote: Over last year, which is FY26, we increased our annual handling capacity by nearly 20% to approximately 1.03 million TEUs.

items.statement: Speedy JNPT expansion adds ~60,000 TEUs annual capacity, work starts post-monsoon
items.quote: This will add approximately 60,000 TEUs of annual handling capacity for us in Speedy JNPT, which is the closest facility to the port in Nhava Sheva.

items.statement: Farukhnagar PFT completion by March 2027, ICD by Q3 FY28 (Oct-Dec 2027)
items.quote: The PFT portion should get completed by February, March '27, and the ICD portion should get completed by Q3, which is October, November, December '27.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved from 60-65% to 80-85% over 3-3.5 years
items.quote: But the capacity utilization from a 60%- 65% ;3-3.5 years back, hovers at a healthy 80% to 85% at this point in time.

items.statement: EBITDA per TEU improved to INR2,690 (corrected to INR2,898) in Q1 FY27 from INR2,400 level
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income, for Q1 FY27 stood at INR47 crores as compared to INR35 crores for Q1 FY26 and INR44 crores for Q4 FY26. This implies an EBITDA per TEU of INR 2,690 for Q1 FY27. * Refer Footnote

items.statement: Revenue per TEU increased from INR11,000-11,500 to INR13,000 over a year
items.quote: In terms of pricing, if you see, I think a year back, we were hovering around INR11,000 to INR11,500 per TEU. Now that is something which we have been able to push at INR13,000 per TEU in the current financial quarter.

items.statement: Container volumes grew 7% YoY in Q1 FY27 to 176,499 TEUs
items.quote: Our container volumes grew 7% year -on-year, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our customer relationships.

items.statement: Higher share of transhipment containers and upward rate revisions drove profitability improvement
items.quote: The improvement in profitability came on the back of operational efficiencies supported by technology improvements and by higher share of transhipment containers volume plus upward rate revisions at various locations.

items.statement: Allcargo Group contributes 10-12% of revenue at similar margins to third-party customers
items.quote: It comprises close to 10% to 12% of my overall revenue and margins are on a similar level as we get it from our third -party customers.

items.statement: Pranav Choudhary appointed MD Designate, takes charge Sept 1, 2026; Suresh Kumar superannuates end of month
items.quote: I'm very happy to share with you that we have a new Managing Director Designatie, which is Pranav Choudhary, who comes in from Adani Ports. That was his allcargo last assignment. He was the Chief Executive. He will take over the reins from me as I superannuate and step down from my role of Managing Director by the end of this month. So Pranav will

items.statement: JNPA Speedy CFS contract renewed for 10 years under SAMO model
items.quote: The earlier contract was for 20 years, which got over in 2025, and we have now been able to successf ully get the 10 -year extension for that.

items.statement: Rail coefficient at Mundra among highest in country; JNPA catchment 200-250 km radius
items.quote: Mundra, you can look at it that way, rail coefficient being high in Mundra, one of the highest in the country. JNPA, there is a scope for rail coefficient to become better. Largely, the JNPA allcargo CFS has catered to a 200 -250 kilometer radius

items.statement: Farukhnagar terminal volume mix projected at 20-25% domestic, 75-80% EXIM
items.quote: In our business estimate and projections that we have, the volumes that this terminal will handle will be in the range of 20% to 25% domestic and about 75% to 80% EXIM.

items.statement: No dividend planned currently; prioritizing capex and growth investments
items.quote: As of now, because considering the plans which we are having, we are staying away from declaring dividend at this point of time.

items.statement: Debt requirement of INR100-150 crores tied up with banks for capex funding
items.quote: There could be a certain debt requirement in the range of INR100 crores to INR150 crores for which we have already tied up with various banks and that they could be raised at respective point of time.

items.statement: Raised INR120 crores equity; INR25 crores called, INR90 crores to be called for capex
items.quote: Recently, we have raised an equity of INR120 crores. Out of that, INR25 crores we have already called and close to INR90 crores is yet to be called.

items.statement: Tax rate expected at 25% under concessional tax regime going forward
items.quote: Going forward, tax rate is expected to remain at 25% as we have moved to concessional tax regime from now onwards.

items.statement: Mundra expansion decision pending on landlord license extension discussions till 2030-31
items.quote: Depending upon what happens to the extension discussions with the landlord there, we will take a call whether to continue with the same or build a larger facility outside. So that's a call that we will take during the year.

items.statement: Nepal JV contributes 2-3% of overall profitability/revenue; operates 1 ICD and 3 ICPs
items.quote: This contributes at best about 2% to 3% of the overall profitability revenue that we have.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target ~15% and EBITDA margin upwards of 10%
items.quote: For financial year 27, our objective remains to deliver approximately 15% revenue growth and EBITDA margins on upwards of 10%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 11-12% for FY27
items.quote: Our target this year is to achieve 11 -12%, more than 10%. so that we can focus more on the coming years.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization target 70-75% by year end
items.quote: Overall, it will be around 70-75%.

items.statement: WADA facility utilization expected to reach 80% during FY27
items.quote: We expect it to reach 80% during this year.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at Rs 20-25 crore primarily for Kutch expansion
items.quote: We have also maintained a disciplined approach to capital allocation with FY27 Capex planned at approximately 20 to 25 crore, primarily towards K utch expansion and deployed in line with actual.

items.statement: Kutch new facility investment Rs 20-25 crore for 10,000 IBC units/month, commissioning by March 2027
items.quote: We are investing approximately 20 to 25 crore in a new facility with a capacity of 10,000 IBC units per month, which is expected to be commissioned by March 2027.

items.statement: Installed capacity 20,936 MT/quarter; Q1 FY27 utilization 62%
items.quote: So today we have an installed capacity of 20,936 metric tons per quarter, while volumes stood at 1,292 metric tons, translating into a capacity utilization of around 62%.

items.statement: WADA facility operating above 70% utilization, contributed Rs 43 crore (19% of revenue) in Q1 FY27
items.quote: our WADA facility is in full swing now across HDPE, IBCs, and MS Drums, and is already operating above 70% utilization. We expect it to reach 80% during this year. The facility contributed approximately 43 crore or 19% of revenue from operations in this quarter

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased to Rs 16,380 in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 11,252 in Q1 FY26 and Rs 15,053 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA per ton increased to approximately 16 ,380 in Q 1 FY26 compared with 11 ,252 in Q1 FY26 and 15 ,053 in Q4FY26.

items.statement: Gross margin compressed to 23% in Q1 FY27 as raw material costs rose with price increases; HDPE gross margin in rupee terms stable
items.quote: Gross profit rose 19% year -on-basis, but gross margin compressed a little to 23% as raw material costs rose in step with price increase. Importantly, gross margin in rupees terms for HDPE remained stable.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 50% YoY with margins at 10% in Q1 FY27; PAT grew 32% YoY to Rs 10.5 crore at 5% margin
items.quote: EBITDA grew 50% year-on-year basis with margins at 10%, reflecting the operating leverage kicking in as the total expenses rose only modestly despite new plant commissioning. PAT grew by 32% year-on-basis to 10.5 crore with margins at 5%.

items.statement: Raw material price expected to fall Rs 20/kg in next 2-3 months from current Rs 160 to Rs 140, then stabilize near old rates
items.quote: Sir, I think in the next 2 -3 months, it will go down by Rs. 20. In the next 3 -4 months, we will be selling at a rate of Rs.140 from the current 160. And after that, it will come at par with the old rated, or 10 rupees higher than that.

items.statement: HDPE polymer drum tonnage down 4% YoY; IBC volumes hit by export demand; MS drums growth strong
items.quote: HDPE polymer drum tonnage was down 4% year on year and I BC volumes were little hit as export demand suffered due to the war. This was partly offset by strong MS drums growth.

items.statement: New product line in testing phase; machine added, customer trials ongoing, 2-3 months for approvals
items.quote: Its in the testing phase, but the machine has been added, the marketing is still on. Jai Prakash Agrawal Customer has taken some. They will send it to their customer. It’s a 2 -3 months process, until we get approval from there, we can’t do anything

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% year-on-year
items.quote: Despite the prevailing geopolitical uncertainty and the challenges arising from West Asia situation, we remain confident in the underlying demand environment and reiterate our FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin of 17% to 18% for the year as cost pressures ease
items.quote: And we expect to target an EBITDA margin of 17% to 18% for the year.

items.statement: Incurred INR43.42 crores capex in Q1 FY27, including INR33.25 crores for Valsad factory building
items.quote: During Q1, the company incurred a total capital expenditure of INR43.42 crores, of which INR33.25 crores was capitalized towards the factory building in Valsad facility.

items.statement: Planning INR15 crores investment for new steel bottle manufacturing line
items.quote: We have taken a call that to increase the capacity by 35%, where we will be investing in one more state-of-the-art automatic line of Steel Bottles, where we would be investing about INR15 crores.

items.statement: Fourth steel bottle manufacturing line ordered, commissioning expected by Q4 FY27, adding 30-35% capacity
items.quote: The new line is expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY27 and increasing our manufacturing capacity by approximately 30 to 35 percentage.

items.statement: Current steel bottle capacity utilization at 65%, new line expected to generate INR30-35 crores revenue
items.quote: currently, so if you look at Stee l Bottles, currently, the capacity utilization is about 65% and going forward, historically also, whenever we cross 65%, 75%, we tend to invest in the new expansion

items.statement: Valsad plant to be fully operational by end of Q2 FY27, will serve both Writing Instruments and Creative segments
items.quote: By end of next quarter is when we have the entire capacity in place. The building has been capitalized so far. It is built, but the machineries and mould, etcetera, are yet to be installed.

items.statement: Creative and Steel Bottles contributed 31% of revenue in FY26, expected to reach 35-38% in FY27
items.quote: Together, these businesses contributed approximately 31% of the company's total revenue in FY26 and both continue to witness strong momentum. With the planned capacity expansion in Steel Bottles and continued scaling up of the Creative Product business, we expect the combined contribution to increase to approximately 35% to 38% of overall company revenue in FY27.

items.statement: Domestic demand growing across key categories despite geopolitical challenges
items.quote: We are seeing increase in demand of our products in the domestic market with growth across key categories despite challenging arising from the prevailing geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Pen segment grew 9% YoY driven by volume growth and back-to-school season demand
items.quote: Our core Pen segment delivered 9% year-on-year growth with demand remaining positive during the back-to-school season.

items.statement: Creative segment grew 23% YoY, impacted by raw material costs in some categories
items.quote: The Creative segment witnessed a growth of 23% Y-o-Y to INR80 crores as compared to INR65 crores in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Steel Bottles and Houseware grew 54.3% YoY to INR19 crores
items.quote: Our Steel Bottles and Houseware business grew by 54.3% year-on-year to INR19 crores compared to INR13 crores in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Gross margin at 50%, down 31 bps YoY due to geopolitical uncertainties and elevated costs
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR158.6 crores, up 10% year-on-year, with gross margin at 50%, broadly in line with historical levels with a modest 31 basis point year-on- year decline, which is driven by geopol itical uncertainties and an elevated cost environment across the industry

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 16.7%, down 46 bps YoY due to volatile raw material costs
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR53.3 crores, growing 7.7% year-on-year, while EBITDA margin stood at 16.7%, a 46 bps decline year-on-year.

items.statement: Implemented price increases, rationalized schemes and discounts to protect margins
items.quote: We have also taken proactive measures to protect margins, including rationalizing schemes and discounts and implementing selective price increases across all our three segments of businesses.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased 10-15%, company took ~10% price hikes in household categories
items.quote: A total of the price hike has been price increase in the raw materials have been to the tune of 10% to 15%. But our price hike here, we are talking of 10% plus/minus in household.

items.statement: Launched 32 new products in Q1 FY27 across Pens, Creative and Steel Bottles
items.quote: During the quarter, we introduced 32 new products across categories, further expanding our product portfolio.

items.statement: Focus on premiumization and higher-value formats in Pens, expanding Steel Bottles portfolio across channels
items.quote: We will continue to deepen our pencil portfolio, introduce higher-value formats in Pens and expand our Steel Bottles and Houseware portfolio across channels.

items.statement: Domestic OEM business fully phased out, export OEM impacted by West Asia crisis, OEM now ~5% of business
items.quote: Overall, if you look at the OEM business, it is hardly contributing to about 5% of our overall business.

items.statement: Creative distribution focused on existing 68,000 outlets, increasing throughput rather than adding outlets
items.quote: Current year also, we are focusing mainly - to cater to those 68,000 only and to increase the throughput and increase the sales in the existing outlets only.

items.statement: Exports flat YoY at INR43 crores due to West Asia disruptions, but seeing positive growth in other geographies
items.quote: Exports stood at INR43 crores and remained broadly flat year-on-year, primarily due to disruptions in the West Asia, resulting in longer transit times and higher freight costs during the quarter.

items.statement: Working capital improved by 6 days YoY, expect further 10 days improvement by end of FY27
items.quote: We expect to streamline inventory levels as the West Asia crisis stabilizes with an anticipated improvement of approximately 10 days in our entire working capital cycle levels.

items.statement: Company is zero debt, all internal accruals used for expansion and shareholders
items.quote: We are a zero debt company and all the internal accruals are for future expansion and for the shareholders.

items.statement: Pen market share at 18% per CRISIL report, confident of maintaining leadership despite competitor acquiring Reynolds brand
items.quote: So currently, the market share as per the CRISIL report, last CRISIL report, in writing instruments, we have a market share of 18%.

items.statement: Added ~250 sales people in last 2 years, manufacturing headcount also increased with capacity expansion
items.quote: And as well as sales side also, we have increased around 250 people in sales in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in West Asia causing raw material cost volatility, supply chain disruptions, and export challenges
items.quote: All these were primarily due to geopolitical situation in West Asia with sharp increase in raw material prices.

items.statement: Marketing spend guided at 8% to 10% of revenue for FY27
items.quote: Marketing investment during the quarter was approximately 8.5% of revenue, which is in line with our full year guidance of 8% to 10% through FY27.

items.statement: Consumer interest healthy in April and early May then moderated mid-May; near-term demand visibility uneven
items.quote: We saw healthy consumer interest through April and part of May which moderated towards the mid of May.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 61.6%, EBITDA margin 21.2%, PAT margin 1.8%
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR77.2 crores with a GP margin of 61.6% for the quarter. EBITDA stood at INR26.6 crores. Our EBITDA margin stood at 21.2%.

items.statement: Focus on improving quality and productivity of network by replacing lower productivity locations with experience-led stores
items.quote: Our focus is on improving the quality and productivity of our network by progressively replacing lower productivity locations with stronger experience-led stores, thereby improving output per store while enhancing customer experience and brand salience.

items.statement: Premiumization involves change in merchandise mix, not larger inventory base
items.quote: In fact, we are looking to sharpen our inventory, and it will not be a larger inventory base. It's just going to be a change in the merchandise mix.

items.statement: Strategy targets both retaining existing customers and acquiring new younger customer base
items.quote: So it's both. We intend to do both. See, as a brand to remain healthy and sustainable through its growth journey, what we need to do is we need to retain our customers and we need to acquire new customers.

items.statement: Competition intense, some competitors spend 15%+ on advertising vs Mufti's 8-10%
items.quote: The competition, etcetera, is very intense at this time. And in fact, some of them even spend more than 8% to 10% in terms of advertising. They spend close to 15% and even higher.

items.statement: Inventory days at 74 in Q1, some reduction expected but cyclical; no inventory write-offs historically
items.quote: So Jay, there should be some reduction in the inventory days. That is always the endeavour to.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: And see what we're looking to do this year, we are looking to increase the same-store revenue in the mid-single-digit numbers.

items.statement: Near-term demand visibility uneven, geopolitical tensions keeping consumers cautious, unable to extrapolate growth numbers for next couple of years
items.quote: For the next 2-odd years, it's going to be very difficult for us to say what exactly the numbers will pan out.

items.statement: Industry AC growth expected around 20% in FY27; EPACK aims to surpass industry growth and grow non-AC categories faster
items.quote: For AC, we are very confident that this year, the industry is expected to grow at around 20%. So we would definitely surpass the industry growth as we have done it in Q1.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex ~INR10 cr; total FY26-27 capex budget INR450 cr, of which INR340-350 cr booked, INR40-45 cr in CWIP, balance INR60-70 cr for rest of year
items.quote: Out of a total budget of INR450-odd crores, which we announced in the beginning of FY26, out of which INR340 crores to INR350 crores is something which is already booked. An additional INR10 crores of capex has been booked in the last quarter, Q1 of FY27 and almost INR40 crores to INR45 crores is something which is in CWIP. So we are estimating a total additional capex of around INR60 crores to IN

items.statement: Q1 FY27 utilisation: Dehradun & Bhiwadi ~90%, Sri City ~50%; FY27 target average utilisation >60% across all three plants
items.quote: So we are looking at overall utilization of all 3 plants put together at more than 60%.

items.statement: Robust order book driving Sri City ramp-up; non-AC categories (SDA, LDA, components) scaling with new customer additions and product pipeline
items.quote: The company with its current robust order book is very confident that the utilizations going forward, especially for Sri City, where there has been a concern over the last few quarters, improving significantly.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 6.21% reported; underlying ex-PLI ~6.4% in Q1 FY26 vs 6.21% now, a ~15 bps YoY improvement
items.quote: If you s trip that INR13.3 crores out of both the revenue and EBITDA base for financial year 2026, last year, underlying EBITDA margin was closer to 6.4% and not 8.24%. On a like -to- like basis, our year-on-year margin improvement this quarter is closer to 15 basis points and not 203

items.statement: Commodity price increases passed on quarterly with a lag; forex loss of INR6-7 cr in Q1 was key margin headwind; minimal residual commodity pass-through pending
items.quote: What impacted us most for the last quarter was especially the forex exchange rate. So that is 1 line item we'd like to flag, which like the forex loss is something which has impacted us largely.

items.statement: Customer base expanded to 73 (from 72) and 19 product categories (from 18); 3 new categories added in Q1, 4 more in pipeline; target 75 customers and 20 product lines by year-end
items.quote: Currently, at this time, we have closer to 73 customers and 19 product lines already productionized and 2, 3 more lines are for which PP has -- or the pilot production has already been done. So by end of this year, we are looking to have closer to 75 customers and 20 product lines.

items.statement: Working capital days ~50-60; inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO changes but now at comfortable levels; focus on normalising inventory to reduce finance cost
items.quote: Generally, with respect to the cash-to-cash cycle, we have the working capital days around 50 to 60, depending on the season of the company.
