items.statement: Logistics EBITDA ~INR1,000 per ton; sourcing EBITDA ~$85-90 per ton (low contributor)
items.quote: If you come to LPG EBITDA, it's very standard that the throughput or the logistics volumes that we do delivers close to INR1,000 EBITDA. And then what is left, you divide it by the distribution margin, leave out sourcing, sourcing hardly matters as far as EBITDA is concerned, it is a very low contributor.

items.statement: VLGC compliance at ports enables freight cost savings: VLGC freight ~$15 vs medium gas carrier ~$50, saving ~$35 per ton translating to ~INR3,000 margin top-up
items.quote: So instead of getting it on a medium gas carrier, which has probably a freight of $50, we would get it on a very large gas carrier, which has a freight of, let's say, $15. So this $35 odd, I mean, I'm just quoting approximate numbers, please don't take me on that. But then that gives you that top-up of another INR3,000.

items.statement: Added multiple private sector customers in gas distribution; 15-year take-or-pay agreement with leading conglomerate for petroleum products at Pipavav rail gantry (>0.5 MMTPA); 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc for ammonia t
items.quote: have already secured a 15-year take-or- pay agreement with a leading conglomerate for petroleum products. The committed volumes under this agreement exceed 0.5 million metric tons per annum with operations expected to commence by the end of the year

items.statement: ITOCHU Corporation acquired 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited, representatives joined Board, intends to increase stake to 25% over 3 years
items.quote: And the attractiveness of this opportunity is also reflected in the confidence shown by our strategic partner, ITOCHU Corporation, which has acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited. And ITOCHU has -- representatives have joined the Board with a long-term -- have come on board, sorry, with a long-term strategic vision and has -- they have expressed their intention to increase their s

items.statement: Signed nonbinding MoU with Larsen & Toubro for potential joint development of ammonia terminals at Kandla Port
items.quote: We have signed a nonbinding memorandum of understanding with Larsen & Toubro for potential joint development of ammonia terminals, which positions us well in the energy transition opportunity at Kandla Port.

items.statement: Targeting 2 million tons LPG distribution volume in coming years; logistics volume growth benchmark 25% YoY with potential step-up from enablers; EPS CAGR 25%+ sustained from INR26 base
items.quote: We have always had aim to reach 2 million tons in distribution in coming times ahead. And that's not because of the war, but because of the infrastructure layout that we are executing in LPG business.

items.statement: Liquid segment EBITDA per CBM derived by dividing EBITDA by 2 million CBM capacity
items.quote: You divide the EBITDA by the capacity that we have, 2 million, you will get the per CBM EBITDA margin as far as liquid is concerned, right?

items.statement: Targeting gearing ratio ~0.6; funding capex through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt; fortress balance sheet with INR5,940 crores liquidity reserves on consolidated basis
items.quote: We'll pursue this growth with disciplined funding through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6. Low leverage, strong cash generation and a resilient fortress balance sheet gives us the financial flexibility to move quickly on opportunities.

items.statement: Aegis Vopak self-funded via equity dilution agreed; equity infusion enables additional borrowing capacity for $5 billion capex journey
items.quote: Aegis Vopak is self-funded. Aegis Vopak has its own funding, which is by equity. We have already agreed to dilute so that the funding happens so that the capex happens. And of course, when the equity comes in, you are also then eligible to borrow more. And then you do your journey of $5 billion.

items.statement: Not driven by greed or trading positions; focus on month-on-month distribution not inventory gains; avoid positions like global traders (Trafigura, Glencore, Vitol)
items.quote: We don't want to be driven by greed. We don't want to become traders. We can fill up the tanks and try and sell them, but it's an industry which is very volatile. We can't take positions where if you are left footed, then you end up really taking a big fall. So we are distributors.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal at Pipavav commissioned with 36,000 MT static storage; industrial distribution starting within weeks; margins not disclosed yet; ITOCHU 10% stake with intent to increase to 25%
items.quote: I'm really pleased to announce the commissioning of our specialized ammonia storage and terminaling facility at Pipavav Port with a static storage capacity of 36,000 metric tons. This marks a significant milestone in our infrastructure expansion journey.

items.statement: CPG quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: In terms of a quarterly breakeven for this business, we are working towards another 4 or 5 quarters. We should have a quarterly breakeven on this business.

items.statement: Nutra steady-state EBITDA margin 12-15%
items.quote: From an EBITDA margin perspective, steady state is likely between 12% and 15%.

items.statement: Nutra to achieve highest ever revenue this year
items.quote: I will say that we are pe rhaps going to do this year our highest ever revenue in Nutra, and I think consequently EBITDA will also be

items.statement: Jaggery plant commissioning in 6 months in Karnataka, will more than double capacity
items.quote: The plant will be commissioned in 6 months' time. It is coming up in Karnataka. It will more than double our current jaggery capacity.

items.statement: Jaggery turnover target ~Rs 100 cr from both plants
items.quote: once we have both plants running, we should be able to do closer to Rs. 100 crores in terms of turnover, just from both of these plants

items.statement: Sugar prices moved above Rs 45-46/kg, may correct once crushing starts
items.quote: In the current month, sugar prices have moved well north of Rs. 45-Rs.46 per kg. We will need to wait and see if these hold. Perhaps once crushing starts, it is very likely that there may be some correction.

items.statement: TN/AP crushing flat to 5% lower in SY2026-27; Karnataka key for makeup
items.quote: In the current year, yes, probably there is going to be a flat or about a 5% drop in these geographies.

items.statement: TN sugarcane incentive is direct benefit transfer to farmers, no working capital impact
items.quote: There is no impact on working capital. There is a direct benefit transfer from the government to the farmer account. We play a facilitating role.

items.statement: Ethanol vs sugar mix evaluated constantly to maximize margins; committed OMC volumes limit switching
items.quote: We evaluate our options of producing ethanol, ENA and sugar, from which feedstock is a constant review mechanism where we have, and we try to maximize our margins. But there is a base volume of sugar we should produce to take care of our customers.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity 582 KLPD (~18 cr litres/yr), including 120 KLPD grain
items.quote: 582 KLPD is our capacity, which is roughly about Rs. 18 crore liters, out of which about 120 KLPD is our grain capacity.

items.statement: Standalone debt 30 Jun: short-term ~Rs 980 cr, long-term ~Rs 150 cr
items.value: Rs. 980 crores short-term, Rs. 150 crores long-term
items.quote: 30 th June, about Rs. 980 crores as far as the short-term debt is concerned, Rajesh, about Rs. 150 crores on account of long-term.

items.statement: Short-term debt seasonal: was Rs 1,250 cr at 31 Mar, down to Rs 980 cr, will rise when crushing starts
items.quote: even if you look at it as on 31 st March, our short-term debt was about Rs. 1,250 crores. So now it has come down to Rs. 980 crores. So once the crushing starts, then because it is in quarter 2 also, then further it will reduce. Once the crushing starts, it will go up.

items.statement: PSRIPL closure: Rs 610 cr infused, Rs 55 cr loan given in Q1, Rs 65 cr more may be needed over time
items.value: Rs. 610 crores infused, Rs. 55 crores loan given, Rs. 65 crores left
items.quote: Rs. 610 crores is already done. That is there in the public, Rajesh. Rs. 610 crores is already there. Over and above, we have also given Rs. 55 crores loan. Total Rs. 665 crores which we have infused during the current quarter to settle all the bank liabilities.

items.statement: Employee cost up due to VSS at legacy plants; more VSS planned, not due to CPG hiring
items.quote: Rajesh, they have gone up because of VSS which we have done. A lot of our legacy plants we are offering VSS. You will see more of that. This is being done with a longer term interest in mind. And overall bringing the fixed cost position down.

items.statement: Focus on efficient working capital, leverage debt cost, improve current ratio, monetize non-performing assets
items.quote: As far as the financial KPIs are concerned, we are more looking at efficient working capital. And, we are working on how we leverage the debt cost. Also, as of date, we have about Rs. 150 crores of long-term debt, about Rs. 800-Rs. 900 crores of the short-term debt. We are also closely working towards the monetization of all non-performing assets or something to bring the cash pool into the busine

items.statement: CPG revenue recalibrated lower intentionally; margin pool grown via value-added mix, new products, distribution expansion
items.quote: Yes, the CPG division revenue has fallen significantly. This has been on account of a recalibration of the model. So this is intentional. Our contribution margin pool, the absolute margin pool, however, has grown very well as we have focused on more margin accretive products and a margin accretive operating model into the market.

items.statement: Sugar inventory 1.16 LMT valued at ~Rs 41.50/kg
items.quote: 1.16 LMT Gautam. We are valuing at about Rs. 41.50.

items.statement: Nutra India business ~20% of consolidated turnover; certification issues in Europe resolved
items.quote: The India business is only about 20% odd of the consolidated Nutra turnover, but we had some certification issues in Europe, not entirely our fault. In the past, those have been resolved.

items.statement: JLR Q1 results not inconsistent with full-year guidance; no change implied
items.quote: It should be recognized our first quarter results are typically our weakest in cash, in particular suffers from a seasonal working capital swing. So, the results was weaker than we would have liked, are not inconsistent with our full year guidance.

items.statement: JLR targets 10% revenue growth per annum with significant focus on US market
items.quote: So we are setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum and focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.

items.statement: JLR intends to save $1.7 billion on ex-works cost, warranty and fixed cost base
items.quote: On costs, our focus is the ex-works cost of our cars, warranty, and our fixed cost base. And our intent is to save $1.7 billion in this space.

items.statement: TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27, aiming to maintain 2x industry growth pace
items.quote: We would like to keep that kind of momentum going forward. So, I would definitely be targeting higher double-digit growths in FY 27.

items.statement: TMPV expects Q2 margins flattish vs Q1 despite 3% commodity hit, offset by price hikes, cost reductions and no IPL impact
items.quote: Net-net, in Q2, despite the 3% commodity hit, we are expecting margins to be f lattish with respect to Q1

items.statement: India PV industry volumes crossed 1.3 million units in Q1 FY27, up 24% YoY on low base; growth to moderate in H2
items.quote: The Passenger Vehicle industry remained on a strong footing during the quarter with volumes crossing 1.3 million units, which was supported by a healthy demand environment following the GST 2.0.

items.statement: EV industry grew 77% YoY in Q1, penetration reached 8% in June 2026; EVs and CNG together 31% of industry sales
items.quote: In particular, EVs remain the fastest growing segment in the industry, registering 77% year-on-year growth. EV penetration continues to increase every month, as the industry exited the quarter with 8% penetration in June 26.

items.statement: TMPV wholesale volumes grew 46% YoY to ~182,000 units in Q1, nearly twice industry pace; market share up 200 bps to 14.3%
items.quote: We delivered overall wholesale volumes of about 182,000 units, which was a year-on-year growth of 46%, nearly twice the pace of the broader industry growth.

items.statement: TMPV EV volumes doubled YoY to over 34,000 units in Q1; June/July exit rate 15,000/month; EV mix 19% in Q1, 23-24% in June/July
items.quote: We delivered our highest-ever volumes of over 34,000 units in the quarter and sustained market leadership position. Now, roughly 20% of our sales came from EVs in quarter one. Actually, in July, it went up to 24%.

items.statement: TMPV has strong EV order book; bookings up ~3.5x vs pre-Mid-East crisis average; production ramping from 9k to 15k/month
items.quote: If I compare with actually the pre-Mid-East crisis, which was Jan, Feb, whatever the average bookings that we used to get, that has gone nearly 3.5x of that.

items.statement: TMPV EV market share rose from 37% to 43% in last year; expects to protect or increase share despite intensifying competition
items.quote: If you would have seen in the last one year, actually, we have increased our market share from 37% to actually last month it was 43%.

items.statement: TMPV India EBITDA margins flat at 4% YoY; 2% material cost reduction and fixed cost leverage offset by 6% commodity impact
items.quote: While margins have remained f lat at around 4%, we had significant gains coming from fixed cost leverage and another 2% material cost reductions, but it was entirely offset by 6% commodity impact we saw on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: JLR EBIT margin 2.8% in Q1; VME rose to 7.1% driven by China luxury taxes and US market conditions
items.quote: VME in the second big column is significantly higher. It's now at 7.1%. China is the most difficult market year-over-year for us given economic and retailer stress and also the effect of the new luxury taxes that came into force after Q1 last year.

items.statement: TMPV took cumulative 1% price increase in April and July (0.5% each); will take further calibrated increases through the year
items.quote: We have already taken a 1% cumulative price increase across April and July and while we will be taking calibrated increases through the rest of the year, a large part of the set off for commodities will have to come through accelerated commercial reductions.

items.statement: JLR expects new BEVs to be at least margin neutral vs ICE models; pricing Range Rover EVs at no discount
items.quote: We expect to price them to be at least margin neutral. And if you think of the EMA cars, these are the smaller cars of which Range Rover GT is one. They are replacing vehicles which are at the end of their life and relatively low in terms of margin.

items.statement: JLR key commodity exposures are aluminum, palladium, copper; aluminum fell from $3,500 to $3,150/ton in Q1; hedging program in place
items.quote: Aluminum prices came off, they were about $3,500 a ton at the end of March. They were about $3,150 a ton at the end of June. So although they remain high, during the quarter, some of our key commodities came down in price.

items.statement: TMPV commodity impact 4.5% in Q1; expects additional 3% hardening in Q2; accelerated cost reductions underway
items.quote: The commodity impact in Q1 was 4.5% and we are expecting another 3% plus residual impact to f low into Q2

items.statement: JLR Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender now 81% of sales; average sale price rising, targeting >GBP 80k in 18 months
items.quote: Volume and mix actually wasn't too bad given the wholesale drop, as we balanced more into Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender, which are now 81% of our sales.

items.statement: JLR launching 4 BEVs imminently: Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric, Range Rover GT, Jaguar Type 01; 2 more in pipeline
items.quote: Four imminent launches, two more in the way. The four below in the last stages of testing or in pre-build down the production lines. Range Rover and Range Rover Sport Electric come later this year. The radical Range Rover GT, which is bottom left, and Jaguar Type 01 early next year.

items.statement: TMPV launched Tiago ICE facelift, Tiago.ev facelift, Sierra.ev in Q1; Curvv and other refreshes under certification for PLI from Q3
items.quote: We launched the Tiago ICE Facelift in May, which enhanced the styling and tech quotient, ensuring greater aspiration for the hatch segment. And in EVs, we launched the Tia go.ev facelift, which strengthened the value proposition in the EV entry segment, and also launched the all-new Sierra.ev to further expand our portfolio in a key high-growth space

items.statement: TMPV capex Rs. 1,300 Cr in Q1; will step up for next growth phase per Investor Day guidance
items.quote: Our Capex at Rs. 1,300 Cr for the quarter, this is still tracking last year's trends, but we will see it step-up as we execute our next phase of growth in line with our Investor Day guidance.

items.statement: JLR investment levels remain high near peak cycle; capitalization 74% in Q1; spend shifting from engineering to capital as facilities come online
items.quote: With six vehicle launches approaching, four imminently and two in the pipeline, our investment levels remain high, as do our capitalization levels, which was 74% in the quarter.

items.statement: TMPV monthly production run rate scaled to >60,000; targeting 65,000-70,000/month; supply constraints easing from October
items.quote: So hopefully, from this month, we will be seeing 65,000 plus production, more closer to 70,000 is what we are targeting for. But in the coming months, it should be more closer to 70,000 is what we are trying to achieve.

items.statement: TMPV EV production ramped from 9,000 to 15,000/month; further increases planned to close demand-supply gap
items.quote: 3-4 months back, we were doing about 9,000 a month production, now we have, last month we crossed 15,000. And hopefully, in the coming months, this should further increase.

items.statement: JLR Q1 free cash flow pre-working capital negative GBP 352M; post-working capital negative ~GBP 1B; working capital build-up to reverse through year
items.quote: capital reflecting a naturally high production and low sales quarter has built-up, though should largely reverse out through the year. For reference, Q4 last year, working capital was GBP 814 million favorable. In the quarter post-working capital, our free cash f low was just under GBP 1 billion negative

items.statement: TMPV dealer inventory at ~30 days; building stock ahead of festive season; FCF Rs. 1,100 Cr in Q1 aided by working capital releases
items.quote: Inventory levels are right now around 30 days. We had an increase last month, as we were able to produce slightly more. Now, we have to significantly increase the inventory because these are not at comfortable levels ahead of the festive period.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt Rs. 42,000 Cr; India business net cash positive; JLR net debt GBP 3.6 billion; JLR on negative watch at investment grade border
items.quote: Consolidated net debt stood at Rs.42,000 Cr at the end of the quarter. India business continues to remain net cash positive, while net debt at JLR was GBP 3.6 billion.

items.statement: JLR hedge book ~1.28 GBP/USD; prefers weak sterling (1.20s) as exporter; Stellantis MoU to create natural USD hedge
items.quote: I don't actually think I've ever said our hedge book is around 1.28. But to be entirely honest, you're not that far wrong. Look, we prefer a weak sterling environment as an exporter.

items.statement: TMPV exports grew 4x in FY26 on low base; targeting ~2x growth in FY27; South Africa market opened last year
items.quote: Last financial year, we grew by 4x on a low base of course, but this year, we are targeting more closer to 2x growth of what we did last year.

items.statement: JLR MoU with Stellantis for US production of Defender-branded vehicles; targeting definitive agreement by year-end
items.quote: We signed an MoU a couple of months ago. We are aiming to get that to a formal and definitive agreement by the end of the year.

items.statement: TMPV PLI certifications for Tiago.ev, Punch.ev, Sierra.ev, Curvv under process; expect accruals from Q3, full portfolio by Q4
items.quote: All the other refreshes and the new launches including Tiago.ev, Punch.ev, Sierra.ev are under fresh certifications. Shailesh Chandra Curvv as well. Dhiman Gupta And Curvv. And we expect that we will be getting the PLI certifications as well as the TCA and start accruing the PLIs from Q3. And by Q4, almost our entire portfolio should be PLI accredited

items.statement: JLR China outlook worsening before stabilizing; retailer overcapacity, economic slowdown, retrospective luxury taxes adding pressure
items.quote: I think the reality of China market at the moment where the economy is not growing at the pace that they are used to, and the retailers are suffering industry-wide from large overcapacity of domestic manufacturers, means that China is very unlikely to get any easier for us. It is most probably going to get a little bit worse before it stabilizes.

items.statement: TMPV supply chain constraints persist in select areas; commodity inflation stress across key inputs; sustained mitigation actions needed
items.quote: Supply chain constraints persists in select areas and commodity inflation continues to be a stress point across several key inputs and Dhiman already mentioned about the Q1 impact and what potentially we can see in Q2. These remain important areas of focus for the industry and sustained actions will be required to mitigate their impact.

items.statement: Management expects revenue growth momentum to continue for the next three to four quarters but declines to provide a specific number.
items.quote: I would not put any number, but this growth momentum would continue for coming quarters, three to four quarters, which we have seen in first quarter also.

items.statement: Volume growth was 6-7% YoY in Q1 FY27; the remainder of the 18.4% revenue growth came from higher freight rates driven by geopolitical volatility.
items.quote: If you see the number of shipment, the shipment growth is around 6% to 7% as compared to last year. And rest of the growth has been happen from the freight rates.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 275 bps YoY to 9.34% in Q1 FY27; management expects further operating margin improvement from technology-driven cost reduction and freight rate tailwinds.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.

items.statement: Warehousing gross margin is 15-20%; reported margins appear disproportionately high due to Ind AS 116 lease accounting treatment.
items.quote: But on absolute margin if you talk about it is 15 % to 16% gross margin at which we operate in the warehousing business, 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Warehousing revenue contribution targeted to grow from ~15% currently to 17-18% by end of FY27 and ~20% over time.
items.quote: At present in our business around 15% contribution is coming from the warehousing which we say that by end of this year or maybe in coming quarters it will grow up to 17% to18% and by end approximately 20% it will reach.

items.statement: Freight forwarding contributes 80-85% of revenue; focus is on growing higher-margin warehousing, project logistics, and specialized logistics.
items.quote: Freight forwarding is the major because that is the major contributor, around 80% of our business is 80%-85% of our business comes from freight forwarding.

items.statement: Strategy targets mid-size customers for better margins and payment terms; avoids very large enterprises and small startups.
items.quote: Our main idea of having the sales team is purely to identify the middle level customers. We do not want the top big companies wherein they do not give you good margin or the lowest customers who are beginners or startups where they do not have any margin or they do not have the money to pay.

items.statement: Over 50% of revenue comes from customers with 3+ year relationships (52% last quarter), indicating a balanced new vs. old customer mix.
items.quote: In our top line, more than 50% business is f rom the old customers, approximately 52% last quarter

items.statement: DSO / collection cycle improved from ~72 days to 56-57 days, reducing working capital investment and interest cost.
items.quote: At one point of time our DSO or collection cycle increased to almost 72 days, which has come down now to 57 day, 56 days.

items.statement: AI-based application launched 1 July 2024 to automate documentation, customs filings, and back-office processes, targeting lower manpower cost and faster turnaround.
items.quote: We have recently done some means we have changed our application also, the application which we were using, the AI-based application we have recently started from 1st July.

items.statement: Shipment volume grew 6-7% YoY to ~42,000 shipments annually; automation aims to eliminate manual file creation for each shipment.
items.quote: We have almost we have done 40,000 shipments last year, 42,000 shipments. So we created 42,000 files manually. Now we are basically automating this entire process.

items.statement: Ocean export freight rates are rising, driving incremental profitability; air freight benefiting from cargo shifting from ocean due to geopolitical disruption.
items.quote: Incremental profitability in our industry is in ocean exports, if the ocean exports right now going up because the freight rates are going up.

items.statement: Freight rate-driven growth may not be sustainable long-term; volume growth on the export front is essential for durable performance.
items.quote: The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term. So our growth has been a mix of 6 %, 7% growth in the volume growth and another growth is the freight rate growth.

items.statement: Second-generation leadership (Alan Barboza) actively involved alongside professional management team across functions for continuity and execution depth.
items.quote: Today, the second generation is also actively in volved in the business. Alan is working closely with our senior leadership team and HODs on customer development, systems, expansion, and future growth areas

items.statement: Company rationalized branch network by closing loss-making locations; will continue reviewing network for profitable growth over pure expansion.
items.quote: We keep on looking to the opportunities and we are focusing that we should chase the profitable business only instead of just opening the numbers.

items.statement: Home Appliances Division targets 20% revenue growth for FY27; Q1 achieved 18% growth
items.quote: So the 20%, as I said, that is definitely what we are working towards. And Q1 has been at 18% growth, as far as revenue is concerned.

items.statement: Engineering Division targets INR2,000 crores revenue with 20% growth from existing business plus capex-driven expansion
items.quote: So what we you talking of the number should be reachable if all things fall in place and we get the businesses, we invest in the thing. So it should fall in place.

items.statement: Cost savings target for FY27 is INR120-150 crores; INR42-43 crores achieved in Q1
items.quote: So, as far as cost is concerned, what you said is right, we are looking at INR150 crores to come in this year in the form of various cost initiatives that are there. In the first quarter, we have already got -- about INR42 crores, INR43 crores has already flowed in.

items.statement: Home Appliances gross margin down 160 bps YoY due to commodity and forex; PBDIT margin improved to 5.79% from 5.34%
items.quote: So when you look at it, as I've been mentioning, our gross margin is down because of the material cost increase. So when you look at it, our gross margin is down by about 160 basis points because of the material cost increase.

items.statement: Steel division ROCE target around 20%
items.quote: So here also the ROCE is in the similar line what we have in other divisions, which is somewhere around 20-odd percentages.

items.statement: Unable to fully pass on commodity and forex cost increases; took price increases across categories in Q1 but not enough to cover cost pressure
items.quote: we have not been able to pass on the commodity and Forex to the customer in the form of a price increase

items.statement: Steel division expects to recover Q1 raw material price increase of INR4,125 per metric ton from customers in coming quarters
items.quote: In this current quarter itself, the prices have increased by around INR4,125 per metric ton. So that is the way the industry works is like that this price increase gets passed on to the customers from the next quarter onwards.

items.statement: Home Appliances revenue grew 18% YoY in Q1 FY27; all product lines grew
items.quote: In fact, if you look at the P&L, you would find that our revenues -- the HAD division revenues went up by 18% for the quarter.

items.statement: Engineering Division sales grew 17% YoY in Q1 FY27; exceeded budget
items.quote: As far as Engineering last quarter is concerned, we -- as sales is concerned, we have exceeded the budget, and we have grown by 17%.

items.statement: Services business grew ~17% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the services, we have 3 products. One is the Essentials sales and then we have Accessory sales and the service products we have. And we have -- we are growing a good percentage in terms of this, and we have almost around a growth of around 17%.

items.statement: AC capacity 75,000 units/month; running at 85% utilization in peak month; debottlenecking can raise to 80,000 without new shifts
items.quote: Right now, our capacity in air conditioner is about 75,000. And in the peak month, we are using about 85%. At the same time, we are working on improving the capacity through debottlenecking and some automation. So there is no need for us to in crease the number of shifts, etcetera. We will be able to achieve 75,000 to 80,000, when it is required, per month

items.statement: Engineering Division capex ~INR110 crores for FY27; INR400 crores planned for stamping capacity across Gujarat, Gurgaon, Bangalore contingent on order wins
items.quote: The capex is about INR110 crores.

items.statement: Land acquired in Gujarat for EV battery and stamping projects; battery project on hold pending Tata Group decision; stamping project discussions ongoing with OEMs
items.quote: We have already acquired the land in Gujarat. But other investments, we have machine, etcetera, we have not done yet because this change of situation, we wanted to understand because the project is a go-ahead from our side.

items.statement: Engineering Division has visibility of ~INR250 crores+ new business from OEMs; targeting INR1,000 crores new business to support capex
items.quote: We are close to closing in businesses, which is around INR250 crores plus already. So to auger this capex, we must have at least INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: AC growth impacted by transition to new energy ratings (10-15% costlier); focusing on higher-capacity models
items.quote: The new rating, as you might realize, is about 10% to 15% more expensive than the market. And therefore, we did not have the advantage of the older-rated products with a price advantage in the market.

items.statement: SKU rationalization: front-load models reduced from 55-57 to 24-25; washer SKUs halved from ~9,500
items.quote: For example, in a front loader, we had some 55, 57 models and what we have done is we have been able to bring it down to about 24, 25. So it reduces the complications at the counter.

items.statement: Channel expansion driving growth: increasing manned counters and in-store promoters
items.quote: We are ensuring that we have got people on the ground at the counters, manning the counters and things like that. So a lot of work is happening on the harder things, which is getting our distribution up and running.

items.statement: Front-load market share top 2; top-load lower; AC aspiration 7-10% share; no consolidated market share data available
items.quote: Front-loader, we would be definitely in the top 2. And top-loader could be a little -- would be less.

items.statement: Commodity and forex cost pressure continues in Q1 FY27; not behind us
items.quote: Commodity and Forex continues to be an issue. So even when you look at Q1, we have an issue as far as commodity and Forex is concerned. And whether it is behind us, as of now, no.

items.statement: Trade schemes and discounts ~INR1,800 crores; acknowledged as high and being reviewed for leakages

items.quote: EBITDA level was what was budgeted.

items.statement: Target debt-to-equity of 4-4.5x for FY27 with co-lending at 15-20% of AUM

We would like to be in that range of 4 to 4.5x.

items.statement: Target AUM growth of 50-60% for FY27
items.quote: As we have given the guidance earlier, we were expecting to grow this year by 50% to 60%. As well as both the branches expansion as well as AUM expansion.

items.statement: Target steady-state ROA of 3-3.5% and ROE of 18% over long term
items.quote: If you ask us ROA, ROE guidance for the next five years, we ideally would want to be at a 3%, 3.5% ROA and a 18% ROE kind of a number. That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Investing in compliance software and team for middle-layer NBFC and RBI gold loan regulations
items.quote: We got head of compliance as well as a whole team under the compliance set, as well as we are investing in software to ensure that we are fully compliant for both, middle layer regulation as well as new RBI compliance regulations.

items.statement: Branch network expanded from 83 to 118 branches (42% increase) as of June 30
items.quote: Our branch network has increased from 83 count to 118 branches as of 30th June, which is a 42% increase.

items.statement: Q1 AUM grew ~16% QoQ despite gold price correction; annualized supports 50-60% FY27 guidance
items.quote: Even in our guidance which we have given in Q1 if you look at, in Q1 there was no prices impact, a very, in fact the prices were correcting. We still grew our AUM by 15.9%, around 16%. So, if you annualize it, this will come up to 50% to 60%.

items.statement: No major gold-loan-specific regulatory changes expected in next 12-24 months; RBI has given clear equalizer for all players
items.quote: As for regulation, RBI has given a very clear regulation equalizer for all banks, NBFCs, PSUs, all put together. There are minor regulatory changes which are there, which are affecting other products as well. But these are like we assume that these are regular course of business. We are not expecting anything specialized for gold loans. I think whatever they had to give, they have given already.

items.statement: Gold price correction leads to smaller ticket sizes (Q4 to Q1/Q2); industry-wide correlation; new branch growth offsets impact on overall AUM growth
items.quote: During these times, the ticket sizes are subdued. So, if you look at, I think you will be looking at subdued ticket sizes from Q4 to Q1 and Q2 you will find the major difference that the ticket sizes are getting smaller. items.statement: Management does not comment on share price; commits to consistent quarterly performance
items.quote: We really don't comment on what happens in the share prices. We refrain from giving any guidance or any comments on that. But all we can say is that if you see the past performance of the organization, QoQ we've been performing consistently. Our only commitment to the investors is that we've been consistently showing performance and we will continue to do so.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 thermal plant full commissioning expected by Q2 FY27-28 (June-July timeframe)
items.quote: So, what I am talking about is the complete commissioning of both the units. So, you probably would have the first unit being commissioned slightly earlier, and then the second unit would complete its commissioning by Q2 of FY27-28.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 thermal plant expected revenue around INR200 million
items.quote: From MEL phase 2, we will get around INR200 million of revenue.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 project cost INR400 million with debt-equity mix of INR300 million debt and INR100 million equity
items.quote: So, right now, the debt profile does not change. Basically, the project cost is INR400 million, out of which INR300 million is debt and INR100 is equity.

items.statement: 100 MW solar power project set to be commissioned by end of September
items.quote: Yes, solar plant is set to be commissioned by the end of September.

items.statement: Dividend policy of Nava Global at minimum 30% of PAT
items.quote: Yes. That is the policy of Nava Global at a minimum of 30%.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin for Zambian energy segment around 45% to 50%
items.quote: Around like 45% to 50% is the EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected between 35% to 40%
items.quote: And when it comes to consolidated EBITDA, it will be between 35% to 40%.

items.statement: MEL 300 MW plant operating at 89.3% PLF in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Energy and Mining business delivered healthy operating performance with MEL's 300 - megawatt plant operating at a strong 89.3 PLF.

items.statement: Phase 2 of MEL expected to commence operations next year, delayed by a couple of months due to logistical delays from global conflict
items.quote: Phase 2 of MEL is expected to commence operations next year, later than originally envisaged owing to certain challenges beyond our control with no material impact on project capex.

items.statement: Bi-annual maintenance shutdown scheduled for Maamba plant in current quarter
items.quote: We have a bi-annual shutdown that is scheduled in the current quarter.

items.statement: Metals business volume-driven, 70% of production committed under long-term or quarterly contracts providing stability
items.quote: Going forward, we are quite well ring -fenced against any volatilities because almost 70% of our production is already committed, either under long -term contracts or quarterly contracts.

items.statement: Metals business margins expected to remain stable or see slight increase, no downward trend until end of financial year
items.quote: So, to answer your question with respect to margins, we could probably either see stability in terms of where we are today or if not, a slight increase. But I don't see a downward trend, at least until the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Zambia energy EBITDA decline due to less reversal of ECL credit
items.quote: The reason for decreasing EBITDA is on account of less reversal of ECL credit.

items.statement: Metals business saw 5-10% improvement in spot market pricing quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter basis, we have seen a slight improvement in terms of pricing on the spot market to the extent of about 5% -10%.

items.statement: Actively investigating renewable opportunities including solar, wind, and battery storage for round-the-clock power; monitoring SMR nuclear developments
items.quote: We, as a company, are looking seriously at the renewable space, and not just solar. We're looking at solar. We're looking at wind. We're looking with a combination of both of them with battery storage. So, you have around-the-clock power.

items.quote: Now, the Kwacha-USD exchange rate is around INR18 as on 30th June. So, it is stabilizing as on today. You never know what happens in the future. It depends upon the prevailing exchange rate as on the date of report.

items.quote: Yes. So Zambia has gone through elections. Elections were actually yesterday. No, our operations in Zambia are not linked or related to any political party. We've been through many political parties' changes since we started. So, yes, we are not affected.

items.quote: But anyhow, that is behind us now. We have resumed operations in Orissa as well on the 1st of August.

items.statement: Revenue target raised to over INR3,200 crores for FY27, confident of surpassing INR3,250 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, our revenue outlook remains unchanged, and we continue to work towards our previously stated target of around INR3,000 crores this year. We are confident we will be surpassing this and we will be achieving a revenue more than INR3,200 crores in FY 2027.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue trajectory: Q2 ~INR840 crores, Q3 ~INR850 crores, Q4 ~INR900 crores
items.quote: Yes. We'll be crossing INR840 crores for Q2. And the total comes to about INR3,250 crores plus. And Q3, we'll be crossing INR850 crores and then Q4 is about INR900 crores.

items.quote: Our target -- we had mentioned last year that we -- our target should be around 12%. We will be achieving the 12% target.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expected between Q1's 4.6% and Q3's normalized levels

items.statement: 55 new programs in launch phase, 28 already launched and in ramp-up; long-term programs (7-8 years) for Toyota, Ford, BMW; single-source on all
items.quote: There are around 55 new programs in launch phase, out of which 28 programs already launched and are in ramp-up phase. items.quote: From a segment perspective, aluminum casting continued to be the principal contributor, accounting for 89% of the consolidated revenue, while the ferrous casting contributed the remaining 11%. Exports accounted for almost 15% of our total revenue during the quarter.

items.quote: During Q1 FY27, consolidated revenue stood at INR755 crores compared to INR543 crores in Q1 FY26, reflecting a growth of around 39%-odd.

items.statement: Land sale proceeds to be used for debt repayment

items.quote: Fortunately, this quarter, it is coming down slightly, and we hope that it keeps on sliding down. And -- but we don't know what the U.S. decides to do if they continue with the war, again, there could be a spike.

items.quote: This is primarily on the oil and gas, all the imported materials like carbides, etcetera, etcetera, and also the general inflation that is segment and the labor cost, which went up with the government of Haryana, they jacked up by almost 40%.

items.quote: We started focusing on machines which are above 1,000 tons. So going up to 1,400 tons, 1,700 tons, 2,000 tons, 2,700 tons die casting machines. Those are expensive equipment. So we have

We're also adopting it for designing of dies, etcetera, and that's a nascent stage, but we are in the process of

items.statement: Five-year revenue target to more than double current levels
items.quote: And in five years down the line, we look forward for a revenue which would be more than double of what it is right now.

items.statement: New Andheri facility 5,360 sq ft with 125-150 kg annual capacity, increasing overall capacity 50-60%
items.quote: We have recently established a new manufacturing facility at Andheri, Mumbai. The facility covers approximately 5,360 square feet and has an estimated manufacturing capacity of around 125 kg to 150 kg of jewellery per annum.

items.quote: So, as we said that , we have done a preferential, we have raised capital through preferential allotment recently. So that would predominantly suffice our expansion in the domestic market in terms of working capital, which is around what we are raising is around INR27 crores.

items.statement: New facility expected to generate INR250-300 crores additional revenue at peak capacity
items.quote: So we expect all this put together, it should be around a INR250 crores to INR300 crores kind of a revenue generation capacity.

items.statement: New facility revenue expected INR15-20 crores in FY27, reaching peak INR250 crores in 3 years
items.quote: So currently as I said, because we have just started with the sample lines and all, and so we are currently expecting only around say around INR15 crores to INR20 crores in the current year. items.statement: Domestic B2B strategy targeting major retail chains, leveraging existing Middle East relationships
items.quote: We are also looking at manufacturing and selling jewel ry to major retail operators of India. Some of whom we are already established in the Middle East market, and we already share business with them. So, we are looking to expand into their retail operations in India.

items.quote: EBITDA increased by approximately 69.30% year-on-year to rupees INR8.64 crores, while EBITDA margin improved from 7.35% to 10.14%.

items.statement: B2C expected to have better margins than B2B but too early to quantify
items.quote: B2C should be definitely better in terms of margin. But as I said, if we are just in the beginning off. So right now, I cannot like tell you much about B2C.

items.quote: Right now our lab -grown jewelry percentage is maybe less than 5%, 7% because most of our business in Middle East which is not, you know, too much active into lab-grown yet.

items.quote: Top 10 customers would be, one second I'll just have a look. Maybe around 60% to 65%.

items.quote: Currently it is, so till about a year before it used to be around 20 % to 30%. Now it has dropped right now below 10%. Because last year we were facing a lot of issue in terms of tariff and, workability and how we circumvent this tariff cost.

items.quote: For gold there is a natural hedge because we import and export the gold at predominantly the same price. For diamonds we have a forward contract policy where we based on our receivables planning, we do a hedging of the receivables for four to six months based on the on the receivables expectation.

items.statement: Export inventory turnover 10-11x; domestic expected to be similar or better due to smaller ticket sizes and less competitive credit terms
items.quote: So, export markets if you see our inventory levels are generally 10, 10, 11 times. And we see the domestic market to be similar. Maybe I think domestic might be better than export because export is more competitive in terms of credit and inventory cycles.

items.statement: Hormuz/logistics disruption caused ~1 month shipping halt in Feb-Mar; no material business impact, Q1 revenue grew 22.7%

items.statement: Company develops 500+ commercial designs per month, all production-ready

items.quote: There are no specific competitors right now because it's a very new segment altogether in India. I mean it's been making news only the last couple of years. So, everybody is at a very nascent stage right now.

items.statement: US tariff issues impacted exports last year; now largely stabilized enabling better lab-grown growth
items.quote: In exports, we are now, I mean last year has been a little bit of a downer because of the tariff and all these things that happened in US. But this year we have we have done a better growth in lab-grown in US.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility in export markets driving strategic focus shift to domestic India for greater control
items.quote: As we would be seeing last couple of years for any export , it is like always at the edge with whatever is happening in different parts of the world. So, I would rather focus more on India right now.

items.statement: B2C retail launch targeted around Diwali (Sep-Oct) current calendar year; third floor of new facility being built as retail lounge
items.quote: I mean we are actively looking into different options. But anytime in the current year we are we are definitely, current calendar year. So we are looking at say around Diwali time or something, we should be launching something in B2C.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 800 crore for FY27 maintained
items.quote: But like I said, once again I am repeating that for FY27, we are on track with, you know, whatever we have targeted in terms of the top line. And we don't anticipate any problem in achieving that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance conditional on export recovery

But in case that does not happen and if we are more relied on the local market, then there will be a slight dip in that.

items.statement: Export demand firm but customers lifting minimum volumes due to shipping costs
items.quote: Underlying customer demand in both regions remains firm, but customers are currently lifting the bare minimum volume they need.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin impacted by lower export mix and partial raw material cost pass-through
items.quote: Profitability margins for the quarter reflect both. A lower export mix and partial pass-through of higher raw material prices.

items.statement: Passed on 50-60% of raw material price increase for Q1 orders; current orders at market prices
items.quote: Sir, whatever, you know, orders we had during Q1 which were to be executed in Q4 and... But whatever we are executing now is all at the current market price.

items.statement: Domestic vs export EBITDA margin difference about 10%
items.quote: Again, it's difficult to say because, you know, our product is based on project-to-project, but I would say the difference is about 10%.

items.quote: We have an order book of almost very close to 500 crores as of today. This is over and above whatever we have already shipped out till yesterday. So, we have a very strong order book and lot of new inquiries are on hand for which we are negotiating.

items.quote: These orders are mostly for Q2, Q3 and some of them are for Q4 also. And as I said earlier, we are expecting more orders which will be again for Q3 and Q4. We are fully booked for Q2.

items.statement: Phase-3 expansion adding 6,500 MVA capacity on track for April 2027 commissioning
items.quote: Our CAPEX project, our expansion Phase-3, which will add about 6,500 MVA capacity, remains on track for commissioning in April 2027. Civil foundation work has been completed, PEB erection and utility infrastructure work are progressing well, and all equipment have been ordered.

items.statement: Existing 7,500 MVA capacity to be utilized at almost 100% in FY27
items.quote: Our annual outlook remains unchanged for FY27, and we expect to operate our existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization.

items.statement: Q1 capacity utilization around 60-65%
items.quote: No, in Q1 I think we did only around 60-65% of the capacity utilization.

items.statement: Shipping container costs risen 3-5x for certain geographies vs pre-crisis levels
items.quote: Container costs have risen between three to five times for certain geographies as compared to levels before the crisis.

items.quote: No, like I said earlier, I mean, you know, the overall shipping cost has gone up for all the geographies. So, we do exports to, you know, North America, we do export to Africa and Middle East. And because of the shipping cost, overall, everything is, you know, affected.

items.statement: New 220kV transformer production to start at lower margins initially to build references

items.statement: Confident of regaining export business once shipping normalizes due to quality, service and lead time advantage
items.quote: Yes. So, we are very confident because it's not that, you know, our product is expensive or the customer has some, you know, cheaper source, you know, somewhere else. So, once the situation becomes normal, we will get back that business for sure.

items.statement: West Asia crisis and elevated shipping costs persist longer than expected, impacting export dispatches
items.quote: The quarter was shaped largely by the continuing effects of the crisis in West Asia, which affected our Middle East exports directly and through a sudden increase of price for certain raw materials, which affected our domestic businesses.

items.statement: Geographic mix may shift if West Asia situation persists; domestic focus increased to compensate
items.quote: We remain on track with our revenue ambitions for the year, although the geographic mix may change if the situation in West Asia persists. Demand across our key domestic and export markets remains strong, and our overall business outlook continues to be robust.

items.statement: Additional 4.5 acres land purchased adjacent to existing facility for future expansion
items.quote: Yes. So we have purchased an additional about four and a half acres of land and next to our land is Common wall so we are planning for further expansion in that particular area.

items.statement: New commercial project planned at Hebbal, Bengaluru (~1.3 msf); construction start targeted by end of Q4 FY27
items.quote: Yes. I think we are scheduled to start a new commercial project for a recently acquired land in Hebbal in Bangalore. Hopefully, by end of quarter 4, we will start construction at the site. That's going to be approximately 1.3 million square feet.

items.statement: Purva Miami (Breach Candy) receiving encouraging response from ultra-luxury segment

items.statement: Aerocity seeing strong traction from GCCs and large players; RFPs submitted for ~2.5 msf
items.quote: We're getting a lot of good response from GCCs and other large players. We've been filling RFPs. We filled in RFPs to close to approximately around 2.5 million square feet now.

items.statement: Top Q1 FY27 gross sales contributors: Estrella ~INR200 crores; South projects Northern Light & Provident Equinox; West & Commercial total INR393 crores
items.quote: Estrella in the quarter contributed close to around INR200 crores overall as a gross sales numbers. And I think at a portfolio level, we've done almost around INR800-odd crores of sales since launch.

items.statement: Launch pipeline GDV ~INR27,300 crores plus INR10,000 crores sustenance projects supports FY27 presales guidance
items.quote: In addition to that, the launches that what we have -- what the guidance that we have given is around INR27,300 crores. What may happen in the real world is that some projects may be coming in Q2 may go to Q3, Q3 may go to Q4.

items.quote: I think we are evaluating the growth possibilities in NCR market, more focused on Noida as NCR market right now. We see great potential in the market for branded players like Puravankara entering.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, energy prices, weather-related risks warrant vigilance despite stable RBI policy environment
items.quote: Consumption, public infrastructure, ser vices and manufacturing continues to support activity even as geopolitical tensions, energy prices and weather-related risk warrant vigilance.

items.quote: If you look at our Mumbai landscape now, I think we have almost INR25,000 crores of GDV value spread across all price points from South Bombay to Thane to even Dombivli for that matter.

items.quote: Our new cotton products did very well. They now make up 37% of our cotton sales against 22% last year. This is a big jump in single year, and it shows the farmers are choosing our newer hybrids despite challenges from illegal cotton and reduced sowing acreages.

items.quote: Our new single-cross maize hybrids are doing well. They now make up more than 20% of our maize sales. A bigger share of maize now comes from our newer and better products, which gives a stronger base to grow from once maize sowing returns to normal.

items.quote: We launched 2 new hybrids paddy products, KRH7344 and KRH7227 in their very first season. They brought in 62% of our new product sales. This is a strong start for our new rice products.

items.quote: Our export business grew close to 4x from RS. 1.1 crores to RS. 5.79 crores. Demand from overseas markets is clearly building, and this is an area we will keep pushing on.

items.quote: Basically, it was because of monsoon. As the season gets prolonged, as the monsoon gets delayed, the farmer compromises on the seed. items.quote: And even internationally as of today, because of the Strait of Hormuz and overall general shipping issues, we are seeing delays, we are seeing backed-up shipping, we are seeing the freight prices which have multiplied more than five times to 10 times.

items.statement: Minimal capex planned for FY27 and FY28 as major investments (bunker, robotics, MedTech) already deployed

items.statement: MedTech inventory holding days expected to improve 30%; consolidated revenue run-rate supports working capital discipline

items.statement: MedTech India EBITDA grew to ~₹22.9 crore from ₹2.9 crore QoQ (191% growth) and ₹12.8 million YoY (130% growth)

items.statement: MedTech consolidated EBITDA positive for 4th consecutive quarter at ~₹1.7 million; Singapore EBITDA ₹5.8 million; US EBITDA marginally negative
items.quote: At the consolidated level as I mentioned earlier the EBITDA has been posted positive at about ₹1.7 million in the Quarter 1 of the '27 and it has been the fourth quarter consecutively reporting a positive EBITDA.

items.statement: Hospital segment migrated to new tax regime at ~26% vs 35% earlier; group ETR fell to 47% from 66% YoY; Gurgaon unit tax-free for 2-3 years due to carried losses
items.quote: at the hospital level we have already transited to the new tax scheme with a lower tax rate of about 26% from earlier of 35% in the previous year. So the benefit is a permanent benefit showing already going to a standalone P&L. At the overall group level if you would notice, our ETR has significantly come down to 47% as against the 66% in the Quarter 1 of the last

items.statement: MedTech US profitability impacted by forex and regulatory timelines (6-12 months for FDA-related changes); half of cost-reduction initiatives done, rest in next 6 months
items.quote: Any changes that we have to make within this segment where it concerns the US FDA and other regulatory bodies it takes about 6 to 9 months or one year often to make these changes. So, this is all underway and half of the progress is already made the other half is expected in the next 6 months from here on.

items.statement: MedTech Q1 bottom line affected by one-time forex gain in Q4 FY26 not recurring; depreciation on intangibles and capex from prior years impacting P&L
items.quote: This is also by the one-off if you would not have noticed, the earlier quarter had some impact of the forex gain which was of the FOREX which had been otherwise in the current quarter. So once that stabilizes we would see that the one-off would not be there into the P&L.

items.statement: Doctor recruitment and replacement ongoing at Surat, Indore, Gurgaon (Onco, ENT, liver transplant, KTP, bone marrow); full revenue impact from Q2/Q3
items.quote: The full effect you would see coming in the Quarter 2 and also to mention our bone marrow transplant which had been not there in the last quarter, the active discussion is on with the doctors and that effect would also see in the in the Quarter 2 and Quarter 3.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue ₹338.6 crore (+11.6% YoY); EBITDA ₹49 crore (+1% YoY); PAT ₹10.5 crore (+36% YoY); gearing 0.46x
items.quote: For the Quarter 1, the company delivered a healthy improvement across all key financial parameters starting with our consolidated revenues stood at ₹338.6 crores as against ₹303.4 crores in the Quarter 1 of the last year. This is with a strong growth of 11.6% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Mobile phone trial production by Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28; first year 8 million units, second year 15-16 million units
items.value: 8 million units first year, 15-16 million second year

On the scale front, we expect to begin with around 8 million units in the first year, followed by a calibrated phase-wise ramp-up and expect to double to almost about 15 million, 16 million in the second year of operations.

items.statement: Consumer Durable division full-year growth expected in line with RAC industry growth of 13-15%
items.quote: Yes, sir, your question was that does our guidance stand intact? So it's intact to the industry growth. It can vary from like between -- it should range between 13% to 15%. So we are in line to that.

items.statement: Electronics division full-year revenue growth guidance of 40%+ maintained
items.quote: Yes. I mean, as guided earlier, we hope that we will be able to deliver that number.

items.statement: Railway Sub-systems & Defense division expected to deliver 30-35% revenue growth and 15-16% margins for FY27
items.quote: On the revenue front, 30% to 35% looks doable. And the margins in this financial year, we look at around in the range of 15% to 16% for this division.

items.statement: Multilayer PCB facility at Hosur (Tamil Nadu) construction progressing; plant to be up and running this financial year; INR1,000 crore capex approved under ECMS

items.quote: The plant of air conditioners, that construction will start next year. So it is under -- we are just at a planning mode right now. And we expect that '28, the construction will start. And by '29, it will start the trial production.

items.statement: Sidwal's greenfield facility for HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways in Faridabad now operational
items.quote: On the expansion front, Sidwal's greenfield facility of heating, ventilation, air conditioners, pantry, doors, and gangways in Faridabad is now operational, positioning us well for scalable growth and business expansion.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA grew 28% YoY to INR337 crore; margin pressure from commodity prices, currency depreciation, wage revisions expected to persist through H1
items.quote: Overall, on the margin, let me reiterate, the business continue to face pressure from elevated commodity prices, currency depreciation and minimum wage revision and expect this to persist through H1, which is temporary in nature and expect to normalize as macro environment improves.

items.quote: The operating EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crores, and the margin has expanded to 10.8%.

items.quote: So currently, it is difficult to tell you the exact quantum. So we have given the clarification that we'll be raising up to INR5,000 crores. So we'll tell you that by -- whenever we finalize that how much fundraise is happening, we'll update everyone that how much is the fund raise.

items.quote: We have also onboarded a Chief Operating Officer for the mobile vertical, bringing along extensive experience and deep expertise from the mobile industry.

items.quote: We are on track and meeting our targets, what you said, 3 digit in quarter 4 and significant ramp-up in the following financial year.

items.statement: R32 capacity expected to be fully utilized in calendar year 2027 after expansion

items.quote: The Oman project right now, we have put on hold, okay? And we are -- in fact, what we are doing is that those capex is now -- we are bringing it to India and planning to add those capacities in India.

items.quote: We are already -- our fundraise process is on, and we are raising as we are going along in terms of our fund requirement. items.quote: Taken together, these three pillars give us 12,000 plus seats on track in H1 of FY27, and we remain on course to meet our full-year supply guidance.

items.quote: A part of our rental expenses are also disposed in the other expenses. items.quote: Broadly, the way we are looking at it is a couple of these properties will go live over a period of six months to next 12 months where these properties will go live.
