Second, in terms of a couple of premium straight lease centers, which we are signing across various gr

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; team includes Chairman & MD Amit Ramani, CEO Sumit Lakhani, CFO Sumit Rochlani
items.quote: The management is represented by Mr. Amit Ramani, Chairman and MD; Mr. Sumit Lakhani, CEO; Mr. Sumit Rochlani, the CFO.

items.statement: Management targets 15-20% year-on-year same-store sales growth for mature stores once product mix transition completes.
items.quote: So a matured store, if we are growing at about 15% to 20% year-on-year, we should be very happy, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Capex for Sofas & More stores is roughly INR 2 crores per store (5,000-6,000 sq ft); large format Stanley Superlative stores can cost up to INR 20 crores.
items.quote: So the capex as of now for Sofas & More is roughly about INR 2 crores per store. The average size is 5,000 to 6,000 square feet is what we are looking for. But for the larger one city, one store, the capex can go up to INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity utilization is currently at 68-70%; management believes existing facility can support 2x revenue growth with minor recalibration.
items.quote: Currently, our utilization of our manufacturing facility is at about 68% to 70%. We can easily kind of go up to 2x our revenues in the next coming quarters by kind of recalibrating our factory by adding a few machines if required.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS gross margin is 56-60%; pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is 11-13% consolidated across all formats.
items.quote: Gross margin is 56%-60%. EBITDA margin is between 11%-13% currently.

items.statement: Customer inquiries and store footfall remain encouraging, but conversions are slower as customers await home possession delayed by 12-18 months.
items.quote: As a result, while customer inquiries and store footfall remains encouraging, conversions are slower as customers await possession of their homes.

items.statement: Brand architecture being simplified to two brands: Stanley (complete home solutions, luxury) and Sofas & More (furniture retail, value premium); transition to complete in 3-4 quarters.
items.quote: Going forward, there will only be one Sofas & More and one Stanley brand. That is a brand architectural change we are doing after 8 to 9 years because that is the way that we see is going to be more conducive.

items.statement: 80-85% of retail customers are new home buyers in premium/luxury residential segment; residential project handovers delayed 12-18 months impacting conversions.
items.quote: Stanley's customers are primarily new home buyers in the premium and the luxury residential segment, representing 80% to 85% of our base. Residential project handovers have been delayed by 12 to 18 months in several cases.

items.statement: Inventory higher in Q1 due to forward loading for September season start as Europe closes in August; this is a normal seasonal pattern.
items.quote: Secondly, in terms of our inventory because August usually Europe closes, so we have to forward load, so we have a little higher inventory just now. Because for us, the season starts in September, and August, usually Europe closes. So we normally, in the first quarter, our inventory increases a little bit.

items.statement: Corporate cost is approximately INR 90 lakhs per month (~2.25% of annual revenue); expected to hover at similar levels as company scales.
items.quote: Corporate cost. See it's roughly about INR 90 lakhs per month.

items.statement: BIS certification mandatory from February 14 (6-month gazette until August 14); management believes this will help domestic business by restricting non-certified imports.
items.quote: Nevertheless, we are more excited because BIS is coming into effect actually from today itself, today is a very special day for us. 14th February BIS came into effect 6-month gazette has put it till 14th August. I think from today will be the last date. People cannot import anything from tomorrow where there is no BIS certification.

items.statement: Exports currently minimal; first international store opened in Colombo, Sri Lanka via JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC; US export discussions paused due to tariffs.
items.quote: We entered our first international market in July, opening Stanley Boutique in Colombo, Sri Lanka. This was achieved through a strategic joint venture with Singer Sri Lanka PLC, one of the country's leading retail companies.

items.statement: Proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Limited to simplify corporate structure, improve resource deployment, and enable future growth/fundraising/M&A.
items.quote: The objective of the amalgamation is to create a simpler and more integrated corporate structure. This will reduce the number of legal entities within the group and make management, governance, and reporting more efficient.

items.statement: Sudhir Iyer appointed as new Group CFO with 20+ years experience in corporate finance, M&A, IPOs, and corporate governance.
items.quote: Furthermore, as we continue to strengthen the organization and build the right leadership team for the next phase of growth, we welcome Mr. Sudhir Iyer as our new Group Chief Financial Officer.

items.statement: Internal audit in Q1 uncovered fraudulent activity by Company Secretary; investigation ongoing, findings to be disclosed publicly upon completion.
items.quote: So we found that in the Q1 audit on the internal controls, so we found some fraudulent activity has been done by the company secretary, and the investigation is going on, and we will let you know to the public in short while once we complete the investigations.

items.statement: Mature store payback period (ROI with interest) is 24-36 months; store-level EBITDA positivity expected within 6-12 months of opening.
items.quote: EBITDA positive should happen between 6 months and 12 months, and our ROI should happen between 24 to 36 months. When I say ROI, we call it as return of investment after calculating the interest.

items.statement: Rent expense is 10% of revenue for Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Yes, 10% revenue is the rent expense for Q1 FY27

items.statement: 35 out of 42 COCO stores are EBITDA positive at store level (after cash rent); FOFO stores operate on cash-and-carry model with no credit extended.
items.quote: 35 stores are EBITDA positive. Some of them are brand new. One or two, which we are setting are not EBITDA positive, but out of the 42, 35 are EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 375.43 crores as of Q1 FY27, up from Rs 200 crores guided in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our order book as of quarter stood at approximately Rs. 375.43 crores comprising infrastructure deployment projects along with cloud and managed services contracts. Compared to approximately Rs. 200 crores guided for the Q4 of FY26 period on the previous call, we continue to see the annuity -style managed services share increase as our noc -and-soc operations at Turbhe scale up.

items.statement: Maximum billing from the Rs 375 crore order book will occur in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: The maximum billing will happen between Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Annuity revenue is 23% of total revenue in Q1 FY27; target is 51% over next three years
items.quote: Yes, currently, it is 23% is what the annuity-based income. And the balance is project-based.

items.statement: Management targets annuity revenue mix to reach 51% over the next three years
items.quote: So, our constant effort will be there to keep on increasing this maximum to 51%. Okay. But yes, still I would prefer it will take another three years to achieve that because our SOC revenue, our NOC revenue and managed services, which is our annuity recurring revenue, which is going to take some time to materialize.

items.statement: Revenue growth in Q1 FY27 was 80% from existing customers and 20% from new customers
items.quote: So, this quarter, I can talk about that 80% growth has come from our existing customers. 20% is, of course, from the new customers. So, that's how the ratio we want to maintain it in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 438 bps QoQ to 7.57% in Q1 FY27; management says current level is sustainable due to operational efficiency and margin-led deal selection
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin extended by 438 basis points to 7.57% compared with 3.19% EBITDA in Q4 of FY26, reflecting a significant sequential improvement in operating profitability.

items.statement: Management indicates sustainable EBITDA margin in current range driven by operational efficiency and shift to higher-margin managed services, cybersecurity, and cloud
items.quote: So, you can expect, because of the operational efficiency and the margin -led approach, more or less this will be sustainable EBITDA.

items.statement: Supply conditions stable in Q1 FY27; pricing competitive; working with OEMs for timely cost pass-through
items.quote: During the quarter Q1 of FY27, supply side conditions remained stable while pricing continued to be competitive across key segments. The company continued to work closely with OEMs to ensure timely cost pass through with the impact of input cost movement being progressively reflected in pricing.

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization nearly complete; only Rs 35 crores remaining for DaaS, expected to be deployed in next couple of quarters
items.quote: And the balance amount which is remaining now is only Rs. 35 CR, which we are expecting to be utilized in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Turbhe NOC/SOC center commissioned in Q3 FY26; scaling up; revenue currently single-digit percentage but growing
items.quote: But the revenue is still a minuscule revenue, single -digit percentage revenue, which I am seeing in the entire Q4. But moving ahead, you will hear more and more numbers coming up for NOC and SOC.

items.statement: India data center market growing 30-35% CAGR and public cloud 22-28% CAGR through FY27 per CRISIL; company aligned to capture opportunity
items.quote: Okay, so yes, the data center business is going to grow exponentially as the cloud is also moving accordingly. We are concentrating on both the views as per the CRI SIL report, which we have already submitted at the time of IPO as well as every yearly, we just keep on updating ourselves on what's happening in the industry.

items.statement: Company consciously avoids low-margin large deals; lost a large order to competitor due to penalty terms and delivery risk; focuses on bottom-line over top-line
items.quote: We play in a fair way. We concentrate on our bottom-line approach. We all know whom we are referring to. We got good contracts from the same customers for lower ticket value compared to the competition. That's a conscious call not to go aggressive in that big ticket item.

items.statement: No active international expansion planned for FY27; UAE and Singapore offices serve existing customers only; revenue from these geographies is small
items.quote: Unfortunately, we are not looking at international business, at least for this financial year, because we find that India is a really big, big market and India is growing tremendously.

items.statement: Contingent liability of Rs 4.4 crores due to two telecom customers withdrawing at last minute; AWS savings plan ended Aug 7; management says unlikely to recur
items.quote: That's an unfortunate thing which has happened because a couple of tele commissioned customers have withdrawn their services in the last minute. And that is where in contingent with our OEM AWS, to reverse those kinds of billing and that saving plan which we have bought from AWS, which has got ended on 7th of August.

items.statement: Shailesh Mandani appointed as new CFO; previously Finance Controller, led IPO, ERP implementation, finance transformation
items.quote: For the financial and operational highlights, I would like to hand over the call to Mr. Shailesh Mandani, our newly appointed CFO. He brings with him extensive experience in financial management and strategic leadership.

items.statement: Key Q1 FY27 wins: Rs 20 crore public sector insurance deal, Rs 24 crore cloud engagement with general insurer; expanding in BFSI, cloud, managed services
items.quote: Notable wins included Rs. 20 crores engagement with a leading public sector insurance company, strengthening Orient Technologies' presence in the insurance and enterprise technology segment, another deal of Rs. 24 crores cloud engagement with a leading general insurance company, reinforcing the company's growing capabilities and presence across cloud services and BFSI.

items.statement: DaaS (Device as a Service) seeing good response from GCCs, MNCs, startups, and banks; customers shifting IT spend from CAPEX to OPEX; Rs 35 crore IPO capex remaining for DaaS rollout
items.quote: Most of the customers do not want to spend money in CAPEX for IT. They are converting that into OPEX and that's where DaaS comes in. And that's where I'm seeing, even banks who are cash rich actually, uses it DaaS solutions of ours.

items.statement: Cybersecurity a strategic growth area; invested in Turbhe SOC, signed Securonix for SIEM; revenue expected to ramp as POCs convert
items.quote: Cybersecurity is a space where every customer is talking. Whether it's in the data center, whether it's in the cloud, whether it's at age. You need cybersecurity everywhere. That's where we have invested in Soc in Turbhe. We have signed a big contract with Securonix as a team tool. With that, it is going to do a lot of revenue -driven approach you will see in Soc and the cybersecurity business.

items.statement: Minimum gross margin to survive is 5-6%; most deals exceed this
items.quote: To survive in the market, I think 5-6% is the minimum gross margin that we need to earn. That's our operating cost which I can share with you. But most of the deals are beyond that. So, that's where the profit comes in.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 201.92 crores, up 9.70% QoQ from Rs 184.07 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at Rs. 201.92 crores, an increase of 9.70% Q -o-Q basis which compared to Rs. 184.07 crores in Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA Rs 15.42 crores, up 161% QoQ from Rs 5.91 crores; EBITDA margin 7.57% vs 3.19% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 15.42 crores, an increase of 161% QoQ quarter compared with Rs. 5.91 crores in the preceding quarter. Our EBITDA margin extended by 438 basis points to 7.57% compared with 3.19% EBITDA in Q4 of FY26, reflecting a significant sequential improvement in operating profitability.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 profit Rs 5.17 crores vs loss of Rs 4.99 crores in Q4 FY26; EPS Rs 1.13 vs negative Rs 1.09
items.quote: The quarter also marked a strong earnings turnaround. Profit for the quarter stood at Rs. 5.17 crores against a loss of Rs. 4.99 crores in FY26 Q4. Consolidated EPS returned to positive territory of Rs. 1.13 per share compared with a negative EPS of Rs. 1.09 in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: BFSI 24.92%, ITES 16.82%, Mid-market & others 44.06%, Government/PSU 12.29%, Telecom 1.92%
items.quote: In terms of Q1 FY27, industry-wise revenue was BFSI contributed 24.92%, Telecommunications contributed 1.92%, Government and PSU contributed 12.29%, ITAs contributed 16.82%, and mid-market and others contributed 44.06%.

items.statement: Revenue growth aspiration 15-20% and EBITDA margin target 18-20%
items.quote: So, I think in last time. Yes, so on the aspiration side, so we had said that on the revenue side, 15% to 20% growth and on the margin side, 18% to 20% is the goal.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 19.2% from 18% yoy
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 19.2% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 78.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin improved and stood at 78.6%.

items.statement: International dental lab business grew 37.4% yoy in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Notably, the international business registered an impressive growth of 37.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Aligner solutions grew 28.6% yoy with Bizdent at 27.8% and Vedia at 29.3%
items.quote: Our aligner solution business also delivered another strong quarter, recording a healthy 28.6% year-on-year growth. With this segment, Bizdent grew by 27.8% year-on-year, while Vedia registered a 29.3% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Kids-e-Dental paediatric business grew 54.4% yoy in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our paediatric dental business, Kids-e-Dental, continued its strong growth trajectory, delivering an impressive 54.4% year-on-year growth during this quarter as the business is steadily scaling up.

items.statement: Domestic dental lab ex-scanner growth at 12% yoy, expected to accelerate in coming quarters
items.quote: Yes, this quarter y-o-y it's 12%. But if you see our messaging, we have added satellite labs, which so we are much closer to the customer and we only see the momentum upwards from here.

items.statement: Plan investments in new machinery to modernize and expand manufacturing capacity in FY27
items.quote: In FY27, we plan to make investments towards the addition of new machinery to modernize and expand the capacity of our manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Executed LOI to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra for owned facility to replace leased premises
items.quote: We have also executed a letter of intent to acquire a new land situated in Palghar, Maharashtra. This is towards transitioning from our currently leased premises to a newly owned facility

items.statement: Current rent ~INR2 cr/year for two domestic facilities; owned facility could support 3x scale
items.quote: So currently we are almost paying close to INR2 crores worth of rent just for these two properties. And now you know, per year, as it's expanding, people are expecting a raise on the rental as well.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with finance cost of INR0.3 cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Finance cost for the quarter stood at INR0.3 crores as the company remains debt-free.

items.statement: Appointed new USA-based CEO with 32 years medical device and dental experience
items.quote: I would also like to highlight that we have recently appointed a new CEO to head our USA business. Based in the USA, he brings over 32 years of experience in medical devices and dental industry.

items.statement: AI-led automation expenses higher initially but expected to reduce next year
items.quote: So, there is some cost which is initial, which is coming in, which is slightly higher. But as we scale this up, you know, the cost will become much better. So probably a little bit for this year, but I think moving next year, the cost will be, I would say much lesser than what it is right now.

items.statement: Digital penetration 75-80% domestic, majority digital internationally
items.quote: So, we are currently, I would say in the range of--it varies, you know, month on month, but I would say probably between 75% to 80% in domestic. Internationally it's majority digital

items.statement: Scanner deployment target 800-1,000 units for FY27
items.quote: So current year, based on, you know, last estimate, we had thought that we should be able to again deploy about 800 to 1,000 in this financial year.

items.statement: Scanner adoption estimated at 7-8% currently with significant headroom
items.quote: So today, I would say we are estimating it at around maybe 7%, maybe touching 8% right now. So, there is a lot of headroom for the scanner to come in and digitization to happen.

items.statement: Target all dentist types (general, orthodontist, etc.) for aligners; no B2C direct sales
items.quote: So, coming to your question, B2C absolutely no. We are not selling aligners to patients directly, neither we intend to do so in the future as well. Our goal or our strategy is to go through the dentist. And in that for us, you know, all dentists are same, whether orthodontist, general dentist

items.statement: Aim to outgrow aligner industry CAGR through branding, education, and cross-selling
items.quote: I think always you know, as market leaders, the goal that we have is to grow beyond the industry. So it is not that we want to grow with the industry, and we are putting in a lot of efforts in terms of how we can grow

items.statement: USD appreciation from INR85 to INR95 (~12%) contributed to international growth alongside volume
items.quote: So, over the period of time, the USD has almost increased from INR85 to INR95. So close to about 12% kind of is the change in the USD over the y-o-y basis.

items.statement: Scanner revenue creates margin lumpiness; excluding scanner shows stable rising margins
items.quote: Now with the scanner, it can happen that you will see minor fluctuations. But that is part and parcel of a business where we want to enable digital dentistry for long-term growth of the organization.

items.statement: Branding initiatives include brand ambassadors, in-clinic branding, social media advertising to educate patients
items.quote: So, what we have done is we have got brand ambassadors on board, we are doing a lot of in-clinic branding, we are advertising on social media and a lot of other channels, where we are trying to educate a patient to ask your dentist about the right kind of restoration.

items.statement: Targets 25% year-on-year volume growth in LPG business
items.quote: We like to at least grow in our volumes 25% year-on-year every year. That's our hope. That's how we work for.

items.statement: $5 billion capex target by 2030-31 with 0.6 debt gearing cap and 3.5x EBITDA leverage limit
items.quote: If I am talking about a $5 billion capex by 2030-'31, it means that $3 billion can max come from debt. So I have to ensure and try my best to reach an equity net worth of $2 billion.

items.statement: INR 10,000 crore first phase capex to be commissioned by March or June 2027
items.quote: So what you said 10,000 crores, I think we should reach by March or worst case June '27. So you will see all of that commissioned and all cylinders firing in '27, '28.

items.statement: Liquid storage capacity to grow from 1.7 to 2.2 million cubic meters in FY27 and close to 3 million by FY28 end
items.quote: We are adding half a million by March, one or two months here and there. Half a million in liquid, another half a million to 1 million in FY28. So we jump from 1.7 to 2.2, 2.2 to maybe close to 3 by FY28 end.

items.statement: JNPA expansion of 318,100 cubic meters liquid and 77,236 MT LPG plus bottling plant with INR 1,675 crore outlay
items.quote: We are executing a major expansion at this port, comprising of 318,100 cubic meters of additional liquid storage and 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity, and an LPG bottling plant with an annual capacity of 35,000 metric tons. And the total capital outlay for this expansion is INR1,675 crores.

items.statement: Board approved 52,000 MT refrigerated double-wall steel LPG tank at JNPA
items.quote: I am pleased to share, as I stated earlier, that the board has now approved the development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-wall steel LPG storage tank at JNPA.

items.statement: Board approved 49,577 cubic meters additional liquid capacity at Kochi for commissioning by early next financial year
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the board has now approved this expansion and sanctioned the construction of a further 49,577 cubic meters of liquid capacity at this site. And this is expected to be commissioned by early next financial year.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal commissioned at Pipavav with 36,000 MT static storage and 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc
items.quote: We have officially commissioned our specialized ammonia storage and terminaling facility at Pipavav with a static storage capacity of 36,000 metric tons, marking an important milestone in our infrastructure expansion journey.

items.statement: Four cross-country LPG pipeline connections coming online in FY27 including Jamnagar-Loni, Kandla-Gorakhpur, Haldia-Panagarh, and Mangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli
items.quote: There are 4 pipeline connections getting online this year. One has already happened, Jamnagar-Loni. We are operational. Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla, Kandla-Gorakhpur at Pipavav should be up and running and operational within the next 2 to 3 months. Fourth one, which is Haldia-Panagarh is also expected to get up and running probably in another 2 to 3 months' time.

items.statement: 15-year take-or-pay agreement with leading conglomerate for petroleum products at Pipavav exceeding 0.5 million MT per annum
items.period: operations commence by end of year
items.quote: We have secured a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with a leading conglomerate for petroleum product handling, with committed volumes exceeding 0.5 million metric tons per annum. Operations are expected to commence by the end of the year.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA increased 15.6% YoY to INR 179.4 crores with 76.7% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27
items.quote: At the operating level, operating EBITDA increased 15.6% year-on-year to INR179.4 crores. This translates into an EBITDA margin of approximately 76.7%, reflecting the strong operating characteristics of our terminaling business and the benefit of additional capacity coming online.

items.statement: Industrial LPG demand expected to grow due to portability, energy content, cost advantage and low carbon footprint
items.quote: So, it is so inherent, there are so many inherent advantages, yeah, that we believe that industry, now that they have seen how shortage can lead to industry closing down will make proactive steps to do infrastructure needed for energy custody.

items.statement: LPG throughput tariff standardized at INR 1,175-1,200 per MT across all terminals and customers
items.quote: We generally follow a standard rate of INR1,175 across our customer profile. But our principals may pay us a little bit more, maybe INR25 more to at INR1,200. Otherwise, we have a standard rate across our customers in the industry.

items.statement: Liquid terminal realization at JNPA of INR 6,000 per CBM per year vs blended average of INR 3,000
items.quote: You know JNPA gives you a realization of INR6,000 a year against your average blended rate of INR3,000. So that is what makes the difference.

items.statement: Revenue from operations increased 12.4% YoY to INR 233.8 crores in Q1 FY27 with liquid up 31% and gas down 3.5%
items.quote: revenue from operations increased 12.4% year-on-year to INR233.8 crores. Within this, the liquid terminaling business contributed INR126.5 crores, growing 31% year-on-year, and gas terminaling contributed INR107.2

items.statement: Debt gearing capped at 0.6 and leverage at 3.5x EBITDA; $5 billion capex funded by $3 billion max debt and $2 billion equity target
items.quote: So take it from us that we do not cross the limit of 0.6 debt gearing, cap to 3.5 times EBITDA. If I am talking about a $5 billion capex by 2030-'31, it means that $3 billion can max come from debt.

items.statement: Mandatory equity dilution to 25% by June 2, 2028 to help reach $2 billion equity net worth for capex funding
items.quote: I would almost with my second phase of equity which I have to do mandatorily to dilute to 25% by 2nd June 2028, we are confident that this $2 billion mark, along with this equity infusion and internal accruals, we will be able to reach.

items.statement: Liquid revenue growth driven by new capacity maturation, product mix change and higher utilization at JNPA Plot 1
items.quote: As you are aware, the capacities that came up last year were for part of the year. And now they have matured. Once the capacities come up, the mix of product changes, that takes some time. So now you have JNPA 1 fully firing and delivering on its performance.

items.statement: LPG terminal turnaround capability of 70-100 times per year vs 26-30 times for older terminals
items.quote: For example, the ones which are in existence and which are old, turn around 26 to 30 times a year. My terminal can do and handle by turning around maybe 70 to 100 times.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal theoretical throughput of 1 million MT per year at 20-25% utilization in first full year with 2.5-3x LPG realization
items.quote: So ammonia terminal can do 3 tons, so that is, it would probably be able to do a million tons theoretically. We are not again, like LPG, we are projecting 20% to 25% in the first year. Of course, first full year of operation. So, you have to prorate it because it has come up in August, but the realizations are 2.5 to 3 times the LPG realization.

items.statement: Strategic storage initiative progressing but timing uncertain due to multi-stakeholder decision complexity
items.quote: Progressing as we speak, and it takes time. These are big decisions, and there are a lot of factors to be considered by the national oil companies, government, and everyone, all stakeholders who are involved. It is not an easy decision.

items.statement: COGS as percentage of revenue improved by 175 basis points driving EBITDA margin expansion

items.quote: We have deployed a new technology whereby through RFID you are able to track our fixed assets, machines, and which has resulted in far more disciplined approach in deploying the capital assets, resulted in a reduced depreciation cost in markets like India.

items.statement: India RPT remains at $22-23 average price point
items.quote: I think in our previous calls we have mentioned the high-level RPT for each country. So, the India RPT remains at a $22, $23 price point. That is the RPT which is at the average level for the country.

items.quote: We have indicated in our calls that we intend to open 40 to 50 clinics in India every year. 10 to 15 clinics in Philippines every year. And we intend to open a new international market every 12 to 18 months.

items.quote: I think a 20, the current number probably reflects a good proxy you can use. The numbers may fluctuate a little bit depending on the mix, but the current numbers are a good proxy.

items.statement: Annualized adjusted ROCE at 21% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We also remained focused on disciplined capital deployment and improving capital efficiency. Our annualized adjusted ROCE stood at 21% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Incorporated subsidiary in Kazakhstan; evaluating Central Asia opportunities with universal coverage model at ~$75 price point

items.quote: Our first attempt at predicting adverse events, the confidence level was not up to the extent that we were expecting. So that initiative is the second phase of that initiative is underway, but that's the holy grail.

name: Gaudium IVF and Women Health Ltd

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30% year-on-year with EBITDA and PAT sustained at FY26 levels
items.quote: Yes, so we, I would say a guidance of 30% growth year-on-year, which we have delivered historically also and we will be able to sustain our EBITDAs and PAT respectively.

items.statement: FY27 capex of ₹25 crores for 10 new hubs at ₹2.5 crores per hub funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: On the capex front, for FY27, we had earlier guided a capex of approximately ₹25 crores for the 10 new hubs at an estimated average cost of ₹2.5 crores per hub, funded primarily through IPO proceeds and internal accruals. This remains on track.

items.statement: Board approved up to ₹15 crores for Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow funded by internal accruals, commercialization expected FY28-FY29
items.quote: In addition, our board has approved an estimated project cost of up to ₹15 crores for the Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow, which will be incurred progressively over the setup and commissioning phase, with the commercialization expected in FY28-FY29.

items.statement: Operating 8 hubs and 28 spokes; South Extension operational 16 July 2026, Gurgaon in 10 days, Nagpur in 25 days; target 10 new hubs FY27, 8 in FY28, 1 in FY29
items.quote: We are operating out of eight hubs and 28 spokes. And as I said, out of the 10, one is now operational. The second one in Gurgaon will be operational in 10 days from now, and the third one in Nagpur, as we said we will be including Tier 2, will be operational in 25 days from now.

items.statement: Three international spokes started at Paris, Nigeria, Sydney; international patients 25-30% of mix, expected to grow
items.quote: we are also progressing on our three international spokes. Those spokes have begun at Paris, Nigeria, and Sydney. The response from medical tourism inquiries has been very encouraging. International patients today contribute approximately 25% to 30% of our patient mix, and we expect this share to grow steadily as these spokes come on board

items.statement: Margin decline mainly due to one-time pan-India marketing push for SiD and ERICA AI tools
items.quote: Yes. So as I said that this margin decline is mainly because of just one heavy marketing push that we did. This was a one-time marketing push which contributed to this difference.

items.statement: IVF seasonality: Q1 and Q3 slower due to heat and festivals; Q2 and Q4 stronger; historical growth ~30% YoY vs industry CAGR 10-12%
items.quote: So what I want to reiterate here is that basically IVF has a seasonality about it and Q1 because of heat and Q3 because of festivals are usually poor, whereas Q2 and Q4 more than make up for them, and that has been the historical trend as well.

items.statement: Indian fertility market structurally attractive: 27.5 million infertile couples, only 3 lakh IVF cycles annually, large untapped market
items.quote: Nearly 27.5 million couples in India are affected by infertility and yet around 3 lakhs IVF cycles are performed annually. So imagine what a huge amount of untapped market is lying there.

items.statement: AI embryology tools SiD and ERICA integrated from 1 April 2026; first IVF chain in India to formally integrate AI-led embryology; ~8% improvement in first-attempt outcomes
items.quote: As I mentioned in the last call, in the very early results we are seeing close to an approximately 8% improvement in first attempt outcomes with these tools in the patients where this has been used. That trend continues to hold as we scale usage across our network.

items.statement: Janakpuri flagship centre growing ~30% YoY; Patna relocated to Kankarbagh medical hub; Srinagar seasonal (better in winter); Ludhiana expanding spokes in Punjab
items.quote: So our Janakpuri center has been growing roughly 30% year-on-year and is still growing. You know, Delhi is such a huge market and it is still growing at 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Patient financing tie-up with HDFC Bank helping reach Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets more meaningfully
items.quote: Our patient financing tie-up with HDFC Bank is helping us reach patients in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets more meaningfully.

items.statement: ART Act implementation driving consolidation; organized player share 30% to grow rapidly as unorganised 70% cannot survive regulations
items.quote: And hence a lot of consolidation is set to happen in the market. And what is now 30% is the organized player market and 70% is unorganized, so this 30% is going to rapidly grow.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances ₹8.12 crores vs borrowings ₹6.74 crores; debt-to-equity ~0.04x; debt-light balance sheet post IPO
items.quote: Cash and bank balances as on 30th June stood at ₹8.12 crores against the borrowings of ₹6.74 crores and our consolidated debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortably at approximately 0.04 times.

items.statement: Debt-light structure maintained; expansion funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals; no debt raise for Lucknow hospital
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain robust and debt-light post the IPO, giving us the flexibility to fund our expansion plan with adequate financial cushion.

items.statement: Average revenue per patient ₹3.5 lakhs; excluding low-value services rises to ~₹4 lakhs for fresh pickups
items.quote: Yes, if we will remove all the minimum services, then it will go up to like ₹4 lakhs. Average revenue will go up for this quarter.

items.statement: Mature hub revenue potential: Tier 2 ~30 cycles/year, Metro ~50 cycles/year; package ₹2-20 lakhs per cycle
items.quote: See if at a matured hub if it is in a tier 2 cities, then 30 cycles annually is what we are expecting. And if you talk about a metro then we are talking about like somewhere 50 cycles.

items.statement: New hub breakeven historically 3 months (guided 6 months); centres break even in first 3 months
items.quote: Okay. So, the breakeven usually comes, like we say six months, but historically it has always come in three months. So that is what we've been doing. And in the first three months our centres have break even wherever we have opened them in the past.

items.statement: IVF cycle cost in India roughly 1/5th of US cost; medical tourism opportunity significant
items.quote: Add to this delayed parenthood, rising awareness, a steadily reducing stigma, and a very meaningful medical tourism opportunity where the cost of an IVF cycle in India is roughly 1/5th of what it is in the United States

items.quote: While these segments carry structurally lower margins compared to our core IVF business, they play an important role in strengthening the patient journey end-to-end, deepening the wallet share per patient, and reinforcing Gaudium's positioning as a comprehensive women's health platform rather than a pure IVF chain.

items.quote: Yesterday, we announced the first step in what we envisage as DCW's next 5-year growth journey, a INR250 crores investment program over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: The Basic Chemicals segment reported a negative EBITDA of INR14 crores, primarily due to losses in the PVC business arising from temporary supply chain disruption, elevated VCM prices caused by the West Asia crisis.

items.quote: The West Asia disruption constrained VCM availability, resulting in lower PVC production, while VCM prices were elevated.

items.statement: Domestic demand reasonably resilient supported by infrastructure, housing, water management and manufacturing
items.quote: Domestic demand, however, remained reasonably resilient, supported by infrastructure, housing, water management and manufacturing activity.

items.quote: So far as SIOP is concerned, our margin remains robust, and we are this year, finally, we'll be able to tie up our entire capacity of 28 kt for which we did a capacity debottlenecking 1.5 years back.

items.statement: Legacy long-term debt to be fully repaid during FY27; target effectively net debt free by end of FY27 before new growth borrowings
items.quote: We expect our legacy long-term debt to fully be repaid during this year. Before incremental borrowings for new growth projects, we remain on track to become effectively net debt free by the end of FY27.

items.quote: As this is my first earnings call since assuming charge on June 1, 2026, I would like to take this opportunity to say that I look forward to engaging with all of you over the coming quarters as we progress through the year.

items.statement: Focus on profitable growth, disciplined underwriting, efficient claims management; technology as key enabler; near-term challenges in motor OD, health, commercial lines pricing
items.quote: While market conditions remain challenging in the near term, particularly in motor OD, health, and commercial lines pricing, we remain firmly focused on profitable growth, disciplined underwriting, and efficient claims management. Technology will continue to serve as a key enabler in delivering these objectives.

items.statement: Management aims to complete the Kendriya Bhandar order by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: by end of the quarter, we aim to complete the entire thing

items.statement: Appliances segment targets EBIT breakeven next fiscal year
items.quote: Our goal is to become very quickly EBIT breakeven. But I think that's going to happen next year.

items.statement: Bhiwadi factory pilot production planned for second half of the year
items.quote: setting up of our new factory in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, is progressing well and we plan to commence Pilot production from second half of the year

items.quote: we will be at 10,000 plus per month capacity

items.quote: The Fans business has grown by around 61 % in Ql.

items.quote: Despite the growth in revenue, the segment result is lower by approximately Rs.74 lakhs compared to last year Ql, mainly due to the impact of EPR and our investment in strengthening organization for market expansion and fan business.

items.statement: EPR cost approximately Rs 1.2 crores for Q1 FY27, proportionate for the year
items.quote: The absolute amount of EPR is approximately Rs. 1.2 crores for this quarter, and this is proportionate for the year.

items.statement: Revenue split: Zigzag ~20%, Black machines ~50%, Industrial & accessories ~30%
items.quote: The ZigZag Sewing Machine is approximately 20%, Black Sewing Machines put together is approximately 50%, and around 30% is the Industrial Sewing Machine and the accessories.

items.statement: Kendriya Bhandar order Rs 202 crore; 25% volume expansion clause could add Rs 50 crore
items.quote: what is the pending balance by value and/or volume of Rs. 202 crores order?

items.statement: Government considering higher-end Zigzag and Industrial machines in upcoming tenders
items.quote: there are other government initiatives coming in, wherein higher end machines like ZigZag Machines or Industrial Machines are being considered and being discussed.

items.statement: Singer is the only company manufacturing Zigzag machines per new BIS standards in India
items.quote: I'm happy to say that a Singer is already compliant with the new standard and we are already now manufacturing the ZigZag machines as per the new standards. And we are the only Company who are manufacturing these machines as per new standards in India.

items.statement: Revised BIS standard IS 15449 effective from 12th August; no more import NOCs
items.quote: You're right, it is from 12th of this month, the concurrence has stopped. And therefore, to the best of my knowledge, no more NOCs will be made available, and no more imports will be done.

items.statement: Closing cash and bank balance including liquid investments at ~Rs 58 cr
items.quote: the closing quarter cash number is still with us at about Rs. 58 crores in value

items.statement: Open to inorganic growth if right opportunity found; factory build-out in phased asset-light approach
items.quote: We are absolutely open on all sides. We are also looking at inorganic, but we would consider them only if we find something that is really good.

items.statement: Industrial sewing machine demand driven by garment sector expansion but dampened by commodity price pressure
items.quote: one is the commodity pressure, which is creating a lot of pressure on the price, which dampens the demand and on the other side, is lot of encouragement on garment manufacturing which is going to encourage expansion of the factories and thus creating demand for these machines

items.statement: Transition from imported to domestic Zigzag production involves learning curve; import advance of Rs 14.3 cr for de-risking
items.quote: these machines are fairly complex to make, and we are going through a good learning curve. Although we have stabilized the production to a large extent, the production capacity still has to ramp up to the numbers that we require, and this is a de-risking proposal to have sufficient stock in hand while we are going through the transition period.

items.statement: Built strong technical team capable of manufacturing high-precision Zigzag machines in India
items.quote: I'm happy that we have been able to build up a strong technical force today. A team that has been capable of producing the Zigzag Machines, which many people thought cannot be Made in India.

items.statement: Acquired group FY2027 guidance: EUR 700 million turnover and EUR 35 million EBITDA; not revising despite strong Q1
items.value: EUR 700 million turnover, EUR 35 million EBITDA
items.quote: We feel very confident to deliver the numbers, which we had stated and we have given a turnover guidance of Eur 700 million and EBITDA of EUR 35 million for the acquired group . Though the Q1 performance has been much stronger, currently we are not revising our guidelines given the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Consolidated FY2029 target: Rs.12,000+ Crores revenue; acquired group margins targeting high single to low double digits
items.quote: Absolutely, Sir and that is where if you see a slide number nine, that is where I think we have done our projection on the investor deck from that perspective, where we said we could reach Rs.12,000 Crores plus.

items.statement: Q1 acquired group business EBITDA grew from Rs.65 Cr to Rs.128 Cr; reported EBITDA Rs.146 Cr; One Sudarshan pigment EBITDA Rs.275 Cr
items.quote: We have grown the business EBITDA from Rs.65 Crores to Rs.128 Crores and of course the reported EBITDA from Rs.78 Crores to Rs.146 Crores and as one Sudarshan delivered EBITDA for the pigment business of Rs.275 Crores.

items.statement: Business gross margins expected to sustain at 50%+ range; Q1 saw ~2% improvement from cost reductions in yields, utilities, production
items.quote: So I would say that we should continue to be in the range of 50% plus of gross margin.

items.statement: Value capture (cost reduction) to drive major EBITDA improvement through FY2027-FY2028, some flowing into FY2029
items.quote: The second is the value capture will be continuous, we will be delivering more value capture in terms of FY2027-FY2028, major portion will be FY2027-FY2028, some will be, of course, some of the 2028 value capture will also flow into the 2029.

items.statement: Coatings demand subdued in US/Europe (decorative and automotive); plastics facing hand-to-mouth supply due to polymer price spikes; printing inks volume declining long-term but specialty packaging growing; special applications (agro, digita
items.quote: If you look at the coatings market, the current situation in US, both the decorative market, which is the house paint market and the automotive have been subdued and both in US and Europe perspective. If you look at plastics, this is probably short term, given the whole geopolitical situation there has been a substantial increase in polymer prices and that is where I think our customers are runnin

items.statement: No substantial capex needed for volume growth; moderate capex only for backward integration or special projects based on ROI
items.quote: From a volume perspective, we do not need any new capex we have enough capacities to grow on the numbers which we have indicated; however, we are looking at some special initiative, either backward integration or special projects and these are determined by the ROI and if the return is good we are going to do this. We do not expect any substantial there would be some moderate capex.

items.statement: Sufficient existing capacity to support guided growth; no new capacity required for volume targets
items.quote: From a volume perspective, we do not need any new capex we have enough capacities to grow on the numbers which we have indicated

items.statement: Price increases only to pass through raw material cost inflation; no opportunistic pricing; will reverse if input costs soften
items.quote: So most of our price increases right now have been only to pass on whatever cost increases we have experienced. In order to build a trusted customer we have been very particular not to take any advantage of the demand and supply situation, so if the raw material prices kind of soften, etc., oil prices soften etc., at that point we will only reverse some of the pricing.

items.statement: Raw material basket categories unchanged (benzene, toluene, acetic acid etc.) but mix shifted toward high-performance and pigment dispersions requiring phosphorus-driven and other specific categories
items.quote: It is like phosphorus driven category becomes important there and then there are very specific categories, which we can share with you offline later.

items.statement: High-performance pigments and pigment dispersions growing substantially vs azo pigments
items.quote: what has changed in our product mix, azo is good but I think high performance has grown substantially and our pigment dispersion business has grown substantially

items.statement: Business is sticky with long qualification cycles (1-2 years general, up to 5 years automotive); prefer quarterly price negotiations in steady state
items.quote: I think our business is quite a repetitive business, so to change any of the pigments in the coating industry is a substantially long period and it will depend from customer-to-customer but it may take anywhere between one to two years and if it is automotive paint it would even take five years, so that way it is a sticky business. Generally what we like to do is we would love to negotiate quarter

items.statement: Priority to release cash from working capital in remaining FY2027; net working capital at 23.6% annualized
items.quote: We want to ensure that we are able to release some cash also from the working capital in the remaining year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from Rs.922 Cr peak to Rs.531 Cr; debt-to-equity 0.2x; accelerating acquisition debt repayment as net debt improves
items.quote: As our net debt position is improving as visible in the presentation, we think we will be able to accelerate the payment of the acquisition debt.

items.statement: Acquired 70% stake in Sudarshan Colorants from overseas subsidiaries for group holding structure rationalization planned at acquisition; no business impact
items.quote: It is only within the group holding structure rationalization, which was planned earlier itself. There is nothing further to that and we do not see this will have any impact on the business.

items.statement: European Works Council restructuring program signed post June 30, 2026; quantification expected by end Q2; not built into FY2027 EBITDA guidance
items.quote: By the end of Q2 I think we should have clarity on the quantification of this. As of now, we cannot provide anything more than that because the numbers are quite fluid, so by next quarter, we will be able to provide some more color.

items.statement: One Sudarshan Q1: Revenue Rs.2,642 Cr, Business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr, Reported EBITDA Rs.266 Cr (~60% YoY growth); ROCE 22.7% (annualized); EPS Rs.12.3 (not annualized)
items.quote: So just to recapture the key numbers, the revenue from operations is Rs.2642 Crores with the business EBITDA of Rs.247 Crores and the reported EBITDA of Rs.266 Crores for the quarter under review showing around 60% plus growth year-on-year and 5% in terms of the revenue.

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan targeting 12-13% growth; acquired group grew 5% in Q1 despite geopolitics
items.quote: Legacy Sudarshan, you see a good increase in sales. I would say we should be able to continue a performance of in the region of 12% to 13% in that work mark figure from that perspective. In terms of acquired group, given all the geopolitical situation, we have still been able to grow by 5%.

items.statement: Critical leadership gaps filled in finance, HR, legal, IT, supply chain; global capability center established in Pune; second global HQ opened in Frankfurt
items.quote: There were critical gaps in the leadership pipeline. If you look at finance, HR, legal, IT, and supply chain, there were very big critical gaps and we have been able to get very good talent now and set up a very good organization structure and again that gives us a great confidence to boost our governance and our performance.

items.statement: Project Integra (One SAP) expected to go live in FY2027, replacing 4 SAPs and 130 applications; interim MIS in place
items.quote: What we are moving towards, we have set up a very good interim MIS, and are moving towards an advanced One SAP project, we call it Project Integra and we expect to go live with our integrated system and reducing a lot of complexities in this financial year.

items.quote: We expect the things to normalize from the current quarter onwards. We are confident that before the year end it will be posting a positive number that is the work that we are trying to do.

items.statement: Karnataka volumes up 30% YoY in Q1; Odisha volumes up ~40% YoY
items.quote: We have seen a 30% increase in the cases sold in Karnataka in Q1. And similarly, I thi nk, in Odisha also, we have seen about -- close to about Som Distilleries & 40% increase

items.quote: The facility adds approximately 10 million cases of annual beer capacity, giving us a significant new manufacturing and marketing -- market access platform.

items.quote: we have seen an increase in the price of cans, malt, bottles during the first quarter as compared to quarter one last year. Average increase has been about 7.5% to 8%.

items.quote: I think they are also planning a INR700 crores, INR80 0 crores brewery over there in UP state. So it means that the demand is there, they are also projecting there will be huge demand.

items.quote: Hiten Boricha: Yes, sir. So I have that. It's INR5 crores, right? Management: Yes, yes. Hiten Boricha: Okay. This INR5 crores is attributed to this Bhopal employee cost? Management: Yes.

items.quote: The Hassan facility operated at approximately 60% capacity utilization, while the Odisha facility operated at around 70% capacity utilization.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR5,500 crores with approximately 13% EBITDA margins
items.quote: Our performance for Q1 is in line with our stated guidance for the year of INR5,500 crores with approximately 13% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Core business FY27 volume guidance of 105-110 million meters and revenue of approximately INR4,000 crores
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering our FY27 volume guidance of 105 million to 110 million meters and core business revenue of approximately INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: New business FY27 revenue target of INR1,500 crores
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our FY27 business revenue target of INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Non-U.S. core business revenue expected to grow 20% plus in FY27
items.quote: As mentioned in the previous earnings call, we expect strong traction from non-U.S. markets going forward and anticipate revenues from non-U.S. markets to grow by 20% plus in

items.quote: Looking further ahead, we remain committed to our INR8,000 crore s revenue aspiration by CY2028, supported by continued core business growth and our USD275 million new business ambition

items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 241 bps to 13.1% from 10.7% in

items.quote: So again, as we mentioned, I just want to be clear that from a long-term perspective, we expect our bed linen business to do 15%. We expect our utility bedding business to do 15%, and our brand business should do 100 to 200 basis points better than 15%.

items.statement: Core business volumes grew 12% sequentially to 23 million meters in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Q1 FY27 volumes stood at 23 million meters compared to 20.5 million meters in Q4 FY26, representing a 12% sequential growth.

items.statement: Q1 typically softer quarter; Q2 and Q3 stronger driven by U.S. festive period
items.quote: Q1 volume should not be viewed as a benchmark for t he full year as Q1 is typically a softer quarter for us, while Q2, Q3 are stronger, driven by the U.S. festive period

items.quote: Coming to our new business comprising utility bedding and the U.S.A. brand business, momentum continued to strengthen with Q1 FY27 revenue reaching INR387 crores.

items.statement: U.S. manufacturing utilization at 60-65% despite greenfield facility addition in North Carolina January 2026
items.quote: Overall, utilization has remained around 60% to 65% despite the recent addition of our greenfield facility in North Carolina in January 2026.

items.statement: Utility bedding utilization target of 60-65% for FY27
items.quote: So for utility bedding for this year, our endeavor is to be at 60 to 65% utilization.

items.statement: Price increases concluded with customers, impact from Q2 onwards due to raw material cost increases
items.quote: So on a case-to-case basis, we've gone back to all our customers, and we've concluded all our price conversations. So those are -- those impacts will come from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Input cost inflation in utility bedding passed on to customers with possible 2-3 month lag
items.quote: We are able to pass that on. I mean there could be some laggard effect of two, three months here and there, but otherwise, it's passed on.

items.statement: Product mix impacted Q1 realizations; full year realizations expected to remain broadly intact
items.quote: The change in product mix impacted quarterly realizations. However, the underlying volume trajectory remains steady and EBITDA margins improved. items.statement: U.K. customer interactions doubled from 4 to 8 times per year post-FTA
items.quote: And our interaction has -- let's say, we were interacting with a client, I'm making it up 4 times in a year, that interaction has gone up 8 times in a year.

items.statement: U.K. FTA restores level playing field; EU FTA expected to open large market duty-free
items.quote: The U.K. FTA restores a level playing field for Indian exporters, while the expected EU FTA will further open a large market on duty-free terms.

items.statement: Core business 70% U.S., 30% non-U.S.; new business 100% U.S.
items.quote: So I can tell you our core business, 70% of our revenue comes from the U.S. and 30% comes from non-U.S. countries. And the new business is all U.S.

items.statement: Container availability constraints from West Asia conflict impacted Q1 volumes; issue continues
items.quote: Volume throughput was impacted by container availability constraints arising from the West Asia conflict. With the external environment stabilizing, we expect this momentum to strengthen through the year.

items.statement: Interest cost run rate of INR30 crores per quarter (INR120 crores annually); weighted average cost 6-7%
items.quote: Raman, I mean, our interest cost, we are at a INR30 crores run rate per quarter, so we are at INR120 crores, not INR70 crores.

items.statement: Company rated A1+ with competitively priced borrowings
items.quote: Depends bank to bank. I mean, but we are competitively -- we have a rating of A1+, and we are competitively priced.

items.statement: Bhilad plant flooding disruption; fully insured for property, inventory and loss of profit
items.quote: All our facilities are adequately insured, whether it's for property, whether it's for inventory, whether it's for loss of profit. So as a company, we are adequately insured in all our locations, including Bhilad, of course.

items.statement: No material financial benefit expected from potential U.S. tariff refunds; 80% exports on FOB basis
items.quote: Bhavin, we do no t expect any materia l financial benefit from the potentia l U.S. tariff refund, Bhavin. Nearly 80% of our exports are on FOB basis where the tariff is borne by the importer

items.statement: FTAs take 12-18 months to materialize; not a switch-on effect
items.quote: As soon as the FTAs happen, something happens dramatically the same quarter or next quarter. It takes, I would say, 12 to 18 months to pan out.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to improve from current levels, targeting 18% by 2031 and aspiring to reach 20%
items.quote: Our target is to grow to 20. We had given a guidance that we will go to 18% by 2031.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin maintained at same level as last year despite 5% raw material cost increase, with price corrections expected to take effect by end of Q2 or fully in Q3
items.quote: So even this quarter, we have maintained our EBITDA percentage same as last year. In fact, we have slightly better. I think it will only continue to improve into the future.

items.statement: Raw material costs rose 5% vs expected 3-4%, price corrections implemented but full impact expected end of Q2 or Q3 FY27
items.quote: We started off the year thinking that there will be a 3% to 4% increase in material cost, cost by commodity, metal commodity prices, but in reality it was 5%.

items.statement: India demand strong across all verticals with significant growth in EV ecosystem, renewable energy, and semiconductor ecosystem
items.quote: In India, we have made some strong inroads into some of the growth sectors like EV. Our growth in EV has been pretty significant. Our growth in the renewable energy segment has been pretty significant. And the growth in semiconductor ecosystem has also bee n significant

items.statement: Demand=Match technology launched in India last September driving significant growth, global rollout planned this year with validation machines installed in major geographies
items.quote: Demand=Match was launched in September of last year, and the traction and receptivity has been really outstanding right. And we've been able to gain entry into customers who have never been our customers.

items.statement: Capex split between MK2 campus relocation project (about half) and land purchase in Italy contracted six years ago plus normal factory equipment
items.quote: Our CAPEX, one is our MK2, which is our program for shifting our campus to the new campus from our city factory. That's been about half of the CAPEX is towards that. And the other is we bought some land in Italy, which was contracted six years ago that we had to make that commitment and some equipment, normal CAPEX in the factory.

items.statement: Tier 4 compressor project on track with products validated, first orders received, formal launch in September in Hyderabad, distributors lined up and training underway

items.statement: Aftermarket revenue share at 28-30% in India and 15-16% globally (parts only), with global benchmark around 35-40% indicating headroom for growth
items.quote: I would say it's fair to say, in India, we are at around 28, 30% rest of the world at part level at around 15 %-16%.

items.statement: International subsidiary margins improving due to top-line growth, reorganization cost reductions, in-house motor manufacturing savings, and upcoming price corrections
items.quote: The large percentage of growth of the top line has obviously been a contributor to the bottom-line health as well. So there is no doubt about that. But that's not the only factor. We have also, like you saw one of the expense items of reorganization, we are taking cost out to make the organization more leaner and more nimble and more efficient.

items.statement: Current US tariff at 25% absorbed effectively, received partial refund of ~$1.6-1.8M out of approved $4M, balance pending
items.quote: Right now, our tariff is at 25% and we've been able to absorb that very effectively. Barring no unforeseen kind of shocks of that nature, we should continue to improve.

items.statement: Net cash position remains very strong
items.quote: Net cash position in the company continues to be very strong.

items.statement: Reorganization underway in Australia, Europe, and US with some costs continuing into the year but expected to benefit company in short time
items.quote: We are going through some reorganization in Australia, in Europe, and a little bit in the US. And we think there will be a little bit of these costs continuing into the year. But, you know, the benefit of doing this is, you know, a very short time and it's good for the company.

items.statement: Plan to embed Demand=Match technology in all products globally within a year, already standard in Tier 1-3 compressors in India
items.quote: I expect in another year, all our products will have Demand=Match embedded in it all over the world.

items.statement: No technology gap with Atlas Copco or Ingersoll Rand, Demand=Match demonstrates mastery of 'know-why' enabling next product development, some understandings superior
items.quote: As far as technology is concerned, there is no gap, right? The fact that we launched Demand=Match is a demonstration and evidence that we have a good mastery of the, not just the know-how of technology, but the know-why of technology, right?

items.statement: Steel industry bleeding out capacity utilization before new investments, inquiries exist but conversion delayed
items.quote: I think the steel industry is bleeding out capacity first utilization before they start looking at further investments.

items.statement: Warranty cost less than 1% of revenue, lower than competitors estimated at >1%
items.quote: Our warranty cost, I don't want to give you a specific number, Vipul, but it is less than 1% of our revenue.

items.quote: We started off the year thinking that there will be a 3% to 4% increase in material cost, cost by commodity, metal commodity prices, but in reality it was 5%. Then there was a possibility that it could go to 9%.

items.quote: We don't make gas compressors, no.

items.quote: Oh, vacuum is already in the market, Kamlesh. We have indigenized it, local production has already started. We have started selling. It has been a; the first quarter has been very good.

items.quote: Accordingly, we continue to maintain our FY27 expectation of around INR700 crores on a consol revenue basis with EBITDA of 20%.

items.quote: we have already secured approximately INR190 crores of order inflows in the current financial year till date a t the group
