items.quote: if you look at the closing order, that is around INR485 crores.

items.statement: Target group order inflows of INR800 crores for FY27
items.quote: We still continue to target the group order inflows at INR800 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Healthy inquiry activities across businesses with INR4,000 crores pipeline at group level
items.quote: Today, we continue to have an inquiry pipeline in the range of INR4,000 crores across sectors and geographies at the group level.

items.statement: Strong traction in fertilizer, nuclear, and data center infrastructure sectors
items.quote: We are particularly encouraged by the opportunities in the fertilizer and nuclear where we noticed maximum traction and rapidly developing data center infrastructure ecosystem.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity expansion at Kilburn Engineering and M.E. Energy expected to complete by end October
items.quote: Kilburn Engineering and M.E. Energy are expanding the manufacturing and execution capabilities, which are at advanced stage and expected to complete by end October this year.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield expanding metal sheet fabrication capacity for data center infrastructure
items.quote: At Monga Strayfield, we are in the process of expanding metal sheet fabrication capacity, details of which will be disclosed over a period of time.

items.statement: Capacity investments designed to enable group aspirations of INR1,000 crores annually
items.quote: The capacity investments being made today are designed with a medium -term objective to enable the group's aspir ations of INR1,000 crores

items.statement: Equity fundraising completed, balance sheet strengthened, net debt-free, no further fundraising needed for INR1,000 crores revenue target
items.quote: So we are done with all the equity raising we needed to do. Our balance sheet has been completely strengthened. As to achieve the INR1,000 crores revenue, complete all the capex, we are very, very comfortable.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin maintained at 20.1% despite lower revenue
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR24.2 crores, translating into EBITDA margin of 20.1%.

items.statement: Cost discipline and execution discipline maintaining 20%+ margins on consolidated basis
items.quote: We have always been maintaining a 20 -plus margin, which I think in spite of this m odest turnover also, we have been able to maintain because of cost discipline as well as execution

items.statement: Raw material booked within 48-72 hours for 80% of order value, seek compensation for customer-caused delays
items.quote: we always book our raw material within the first 48 to 72 hours, 80% of it. Now if there is a delay from the customer's end, we endeavor to keep the customer informed that there is a certain escalation happening on account of delays at their end.

items.statement: Collections improved post-March, net working capital position better than March quarter
items.quote: Quite a few collections post March we have received. But more or less, our debtors and other total net working capital position will -- has not substantially changed, but it is better than what it was in the March quarter.

items.statement: Company now net debt-free after equity fundraising
items.quote: Today, we are sitting on a net debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Customer approval delays on engineering drawings and quality inspections causing execution cycle extensions
items.quote: customers are actually delaying this whole process, including approval of our engineering drawings and all. So overall, your execution cycle increases.

items.statement: No current orders from Middle East, but large inquiries at final commercial negotiation stage before conflict
items.quote: Middle East, we don't have any orders currently from Middle East, but we have a couple of large inquiries based in that region. And in fact, we were already at the final stage of commercial negotiation before the conflict had begun.

items.statement: Entry into ferrous alloy segment bolstering M.E. Energy growth with multiple inquiries
items.quote: our entry into the ferrous alloy segment is allowing us to bolster M.E. Energy's growth plans as we are seeing multiple inquiries in the ferrous alloy space.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield sheet metal division seeing potential for storage equipment in data center infrastructure growth
items.quote: we are seeing a lot of inquiry and potential for a lot of equipment, basic ally storage equipments, which Monga Strayfield sheet metal division makes for the data center infrastructure

items.statement: Steel sector expansion driving multiple INR10-15 crore inquiries for M.E. Energy
items.quote: The steel sector is seeing a lot of expansion taking place. Due to that also, there is a potential large pipeline of inquiries, multiple inquiries in the INR10 crores to INR15 crores segment for M.E. Energy addressing the steel sector.

items.statement: Nitin Varadkar and Dinesh Nikam designated as Senior Management Personnel per SEBI LODR rules
items.quote: As per SEBI LODR rules, any reporting on one level below the CEO are to be included in the management list. That is the reason they have been. That is the reason they have been because they were promoted this year and they started reporting directly to the CEO

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causing longer customer decision-making cycles and project deferrals
items.quote: the geopolitical situation has resulted in longer decision-making cycles for some customers and projects.

items.statement: Greenfield project orders on hold due to environmental clearances and land acquisition delays
items.quote: we have certain jobs from the carbon black sector where we got the order, but it's on hold because of certain environmental clearances and land acquisition, etcetera.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities adjacent to current business lines, will inform investors if any fructify
items.quote: Regarding acquisitions, we keep looking out for opportunities, both in organic and inorganic way. In the inorganic side, if any opportunity does fructify, we will ably inform the investor community.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% with EBITDA margin 14-15% and exports 25-30% of revenue
items.value: 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin, 25-30% export share
items.quote: For financial year 27, we remain confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue growth with an EBITDA margin in the range of 14% to 15% and exports contributing approximately 25% to 30% of the revenue.

items.statement: FY28 preliminary outlook of 15-20% top-line growth and EBITDA margin 15-17%
items.quote: Definitely, we have a plan to grow about 15% to 20% in top line and EBITDA to 15% to 17% in '28 approximately.

items.statement: Healthy demand across key pharma products and chemical segment supported by improved realizations and higher exports
items.quote: We have started FY27 on a strong note, with healthy demand across key products, improved capacity utilization, favorable product mix, and continued focus on operational efficiency.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 12.4% YoY driven by higher capacity utilization, better product mix, operational efficiencies and stronger non-ibu API demand
items.quote: We have achieved the EBITDA margin 14.6% in this quarter. And the key factor for this rise in EBITDA margin are higher capacity utilization, better product mix, operational efficiencies, and also stronger non -ibu segment API demand.

items.statement: Reasonable visibility into order book for coming quarter giving confidence in full-year guidance
items.quote: And we have reasonable visibility into our order book for the coming quarter. So this gives us confidence in the overall guidance for the year.

items.statement: Annual capex ~INR200 cr with 60% for expansion/new products and 40% for infrastructure/efficiency improvements
items.quote: Jainam ji, we follow a capex of approximately INR200 crores every year, which is planned with a long term view to s upport sustainable growth. Out of total capex planned, 60% is directed towards expansion and new product . And the remaining 40% goes to infrastructure, improvements for better efficiencies and reduction in

items.statement: Paracetamol capacity tripled to 10,800 MTPA, operating at ~55% currently, expected to reach ~70% by end of FY27
items.quote: So the paracetamol for the IOL, we started around two years back, with 3,600 MTPA capacity which we tripled last year. And this was 10,800 MTPA. And as of now we are operating at around 55% of enhanced capacity, which we expect , by the end of this financial year , will be reaching to around 70%.

items.statement: Most API assets operating at 80-95% capacity utilization except paracetamol
items.quote: Apart from paracetamol, most of the assets are operating at around 80% to 95% capacity utilizations.

items.statement: Non-ibuprofen products contributed 43% of pharma revenue in Q1 FY27 vs 36% YoY, growing 67% YoY
items.quote: Non-ibu products contributed 43% of pharmaceutical revenue in Q1 FY27 compared with 36% in Q1 FY26, with revenue growing 67% year -on-year basis, and emerging as a key driver of growth in our pharma business.

items.statement: Targeting 50-50 split between ibuprofen and non-ibuprofen in pharma revenue in near term
items.quote: And what we were discussing for last few quarters, that we are looking to achieve in mid to short term range,… around 50% from ibuprofen and about 50% from non-ibuprofen.

items.statement: Non-ibu segment expected to reach 50-55% of API revenue by FY29 with margins equivalent to ibuprofen
items.quote: For FY '29 only after three to four years, we are expecting that non-Ibu segment will contribute around 50% to 55% of our API segment with good margin equivalent to the other Ibuprofen margins.

items.statement: Exports increased to 28.5% of revenue from 24.4% YoY, with majority from regulated markets
items.quote: Our export contribution also increased to 28.5% of revenue compared with 24.4% in same quarter of last financial year, reflecting the continuous strengthening of our international business.

items.statement: All API products have CEP approval, 5 products have US FDA approval, 2-3 more lined up via formulators' ANDA filings, clopidogrel recently got NMPA approval in China
items.quote: So basically, our all the products got CEP approval, and apart from CEP approval for all products, we have also got approval from the US FDA for our five products and another two, three products are already line d up as the formulators ha ve filed their ANDA.

items.statement: Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices surged in March due to geopolitical events but stabilized since; delta between raw material and ethyl acetate expected to remain constant
items.quote: Due to war, the prices were increased substantially in the month of March itself, but after that it is stable to some extent. And now the prices are -- you can say not on the upward trend from the last one month. So we think that ultimately the prices of ethyl acetate and the delta between raw material and ethyl acetate will remain constant in upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Metformin not backward integrated; dependent on DCDA raw material sourced from China
items.quote: So, I think .. metformin, is not the backward integrated products in our portfolio and perhaps we'll not be doing the backward integration, for the it we are depending for DCDA ,a raw material. from China

items.statement: No inventory gain in Q1 FY27; Q4 FY26 had 10-15 days of inventory valuation benefit
items.quote: So basically, this is not due to the inventory gain , we might be having little bit inventory gain during the later part of the last quarter around 10 to 15 days, but this quarter we are not having inventory gain.

items.statement: Disciplined capital allocation with focus on projects offering attractive long-term returns
items.quote: At the same time, we will continue to maintain a disciplined approach towards capital allocation and investments with a focus on projects offering attractive long-term returns.

items.statement: Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production in May, steady-state revenue potential ~INR120 cr/year
items.quote: Hello? Around INR120 crores per year.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain challenges, and inflationary pressure on select raw materials persist
items.quote: This progress is particularly encouraging against the backdrop of continued geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain challenges, and inflationary pressure across select raw materials.

items.statement: 101-acre land parcel for future expansion; statutory permissions underway, first project not expected in FY27
items.quote: So again, like we are in the process of getting all the statutory permissions which is underway. Parallelly we are working on different product mix in our R&D section. And once we have very clear cut idea or proof -of-concept ready with us, definitely we will start the work there and product will come at that site also. Abhay Raj Singh: But probably not in this FY

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 20-21% despite strong Q1
items.quote: No, I think we'll stick with that plan because of the volatility that you see, the geopolitical scenarios that you see prevailing, surrounding us and pretty much all countries.

items.statement: Guided QliniQ acquisition to contribute INR150-175 crores revenue for full year FY27
items.quote: We expect QliniQ will do around INR150 crores to INR175 crores in terms of the revenue overall for the year.

items.statement: Guided Europe region revenue around INR180 crores for FY27 including QliniQ and ABCnow
items.quote: So we do expect Europe to be somewhere around INR180 crores to -- yes, about INR180 crores. You can put it at INR180 crores.

items.statement: Guided full-year gross margin around 55-56% versus Q1's 59.1%
items.quote: And yes, in terms of sustainability of that 25 -odd percent -- yes, 59%, I think we should be around 55%, 56% gross margin per se.

items.statement: Guided full-year EBITDA margin 21-22% versus Q1's 25.3%
items.quote: Yes. End of the year, 21% to 22% is achievable. Yes.

items.statement: Target to double revenue to INR4,000 crores within next two years
items.quote: We are still very much on our target of hitting INR4,000 crores within the next two years. So I think we still stand by it.

items.statement: Europe geography target INR1,000 crores revenue within five years
items.quote: In the next three to five years, let's say, more or less within five years, we are hoping that that geography can do about INR1,000-odd crores.

items.statement: US revenue target $300 million near-term, then $400 million in five years
items.quote: So obviously our immediate outlook, you know, we don't talk about $200 million anymore, but we are now working towards a $300 million and then we'll probably look at a $400 million, if you have to look at a horizon of maybe five years.

items.statement: US order book remains strong; growth expected from all geographies in FY27
items.quote: Well, we do see -- the order book is still strong. So that's not a problem. But we do see contribution in this financial year coming from around the geographies.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 59.1% (+138 bps YoY, +478 bps QoQ) driven by favorable mix, low-cost inventory, FX
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR497.3 crores, up 38.9% year -on-year from INR358.2 crores. While gross margin improved to 59.1% from 57.8%, an expansion of 138 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 25.3% (+919 bps YoY, +251 bps QoQ) on higher gross margin and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 25.3% from 16.1%, an improvement of 919 basis points. Sequentially, EBITDA increased from INR195.4 crores, while EBITDA margin expanded by 251 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 net capex INR33 crores; free cash flow INR152 crores
items.quote: After net capex of INR33 crores, free cash flow stood at INR152 crores.

items.statement: Goa Unit 2 (Teva facility) at 60-65% utilization, currently INR50+ crores revenue vs INR80 crores target
items.quote: We had projected about moving towards an INR80 crores revenue generation from that plant. We are right now at INR50 -plus crores. So I think we are pretty much at 60% to 65% out there.

items.statement: Planning another manufacturing unit in India within 1-2 years to support 3-5 year plan; evaluating greenfield/brownfield options
items.quote: If we have to achieve our three to five -year plan, yes, we are aware that we may need manufacturing capabilities, probably another unit in India. We are working in that direction, but nothing concrete as of now.

items.statement: Completed QliniQ B.V. (Netherlands) acquisition effective April 1, 2026; contributed INR44 crores revenue in Q1
items.quote: During the quarter, we completed the acquisition of QliniQ B.V in Netherlands, which contributed approximately INR44 crores of revenue in Q1.

items.statement: Completed ABCnow GmbH (Germany) acquisition with consolidation from Q2 FY27
items.quote: We then completed the acquisition of ABCnow GmbH, Germany with consolidation commencing from Q2.

items.statement: Actively exploring further acquisitions in Europe; no concrete deals yet but have capital for inorganic growth
items.quote: We are actively looking at other acquisitions. Nothing concrete or no pen to paper, but we do believe the resources and the money sitting on our balance sheet will fuel our growth in terms of both organic and inorganic strategies that we plan to pursue.

items.statement: Europe mix tilted 80-85% Rx / 15-20% OTC; UK split 55% Rx / 45% OTC; US remains OTC-driven (~85% OTC / 15% Rx)
items.quote: So U.K., it's equally distributed. We have about 55% into Rx and 45% into OTC. So it's quite equally distributed. But in Europe, it's going to be tilting more towards Rx, maybe 80% or 85% Rx and 15% OTC.

items.statement: US growth driven by expanding product portfolio with existing key OTC customers; preferred partner status
items.quote: So as and when opportunities do come, we are the preferred choice of partners that they look at. And our product portfolio, in each of those customers are increasing.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to ~132 days in Q1 FY27 from ~159 days in Q1 FY26 and ~138 days in FY26
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved to approximately 132 days compared with approximately 159 days in Q1 FY2026 and 138 days forFY2026 as a whole

items.statement: Net cash position INR1,031 crores at end of Q1 FY27 despite QliniQ acquisition payment
items.quote: While the net cash stood at INR1,031 crores, this was achieved despite the payment towards the QliniQ acquisition during the quarter.

items.statement: Management averse to investing surplus cash in market instruments; prefers safe FDs and using cash for acquisitions
items.quote: No, we don't take that factoring or risk. We are not into that. We make sure it is safe. Yes, our main aim is to use those funds to drive inorganic strategies, which basically will grow the company and its revenue generation.

items.statement: USFDA inspections unpredictable; one plant audited <12 months ago; no fixed timeline for next inspection
items.quote: There is no definite time lines as in such because they can come any moment, although one of our plants was recently audited less than 12 months back. But again, they can come any time based on our filings.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (war, freight, raw material costs) cited as reason for conservative guidance and margin sustainability concerns
items.quote: So obviously, it's a very fluid situation. And you're right, we were sitting on good inventory, which we are depleting over time. We still have some inventory, but there are obviously other parameters within the war -- due to the war, which is having an i mpact like freight or some higher cost of raw material coming in

items.statement: Rest of World markets (Middle East, others) facing challenges due to war, shipping disruptions; minimal contribution
items.quote: Obviously, the other markets besides the western markets are struggling a bit because of the war scenarios, because of vessels unable to pass and the transportation becoming one of the biggest hurdles in those regions.

items.statement: R&D spend INR23.2 crores (2.8% of revenue) in Q1 FY27 vs INR12.1 crores (2.0%) in Q1 FY26; targeting portfolio doubling in each country over 2-3 years
items.quote: R&D spend for the quarter was INR23.2 crores or 2.8% of consolidated revenue compared with INR12.1 crores and 2% in Q1 of FY2026.

items.statement: North America saw softer summer seasonal demand; price erosion in Rx portfolio in single digits; momentum expected to strengthen
items.quote: This quarter saw a softer demand through the summer months, in line with the normal seasonal pattern. Price erosion in our Rx portfolio remained in single digits, and in the coming quarters, we expect momentum to strengthen.

items.statement: Australia/NZ revenue up 53.7% YoY; sequential moderation due to seasonal pattern after strong Q4; momentum expected to build
items.quote: This was in line with our normal seasonal pattern, following a particularly strong fourth quarter during the Southern Hemisphere winter. The underlying business remains healthy, and we expect momentum to build as we move through the year.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR600 crores for FY27
items.quote: Yes. Like we mentioned, we are expecting a target of around INR600 crores turnover, which is a considerable increase in the previous year, 2 years, if you take it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 15% to 20% for FY27
items.quote: Even in earlier conference calls also, we said that we are targeting an EBITDA of 15% to 20%. So I think same line we are trying to achieve.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR200-300 crores for FY27
items.quote: Already, we have INR1,393 crores. So FY '27, we are expecting another INR200 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Export revenue target of INR150-200 crores for Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting some INR200 crores in this quarter based on -- INR150 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,393 crores with 94% from Defense segment
items.quote: As of today, our order book stands at INR1,393 crores with approximately 94% of the order book coming from Defense segment.

items.statement: Defense order book INR1,309 crores, Explosives INR42 crores, Services INR42 crores
items.quote: The company's current order book stands at INR1,393 crores, out of which Defense segment order is majority of INR1,309 crores, which is equal to 94% of the total order book.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBIT margin at 4.7%, PAT margin at 3%
items.quote: Our EBIT for Q1 FY '27 de-grew by 80% year-on-year to INR4.8 crores. The EBIT margin for the quarter stands at 4.7%.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to improve sequentially from Q1 levels
items.quote: The healthy order book and execution pattern, we have already this quarter's movement of materials and all those goods gives us the confidence that it will improve in the coming quarters.

items.statement: RDX/HMX plant integration almost complete, water trials in September
items.quote: Integration of the pipelines and the plant and machinery erection and installation for the RDX and HMX production is almost complete, and then we are expecting to take up the water trials in September month.

items.statement: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installation delayed, dummy trials by end September
items.quote: And about mixing plant where 2.5 tonnes planetary mixer is installed, some of the components which are imported by the supplier of the mixer, they got delayed because of the movement -- maritime movement of ships and all those.

items.statement: Capacity sufficient to execute INR430 crores order in FY27
items.quote: Yes, we have. The chaff material payload, we are dependent on imports, which we have completed, we have executed. The flares we do in our own plant. So we have the capability to complete.

items.statement: Partnering with drone manufacturers for payloads, not developing own UAV technology
items.quote: We are not developing our own drone technologies that is for the birds and all those. We are partnering with several drone manufacturing industries for the payloads.

items.statement: Export licenses received for backlog orders, completion expected in Q2
items.quote: Past 1 week, we have received several export licenses, and we have also moved out the material from the factories. And some of them are in pipeline.

items.statement: INR350 crores international order export license in process, takes 3-4 months
items.quote: It usually takes 3 to 4 months at least for every processing of the export license. And before we submit for processing, we have to receive the import licenses from the importing country.

items.statement: Alternative raw material for mines under DRDO testing, clearance in 6 months
items.quote: They have -- they are conducting the tests of our material, what we have proposed and that is being done by DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL. Once it is complete, I think they will give us a clearance to use that material.

items.statement: Apollo Micro Systems acquisition creates integrated defense platform with electronics and energetic materials
items.quote: The partnership brings together Apollo's strengths in defense electronics and mission-critical systems with Premier's capability in energetic materials, rocket motors, ammunition and propulsion systems, creating a broader and more integrated defense platform.

items.statement: Underlying demand environment remains robust despite Q1 dispatch delays
items.quote: While these factors affected nea r-term revenue recognition, the underlying demand environment for our products and solutions remains robust

items.statement: Bulk explosives margins very thin, many places negative due to low prices
items.quote: Margins are very, very thin. Many places, it is negative.

items.statement: Other expenses sustainable run rate INR9-10 crores per quarter
items.quote: You can say around INR9 crores kind of thing. You can see in 30th June '25 also, it is around INR9 crores. So INR9 crores to INR10 crores kind of thing.

items.statement: Flares order backlog INR75 crores to be completed in 4-5 months
items.quote: Earlier order also, we are going to complete it in another 3 to 4 months. There is a backlog of about INR75 crores. So that will be completed in the next 4, 5 months.

items.statement: Singareni Collieries contract balance INR25-30 crores to execute in FY27
items.quote: We have an executed contract with Singareni Collieries. So the balance part of about INR25 crores to INR30 crores that will be executed this year -- this financial year.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh expansion land pricing under negotiation with government
items.quote: Land parcel, the pricing was an issue. We were requesting the government for a reasonable price, which we can afford to install because as an explosive industry, we require large landed areas.

items.statement: Bulk explosives market has 40+ players, difficult to predict FY28 revenue
items.quote: Difficult to predict that FY '28 because the prices are very much dependent on the raw material input cost prices. So -- and multiple manufacturing capacities are there that also more than 40 players in this field.

items.statement: LD reversal for July 2023 flares order in process, expected by October-November
items.quote: Yes. LD still is in process. May be by this quarter end or by October, November, I think we'll come to know because a lot of processes are there. It's going on.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM reached INR2,925 crores, up 36% YoY as of June 2026
items.quote: Against this backdrop, I am pleased to share that our consolidated AUM reached a record high of INR2,925 crores as of June '26, representing a growth of 36% year -on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated disbursements were INR686 crores, up 76% YoY, highest ever Q1 disbursements
items.quote: Consolidated disbursements during the quarter were INR686 crores, up 76% year-on-year and represented our highest ever first quarter disbursements.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA improved to 2.76% and NNPA to 0.84%; zero DPD flow forwards at ~99.5%
items.quote: Our asset quality has continued to improve over the past four quarters with consolidated GNPA now at 2.76% and NNPA improving to 0.84%. Early -stage delinquencies have also remained largely stable at approximately 99.5% zero DPD flow forwards.

items.statement: Consolidated NIM at 17.4%; annualized ROA 6.4%, ROE 18.9%
items.quote: Our consol idated NIM remained healthy at 17.4%, while annualized return on average AUM was 6.4%. Return on equity was 18.9% for the quarter, annualized, of course.

items.statement: Namra Finance NIM improved to 15.37% supported by better yields and growing individual loan share
items.quote: NIMs improved to 15.37% during the quarter, supported by bette r yields and growing share of individual loans in the portfolio mix.

items.statement: Consolidated cost-to-income improved to 44.3% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26; PPOP increased to INR77 crores from INR59 crores
items.quote: Our consolidated pre-provisioning operating profit increased to INR77 crores during the quarter from INR59 crores in Q4 FY26. Cost to income improved meaningfully to 44. 3% from 51.7% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Target to reduce opex ratio to 7% by end of FY27 (March 2027); currently ~8.5% annualized
items.quote: And the goal is to get it down to 7%, which is what I had stated earlier, I don't know if it was one quarter or two quarters ago by the end of March. So we are well on track to do that.

items.statement: Expect credit cost around 3-3.5% including CGFMU cost; could be 2.5% or 2% if lucky
items.quote: If you probably include the cost of the CGFMU, then yes, probably 3 % sounds about right, maybe 2.5%. 2% if we are lucky. Let's see how the year progresses.

items.statement: Individual loans now 33% of overall book; focus on individualized credit assessment using bureau, cash flow, UPI/e-NACH
items.quote: We continue to see healthy traction in our individual loan portfolio, which now accounts for 33% of our overall book and is becoming an increasingly important part of our microfinance business.

items.statement: Individual loans performing better than JLG; 68-70% eNACH/UPI clearance by month-end, 85% cashless collections
items.quote: When we run the eNACH and the UPI mandates for the individual loans, about 68% to 70% clears, by the end of the month, we manage clearing about 85% through cashless and the balance, whatever, 14%, we are going door-to-door and collecting cash.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 96.6% for Q1, improved further by June
items.quote: Overall collection efficiency for Q1 stood at 96.6%, and we saw a steady improvement throughout the quarter. By June, overall collection efficiency had improved further, which gives us comfort on the behavior of the more recently origin ated portfolio.

items.statement: Namra Finance GNPA improved from peak 3.8% to 2.59% currently
items.quote: On asset quality, GNPA has improved significantly from its peak of 3.8% to 2.59% currently.

items.statement: Liquidity position: INR286 crores cash/liquid investments/undrawn CC; INR335 crores undrawn sanctions from lenders
items.quote: We also maintained a healthy liquidity position with INR286 crores across cash and bank balances, liquid investments, and undrawn CC limits. In addition, we have INR335 crores of undrawn sanctions from existing lenders, providing us with sufficient headroom to support our funding requirement and growth plans.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 33.6% (Arman standalone) and 38.8% (Namra); consolidated equity INR979 crores
items.quote: Capital adequacy stood at 33.6% for Arman stand-alone and 38.8% for Namra Finance. As of June 2026, our consolidated shareholders' equity was INR979 crores.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost ~11.7%, down from 12%+; targeting 20-30 bps reduction via rating upgrades
items.quote: I believe we are approaching rating agencies and stuff at this point also for upgrades. So hopefully, that should meaningfully reduce it by, I don't know, Vivek, 20 bps, 30 bps at least on the plate.

items.statement: No plan to reduce lending rates despite peers cutting; rates justified to RBI and based on customer affordability
items.quote: If we reach a point where we are making too much money, I'm okay with reducing rates, but I've not given it much thought at this point. So that's, I think, the first line item.

items.statement: Cautious on macro: rural income growth weak, inflation rising, job quality concerns; portfolio held up better than expected but monitoring lag effects
items.quote: Inflation is increasing. Jobs are there, but not the jobs that people want. So those kinds of factors kind of, I don't know, judgmentally, I wouldn't say scare me, but of course, concern me slightly.

items.statement: Telangana showing slightly higher stress in MSME/LAP; sectoral issue reported by peers

items.statement: Cat event participation typically 30-40% of market losses
items.quote: In terms of our experience, it has been our stance that whatever might be the market losses, our losses from cat events tend to be around 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Investment book market value INR157,800 crores; 73.4% fixed income, ~17% equity, ~8.67% money market; equity includes NSE stake
items.quote: Market value as told is INR157,800 crores. That includes only equity, which is around INR58,000 crores, because debt is kept at cost only in ours as it is held to maturity. Regarding your second question regarding NSE, it includes NSE also.

items.statement: Investment income Q1 FY27 INR3,265.51 crores vs INR3,313.74 crores YoY
items.quote: Investment income for the quarter stood at INR3,265.51 crores, vis-a-vis INR3,313.74 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32 as of June 30, 2026 vs 3.85 a year ago
items.quote: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32 as on June 30, 2026, as compared to 3.85 as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Profit before tax INR2,490.25 crores, profit after tax INR1,922.04 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Profit before tax stood at INR2,490.25 crores for quarter 1 FY27. Profit after tax was INR1,922.04 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated profit lower due to subsidiary losses: South Africa INR287 crores loss, Moscow INR29 crores loss in Q1
items.value: INR287 crores loss (South Africa), INR29 crores loss (Moscow)
items.quote: If you want to know subsidiary company-wise, South Africa, we have shown INR287 crores loss during this quarter, and Moscow some INR29 crores loss from the subsidiary. That has resulted into the lower figure compared to last year in consolidated operating profit.

items.statement: IFRS and RBC implementation upcoming, affecting rating upgrade timeline and capital planning
items.quote: Also, there are 2 major developments which are in the offing, the IFRS and the RBC. It is not really possible to give any timeline, but if things go all right, probably one can expect in a period of, say, something like 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Management focused on profitability over growth; will not pursue premium targets at cost of risk-return optimization
items.quote: While we have the broader targets and goals and direction, we are not really keen on pursuing those targets at the cost of overall risk-return optimization. We are very much focused on return on equity and shareholder value creation.

items.statement: CIO Radhika Ravishekar and CFO Rajesh Laheri participated in call alongside CMD Hitesh Joshi and Sanjay Mokashi
items.quote: This is Radhika Ravishekar, the CIO. 73.4% is in the fixed income securities, sir. Around 17% in equity and around 8.67% or something in money market instruments.

items.statement: Net worth excluding fair value increased; including fair value flat over 3 years due to equity mark-to-market reductions of INR11,000-15,000 crores offsetting profits
items.quote: What you say is correct. I think almost entire change on the net worth, including fair value, is on account of essentially market value changes. You are right in including the profit or whatever is the financial performance, changing the net worth. The onl y variable which is moving this is market value, fair

items.statement: Management focused on ROE improvement; expects some improvement as combined ratio targets achieved over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think we will continue to be focused on our return on equity, and you can expect some improvement. I think when we are talking about 1% overall improvement in combined ratio or, say, domestic getting targeted at 103 combined ratio and foreign at 95 over a period of, say, something like next 2 to 3 years, that should give you some idea as to what will be the improvement in return on equity.

items.statement: Steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 compressed margins; full recovery expected in coming quarters
items.quote: But basically, you are aware that TI maybe gets those price increases with a lag of sometimes two or three quarters. So we are confident on the steel price increase particularly. We will be able to recover fully and you will see the margin neutralization will happen in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Guidance to grow EBIT margin in double digits; post price recovery, double digit margin improvement to continue
items.quote: Maybe like we have given guidance, we will be able to grow EBIT margin in the double digit. And post the price recovery, we are confident that double digit margin improvement will keep happening in the future also.

items.statement: Engineering volume grew 17% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So volume grew about 17%.

items.statement: Next 1-2 quarters expected to be bullish; exports grew double digits in Q1 and momentum expected to continue
items.quote: I think it is beyond anybody's imagination, but at least for the next one or two quarters, we feel it is going to be bullish. And exports also has done pretty well in particularly quart er one. And there is more than good double digit growth has happened in exports also. And we expect that momentum to

items.statement: Exports at 14% of standalone revenue
items.quote: At a TI level, it is about 14%.

items.statement: EV order book focus on 4x2 tractor trailer; tipper volumes 20-25 units in Q1
items.quote: As far as the existing tippers are concerned, we have sold about 20-25 numbers of tippers and the initial feedback is positive. Also, keeping in view the order book, which we have for some of the other products, where we have a confirmed order book

items.statement: Standalone capex Rs.350 Cr, Shanthi Gears Rs.100 Cr, group ex-CG Power Rs.600-700 Cr for FY27
items.quote: In TI, we are planning around Rs.350 Crores of Capex for the current financial year. And Shant hi Gear will be around Rs.100 Crores. And if you take group as a whole, if you see something like 600 to 700 Crores

items.statement: Capex allocated to engineering, MFP, TI Medical and 3xper CDMO business
items.quote: So in core business, basically the money will be going towards the engineering division and MFP division and rest maybe money will be going in basically TI Medical and 3xper, CDMO business.

items.statement: Rs.250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26; another Rs.250 Cr planned in Q3 FY27; total guidance Rs.750 Cr over time
items.quote: We have already infused Rs.250 crores in the last quarter, maybe basically Q4 of the last financial year and we anticipate maybe in Q3, we will infuse another Rs.250 Crores. We are given a guidance of total put together about Rs.750 Crores infusion will happen over a period of time.

items.statement: TI Medical core surgical business grew ~20% YoY in Q1; IV cannula acquisition revenue from Q2
items.quote: In the quarter one, we had a growth of almost close to 20% in that particular business. And second, maybe to grow business, we have done a very small acquisition in the IV cannula, which is basically maybe infusion therapy, this IV cannulas are used. And we are expecting that business to start giving us revenue from the second quarter onwards

items.statement: TI Medical targets 20% YoY revenue growth with profitability
items.quote: Overall basis for TI Medical, as we said in the previous calls, we are confident to do 20% revenue growth year-on-year along with the profitability.

items.statement: EV volumes: big trucks 86, three-wheelers 1,924, small commercial vehicles 347, tractors 22 in Q1
items.quote: The billing volumes, the big trucks was 86 numbers. The three-wheeler business was 1,924. The small commercial vehicle was 347. And tractor was 22 numbers.

items.statement: Cycle business margin expansion in Q1; targeting at least 200 bps improvement for full year
items.quote: So we are hopeful, like we shared maybe at least another 2 basis point in the cycle business, we will be able to improve margin for overall year in the current financial year.

items.statement: Non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) discussions with OEMs ongoing; hopeful majority recoverable
items.quote: We have already taken up with all our customers. So as of now, we are in the verge of discussions with all the OEMs to recover, which is a non-steel inflation, which is basically fuel freight etc. So maybe we will let you know maybe another quarter down the line time, how those conversations are going on. But we are hopeful majority of that we will be able to recover as on this moment.

items.statement: MFP Greenfield plant in western region delayed by six months, causing capacity lag
items.quote: We have declared to do a Greenfield plant launch in the western region that is running delayed by six months. So capacity may be in terms of expansion, whatever growth was there. So we are having a lag of six months to catch up on that.

items.statement: EV cell supply challenge persists; tax exemption removal in China may lower prices in 2-3 quarters; pre-booking and price locking as mitigation
items.quote: However, in light of what is happening across the world and also growing demand for BESS business, which is battery energy storage system, we are seei ng some challenges on the cell prices. However, in our case, what we are relying is in terms of pre-booking some of the orders with long lead time items and locking the prices with the cell and the battery manufacturers

items.statement: EV exports: 100+ three-wheelers shipped to Nepal; exploring Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Ethiopia
items.quote: About 100 plus is the unit which have been shipped or in the process of getting shipped to Nepal and initial product feedback is very positive and we are very bullish on Nepal as a country going forward.

items.statement: NCR EV policy mandatory in couple of months; huge traction expected; ramping dealer network
items.quote: we are increasingly seeing more and more traction gaining into when it comes to NCR market not only for us for the entire industry of EV in let us say couple of months from now once this becomes mandatory we will see huge traction gain ing into NCR

items.statement: Orange Koi (metal injection molding) acquired; small startup to develop capability; guidance in two quarters
items.quote: This is a very small business which we have acquired. Basically, it is a step towards additive manufacturing, which is metal injection molding. So this is a small startup, which we have acquired to develop the capability. And going forward, we will be scaling it up. So first one or two quarters, we would like to study what market and what segment we want to play. And maybe I think two quarters dow

items.statement: Jayem diversifying into battery manufacturing; assembly line setup this year; initially for in-house consumption
items.quote: Jayem has now diversified into battery manufacturing, which has a good potential going forward. So, in this financial year, they have a battery assembly line set up. So going forward, apart from the core business of design and development and fast prototyping, validation and testing. These two were the core business for Jayem. We will see a third revenue generation stream of battery business also

items.statement: TI Clean Mobility CCPS conversion only at IPO; no fixed timeline; stake depends on market valuation
items.quote: The conversion happens only at the time of IPO. IPO, we have a time and there is no fixed timeline for this. And whenever, once the market is there and once we start selling more and revenue start coming up and once the profitability comes, we will go to the market for IPO. At that point, it will get converted.

items.statement: Shanthi Gears revenue Rs.115 Cr vs Rs.135 Cr YoY; PBT Rs.14 Cr vs Rs.31 Cr YoY
items.quote: Shanthi Gears Limited, a subsidiary company in the gears business in which company holds 70.46% stake, registered a revenue of Rs.115 Crores during the quarter against Rs.135 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before tax for the quarter was Rs.14 Crores against Rs.31 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: CG Power revenue Rs.3,281 Cr vs Rs.2,878 Cr YoY; PBT Rs.423 Cr vs Rs.364 Cr YoY
items.quote: CG Power an d Industrial Solution s, a subsidiary in which company holds 56.29% stake, registered a consolidated revenue of Rs.3,281 Crores during the quarter against Rs.2,878 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before tax for the quarter was Rs.423 Crores against Rs.364 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs.6,215 Cr vs Rs.5,309 Cr YoY; PBT Rs.461 Cr vs Rs.449 Cr YoY
items.quote: TI consolidated revenue for the quarter was Rs.6,215 Crores against Rs.5,309 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The profit before share of profit for JVs, exceptional items, and tax for the quarter was Rs.461 Crores against Rs.449 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 volume growth guidance maintained at 6-8%; EBITDA per metric ton guidance raised to INR 24,000-25,000 from INR 19,000-21,000
items.quote: As regards to our guidance for the full year, we maintain our volume guidance at 6% to 8% for the full -year FY26 -27, but I, however, increased the range of the EBITDA per metric ton guidance from the current INR 19,000 to INR 21,000 per metric ton to INR 24,000 to INR 25,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR 252.5 crore, up from INR 135.1 crore YoY; EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR 35,458 from INR 20,009
items.quote: For quarter one, I'm pleased to inform you all that the EBITDA stood at INR 252.5 crores compared to INR 135.1 crores in Q1 FY26, while EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR 35,458 per metric ton from approximately INR 20,009 per metric ton in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY with both segments in mid-single digits; India grew 11% led by double-digit performance segment growth and recovery in Tier 1 demand
items.quote: Consolidated volumes grew by 5% year-on-year with both our segments growing in mid-single-digit. Moving to our regional performance now. India, our primary engine grew by an impressive 11% led by double -digit growth in performance segment and high single -digit growth in specialty products

items.statement: Specialty Care mix improved, contributing positively to EBITDA per metric ton; specialty portfolio absolute growth strong but percentage share declined due to faster performance segment growth
items.quote: Specialty Care mix has improved, contributing positively to growth in EBITDA per metric ton, moving us steadily towards objective of improving the quality of our earnings through a richer and more differentiated product mix.

items.statement: Feedstock volatility sharp: crude averaged above USD 100/bbl; oleochemical feedstock moved from USD 2,800/MT to USD 3,300/MT before correcting below USD 2,500/MT by end-June
items.quote: Crude remained elevated throughout most of the quarter, averaging above USD 100 per barrel. The oleochemical feedstock prices also moved from average levels of USD 2,800 per metric ton to a high of USD 3,300 per metric ton for the quarter before correcting below USD 2,500 per ton towards the end of June.

items.statement: Fatty alcohol prices expected to move sideways between INR 2,600-2,800 per kg; Indonesian biodiesel mandate (40% to 50%) already factored into palm oil prices at USD 1,100-1,200
items.quote: We do see that there should be some steady state in the prices of fatty alcohol, because it's currently at about INR 2,700, INR 2,800 ship India. We do see that it should move sideways between INR 2,600 to INR 2,800.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 at INR 150 crore; Mexico EPC project on track for commercialization within 12 months; front-loaded capex for Beauty & Wellness capacity
items.quote: We talked about capex guidance. So I think this year, we will be at about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Mexico EPC project progressing as planned, contributing EPC service income; on track for commercialization over next 12 months
items.quote: I'm also pleased with the progress being made with our EPC project in Mexico. The project continues to progress as planned, contributing EPC service income during the quarter, and we remain on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.

items.statement: US market recovery driven by TRI-K premium specialties and Everbond new product; customer approvals and project pipelines maturing since February tariff clarity
items.quote: U.S. market as I said, our premium specialties led by our T RI-K business, , is certainly doing well. We also launched a new product called Everbond last year. It is showing very significant momentum in terms of customer acceptance.

items.statement: BASF announced closure of sulfation plant in Dahej; potential demand upside but too early to quantify as announcement only one week old
items.quote: With regard to BASF announcing its closure of its carry chemicals plant, sulfation plant in Dahej, ? This is something that, yes, it can. So we are waiting for our customers to engage with us, but to know whether we are able to sell, because it was only last week that they announced.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in West Asia remains fluid; longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs require close monitoring; El Nino may impact palm production next year
items.quote: We remain watchful of the evolving geopolitical situation and its potential implications for global supply chains. The operating environment continues to remain dynamic, and while the long-term growth potential of the region remains intact, we'll continue to prioritize agility, supply continuity and exceptional customer service as we navigate the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Export freight rates more than doubled due to West Asia crisis, impacting CIF pricing; supply chain disruptions caused 7-week washout at Egypt operations in April-May
items.quote: First of all, there was also a cost increase because if you look at my freight rates have more than doubled in the export side, which also goes into your price because the CIF price.

items.statement: Inorganic growth evaluation ongoing for Beauty & Wellness segment; significant work underway but no announcement yet; will not pursue deals that don't meet strategic and profitability criteria
items.quote: A lot of work has happened, but we have not been able to come up with any announcement. But it is suffice to say that a huge amount of work is happening. I do hope that we will be able to come up with something in the coming months.

items.statement: New product launches include SimpliX platform for personal care, Galaxy Hearth Biosurf for laundry (Innovation Zone Award winner), and Everbond from TRI-K; pipeline targeting >5% revenue contribution by 2030
items.quote: During the quarter, we introduced SimpliX, an innovative platform designed for modern personal care formulations such as body washers, facial cleansers and shampoos. SimpliX helps fo rmulators simplify product development while delivering superior mildness, enhanced sensorial attributes and formulation flexibility to meet evolving consumer preferences.

items.statement: AMET volumes down 4% YoY but up 19% sequentially; Egypt supply chain disruptions resolved by end-May; demand momentum strong, June onwards recovery substantial
items.quote: While AMET volumes were down 4% year -on-year, they improved by an impressive 19% sequentially, reflecting both the underlying strength of customer demand and the resilience of our business model in the region.

items.statement: Pricing discussions with customers are transparent; no pressure on rupee-term pricing as customers accept rationale for cost pass-through including currency depreciation
items.quote: No. I would not say there's any pressure on pricing because one of the things that the way that we engage with the customers on any pricing discussions is being transparent. So they know that we don't use any opportunity to profit here, but they're also very clear that based on the transparency, they know as to what are the reasons and why, you know, the price are increasing, what is the reason wh

items.statement: Indonesian biodiesel mandate increase from 40% to 50% already factored into palm oil prices; El Nino impact on next year's production a supply-side risk for fatty alcohol
items.quote: In fact, I'll be happy if it comes down, logically, it should, ? But there's also this aspect of El Nino next year, it will get impacted because El Nino this year is going to impact production use next year. So there can be supply-led support to the prices.

items.statement: No acquisition planned in AMET; future capex limited to debottlenecking; focus on diversifying Egypt portfolio to other countries to offset local customer churn
items.quote: See, AMET market very clearly, we have already done our capex. We obviously will be -- any capexes that we'll be doing there will be more in terms of certain debottlenecking exercises we'll do investments. There is no acquisition we are planning in AMET for sure.

items.statement: India rural demand outpacing urban; customers positive on demand momentum and launching market development initiatives; reformulation risk currently balanced but monitored
items.quote: With regard to India, we do see that the consumer demand. I think rural continues to outpace the urban demand. All our customers are their commentary, they're very positive in terms of the demand momentum getting better.

items.statement: Monsoon deficit could impact rural demand in H2; clarity expected by end of Q2; if rural demand impacted, H2 volumes could be lower than guidance upper range
items.quote: If that really is not an issue, I think, the H2 will be very different. It will certainly be better. But when we are looking at the guidance, we are also constrained to look at the guidance based on what our customers are looking at in terms of the demand, the way it's going to pan out.

items.statement: US customer approvals and project pipelines maturing sequentially since February; TRI-K Everbond showing significant customer acceptance and revenue contribution
items.quote: And we expect this to continue, because we're also seeing a good customer acceptance, a lot of project approvals and customer approvals also started falling in place, which also has led to this.

items.statement: Egypt operations team demonstrated resilience recovering volumes after 7-week supply chain washout; cross-functional coordination across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement and commercial teams
items.quote: What I found particularly encouraging, however, is the resilience demonstrated by our Egypt business and operations teams. As conditions gradually stabilized, we saw a strong recovery in momentum, supported by close coordination across manufacturing, suppl y chain, procurement and commercial teams

items.statement: Management aims to sustain double-digit revenue growth over the long term, averaging out quarterly volatility.
items.quote: we have been saying for the past few investor calls that what we have been aiming at to sustain a double-digit growth. So, whether that translates into what was the growth over the corresponding period last year or it would be more or less, the average would be a double-digit growth, which we would be trying to maintain.

items.statement: Mineral block sales are sustainable; scrap sales are cyclical but contribute 50-55% of e-commerce revenue and are somewhat sustainable on average.
items.quote: Regarding the second part of your question, whether it is sustainable, yes. As far as the mineral sale is concerned, it is sustainable. But scrap has always been a cyclical thing. The steel sector as such is very cyclical. So, the rates keep going up and down. And the volume of scrap, that also keeps changing from time to time.

items.statement: Management endeavors to maintain average EBITDA margins in the current 60%+ range, but cautions margins may face pressure at higher volumes.
items.quote: although the endeavor will be to have an average margin in the range of these, but of course, in a higher volume, it may get little bit steep.

items.statement: EPR certificate trading portal is developed and ready; awaiting government notification to operationalize, initially for 5 sectors expanding to 15.
items.quote: EPR ATP electronic portal for EPR certificate exchange that is also ready for CPCB. We are just waiting for the government now to formalize it so that the transactions can take place. As already intimated in the past few concalls this is as of now is going to be opened only for 5 sectors but slowly it will expand to about 15 sectors.

items.statement: TReDS platform is at advanced stage; awaiting RBI approval, targeting operationalization within FY27.

This project is also at an advanc

The initial discussion with certain stakeholders is already there. So, you will be updated about the progress in due course.

items.statement: Won Coal India coal linkage auction contract; first batch underway, to be extended sector-wise.
items.quote: We have also we had informed the stakeholders last time that we have won the contract with Coal India for coal linkage auctions. So, the first batch of auctions for the same is underway right now and it is expected to be extended to other sectors. This is the NRS linkage then it will be sector wise. Sectors wise also we will be doing shortly.

items.statement: Entered agreement with Tamil Nadu Forest Department for international competitive bidding of 100 tons of Red sandalwood.
items.quote: We have entered into an agreement with Tamil Nadu Forest Department. We had done this exercise about 4-5 years back where we sold some Red sandalwood in the past but again this time also we have entered into an agreement and this transaction will be taking place shortly for sale of about 100 tons of Red sandalwood that is available in the state but this will be through an international competitive

items.statement: Conducting first-ever auction for liquor licenses for Government of Karnataka.
items.quote: Another first that we have done in this quarter is the auction for liquor licenses for the government of Karnataka. We had done this exercise for Government of Rajasthan in the past but right now the other states are very slow in adopting this model and Karnataka Government has this time come up with this plan for conducting auctions for liquor licenses.

items.statement: Conducting charge point operator selection auction for Kerala State Electricity Board; model replicable to other states.
items.quote: for the first time we have done another auction for selection of charge point operators for Kerala State Electricity Board. Now this is a model that probably can be replicated by other states who will be approaching the other states for this kind of a model for allocation and selection of charge point operators given the impetus that is being given for EVs and other such electric vehicles.

items.statement: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited process scrap auction ongoing; expanding market for this product.
items.quote: We have entered into a very niche kind of auction for Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited. They have lot of process scrap, scrap that is generated during the steel making process which has to be cleared in a very time bound manner and the parameters for sale and the methodology of sale are slightly different from the normal scrap auction. So, we have had quite a good transaction with them and the sale i

items.statement: Land parcel auctions for Telangana state (HMDA and TSIIC) providing steady business.
items.quote: We have also been very steadily doing the land parcel auctions for Telangana state both for ( Metropolitan Development Authority and Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation which gives us steady business and steady remuneration.

items.statement: Commercial coal block auctions continuing (15th round, ongoing for 6-7 years).
items.quote: Commercial coal block auctions are also continuing and this is the 15th round. It has been going on for about almost 6-7 years now and for the first time we have done another auction for selection of charge point operators for Kerala State Electricity Board.

items.statement: Company remains asset-light; no major capex indicated, leveraging existing infrastructure for new verticals.
items.quote: We also took a decision to remain an asset-light company. So, apart from scaling up existing e-commerce business by aggressively expanding our client footprint, we decided to venture into a limited number of new verticals, stabilize those, scale them up and before thinking of expanding further.

items.statement: Travel portal infrastructure and software ready in-house; partnering with EaseMyTrip initially for B2B.
items.quote: See, as we said, the B2B segment is ready and we are using it internally and maybe for our other PSUs. To start with, we have partnered with EaseMyTrip because they have been in this sector for quite some time because they are a great aggregator and they were ready to partner with us. But going forward, we will be doing all these things on our own because the infrastructure is already available wi

items.statement: E-commerce revenue: 50-55% from scrap (3000+ sellers), balance from minerals, coal, platform services, software development.
items.quote: First of all, you need to understand that when I said more than 50%-55% of our revenue is coming from scrap doesn't mean that it is coming from one single seller. It is probably coming from 3000 sellers. So, even if one or two of our sellers are not really keen on doing transactions with us, we already have another set of clients and who are already onboarded.

items.statement: Focus on expanding private sector clientele (Tata, Reliance, Vedanta, ArcelorMittal) for scrap and other commodities to diversify from government business.
items.quote: So, we are interested in expanding the private sector business for scrap and other commodities also. So, I think in the past also we have very clearly mentioned that a lot of these big entities like Tata, Reliance, Vedanta and ArcelorMittal, they are doing their scrap as well as iron ore auctions, some coal auctions. These are also being transacted through our platform.

items.statement: Multiple coal exchanges expected per Gazette notification; MSTC evaluating own exchange, cites credibility advantage but acknowledges competition.
items.quote: Yes, actually, there are other entities also who are planning to launch their own coal exchanges. So, there will be multiple exchanges in the Gazette notification itself. It's very clearly mentioned that there will be multiple exchanges. So, basically, the transactions that actually happen on the exchanges, the volumes that actually get through those platforms, that will determine as to how much v

items.statement: EPR portal launch pending government notification; TReDS platform pending RBI approval; both are policy-driven timelines.
items.quote: Anytime it is expected to happen. These are policy decisions actually, so we cannot predict as to when the government will actually issue the notification.

items.statement: Revenue models vary: percentage of transaction value for some products, event-based fees for others, software development charges and AMCs for customized solutions.
items.quote: See, both the models are there. For certain products, it is the percentage of the transaction done and for certain things, it is based on the events only. And as I said, we are also into some kind of software development for our clients customized solutions. So, there again, it is a development charge and then AMCs. So, depending on the scope of work, these things vary.

items.statement: Dividend policy guided by DIPAM: minimum 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT, whichever is higher; FY26 dividend declared, subject to AGM approval.
items.quote: Already declared dividend, it was declared in the Quarter 4 Result, which will be subject to the approval of the shareholders in the ensuing annual general meeting. It is already there in the published in the Quarter 4 result. This year is concerned, it will be guided by the policy of the Government of India, that is a DIPAM. Minimum that is 4% of the net worth or 30% of the PAT, whichever is high

items.statement: MMRPL JV with Mahindra turned profitable in Q1 FY27 (PAT ~Rs 10 lakh share); driven by higher ELV feedstock from EPR norms and OEM/government incentives.
