items.statement: Capex of INR7.36 billion in Q1 FY27, of which INR5.88 billion deployed at Sri City plant; capitalization expected from H2 FY27
items.quote: On the capital expenditure, for the quarter, we land up at INR7.36 billion of out of which INR5.88 billion was deployed at Sri City. We expect capitalization to begin from the second half of this fiscal year as the aircon compressor and room air conditioner lines come on stream.

items.statement: Sri City plant: compressor production commenced Q3 FY27, room AC production in Q4 FY27; adding 2 million rotary compressor capacity; Greater Noida has 1 million AC compressor and 7 million refrigerator compressor capacity
items.quote: For air conditioners, we already operate 1 million capacity unit at our Greater Noida factory, and we are furthermore adding 2 million capacity at our Sri City plant. As far as refrigerators are concerned, we are already having a 7 million capacity at our Greater Noida factory.

items.statement: Localized major import resin for plastic molding components in Q1 FY27; using strategic sourcing, multiple suppliers, and value engineering to manage raw material costs
items.quote: For instance, in this first quarter of 2027, we localized a major import resin for our plastic molding components which have directly reduced our exposure to the rising import prices. Second is the strategic sourcing. We move flexibility between sourcing from local and import sources, whichever offers a better cost at that given point.

items.statement: B2B segment delivered strong growth in Q1 FY27; Information Display LED signages recorded highest ever quarterly sales with 36% market share; commercial AC expanding distribution network
items.quote: In information display panels, our LED signages recorded its highest ever quarterly sale in the Q1. And with continuous inflow of government and corporate orders, we have also achieved 36% market share in this business and now we have created roughly aroun d 5% gap with the number 2 player

items.statement: TV market share at 26%, OLED market share at 59%; widening gap with number two player across categories
items.quote: The TV market share is now touching 26% and OLED market share is touching 59%. And we are continuously increasing our gap with number two player.

items.statement: Government imposed quantitative restrictions on compressor imports from May 8, 2024: 60% of FY25 levels for reciprocating, 70% for rotary; LG positively positioned with local compressor production
items.quote: In this year, 8th of May, the Government of India, they introduced quantitative restriction on the import of compressors. So import of compressors are restricted against the financial year 2024-2025 up to 60% for the reciprocating compressors which we use for refrigerators and around 70% for the rotary compressor which we use for air conditioners.

items.statement: Working capital at INR12.56 billion as of June 30, 2026; optimized channel inventory and faster receivables realization; cash and bank balance at INR57.07 billion
items.quote: Working capital as of 30th June 2026 stood at INR12.56 billion. This reflects a strong sell-through season with optimized channel inventory and faster realization of receivables, giving our trade partners confidence as we head into the festival season. Our cash and bank balance stood at INR57.07 billion.

items.statement: Funding Sri City investment of INR5,000 crores through internal accruals without external borrowings; no debt raised for capex
items.quote: Preserving our internal accruals to fund this investment entirely without any external debt is a conscious and deliberate decision that we believe is in the best long -term interest of our shareholders.

items.statement: Dividend payout under review; preserving cash for Sri City investment; commitment to sustainable shareholder value remains unchanged
items.quote: We would like to assure our shareholders that this is not a permanent position. As our Sri City investment progresses in a phased manner and our cash generation strengthens further through revenue growth and margin improvement, we definitely plan to review our dividend plans.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned in transcript
items.quote: Today, we have our senior management with us, being represented by Mr. Dongmyung Seo, our Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Sanjay Chitkara, Co -CSMO; Mr. Atul Khanna, Chief Accounting Officer; Mr. Gaganjeet Singh, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Mr. Gurpinderjeet Singh, Head Financial Planning; and Mr. Soonjoo Seo, Investor Relations Officer.

items.statement: B2B segment targeting 20% CAGR growth trajectory (FY22-FY25 achieved); Information Display at 36% market share
items.quote: Backed by these multiple growth catalyst, we are very confident of delivering 20% CAGR growth trajectory which we have already delivered from financial year 2022 to 2025.

items.statement: Macroeconomic environment with currency depreciation, elevated raw material prices, and geopolitical uncertainties require financial prudence
items.quote: Additionally, the current macroeconomic environment with currency depreciation, elevated raw material prices, and geopolitical uncertainties require a certain level of financial prudence.

items.statement: Data center cooling seen as meaningful long-term opportunity for B2B; mid-scale segment already live with Multi VRF and chiller systems; hyper-scale segment at preliminary stage
items.quote: LG India, we see this data center cooling as a meaningful long -term opportunity and this is for our B2B business. While we look at this opportunity in 2 parts, yo u know, and we are at different stages in each. On the mid-scale side, this is already a live business for us

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR840 crores (INR720 crores granite, INR100-120 crores quartz)
items.quote: FY27 we will be close to -- we are estimating around INR840 crores against past year's number of INR645 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected in same range as previous years (26-27%) with slight quartz impact
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the same range. Except the quartz-related weighted average factor if at all there is a little impact, to that extent there will be impact on the EBITDA.

items.statement: Granite revenue growth guided at 10-12% for FY27
items.quote: if you remember in the last call, last few calls also we have guided 12% on the granite, so we have beaten that by good margin.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 2 capex of INR125 crores split over current and next year
items.quote: Capex on quartz would be approximately INR125 crores.

items.statement: Sri Lanka project plant building capex around INR120 crores
items.quote: Sri Lankan project for plant building it's around INR120 crores.

items.statement: Indonesia JV capex higher than Kerala project, details in 45-60 days
items.quote: So I think the capex will be a close if the first project will be higher than in Kerala, but the absolute number I think we will be able to give you next during next call because we are still doing a lot of work on the project report right now which will be ready in next 45 to 60 days.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 1 targeting 15,000 tons/month run rate by year end, currently at 5,000 tons sold in Q1
items.quote: We will be stabilizing by the year end at around 15,000 tons plus above per month.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 2 commissioning within 10-12 months
items.quote: We will be in line to commission the Phase 2 in the next within the next 10 to 12 months.

items.statement: Indonesia MoU with PERMINAS for rare earths access, JV formation this quarter
items.quote: Now, this MoU will be translated into an agreement to form a JV along with them and I think you will find developments on that during this quarter which we will update you in the next meeting.

items.statement: Sri Lanka policy finalized, license expected this quarter, ground breaking in October
items.quote: And post that, we have received the necessary communication from the government to complete the data points wherein we are confirming our production, our investment, and our timelines to them to develop this project. I think that is the final milestone before we receive the eventual license.

items.statement: Granite demand good with 35% topline growth, pricing realization better
items.quote: Demand is good, you can see from the numbers we have 35% topline growth. I think if you remove the quartz part, we are still above 30.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin down 190 bps due to diesel cost spike from INR85 to INR125-130/litre
items.quote: The reason being that we were very proactive and we got our fleet electrified from and whatever vehicles we are sweating, we electrified that fleet and then we back integrated with solar, so our opex costs are less dependent now on diesel fluctuations.

items.statement: FY28 blended EBITDA margin expected around 29-30% with quartz contribution
items.quote: EBITDA would be close to 30%, little above 30%. And overall blended EBITDA might be around 29%, 30%.

items.statement: Granite price increase of 3-5% implemented to offset diesel cost
items.quote: Around that, around that range.

items.statement: Diesel cost is 13% of total cost, fleet electrification and solar reducing dependency
items.quote: The biggest lever in this is the volume growth, right revenue growth. So if if revenue growth is able to absorb most of the other costs, fixed costs and I think that revenue growth we will be able to meet, we feel as of now.

items.statement: Quartz sales mix 65% engineered stone, 35% solar
items.quote: Around 60% to 65% engineered stone, balance solar. I think 65-35 is a reasonable assumption.

items.statement: Quartz realization around INR10,000 per ton
items.quote: Around INR10,000 per ton.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 1 FY28 revenue estimated at INR180-200 crores at 15,000 tons/month
items.quote: 180 to 200. Management: So that is the range once you have touched the 15,000 ton mark per month

items.statement: Quartz Phase 1 + Phase 2 FY28 revenue target INR200-240 crores
items.quote: I think we are targeting 200 plus definitely for next financial year. That number could be anywhere between 200 to 230, 240, let's look at it.

items.statement: Most shipments on FOB basis, freight cost passed to customer
items.quote: So usually most of shipments are FOB basis. So freight is always to the customer historically.

items.statement: Gearing ratio at 0.2x, capex funded from internal accruals and fresh equity
items.quote: Our gearing ratio today is at a 0.2 times. So we have leverage on that front.

items.statement: No near-term plan to reduce promoter holding from 77% to 75%
items.quote: No, we have enough time and I don't think we are looking at it in near term to get down to 75%.

items.statement: Kerala JV stalled due to new government, awaiting MD appointment at KMML
items.quote: So post signing the -- post last development, there is no development this quarter, primarily because there is a new government there and they are just settling down.

items.statement: Sierra Leone subsidiary has no update, minimum expenditure, still evaluating concessions
items.quote: So this quarter there is no update and there is -- we have looked at a couple of concessions which had local issues, so we are still actively looking for there.

items.statement: Indonesia ionic clay deposits provide access to heavy rare earths (Dy, Tb) not available in India
items.quote: Heavy rare earths are only in certain geographic areas, which are already mostly contracted or acquired by the Chinese companies. So which means there are very less territories where we can get access to DyTb.

items.statement: Not participating in India PLI scheme for magnet production, focused on oxide production
items.quote: No, we are not looking at any magnet production as of now. All those schemes are for magnet production.

items.statement: Middle East crisis negatively impacting volumes for last 5-6 months; sequential improvement seen in transatlantic, transpacific, intra-Asian lanes
items.quote: we are all aware that there's a crisis going on in the Middle East, which is impacting trade and is naturally impacting our volumes also negatively, and that has remained so for the last 5 months to 6 months

items.statement: LCL and air volumes up ~5% QoQ; FCL up ~1% QoQ; half of growth from market, half from outperformance
items.quote: we have seen incremental volumes in both LCL and air of the magnitude of about 5%, while on the FCL, we have seen a quarter-on-quarter growth rate of about 1%

items.statement: Carrier capacity constrained, freight rates higher over last few months, reflected in revenues and operating costs
items.quote: the capacity on the carrier side has been somewhat more constrained with all these disruptions. And as an outcome of that, the freight rates prevailing over the last few months have been on the higher side

items.statement: Focus on cost control via technology, Agentic AI, offshoring to lower-cost geographies; single global system for finance, HR, operations
items.quote: We have also focused a lot on company-specific initiatives on how we could keep our cost under control and not just mitigate the inflationary measures, but also perhaps bring down the costs over the last year's base using opportunities on both technology-led automations, replacing some of the work with Agentic AI

items.statement: No significant economic improvement assumed; base case plans for no major change over next 12 months; focus on market share gains and cost control
items.quote: As we move forward, we are not taking into account any significant improvements in the economic environment as we prepare for our business strategy

items.statement: Reduced loss-making trade lanes, improved container utilization; gross profit per unit improved; staff/admin cost focus via tech and offshoring
items.quote: we have brought down our loss-making trade lanes, focused on container utilization, and all of these factors contribute to improved gross profits per unit of cargo that we carry

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 3,522 cr, up 5.8% YoY and 20.8% QoQ; gross profit INR 733 cr, up 2.5% YoY and 6.5% QoQ
items.quote: consolidated revenue of INR3,522 crores for Q1 of FY '27, representing 5.8% year-on-year growth and 20.8% sequentially. Gross profit stood at INR733 crores, up 2.5% year-on-year and 6.5% quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: EBITDA INR 33 cr vs loss of INR 31 cr YoY and INR 17 cr QoQ; EBIT loss INR 18 cr vs loss INR 77 cr YoY and loss INR 33 cr QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR33 crores compared to a loss of INR31 crores last year in Q1 of FY '26 and EBITDA of INR17 crores in Q4 FY '26

items.statement: Standalone borrowings reduced to INR 272 cr as of June 30, 2026 from INR 314 cr as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: We further reduced higher cost standalone borrowings to INR272 crores as of June 30th, 2026, from INR314 crores a s of March 31, 2026

items.statement: Gross margin % not relevant due to volatile freight pass-through; focus on gross profit per CBM (LCL) and per TEU (FCL) as yield metric
items.quote: gross margin honestly does not hold any significant value because gross margin means your profit in percentage terms. In our business, a significant amount of our cost is ocean freight, which is extremely volatile and can vary signif icantly, and this largely serves as the pass-through cost

items.statement: Intent to keep costs flat in USD terms; rupee translation effects offset on revenue side
items.quote: our intent is to keep the cost flat in dollar terms. And so, therefore, only increase that you would see would be on account of, you know, translation of the global cost from U.S. dollars into rupees

items.statement: Global LCL market share ~14.5%; FCL share <1%; LCL highest margin, lowest working capital; LCL grows ~2x FCL industry rate
items.quote: across these markets the re are only a handful of global players, and we are the market leaders globally, holding about 14.5% market share in this business

items.statement: LCL volumes ~4% below couple years ago; industry LCL down 13-14%; Allcargo outperforming by ~3-4%; FCL grew 18-20% CAGR over 7-8 years but recent de-growth
items.quote: we are almost 10% below on the LCL volumes to where we were a couple of years back. And last 2 years, the environment has been quite worse. The actual volumes possibly for the industry have come down by almost 13% to 14%

items.statement: Base case: marginal volume uptick for next few months (seasonal pre-Christmas), no substantial growth; profitability improvement via yield maintenance and cost control
items.quote: the base case that we are running is a continued marginal uptick in volumes for the next few months, which is the typical trend in the industry

items.statement: Historical ROCE north of 20%; target to return to that zone; 12-15% volume growth from current levels would achieve desired trajectories
items.quote: maybe a 12% to 15% growth on volumes from here should put us in all the right desired trajectories

items.statement: No near-term acquisition needs; present in all relevant markets and products; strategy to grow organically by investing in people
items.quote: At this point in time, we do not foresee any need for any further markets. We are present in all the relevant markets. We are present in all the products that we want to be. And with the network strength that we have over the last couple of years, we have grown more organically

items.statement: Asset-light business; capex tiny fraction of P&L; depreciation largely non-cash from goodwill and past acquisitions
items.quote: it's an extremely asset-light business with hardly any capital assets owned or even the capex investments are a tiny fraction of the company's P&L and therefore, most of the depreciation would be non-cash in nature

items.statement: Working capital debt largely offset by cash balances; single global bank used; net debt ~60% of gross; target significant net debt reduction in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: some part of this is also not interest bearing as it gets offset by the cash sitting on books as well. And being a global company, sometimes moving cash across borders may not be most efficient

items.statement: LCL ~2/3, FCL ~1/3 of volumes; LCL yield higher than FCL; air freight sits in middle; LCL most profitable, lowest working capital
items.quote: As we have historically stated the LCL and FCL breakup is about two-thirds, one-third

items.statement: Higher freight rates improve LCL container utilization and FCL margins; absolute gross profit correlates with freight environment despite pass-through
items.quote: in higher freight rate environments, we tend to see marginal improvements in our utilization, which leads to improved profitability. On the FCL side, that to some extent has a profitability bearing

items.statement: Q1 gross profit grew 6.6% QoQ vs ~4.2% expected from volume alone; extra 2-2.5% from freight rate tailwinds and efficiencies
items.quote: Compared to that, the gross profit has grown about 6.6%. So that extra two to two and a half percent is largely coming from slightl y marginal impact of the freight rate environment and some of the efficiencies brought in as

items.statement: Monthly business updates to commence providing yield trends (scale/index) for LCL and FCL; no absolute yield numbers disclosed
items.quote: we provide a monthly update, which would commence, as the company has now got listed earlier, we used to provide it as a business update, now it will come in for the company update starting this month

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts unpredictable; Middle East crisis timing unknown; trade environment volatility increased over last 5 years
items.quote: geopolitical conflicts cannot be predicted at least by us on the business side, and therefore we go in with the assumption of no significant growth over the next 12 months

items.statement: ~15% business in India, 80-85% outside; costs in USD, EUR, local currencies; USD dominant for analysis; rupee volatility affects reported INR numbers
items.quote: 15% of our business sits in India, approximately. 80% to 85% business sits outside India. Now, the biggest cost contribution comes in from ocean freight, which largely operates in U.S. dollar terms

items.statement: Continued focus on offshoring resources to lower-cost geographies enabled by single global system investments
items.quote: continuing our drive to have more and more resources based in lower cost geographies, which is made possible by our continued focus and investments in creating one single system for finance, HR, operations across the globe

items.statement: Business generates cash; debt reduced sequentially over last couple of years via operating initiatives and asset divestments
items.quote: we have sequentially brought down the debt on our books, which has been an outcome of cash generation with both, you know, operating business initiatives plus some of the asset divestmen t initiatives as

items.statement: Non-core asset sales (warehousing, office) estimated USD 10-15 million combined to aid net debt reduction
items.quote: these would be some of the warehousing and office assets that we own, which combined could be just a very ballpark number would be somewhere around USD10 million to USD15 million all combined

items.statement: Annual revenue growth guidance of 30% and 100% EBITDA improvement maintained for FY27
items.quote: To add on here, the annual guidance was 30% revenue improvement and 100% EBITDA improvement remains the same.

items.statement: Offline business guided to near profitability in FY27
items.quote: So, I think the overall guidance for offline business is near profitability this year. We are we are confident that we will achieve those guidance.

items.statement: Online early learning and K-12 revenue grew 88% YoY to INR105 crores; enrollments up 41% to 0.78 million
items.quote: Revenue-wise, it has grown by 88% year-on-year from INR56 crores to INR105 crores. This includes Pre-Foundation Grade 6 to 8, Curious Junior, our state boards categories across different states.

items.statement: NEET PG enrollments grew ~50% and collections grew 100% YoY
items.quote: We have seen NEET PG enrollments growing approximately by 50% and the collection are growing by 100% in NEET PG.

items.statement: Vernacular category enrollments and revenue up 1.7x YoY; state board enrollments and revenue doubled
items.value: 1.7x enrollment and revenue growth (vernacular); 2x enrollment and revenue growth (state boards)
items.quote: vernacular, which is a vision to make a pan-India brand, we have 1.7x jump in our enrollments and revenue in vernacular categories. K-12, Alakh already spoke about, like 41% jump in enrollment and 88% jump in our revenue. Along with that, our state board, which is a huge, huge TAM, the enrollments are doubled, so does the revenue is doubled.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA loss narrowed to INR44 crores (4% margin) from INR106 crores YoY, a 624 bps improvement
items.value: -4% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin; 624 bps improvement
items.quote: our first quarter pre-Ind AS EBITDA closed at negative INR44 crores, equating to 4%, with an improvement of 624 basis points from Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Online EBITDA margin improved ~600 bps YoY in Q1; FY26 online margin was ~27%
items.quote: last fiscal year we witnessed around 27% margins. As Prateek sir already mentioned, I think path to higher profitability some of these categories UPSC, GATE, Foundation and state boards, we are already seeing that they are approaching towards higher profitability and mature categories like JEE, NEET. So, margins from here onwards are definitely going to improve.

items.statement: Offline expansion to be opportunistic and limited to geographies fitting cohort economics; new center planning to be decided over next 2 quarters
items.quote: Our approach to offline expansion will be opportunistic and limited to geographies that fit into our cohort economics. Accordingly, new centers planning would probably get decided over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Treasury increased by INR600 crores QoQ to INR5,600 crores due to negative working capital cycle (upfront student fee collections)
items.quote: Again, this is a cyclic nature of business where it's a negative working capital cycle business where student pays the fees upfront and that remains in our treasury. So, that is one primary reason that quarter specifically quarter one if you compare the cash position from the last year, like from last quarter to this quarter is improved by INR600 odd crores.

items.statement: Treasury of INR5,600 crores includes INR2,000 crores IPO proceeds; capital allocation focused on online content/categories (organic and inorganic)
items.value: INR5,600 crores treasury (incl. INR2,000 crores IPO proceeds)
items.quote: as of June 30, our treasury is INR5,600 crores, including IPO proceeds of INR2,000 crores. Like I mentioned last time, our capital allocation will largely be towards new online content and categories, both organic and inorganic.

items.statement: Divesting Finzy Fintech; received interest and signed 2 non-binding term sheets; expect completion in a quarter
items.quote: Along with the capital allocation, we have decided to divest Finzy Fintech and we have already received couple of interest and signed 2 non-binding term sheets. So, probably in a quarter timeline we will be able to achieve this divestment.

items.statement: School integrated program expanded from 15 to 50+ partner schools pan-India; asset-light model with admission guarantees
items.quote: School integrated program is a pan-India program in which we do partnership with existing schools and send our Vidyapeeth faculties so that students can prepare then and there within the schools. And that partnership number grew from 15 schools to more than 50 school last year.

items.statement: Offline ARPU rising 7% despite competition; competitors' ARPU flat or shrinking; focus on results and experience over affordability
items.quote: we are continue to show ARPU improvement in our Vidyapeeth, which is 70% of our offline business, and we have already demonstrated 7% ARPU improvement. That shows that despite the intensified competition, we are continued to show the higher ARPU in our offline business and where our competitors' ARPU is almost flat or shrinking.

items.statement: NEET UG calendar shifted by 5-7 weeks in 2024 and 2025, causing enrollment timing shifts between quarters
items.quote: This is primarily because of the shift in the cycle of the NEET examination, which happened in 2024 as well, and annual basis we saw no change in the overall enrollment in 2024 and similar results we are expecting this year and we can witness this happening in July as well. So, the enrollment for NEET have shifted.

items.statement: Gross margin expected in 67%-69% range for FY27
items.quote: I would try to kind of keep it in the 67% to 69% zipcode, right, like at least for this year and see where it goes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin 11.5%, up from 5% YoY and 1.2pp QoQ
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA increased from INR 17 crores to INR50 crores. That's 201% growth year-over-year. Margins expanded from 5% to 11.5%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 PAT margin 7.5%, up from 1.1% YoY
items.quote: PAT increased from INR4 crores to INR34 crores. PAT margin expanded from 1.1% to 7.5%, almost a 6.3 percentage point improvement.

items.statement: Gross margin 67.3% in Q1 FY27, down 2.2pp YoY but up 0.5pp QoQ
items.quote: The ratio moved from 31% to 33%. So gross margin was 67.3%, down 2.2 points year-over-year but up about 0.5 point sequentially.

items.statement: Revenue grew 32% YoY (21% constant currency) to INR 437 cr, highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: Revenue was INR 437 crores, up 32% year-on-year, and 21% on a constant currency basis. That's a strong start of the year and our highest ever quarterly revenue in the history of the company.

items.statement: Cloud Modernization grew 17% reported YoY; excluding base effect would be ~32%
items.quote: Cloud modernization grew 17% reported. And as I mentioned earlier, excluding the base effect would have reported a 32% growth rate.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month net revenue retention (NRR) reached 125%
items.quote: We saw our trailing 12-month net retention, NRR going up to 125%.

items.statement: Content processed 959,000 hours (+43% YoY); deliveries 9,900+ endpoints (+21% YoY); ad impressions 13.6B (+59% YoY)
items.quote: The content processed reached 959,000 hours, which is almost a 43% year-on-year uptick that we've seen there. Our deliveries reached 9,900-plus delivery options today in endpoints. Distributors, we've reached almost 451, up again by 21%. And more importantly, all of this leads to ad impressions reach of 13.6 billion for the quarter, which is almost up 59%.

items.statement: AI product Newspulse has 10+ active pilots; major US news network selected it for AI-first newsroom transformation
items.quote: We have more than 10 active pilots across different customers. And more importantly, we had a major U.S. news network that selected Amagi's Newspulse to transform themselves into an AI-first newsroom.

items.statement: Planning broader AI product suite launch at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27
items.quote: currently, we plan to introduce a broader product suite at our flagship industry confere nces in Q2

items.statement: Global customer wins across US, Australia, Middle East, India, APAC; 400+ content providers, 451 distributors, 80+ advertisers
items.quote: We have wins across not only U.S. but Australia, the Middle East, India and the broader APAC region as well. So clearly, you see that there's a global expansion that's starting to happen in our business.

items.statement: Major US broadcaster achieved 100% on-air availability for FIFA World Cup (104 matches, 325 events, 450 hours)
items.quote: For one of the U.S. broadcasters, we supported 325 different events and 450 hours of events, including shoulder programming, and we had to provide them 100% on-air availability, which is what we provided.

items.statement: DSO improved sequentially by ~8 days in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The biggest piece being receivables where on DSO, we saw a sequential improvement of about 8 days quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Generated $282,000 monthly run-rate cloud cost savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives
items.quote: In Q1, we generated about $282,000 of monthly run rate savings in gross margin cloud cost optimization that we've reinvested into the AI-related initiatives.

items.statement: Evaluated 33 M&A opportunities since Jan, passed on 23, 10 under active evaluation; capability-led focus
items.quote: Since January, we've evaluated 33 opportunities, passed on 23, and we have 10 under active evaluation.

items.statement: Pricing adjustments made only when volume run-rate clearly outweighs price trade-off; one customer tracking >30% run-rate growth post-adjustment
items.quote: Our approach is fairly disciplined. We adjust only when the volume run rate clearly outweighs the price trade-off like we've mentioned in previous calls. The customer example we shared earlier is tracking at more than 30% run rate growth even after the pricing adjustment.

items.statement: AI pricing model uses credit-based system mimicking cost-plus; outcome-driven pricing being tested with telemetry
items.quote: We've built an AI credits model. For example, if you're a customer coming to Amagi and you want to, I don't know, convert your language to Spanish from English, for example, you pay on a number of credits with the company.

items.statement: AI gross margin impact may follow S-curve: initial dip then recovery over 2-3 years, similar to historical 64% to 69% trajectory
items.quote: You may see a little bit of a dip initially, but it will come back to where it needs to be. And that's exactly been a historical trajectory as well. If you look 3, 4 years back, our gross margin was around 64%, right? And we've kind of taken a long-term sort of approach to get to 69%. And I think AI is going to sort of play out a similar curve in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 YoY compare has ~600bps headwind from prior year rev rec timing benefit; H1 historically 47% of revenue, 37% of EBITDA
items.quote: Q2 FY 26 had the same rev rec timing benefit, which we've disclosed in the earlier calls. So, the Q2 year-over-year compare has a headwind of about 600 basis points.

items.statement: Logo churn in low single digits; top 10 customer average vintage ~5 years
items.quote: if you look at our logo churn, it's pretty much in low single digits. And the average vintage of our top 10 custom ers is sort of 5 years

items.statement: No in-sourcing risk seen; platforms outsourcing ad insertion due to scale and complexity
items.quote: Platforms today are fundamentally looking to outsource rather than in-source. So, in-sourcing is not happening, and at least we are not seeing that across the industry.

items.statement: Video fabric infrastructure investments enable mission-critical scale; 100% availability for FIFA World Cup delivery
items.quote: We operate what we call a video fabric, the underlying mesh of compute, networking, storage and orchestration that makes this whole glass-to-glass operations possible.

items.statement: TAM ~$17B across modernization, unification, monetization; AI could nearly double opportunity over time
items.quote: Across modernization, unification and monetization and marketplaces, our total TAM is roughly $17 billion. But I wanted to highlight a bigger point that's starting to evolve in our industry and in the market that we serve today is that AI, we believe, could nearly double that opportunity over time.

items.statement: Aspiration to maintain growth rates; Q2 not best marker due to base effect lapping
items.quote: our aspiration is to continue to kind of maintain those sort of growt h rates, Rishi. We'll obv iously see how things play out. But again, Q2 will have a little bit of, again, a big lapping of that year-over-year comparison like we disclosed proactively

items.statement: Management targets adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full year FY27 and expects service EBITDA margin to reach 23-24% over next 4-5 years
items.quote: We also indicated that we'll try really hard for the entire year to be adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the current year.

items.statement: Corporate overheads expected to fall below 7-8% of revenue over next 4-5 years
items.quote: Our corporate overheads continue to reduce and we expect over the next four to five years for it to come below to 7-8%.

items.statement: Platform premium grew 49% YoY to INR 1,204 crores in Q1 FY27, largely from B30 markets
items.quote: Our platform premium grew 49% to INR 1,204 crores, large part of it comes from B30 markets.

items.statement: Health premium grew ~45% YoY and term life grew ~60% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For example, health has grown at about 45% plus. Term life has grown at about 60% plus.

items.statement: Total digital partner base reached ~690,000 with 32,000+ recruited in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In Q1, we recruited more than 32,000 digital partners, taking our total DP base to about 6,90,000 plus.

items.statement: P3M active digital partners grew ~33% YoY to 90,791 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our past three months active DPs increased to 90,791 in Q1 compared with 72,244 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Service EBITDA grew 89% YoY to INR 39 crores (13% of revenue) in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our service EBITDA grew by 89% to INR 39 crores as margins continue to expand.

items.statement: Corporate overheads fell from 30% to 22% of revenue YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On a YoY basis, our corporate overhead as a percentage of revenue came down from 30% to 22%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -9% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from -21% a year ago
items.quote: Led by strong growth, margin expansion and operating leverage, our adjusted EBITDA loss as a percentage of revenue compared to last year of minus 21% is now minus 9%.

items.statement: Renewal service EBITDA is 2.5-3x higher than new business service EBITDA due to lower CAC and better insurer terms
items.quote: Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

items.statement: Renewal revenue share increased to 22% of total revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19% a year ago
items.quote: Renewal revenue last year was 19%. This year, it has gone up to 22% in Q1.

items.statement: Renewal revenue grew 66% YoY to over INR 65 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our renewal revenues grew to over INR 65 crores in the quarter.

items.statement: Policy count reached 3.1 crores as of Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our policy count up to Q1 now has touched 3.1 crores.

items.statement: Claims settled exceeded INR 26 crores with 1.5 lakh+ servicing requests handled in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During Q1, we helped policyholders settle claims amounting to more than INR 26 crores, there would have been some complexity delay or rejection. We handled around 1.5 lakh plus unique servicing requests during this quarter.

items.statement: Take rates remain stable; revenue mix shift toward renewables drives margin expansion
items.quote: Take rates are more or less similar of what it was before.

items.statement: AI handles 55% of support tickets; 2M documents processed via AI; 75% of new code AI-generated in Q1 FY27
items.quote: AI also now handles 55% of our support tickets. Nearly 2 million documents were fully processed using AI last quarter. AI not just is improving efficiency, but also it improves customer experience.

items.statement: Voice AI renewal calls achieve 500 bps higher renewal rates vs non-AI calls
items.quote: These AI-called customers show a renewal rate that is higher by 500 basis points, primarily due to stronger follow ups and use of local language by the AI.

items.statement: Turnaround times reduced 50-60% across processes through AI adoption
items.quote: Across various processes, we have seen our tATs reduced by 50-60%.

items.statement: Cross-sell activation: motor-only DPs selling health grew 40%+ YoY
items.quote: we have been able to grow motor -only digital partners starting to sell health by 40 plus percent

items.statement: Supreme Court TP reserving judgment impact uncertain; insurers await GIC appeal outcome before provisioning
items.quote: Other insurance companies are waiting for the GIC's appeal (GI counsel's appeal) in the Supreme Court and waiting to hear the outcome of it before they look at their provisioning.

items.statement: Potential fuel denial for uninsured vehicles could create massive demand tailwind as seen with 2019 two-wheeler fines
items.quote: What we have seen in the past is when th is two-wheeler fines were implemented in 2019, the awareness of this requirement for a TP policy goes up significantly and the demand shoots up

items.statement: Disciplined cash management keeps cash conversion from profitability very high
items.quote: Disciplined in cash management and working capital management that keeps our cash conversion from profitability very high.

items.statement: ESOP cost modest at INR 7 crores in Q1 FY27; minimal gap between adjusted EBITDA and PAT
items.quote: Our ESOP costs are modest, which I guided for this quarter, for example, the ESOP cost is about INR 7 crores and that's it.

items.statement: DP attrition stable: 28-30% in first 24 months, then 2-3%; 65% retention at year 5-6
items.quote: Basically, over the years, we know that in the first 18 months, there is a learning curve. And you see some attrition of about 28 -30% in the first 24 months. Then the attrition rate drops to 2-3% where basically 95% of the people after 18 months retain on the platform.

items.statement: Commission regulation changes speculative; health GST commission reset passed through but volumes grew
items.quote: The way we had operated that time was whatever reset happened in the market, that reset was passed down, but we also saw increase in the volume in terms of how much business started happening on the platform, and that led to growth in both the categories of product that were impacted life and health.

items.statement: Management expects 35% top-line and EBITDA growth in FY27 versus FY26, with similar growth continuing in FY28 and FY29
items.quote: I think we're expecting 35% growth in our top line in this financial year. And similarly, EBITDA also, we'll see the same growth coming up in this financial year as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Management expects at least 30% top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 and FY28, with visible growth through FY29
items.quote: Both for top line and bottom line, you can expect a decent growth, 30% plus in coming year. And same growth will continue in FY28 also because these capex's, what are coming on a stream, this year where 2 have come on stream, 1 is coming up in the first half.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin was 15.5% in Q1 FY27; management expects 14%+ EBITDA margin for full FY27
items.quote: As of now, what we can perceive that, that will happen. But if things remain as good as they are currently and no untoward incident happens on the geopolitical front, we'll give you better results than this.

items.statement: Management confident of holding current margins throughout the year despite potential price corrections
items.quote: We are confident that we will hold those margins throughout the year.

items.statement: Capex cycle for FY27 is ~75% complete; remaining new capex estimated at USD 80-100 million for FY27-28
items.quote: From this, you can see our capex cycle for this financial year is almost 75% done. And whatever capex's are remaining, which are new capex's of around, if you put total all this will be around USD 100 million or less USD 80 million capex, we'll be doing going forward.

items.statement: Noida 39,000 MT recycling plant commissioned April 30, 2026; Mexico 80M unit WPP bags plant commissioned July 31, 2026; Egypt 12B pack Aseptic plant on schedule for H1 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: 39,000 metric tons per annum recycling plant at Noida Sector 155 was successfully commissioned on April 30, 2026. 80-million-unit WPP bags plant in Mexico was commissioned on July 31, 2026. Work on our Greenfield Aseptic project in Egypt, 12 billion packs remain on schedule for commissioning in FY27.

items.statement: Egypt Aseptic plant targeting 30% utilization (2B packs) in first year, 60-70% in second year, 100% by third year
items.quote: Out of 12 billion packs, which is the annual capacity, we can do 30% in first year. Second year, certainly, we'll reach around 60% to 70%. And third year, we'll reach around 100% capacity there.

items.statement: Management expects to double volumes from current ~173,000 MT to ~346,000 MT by FY29 as new capacities ramp up
items.quote: If you add up the capacities what are coming up, if I can add up, we should double our quantity in next 3 years' time.

items.statement: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET prices up 30-35% from February 2026 levels; prices currently stable with no major correction expected while West Asia crisis continues
items.quote: BOPP prices have gone up by 25%, and BOPET prices have gone up by almost 30%-35% from, to be specific from February '26 level to now, it is 25-32% higher on BOPP and BOPET rate is around 30-35% higher.

items.statement: Raw material prices rising but less than finished goods prices; spreads normalizing
items.quote: See raw material prices are also moving up, but not to that extent what the finished good prices are moving up because it is being normalized now and prices are, I think, getting normalized as of now.

items.statement: Overseas operations drove 80% of incremental revenue; Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria and India PET chips key profitability drivers
items.quote: With 80% incremental revenue contributed by overseas operations and 20% by India, our incremental revenue was RS. 14,753 million in Q1.

items.statement: Americas volumes up 18% YoY supported by US onshoring push; Middle East & Africa up 14.9% YoY on supply chain derisking; Europe flat YoY with seasonal moderation expected next quarter
items.quote: Americas sales volume increased 18% Y-o-Y to 31,724 metric tons. This was supported by the U.S. government push for domestic production and onshoring amid evolving trade policies.

items.statement: Strategic shift to high-margin products in India flexible packaging; Aseptic volumes soft due to duty-free imports but value growth maintained; 60-70% of future capex allocated to value-added products
items.quote: Whatever capex we do going forward, at least 60% to 70% will go into value-added products only and balance can go into maintenance or regular products.

items.statement: Debt/EBITDA reduced from 4.5x in FY26 to 3.5x in Q1 FY27; targeting below 3x by FY28 as capacities reach full utilization
items.quote: Our Debt-EBITDA margin was around 4.5x, which you would see in this quarter itself, it has come down to 3.5. And going forward also, we'll ensure that we retain the same kind of leverage what we have as of now. And this leverage will come down by end of FY28 much lower once all these capacities, what are not utilized to the 100% becomes 100% capacity utilization, then you will see our leverage goi

items.statement: Interest cost reduced 0.3-0.4% in Q1; targeting further 1% reduction over next year
items.quote: we should reduce our interest costs by 1% in next 1 years' time. And you will see that even if you reduce by 1% going forward, there will Q1 FY27 EARNINGS CONFERENCE CALL: AUGUST 17, 2026 Page 23 | 25 be a great reduction. That's why you can see the reduction of 0.3% -0.4% in this quarter itself

items.statement: Company does not carry significant inventory due to price volatility; pricing gains passed through to customers
items.quote: In our business, we don't carry much inventory in our books of accounts because prices fluctuate too often here. Whatever gain you are seeing in our volume as well as in our prices, they are the prices which have been passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs. 53,972 million; EBITDA rose 92% YoY to Rs. 9,198 million with margin expanding 480 bps to 17% (highest in 21 quarters)
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 grew 38% Y-o-Y to Rs. 53,972 million. EBITDA rose 92% Y-o-Y to Rs. 9,198 million with EBITDA margin expanding 480 basis points Y-o-Y to 17%, marking our highest EBITDA performance in the last 21 quarters.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA (ex forex derivatives) grew 78% YoY to Rs. 8,373 million at 15.5% margin; PAT Rs. 4,233 million at 7.8% net margin vs 1.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA post adjustment of Rs. 825 million on forex derivative transactions reached Rs. 8,373 million, which is 78% growth year-on-year, expanded to 15.5%.

items.statement: Overseas customers prefer local/regional sourcing to derisk supply chains; UFlex's geographic diversification and integrated model commands premium pricing
items.quote: We are derisking our top-line model in such a way that where we are present at least 75% of our turnover should come from near to our customer policy, that is what we are adopting.

items.statement: Aseptic packaging facing duty-free imports from Indonesia under trade treaty; India consumer market growing 5-8% annually supporting long-term demand
items.quote: What has happened in Aseptic, we are getting a lot of duty-free imports from Indonesia, where India has signed a treaty where duty-free imports keep on coming. But Indian consumer market is growing at least 5% to 8% each year now.

items.statement: Articles of association amended to include paper, electronics, software, hardware, infra to enable commercialization of R&D in value-added packaging products
items.quote: We are also adding the value-added products now, which can be paper, which can be other materials, so just to enable that whatever R&D is doing, and it should not remain in the R&D, it should come as a commercial thing for us, so we are enabling those things.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (West Asia crisis, Bab-el-Mandeb) could disrupt shipping; quarter-on-quarter fluctuations possible due to shipment timing; no major price correction expected while crisis continues
items.quote: But if everything normalizes, you may see some correction in the prices, but our raw material sourcing and our finished selling prices will have the same margin what we have now, so we are not much concerned on the pricing front.

items.statement: Management prioritizes wealth creation through growth over buybacks; surplus cash to go toward debt reduction; no dividend/buyback guidance given
items.quote: Our policy is that we should reward shareholders by increasing their wealth, which you see in the next 3 years, I think wealth creation will happen, so that shareholders will not have any point to complain about that.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned; focus on operational execution across geographies
items.quote: Building on the momentum established in Q4 FY26, this performance reflects the resilience of our integrated global business model and operational execution.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected around 20% for FY27, higher than previous 12% guidance
items.quote: See, 27% is obviously very good growth, but we expect the revenue growth to be in the range close to 20%, right, much better than the 12% guidance we had given earlier, around 20% something.

items.statement: EBITDA margin around 17% considered normalized and expected to sustain for next 2 years
items.quote: Lastly, this 17% margin that we are seeing, this is a largely normalized margin, right? This is the range in which we expect the margin to be for the next 2 years or so, right? Shailesh Sharma: Yes, this is what we expect

items.statement: Capex of INR 170-180 crore planned for FY27, part of INR 500 crore total capex largely completing by FY28
items.quote: See this plan, I wouldn't right now comment on the capex for Q1, but it's largely this year, we are expecting to have a capex of about INR170 - 180 crores at least in the current financial year.

items.statement: Capacity expansion underway via cycle time improvements (5 million pieces unlocked) and new channels at Haridwar factory
items.quote: We have already unlocked about 5 million pieces this year by doing some technological upgradation of our assets, which are in ramping up stage. On top of it, we are also putting channels in our Haridwar factory.

items.statement: OEM sales mix: 2-wheeler ~54%, passenger vehicle ~31%, commercial vehicle ~15% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So our OEM basically, it contributes about 62%, as you have seen it, out of which our 2-wheeler is about 54%, passenger vehicle is around 31% and commercial vehicle is about 15%.

items.statement: Vehicle aftermarket volumes plateaued or slightly declining; new strategy over next 5 months to recover volumes
items.quote: So vehicle aftermarket business has a certain different set of challenges. So far, it's kind of plateau or a small decline in our revenue. The next 5 months, we have some different strategy to cover up or recover our volume.

items.statement: OEM contracts have commodity inflation pass-through clauses; current round of price negotiations work in progress with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: On price and commodity inflation, if you see our OEM contracts usually have a clause around the commodity inflation linked to the index in which we keep working along with the OEMs. And even currently, it's the work in progress for the recent round of commodity inflation.

items.statement: Gross margin 1% lower YoY but 6.5% higher QoQ due to mix and inventory revaluation (FIFO); 51% in Q1 vs 42.5% in Q4
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter is about 1% lower year-on-year while quarter-on-quarter is higher by about 6.5%. This variance in gross margin from previous quarter is a composite impact of price, mix and inflation.

items.statement: EV bearing programs in development phase; full production ramp-up expected mid-2027 with revenue visibility in 2028
items.quote: These are the businesses that will come on stream during 2028, more precisely towards the last quarter of the calendar year, 2028.

items.statement: Haridwar capex primarily for 2-wheeler traction motors and some driveline; reduces dependency on industrial sourcing
items.quote: I would say much of the investments that are happening in Haridwar primarily for the 2-wheelers, I would say, to begin with and some of the driveline, as you were asking previous question, a little bit of that, but majorly it is for the traction motors coming for the 2-wheelers.

items.statement: Sales to SKF Industrial not a growth priority; expected to decline over next few years as capacity shifts to automotive
items.quote: As far as the volume is concerned, as Shailesh mentioned, it's not a priority for growth. This is something which over the next few years is expected to come down. And we focus that capacity towards serving our automotive customers.

items.statement: All three plants achieved >98% renewable energy sourcing; Bangalore and Haridwar sites water positive (2x and 2.57x)
items.quote: Now our all the 3 plants have been achieved more than 98% renewable energy sourcing. And group has given the certificate as decarbonized plant for all the 3 plants of SK India Limited, Pune, Bangalore and Haridwar.

items.statement: Aftermarket discounts given in last 2 months will not continue; no further price mix decline expected
items.quote: We needed to give some discount in last 2 months, but which will not be continued now. So there will be no decline in price mix.

items.statement: Portfolio rationalization involves factory-level portfolio shifts for economies of scale and exiting unprofitable businesses; no major FY27 impact
items.quote: One is what we make and where we make. We have 3 factories. So to use economy of scale and bring some synergy, we just change our portfolio in different factories. That is one part of it. Another is, of course, our sales mix where there are certain businesses which are kind of not so profitable or loss makers, we would like to do something about it.

items.statement: Exports at 8% of sales; not a strategic focus, expected to remain in current range
items.quote: So our main focus is on our domestic demand. Export is not a very big pie of our strategy also as of now. So it will remain in this range only.

items.statement: Gross margin fluctuations within normal historical range due to commodity pass-through lag of 1-2 quarters and mix changes
items.quote: See, even historically, this has been the normal gross margin range, right? It could be based on the mix or certain timing gap, due to which there could be certain movements within quarter because even what happens is when you see the commodity inflation realization, it doesn't happen immediately in the same quarter, right?

items.statement: Commodity cost pressure expected to peak in Q2 FY27, with softening from Q3 and turnaround in Q4 FY27
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: Respite from that we think will come in Q3 and Q4 only. So it will be a challenging quarter, but then we are accelerating a few things internally, looking again at those levers that I just described, product mix and business mix.

items.statement: Industry MHCV growth expected at high single digit for full year FY27; LCV outlook slightly better
items.quote: even if we take a conservative outlook for the second half of the year, let us say, October, November onwards, we still believe that the industry has potential to grow by high single digit. This is for MHCV. And for LCV, the LCV outlook is actually slightly better than this, yes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA flat at INR970 crore, margin 10.1%, down 100 bps YoY due to rising material costs
items.quote: Despite record revenues, the EBITDA was flat at INR970 crores as compared to same quarter last year. EBITDA margin was 10.1%, 100 basis points lower on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Material cost at 71.5% of revenue in Q1 FY27, up 90 bps YoY but flat sequentially; inventory absorption and cost savings offset half of commodity impact
items.quote: As a percentage of revenue, the material cost stood at 71.5% for the quarter, higher by 90 basis points Y-o-Y, but in line with Q4.

items.statement: Price increase of 1.2%-1.25% taken in Q1 FY27; additional hikes in July: >1% MHCV, >2% LCV; cumulative FY27 hikes ~2.25% MHCV, >3.5% LCV
items.quote: Price increase during the quarter was about 1.2% - 1.25%. That also helped us in negating the commodity cost increases.

items.statement: Domestic MHCV industry grew 13% YoY in Q1 FY27; LCV VAHAN industry grew 17% YoY; June and July MHCV industry growth >20% YoY
items.quote: Overall, in Q1, the domestic MHCV industry volume grew by 13% on Y-o-Y basis, while the domestic LCV VAHAN industry grew by 17%.

items.statement: Switch Mobility order book at 2,100 e-buses after 650-bus order; delivered 225 e-buses and ~300 e-LCVs in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our EV subsidiary, Switch Mobility India, recently bagged an order of 650 electric buses. With this, Switch Mobility has a healthy order book of 2,100 e-buses.

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance AUM grew 20% YoY to INR60,310 crore; Hinduja Housing Finance AUM grew 13% YoY to INR16,157 crore
items.quote: Hinduja Leyland Finance, our vehicle financing subsidiary, delivered robust growth in the quarter with its AUM expanding by 20% year-on-year to INR60,310 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex INR153 crore; full-year FY27 capex expected to continue in INR900-1,000 crore range and increase over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was at INR153 crores. New products, including future technology development, alternate powertrain technologies and EVs remain the focus areas for the new capex.

items.statement: RAK UAE plant halted in April-May, produced 600 units in June, targeting 700 in July, 800 in August; Saudi plant timeline accelerated from 18-24 months
items.quote: last month, we did 600 units there. This month, we are expecting to do 700. And next month, we will come to our peak production of 800.

items.statement: Launched industry-first air suspension in multi-axle trucks; HIPPO tractors and TAURUS tippers gaining momentum; focus on premiumization and higher horsepower segments
items.quote: the highlight of the quarter was introduction of new air suspension technology in multi-axle trucks, which is an industry first and provides our customers industry best payload

items.statement: Added 33 touch points in Q1 FY27; total network 2,137 (1,177 MHCV, 960 LCV); North market share improved from ~15% to ~27% over 4-5 years
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 33 touch points in our MHCV and LCV businesses. The focus of new additions continues in North and East region, where we have a higher headroom.

items.statement: Air suspension launch not a reactive move; project started 2.5-3 years ago; offers 4-ton extra payload vs competitor's 2-ton; expect competitors to follow in 6-12 months
items.quote: this is not like a quick reaction response from our side. This project was started about 2.5, 3 years ago. And now fortunately, when this launch happened, we were quite ready with this new product.

items.statement: BS7 implementation not expected before 2031-2032; regulatory burden high but focus on positive TCO impact for customers; AC mandate example shows customer acceptance of value
items.quote: my personal opinion is BS7, we should not see in India in CV before 2031, and it could also be 2032.

items.statement: Optare debt GBP 50 million remaining; plan to repay GBP 25 million in FY27 and GBP 25 million in FY28 to avoid interest cost
items.quote: We had debt of about GBP 80 million. We paid about GBP 30 million last year. And now we have about GBP 50 million debt, which is there, and we don't want to incur interest cost.

items.statement: HLF and HHF consolidated net NPAs at 2.1% on book basis; HLF pre-provisioning operating profit up 56% YoY to INR587 crore, PAT up 37% to INR123 crore
items.quote: Both HLF and HHF maintained healthy asset quality with consolidated net NPAs at 2.1% on book basis.

items.statement: Opening inventory 6,500 vehicles, increased to 8,500 at Q1 end; absorbed one-fifth to one-fourth of commodity cost increases via inventory; overheads also capitalized
items.quote: For us, we carried about 6,500 vehicles at the opening level. And again, this 6,500 level of stock at the opening level, it got increased to about 8,500 level as at the quarter end.

items.statement: Manpower cost to increase 4-5% QoQ in Q2 FY27 due to July increment cycle; centralized commercial negotiation team created to control admin overheads >INR50 lakh
items.quote: you will see a marginal increase in the manpower cost because our increment cycle, it starts from July of every year, every financial year, so you will see a marginal 4%, 5% increase in the manpower cost over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Key risks: elevated commodity prices (steel, natural rubber), regulatory cost increases; mitigation via price hikes, cost savings (Achieve 2K project), mix improvement, inventory management
items.quote: We remain mindful of the key risks, particularly the elevated commodity prices, but shall continue to put all efforts to achieve better price realization and mix, higher cost savings and enhanced operational discipline.

items.statement: Net cash position strengthened to INR2,252 crore, up INR1,431 crore YoY; aftermarket revenue up 12.7% YoY, Power Solutions up 51%, Defense up 64% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our cash position, net of debt, has got stronger on Y-o-Y basis. We had net cash of INR2,252 crores at the end of the year, an increase of more than INR1,431 crores on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Management guides INR900 crore profit repatriation from St. Regis Dubai project in FY27, with INR142.58 crore already received in Q1.
items.quote: We have always given a guidance that we should expect to complete a repatriation of about INR900 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Zuari Envien Bioenergy secured ethanol orders until October 2026.
items.quote: Our ethanol joint venture, Zuari Envien Bioenergy Private Limited, stabilized its plant operations during the current quarter and has secured orders until the month of October 2026.

items.statement: Simon India executed INR30 crore projects in Q1 with INR70 crore orders under execution.
items.quote: During the quarter we executed projects worth about INR30 crores with approximately INR70 crores worth of orders currently under execution.

items.statement: Zuari Infraworld has gross development value of INR4,900 crore in hand, targeting INR10,000 crore GDV.
items.quote: I think the gross development value of the projects Alok, that you have in hand is closer to INR4,900 crores. Alok Banerjee: Right. Athar Shahab: And we did mention that our aspiration is to have a GDV of INR10,000 crores

items.statement: Sugar margins pressured by 8% SAP increase to INR400/quintal and lower ethanol recovery from molasses route.
items.quote: Despite the improvement in sugar volumes and realizations, margins remained somewhat under pressure, substantially due to about 8% increase in the SAP, which was INR30 per quintal for the last season, as well as somewhat lower recovery from ethanol, which was manufactured through the molasses route.

items.statement: Sugar realizations improved to INR4,116/quintal in Q1 FY27 from INR4,036/quintal in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Average sugar realizations also improved to INR4,116 per quintal from INR4,036 per quintal last year.

items.statement: Ethanol realization static at INR60.70/liter, weighing on margins; management expects government price revision soon.
items.quote: As regards our ethanol business, the realization, the prices continue to be static and therefore they weigh on the margins. However, we remain optimistic about the sector's outlook and expect the government to consider a price revision in the near term.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices risen 10% over past month to record highs; UP prices at INR4,860-4,920/quintal.
items.quote: Indian sugar prices have risen 10% over the past month to record highs. Prices in Uttar Pradesh are currently at INR4,860 to INR4,920 per quintal, with Maharashtra also registering reasonably high prices.

items.statement: Festival demand expected to support sugar realizations; global prices at 16.6 cents/pound near yearly highs.
items.quote: With festival demand expected to gather pace, the pricing environment is expected to support sugar realizations. The global sugar market has also remained supportive with prices at around 16.6 cents per pound, close to their highest levels in over a year.

items.statement: Sugar mill operated at 100% capacity utilization in previous season; no capacity addition unless ethanol blending policy changes.
items.quote: On the sugar side, we are now operating a facility at 100% capacity utilization. It has demonstrated robust performance. And while we hope to continue our performance in the ensuing season, we remain open to the idea of acquisitions, should they present themselves.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity expansion on hold due to overcapacity; last tender saw 1,800 crore liter offers vs 1,050 crore requirement.
items.quote: We had to take a pause because of the substantial overcapacity that came to ligh t during the last tenders against the INR1050 crore s of tenders, INR1800 crore s worth of offers were received. So obviously we have put our capex plans on hold

items.statement: External debt (excl. working capital) reduced to INR1,888 crore from INR1,909 crore QoQ; targeting further reduction via Dubai repatriation and Zuari Agro loan repayment.
items.quote: Friends, we are making decent progress on our deleveraging exercise, excluding working capital, the aggregate external debt of the company and its subsidiaries was INR1,888 crores as against INR1,909 crores at the end of the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Average borrowing cost declined 56 bps YoY to 9.73% in Q1 FY27; INR1,100 crore debt repayment could save ~INR100-110 crore annual interest.
items.quote: The average cost of borrowings declined by 56 basis points year-on-year to 9.73% in Q1 financial year '27 from 10.29% in Q1 financial year '26.

items.statement: Approved ICD to buy shares of Zuari International for INR150 crore to consolidate listed investments into holding company.
items.quote: We have taken an ICD approval and the strategy behind this transaction is that we want to consolidate the investments which are there in our different companies at the holding group level.

items.statement: Expecting INR258 crore loan repayment from associate Zuari Agro Chemicals in current quarter.
items.quote: We are expecting, as I mentioned earlier, the entire INR258 crores outstanding debt to be repaid to us in the current quarter.

items.statement: Sugar recovery at 11.7% in Q1 FY27; mill operated only 6 days in April 2026 vs no crushing last year.
items.quote: Sugar recovery for this first quarter stood at 11.7%. Last year we had not operated the mill, we produced so the numbers cannot be compared with last year. The performance of the current quarter included six operating days in April '26, whereas there was no crushing operation in the last year.

items.statement: Ethanol production up 1% to 10,138 KL, sales up 5% to 10,248 KL in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our ethanol business remained on a steady momentum with production increasing by 1% to 10,138 KL and sales grew by 5% to 10,248 KL.

items.statement: Power sales surged to 62.8 lakh units from 7.7 lakh units YoY in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Power sales for the quarter stood at 62.8 lakh unit compared to 7.7 lakh units for the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Ethanol export fee case (INR507 lakh exposure) not provided for; management confident law cannot be applied retrospectively.
items.quote: So we have not created the provisions, but we have given an indemnity and the court cannot make a retrospective change in the law bringing in an effective adjustment that you pay an export fees for the ethanol that you export out of Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Exports currently not allowed; management does not foresee export permission in current situation.
items.quote: As far as exports are concerned, currently the exports are not allowed, so we don't foresee that in the current situation exports will be permitted.

items.statement: St. Regis Dubai handovers commenced; 40-45% of customer collections outstanding, demand notes raised post completion certificate.
items.quote: In terms of our payment plan, the payment plan is 50-50%. So now we have raised the demand notes to the customer post receipt of the completion certificate. So we expect to receive the money from the customers in this current quarter.

items.statement: Furniture division losses minimal (maintenance, staff, ICD service); decision on revival or closure by end of FY27.
items.quote: We have been talking to people who could potentially revive that business. If something works out as part of the revival plans, we will revive it. But otherwise, we will make some decisions about this business by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic growth opportunities across businesses; open to sugar acquisitions if worthwhile.
items.quote: As I have been mentioning in the previous calls, we continue to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities across our businesses. We also continue to adopt digital solutions across businesses to improve efficiency and streamline our work processes.

items.statement: Simon India exploring digitalization and AI-led initiatives to compress engineering hours; early stage, not yet quantifiable.
items.quote: These are too early to be quantified. Honestly, if you ask this question to any CEO, they will find it very difficult to answer. I think these are early days, we are experimenting and implementing various tools.

items.statement: Cane availability risk for upcoming season dependent on weather and disease; command area crop maturing well currently.

items.quote: It will all be tested and proven when they come up with the new tenders in the month of October. So I think it's just a couple of months away and when we will see the tenders coming in and we will know the numbers and then we can plan accordingly.

items.statement: Listed strategic investments valued at INR4,223 crore as of June 30, up 15% QoQ due to market movement.
items.quote: The value of our listed strategic investments as on 30th June was INR4,223 crores, which was up 15% quarter on quarter due to market movement.

items.statement: Targets >Rs 2,000 crore revenue and 10-11% PAT margin by FY28
items.quote: Bottom line, top line would be by 28, we expect to cross more than 2000 crores in terms of the total revenue. And bottom line somewhere around in terms of PAT, around 10 to 11% on a conservative basis.

items.quote: See, we have a running order book in renewable energy, LED business, which is around 3000 crores of an order book, which we have in LED.

items.statement: Dialysis machine order book exceeds 500 units across exports and domestic
items.quote: Dialysis we have an order book of around more than 500 machines. Spread across exports and domestic as well.

items.statement: B2G business seasonally stronger in H2 (Q3/Q4); expects same trend this year
items.quote: B2G is a segment that, as you also know by nature, it happens in the third and fourth quarter. Correct? So previously what our track has been is that our third and fourth quarter numbers have been better, always better than our first and second quarter numbers.

items.statement: Q1 revenue split: ~55% from IVD & Medtech, balance from renewable energy
items.quote: So probably around 55% comes from the IVD and MedTech space, and the balance comes from the renewable energy space.

items.statement: IVD & Medtech EBITDA margin ~20%; Renewable energy EBITDA margin ~11%
items.quote: In terms of if you talk about the EBITDA level in the IVD and Medtech space, so probably around 20% of EBITDA is there in the IVD and Medtech space. Whi ch we compare to renewable energy, so it would be somewhere around 11
