items.statement: Targets internal EBITDA margin of 20% over coming quarters, up from current 16.2%
items.quote: We are targeting internally 20% as an EBITDA margin over the coming quarters, and this is in line with our industry benchmarks.

items.statement: Aims for at least 20% revenue CAGR over next five years based on growth strategy
items.quote: In terms of sales CAGR over the next five years, again, we don't give revenue guidance, but I would say at least 20% CAGR is something we aim at.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 16.2% in Q1 FY27, up 640 bps year-on-year from 9.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 16.2%. This is another result that we are particularly happy about, as EBITDA margin is one of our main KPIs for our transformation journey. It is up 640 basis points year-on-year from 9.3% last year.

items.statement: Vriddhi Council cost savings of ₹19.1 crore realised to date against ₹50 crore annual target
items.quote: Vriddhi Council cost savings of ₹19.1 crore realised to date against a ₹50 crore annual target.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY27 is ₹30 crore, funded 75% by debt and 25% by internal accruals
items.quote: Apart from that, overall, our capex plan for FY27 is ₹30 crore, and that's what we are progressing on.

items.statement: Capex funded by combination of debt and internal accruals at 75% debt, 25% internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, the capex is going to be funded by a combination of debt and internal accruals. So we're looking at 75% funding from debt and 25% from internal accruals.

items.statement: Machining capacity to expand from 1.8 lakh to 3 lakh pieces per month by end of FY27
items.quote: We are planning to expand our machining capacity from 1.8 lakh pieces per month to 3 lakh pieces per month by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Forging capacity at ~20,000 tonnes with 50-60% utilisation; machining at 1.8 lakh pieces/month with 90-95% utilisation
items.quote: On the forging side, we have close to 20,000 tonnes of installed capacity, and the utilisation there is in the range of 50 to 60%. On the machining side, we look at capacity in number of pieces. So we currently have a capacity of — I'd say 1.8 lakh pieces per month.

items.statement: Wheel hub samples in validation phase with ~₹20 crore annual revenue potential; new wheel hub line expected online by end of Q2
items.quote: Wheel hub samples are in progress, which constitute approximately ₹20 crore of annual revenue. We also have a new wheel hub line installation in progress, where we are utilising existing CNC machines from the recently phased-out businesses.

items.statement: New business revenue at 22% of total (₹13 crore in Q1), highest in five quarters; connecting rod share gains from three customers
items.quote: At 22%, we are at an all-time high in the last five quarters or possibly even more, and at an absolute level it's around ₹13 crore of the quarter's revenue.

items.statement: Strong growth across segments: passenger cars 35% YoY, trucks 48% YoY, industrial 67% YoY; agro down 31% due to consolidation
items.quote: Passenger cars: 35% year-on-year growth, with strong OEM growth and new business ramp-up. Trucks: 48% year-on-year growth, the fastest-growing segment. Industrial segment: 67% year-on-year growth, with a smaller base but the strongest percentage growth.

items.statement: Engine 60% of revenue (up from 57%), axle and driveline growing; OEM revenue up 31% YoY to ₹40.7 crore, fourth consecutive quarter of growth
items.quote: OEM revenues have increased to ₹40.7 crore in Q1 FY27 — 31% year-on-year growth and 9% quarter-on-quarter growth. And I'm happy to share that this is the fourth consecutive quarter of OEM revenue growth.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 30-40% of revenue; focus on top 20 high-value customers for wallet share growth
items.quote: Revenue from the top five customers would be in the range of 30–40%.

items.statement: Export mix revived to 16% in Q1 FY27 from 11% in Q4, with new high-volume business replacing legacy non-fit business
items.quote: Export sales mix has revived to 16% in Q1 FY27 compared to 11% in Q4. This has happened with new high-volume business replacing some of the legacy non-fit business.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 148 days from 168 days previous quarter; focusing on inventory reduction, structured collections, bill discounting
items.quote: cash conversion cycle has actually reduced to 148 days compared to 170 last quarter. A big part of our effort has been on reducing inventory which is non- moving, or indirect materials inventory, and focusing on direct materials which are required for sales

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA improved to 2.51 from 3.53, below target level; plans to raise equity with promoter participation to repay debt
items.quote: The deleveraging trend continues, and this is a ratio that we are now tracking: debt to EBITDA has improved from 3.53 to 2.51, which is now below our target level.

items.statement: Evaluating equity raise with promoter participation to repay debt; no numbers disclosed yet
items.quote: We do have plans to raise equity in the future. There are multiple options that we are evaluating, and the promoters themselves would be putting in equity along with other participants.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through mechanism with all customers; received price increases for recent raw material rate hikes
items.quote: We are fairly well insulated from raw material price changes, because we have a pass-through mechanism with all our customers. We have received pricing increases from our customers for whatever recent raw material rate increased there were.

items.statement: Indirect material costs up 15-30% due to Middle East disturbances; controlled consumption quantities and received customer price increases for conversion cost
items.quote: There were increases in indirect materials like consumables and cutting tools and so on, due to the Middle East war and disturbances which were taking place in the last five to six months. Because of that, a lot of our smaller suppliers of indirect materials have asked for price increases of anywhere between 15 to 30%.

items.statement: ROCE crossed 20% for first time at 22%, up from 18% in Q4; fixed asset turnover currently 2.5-2.6, targeting 2.0 long-term
items.quote: ROCE — return on capital employed — crosses 20% for the first time; this has improved to 22%, up from 18% in the previous quarter, Q4.

items.statement: EV risk limited to passenger car engine business where exposure is low; engine business focused on heavy commercial vehicles and industrial off-road with long lifecycle
items.quote: The only place where we see a lot of risk from electrification of vehicles is the engine business in passenger cars, where we have very low exposure. So that's how our business mix is quite well set up.

items.statement: Yash Patil joined as Investor Relations Manager; first IR department created to deepen investor relations
items.quote: Yash Patil has joined us recently as Investor Relations Manager. With his joining, we have created the Investor Relations department in Kalyani Forge for the first time.

items.statement: Competitive moat from complex forging precision, deep engineering expertise of 4-5 decades, multi-decade customer relationships, and unique hot+warm forging combination offering engine+driveline+axle
items.quote: Our products are highly complex forgings, and we offer complete, fully forged and machined, ready-to-assemble parts. There are not many players in the market who are able to make this level of precision and accuracy at a high-volume scale. So our quality and our deep engineering expertise of four to five decades — that is one of our biggest competitive moats.

items.statement: FY2026-27 revenue guidance of approximately ₹500 crore
items.quote: Based on the response provided in the chat, ₹500 crore appears to be a reasonable revenue guidance, considering the growth in CHUK and PM4 coming into operation.

items.statement: FY2026-27 EBITDA margin target of approximately 19%
items.quote: We expect the gross-margin contribution to improve through a better variable-cost structure. Since fixed costs are not expected to increase proportionately, the higher contribution should support an improvement in margins.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to be approximately 26% for FY2026-27
items.quote: Accordingly, the effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 26%.

items.statement: Project Jagriti total cost approximately ₹753 crore
items.quote: The current total project cost is approximately ₹753 crore, and the project will add slightly more than 30,000 tonnes of annual capacity.

items.statement: Initial delivery container facility investment less than ₹2 crore
items.quote: The initial facility is expected to require an investment of less than ₹2 crore.

items.statement: PM4 commissioning expected end of October, reeling paper in November
items.quote: We are confident of starting the machine by the end of October and reeling out paper in November.

items.statement: Power Boiler and Recovery Boiler start-up targeted end of August or first week of September
items.quote: Start-up is targeted for the end of August or the first week of September.

items.statement: Existing plant operating at more than 100% of rated capacity
items.quote: The existing plant is operating at more than 100% of rated capacity.

items.statement: New plant utilisation projected at 40-50% initially, 60-70% next year, 80-90% by 2028
items.quote: For the new plant, our financial projections assume utilisation of approximately 40%–50% during the initial months, 60%–70% in the following year, and stabilisation at approximately 80%–90% by 2028.

items.statement: Outsourced capacity to increase from ~300 to 800-900 tonnes per month
items.quote: We intend to increase outsourced capacity from approximately 300 tonnes per month currently to approximately 800–900 tonnes per month over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Food Services current production ~350 tonnes/month (180-200 in-house, balance outsourced)
items.quote: Current total production is approximately 350 tonnes per month. Shubham Tibrewal 1:20:33 Of this volume, approximately 180 –200 tonnes per month are produced internally, with the balan ce supplied by outsourced

items.statement: Plan to add ~400 tonnes outsourced capacity over next two quarters
items.quote: We expect to add approximately 400 tonnes of outsourced capacity over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin ~14.5%, targeting 18-19% for FY2026-27
items.quote: I think first, the EBITDA margins for the first quarter is not 13 percent, it is about 14 and a half percent. And with the revised increased production coming into place, the EBITDA margin should go up.

items.statement: Historical EBITDA margins of 23-25% achieved in FY2020-24
items.quote: We were consistently working at an EBITDA in excess of 23, 24 percent all across 2023, 24, 25.

items.statement: Delivery containers priced 40-50% above comparable plastic containers
items.quote: The product is currently priced approximately 40%–50% above comparable plastic containers, but it offers advantages in packing, unpacking and food quality.

items.statement: FlexC base paper target cost ~₹24/sqm vs petroleum-based ₹16-18/sqm
items.quote: In the targeted applications, petroleum-based substrates generally cost approximately ₹16–₹18 per square metre, whereas our current target is approximately ₹24 per square metre.

items.statement: Neo financing increased borrowing cost from ~11% to ~17%
items.quote: As a result, the borrowing cost increased from approximately 11% to approximately 17%.

items.statement: Neo financing aggregate interest outflow ₹120-122 crore vs ₹150-155 crore under bank structure
items.quote: Under the present transaction, despite the higher stated interest rate, the estimated aggregate outflow is approximately ₹120 crore–₹122 crore.

items.statement: Plan to refinance Neo debt within 16-18 months after project stabilisation
items.quote: A reasonable timeframe for retiring the debt is approximately 16 to 18 months.

items.statement: Promoter shares pledged as security for Neo loan, to be released upon refinancing
items.quote: This is intended to be a short-term, higher-cost arrangement, and we expect to refinance through banks within approximately one to one-and-a-half years, following stabilisation of the machine and improvement in the Company's financial performance. At that stage, the shares are expected to be released from pledge.

items.statement: Current inventory ~15 days, new products may range 15-30 days during stabilisation
items.quote: Current inventory is approximately 15 days. For new products, considering the stabilisation period, inventory may range from approximately 15 to 30 days.

items.statement: Raw material procurement seasonal, peak working capital varies with procurement cycle
items.quote: Our principal raw materials, including bagasse and paddy husk, are seasonal. Since procurement is concentrated during the season, the working-capital position should be assessed in that context; peak working capital varies with the procurement cycle.

items.statement: FlexC base paper targeting release liners, labelling, heat-sealable bags, confectionery wraps, snack pouches, sachets, tea pouches, seed packs, medical packaging
items.quote: Initial target applications include confectionery wraps, snack and sweet pouches, sachets, tea pouches, seed packs, medical packaging, release liners and dry-food liners.

items.statement: B2C presence increased from 3 to 12 retail platforms
items.quote: On the B2C side, our presence has increased from three to 12 retail platforms.

items.statement: Middle East situation affecting exports
items.quote: Our principal challenges are the start-up of PM4, which is expected around the end of October or in November; market acceptance of products manufactured on PM4; the continuing Middle East situation, which is affecting exports; and the high financing cost associated with Project Jagriti.

items.statement: Proposed addition of 3,550 metric tons per annum to existing 32,450 metric tons per annum capacity
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce a proposed addition of 3,550 metric tons per annum to our existing manufacturing capacity of 32,450 metric ton per annum overall.

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization stood at 64% in FY26
items.quote: Our existing capacity utilization stood at 64% in FY26, providing a strong base for further product and capacity expansion.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 16.29% from 5.87% in Q1 FY26, expansion of 1041 basis points
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 16.29% compared to 5.87% in quarter 1 FY26 representing an expansion of 1041 basis points.

items.statement: Management indicates sustainable EBITDA margin range of 10% to 13%
items.quote: But sustainable margins are like 10% to 13% or 10% to 12% is a very, very reasonable amount, I would say, always.

items.statement: Long-term objective of achieving INR 1,000 crores in annual revenue by FY28
items.quote: The company continues to work towards its long-term objective of achieving INR 1,000 crores in annual revenue by FY28.

items.statement: Expecting similar quarter-on-quarter growth trajectory in FY27, focusing more on bottom line than top line
items.quote: Yes. So I think going forward, we are looking for the same growth quarter-on-quarter. Almost same. I will not say 100% same, but almost same growth we are looking for the quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Capex for 3,550 metric tons capacity addition approximately INR 2 crores, funded through internal accruals and debt
items.quote: So it's approximately INR 2 crores. Nishita: Okay. Understood. Manish Dedhia: It depends on which kind of machinery from where you are getting, how you are getting, it's all depend on this

items.statement: Healthcare furniture segment contributes approximately 19.80% of portfolio, packaging 80%
items.quote: Approximately as of today, we are at around 19.80%. So it includes furniture parts and other parts. And the rest is 80% is our packaging business.

items.statement: Expecting higher revenue share from furniture parts and other verticals over next 2-3 years, but 80-20 packaging to furniture ratio likely to remain similar till INR 1,000 crores milestone
items.quote: So definitely, going further, you will have a good business and revenue sharing -- I mean like revenue in the percentage sharing, you will find more in furniture parts and others for sure, than container.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed on to customers with approximately one-month lag for normal cases
items.quote: So it's one month later only. Generally, it's one month, if it is a normal case. If it is a specialized case, we have to talk to individually one-on-one customer.

items.statement: Company sources raw materials locally, not importing, and passes on supplier price increases to customers
items.quote: But I think we have stopped buying imports since many years. And as like locally material available in India, and hence, we are buying from local only.

items.statement: Added more than 30 customers in Q1 FY27, over 100-150 customers added in FY26
items.quote: This time also, we have added more than 30-plus customers in our kitty. So every quarter, we are also adding -- we are also managing the customer.

items.statement: All verticals (containers, furniture parts, others) seeing strong demand and good profitability
items.quote: So currently, everything is in a demand, sir. And -- the product -- the containers also in a big demand. And we have 3 verticals, which is the containers, furniture part and others. So all verticals are doing very well.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 total income INR 9,532.78 lakhs, up 11.62% YoY; EBITDA INR 1,549.48 lakhs, up 209.50% YoY; Net profit INR 873.83 lakhs, up 566.23% YoY
items.quote: Total income for the quarter stood at INR 9,532.78 lakhs, registering a growth of 11.62% year-on-year compared to INR 8,540.39 lakhs in quarter 1 FY2026. EBITDA increased significantly to INR 1,549.48 lakhs, registering a growth of 209.50% year-on-year.

items.statement: International market penetration for Furnastra taking time, results still awaiting
items.quote: Very, very lower side. Because see, it takes a lot of time to establish our product in the international market. Now we have already entered into that. Now the results are still awaiting.

items.statement: Additional 3,550 metric tons capacity already operational as of announcement
items.quote: Yes, already online, already online.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility not planned for manufacturing/assembly conversion as of now
items.quote: Not as of now, once we haven't decided yet anything.

items.statement: Rationalizing low-margin SKUs and introducing new higher-margin products simultaneously
items.quote: So we have already done that, and this is -- you can find the result because, see, we have done rationalized things. Even -- see, we are doing a lot of product expansion and product reducing, like both the things we are doing together.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 net profit margin improved to 9.18% from 1.54% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Net profit margin improved to 9.18% compared to 1.54% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EPS INR 6.44 vs INR 0.97 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Earnings per share for the quarter stood at INR 6.44 compared to INR 0.97 in quarter 1 FY26.

items.statement: Sequential EBITDA increased from INR 1,422.74 lakhs in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,549.48 lakhs in Q1 FY27; net profit from INR 771.73 lakhs to INR 873.83 lakhs
items.quote: On a sequential basis, the company also continued to maintain strong profitability. EBITDA stood at INR 1,549.48 lakhs in quarter 1 FY27 compared to INR 1,422.74 lakhs in quarter 4 FY26, while net profit increased from INR 771.73 lakhs in quarter 4 FY26 to INR 873.83 lakhs in quarter 1

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order inflow of INR90 crores, including INR19.34 cr railway authority engineer, INR8.34 cr MPRDC independent engineer, and INR40.92 cr OBCC assignment (highest ticket size)
items.quote: On the order front, we received a total order of INR90 crores only in the first quarter of FY27, some of them being INR19.34 crores order for authority engineer and project management services for 140-kilometer Rowghat-Jagdalpur railway line, along with the consultancy order for rail-over bridge construction supervision in Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Additional INR60-65 crores orders secured in Q2 FY27 so far
items.quote: And again, in Q2, which is in running condition, we have got additional INR60 crores, INR65 crores of the orders in our kitty.

items.statement: Roughly 15-20% of order book converts to revenue annually
items.quote: So what I can say specific answer to your query, roughly 15% to 20% of the order book gets converted into the revenue.

items.statement: Management declines to give specific FY27 revenue guidance citing SEBI LODR restrictions, but notes Q1-Q2 typically 30-40% of annual revenue with Q3-Q4 higher
items.quote: So usually, the Q1 -- entire Q1 goes in securing new orders, Q2 goes in mobilization. And Q3 and Q4, we start recognizing these revenues. So it's difficult for me to give any numbers as the SEBI LODR doesn't allow us to do that.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 operating loss of ~INR3-4 crores attributed to Ind AS estimate corrections (NHAI scope reduction) and insufficient revenue base to absorb high fixed cost structure
items.quote: Basically, this is only a paper loss, which is correction in the estimates you might be aware. Our revenue is based -- it is an Ind AS type of accounting system and our revenue is based on the accounts -- sorry, our revenue is based on the expenditures done on particular project

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from Q3 FY27 as new order billing starts and utilization improves
items.quote: And once the billing starts converting, there will be margin improvement. So these billing is expected to start somewhere in Q3.

items.statement: New bids being submitted with better profit margins; won 6km Brahmaputra bridge assignment at INR33 cr vs competitors at INR12-20 cr due to improved technical rating (ranked 9/100)
items.quote: In that competition, there were 4 bidders. One bidder was INR12 crores, another bidder was INR13 crores, third bidder was INR20 crores. Our bid was INR33 crores. Still we win the assignment.

items.statement: Formed SPV Verul Drivehub Private Limited with 55% stake for Wayside Amenities vertical; first project agreement signed 4th August, physical possession received
items.quote: We have formed an SPV in which 55% of the stake remains with Dhruv Consultancy in Verul Drivehub Private Limited. This will strengthen our new infrastructure vertical of Wayside Amenities.

items.statement: First Wayside Amenities project revenue expected from February 2025 (fuel pump installation 4-5 months critical path); 3 more LOAs expected in September 2024
items.quote: So we are expecting to start the revenue of first wayside amenity project somewhere I can say in the month of February next year.

items.statement: Hiring 108 manpower for Rowghat-Jagdalpur railway project (60-70% done), project commencement expected within a month
items.quote: So for the project to deploy on the site, all the manpower needs to be hired externally, either some of them will be on contract basis, but total manpower recruitment being done is 108.

items.statement: Expanding into railway consultancy (dedicated team, 108 hires for Rowghat-Jagdalpur) and Wayside Amenities (15-year lease-based O&M projects)
items.quote: So such high level -- high expert -- all of them working from -- for the railway sector only. So all these manpower coming in will further strengthen our railway sector.

items.statement: Empaneled by BMC for 5-year PMC for municipal infrastructure and by India Exim Bank for DPR/TEV/PFR and lenders independent engineering
items.quote: We were empaneled by BMC for project management consultancy for municipal infrastructure works for a period of 5 years and also by India Exim Bank for DPR technical advisory work and lenders independent engineering.

items.statement: Targeting 10-15% of order book from international markets (Africa, Southeast Asia, Gulf, South/Central Asia); empaneled in Mozambique, preferred bidder in Ghana, bidding in Saudi Arabia
items.quote: We are hopeful of getting 10% to 15% of our order book from the international market.

items.statement: Receivable cycle typically 60-90 days, up to 120 days in Northeast states with accessibility issues
items.quote: So collections are typically the same right now. You can say minimum 60 to 90 days. Very -- I think a few states, say, in the Northeast or where accessibility becomes an issue, it might go up to 120 days, but not more than that.

items.statement: Employee costs rising due to 108 hires for railway project; head office staff of 80-85 trained monthly on project management and AI dashboards; NHAI Skill Bridge empanelment for key personnel
items.quote: Our employee costs have risen quite higher. With respect to extra expertise, I would say we are conducting certain trainings with respect to building information modeling, which is BIM.

items.statement: Project execution timeline: ~3 years construction + 3 years defect liability period (DLP); 70-80% revenue in construction, 20% in DLP
items.quote: So at an average, the execution time line is 3 years construction. And post that, 3 years DLP, which is a defect liability period or you can call it a maintenance period. So 70%, 80% revenue comes in the construction period and balance 20% comes in the defect liability period.

items.statement: No major mobilization or approval delays expected in next 9 months; prior estimate correction of INR30-35 crores (<5% of INR600 cr total order book) now complete
items.quote: Our total order book is INR600 crores and the correction happened is about INR30 crores, INR35 crores, which is completed now, and it is less than 5%. So now we don't expect any big challenge or any threat or any surprise for current year.

items.statement: Ranked 9th among 100 NHAI-rated consultants; top 6-7 above rarely bid, giving Dhruv technical advantage in large ticket bids
items.quote: We have rated number 9 in India among the 100 consultants. And out of that above 9, there are 6 to 7 consultants which are bidding -- not bidding regularly or they are bidding rarely.

items.statement: NHAI policy change removed network survey vehicle scope from assignments across India, triggering Ind AS estimate correction and Q1 loss
items.quote: The main client is NHAI, of course, like network survey vehicle scope was removed from our assignment and it is given separately to someone else as a policy and all over India, not alone to Dhruv.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target of 18% excluding West Asia conflict impact
items.quote: For FY27, yes, it remains -- that remains about 18% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR125-150 crores for glassware projects, solar and furnace rebuild
items.quote: So the total capex for FY27 is estimated to be about INR125 crores, which is for the 2 glassware projects. One is the expansion of borosilicate glass furnace. And second is the Bharuch facility for the glassware. And also, we might do some solar projects further going forward and some maintenance capex on the furnace rebuild for opal glass furnaces, which is going to come for rebuild in this year.

items.statement: FY27 depreciation guidance of approximately INR92 crores at consolidated level
items.quote: So current year, overall depreciation would be approximately INR92 crores, including stainless at a consol level.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 17.8% in Q1 FY26 due to input cost inflation from West Asia conflict
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, the company achieved an operating EBITDA of INR35.9 crores against INR40.2 crores. In Q1 FY26, the EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 was 14.6% as compared to 17.8% in Q1 FY26. The lower margins are primarily attributable to input cost inflation, particularly in fuel and packaging materials arising from the West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Overall business targets 18-20% EBITDA margin in steady state without West Asia conflict impact
items.quote: At an overall level, we are still confident that barring aside the West Asia conflict impact probably, we are good to maintain about 18% to 20% EBITDA margins on the overall business.

items.statement: Price hikes of 5-7% implemented across categories to offset cost inflation, realization expected from Q2
items.quote: So it ranges betwe en 5% to 7% depending on the category. In some cases, it could be even more than 5% to 7%. So it's not a standard price increase, okay

items.statement: West Asia conflict impact of ~INR10 crores in Q1 FY27 partially offset by price increases
items.quote: The overall net impact of the conflict on Q1 FY27 was approximately INR10 crores, which was partially offset through price increases implemented across multiple categories.

items.statement: Fuel cost impact in Opalware reduced from INR6 crores to INR1.5 crores per quarter; borosilicate from INR2.5 crores to INR60-70 lakhs per quarter
items.quote: So just to add on this point, I think what we have seen as an impact, maybe roughly, we have seen about a INR6 crores impact on the fuel prices in our Opalware business. And currently, at the current levels, probably what we see is that, that impact could reduce to maybe INR1.5 crores a quarter. And even on a similar borosilicate business, the impact due to fuel that was seen around INR2.5 crores

items.statement: Fuel cost as % of sales: 5.8% in Q1 FY27 vs 2.9% in Q1 FY26; Opalware steady state ~4%, glassware ~5.5%
items.quote: So if you look at basically the first quarter last year, the fuel would have been maybe about 2.9% of the overall sales. And this year, it's about 5.8%. And at Opalware level, maybe fuel cost on a steady state prices would be about 4%. And on the glassware it could be around 5.5% without the inflation effect.

items.statement: Hydra plant: 2 double-wall lines commissioned 30 June 2026, 3rd line expected Q2 FY27
items.quote: The commercial production from 2 double -wall lines commenced on 30th June 2026, and the production from third double -wall line is expected to commence during Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Bharuch glassware project: INR42 crores capex, commissioning by end Q3 FY27
items.quote: The project involves an estimated capital expenditure of INR42 crores. This strategic investment positions us to strengthen our presence in high-growth glassware categories and capture greater value through in-house manufacturing. The project is progressing as per plan and expect to commission by end of Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Borosilicate furnace expansion: 25 to 32 tons/day with 3rd forming line, INR50 crores capex, commissioning by end Q4 FY28
items.quote: Board approved expansion with third additional forming line with an estimated capex of INR50 crores. This capacity expansion will help company to remove capacity bottlenecks, improve operating efficiency, lower production costs and enhance competitiveness. It will further help to improve product diversification and portfolio expansion. The project is progressing as per plan and expect to commissio

items.statement: Glassware furnace utilization at 90%, Opalware at full capacity utilization
items.quote: I think Opalware also, we have full capacity utilization. I mean, like I said, for Glassware, it is 90%, and similar for Opalware.

items.statement: Solar: 20 MW peak plant with battery storage commissioned Q1 FY27 under Green Energy Open Access Regulations 2025
items.quote: With the introduction of new Green Energy Open Access Regulations 2025, we are pleased to inform you that the company has successfully commissioned its third captive solar plant in Bikaner during Q1 FY27 with a capacity of 20-megawatt peak integrated with battery energy storage system.

items.statement: Solar now meets 61% of overall energy requirement; evaluating additional 6.5 MW at Borosil and 3-4 MW at Stylenest
items.quote: As a result, solar power now meets about 61% of our overall energy requirement. We are further evaluating opportunities to set up an additional 6.5 megawatt peak captive solar plant at Borosil Limited and another 3 to 4 -megawatt peak plant at Stylenest India Limited to meet the power demand of our Hydra facility.

items.statement: Solar savings of INR27-28 crores at EBITDA level expected in FY27 from Phase 3 implementation
items.quote: So FY27, the overall savings from the solar with the Phase 3 implementations that we have done so far, that will be about INR27 crores, INR28 crores at EBITDA level.

items.statement: Expect continued growth momentum in both Glassware and Opalware segments for rest of FY27
items.quote: So we expect growth to happen in both the segments, both Glassware and Opalware, like you saw in Q1, Opalware volume-led growth, and similar was the case for glassware. So we expect to maintain the momentum.

items.statement: Opalware growth estimate around 9% for FY27 similar to Q1
items.quote: I would say, for example, for Opalware, we had about 9% in Q1. So I think a fair estimate would be around the same going forward, we'll see how the market goes, but we would continue to grow, it's for sure.

items.statement: Net debt of INR99 crores as of 30 June 2026 (cash INR56.2 crores vs total debt INR155.2 crores)
items.quote: As on 30th June 2026, at the consolidated level, Borosil Limited maintained a strong balance sheet with investments, cash and bank balances of INR56.2 crores against total debt of INR155.2 crores, resulting into a net debt position of INR99 crores.

items.statement: Medium-term ROCE target of 20-24% as capacity utilization improves and margins expand
items.quote: I think going forward, as we enhance our capacity utilization and improve our margins, I think we should definitely look at basically 20% to 24% ROCE margins on the business.

items.statement: Targeting FY27 revenue of Rs 500+ crore, implying 35-40% growth over FY26's Rs 365 crore
items.quote: Yes, so here targeting the FY26, we closed at Rs. 365 crore and we are targeting 500 plus crores for FY27. Approximately 35 to 40% of the growth.

items.statement: Targeting 35-40% CAGR over next three years with data center at 50-55%, enterprise applications 20-25%, proprietary platforms and digital services 30%+
items.quote: Overall goal is basically we want to grow around 35% to 40% CAGR in the next three years' time. And on my four verticals, the biggest vertical will always be my data center, which will be around 50-55 odd percent.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 373 crore as of June 30, 2026, with 55% executable in FY27
items.quote: As of June 30, 2026, XtraNet had a strong order book of approximately INR 373 crores across 55 projects. Importantly, approximately 55% of this order book is expected to be executable during FY27.

items.statement: Fresh orders of Rs 60 crore secured in Q1 FY27; active bid pipeline of Rs 1,200 crore
items.quote: We continue to see healthy momentum in order inflows during the quarter, securing fresh orders worth approximately Rs. 60 crores. This took our order book to around INR 373 crores as of June 30, 2026. In addition, our active bid pipeline stood at approximately Rs. 1200 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 855 bps YoY to 20.59%; PAT margin up 444 bps to 11.88%
items.quote: More significantly, operational EBITDA increased by 89% Y-o-Y to approximately INR 10 crores, with EBITDA expanding by 855 basis points to 20.59%. Profit after tax stood at approximately INR 6 crores, representing a 77% Y-o-Y increase, while PAT margin improved by 444 basis points to 11.88%.

items.statement: Product deployment EBITDA margin 6-8%; services margin 20-22%; targeting 60%+ services mix for 50-75 bps margin improvement in FY27
items.quote: But when I move to services, this gives me end-to-end margins of around 20 to 22 odd percent. That is why you will see this first quarter, wherein my growth was just 11% on the top line. But my bottom line on the EBITDA and PAT improved drastically because my revenue here was almost 66% to 67% in the first quarter itself, ma'am.

items.statement: Data center segment targeting 35-40% annual growth driven by infrastructure modernization, disaster recovery, NOC and cyber security operations
items.quote: So, data center portion, we want to keep it at 50% of the overall revenue and year on year, we are expanding. We are looking forward to 35% to 40% of the annual growth in this segment from our business perspective.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: data center 48%, enterprise applications 26%, proprietary platforms 14%, digital services 12%; services share 65-68% vs 46% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Services accounted for approximately 65 to 68% of Q1 FY27 revenue, compared with around 46 Q1 FY26. This shift towards a higher service-led revenue makes it strategically important for us as we look to build greater customer stickiness and deepen our engagement through managed and value-added services.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: 60% services, 40% products; targeting 60%+ services and <40% products in FY27
items.quote: It was around 60% from the services side and 40% from my product side. And talking about the margins, when I do a product deployment, it gives me an EBITDA margin of around 6 to 8 odd percent. But when I move to services, this gives me end-to-end margins of around 20 to 22 odd percent.

items.statement: Government/PSU customers 45% of order book, non-government 55%; direct/indirect order mix 45%/55%
items.quote: 55% revenue is from non-government customers and 45% from government customers, while the mix between direct and indirect orders stands at approximately 45% and 55%.

items.statement: 11 private certifying authorities in India; XtraTrust competes mainly with eMudhra, differentiates with proprietary PKI engine, B2B deployments, 24x7 operations
items.quote: Yes, I will just confirm that approximately 11 private players are there who already have the license to operate as certifying authority in India. So, we have the advanced portal and the mechanism of 10,000 plus partners across country, those who are already using our platform

items.statement: Government project cycle 120-150 days; O&M/services cycle 45-60 days; full deployment cycle 12-15 months
items.quote: And with respect to the working capital, it's a stage-wise process on which we keep on getting our invoicing doing, and then we keep on getting our money. So, on the outer side, on the government cycle, it is roughly around 120 to 150-odd days. And when we move to the revenue part, which is on my O&M, which is on the services side, it is 45 to 60-odd days.

items.statement: Hardware costs up 3-4x in last year; company pre-built inventory to avoid escalation on existing projects; new bids factor in price escalation and USD variation clauses
items.quote: The cost of hardware has moved almost 3x-4x size basically. That was the strategic call of the company which was very different from the many other players as well that we had kept some good inventory with us for my past projects wherein there is no price escalation with government.

items.statement: No pass-through model; prices locked at bidding via firm OEM rate confirmations; inventory built immediately after order receipt
items.quote: Generally, as I have already informed you the life cycle, from the bidding to order conversion, it is approximately 60 to 90 days. And we already have a firm rate confirmation from the respective manufacturer. We take it in writing for a particular project, and the price is locked for the project.

items.statement: Enhancing XtraTrust data center capacity in next quarter to onboard more subscribers
items.quote: We are enhancing the capacity and capability of our data center, and we are targeting XtraTrust in the next one quarter of time.

items.statement: ROE and ROC both above 30% in FY26
items.quote: Our FY26 return ratios remain healthy, with both ROE and ROC in excess of 30%.

items.statement: Internal IRR benchmark of 17-18% for project bidding
items.quote: Even in that case also we maintain a benchmark of at least 17% to 18% as an IRR then only we enter into the project basically.

items.statement: Team of 500+ permanent and 370+ contractual employees
items.quote: Today, our team comprises 500 plus permanent employees and 370 plus contractual employees, giving us strong workforce-based support for our expanding business opportunities.

items.statement: Hardware price escalation and supply chain challenges monitored closely; no order cancellations yet but future uncertainty acknowledged
items.quote: But yes, instead of even the prices which is high, getting a product also is becoming a little bit challenge. But till now, on our company side, we have not faced any kind of a cancellation or anything. We are very strategically working on wherein we can fulfil the requirement of the customer end-to-end and we are trying to cope up as of now. But what happens and how the future will play, we alway

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at ~25% for next two years
items.quote: It will be close to 25 odd percent. That tax rate will be considered for the next two years, ma'am.

items.statement: Management aims for double-digit revenue growth for the full year, contingent on nuclear testing issues being resolved.
items.quote: Our goal is to have a double -digit growth. This is what we are aiming for. Of course, there are challenges on the way and nuclear is one.

items.statement: Order intake grew at 14% CAGR; orders on hand stood at INR 27,445 million as of June 2026.
items.quote: Very strong orders on hand, I think this shows the very robust orders on hand and you can see it is continuously growing, June 2026, we have INR 27,445 million orders on hand.

items.statement: Nuclear order book is INR 1,235 crores, covering GHAVP 1&2, Kaiga 5&6, and Kudankulam safety package.
items.quote: The current order on hand is INR 1,235 crores which mainly includes pumps for GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5, 6, and the safety package which we got for Kudankulam project.

items.statement: Energy (nuclear, conventional, renewable), water/wastewater, and infrastructure (airports, metros, railways) are key growth drivers for the next 2-3 years.
items.quote: I see Energy leading the pack on a macro level and apart from that the infrastructure, the infrastructure which I mean is the W ater, Wastewater sector where a lot of projects are being announced and being executed

items.statement: Thermal power expected to spur extra growth beyond normal levels due to boiler feed and circulation pump localization success.
items.quote: Thermal will play a very important role, because KSB is a very leading player in this Energy segment. And also with our recent success in also getting the first order for the boiler circulation pump which was so far imported.

items.statement: Solar pump revenue was INR 50-60 crores in H1, below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay; scheme expected to launch in H2/Q3.
items.quote: The first half solar revenue was INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores, I would say, much below than our expectations or planning, specifically due to the KUSUM scheme, which is 2.0, which is delayed to the last quarter

items.statement: Solar pumps currently 5-7% of order book; target is 10-12% once KUSUM 2.0 ramps up.
items.quote: It would be presently less than 10%. We have targeted more than 10%, between 10 % to 12%. Right now, I would say it 's 5% to 7%, specifically, because of the delay in the KUSUM 2.0.

items.statement: Valves margin dropped to single digits in H1 due to commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and sales; expected to return to double digits as situation normalizes.
items.quote: No specific reason. I think partly due to the commodity prices, partly due to the product mix, our exports have been down, partly due to the sales being down. So it 's a combination of all these factors.

items.statement: Foundry gas supply stabilized at 85-90%; price agreements settled with suppliers and customers, but margin recovery will take 3-6 months to reflect in books.
items.quote: From the supply side, now we see almost 85% to 90% stability on this front. So we don' t see an issue because we have settled the price agreements and we have started coming back to their normal supplies.

items.statement: Shirwal plant expanded by ~7,000 sq m (on 15,000 sq m land), adding ~20% capacity; plant now at 80-90% utilization.
items.quote: I think we recently also announced we expanded this facility by building one more shed approximately 7,000 square metres on this recently bought out land of 15,000 square metres. This will approximately add to capacity of 20% in this plant.

items.statement: Shirwal plant overall capacity ~1,200-1,300 pumps/year (Energy, Oil & Gas, Nuclear combined); nuclear testing capacity up to 6 pumps/year after GHAVP qualification.
items.quote: Separately, Nuclear, we don't have, but overall our capacity, I think, is approximately 1,200 to 1,300 pumps in Shirwal. Now that we see an approximate increase by 20%.

items.statement: Nuclear testing for GHAVP first pump requires ~500 hours (2-3 months); one pump per quarter dispatch rate, max 6/year; Kaiga testing follows GHAVP.
items.quote: So testing, the first pump is to be tested for 500 hours, which typically will take around 2 to 3 months, because it's not continuous testing. And after that, the dispatches will happen. We see one pump every quarter, but we can maximize this to up to six pumps per year.

items.statement: Next nuclear tender expected in next few months for 8 reactors at Mahi Banswara (ASHVINI JV) and other projects; KSB is currently approved supplier.
items.quote: What we are given to understand that it should come in next few months. What we understand is this will be for the projects in Mahi Banswara, which is under ASHVINI, that is NTPC/NPCIL JV, as well as some other projects. So it will be probably for eight reactors.

items.statement: Export business grew despite geopolitical issues in H1; supply chain reliability improved with revised pricing; export inquiries showing momentum for H2 recovery.
items.quote: Export business continued to grow despite of geopolitical kind of a pause or hassles what we faced in H1 2026. However, we hope to come back in H2 as the situation becoming more normal.

items.statement: Order intake split: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves 19%.
items.quote: Just to overview how we distribute the order intake, you can see Standard is 51%; Engineered, 14%, SupremeServ, 16%; and Valves is around 19%.

items.statement: H1 CY2026 revenue INR 12,920 million, EBITDA INR 1,465 million, PBT INR 1,279 million; 17% revenue CAGR, 22% PAT CAGR, 17% EBITDA CAGR.
items.quote: So INR 12,920 million half year ended, which KSB Limited (KSB) Institutional Investors Meet August 19, 2026 is the revenue from sales. EBITDA INR 1,465 million and profit before tax INR 1,279 million for the first half of

items.statement: SHANTI Act passed, rules published for comments; NTPC targeting 30 GW nuclear via JV with NPCIL and independently, part of 100 GW by 2047 target.
items.quote: And recent policy initiatives if you see SHANTI Act was passed and then recently the rules have been published for comments from the public and the stakeholders. And then we also have, I think, NTPC also is with joint venture with NPC IL as well as they are independently looking to add around 30 gigawatt.

items.statement: KSB is approved supplier for nuclear primary coolant pumps; competition (Kirloskar, Flowserve) entry depends on NPCIL decision; KSB has localization learning curve advantage.
items.quote: As far as competition is concerned, as of today, I think we are the approved supplier. What NPCIL will do, I think we can't say. It is finally left to them. But one thing is that we are at, I would say, leaders in this because we have already gone through the learning curve of the localization.

items.statement: Localization of nuclear pumps includes raw material, Hurth gear machines, mechanical seals, rotor parts, and castings now made in India; design tech already available.
items.quote: Localization meant in the earlier project, some of the parts were imported that have been completely produced in India. It includes raw material as well as some of the critical machine like we say Hurth gear machine and mechanical seals.

items.statement: SAP HANA implementation globally in H1 next year; cost allocation expected next year on revenue model.
items.quote: KSB worldwide as a global company is implementing HANA somewhere in H1 of next year. And we, of course, the model is a revenue model and we expect cost allocation in the next year.

items.statement: Nuclear test bed issues at NPCIL delayed GHAVP pump testing; resolution expected by end-August, testing to resume September.
items.quote: GHAVP is concerned, the pumps were tested somewhere in April and – the testing had started in April and May, but some issues were encountered in some other equipment in the test bed which was built by NPCIL

items.statement: Data centre cooling (liquid cooling) orders received from international OEMs in India; dedicated teams and product adaptation underway for HVAC, fire-fighting, plumbing applications.
items.quote: In India also, we have started focusing on this business and, especially, on the application of cooling liquid, liquid cooling application. We have got orders from international OEM based in India.

items.statement: Marine, mining, fire-fighting, and water project segments are emerging; product development ongoing for vertical turbine, large split case, submersible pumps to expand addressable market.
items.quote: We have been out of this project business market for many years, decades I would say. But, now, the products are being developed, vertical turbine pumps, big size split case pump, big size submersible pumps.

items.statement: H1 sales grew only 2-3% YoY, missing plan; EBIT impact attributed to volume shortfall, gross margin pressure, and OpEx absorption.
items.quote: A major thing if you saw overall sales, we hardly grew 2% to 3% over the last. So I would attribute that as one of the things and the growth which we wanted did not happen.

items.statement: BP&CL acquisition (2023) brought reciprocating pump capability and nuclear aftermarket installed base.
items.quote: And then we also acquired, as Mr. Bhave also said, BP &CL technology. During this acquisition, I think, we also had the nuclear aftermarket or nuclear installed base in our mind.

items.statement: Shirwal plant has dedicated nuclear organization with engineering and quality manpower per required codes; ISO-19443 recertified recently.
items.quote: We are, I think, one of the leaders in having the complete infrastructure for Nuclear Business, including the required manpower in engineering and quality as per the required code.

items.statement: Management targets 10-15% volume growth and 15% value growth; 20% possible but with peaks, not consistent.
items.quote: Yeah, in terms of volume, I would still put it between 10% to 15%. And in terms of value, maybe 15% would be a reasonably good figure. 20% is also possible, but that would come with peaks.

items.statement: SupremeServ aftermarket business growing steadily at 15% per annum; target revenue share 25-30% (excluding agri).
items.quote: I can say that steadily this business is growing 15% per annum. We want to continue to grow in that segment, because it's a profitable segment.

items.statement: BP&CL business expected to reach INR 40-50 crores annually once stabilized and able to participate in all tenders.
items.value: INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores annually
items.quote: Yeah, it would be constantly, at least we expect annual once we have stabilized, once we are able to participate in all tenders business, when I say reciprocating pumps, for example, and all those things. Yeah, a business of INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores annually is a figure which we could do

items.statement: Marine segment target INR 100 crore by next year, representing 3-5% of sales turnover.
items.quote: you ask me in our company, if we would reach a figure of INR 100 crore by next year, we would be happy. If I would say that to answer your question. 3% to 5% of my sales turnover in that business, we would be happy

items.statement: Export target 20% of sales; current order book at 15% of sales.
items.quote: Current order book is behind, I would say today it is, if I remember, it is 15% of the orders, 15% of the sales, whatever it is. And we want to kind of target 20%.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR 80-120 crores for sustenance and growth, including capacity, product development, offices, service stations.
items.value: INR 80 crores, INR 100 crores, INR 120 crores annually
items.quote: So whatever you see investment of INR 80 crores, INR 100 crores, INR 120 crores annually, we intend to do that.

items.statement: Good momentum in inquiries across infrastructure (railways, airports, metros), water, wastewater, energy; slight drop vs earlier forecast but no major impact.
items.quote: I think we are seeing a quite good outlook and a good momentum from the inquiries. I said about infrastructure, so infrastructure development, there is whether you talk of railways, whether you talk of airports, whether you talk of metros, those continuous activities continuously happening, Water, Wastewater, Energy.

items.statement: JJM 2.0 traction limited; some positivity but still struggling with past projects.
items.quote: Not so much. When I talk to my team, yeah, we are there. We are getting into there because of our product range. There is a bit of positivity, but there are still projects where we are still struggling from the past.

items.statement: First half slow on project pumps; many projects awaiting finalization; second half expected to be much better.
items.quote: Yeah. First half has been slow on the project pumps, I would say. But as I said, there are a lot of projects waiting to get finalized. So I just see that as a temporary thing. The second half should be much better.

items.statement: EBIT margin declined due to 2-3% sales growth vs plan; gross margin and OpEx affected; target EBITDA 13-14%.
items.quote: Yeah, basically we did not achieve our planned sales, I would say. A major thing if you saw overall sales, we hardly grew 2% to 3% over the last. So I would attribute that as one of the things and the growth which we wanted did not happen. So that was the major reason of having an impact on the EBIT.

items.statement: Aftermarket spare parts gross margins 2-3x new pump business; strategic orders at lower margins; day-to-day business in between.
items.value: 2 times, 3 times of our normal business
items.quote: Of course, if you talk spare parts are the higher margins business. Gross margins are much higher , 2 times, 3 times of our normal business, whatever we do for the new pumps.

items.statement: Export margins generally better than domestic due to higher market price levels.
items.quote: Yeah, in general, that would be a reasonable assumption. The market price levels in export markets are much better than Indian market.

items.statement: Foundry costs up 12-15%; standard market price hikes only single-digit so far; phased pass-through planned.
items.value: 12% to 15% foundry increase, single-digit price hike
items.quote: We have not been able to pass on the 100%. Let's say we give have been given foundries maybe in the range also of 12% to 15%. Our price hike to our standard markets would be still single-digit so far.

items.statement: Receivable days inched up due to solar business (state govt payments); improvement expected in H2 but not dramatic.
items.quote: Yeah. Like we discussed last time, this is meant to do to the solar business, what we elaborated last time. But we definitely see a good moment, I mean, this H2 actually.

items.statement: Export working capital cycle not necessarily higher; often lesser than domestic due to agile deliveries.
items.quote: Not necessarily. Because that working capital cycle is typical similar as India. And in fact, export deliveries are much less. They don't offer that luxury, so we have to be much more agile and efficient in export deliveries.

items.statement: Supply chain issues (castings, materials) impacted H1 deliveries; 80-85% resolved, supplies streamlining.
items.quote: We had issues on the supply chain as well. So we could not get all the castings and the material what we needed to deliver for our thing. So that was also equally impactful.

items.statement: Nuclear pumps mostly tailor-made/project pumps; standard pumps few (fire-fighting) but adapted to nuclear seismic standards.
items.quote: More or less, the critical pumps are all project pumps. Standard pumps are very few in the utilities like fire-fighting, et cetera, in the nuclear plant. But they also will be needed to be adapted to some nuclear standards of seismic, et cetera, et cetera.

items.statement: Nuclear pump execution cycle 24-36 months standard; deliveries to NPCIL ~48 months from order; dependent on NPCIL test bed.
items.value: 24 to 36 months standard, 48 months to NPCIL
items.quote: Our standard cycle is 24 to 36 months. But typically, our deliveries to NPCIL is around 48 months from the date of order.

items.statement: BP&CL making inroads into PSU customers (ONGC, Oil India, Fertilizer); building proven track record for tenders; reciprocating pumps EIL approval pending.
items.quote: We are making inroads into customers where we were not there. ONGC, for example, Oil India, all these customers and step by step, it will grow.

items.statement: Export sales 100% KSB India efforts; parent only sets territory/product guidelines; ground sales team local.
items.quote: It's our efforts, 100%. So the parents only makes a guideline that which territories and which products you're allowed to export. And so this is a general guideline so that they balance the loading of all factories globally.

items.statement: EU FTA unlikely to change export competitiveness (duties already low); may allow importing automation, circulator pumps, IE5 motors from parent to India.
items.quote: Talking of exports, I think it would not make much difference to us, because today we export to majority of the countries. T he import duties are hardly there. In Europe, it is not there at all

items.statement: APA signed this year, valid 5 years; royalty/license terms set; only change expected for S/4HANA cost allocation.
items.quote: You may be aware that KSB India signed the Advance Price Agreement, APA. So it was signed in this year. This means that all the guidelines are in place. And these APA regulations are valid for 5 years.

items.statement: S/4HANA implementation next year will increase OpEx; cost amount not yet quantified; lift-and-shift first, then process innovation.
items.quote: And, yes, there will be an impact next year on S/4HANA, which will be in the O pEx. It will be coming next year. So this is definitely we would like to share this with all of you that whatever cost comes normally from changing over to SAP to S/4HANA, the same would be also applicable to KSB India.

items.statement: Export growth dependent on external geopolitics (US tariffs, Middle East war); potential huge but unpredictable.
items.quote: But as, these external situations, become more and more, I think, disturbing factors to disturb that export growth. But, let's talk of U.S. market, we went there, then the tariffs came, and then some orders got cancelled. Then, we are still strong in Middle East, and then the war came.

items.statement: Inventory build-up from export orders awaiting clearances, FGD business closure, solar slowdown; being resolved over time.
items.quote: It is mainly due to the export orders, which is still waiting for clearances. There are some inventory due to the FGD business which suddenly closed down. So these have been some has been due to solar, which again slowed down.

items.statement: Pump portion typically 3-5% of total project value in segments like Data Centre, Marine; exact sizing difficult due to project execution uncertainty.
items.quote: And I say it always in anything that the pump portion in all these whatever you call it projects is a 3% to 5% is something of the total value of the project value. This is the normal ballpark or rough figure.

items.quote: Also, the raw material market was quite volatile, rig ht? So, in order to protect our business economics, we had that 233 basis points decline

items.quote: Since in last fiscal '26, we have deployed significant amount in our current assets. So, in this financial, we are expecting, converting into basically converting current assets into cash.

items.statement: Average retail sales per square foot INR20,000; monthly sales per store INR80-90 lakhs; ticket size INR500-1,000
items.quote: On an average, INR20,000 per square foot is our retail sales.

items.statement: Mature stores performing well; new stores in Rasayani, Babgaon, Uran responding better than expected

items.value: INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month

items.statement: Planning to launch whole spices category this quarter and 2-3 more categories next quarter targeting markets >INR2,000-3,000 crores
items.quote: Right, so within Indian Chaska we are -- we will be introducing one more category of whole spices for this quarter and moving on from next quarter we would also like to get into 2 or 3 more categories which are gaining more traction

items.statement: Focus on private label combos for quick commerce to sustain margins; pilot runs delivering in 20-30 minutes
items.quote: So, once we do that combo, then their margins and their advertising cost and their per SKU listing cost is sustainable.

items.statement: Cluster-based expansion in Tier-2/3 cities and suburban areas; avoiding high-cost urban centers like Navi Mumbai core
items.quote: So, we are focused on developing the pockets where there is less competition, we get that competitive and the first mover's advantage.

items.statement: Automation to reduce labour cost and improve quality control across contract manufacturing
items.quote: So, the very first that we would the very first effect that we would see is would be reduction of our labour cost for that matter. With that being said, our quality control would be much better.

items.statement: Online sales limited by touch-and-feel consumer behavior in Tier-2/3/4 cities for staple categories (>50% revenue)
items.quote: The online trend in certain categories where we have our USP, let's say, like a staple category, which contributes to more than like a 50% of our revenue, comes is still a very touch and feel category, right?

items.quote: Yes, certainly not per se brand ambassador but surely, we are now that we think that we know that the products right, the market acceptance is good, we would be doing a lot more marketing activities in terms of above the line and below the line as well.

items.statement: Retail wastage <0.1%; manufacturing achieves 360-degree processing with minimal waste
items.quote: Yes, it is it is less than 0.1%, and in manufacturing and processing, except for the sand that comes when we procure from our farmers, right, nothing really goes t o wastage

items.statement: Five-year focus on steady profitability, capital allocation, and volume; targeting Western suburbs and Pune PCMC expansion
items.quote: Right. So in the next five years, we in terms of our retail store footprints, we would try we will try to enter the Western suburbans as well as Pune PCMC regi on once the cluster is been identified

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-25% for FY27
items.quote: We expect to grow in the range of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 20% as new normal
items.quote: We currently are maintaining that we internally target 20% as our EBITDA number.

items.statement: Order book at INR1,778 crores, up 30% since March 2026 and 195% since June 2025
items.quote: Our order book for machines, as of the end of the quarter, stood at approximately INR1,780 crores, up 30% since March '26 and up 195% since June '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 19.9% vs 11.5% YoY, driven by volumes, operating leverage, efficiencies
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR100 crores compared with INR36 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 276%. EBITDA margins stood at 19.9% compared with 11.5% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Order book growth driven by domestic capacity expansions and non-packaging applications; not at peak yet
items.quote: We do not see a peaking of this order in the near future. There'll be a while before, you know, it kinds of because capex always happens in cycles. So, but we believe that this is not the, you know, peak.

items.statement: Exports at 41% of Q1 revenue; expected to stabilize at ~50% of revenue and order book
items.quote: We believe that exports would stabilize at around 50% of our revenue and order book going forward.

items.statement: Export sales prices 12-15% higher than domestic; command 15-20% premium over Chinese competitors
items.quote: As far as our offerings are concerned, we demand, we command, let's say, 15% to 20% higher prices than Chinese currently.

items.statement: Current utilization ~70-72%; peak capacity 80-85%; current capacity supports INR2,400-2,500 cr revenue
items.quote: We are currently operating at around 70%, 72% of capacity. And what we earlier said is that we can reach up to ideal capacity of around 85%.

items.statement: Light capex model; INR80-100 cr per INR500 cr incremental revenue beyond INR2,500 cr; 5-6 months to expand
items.quote: For every INR500 crores turnover going forward after we achieve INR2,500, we would require a capex of around INR80 to INR90 or INR100 crores.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle 81 days vs 84 days end of previous FY; focus on inventory, receivables, advances
items.quote: Our net working capital cycle at the end of the quarter stood at approximately 81 days compared with 84 days at the end of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-negative
items.quote: The company continues to be a net debt-negative company.

items.statement: Launched CoEx 1600 multi-layer coating line, Nova 6 Plus high-speed circular loom, FIBC cutting machines
items.quote: These included the multi-layer coating line, CoEx 1600, developed for demanding high-barrier applications in the flexible packaging industry, and our nova 6 plus, a high-speed six-shuttle circular loom with maximum weft insertion speed of up to 1,150 picks per minute.

items.statement: Established virtual remote assistance center at Kanpur; launched 3-month residential operator training program at TTRC
items.quote: We established a virtual remote assistance center at Kanpur, enabling our technical teams to connect with customers remotely and provide real-time audio and video guidance.

items.statement: Inquiry-to-order conversion rate 10-15% over 2-3 years; execution cycle 6-9 months
items.quote: we have seen a conversion rate of approximately 10% to 15% of the inquiries that we have. It varies from time-to-time, but generally speaking, 10% to 15% of the inquirie s that we have, they get converted into executable orders

items.statement: Spare parts revenue ~2-3% of installed plant value annually; perpetual recurring revenue stream
items.quote: We believe that around 2% to 3%, 3% approximately would be our revenue from the parts that he would require after commissioning every year, which are consumable parts.

items.statement: Spare parts gross margins 2-3% higher than machinery business
items.quote: So the spare parts margins gross margins are 2% to 3% higher than the machinery market, machinery business.

items.statement: Recycling machinery (polyolefin) currently 5-6% of revenue; targeting material contribution going forward
items.quote: Around 10% to 12% would be coming from the spare parts, and the balance 5%, 6% would be coming from these new initiatives that we have taken.

items.statement: R&D spend ~3% of revenue; focus on automation, IoT, confidential hero products
items.quote: So our R&D spend, like you mentioned, is around 3%. That continues to be our average going forward as well.

items.statement: Chinese competition faced globally; service is their weakness; command premium over Chinese pricing

items.statement: No specific regulatory benefit vs Chinese imports beyond customs duty; no BIS or other restrictions favoring Lohia
items.quote: No, not really. I mean other than the fact that Chinese and the European players have to pay custom duty to bring that equipment to India.

items.statement: Margin outlook subject to raw material price volatility, geopolitical risks, supply chain uncertainties
items.quote: In this world which is so changing fast, wars are happening in everywhere. So, one war ends and another war starts. The long-term impact of the movement of raw material or the parts, and China is also very strong player, what they supply and what they don't supply, all these will play a role in deciding the margins.

items.statement: Management expects to spend INR4,000 crores capex over next 3-4 years adding 3,000 beds
items.quote: We have in the next 3-4 years as we add the 3,000 beds, we will spend around INR4,000 crores of capex.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to be INR2,000 crores with INR900 crores already spent in Q1
items.quote: As far as the capex for the current year is concerned, I think so current year, we will end up spending almost INR2,000 crores of capex because of the greenfields and brownfields that are coming up.

items.statement: INR900 crores capex spent in Q1 FY27, front-loading investments for full-year benefit
items.quote: You'll also be happy to note that we have spent quite a lot of money in Quarter 1 itself. Almost INR900 crores has been spent in Quarter 1, so we're trying to front-end a lot of capex so that we get the benefit and leverage of that for the entire financial year.

items.statement: Electronic City 300-bed hospital launched in July (Q2 FY27); Raipur greenfield expected Q4 FY27; Kinder acquisition 100 beds may commission in FY27; Ahilya Nagar 80 beds in FY28
items.quote: The near 300-bed addition in terms of our Electronic City facility, which came up in Q2, that will happen. And we're expecting Raipur to get commissioned in, the Q4 of FY27. And Nashik is already added in terms of the 103 beds.

items.statement: Nashik brownfield added 103 beds with LINAC and PET-CT, taking licensed capacity to 307 beds
items.quote: We commissioned a brownfield capacity addition of 103 beds along with the newly installed linear accelerator and PET-CT at our Nashik hospital, increasing its overall licensed bed capacity to 307 beds.

items.statement: Bangalore licensed bed capacity now nearly 3,000 beds across 13 facilities after Electronic City launch
items.quote: This marks our 13th facility in the city, taking the overall licensed bed capacity in the city of Bangalore to nearly 3,000 beds.

items.statement: Sahyadri Q1 EBITDA margin 17.5%, up from acquisition; target to converge to network 24-25% over 16-18 month integration

items.statement: Digital revenue INR710 crores (23% of total); e-pharmacy 15,000+ orders, telehealth 17,000+ consults, chatbot 9,600+ interactions

items.quote: Now, like you mentioned, there is expansion happening in almost all locations of Sahyadri. Deccan Gymkhana is undergoing an expansion. An entire tower is getting added. Hadapsar is adding beds. Like you also know that we have started a greenfield in Wakad in North Pune.

items.quote: So there are about 58 of the clinicians now, because we've got nine hospitals in Pune, seven from the Sahyadri network, two from Manipal. So the interoperability has been increased. So about 58 clinicians now move across both the brands.

items.quote: Based on our recent performance and the current environment, we are raising our growth guidance to high teens for next few quarters while holding on to our margin range of underlying 20% EBITDA.

items.statement: Broad-based double-digit growth across categories and geographies with Beauty & Cosmetics and Oral Care both exceeding 20% growth
items.quote: Our growth continued to be broad-based across both categories and geographies. Beauty & Cosmetics maintained its strong growth trajectory with growth exceeding 20%, while Oral Care also crossed the 20% growth mark.

items.statement: Full cost inflation passed through to customers across all regions including raw material, freight and currency impacts

items.statement: Significant ahead-of-curve investments in capacity expansion, new technologies, and front-end capabilities for Beauty & Cosmetics growth

items.statement: Europe capacity expansion in extruded tubes, printing, and Beauty & Cosmetics capabilities like die and tooling
items.quote: We are expanding our capacities in extruded. We are expanding our capabilities on printing side and on multiple Beauty & Cosmetics capability like die and tooling, etcetera.

items.statement: Personal Care & Beyond now 54% of portfolio; sustainable tubes at 44% of product mix
items.quote: Personal Care & Beyond continues to expand and now accounts for 54% of our portfolio, further strengthening our presence in high-growth categories.

items.quote: So you're right that our working capital has gone up during this crisis period. However, this is largely driven by inventories. There are 2 reasons. One is the pricing of the inventory itself. With the raw m aterial prices going up, our inventory cost has gone up

items.statement: Net debt increased due to working capital build and ahead-of-curve capex investments
items.quote: One of the reasons for the net debt growing also is some of the ahead of the curve investments that we have made in our CapEx.

items.statement: Merger with Indovida progressing with CCI approval received; on track for planned timeline completion

items.quote: I think this year, on a full year basis, we should land anywhere between 20% to 22%. That's how we are looking at it.

items.statement: Europe operational challenges identified and getting disproportionate focus; margins expected to progressively recover to mid-teens
items.quote: We have identified certain cost inefficiencies, which are there in Europe today. And those we are working through very specific cost programs. And I think in the coming quarters, we will see Europe margins improving to our target range of mid-teens.

items.quote: We've fully divisionalized our front-end sales team, which means that in the past, we had one sales team which would sell both -- all our categories. Now we have a separate team which sells B&C and a separate team which focuses on Oral and large key accounts.

items.statement: Currency depreciation fully recovered through blended cost basis customer contracts
items.quote: All our customer contracts, Sanjesh, are on blended cost basis. So currency depreciation also gets recovered. Freight also saw a sharp increase, and we have been able to recover that from the customers.

items.statement: Recognized as one of India's Best Companies to Work For 2026 and won IMC Ramkrishna Bajaj National Quality Award
items.quote: Our focus on operational excellence and our people was also recognized through the prestigious IMC Ramkrishna Bajaj National Quality Award for Performance Excellence and our recognition as one of India's Best Company to Work For 2026.

items.statement: Group capex of about Rs 15 crore planned for FY27, with Rs 10 crore for automotive and Rs 5 crore for Future Tech metals

items.quote: In the tube valve segment, we have still not maxed out fully. There's, there's still more, I would say capacity available, but when it comes to tubeless, TPMS and even maybe the EV segment, we are kind of, you know, running at capacity utilization levels in excess of 85-90 %, right.

items.statement: Strong demand continues in Q2 across automotive and metals; EV two-wheeler demand outstripping supply
items.quote: So broadly I would say strong demand continues even now in Q2 with both automotive and metals, right.

items.quote: So sequentially, if you look at the gross contributions come down a little bit, I would say quarterly basis or let's say sequential basis, 145 bps, year on year basis down about 181 bps.

items.quote: Typically what happens is that when commodities move up. Or down for that matter. We are just pricing with our automotive customers both ways up and down. It's a pass through, right.

items.statement: New LOIs received from AUMOVIO, SENSATA and BOSCH for TPMS sensor base; programs lined up for Q3-Q4
items.quote: We've received some LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA these are two large global players in the TPMS census base and BOSCH, of course, is our existing customer also scaling up right now.

items.quote: So sequentially we moved up from 159 group consult sales to about 18 6. So that's that growth of about 17 and a half percent.

items.quote: Of course EBITDA also has, performed fairly well. I would say that we're up from about 11.3 crores to about 12.4 crores sequentially and up from 8.8 crores to about 12.4 crores YOY.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expanded due to record copper prices; short-term loans increased in line with drawing power and inventory
items.quote: So the working capital cycle has increased, it's expanded. So, you know, we were luckily able to raise and allocate sufficient funds for the business to continue smoothly and to keep growing.

items.statement: Debt/EBITDA hovering around 3x; targeting 2.5-3x by year-end
items.quote: Debt to EBITDA, we are just kind of hovering around the three mark. We are trying our best to bring that under three maybe somewhere between two and a half to three by the end of the year.

items.statement: Rs 4.2 crore capex spent in Q1; Rs 15 crore planned for full year FY27
items.quote: Cash flow side, of course, this is what it is, this is still the Q1, so you know there is a lot of, you know, money that we need to put into CapEx 4.2 crores already gone in there.

items.statement: Deepening engagement with Government of India to address Chinese dumping in climate control segment; not compromising margins
items.quote: I'll also have to say that we are deepening our engagement with government of India as well to kind of level the playing field between us and, you know, some of the large Chinese players are dumping goods right now into our country and of course we are not making any compromises in achieving our gross margins, right.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions (Middle East conflict, trade wars, rare earth weaponization) expected to persist for 5-10 years; vertically integrated model provides resilience

items.statement: EV component supply to Ather, TVS, River; engaged with other major players (Ola, etc.) but not yet supplying in volume; import substitution strategy

items.statement: Automotive growth to be sustained through FY27 via new programs (AUMOVIO, SENSATA, automotive AC, aftermarket, EV 2W); organic vehicle production growth may moderate from 18-20%
items.quote: moving into Q3 Q4, our growth will be fueled by newer and newer programs, right. items.statement: EV two-wheeler capacity investments needed to avoid running out of capacity by year-end; demand outstripping supply for Bajaj, TVS, Ather, Ola, River

items.statement: 3:1 bonus issue completed in first week of April 2026
